units.la: VEMADMODVM in amplissimo hoc immortalis Dei theatro, viri nobilitate, prudentia, & pietate spectatissimi, non solum infinita res in abditis Naturae penetralibus latentes, quarum modum causasq; nemo mortalium assequi potest, sed & cetera omnia quae propalam spectari & percipi queunt, admiratione plena sunt, sic ut illorum cognitione & contemplatione hominis animus mirifice pascatur ac delectetur: ita eorum etiam eventuum inspectio & consideratio, quae ante nostram aetatem inter mortales acciderunt, ob innumeras vicissitudines quibus haec vita redundat, liberales mentes incredibili voluptate perfundit. Maxime vero patriae historiae lectio, quae maiorum, quibus ortum nostrum debemus, quae terra cuius gremio fovemur & alimur, quae Reip. cuius sub umbra requiescimus, res memorandas tradit, sic animos nostros delinit & retinet, praesertim ubi aliquod vetustatis cognoscendae desiderium antecessit, ut ea nunquam satiari posse videantur. Idque tanto magis praestat, quo fortioribus ipsa radiis, ad caliginosam ignorantiae nubem depellendam, & priscae aetatis statum ob oculos ponendum, instructa est. Eum profecto robur & aes triplex circa pectus habere oportet, quem non maiorum res afficiunt, nec domesticae antiquitatis cognoscendae desiderium tangit.
units.tr: Just as, in this vast theatre of the immortal God, not only the infinite things hidden in the inner sanctuaries of Nature, whose manner and causes no mortal can grasp, but also all the other things that can be openly seen and perceived, are full of wonder, so that the mind of man is wonderfully nourished and delighted by their knowledge and contemplation; so too the inspection and consideration of those events which have happened among mortals before our own age, abounding as this life does in countless changes, floods free minds with incredible pleasure. Yet most of all the reading of the history of one's homeland, which relates the deeds worthy of remembrance of our forefathers, to whom we owe our origin, of the land in whose bosom we are cherished and nourished, and of the commonwealth under whose shade we rest, so charms and holds our minds, especially when some desire to know antiquity has gone before, that these seem never able to be satisfied. And this is all the more excellent, the more it is equipped with stronger rays, to drive away the dark cloud of ignorance and to set the condition of earlier times before our eyes. Surely he must have a heart of oak and triple bronze about his breast who is not moved by the deeds of his forefathers, nor touched by the desire to know the antiquity of his own people.

units.la: Haec cum ita sint, arbitror, viri amplissimi, intelligere vos, quamobrem duos hosce libros, nunc demum e pulveribus erutos, fastos nempe Colmarienses & M. Albertum Argentinensem, vobis deberi existimarim, eosdemq; nomini vestro inscribere ausus fuerim: scilicet, quod eorum auctores, e vestris urbibus ortum nomenve trahentes, non Germanorum solum, sed & specialiter Alsatarum, vestrarumq; Rerump. res plurimas, quae a Rudolfi Habspurgensis seculo, usq; ad Caroli quarti decessum, annis amplius centum, contigere, literarum monumentis bona fide commendarunt, quarum notitia, nisi illorum opera conservata fuisset, dudum oblivione sepulta evanuisset. Cum igitur & aliae nationes maiorum suorum egregia facinora disseminare studeant, existimavi non ingratum vobis fore, si videretis esse nonnullos, qui in nostra gentis antiquitate proferenda & illustranda laboris aliquid impenderent, quique vestrarum Rerumpubl. scriptores, diutius quam par erat a tineis corrosos, perennes reddere studuissent: nihil dubitans, multos ex ordine vestro Latinae linguae usu instructos, hosce, si non summae, attamen haud aspernanda classis auctores, attentius q exotericorum historias lecturos esse, degue rerum ab ipsis traditarum veritate omnium optime iudicare posse. ἐχαρος γὰρ χρίνη χαλὰς ἀ γνώσκει, ἡ τὸπῶ ἐς ἀγαθὸς χρῆς.
units.tr: These things being so, distinguished sirs, I think you understand why I have judged that these two books, now at last dragged out from the dust, namely the Colmar Annals and Master Albert of Strasbourg, are owed to you, and why I have dared to inscribe them to your name: plainly because their authors, drawing their origin and name from your cities, have faithfully committed to the written record very many events not only of the Germans but especially of the Alsatians and of your commonwealths, which happened over more than a hundred years, from the age of Rudolf of Habsburg until the death of Charles IV, and of which the knowledge, had it not been preserved by their labour, would long since have vanished buried in oblivion. Since, therefore, other nations also strive to spread abroad the outstanding exploits of their forefathers, I thought it would not be unwelcome to you if you saw that there were some who would expend some labour in bringing forward and illustrating the antiquity of our own people, and who strove to make perennial the writers of your commonwealths, eaten away by moths for longer than was fitting. I have no doubt that many from your order, trained in the use of the Latin tongue, will read these authors, if not of the highest class, yet not to be despised, more attentively, and will be able to judge best of all the truth of the things they relate. For "the good man judges the good, and knows them, and is good to them who are good" [ἐχαρος γὰρ χρίνη χαλὰς ἀ γνώσκει, ἡ τὸπῶ ἐς ἀγαθὸς χρῆς].

units.la: Oro igitur, quod auctores hos attinet, ut eos vestra clientela non indignos, & quasi diuturno exilio reduces factos, pro vestra virtute atque prudentia complectamini. Qui hominum coetibus agendo magnopere prosunt, hos merito colimus: at & iis etiam nihil officii & amoris debemus, qui ut lucubrando atque scribendo perpetuo prodesse possint, adnituntur. Siquidem saepe dubitatum video, utrum eo beneficio, quod per negotia agendo atque egregia multa nanciscendo comparatur, an eo quod per otium contemplando atque scribendo praestatur, amplius prodesse queamus. Me vero quod attinet, quanta possum observantia a vestra amplitudine contendo, ut hocce consilium meum, quo vos librorum istorum tutores publico testimonio constituere volui, simulq; laborem meum, in ius proferendis & lima anagnostica poliendis insumptum, aequi bonique consulere dignemini. Deum Opt. & Max. precor, ut vestris Rebuspublicis benedicat, & ornamenta vobis benigne concessa, clementer adaugeat atq; conserved. Basilea Helvetiorum die S. Thomae apostoli, anno virginei partus M.D.XXCIV.
units.tr: I therefore beg you, as far as these authors are concerned, to embrace them, as not unworthy of your patronage, and as if restored from a long exile, in keeping with your virtue and prudence. Those who greatly benefit human society by their public activity we rightly honour; yet we also owe no less duty and love to those who strive to be of constant service by study and writing. For I often see it doubted whether we can do more good by that benefit which is gained through conducting affairs and obtaining many excellent things, or by that which is rendered through leisure, contemplation and writing. As for myself, I beseech your magnificence with all the respect I can that you deign to take in good part both this my counsel, by which I have wished to appoint you guardians of these books by public testimony, and also my labour, spent in bringing them forth into the light and polishing them with an anagnostic file. I pray God, Best and Greatest, to bless your commonwealths, to graciously increase the honours kindly granted to you, and to keep them safe. Basel in Switzerland, on the feast of St Thomas the Apostle, in the year of the virginal birth 1584.

units.la: VETVS est illud & omnium ætatum assensu comprobatum: Dies diem docet. Ve-nim id in omnibus vitæ humanæ partibus suo modo quotidiana experientia satis comprobat: itaque in eo quoq; respub. literaria verum esse comperit, quòd vel indies novi ingeniorum fœtus eduntur: vel editi quidem & elaborati quodam, sed temporum iniuria, aut hominum imperitia invidiaue tenebris oppressi, in lucem tandem ac vitæ theatrum producuntur.
units.tr: It is an old saying, approved by the agreement of all ages: one day teaches another. And experience every day shows well enough that this holds in every part of human life. So too in the republic of letters it is found to be true, since new offspring of minds are brought forth almost daily; and those which have been produced and laboured over with some care, but have been overwhelmed in darkness by the injury of time, or by the ignorance or envy of men, are at last brought into the light and onto the stage of life.

units.la: Cœperant hi Colmarienfium fasti ante trecentos penè annos, à diligenti quodam monacho ordinis Prædicatorum, eiusdem vrbis, operæpretium ducente, memoriam rerum, quæ vel in ea vrbe vel circa illo ævo contigissent, inter efflorescentis suæ domus homines conseruari, quas illiterati suis studiis & occupationibus intenti, negligere, ac temporum progressu oblivioni mandare solerent. Eos deinde cum suam [illegible, ~10 letters] fastos (quod ex ipso exemplari haud obscurè animadverti potuit) alij eiusdem instituti & collegij socij locupletauêre, qui tamen suis quibusdam latebris occultati, in paucorum manus hactenus deuenerunt. Allatus est is mihi liber, edita Basilensi historia, ab amico, qui eũ Dn. Nicolai Briefferi Iurisconsulti, & S. Petri Basiliensis decani, viri antiquitatis Germanicæ peritissimi, & in conquirendis huius generis scriptoribus industrij & solertis, fuisse testabatur. Quem cum percurrissem, euidenter apparuit, eodem etiam Ioannem Stumpfium, in operoso illo rerum Helueticarum volumine contexendo, ante XL annos vsum esse: nec dubium, hunc illi à Briefero, vt & alia multa, communicatum fuisse. Etsi igitur priori parti, Annalibus nempe, minimi momentirtes, nec vllo delectationis aut utilitatis fructu commendabiles, hinc inde asperse fuerint, vtpote quando pluisset, quando traiectiones visa, quando porci Colmarienses subulcum laniassent, & similia: tamen cum de oppidorum, castrorum ac cœnobiorum in circum vicina regione ortu & incrementis, aliúsq; eo seculo apud Alsatas gestis, scitu non indigna & utilia, colligantur, haud aspernandos esse duxi: præsertim cum & Stumpfio vsui esse potuerint, eosq; in probatissimorum auctorum elencho, loco non indignos iudicârit. Humilibus itaq; & friuolis istis rebus, quæ fastidium parere poterât, rejectis, ceteris omnibus, etiam iis quæ vel leuis tantum pretij esse videbantur, retentis, librum in hocce Scriptorum choro comparêre volui: quod æquos & candidos omnes boni consulturos esse, confido.
units.tr: These Colmar annals were begun almost three hundred years ago by a diligent monk of the Order of Preachers of the same town, who thought it worth his while to preserve, among the men of his flourishing house, the memory of events that had occurred either in that town or in the surrounding region in his age, things which the unlettered, intent on their own studies and occupations, were accustomed to neglect and, as time went on, to consign to oblivion. Afterwards other fellow members of the same order and college enlarged these annals (as can be quite clearly seen from the exemplar itself), but, hidden away in certain corners, they have so far come into the hands of only a few. This book was brought to me, with the Basel history already published, by a friend who testified that it had belonged to Mr Nicolaus Brieffer, jurist and dean of St Peter's in Basel, a man most skilled in German antiquity and diligent and clever in searching out writers of this kind. When I read through it, it became quite evident that Johannes Stumpf had also used it forty years ago in composing that laborious volume on Swiss affairs; and there is no doubt that Brieffer communicated it to him, along with many other things. Although, therefore, the first part, namely the annals, has been disparaged here and there as being of very little importance and recommended by no fruit of pleasure or usefulness—for instance, when it rained, when floods were seen, when the Colmar pigs had mangled a swineherd, and similar things—nevertheless, since there are gathered from it matters worth knowing and useful concerning the origin and growth of towns, fortresses and monasteries in the surrounding region, and other events in that age among the Alsatians, I thought it not to be despised. Especially since these could be of use to Stumpf, and he judged them not unworthy to be placed in the list of the most approved authors. Therefore, with those humble and trivial matters, which could cause disgust, rejected, and all the rest, even those that seemed to be of slight value, retained, I wished to bring this book into this choir of writers; and I trust that all fair and candid readers will take it in good part.

XII. Passagium extitit puerorum. Ordines Teutonicorum, Minorum & Prædicatorum oriuntur. M. CC. XIII. Regina Vngariæ occisa à comite recitatur. Lutoldus episcopus Basiliensis obiit. M. CC. XIIII. Fridericus rex venit ad partes Alemanniæ. M. CC. XV. Hæretici comburuntur. Waltherus electus Basiliensis deponitur ab honore. M. CC. XVI. Innocentius papa obiit. Otho Imperator obiit. Ordo Prædicatorum confirmatur. M. CC. XVII. Facta est expeditio transmarina à rege Vngariæ & duce Austriæ. M. CC. XVIII. Dux Zeringiæ Bertoldus obiit. Rex Rudolfus nascitur, Calendis Maij. M. CC. XIX. Fridericus rex pro imperiali benedictione proficiscitur Romam. Dux Lotaringiæ cum exercitu Alsatiam ingreditur. M. CC. XX. Circa hunc annum destruxit miles, Curto nomine, turrim capellæ, quæ est in Ongersheim, & ædificauit castrum ex ea. Eodem anno phreneticus factus est. Henricus filius Friderici Imperatoris in regem Romanorum declaratur. M. CC. XXI. Fulco abbas Morbacensis obiit. Tartari Vngariam vastauerunt. Beatus Dominicus obiit. M. CC. XXIII. Henricus episcopus Argentinensis obiit. Orta est pestilentia pecorum. Eclipsis Lunæ apparuit. M. CC. XXVI. Ludouicus rex Franciæ obiit. Fundata est sancta Trinitas in Argentina. M. CC. XXVII. Bertoldus episcopus Argentinensis Berinstein obtinuit.
units.tr: Containing annals of various events that happened chiefly among the Alsatians in the thirteenth century after the Theophany [θεοφανείας]. In 1211 Emperor Otto was excommunicated throughout all Alemannia. In 1212 the Children's Crusade took place. The orders of the Teutonic Knights, the Minorites and the Preachers arose. In 1213 the killing of the queen of Hungary by a count is recorded. Bishop Lutold of Basel died. In 1214 King Frederick came to the parts of Alemannia. In 1215 heretics were burned. Walter, elect of Basel, was deprived of his office. In 1216 Pope Innocent died, and so did Emperor Otto. The Order of Preachers was confirmed. In 1217 an overseas expedition was made by the king of Hungary and the duke of Austria. In 1218 Duke Berthold of Zähringen died. King Rudolf was born on the Calends of May. In 1219 Frederick set out for Rome to receive the imperial blessing. The duke of Lorraine entered Alsace with an army. In 1220, about this year, a soldier named Curto destroyed the chapel tower at Ongersheim and built a castle out of it. In the same year he went mad. Henry, son of Emperor Frederick, was declared king of the Romans. In 1221 Fulco, abbot of Murbach, died. The Tartars laid waste Hungary. Blessed Dominic died. In 1223 Henry, bishop of Strasbourg, died. A pestilence broke out among the cattle. An eclipse of the moon appeared. In 1226 King Louis of France died. The Holy Trinity was founded in Strasbourg. In 1227 Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, obtained Bernstein.

units.la: Ludouicus comes Turingiæ iter transmarinum arripuit. M. CC. XXVIII.
units.tr: Louis, count of Thuringia, undertook an overseas journey. In 1228.

units.la: Bertoldus episcopus Argentinensis in Bladolsheim homines imper. deuicit.
units.tr: Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, subdued the men of Bladolsheim, who were subject to the Empire.

units.la: Messis terminata fuit ante festum S. Ioannis baptistæ. M. CC. XXIX.
units.tr: The harvest was finished before the feast of St John the Baptist. In 1229.

units.la: In Argentina Guldin crematur hæreticus. Fuit is vnus de ditioribus & potentioribus ciuibus Argentinensis ciuitatis.
units.tr: In Strasbourg Guldin, a heretic, was burned. He was one of the wealthier and more powerful citizens of the city of Strasbourg.

units.la: Conradus de Marburc prædicat. M. CC. XXXI.
units.tr: Conrad of Marburg preached. In 1231.

units.la: Ludouicus dux Bauariæ interficitur. Facta est persequutio hæreticorum. M. CC. XXXII.
units.tr: Duke Louis of Bavaria was killed. A persecution of heretics took place. In 1232.

units.la: S. Wilhelmus miraculis claruit.
units.tr: St William became famous for miracles.

units.la: Inchoatum est claustrum sororum in Columbaria.
units.tr: The convent of sisters at Columbaria was begun.

units.la: Tantus fuit æstus, quòd per Iulium & Augustum oua in fabulo coquerentur. M. CC. XXXIII.
units.tr: The heat was so great that eggs were cooked in the sand through July and August. In 1233.

units.la: S. Elisabeta claruit. Episcopus Curiensis occiditur.
units.tr: St Elizabeth became famous. The bishop of Chur was killed.

units.la: Conradus de Marburc occiditur. Translatus S. Dominicus. M. CC. XXXIIII.
units.tr: Conrad of Marburg was killed. St Dominic was translated. In 1234.

units.la: Fridericus comes Phirretarum, à filio suo, dicto Grimmel/ occiditur.
units.tr: Frederick, count of Pfirt, was killed by his son, called Grimmel.

units.la: Hyems frigida vineas extirpauit.
units.tr: A cold winter destroyed the vines.

units.la: Translatæ sunt sorores ad Basileam, & obtinuerunt ordinem sororum de Columbaria. M. CC. XXXV.
units.tr: The sisters were transferred to Basel and obtained the order of the sisters of Columbaria. In 1235.

units.la: Henricus rex accepit pueros à ciuitatibus.
units.tr: King Henry took boys from the cities.

units.la: Fridericus Imp. venit Columbariam, in multitudine camelorum. M. CC. XXXVI.
units.tr: Emperor Frederick came to Columbaria with a great number of camels. In 1236.

units.la: Vini abundantia fuit, & quartale pro denario dabatur, quod breui post vix xvi denariis poterat comparari. M. CC. XXXVII.
units.tr: There was an abundance of wine, and a quart was given for a penny, which shortly afterwards could scarcely be bought for sixteen pennies. In 1237.

units.la: Fridericus Imperator Cunradum filium suum in regem Teutoniæ coronauit.
units.tr: Emperor Frederick crowned his son Conrad king of Germany.

units.la: Gregorius ix excommunicauit Fridericum, in cœna Domini. M. CC. XXXVIII.
units.tr: Pope Gregory IX excommunicated Frederick on Maundy Thursday. In 1238.

units.la: Henricus de Thun episcopus Basilien sis obiit.
units.tr: Henry of Thun, bishop of Basel, died.

units.la: Coloniensis episcopus obiit: & electus est frater comitis de Hohenstraten.
units.tr: The bishop of Cologne died, and the brother of the count of Hohenstaufen was elected in his place.

units.la: Intrauit ordinem Prædicatorum, natus anno M. CC. XXI. M. CC. XXXIX.
units.tr: He entered the Order of Preachers; born in 1221. In 1239.

units.la: Terræmotus factus est mense Septembri. M. CC. XL.
units.tr: An earthquake occurred in September. In 1240.

units.la: Tartari Vngariam deuastant tribus annis. M. CC. XLI.
units.tr: The Tartars devastated Hungary for three years. In 1241.

units.la: Eclipsis Solis accidit, nonis Octobris.
units.tr: An eclipse of the sun occurred on the nones of October.

units.la: Gregorius papa obiit, & vacauit sedes per triennium. M. CC. XLII.
units.tr: Pope Gregory died, and the see was vacant for three years. In 1242.

units.la: Destructum est castellum Bruccum. M. CC. XLIII.
units.tr: The castle of Bruck was destroyed. In 1243.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus de Habispurch miles efficitur. M. CC. XLIIII.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg was made a knight. In 1244.

units.la: Innocentius papa obiit apud Lugdunum. Bertoldus episcopus Argentin. obiit. M. CC. XLVI.
units.tr: Pope Innocent died at Lyons. Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, died. In 1246.

units.la: Henricus Lantgrauius Turingiæ in regem eligitur Romanorum.
units.tr: Henry, landgrave of Thuringia, was elected king of the Romans.

units.la: Pugna fuit in Frácfurt, die Osualdi: Coradus rex Teutoniæ victus ab episcopis.
units.tr: There was a battle at Frankfurt on the day of St Oswald: Conrad, king of Germany, was defeated by the bishops.

units.la: Pugna fuit apud Veltchilchi prope Colmariam. M. CC. XLVII.
units.tr: There was a battle at Veltchilchi near Colmar. In 1247.

units.la: Henricus rex obiit. Fridericus dux Austriæ occiditur.
units.tr: King Henry died. Frederick, duke of Austria, was killed.

units.la: Fratres Prædicatores de Turego expelluntur tribus annis.
units.tr: The Preaching Friars were expelled from Zurich for three years.

units.la: M. CC. XLVIII.
Parmenses obsessi liberantur.
units.tr: The besieged men of Parma were set free.

units.la: Sorores de Klingental obtinuerunt ordinem.
units.tr: The sisters of Klingental obtained the order.

units.la: Rubeacenses Colmarienses vicerunt, & ceperunt multos ex eis.
units.tr: The men of Rappoltsweiler defeated the men of Colmar and captured many of them.

units.la: M. CC. XLIX.
Lutoldus Basil. episcopus obiit, Bertold· succedit. Nicolaus de Tittinheim obiit.
units.tr: Lutold, bishop of Basel, died, and Berthold succeeded him. Nicholas of Tittinheim died.

units.la: M. CC. L.
Fridericus depositus Imperator obiit.
units.tr: Frederick, the deposed emperor, died.

units.la: Cunradus filius Friderici, sanctam Crucem oppidum destruxit.
units.tr: Conrad, son of Frederick, destroyed the town of Heiligkreuz.

units.la: M. CC. LI.
Multitudo pastorum in Francia congregatur.
units.tr: A great crowd of shepherds gathered in France.

units.la: Frater Hugo Cardinalis, legatus, cantavit primam Missam in area Prædicatorum in Argentina.
units.tr: Brother Hugh, the cardinal legate, sang the first Mass in the courtyard of the Preachers at Strasbourg.

units.la: M. CC. LII.
Occisus est sanctus frater Petrus ordinis Prædicatorum apud Mediolanum.
units.tr: Holy Brother Peter of the Order of Preachers was killed at Milan.

units.la: Dominæ de S. Ioanne sub-tilia, Colmariam se traστulerunt. Visi sunt tres soles.
units.tr: The ladies of St John (of the Sub-tilia?) transferred themselves to Colmar. Three suns were seen.

units.la: M. CC. LIII.
units.tr: In the year 1253.

units.la: Canonizatus est S. Petrus.
units.tr: Saint Peter was canonized.

units.la: In Altichilchin inventæ sunt duæ caluariæ habentes spissitudinem duorum digitorum.
units.tr: In Altichilchin two skulls were found, each two fingers thick.

units.la: Sorores ordinis Prædicatorum de Hüsgren apud Phaphinetum, recesserunt, quę modò Klingentalenses dicuntur.
units.tr: The sisters of the Order of Preachers at Hüsgren, near Phaphinetum, withdrew; they are now called the Klingental sisters.

units.la: Innocentius papa moritur. Sol videbatur scissus.
units.tr: Pope Innocent died. The sun was seen to be split.

units.la: M. CC. LIIII.
units.tr: In the year 1254.

units.la: Rex Cunradus, filius Friderici Imp. obiit: Wilhelmus de Holandia succedit.
units.tr: King Conrad, son of Emperor Frederick, died; William of Holland succeeded him.

units.la: Ludouicus rex Franciæ rediit de partibus transmarinis.
units.tr: King Louis of France returned from overseas.

units.la: M. CC. LV.
units.tr: In the year 1255.

units.la: Frater Bertoldus de ordine Minorum solenniter prædicat.
units.tr: Brother Berthold of the Order of Minorites preached solemnly.

units.la: Innocentius papa obiit, Alexander succedit.
units.tr: Pope Innocent died; Alexander succeeded him.

units.la: Destructum est castrum apud S. Amarinum.
units.tr: The castle near Saint Amarinus was destroyed.

units.la: Ædificatum est castrum in valle S. Amarini, ab abbate Theobaldo Morbacensi. Destructum autem fuit anno 1268.
units.tr: A castle was built in the valley of Saint Amarinus by Abbot Theobald of Murbach. It was destroyed in the year 1268.

units.la: M. CC. LVI.
units.tr: In the year 1256.

units.la: Wilhelmus rex morte miserabili interiit, interfectus à Frisonibus.
units.tr: King William died a wretched death, killed by the Frisians.

units.la: Fames erat. Dux Bauariæ vxorem suam interfecit.
units.tr: There was famine. The Duke of Bavaria killed his wife.

units.la: Wilhelmus librum contra Prædicatores scripsit, & omnes religiosos. A papa damnatur, & igni traditur in die Francisci.
units.tr: William wrote a book against the Preachers and all the religious orders. He was condemned by the pope and burned on the feast of Saint Francis.

units.la: M. CC. LVII.
units.tr: In the year 1257.

units.la: Richardus frater regis Angliæ donis regnum obtinuit Romanorum.
units.tr: Richard, brother of the King of England, obtained the kingdom of the Romans by gifts.

units.la: In Brusbach monte Brisgaudiæ inuenicbatur argentum in magna quantitate.
units.tr: On Brusbach mountain in Breisgau silver was found in great quantity.

units.la: M. CC. LVIII.
units.tr: In the year 1258.

units.la: Combustum est monasterium Basiliense, & magna pars ciuitatis, in vigilia Martini.
units.tr: The monastery of Basel, and a large part of the city, was burned on the eve of Martinmas.

units.la: Rex Franciæ vincitur à paganis.
units.tr: The King of France was conquered by the pagans.

units.la: M. CC. LIX.
units.tr: In the year 1259.

units.la: Virtuosus dominus Waltherus de Horburch fuit fraudulenter à suis consanguineis interfectus, in festo S. Iacobi in messibus.
units.tr: The worthy lord Walter of Horburg was treacherously killed by his own kinsmen, on the feast of Saint James, during the harvest.

units.la: Translatæ sunt sorores de Hüsgren in Werrahe vallem, quæ postea Klingintal dicebatur: eò quòd dominus de Klingin sororibus fratrum Prædicatorum in remedium animæ suæ liberè contulisset.
units.tr: The sisters from Hüsgren were transferred to the Werra valley, afterwards called Klingental, because the lord of Klingen had freely granted them to the sisters of the Preaching friars for the remedy of his soul.

units.la: M. CC. LX.
units.tr: In the year 1260.

units.la: Interfecerunt Iudæi in Wissenburg puerum.
units.tr: The Jews in Wissenburg killed a boy.

units.la: Dedicata est ecclesia fratrum Prædicatorum in Argentina.
units.tr: The church of the Preaching friars in Strasbourg was dedicated.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Argentinensis obiit.Mulier peperit quatuor pueros in Ratsamhusen.Ciuitas Rubeacum exusta est.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Strasbourg, died. A woman gave birth to four boys in Ratsamhausen. The town of Rubeacum was burned down.

units.la: M. CC. LXI.
units.tr: In the year 1261.

units.la: Flagellatores Teutoniam transfuerunt.
units.tr: The Flagellants passed into Germany.

units.la: Inuenta fuerunt ossa, quæ videbantur hominum, prope castrum <bl>Hertin</bl>/ propè Basileam, magnitudinem & longitudinem nostram triginta pedum excedentia.
units.tr: Bones were found near the castle of Hertin, near Basel, which appeared to be human and exceeded our size, being thirty feet in length and breadth.

units.la: Fui Parisius. Fundamentum Chori nostri.
units.tr: I was in Paris. The foundation of our choir.

units.la: M. CC. LXII.
units.tr: In the year 1262.

units.la: De Argentina fuerunt multi milites interfecti.
units.tr: Many soldiers were killed from Strasbourg.

units.la: Ioannes Scultetus in Columbaria cum multis nobilibus interfectus.
units.tr: John Scultetus was killed at Columbaria together with many nobles.

units.la: Expugnatum fuit castrum in <bl>Mülhusen.</bl>
units.tr: The castle at Mülhausen was taken by storm.

units.la: Alsa ibidem congelata & caristia frumenti.
units.tr: There was frost there in the month of ... and a dearth of grain.

units.la: M. CC. LXIII.
units.tr: In the year 1263.

units.la: Canonici Lutenbacenses castrum sibi vicinum per violentiam destruxerunt.
units.tr: The canons of Lutenbach destroyed by force a castle near them.

units.la: D. Waltherus de Geroltsecke episcopus Argentinensis obiit.
units.tr: Lord Walter of Geroldseck, bishop of Strasbourg, died.

units.la: M. CC. LXIIII.
units.tr: In the year 1264.

units.la: Cometa apparuit in oriente, quadraginta diebus, circa Kalen. Augusti, duabus horis ante ortum Solis. Fuit principio magnus & clarus, comam habens longam & latam, quæ de die in diem coepit deficere, Soli adiungi, & ad nihilum devenire.
units.tr: A comet appeared in the east for forty days, about the Kalends of August, two hours before sunrise. At first it was great and bright, having a long and broad tail; from day to day it began to fade, to draw near the sun, and to come to nothing.

units.la: M. CC. LXV.
units.tr: In the year 1265.

units.la: Castrum & castellum Burcdorf, quidam ex civibus tradiderunt comiti de Habspurch.
units.tr: Some of the citizens handed over the castle and fortress of Burgdorf to the Count of Habsburg.

units.la: Aqua quæ fluit per civitatem Basiliensem & dicitur <bl>Birsich</bl>/ inundauit, & plurima devastauit.
units.tr: The water which flows through the city of Basel, called the Birsig, flooded and devastated very much.

units.la: Mappam mundi descripsi in pelles duodecim pergameni.
units.tr: I drew a map of the world on twelve skins of parchment.

units.la: M. CC. LXVI.
units.tr: In the year 1266.

units.la: Claustrum & villam Luceriam ventus sive turbo pro magna parte destruxit, & pinnam templi in terram a longe deportauit.
units.tr: A wind or whirlwind destroyed for the most part the monastery and village of Lucerne, and carried the pinnacle of the church from afar and cast it to the ground.

units.la: Frater Achilles quondam Prior, prædicator generalis, incœpit crucem ad transmarinas partes prædicare.
units.tr: Brother Achilles, formerly prior and general preacher, began to preach the cross for the lands overseas.

units.la: Scalarij & monachi milites, curiam habuerunt Basileæ.
units.tr: The Scalarii and the monk-soldiers held court at Basel.

units.la: M. CC. LXVII.
units.tr: In the year 1267.

units.la: Conradus Wernherus de Hadstat ordinem Teutonicorum ingressus. Cuius receptioni multi nobiles ex Alsatia interfuerunt, in castro <bl>Bücheim.</bl>
units.tr: Conrad Werner of Hadstatt entered the Teutonic Order. Many nobles from Alsace attended his reception, at the castle of Bücheim.

units.la: Ex Alsatia plus quàm quingenti peregrinati sunt in Quadragesima ad partes transmarinas.
units.tr: More than five hundred people from Alsace went on pilgrimage to the lands overseas in Lent.

units.la: Eclipsis Solis, vigilia Vrbani, prædicta à fratre Godfrido Astronomo ordinis Prædicatorum in Vormatia.
units.tr: An eclipse of the sun, on the eve of Urban, was foretold by Brother Godfrey, astronomer of the Order of Preachers, at Worms.

units.la: Orta est stella in ortu Solis, pulchra & magna, propè Lunam, ea existente decima octaua, in mense Iulij xviii, quæ magno impetu progressa de Luna versus Orientem ad medietatem hemisphærij, relinquens post se comam sive nubem albam, vel nubem incensam, & minorem sequentem, quæ pariter esse desierunt. Annus bonus & in omnibus abundans.
units.tr: A star appeared at sunrise, beautiful and great, near the moon, the moon being in its eighteenth day, in the month of July, the eighteenth. It moved with great speed from the moon towards the east to the middle of the sky, leaving behind it a white tail or a kindled cloud, and a smaller one following, which likewise ceased. The year was good and abundant in everything.

units.la: M. CC. LXVIII.
units.tr: In the year 1268.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis expugnauit <bl>Hertinberch</bl> & <bl>Bladolsheim</bl>/ quæ tunc erant comitis Rudolfi.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel took by storm Hertinberg and Bladolsheim, which then belonged to Count Rudolph.

units.la: Fui in Vrania, *festo Gordiani & Epimachi, cecidit Risina magna prope villam Altorf/ & secum duxit lapidem, qui habebat duodecim pedes in latitudine, & tredecim in longitudine, quæ ecclesiam & multos pene homines deleuerat cum prædicante. Septem autem vaccas & arbores multas devastauit.
units.tr: I was in Uri. On the feast of Gordian and Epimachus a great rockfall (Risina) fell near the village of Altorf, and it carried with it a stone which was twelve feet in breadth and thirteen in length, which had destroyed the church and almost all the people with the preacher. It also laid waste seven cows and many trees.

units.la: Circa Columbariam non pluit duodecim septimanis, videlicet, à festo Mathiæ, vsq; ad festum Septem fratrum, fuitq; calor maximus.
units.tr: Around Columbaria it did not rain for twelve weeks, namely from the feast of Matthias to the feast of the Seven Brothers, and there was the greatest heat.

units.la: Rhenus creuit adeò quòd omnes pontes destruxit.
units.tr: The Rhine rose so much that it destroyed all the bridges.

units.la: M. CC. LXIX.
Comes Rodolphus de Habspurch & ciues Columbarienses, expugnârunt castrum Richenstein/& ceperunt duos dominos castri, dictos Gefelin. Fecit & in Argentina milites plures.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg and the citizens of Colmar stormed the castle of Reichenstein and captured its two lords, called Gefelin. He also made many soldiers in Argentina.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis emit à comite Gotfrido cognato suo, pro CCLX marcis castrum Biedertan.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel bought the castle of Biedertan from his cousin Count Gottfried for 260 marks.

units.la: Ecclesia sororum de sancto Ioanne in Columbaria, consecratur.
units.tr: The church of the sisters of St John in Colmar was consecrated.

units.la: M. CC. LXX.
In Thanfotus fuit pulliculus quatuor pedes habens, ex ouo gallinæ.
units.tr: In Thanfotus there was a little chick with four feet, hatched from a hen's egg.

units.la: Per Basileam transiuit quidam Stochilinus, qui dicebat se esse Conradinum, filiu regis Conradi, quē Carolus frater regis Franciæ cū tribus nobilibus fecit decollari.
units.tr: A certain Stochilinus passed through Basel, claiming to be Conradin, son of King Conrad, whom Charles, the brother of the king of France, had beheaded along with three noblemen.

units.la: Comes Phitretarum cepit fratre suum, nomine Greuelinum, & procuratorem suum Luzardum de Senhen/& extorsit abeis magnam pecuniam.
units.tr: The count of Pfirt captured his brother, named Greuelinus, and his agent Luzard of Senhen, and extorted a large sum of money from them.

units.la: Comes Rudolphus de Habspurc & abbas S. Galli exercitum magnum congregantes, venerunt in Seckingen / vt ciuitatem Basiliensem tribus diebus obsiderent, sed minimè potuerunt.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg and the abbot of St Gall gathered a great army and came to Säckingen, intending to besiege the city of Basel for three days, but they were in no way able to do so.

units.la: Domina comitis Gotfridi, festo Margaretæ, filium peperit.
units.tr: On the feast of St Margaret, the wife of Count Gottfried bore a son.

units.la: Eclipses Lunæ in crepusculo, secunda feria post Palmarum, & Kal. Augusti.
units.tr: Eclipses of the moon at twilight, on the second day after Palm Sunday, and on the first of August.

units.la: Rex Franciæ cū filio cruce signati, imperfecto opere in Tunis pariter perierunt.
units.tr: The king of France, signed with the cross, together with his son, perished in Tunis, the work left unfinished.

units.la: Caput S. Pantali episcopi Basiliensis, qui cum S. Vrsula & sodalibus Coloniæ fuit decollatus, à viro prouido atq; discreto abbate ... in Basileam delatum, ab Henrico episcopo Basiliensi receptum est cum magna reuerentia.
units.tr: The head of St Pantalus, bishop of Basel, who was beheaded at Cologne along with St Ursula and her companions, was brought to Basel by a prudent and discreet abbot ..., and was received with great reverence by Henry, bishop of Basel.

units.la: Translati sunt ad fratres Friburgenses de Basiliensibus.
units.tr: Some of the Basel relics were transferred to the Friars of Freiburg.

units.la: Viri duo religiosi Arnaldus & Tiermarus in russis cappis venerunt in Sueuiam, & quædam contra fidem catholicam differebant.
units.tr: Two religious men, Arnaldus and Tiermarus, came into Swabia in red cloaks and disputed certain matters against the Catholic faith.

units.la: M. CCC. LXXI.

Episcopus Argentinensis & Basil. Henricus Mülhusen obsederunt sex diebus circa festum apostolorum Petri & Pauli. Et frumentum quod vendebatur in principio obsidionis 30 solidis, dabatur circa finem 30 denariis, vel 17 voluntarie.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Strasbourg and of Basel, besieged Mülhausen for six days around the feast of the apostles Peter and Paul. Wheat, which at the start of the siege was sold for 30 shillings, was at the end given for 30 pennies, or 17 willingly.

units.la: Dominus Henricus episcopus Basiliensis emit à comite Phitretarum Vlrico & filio eius comitatum Phitretarum pro mille marcis, & ab eo in feodum receperunt.
units.tr: Lord Henry, bishop of Basel, bought the county of Pfirt from Count Ulrich of Pfirt and his son for a thousand marks, and they received it back from him as a fief.

units.la: Lupi in Ssholtz plures pueros comederunt.
units.tr: Wolves in Schotz ate many boys.

units.la: Fratres S. Augustini in Gebwiler valle, in qua ante paucos annos ciuitas inchoata fuerat, suum Capitulum celebrauerunt.
units.tr: The Augustinian friars in the valley of Gebweiler, where a town had been begun a few years earlier, held their chapter.

units.la: Comes Rud. de Habspurc posuit exactionem super homines suos aduocatitios, & accepit abeis xx mille quartalia frumenti.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg imposed an exaction upon his men subject to advocacy and took from them twenty thousand quarters of wheat.

units.la: Milites Stelliferi expulsi de Basilea hinc inde vagabantur.
units.tr: The Stellifer soldiers, expelled from Basel, wandered hither and thither.

units.la: Gregorius duodecimus electus in festo Ægidij.
units.tr: Gregory XII was elected on the feast of St Giles.

units.la: Comes Gotfridus de Laufenberck obiit.
units.tr: Count Gottfried of Laufenberg died.

units.la: Comes de Friburck obiit.
units.tr: The count of Freiburg died.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus combussit monasterium Grandis vallis, & plures villas.
units.tr: Count Rudolf burned the monastery of Grandvaux and several villages.

units.la: De Richen rustici interfecerunt nobilem virum Wernherum militem Basiliensem, dictum de Argentina.
units.tr: Peasants of Reichen killed the noble knight Werner of Basel, called of Strasbourg.

units.la: Dominus episcopus Basiliensis dedit castrum ..... cum quadraginta marcarum redditibus pro castro Tuffenstein/domino de Tuffenstein.
units.tr: The lord bishop of Basel gave the castle of ..., with an income of forty marks, in exchange for the castle of Tuffenstein, to the lord of Tuffenstein.

units.la: Mures frumenta devastant: caristia magna.
units.tr: Mice devastated the grain: a great dearth.

units.la: M. CC. LXXII.
Tempus nebulosum à xv calendas Septembris vsq; Hilarij: raro apparuerunt Sol vel Luna. Aura temperata.
units.tr: The weather was cloudy from the 18th of August until Hilary's day; the sun or moon rarely appeared. The air was mild.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus de Habspurc castrū Tuffenstein obsedit, & funditus destruxit.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg besieged the castle of Tuffenstein and utterly destroyed it.

units.la: Castrum Werra reædificatur, contra voluntatem sororum de Clingental/ab episcopo Basiliensi Henrico.
units.tr: The castle of Werra was rebuilt, against the will of the sisters of Klingental, by Bishop Henry of Basel.

units.la: Iohannes miles de Lansere à seruis suis occiditur.
units.tr: Knight John of Lansere was killed by his servants.

units.la: In Wadwir & vicinis villis lupi plus quàm xl pueros comederunt.
units.tr: In Wadwil and the neighbouring villages, wolves ate more than forty boys.

units.la: In castro Wolfach gallina quotidie penè duo ova posuit, cum duobus vitellis.
units.tr: In the castle of Wolfach a hen laid almost two eggs every day, each with two yolks.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus de Habspurc cum exercitu veniens prope Friburgum, post Basil. festum S. Margaretæ homines & messes nimis grauiter deuastauit. Volens autem ciues de Nuwenburch lædere, non potuit: quòd dominus Basiliensis affuit eis præsidio festinanter.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg, coming with an army near Freiburg after the feast of St Margaret of Basel, laid waste the men and the crops too severely. But when he wished to harm the citizens of Neuenburg, he could not, because the lord of Basel quickly came to their aid with a garrison.

units.la: Post plures dies episcopus Rhenum transiens, comiti Rudolfo plures villas devastauit, plures etiam igne cremauit: cœmiterium Richishcim prorsus deleuit.
units.tr: Several days later the bishop crossed the Rhine and laid waste many villages of Count Rudolf, and burned many more with fire; he utterly destroyed the cemetery of Richishaim.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus congregato exercitu venit prope Basileam, villam ibidem succendit, & prædam Seconium deduxit. Basilienses ipsum insequuti, ipsi nocere minime poterant vel audebant.
units.tr: Count Rudolf, having gathered an army, came near Basel, set fire to a village there, and led off the booty to Seckingen. The Baslers pursued him, but could not or dared not harm him.

units.la: Die octaua Laurentij ortus est ignis in domo quadam & totum Seconium præter ecclesiam S. Petri, & domos vicinas quatuor, penitus concremauit. Ipso autem die venit episcopus Basiliensis cum suis, oppidum expugnauit, & omnia quæ in eo reperit demolitus est.
units.tr: On the eighth day after St Lawrence a fire broke out in a certain house and utterly consumed all of Sekingen except the church of St Peter and four neighbouring houses. On that same day the bishop of Basel came with his men, stormed the town, and demolished everything he found in it.

units.la: Castrum Othmarsheim ciues Nuwenburgenses igne penitus deleuerunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Neuenburg completely destroyed the castle of Othmarsheim by fire.

units.la: Claustrum Sicikilchen exercitus comitis Rudolfi igne suppositò destruxit.
units.tr: The army of Count Rudolf destroyed the convent of Sicikilchen by setting fire to it.

units.la: Claustrum Gutnowe comes Henricus, frater comitis Friburgensis pro ablutione reddituum suorum penitus deuastauit.
units.tr: Count Henry, brother of the count of Freiburg, utterly laid waste the convent of Gutnow, to settle the accounts of its revenues.

units.la: Suburbium Basiliense prope portam crucis, comes Rudolfus insequente nocte Bartholomeum per flammam deuorauit.
units.tr: Count Rudolf, in the following night, consumed the suburb of Basel near the Cross Gate by fire, as far as St Bartholomew's.

units.la: Frigus fuit magnum tribus septimanis, & præcipuè tribus diebus ante natiuitatem Domini. Congelabatur enim sacramentum dominici sanguinis ante eleuationem Eucharistiæ. Fons congelatus in Sultzmatin, & puteus in Rubiaca. Frigus autem in natiuitate Domini soluebatur.
units.tr: There was a great frost for three weeks, and especially for three days before the Lord's nativity. For the sacrament of the Lord's blood froze before the elevation of the Eucharist. A spring froze at Sultzmatt, and a well at Rubiaca. But the frost melted at the Lord's nativity.

units.la: M. CC. LXXIII.
Vigilia Siluestri, rusticus quidam, Lupus nomine & re, tradidit castrum Werra comiti Rudolfo, & captus fuit in eo dominus de Rötelsheim clericus, filius sororis episcopi Basiliensis, & alij multi.
units.tr: On the vigil of St. Sylvester, a certain peasant named Wolf, Lupus by name and by nature, handed over the castle of Werra to Count Rudolf; and in it were captured the lord of Rötelsheim, a clergyman, son of the sister of the Bishop of Basel, and many others.

units.la: Homines abbatis S. Galli acceperunt comitem Rudolfum in aduocatum.
units.tr: The men of the abbot of St. Gall received Count Rudolf as their advocate.

units.la: Obiit episcopus Curiensis, quondam frater ordinis Prædicatorum.
units.tr: The Bishop of Chur died; he was formerly a brother of the Order of Preachers.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis ædificauit castrum in Büscheim / & castrum ..... Marschalcus interficitur.
units.tr: The Bishop of Basel built a castle at Büscheim, and ..... Marschalk was killed.

units.la: Circa festum S. Dominici fratres Prædicatores perfecerunt suum campanile.
units.tr: Around the feast of St. Dominic, the Preaching Friars completed their bell tower.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus de Habspurc obsedit Basileam tribus diebus cū potentia magna, circa festum S. Margaretæ.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg besieged Basel for three days with a great force, around the feast of St. Margaret.

units.la: Vallis S. Gregorij a comite Rudolfo deuastatur.
units.tr: The Valley of St. Gregory was laid waste by Count Rudolf.

units.la: In vigilia S. Laurentij depraedatus est comes Rudolfus villam Clingin, & castrum pene ceperat, & equitauit cum exercitu prope Basileam, & ciues non audebant prohibere eum.
units.tr: On the vigil of St. Lawrence, Count Rudolf plundered the village of Klingen and had nearly taken the castle; he rode with his army close to Basel, and the citizens did not dare to stop him.

units.la: In festo S. Mauritij factæ sunt treugæ, vsq; ad festum S. Galli, inter Basiliensem episcopum, & comitem Rud. de Habspurc.
units.tr: On the feast of St. Maurice a truce was made, lasting until the feast of St. Gall, between the Bishop of Basel and Count Rudolf of Habsburg.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus de Habspurc in regem eligitur Romanorum.
units.tr: Count Rudolf of Habsburg was elected King of the Romans.

units.la: Milites Stelliferi intrauerunt Basileam.
units.tr: The Knights of the Star entered Basel.

units.la: Exercitus comitis Rudolfi, quo Basileam obsidere voluerat, redit ad sua. Episcopus Basiliensis congregationem suam, qua obsidionem prohibere voluit, dimisit.
units.tr: The army of Count Rudolf, with which he had wished to besiege Basel, returned home. The Bishop of Basel dismissed his own gathered force, with which he had wished to prevent the siege.

units.la: Sopita est controuersia inter Prædicatores & Minores, propter hæresim quæ orta fuit in Rhetia prope Augustam.
units.tr: The controversy between the Preachers and the Minorites was settled, on account of the heresy that had arisen in Rhaetia near Augsburg.

units.la: Tempus vindemiarum fuit siccum & amœnum: parum vini creuit, quòd vineæ circa natiuitatem Domini frigore perierant.
units.tr: The vintage season was dry and pleasant; little wine was produced, because the vines had been destroyed by frost around the Nativity of the Lord.

units.la: M. CC. LXXIIII.

Rudolfus rex Romanorum venit Basileam, sabbato ad vesperas, in octaua Epiphaniæ, scilicet idibus Ianuarij, G litera dominicali. Receptus est ab episcopo Basiliensi, præsentibus fratribus Prædicatoribus XLII, fratribus Minoribus XXXVI, saccatis XII. & fratribus beatæ Mariæ virginis VIII, totaq; multitudine ciuitatis, virorum pariter atq; mulierum. Venit etiam rex cum centum militibus & multis aliis, introduxit Stelliferos, cum magna gloria & honore.
units.tr: Rudolf, king of the Romans, came to Basel on Saturday evening, in the octave of Epiphany, that is, on the Ides of January, dominical letter G. He was received by the bishop of Basel, in the presence of 42 Preaching Friars, 36 Friars Minor, 12 Sackcloth friars and 8 Friars of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and by the whole multitude of the city, men and women alike. The king came with a hundred knights and many others, and he brought in the Stelliferi with great glory and honour.

units.la: Zasusenses se mutuò necauerunt. Filiæ quatuor Rudolfi, festo Purificationis, missam audiuerunt in presbytorio fratrum Prædicatorum, & candelas maximas obtulerunt.
units.tr: The men of Zasusa killed one another. The four daughters of Rudolf, on the feast of the Purification, heard Mass in the choir of the Preaching Friars and offered very large candles.

units.la: Hyems calida fuit valde.
units.tr: The winter was very mild.

units.la: Episcopus Constantiensis obiit in quadragesima.
units.tr: The bishop of Constance died in Lent.

units.la: In cœna Domini natus puer prope <bl>Lauffinberg</bl> habens manus & pedes anseris, & caput monstrosum per omnia.
units.tr: At the Lord's Supper a boy was born near Lauffenberg, with the hands and feet of a goose and a head monstrous in every way.

units.la: Dominabus de S. Marco furatæ fuerunt reliquiæ à quodam monacho.
units.tr: Relics were stolen from the ladies of St Mark by a certain monk.

units.la: Decimo calendas Aprilis fuit pascha Iudæorum.
units.tr: On the tenth day before the Kalends of April was the Jewish Passover.

units.la: In claustro Interlacensi exoculatus fuit quidam canonicus, à tribus conuersis.
units.tr: In the cloister of Interlaken a certain canon was blinded by three lay brothers.

units.la: Iuuenis quidam, quòd virginem vi cognouit, viuus sepelitur in Columbaria.
units.tr: A certain young man, because he had forced himself upon a virgin, was buried alive in the Columbaria.

units.la: Anniuersarium domini Nicolai de <bl>Tittinsheim</bl> x v calend. Iunij translata fuerunt ossa eius de claustro <bl>Istein</bl> / ad fratres Prædicatores, & ibidem in cœmiterio Basileæ solenniter tumulata.
units.tr: The anniversary of lord Nicholas of Tittinsheim was kept on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June. His bones were transferred from the cloister of Istein to the Preaching Friars, and there solemnly entombed in the cemetery at Basel.

units.la: Basileam venit equus venalis duorum annorum, qui altitudine viros non paucos superabat. Æstimabatur c c marcis: venditus esset c marcis.
units.tr: A horse for sale, two years old, came to Basel; it stood taller than not a few men. It was valued at 200 marks, and it was sold for 100 marks.

units.la: Ceræ & mellis copia.
units.tr: There was an abundance of wax and honey.

units.la: Sorores in <bl>Clingental</bl> vendiderunt regi Rudolpho, quod dominus de <bl>Clingin</bl> in Werra dederat ad emendum.
units.tr: The nuns of Klingental sold to King Rudolf what the lord of Klingen in Werra had given them to buy.

units.la: Item festo S. Margaretæ comes Ludouicus de <bl>Froburg</bl>/dedit omnia castra sua regi Rudolfo, tali conditione, quòd pro eo restitueret vniuersis.
units.tr: Likewise, on the feast of St Margaret, Count Louis of Froburg gave all his castles to King Rudolf, on condition that he restore them to everyone.

units.la: In octaua S. Laurentij, G litera dominicali, Luna duodecima, translatæ sunt duodecim sorores de <bl>Clingental</bl> & cœperūt ædificare dormitorium cum lapidibus, magnum & pulchrum prope Rhenum Basileæ, & intra x i i i septimanas, hoc est festo Martini tectum eius vidimus consummatum.
units.tr: On the octave of St Lawrence, dominical letter G, moon twelve, twelve nuns of Klingental were transferred and began to build a large and handsome dormitory of stone near the Rhine at Basel. Within thirteen weeks, that is, by the feast of Martin, we saw its roof completed.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus fecit nouam monetam, imprimens numisma regis coronati.
units.tr: King Rudolf made a new coinage, stamping it with the image of the crowned king.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Basiliensis obiit, octaua natiuitatis Mariæ.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Basel, died on the octave of the Nativity of Mary.

units.la: Festo S. Martini cœpit vindemia.
units.tr: On the feast of St Martin the vintage began.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis præcepit aduocato in Rubiaca, vt confiscaret res ecclesiæ Marbacensis, & solueret debita, quòd abbas & canonici in solutione debitorum non poterant concordare.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg ordered the advocate at Rouffach to confiscate the property of the church of Marbach and pay its debts, because the abbot and canons could not agree on the payment of the debts.

units.la: Filia regis Rudolphi, ducissa Bauariæ, peperit filium, circa quartum nonas Octobris.
units.tr: The daughter of King Rudolf, duchess of Bavaria, bore a son, about the fourth day before the Nones of October.

units.la: In episcopatu Basiliensi, in valle Sufinga, quæ est prope Monasterium, reperiuntur capitones sine viscositate: & coniunguntur quatuor episcopatus ibidem.
units.tr: In the diocese of Basel, in the valley of Sufinga, which lies near Monastery, capons are found without fat; and four dioceses are joined there.

units.la: M. CC. LXXV.

Infra octauam natiuitatis Domini, conuenerunt dux de <bl>Teck</bl> / cancellarius regis Rudolfi, archidiaconus Basiliensis, electus episcopus, & plures alij in Basilea, præparantes iter ad pontificem Romanum, Gregorium papam, vt rex in Imperatorem consecretur.
units.tr: Within the octave of the Lord's Nativity, the duke of Teck, the chancellor of King Rudolf, the archdeacon of Basel, the elect bishop and several others met at Basel to prepare the journey to the Roman pontiff, Pope Gregory, so that the king might be consecrated emperor.

units.la: Domus in <bl>Altkilch</bl> cecidit, & decem homines interfecit.
units.tr: A house at Altkirch collapsed and killed ten men.

units.la: Comes Vlricus de Phitreto obiit, vigilia Purificationis.
units.tr: Count Ulrich of Pfirt died on the eve of the Purification.

units.la: Infra dominicam Paschæ venit legatus Basileam.
units.tr: Within the Sunday of Easter a legate came to Basel.

units.la: Penuria frumenti fuit Basileæ. Quartale frumenti decem solidis vendebatur.
units.tr: There was a shortage of grain at Basel. A quarter of grain was sold for ten shillings.

units.la: Prior Prædicatorum Basiliensium, festo crucis inuentæ, crucem ad transmarinas partes prædicauit.
units.tr: On the feast of the Finding of the Cross, the prior of the Preaching Friars of Basel preached the cross for the lands beyond the sea.

units.la: Rudolfus rex in festo pentecostes in <bl>Wirtiburg</bl> curiam celebrauit: regem Bohemiæ secundario citauit.
units.tr: King Rudolf held court at Würzburg at Pentecost and summoned the king of Bohemia a second time.

units.la: Festo Petri & Pauli Rhenus pontem Basiliensem destruxit, submersis plus minus centum hominibus.
units.tr: On the feast of Peter and Paul the Rhine destroyed the bridge at Basel, and about a hundred men were drowned.

units.la: Tertio nonas Augusti, vetus validissimus, qui vineas & arbores deuastauit, ramos adtria milliaria, puerum cum cunabulo in villa <bl>Herckheim</bl> deportauit.
units.tr: On the third day before the Nones of August, a very strong wind, which laid waste vines and trees, carried branches three miles away and carried a boy with his cradle to the village of Herckheim.

units.la: Rudolfus rex Friburgum obsedit, octauo calend. Septembris.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged Freiburg on the eighth day before the Kalends of September.

units.la: Pridie nonas Maij, venit Basileam presbyter Cardinalis de Capua, receptus à rege & episcopo Legato Lombardiæ, à clero & totius ciuitatis populo.
units.tr: On the day before the Nones of May, the cardinal priest of Capua came to Basel. He was received by the king and the bishop, the legate of Lombardy, and by the clergy and people of the whole city.

units.la: Pridie nonas Octobris, Gregorius papa venit Lausannam. Rex Rudolfus venit ad cum festo Lucae, cum regina & penè cū liberis suis vniuersis. Rex accepit crucem & regina, & comes Phitretensis, & comitissa, & penè nobiles qui ad curiam papæ peruenerant vniuersi. Rex plus quàm Dcccc marcas expenderat in vestes pretiosas. Papa regi consuluerat, vt Romam, ad festum Pentecostes, cum duobus millibus militum veniret, vt eum in Imperatorem Romanorum solenniter coronaret.
units.tr: On the day before the Nones of October, Pope Gregory came to Lausanne. King Rudolf came to him at the feast of Luke, with the queen and almost all his children. The king took the cross, and so did the queen, the count of Pfirt, the countess, and nearly all the nobles who had reached the papal court. The king had spent more than 900 marks on costly garments. The pope had advised him to come to Rome at Pentecost with two thousand knights, to be solemnly crowned Emperor of the Romans.

units.la: Papa fratrem Henricum ordinis Minorum in episcopum Basilienlem cōstituit & consecrauit Lausannæ. Eundem legatum Teutoniæ super congreganda decima clericorum constituit, & vt XII millia marcarum regi Rudolfo daret, postquā montana transiret. Cruce signatis Papa dixit, vt post duos menses à festo Purificationis pariter transfretarent.
units.tr: The pope appointed Brother Henry of the Order of Minors bishop of Basel and consecrated him at Lausanne. He appointed the same man legate to Germany, to gather the clergy's tithe and to give 12,000 marks to King Rudolf after the king had crossed the mountains. The pope told those signed with the cross to set out together two months after the feast of the Purification.

units.la: Fratres Minores quendam Abbatem Cisterciensem incarcerauerunt, poenisq; maximis afflixerunt. Cistertienses Capitulo generali contra statuerunt, ne vllus Minorum recipiatur hospitio in claustris vel grangiis suis, nec Missa vel praedicatio eorum audiatur.
units.tr: The Friars Minor imprisoned a certain abbot of the Cistercians and afflicted him with very severe punishments. The Cistercians, at their general chapter, decreed that no Minorite should be received as a guest in their cloisters or granges, and that their Mass or preaching should not be heard.

units.la: Castellum Sulzbach in valle Gregorij, muris & fossato cingitur, festo S. Lucae.
units.tr: The castle of Sulzbach in the valley of Gregory was surrounded with walls and a ditch, on the feast of St Luke.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Basiliensis venit Basileam, festo Dionysij, à papa Gregorio confirmatus, prandium fecit in domo Praedicatorum. Episcopus primam suam Missam celebrauit & synodum.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Basel, came to Basel on the feast of Dionysius, having been confirmed by Pope Gregory. He gave a dinner in the house of the Preaching Friars. The bishop celebrated his first Mass and held a synod.

units.la: Falsarius monetæ coctus in caldario Columbariæ.
units.tr: A counterfeiter of coins was boiled in a cauldron in the Columbaria.

units.la: M. CC. LXXVI.
Cuntzo Textor de Senhen vixit annis CX, obiit M.CC.LXXVII.
units.tr: Cuntzo the weaver of Senheim lived 110 years and died in 1277.

units.la: Dux Lotaringiæ victus à comite Gemini pontis: vtrunque ceciderunt multi & equi & homines.
units.tr: The duke of Lorraine was defeated by the count at the bridge of Gemini; many men and horses fell on both sides.

units.la: Milites regis Rudolphi aduersariorum multos ceperunt, plurimos occiderunt in Lombardia prope Mediolanum. Ex captiuis plures decapitati, ignorătibus stipendiariis: dolentes ob hoc, diutius ibidem manere noluerunt.
units.tr: The soldiers of King Rudolf captured many of the enemy and killed very many in Lombardy near Milan. Many of the captives were beheaded, since the mercenaries were not aware of it; grieving over this, they refused to stay there any longer.

units.la: Fratres sancti Augustini de Mülhusen se transtulerunt ad Basileam.
units.tr: The brothers of St Augustine from Mülhausen moved to Basel.

units.la: Destructa fuit domus S. Augustini in Nüwenburc à populo, rege minime prohibente.
units.tr: The house of St Augustine at Neuenburg was destroyed by the people, the king in no way forbidding it.

units.la: Gregorius papa XII, obiit, infra octauas Epiphaniæ.
units.tr: Pope Gregory XII died within the octave of Epiphany.

units.la: Frater Petrus de Tarantasio, ordinis Praedicatorum, archiepiscopus Lugdunensis, in Papam eligitur, Innocentius dictus.
units.tr: Brother Peter of Tarentaise, of the Order of Preachers, archbishop of Lyons, was elected pope and called Innocent.

units.la: Regina regis Rudolphi filium peperit elegantem in Reinfelden, festo Valentini: hic breue tempus vixit.
units.tr: The queen of King Rudolf bore a handsome son at Rheinfelden on the feast of St Valentine; he lived a short time.

units.la: In Turego lupa domestica peperit duos lupos rufos, duos veltres albos, & tres catulos maculosos generum diuersorum.
units.tr: In Zurich a domestic she-wolf bore two red wolves, two white greyhounds and three spotted puppies of different kinds.

units.la: In Olsperc ordinis Cisterciensis soror extitit, quæ sine potu vndecim annis permansit.
units.tr: In Olsberg there was a sister of the Cistercian Order who remained without drink for eleven years.

units.la: In Sultz prope Rubeacum decoctus fuit monetarius, seruus domini Ioannis de Jungholtz.
units.tr: At Sulz near Rouffach a moneyer, servant of lord John of Jungholz, was boiled.

units.la: In Laufenberck gallus magnus ex Italia, sub cuius ventre gallina transfibat.
units.tr: At Laufenberg there was a large cock from Italy, under whose belly a hen passed through.

units.la: Rex obsedit dominum de Fleckenstein, pro eo quòd ceperat episcopum Spirensem, pro pecunia quam pro adiutorio promiserat. Dominus de Fleckenstein se & sua in regis tradidit potestatem.
units.tr: The king besieged the lord of Fleckenstein, because he had captured the bishop of Speyer over money that he had promised for help. The lord of Fleckenstein surrendered himself and his possessions into the king's power.

units.la: Carolus Rudolfi regis filius, natus festo Valentini, hoc anno. Sepultus in medio chori maioris ecclesiæ Basiliensis: & interfuerunt exequiis eius omnes religiosi & clerici, minores pariterq; maiores, milites vniuersi, & ex ciuibus honestiores multi: mulieres multæ & regina cum pluribus dominabus. Fuit & feretrum coopertum nobili Baldico, quod ecclesiæ reliquerunt.
units.tr: Charles, son of King Rudolf, was born on the feast of St Valentine this year. He was buried in the middle of the choir of the cathedral church of Basel, and all the religious and clergy, lesser and greater alike, took part in his funeral, as did all the knights and many of the more honourable citizens, with many women and the queen with several ladies. The bier was also covered with a noble cloth of gold, which they left to the church.

units.la: Frater Emundus, quondam prouincialis Teutoniæ Praedicatorum, à rege Rudolfo mittitur ad Curiam, ad occulta negotia pertractanda.
units.tr: Brother Edmund, formerly provincial of the Preaching Friars in Germany, was sent to the Curia by King Rudolf to handle secret business.

units.la: Regina fecit adduci in hortum Praedicatorum in Basilea porcum spinosum, vt viderent in eo Dei mirabilem creaturam.
units.tr: The queen had a spiny pig brought into the garden of the Preaching Friars at Basel, so that they might see in it a wonderful creature of God.

units.la: Pridie calendas Iunij, comes Theobaldus de Phitreto fecit curiam magnam, cui interfuit rex & regina, dux Lotaringiæ, & milites multi.
units.tr: On the day before the Kalends of June, Count Theobald of Pfirt held a great court, attended by the king and queen, the duke of Lorraine and many knights.

units.la: VII nonas Iunij prædicauit frater Eberhardus, ordinis Prædicatorum in Basilea, & receperunt ab eo ad partes transmarinas multi crucem Domini gloriosam.
units.tr: On the seventh day before the Nones of June, Brother Eberhard of the Order of Preachers preached at Basel, and many received from him the glorious cross of the Lord for the lands beyond the sea.

units.la: In Notwilre soror inclusa tres pueros vno die peperit, & quarto die quartum puerum prioribus addebat.
units.tr: In Nottweil an enclosed sister bore three boys on one day, and on the fourth day she added a fourth boy to the earlier ones.

units.la: Rex Rudolphus ad Capitulum Prædicatorum Pisis celebratum, misit xxx marcas.
units.tr: King Rudolf sent thirty marks to the chapter of the Preachers held at Pisa.

units.la: Minores Basileæ capitulum celebrabant, & regina x marcas eis pro seruitio ministrauit.
units.tr: The Minorites held a chapter at Basel, and the queen gave them ten marks for their service.

units.la: Quarto nonas Augusti visa sunt de dormitorio Prædicatorum lumina multa, per modum pugnantium discurrentia.
units.tr: On the fourth day before the nones of August, many lights were seen running about from the dormitory of the Preachers, as if men were fighting.

units.la: In festo Dominici præparauit Rudolfus rex expeditionem suam contra regem Bohemorum.
units.tr: On the feast of the Lord's Day, King Rudolf prepared his expedition against the king of the Bohemians.

units.la: Fraga, quæ Hindber vocantur, & botros comedi in assumptione beatæ Virginis, & eodem die fructum & flores plures arbores habuerunt.
units.tr: Strawberries, which are called raspberries, and grapes were eaten at the Assumption of the blessed Virgin, and on the same day several trees had fruit and flowers.

units.la: In castro Reginsperg crystallum vidi, quem leuare poteram cum labore.
units.tr: In the castle of Reginsberg I saw a crystal, which I could lift only with difficulty.

units.la: Adrianus papa moritur: Ioannes papa eligitur.
units.tr: Pope Adrian dies; John is elected pope.

units.la: Nono calendas Octobris, obiit aduocatissa Alsatiæ, filia comitis Phitretarum, in castro Pfireberg/vxor Conradi Wernheri; sepulta in cœmiterio S. Ioannis subtilia in Columbaria.
units.tr: On the ninth day before the kalends of October died the advocatess of Alsace, daughter of the count of Pfirt, in the castle of Pfirt, wife of Conrad Werner; she was buried in the cemetery of St John, in the Columbaria.

units.la: XV calend. Octob. episcopus Basiliensis venit infirmus de curia Romana, & de familia sua nouem perierunt.
units.tr: On the fifteenth day before the kalends of October the bishop of Basel returned sick from the Roman curia, and nine of his household died.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis visitauit canonicos sancti Leonhardi, de regula sancti Augustini, & vnum ex eis causa correctionis misit ad monasterium Interlacense, secundum ad monasterium Parisiense, tertium vero Bellen, quartum misit Argentinam ad sanctum Arbogastum. Præposito vero nomen mutauit, & Priorem nominauit, & ei Procuratorem adiunxit, sine cuius licentia vel scitu de rebus monasterij nihil poterat ordinare.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel visited the canons of St Leonhard, who follow the rule of St Augustine, and for correction sent one of them to the monastery of Interlaken, a second to the monastery of Paris, and a third to Bellelay; the fourth he sent to Strasbourg, to St Arbogast. He changed the name of the provost, named him Prior, and attached a procurator to him, without whose permission or knowledge he could order nothing concerning the property of the monastery.

units.la: In vigilia S. Clementis, infra matutinas Prædicatorum Basilea, fuit eclipsis Lunæ, quam frater iuuenis eiusdem ordinis prædixit, & fratribus ostendit.
units.tr: On the eve of St Clement, during matins at the Preachers in Basel, there was an eclipse of the moon, which a young brother of the same order predicted and showed to the brothers.

units.la: Crastino S. Catharinæ, facta est copositio inter regē Bohemiæ & regem Rom.
units.tr: On the day after St Catherine, an agreement was made between the king of Bohemia and the king of the Romans.

units.la: In Rinfelden Rhenus opertus extitit glacie, & via patuit cuilibet transeunti. Frigus solutum fuit festo Hilarij.
units.tr: At Rheinfelden the Rhine was covered with ice, and the way lay open to anyone crossing. The frost broke on the feast of Hilary.

units.la: Natiuitas Domini feria sexta fuit. Episcopus Basiliensis cum familia carnes comedit: qui carnes comedere nolebant, habebant pisces magnos.
units.tr: The Lord's Nativity fell on a Friday. The bishop of Basel ate meat with his household; those who were unwilling to eat meat had large fish. ## 1277

units.la: M. CC. LXXVII.
Regina Teutoniæ tempore Quadragesimæ pluribus diebus cum sex tantum dominabus in claustro Clingintal morabatur.
units.tr: For several days during Lent the queen of Germany stayed in the cloister of Klingental with only six ladies.

units.la: Prope Basileā foditur argentū, & ferrum, & plumbū, & aurū inuenitur in aquis.
units.tr: Near Basel silver, iron and lead are dug, and gold is found in the waters.

units.la: In montibus vallis Werræ frequentauerunt ecclesias in circulis, propter niues, die annunciationis Mariæ.
units.tr: In the mountain valleys of the Werra, because of the snows, people attended the churches in groups on the day of the Annunciation of Mary.

units.la: Post Pascha regina de Rinfelden proficiscens venit Constantiā, inde Bauariam. Sequebatur autem ipsam Henricus episcopus Basil. circa ascensionem Dñi cū equis lxx.
units.tr: After Easter the queen set out from Rheinfelden and came to Constance, and then to Bavaria. Henry, bishop of Basel, accompanied her around the Ascension of the Lord with seventy horses.

units.la: In Gowenstein cornua duo cerui longitudine trium pedum, ex quibus xvi cornua processerunt.
units.tr: In Gowenstein two stag's horns, three feet long, were found, from which sixteen horns sprouted.

units.la: In Vrania nigromanticus quidam cum quibusdam rusticis voluit artem suam exercere pro pecunia. Interim grando vallem maximis lapidibus impetebat. Vnde armata manu montes ascenderunt, & ipsum cum discipulis suis ter violenter de propriis finibus eiecerunt.
units.tr: In Urania a certain necromancer, with some peasants, wanted to practise his art for money. Meanwhile hail battered the valley with huge stones. Whereupon they climbed the mountains with armed hands and three times violently drove him and his disciples out of their own borders.

units.la: Comes Eberhardus ciuitatem Friburg in Dechland dedit regi Rudolfo pro tribus millibus marcis: pro qua comes Sabaudiæ ix millia dedisset, si Rudolfus rex vendere sibi promisisset.
units.tr: Count Eberhard gave the city of Freiburg in Breisgau to King Rudolf for three thousand marks; for it the count of Savoy would have paid nine thousand, had Rudolf promised to sell it to him.

units.la: In villa Cella puella octauo anno ætatis suæ puerum peperit.
units.tr: In the village of Zelle a girl in the eighth year of her age bore a boy.

units.la: In Nollinwilre/castro prope Sulz/inuenta est caluaria serpentis magni, & lingua eius vulgo Naterzunge: datur regi Rudolfo pro clenodio: cuius vis toxicum prodere. Regina Teutoniæ in Vienna recipitur.
units.tr: In Nollingen, a castle near Sulz, the skull of a great serpent was found, and its tongue, commonly called the "adder's tongue", was given to King Rudolf as a jewel; its power is said to reveal poison. The queen of Germany was received at Vienna.

units.la: In Austria rex Rudolfus nouâ exactionem adinuenit, & à quolibet aratro quinque solidos postulauit.
units.tr: In Austria King Rudolf devised a new tax and demanded five shillings from every plough.

units.la: Comitem de <bl>Hohinberck</bl> cognatum regis dominus <bl>Haginecke</bl> in regis præsentia vulneravit.
units.tr: Lord Haginecke wounded the count of Hohenberg, the king's kinsman, in the king's presence.

units.la: Noua retia inuenta prope Constantiam, per quæ pisces plurimi capiebantur.
units.tr: New nets were invented near Constance, by which very many fish were caught.

units.la: Episcopus Metensis & Argentinensis ducem Lotaringiæ impugnant. Dux duodecim currus episcopo Argentinensi abstulit: postea res composita est.
units.tr: The bishops of Metz and Strasbourg attacked the duke of Lorraine. The duke took twelve wagons from the bishop of Strasbourg; afterwards the matter was settled.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis de ciuibus in Sultz lxxx marcas accipiebat, qui antecessoribus suis cum murmure vix lx marcas soluebant.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg received eighty marks from the citizens of Sulz, who had grumbled and scarcely paid sixty marks to his predecessors.

units.la: Eps Coloniensis cũ duodecim aliis coniurantes, impugnarunt comitem de Bülsch.
units.tr: The archbishop of Cologne, conspiring with twelve others, attacked the count of Jülich.

units.la: Annus in omnibus abundās, excepto lino. Quartale hordei tribus solidis: aucnæ, octodecim denariis: siligo, quatuor solidis: Triticum, sex solidis.
units.tr: The year abounded in everything except flax. A quarter of barley cost three shillings; oats eighteen pence; rye four shillings; wheat six shillings.

units.la: Canonici S. Petri Basil. aream, quæ sita est ex opposito monasterij S. Petri, plantationibus arborum repleuerunt.
units.tr: The canons of St Peter in Basel filled the area opposite the monastery of St Peter with plantings of trees.

units.la: In Sultz quædam meretrices domesticæ à meretricibus syluestribus baculis ex Albertus Magnus lector Coloniæ. (pulsæ.)
units.tr: In Sulz some domestic prostitutes were beaten with staves by wild prostitutes. Albertus Magnus, lecturer at Cologne.

units.la: Clericus vagus Basileæ serpentes capiebat, ad libitum eis vtrebatur, & mirabilia faciebat.
units.tr: A wandering clerk at Basel caught snakes, handled them at will, and performed wonders.

units.la: In Schlettstat Henricus procurator Hospitale pauperum inchoauit.
units.tr: In Schlettstadt Henry, the procurator, began a hospital for the poor.

units.la: Ioannes papa Magus, in omnibus disciplinis instructus, religiosis infestus, contemnens decreta Concilij generalis, obiit hoc anno.
units.tr: Pope John, a magician, instructed in all the arts, hostile to religious, scorning the decrees of the general council, died this year.

units.la: Nicolaus papa electus est, dictus Caietanus, diu discordantibus Cardinalibus.
units.tr: Nicholas, called Caetani, was elected pope after the cardinals had disagreed for a long time. ## 1278

units.la: M. CC. LXXVIII.
Episcopus Basiliensis & aduocatus Alsatiæ cum exercitu ad regem Rudolfum in Austriam perrexerunt, in mense Iulio.
units.tr: In July the bishop of Basel and the advocate of Alsace set out with an army to King Rudolf in Austria.

units.la: XVI calend. Aprilis, interfectus est comes de Bülich, in ciuitate quæ dicitur Aquisgranum, cum duobus filiis, & ccc militibus, & cum alia familia sua multa.
units.tr: On the sixteenth day before the kalends of April the count of Jülich was killed in the city called Aachen, with two of his sons, three hundred knights, and many others of his household.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ promisit, se pecuniam magnam Teutoniæ principibus daturum, vt pro se contra regem Rudolfum pro viribus pugnarent.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia promised that he would give a great sum of money to the princes of Germany, so that they would fight with all their strength for him against King Rudolf.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ x millia militum congregauit, vt regem Rudolfum de Austriæ finibus extirparet. Sed Domino dante principes exercitus incœperunt fortiter discordare, & sic fuit eorum congregatio dissipata.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia gathered ten thousand soldiers to root King Rudolf out of the borders of Austria. But, by the Lord's will, the princes of the army began to quarrel fiercely, and so their gathering was broken up.

units.la: Dominus papa excommunicauit omnes aduersarios regis Rudolfi, & ipsum Imperatorem publicè nominauit.
units.tr: The lord pope excommunicated all the adversaries of King Rudolf and publicly named him Emperor.

units.la: Sorores de sancto Ioanne, ordinis Prædicatorum muro se cinxerunt, cuius altitudo pedes xx noscitur habuisse: & quercus ex qua sedes ecclesiæ parabantur dominarum, in circumferentia pedes xxiiii comprehendit.
units.tr: The sisters of St John of the Order of Preachers surrounded themselves with a wall, whose height is known to have been twenty feet; and the oak from which the seats of the ladies of the church were made measured twenty-four feet in circumference.

units.la: Ciues ciuitatis quæ dicitur Aquisgranum, castrum quoddam cum hominibus ceperunt, ex quibus xv gladiis occiderunt, reliquos verò carceri deputârunt.
units.tr: The citizens of the city called Aachen captured a certain castle with its men; of these they killed fifteen with the sword and assigned the rest to prison.

units.la: Domini de Horburc, filij sororis comitis Phitretarum, cognato suo reconciliantur, & in Alsatiam reuertuntur.
units.tr: The lords of Horburg, sons of the sister of the count of Pfirt, were reconciled with their cousin and returned to Alsace.

units.la: Obiit comes de Werde.
units.tr: The count of Werdenberg died.

units.la: Rusticus quidam de Billingen candens ferrum portauit nuda manu, sine corporis læsione.
units.tr: A certain peasant of Billigen carried red-hot iron in his bare hand, without any injury to his body.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ pugnauit cum rege Romanorum prope Viennam & interfectus est, ipse & cum eo xiiii millia hominum, vt communiter dicebatur.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia fought with the king of the Romans near Vienna and was killed, he and with him fourteen thousand men, as was commonly said.

units.la: Interfectus est dominus de Echerich, & dominus de Apiaco.
units.tr: The lord of Echerich and the lord of Apiaco were killed.

units.la: Obiit archiepiscopus Cantuariensis, cardinalis, ordinis Prædicatorum.
units.tr: The archbishop of Canterbury, a cardinal of the Order of Preachers, died.

units.la: Obiit frater Probus; prouincialis de ordine Minorum.
units.tr: Brother Probus, provincial of the Order of Minors, died.

units.la: Dominus papa factus est perpetuus senator Romanus: & Carolus cessit ei, & reliquit ei omnia quæ habuerat & spectabant ad Sedem.
units.tr: The lord pope was made perpetual senator of Rome; Charles yielded to him and left him everything he had possessed that pertained to the See.

units.la: Dominus de Gliers vallem Sergowe depræda tur, & tres nobiles interfecit.
units.tr: The lord of Gliers plundered the valley of Sergowe and killed three nobles.

units.la: Festo Simonis & Iudæ intrauit conuentus fratrum ordinis Prædicatorum in Columbariam, in domum suam. Receptus fuit à Canonicis, à dominis S. Ioan. Baptistæ, & ab vniuersitate ciuitatis laudabiliter & honestè.
units.tr: On the feast of Simon and Jude the convent of brothers of the Order of Preachers moved into Columbaria, into its own house. It was received by the canons, by the lords of St John the Baptist, and by the university of the city, praiseworthily and honourably.

units.la: Destructum fuit Zeringen nouiter ædificatum, & turris prope Brisacum, & Coliberc.
units.tr: Zeringen, newly built, was destroyed, and a tower near Breisach, and Coliberc.

units.la: Mures fuerunt multæ & annus in omnibus abundans.
units.tr: There were many mice, and the year abounded in everything.

units.la: Comes Egino de Friburc, ciuibus de Offenburc equos viginti prope portam ciuitatis abstulit. Ciues autem persequentes congressi sunt cum eo, & ex vtraque parte plures vulnera acceperunt.
units.tr: Count Egino of Freiburg took twenty horses from the citizens of Offenburg near the city gate. The citizens pursued him and engaged with him, and on both sides many received wounds.

units.la: Comes Phitretarum cepit abbatem de Luxouio.
units.tr: The count of Pfirt captured the abbot of Luxeuil.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis fossato diuisit nouum castrum ab antiquo, in villa Rubeacensi.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg separated the new castle from the old by a ditch, in the village of Rouffach.

units.la: Hyems calida fuit.
units.tr: The winter was warm.

units.la: In Carinthia tanta fames extitit, vt homines carnes humanas comederent, & fame plurimi perirent.
units.tr: In Carinthia there was such a famine that men ate human flesh, and very many died of hunger.

units.la: M. CC. LXXIX.
Hoc anno dominus Sigfridus, dictus de Gundoltzheim venit de domino Rudolfo rege, qui tunc temporis extitit in Vienna, retulitq; de eo prospera cum fortuna.
