units.tr: In this year Lord Sigfrid, called of Gundoltzheim, came back from King Rudolf, who at that time was in Vienna, and brought favourable news of him.

units.la: Scultetus hic Sigfridus ædificauit castrum in Hohenac, in crastino Purificationis, rege Rudolfo permittente. Et tertia die fracta est Columbariensium melior campanarum.
units.tr: This Sigfrid, the bailiff (scultetus), built a castle at Hohenac on the day after the Purification, with King Rudolf's permission. And on the third day the better of the bells of Colmar was broken.

units.la: Eodem tempore papalis litera venit in Columbariā, in qua continebatur, quòd deberet perfidis Iudæis, Prior prouincialis Teutoniç cum fratribus suis, fidem Catholicam fideliter prædicare.
units.tr: At the same time a papal letter came to Colmar, stating that the Provincial Prior of Germany, together with his brothers, should faithfully preach the Catholic faith to the faithless Jews.

units.la: Post Mathiæ venit aduocatus Alsatiæ, Conradus Wernherus à rege, qui tunc temporis morabatur in Vienna.
units.tr: After the feast of St Matthias, Conrad Wernher, advocate of Alsace, came from the king, who was then staying in Vienna.

units.la: Eodem tempore dabatur in Columbaria siligo pro xvii denariis, hordeū pro xviii denariis, auena pro xix den. frumentum pro xxx denariis.
units.tr: At the same time at Colmar rye was sold for seventeen pennies, barley for eighteen pennies, oats for nineteen pennies, and wheat for thirty pennies.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltzstein castrum Hohenac & Minnewiler cognatis suis abstulit fraudulenter, & in Columbariam transferebat.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein fraudulently took Hohenac and Minnewiler from his kinsmen and transferred them to Colmar.

units.la: Magister Rudigerus de Consheim, præpositus Columbariensis, vir diuitiis & scientia clarus, obiit, circa festum Gregorij papæ.
units.tr: Master Rüdiger of Konsheim, provost of Colmar, a man distinguished by wealth and learning, died about the feast of Pope Gregory.

units.la: XVIII cal. Maij vineæ & nuces perierunt frigore.
units.tr: On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May, vines and walnut trees perished from the frost.

units.la: Longitudo hæc sumpta lx vicibus, facit spissitudinem arboris, quæ est in Sigoltzheim supra fontem, prope curiam & capellam S. Mauritij.
units.tr: This length, taken sixty times, gives the thickness of the tree at Sigoltzheim above the spring, near the court and chapel of St Maurice.

units.la: Lantfridus de Landisperc suffocatus fuit in tormento Argentinæ, in anniuersario patris sui, qui fuit in præcedenti tricesimo anno in eadem ciuitate, & in eodem die hastiludio interfectus à comite Friburgensi.
units.tr: Lantfrid of Landsberg was suffocated in the torture chamber at Strasbourg, on the anniversary of his father, who had been executed in the same city thirty years earlier; and on the same day he was killed in a tournament by the Count of Freiburg.

units.la: Filius regis Rudolfi maior venit in Ensisheim, xiiii calend. Iunij, conuocauitque scultetos ciuitatis, & deliberauit cum eis, quomodo patri suo milites mitterent in armis præparatos.
units.tr: The elder son of King Rudolf came to Ensisheim on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June, summoned the bailiffs of the city, and consulted with them how they should send armed soldiers to his father.

units.la: Conradus de Liechtenberc episcopus Argentinensis castellū Türlac per ignem destruxit, & quæ in eo reperit, deportauit.
units.tr: Conrad of Lichtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg, destroyed the castle of Türlac by fire, and carried off whatever he found in it.

units.la: Dominus de gemino ponte castellum proprium, nomine Copinheim, per ignem deuastauit. Abbatissa de S. Cruce obiit, octauo idus Iunij.
units.tr: The lord of Zweibrücken laid waste by fire his own castle called Copinheim. The abbess of Holy Cross died on the eighth day before the Ides of June.

units.la: Crastino Barnabæ apostoli cecidit grādo cum magnis lapidibus, quorum multi habebāt magnitudinem ouorum: destruxit quasdam domos latericias, & damnum diuersis locis Alsatiæ dedit.
units.tr: On the day after the feast of the apostle St Barnabas, hail fell with large stones, many of them the size of eggs. It destroyed some houses of brick and caused damage in various places in Alsace.

units.la: Per ignem Iudæorum consumitur synagoga.
units.tr: The synagogue is destroyed by fire at the hands of the Jews.

units.la: Filius Rudolfi regis Turicensium est pecora depraedatus.
units.tr: The son of King Rudolf plundered the cattle of the Zurichers.

units.la: Episcopus Basil. venit à rege ex Austria Basileam, & celebrauit curiā magnam.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel came from the king in Austria to Basel and held a great court.

units.la: Interficitur abbas Heremitarum fulmine, & cum eo plures monachi grauissimè puniuntur.
units.tr: An abbot of the Hermits is killed by lightning, and several monks are severely punished along with him.

units.la: Eiiciuntur de Columbaria, qui dicebantur Scultetum interficere voluisse: vnus ex iis postea fuit rotatus. In Ongersheim fuit mulier tabernaria, de qua Physicus eiecit infra decennium tres cattas. Cœmiterium inchoatur in Wintzenheim.
units.tr: Those who were said to have wanted to kill the bailiff were expelled from Colmar; one of them was afterwards broken on the wheel. In Ongersheim there was a female tavern-keeper, from whom a physician cast out three cats within ten years. A cemetery is begun in Wintzenheim.

units.la: Interfectus fuit sculletus, de Aquisgrano in ecclesia cum quodam perfido, a procuratore regis Rudolfi: pro eo quòd dominum de Gülsch comitem cum suis sociis miseriliter occidisset.
units.tr: The bailiff was killed in the church at Aachen, together with a certain treacherous man, by the king's procurator Rudolf, because he had wretchedly killed Count Lord of Gülsch and his companions.

units.la: Dux Brabantiæ cum exercitu magno de voluntate regis Rudolfi venit ad terram inferiorem, ibiq; dicebatur castra plurima destruxisse.
units.tr: The Duke of Brabant, with a great army and by the will of King Rudolf, came to the Lower Country, and there he was said to have destroyed many castles.

units.la: Infra octauam Assumptionis, congregauit filius regis Rudolfi plus q; xx comites & dominos multos, & exercitu magnum, vt destrueret suburbium Friburgense, pro eo quòd iuuissent dominum suum comitem Gebirhardum de Friburgo, qui eo tempore ciuitates imperij pro suis viribus impugnabat.10
units.tr: Within the octave of the Assumption, the son of King Rudolf gathered more than twenty counts, many lords and a great army to destroy the suburb of Freiburg, because its people had aided their lord, Count Gebhard of Freiburg, who at that time was attacking the imperial cities with all his strength.

units.la: Domini de Girsperch in vigilia S. Matthei Türinchen ceperunt, & oppidum Wilre per ignem penitus destruxerunt.
units.tr: On the eve of St Matthew the lords of Girsberg took Türinchen and utterly destroyed the town of Wilre by fire.

units.la: Frigore hoc anno perierê fructus. Vindemia fuit quasi nulla: vix enim decimam partem vini quam confuerunt, protulerunt.
units.tr: This year the fruits perished from the frost. There was almost no vintage, for they yielded scarcely a tenth part of the wine they were accustomed to.

units.la: Indultum est in ecclesia fratribus Minoribus in serico ministrare.
units.tr: It was granted in the church that the Friars Minor might minister in silk.

units.la: Eps Basil. sorores de S. Clara, vel ordinis fratrum Minorum, transtulit trans Rhenum in clausträ Saccitarum. De Saccitis aut quinq; recepit in ordine Minorum: prouinciale vero eorū fecit præpositū apud canonicos S. Leonhardi: reliquis aut saccitis prout po-
units.tr: The bishop of Basel transferred the sisters of St Clare, or of the order of the Friars Minor, across the Rhine to the cloister of the Sack-brothers (Saccitae). Of the Saccitae he received five into the order of the Minors, and made their provincial provost among the canons of St Leonhard; for the rest of the Saccitae he made what provision he could.

units.la: Eps Basil. in ecclesia fratrü Prædic. Basileæ clericos consecrauit. (tuit, prouidebat.20
units.tr: The bishop of Basel ordained clerics in the church of the Preaching friars at Basel.

units.la: Episcopus Colonien. vicit in prælio dñm de Spanheim & cepit quatuor comites.
units.tr: The bishop of Cologne defeated the lord of Spanheim in battle and captured four counts.

units.la: In ciuitatem Bernensem Burgundiæ aues ciconiæ nouiter venerunt.
units.tr: Storks newly arrived in the city of Bern in Burgundy.

units.la: In Nidira münster claustro nigrarum monialiū, furtim sublata fuit corona crucifivi, cum reliquiis multis. Fur in breui comprehenditur ac supplicio condemnatur.
units.tr: In the cloister of the Black nuns at Nidermünster, the crown of a crucifix was secretly stolen, together with many relics. The thief was soon apprehended and condemned to execution.

units.la: Obiit frater Otto, dictus de inferno, frater ordinis Prædicatorū, vir deuotus, Deo ac hominibus dilectus: cui Dominus conflictum regis Bohemiæ & regis Teutoniæ in spiritu ostendit, & regem Bohemiæ grauissimè vulneratum.
units.tr: Brother Otto, called "of hell," a friar of the Order of Preachers, a devout man beloved of God and men, died. The Lord had shown him in spirit the battle between the king of Bohemia and the king of Germany, and the king of Bohemia gravely wounded.

units.la: In Zabernia plures quàm lxiiii homines, muro super eos cadente, perierunt.
units.tr: In Zabern more than sixty-four people perished when a wall fell upon them.

units.la: Domina de Rapoltstein / dicta de Froburch / in Paradis efficitur monialis, prope Schafusiam.30
units.tr: The lady of Rappoltstein, called of Froburg, became a nun at Paradies near Schaffhausen.

units.la: Opposuerunt se domino Basiliensi, dominus præpositus Maguntinus, dominus de Rötilheim / cum militum multitudine copiosa.
units.tr: The provost of Mainz and the lord of Rötteln, with a large multitude of soldiers, opposed the lord of Basel.

units.la: In Rubiaca soror quædam fuit accusata, quòd imaginē cereā baptizasset. Cùm id ipsa negasset, ipsam ad campum duxerunt rustici, & ipsam ignibus cremassent, si fratres eam non ex eorum manibus liberassent.
units.tr: At Rubiaca a certain sister was accused of having baptized a wax image. When she denied it, country folk led her out to the field and would have burned her with fire, had the brothers not freed her from their hands.

units.la: M. CC. LXXX.
Interfectus fuit sculletus Iohannes de Keiserspferch.
units.tr: John Sculletus of Keiserspferch was killed.

units.la: Captus est dominus de Girspferch / plebanus de Lagilnheim. Item captus est de Nortgassen / plebanus de Ostein.
units.tr: The lord of Girspferch was taken, and the parish priest of Lagilnheim. Likewise the parish priest of Ostein was taken from Nortgassen.

units.la: xvi calend. Aprilis, litera dominicali F, dominica, nocte quæ est ante feriam secundam, passa est Luna eclipsin.40
units.tr: On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, with the dominical letter F, on a Sunday, on the night before Monday, the moon suffered an eclipse.

units.la: Domini de Nortgassen ceperunt dominum de Hunnewilre.
units.tr: The lords of Nortgassen seized the lord of Hunnewilre.

units.la: Columbarienses ceperunt clericum domini de Girspferch / & clericum domini de Nortgassen / & quatuor de Sulzmatin.
units.tr: The men of Colmar seized the clerk of the lord of Girspferch, the clerk of the lord of Nortgassen, and four men of Sulzmatt.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis venit Columbariam, petiuitq; à ciuibus, vt clericum suum domini de Nortgassen / suæ redderent libertati. Ciues autem suis precibus acquiescere noluerunt. Interdicta igitur sunt diuina Columbariensibus, propter captiuitatē clericorum.
units.tr: The Bishop of Basel came to Colmar and asked the citizens to restore their clerk of the lord of Nortgassen to his freedom. But the citizens refused to yield to his entreaties. Therefore divine services were forbidden to the people of Colmar because of the imprisonment of the clerks.

units.la: Nonis Aprilis fuit episcopus Argentinensis in Rubiaca cum c phaleratis equis, & ciuitates imperij cum eo, vt expugnaret dominum de Lobigasse, propter captiuos Argentinenses. Qui timore coactus se captiuum tradidit, & reddidit captiuatos.50
units.tr: On the Nones of April the Bishop of Strasbourg came to Rheinau with a hundred decorated horses, and the cities of the empire with him, to storm the lord of Lobigasse on account of the captive Strasbourgers. Forced by fear, he surrendered himself as a prisoner and returned the men he had taken.

units.la: XII calend. Maij, consecrauit dominus Henricus episcopus Basiliensis ordinis fratrum Minorum, chrisma in Peris apud Cistercienses & clericos regulares.
units.tr: On the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, Lord Henry, Bishop of Basel, of the order of the Friars Minor, consecrated chrism at Pairis, among the Cistercians and the regular clerks.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltstein prædam magnā de episcopatu, de pecoribus & iumentis accepit, & plures homines interfecit.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein took a great booty from the bishopric, of cattle and beasts of burden, and killed many men.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltstein diffidauit Columbarienses, & burgenses eorum exterio res quos poterat captiuauit. Henricus episcopus Basiliensis emit propugnaculum, quod est situm prope Rubiacum.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein renounced his allegiance to the men of Colmar and seized whatever of their burgesses' property he could. Henry, Bishop of Basel, bought a fortress that lies near Rheinau.

units.la: Indulta sunt Columbarienſibus diuina, & inceperunt octauo calendas Augusti celebrare.
units.tr: Divine services were restored to the people of Colmar, and they began to celebrate them on the eighth day before the Kalends of August.

units.la: Dominus Basiliensis iuit in Austriam ad regem cum multis militibus.
units.tr: The lord of Basel went to Austria to the king with many soldiers.

units.la: Cessauit concursus in Lebertal ad sanctum Egidium, & factus est in Argetinam: eo quod(vt dicebatur)B. Virgo miracula plurima perpetrasset.
units.tr: The crowds at Lebertal, at the church of St Giles, ceased, and the pilgrimage was moved to Strasbourg, because (as was said) the Blessed Virgin had worked many miracles there.

units.la: Fratribus Praedicatoribus in Columbaria tria altaria sunt consecrata. Fratres iidem apud Turicenses prouinciale Capitulum tenuerunt.
units.tr: Three altars were consecrated for the Friars Preachers in Colmar. The same friars held their provincial chapter among the people of Zurich.

units.la: Fratres Minores laborauerunt vt canonissae de Seconis mutarentur in sorores S.Clarae: sed obtinere minime potuerunt.
units.tr: The Friars Minor laboured to have the canonesses of Seltz changed into Sisters of St Clare, but they could by no means obtain it.

units.la: VII calendas Nouembris fuit terraemotus.
units.tr: On the seventh day before the Kalends of November there was an earthquake.

units.la: Frater Albertus, ordinis Praedicatorum lector generalis, quondam episcopus Ratisponensis, philosophus, obiit.
units.tr: Brother Albert, of the order of Preachers, general lector, formerly Bishop of Regensburg, a philosopher, died.

units.la: Comes Theobaldus Phittetensis cepit filium fratris sui.
units.tr: Count Theobald of Pfirt seized his brother's son.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXI.
Soror Helwigis, priorissa sororum in Columbaria de sancto Ioanne, obiit, v i idus Februarij.
units.tr: Sister Helwig, prioress of the sisters of St John at Colmar, died on the sixth day before the Ides of February.

units.la: Dominus de Ochsenstein, filius sororis Rudolphi regis, aduocatus terrae, depositus Sculteum Columbariensem Sigfridum, cum multorum laetitia quos creditur, perturbasse.
units.tr: The lord of Ochsenstein, son of King Rudolf's sister, the land's advocate, deposed Sigfrid, the sheriff of Colmar; it is believed that this caused much joy to many people and disturbed them.

units.la: Aqua transiens castellum Sultze, magnum damnum ibidem fecit. In Gebwiler magna pars montis propter aquam cecidit. Et torrentes per Alsatiae montana in vineis & agris magnum damnum intulerunt.
units.tr: A flood passing by the castle of Sulz did great damage there. At Gebweiler a large part of a mountain fell because of the water. And torrents through the Alsatian mountains did great damage to vineyards and fields.

units.la: XII Kal. Martij, frater Reinherus ordinis Praedicatorum, octogesimo anno aetatis & quinquagesimo septimo anno, quibus in ordine laudabiliter vixerat, & quadragesimo tertio quibus sororibus de S. Ioanne praefuerat, & eas verbo & exemplo docuerat, in Domino requieuit.
units.tr: On the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, Brother Reinher of the order of Preachers rested in the Lord, in the eightieth year of his age and the fifty-seventh of his life in the order, in which he had lived praiseworthily, and the forty-third in which he had presided over the sisters of St John, teaching them by word and example.

units.la: Guntrannus de Girsperc capitur fraudulenter.
units.tr: Guntram of Girsperg was taken by fraud.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis congregata militum multitudine, domino de Badin quoddam oppidum noscitur obsedisse. Episcopus vero Basil. sibi quinquaginta milites in auxilium transmittebat. Plures autem ex eis a Marggrauio capiuntur, propter quod pax eorum pristina reformatur.
units.tr: The Bishop of Strasbourg, having gathered a great multitude of soldiers, is known to have besieged a certain town belonging to the lord of Baden. The Bishop of Basel sent fifty soldiers to them as help. Many of these, however, were captured by the margrave, on account of which their former peace was restored.

units.la: Regina Rudolfi regis in Nenna moritur, & aliquot centum equis Basileam ducitur, ibiq; a tribus episcopis, & ducentis mille clericis, & multitudine ciuitatis hominum, in vigilia S. Benedicti, cum gloria maxima sepelitur.
units.tr: Queen Rudolf's wife died at Nenning and was brought to Basel with some hundreds of horsemen, and there, on the vigil of St Benedict, she was buried with great pomp, by three bishops, two hundred clerks, and a great multitude of the city's people.

units.la: Filia regis Rudolfi Lombardiam mittitur, a ciuitatibus multis muneribus recipitur, ac filio regis Caroli matrimonio copulatur.
units.tr: The daughter of King Rudolf was sent to Lombardy, was received with many gifts by the cities, and was joined in marriage to the son of King Charles.

units.la: Rex Vngariae Christianam vxorem repudiauit, Cumanam duxit, Christianis odiosus efficitur, a suis capitur, sed postea liberatur.
units.tr: The King of Hungary repudiated his Christian wife and took a Cuman woman; he became hateful to the Christians, was seized by his own people, but was afterwards freed.

units.la: Dominus Simon Francigena, legatus Franciae, presbyter Cardinalis, eligitur in Papam, Martinusq; nominatur.
units.tr: Lord Simon the Frenchman, legate of France, cardinal priest, was elected pope and named Martin.

units.la: Nix in vigilia Purificationis magnae profunditatis cecidit, quę homines, animalia syluestria perturbauit, & vsq; ad festum S. Gregorij perdurauit.
units.tr: On the vigil of the great Purification snow of great depth fell, which disturbed men and wild animals, and lasted until the feast of St Gregory.

units.la: Dominus de Meienhen castrum suum quod habuit Meienhen dedit in Argentinensis episcopi potestatem, & postea recepit illud feudum perpetuum, & episcopus fecit eum Sculteum villae memoratae.
units.tr: The lord of Mayenheim gave his castle, which he had at Mayenheim, into the power of the Bishop of Strasbourg; afterwards he received back that fief in perpetuity, and the bishop made him sheriff of the aforesaid village.

units.la: Antiquae mulieres obierunt, scilicet comitissa de Richenberc, domina de Rapoltzstein, & aliae plures.
units.tr: Several elderly women died, namely the countess of Richenberg, the lady of Rappoltstein, and several others.

units.la: Confluentini domino suo episcopo Treuirensi noluerunt obedire, insuper eum occidere voluerunt.
units.tr: The people of Coblenz refused to obey their lord, the Bishop of Trier, and moreover wished to kill him.

units.la: Ciues de Prumino praepositum suum gladiis occiderunt. Regiq; Franciae nequiter opposuerunt, propter quod ex eis DLX creditur occidisse.
units.tr: The citizens of Prüm killed their provost with swords, and wickedly opposed the king of France, on account of which it is believed that five hundred and sixty of them were killed.

units.la: Grandomagna cecidit circa Kentzingen, xv Kal. Iunij, fecitque damnum magnum, ouesq; centum vel amplius interfecit. Dominî de Byrspberg castrum ædificârunt in monte, qui dicitur ....... sed homines episcopi Argentinensis subitò destruxerunt.
units.tr: A great hailstorm fell near Kenzingen on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June, did great damage, and killed a hundred or more sheep. The lords of Bürgsberg built a castle on a mountain called ....... but the men of the Bishop of Strasbourg suddenly destroyed it.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis congregata hominum multitudine dominos de Napolstein si potuisset, libentissimè perturbasset.
units.tr: The Bishop of Strasbourg, having gathered a multitude of men, would most gladly have disturbed the lords of Rappoltstein if he could have.

units.la: Quarto Kal. Augusti, Wernherus dictus Walch miles, & Cunradus miles dictus de Mortgassen, sunt à Columbariensibus interfecti.
units.tr: On the fourth day before the Kalends of August, Werner, called Walch, a knight, and Conrad, a knight called of Mortgassen, were killed by the men of Colmar.

units.la: Patriarcham Mediolanenses interfecerunt, & cum eo quingentos viros.
units.tr: The Milanese killed the patriarch, and with him five hundred men.

units.la: Hospitalarij S. Joannis conflictum habebant magnum cum Saracenis in transmarinis partibus, & pauci ex eis, multos Sarracenorum ceperunt, & plurimos occiderunt.
units.tr: The Hospitallers of St John had a great battle with the Saracens in the lands beyond the sea; a few of them captured many Saracens and killed very many.

units.la: Multi ignobiles facti milites in Argentina.
units.tr: Many people of low birth were made knights in Strasbourg.

units.la: Sorores poenitentes de claustro suo se mutuò turpiter eiecerunt.
units.tr: The penitent sisters shamefully cast one another out of their cloister.

units.la: Inclusa de Tübilsheim se transtulit in Cazintal.
units.tr: The anchoress of Tübelsheim moved to Kaysersberg valley.

units.la: Mediolanenses de ciuibus, quos eiecerant, quingentos vel amplius occiderunt.
units.tr: The Milanese killed five hundred or more of the citizens whom they had cast out.

units.la: Nonis Octobris, secunda feria, obsedit rex Rudolfus comitem & ciuitatem Friburgensem, cum tribus exercitibus, hominum multitudine copiosa.
units.tr: On the Nones of October, on the second day of the week, King Rudolf besieged the count and the city of Freiburg with three armies and a copious multitude of men.

units.la: Mindæ fuit fratrum Prædicatorum Capitulum celebratum.
units.tr: The chapter of the Friars Preachers was held at Minden.

units.la: Exercitus regis Rudolfi destruxit claustrum dominarum de Adelnhusen, propter quod dedit eis Rex trecentas viginti marcas.
units.tr: The army of King Rudolf destroyed the cloister of the ladies of Adelhausen, on account of which the king gave them three hundred and twenty marks.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus expendit in Columbaria in victualibus infra quindecim dies, mille ducentas marcas.
units.tr: King Rudolf spent, within fifteen days at Colmar, one thousand two hundred marks on provisions.

units.la: Hermaphroditus exoculatur in Brisaco, quòd violenter voluit cognoscere mulierem.
units.tr: A hermaphrodite was blinded in Breisach, because he had violently wished to have intercourse with a woman.

units.la: Comes Sabaudiæ regem Rudolfum hostiliter impugnauit. Comes autem de N. comitem Sabaudiæ læsit, propter quòd comes regem Rudolfum desiit impugnare.
units.tr: The Count of Savoy attacked King Rudolf in hostility. But the count of N. injured the Count of Savoy, on account of which the count ceased to attack King Rudolf.

units.la: Quartale frumenti pro septendecim solidis dabatur, quartale vini, pro denariis nouem.
units.tr: A quarter of wheat was sold for seventeen shillings, and a quarter of wine for nine pennies.

units.la: Festo S. Nicolai Landisperch castrum Sculteti de Columbaria, per aduocatum Alsatiæ & Columbarienses obsidetur, & res eius diripiuntur.
units.tr: On the feast of St Nicholas, the castle of Landsberg, belonging to the sheriff of Colmar, was besieged by the advocate of Alsace and the men of Colmar, and its goods were plundered.

units.la: Vigilia Simonis & Iudæ, rex Rudolfus in Napolstein cum suis consanguineis pernoctauit.
units.tr: On the vigil of Saints Simon and Jude, King Rudolf spent the night at Napoleon's with his kinsmen.

units.la: Omnes piscatores haleces capientes submersi tempestate, saeuissima perierunt.
units.tr: All the fishermen catching herring were drowned by a most savage storm and perished.

units.la: Interfectus fuit Dominus de Meienheim in Phaphinheim.
units.tr: The lord of Mayenheim was killed at Pfaffenheim.

units.la: M. CC. LXXX- II.
Filius Rudolfi regis, Landgrauius Alsatiæ submersus fuit in Rheno, prope Rinaugiam, & sepultus fuit in Basilea à quatuor episcopis & hominibus multis cum humana gloria copiosa.
units.tr: The son of King Rudolf, the landgrave of Alsace, was drowned in the Rhine near Rheinau, and was buried at Basel by four bishops and many men, with a great display of worldly glory.

units.la: Ciues Rubiacenses, cum cæteris hominibus episcopi Argent. deliberauerunt, vt ei amplius non seruirent, nisi sub certa pecuniæ quantitate.
units.tr: The citizens of Rheinfelden, together with the other men of the bishop of Strasbourg, resolved that they would no longer serve him, except on condition of a fixed sum of money.

units.la: Nix intra octauam Epiphaniæ cecidit, tantæ spissitudinis, qualis intra triginta annos in Alsatiæ finibus non credebatur cecidisse. Plures homines dicebătur in ea frigore periisse.
units.tr: Snow fell within the octave of Epiphany, of such depth as was not believed to have fallen within thirty years in the territory of Alsace. Many men were said to have perished from the cold in it.

units.la: Papa Martinus renouauit fratribus Minoribus & Prædicatoribus authoritatem confessiones audiendi, pariterq; prædicandi.
units.tr: Pope Martin renewed for the Friars Minor and the Preachers the authority to hear confessions and likewise to preach.

units.la: Ciues Mülnhusenses mutuò se vulneribus affecerunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Mülhausen wounded one another.

units.la: M. C C. L X X X I I I.
Hyems calida fuit.
units.tr: The winter was warm.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus filium suum ducem Austriæ fecit.
units.tr: King Rudolf made his son duke of Austria.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus emit ius seu aduocatiam dominorum de Liechtenberg, quam habebant super ciuitatem Argentinensem.
units.tr: King Rudolf bought the right, or advocacy, of the lords of Liechtenberg, which they held over the city of Strasbourg.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis coegit Rubeacenses sibi reddere, quæ dederat eis suæ priuilegia libertatis.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg compelled the people of Rheinfelden to give back to him the privileges of liberty that he had granted them.

units.la: Festo Gregorij frumentum in Alsatia floruit.
units.tr: On the feast of Gregory, grain flourished in Alsace.

units.la: Eodem festo, episcopus Basiliensis, episcopus Argentinensis & rex Rudolfus adiutor iuior eorum, obsedit Brunstrut sex septimanis, & Melan castrum cœpit ac destruxit, & Brunnetrut fuit episcopo Basilien si cum villis adiacentibus restitutum.
units.tr: On the same feast, the bishop of Basel, the bishop of Strasbourg, and King Rudolf, their helper, besieged Brunstrut for six weeks. They captured and destroyed the castle of Melan, and Brunstrut, with the adjacent villages, was restored to the bishop of Basel.

units.la: Pridie nonas Iunij, interfectus fuit Friburgi venerabilis Commendator Teutoniæ ordinis, Guntrannus dictus de Bisèche, ab apostata ordinis sui, sculteti Friburgensis filio.
units.tr: On 4 June, the venerable commander of the Teutonic Order, called Guntram of Bisèche, was killed at Freiburg by an apostate of his order, the son of the Freiburg sculthetus.

units.la: Tres domini de Napolstein filij, viam carnis ingressi sunt vniuersæ.
units.tr: Three sons of the lords of Napoltstein entered the way of all flesh.

units.la: Kalendis Iunij, fraga, cerasa, pisa matura in Alsatia vendebantur.
units.tr: On the Kalends of June, ripe strawberries, cherries and peas were sold in Alsace.

units.la: Fratres Minores plus quàm xxxi virgines, & quasdam viduas congregauerunt, & in claustrum Alaspach quod eis emerunt pro mille trecentis marcis, x v Kal. Augusti cum pompa & maxima gloria incluserunt.
units.tr: The Friars Minor gathered more than thirty-one virgins and some widows, and on 17 July enclosed them, with pomp and great glory, in the cloister of Alspach, which they had bought for 1,300 marks.

units.la: Pridie nonas Iunij, obsedit Rudolfus rex Petterlingen.
units.tr: On 4 June, King Rudolf besieged Petterlingen.

units.la: Vigilia S. Galli, domini Richardi de Lobigasse, & plures domus fratrum suorum fuerunt destructæ, seu funditus demolitæ, per suos consanguineos & affines.
units.tr: On the eve of St Gall, the lord Richard of Lobigasse, and several houses of his brothers, were destroyed or utterly demolished by his kinsmen and relatives by marriage.

units.la: Rudolfus rex obsedit Paterniacū, & ædificauit circa munitiones & domos, intendens eos cogere per alimentorum penuriam tradere ciuitatem.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged Paterniacum and built fortifications and houses around it, intending to force the town to surrender by a shortage of food.

units.la: Circa Moguntiam nutrix pueri cuiusdam militis, vendidit eum Iudeis, vt interficerent eum: propter quod nutrix & Iudæi plures à Christianis fuerunt turpiter interfecti.
units.tr: Near Mainz, the nurse of a certain soldier's boy sold the child to the Jews so that they would kill him. On account of this, the nurse and several Jews were shamefully killed by Christians.

units.la: Rudolfus rex circa natiuitatē Domini inter ipsum & comitem Sabaudiæ compositionem fecit.
units.tr: Around Christmas, King Rudolf made an agreement between himself and the count of Savoy.

units.la: Obiit figulus in Sletzstatt, qui primus in Alsatia vitro vasa fictilia vestiebat.
units.tr: A potter died at Sletzstatt, who was the first in Alsace to coat earthenware vessels with glass.

units.la: Obiit frater Conradus Wernherus de Hadistatt, frater ordinis Teutonici.
units.tr: Brother Conrad Werner of Hadistatt died, a brother of the Teutonic Order.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXIIII.
Rex Rudolphus vxorem Gallicam duxit, in Romatico monte, festo S. Agathæ, & necessaria ministrauit superuenientibus abundanter.
units.tr: King Rudolf married a French wife on Romont mountain, on the feast of St Agatha, and abundantly supplied the necessities to those who arrived.

units.la: Regina regis Rudolphi venit in Colubariam in Carnisprimo, sc. Cathedra Petri, recepta à religiosis fuit, à clericis & militibus & ciuibus communiter gloriosè. Ciues dederunt ei expensas pluribus diebus, & insuper pro clenodiis centum libras.
units.tr: The queen of King Rudolf came to Colmar at Carnival, that is, to the Cathedra Petri. She was received by the religious, the clergy, the knights and the citizens alike, with great honour. The citizens gave her expenses for several days and, in addition, one hundred pounds for jewels.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Basiliensis celebrauit ordines in Columbaria, tertio non. Mart. quatuor temporum, & plurimos consecrauit.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Basel, held ordinations at Colmar on the third day before the Nones of March, in the Ember days, and consecrated many men.

units.la: Comes Ebirhardus, frater episcopi Constan. & frater comitis Gotfridi de Lauffenberch virtuosus, obiit ante tempus.
units.tr: Count Eberhard, brother of the bishop of Constance and of Count Gottfried of Lauffenberg, a virtuous man, died before his time.

units.la: Rudolfus rex Alsatiam & Mulnhusenses reconciliauit, & exercitum congregauit vt Colonien sem episcopum impugnaret.
units.tr: King Rudolf reconciled Alsace and Mülhausen, and gathered an army to attack the bishop of Cologne.

units.la: Fratres Minores Capitulum generale in Argentina celebrârunt. Chorū suum recenter consummatum consecrauerunt, quatuor episcopos ibidem habuerunt, & illic homines plurimi conuenerunt.
units.tr: The Friars Minor held their general chapter at Strasbourg. They consecrated their newly completed choir, had four bishops present there, and very many people gathered there.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Basil. ordinis fratrum Minorum celebrauit ordines in Columbaria, in ecclesia fratrum Minorum, x Kalen. Iunij, & habuit in comitatu suo Æthiopem indutum vestibus albis, & nanum scilicet Ritter Conrad, cuius longitudo ad tres pedes minime poterat peruenire.
units.tr: Henry, bishop of Basel, of the order of the Friars Minor, held ordinations at Colmar, in the church of the Friars Minor, on 23 May. In his retinue he had an Ethiopian dressed in white garments, and a dwarf, namely Ritter Conrad, whose height could by no means reach three feet.

units.la: Comes de Friburgo reconciliatus est cum ciuibus Friburgensibus, tali conditione, quòd præter redditus quos habebat de ciuitate, singulis annis centum marcas argenti sibi suisq; successoribus darent. Insuper deberent cum antiquorum suorum iura libere possidere.
units.tr: The count of Freiburg was reconciled with the citizens of Freiburg on this condition: that, beyond the revenues he already had from the city, they would give him and his successors one hundred silver marks each year. Moreover, they were to possess their ancient rights freely.

units.la: Fulgur in ecclesia Sletzstatt in ecclesia sanctæ Fidei, tres homines interfecit.
units.tr: Lightning struck the church of Holy Faith at Sletzstatt and killed three men.

units.la: Milites Alsatiæ, in festo S. Iacobi ad regem Teutoniæ in Moguntiam descenderunt, vt pro rebus imperij fortiter pugnarent.
units.tr: Soldiers of Alsace, on the feast of St James, went down to the king of the Romans at Mainz, to fight bravely for the affairs of the empire.

units.la: Circa Pragam Bohemiæ metropolim multi homines fame mortui.
units.tr: Near Prague, the metropolis of Bohemia, many men died of hunger.

units.la: In Alsatia quartale frumenti pro libra, & quartale vini pro duobus solidis dabatur.
units.tr: In Alsace a quart of grain was given for a pound, and a quart of wine for two shillings.

units.la: Chorus in Napolstwir inchoatus fuit.
units.tr: The choir at Napoltswir was begun.

units.la: Minores emerunt claustrum Alaspach sororibus suis pro M.c c.marcis.
units.tr: The Minors bought the cloister of Alspach for their sisters for 1,200 marks.

units.la: Mel in Alsatiæ finibus pluebat, vnde multi olera seu fructus comedere recusabant. Pestilentia in locis pluribus sequebatur. Comes montis Beligardi obiit, & episcopatui Basiliensi trecentarum marcarum redditus dereliquit.
units.tr: Honey rained down in the territory of Alsace, so that many refused to eat vegetables or fruit. Pestilence followed in many places. The count of Montbéliard died and left the bishopric of Basel revenues of three hundred marks.

units.la: Filius domini Wilhelmi regis Romanorum vindicauit se de Frisonibus, & interfecit ex eis mille quadringentos viros, & accepit corpus patris sui de eorum manibus violenter.
units.tr: The son of Lord William, king of the Romans, avenged himself on the Frisians and killed 1,400 of their men, and by force took the body of his father from their hands.

units.la: Dominus de Hohenstein aduocatus Alsatiae, sororibus de S. Ioanne octo vini vasa violenter abstulit.
units.tr: The lord of Hohenstein, advocate of Alsace, violently took eight vessels of wine from the sisters of St John.

units.la: Dominus Conradus Wernherus exusit dominis de Gyrsperc castrum, quod nouiter construxerant in monte.
units.tr: Lord Conrad Werner burned the castle of the lords of Gyrsperg, which they had newly built on the mountain.

units.la: Rex Arragonum & ciues Messanæ Carolum fratrem regis Franciæ de suis finibus turpiter expulerunt.
units.tr: The king of Aragon and the citizens of Messina shamefully expelled Charles, the brother of the king of France, from their territories.

units.la: Ordo Prædicatorum in Selecistat chorum suum anno precedenti consummauit. Idem fratres sequenti anno sedes in choro posuerunt, & intrauerunt.
units.tr: The Order of Preachers completed their choir at Schlettstadt the year before. The same brothers the following year set up seats in the choir and entered it.

units.la: Obiit mulier, quæ recordabatur, nullum pontem Rheni post Constantiam transiuisse.
units.tr: A woman died who recalled that she had never crossed a bridge over the Rhine after Constance.

units.la: XVII Kal. Decemb. Venus & Mercurius simul fuerunt.
units.tr: On 15 November, Venus and Mercury were together.

units.la: Ciues Friburgenses comiti, domino suo, pro modica emenda viginti millia marcarum tradiderunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Freiburg handed over twenty thousand marks to the count, their lord, for a small payment.

units.la: Item comes de Rapreswir obiit.
units.tr: Likewise, the count of Rapperswil died.

units.la: Wernherus archiepiscopus Moguntinus obiit, qui mille quingentas marcas suis posteris dereliquit.
units.tr: Werner, archbishop of Mainz, died, and left fifteen hundred marks to his successors.

units.la: Messis inchoata fuit, festo sanctorum Petri & Pauli. Eodem die Curiam habuit rex Rudolfus in Basilea cum gloria dominorum.
units.tr: The harvest began on the feast of Saints Peter and Paul. On the same day King Rudolf held court at Basel, with the splendour of the lords.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus, circa Iacobi festum, ciues Rheni ciuitatum, Wormatiam convocauit, iuramenta primo facta, secundario per iuramenti vinculum confirmauit.
units.tr: Around the feast of St James, King Rudolf summoned the citizens of the cities on the Rhine to Worms. The oaths first made he confirmed a second time by the bond of an oath.

units.la: Rex Arragonum Petrus, principem filium regis Caroli cepit, & ex eis multitudinem hominum interfecit.
units.tr: Peter, king of Aragon, captured the princely son of King Charles, and killed a multitude of their men.

units.la: Papa Cardinalem legatum in Franciam misit, qui clericorum ac religiosorum decimam regi Carolo faceret præsentari.
units.tr: The pope sent a cardinal legate into France, who was to have the tenth of the clergy and religious presented to King Charles.

units.la: Comes Reinhardus de Mümpelgart, tres de ciuibus suis cepit, qui se de capitate cum XL librarum millibus redemerunt.
units.tr: Count Reinhard of Mümpelgart captured three of his citizens, who ransomed themselves for forty thousand pounds.

units.la: Rex Rud. ciuitatem Herbipolensem obsidere voluisset. Ciues autem ei sex marcarum argenti millia tradiderunt, quæ eum ab eis fugere coegerunt.
units.tr: King Rudolf wanted to besiege the city of Würzburg. But the citizens handed over to him six thousand marks of silver, which compelled him to withdraw from them.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus circa festum S. Martini, quinq; castra sc. Waldeche, prædonum Sueuiæ, cum magna potentia dicitur obsedisse, ea subito cepisse, & per violentiam destruxisse.
units.tr: Around the feast of St Martin, King Rudolf is said to have besieged five castles with great force, namely Waldeck, the stronghold of the robbers of Swabia; to have taken them suddenly; and to have destroyed them by violence.

units.la: Dominus de Hohenstein aduocatus Alsatiae, castrum Echirc potenter obsedit, spacio breui temporis expugnauit, & in potestatem sibi propriam deportauit. Ideo vero dicitur expugnasse, quia suum cognatum, Iohannem de Echirc, qui consanguineos suos honore ac diuitiis præcellebat, fraudulenter occiderunt.
units.tr: The lord of Hohenstein, advocate of Alsace, besieged the castle of Echirc with great force, took it in a short time, and brought it into his own power. He is said to have taken it because they had treacherously killed their kinsman, John of Echirc, who surpassed his relatives in honour and wealth.

units.la: Posthæc idem aduocatus Alsatiæ, cum episcopi Argentinensis adiutorio Ochsenstein castrum potenter expugnabat, & funditus euertebat.
units.tr: Afterwards the same advocate of Alsace, with the help of the bishop of Strasbourg, stormed the castle of Ochsenstein with force and utterly overthrew it.

units.la: Bonum vinum creuit in bona quantitate, sed non videbatur durabile.
units.tr: Good wine grew in good quantity, but it did not seem likely to last.

units.la: Ante festum Clementis fuit aura pulchra, dulcis & amœna, & quasi sine pluuia per quatuordecim septimanas.
units.tr: Before the feast of St Clement there was a fine, sweet and pleasant air, and almost no rain for fourteen weeks.

units.la: Festo S. Catharinæ cecidit tectu Capellæ, quæ sita est supra vineta, prope Morbacum, vbi & primitus se receperant monachi Morbacenses, & ad quem locum omnia eorum sunt priuilegia & dignitates impetrata.
units.tr: On the feast of St Catherine the roof of a chapel fell in. The chapel lies above the vineyards near Morbach, where the monks of Morbach first withdrew, and to that place all their privileges and dignities were obtained.

units.la: Ciues Columbarienses regi Rudolfo vno anno librarum xxx millia transmiterunt. xvii Cal.....oppositurunt se Columbarienses regi Rudolfo, quia tricesimam rerum suarum sibi dare noluerunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Colmar sent King Rudolf thirty thousand pounds in one year. On 17 ... the people of Colmar opposed King Rudolf, because they were unwilling to give him a thirtieth of their goods.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXV.
units.tr: M. CC. LXXXV.

units.la: Kalendis Aprilis, Abbas Morbacensis ciuitatem suam Gebwiler latenter cepit, & res & eorum corpora in totum confiscauit.
units.tr: On the Kalends of April, the Abbot of Murbach secretly seized his town of Gebweiler, and confiscated both its goods and its people in their entirety.

units.la: Ciuitas Friburgensis in Orlandin & Bernensis obedire regi Rudolfo minime voluerunt. Ciuitas Bernensis fuit ab igne penè totaliter deuorata.
units.tr: The city of Freiburg and the city of Bern refused altogether to obey King Rudolf. The city of Bern was almost totally devoured by fire.

units.la: Papa Martinus obijt.
units.tr: Pope Martin died.

units.la: Instituit anguillas, mortem gustauit in illis,Assas & coctas martyrisauit eas.
units.tr: He instituted eels, and in them he tasted death; he martyred them, both roasted and grilled.

units.la: Nonis Maij, ciues Columbarienses regi Rudolfo se primitùs oppositerunt, & per ignem Theinheim villam & quasdam alias destruxerunt.
units.tr: On the Nones of May, the citizens of Colmar first set themselves against King Rudolf, and by fire they destroyed the village of Theinheim and certain others.

units.la: Circa festum Pentecostes, ciues de Haginogia, aduocatu terrae, filium sororis regis Rudolfi, de castro quod est in ciuitate turpiter expulerunt, & postea regi seruire minimè voluerunt.
units.tr: Around the feast of Pentecost, the citizens of Hagenau, the landvogt, expelled shamefully from the castle in the town the son of King Rudolf's sister, and afterwards they refused to serve the king at all.

units.la: Rudolfus rex obsedit Columbarienses, decimo octauo Kal. Iulij, quinq; diebus.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged the people of Colmar for five days, beginning on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July.

units.la: Ciues Columbarienses posuerunt super se c c marcas, duoq; millia marcarum & milites, qui se Columbarien sibus non opposuerunt, vel in obsidione eorundem non fideliter adiuuerunt, cum ciuibus exactionibus grauabantur.
units.tr: The citizens of Colmar imposed on themselves 200 marks and 2,000 marks, and the soldiers who had not opposed the people of Colmar, or who had not faithfully helped in their siege, were burdened with exactions along with the citizens.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis terram ducis Lotharingiæ pluries intrauit, & eum enormiter spoliauit.
units.tr: The Bishop of Strasbourg repeatedly entered the land of the Duke of Lorraine and plundered him outrageously.

units.la: Domini de Wassilnheim ceperunt hospitem praedicatorum de Eginsheim, & eum ad terram Franciæ transtulerunt. (ter.)
units.tr: The lords of Wasselnheim seized the host of the preachers of Eguisheim and transported him to the land of France. (ter.)

units.la: Nocte Nicolai fugerunt captiui, quos Domini de Wasselnheim ceperat fraudulè-De potestate Rodolfi regis fugit Iudæus captiuus, qui ei mille quingentas trade-re promittebat marcas.
units.tr: On the night of St Nicholas the captives whom the lords of Wasselnheim had fraudulently seized escaped. A Jewish captive escaped from the power of King Rudolf, who promised him 1,500 marks to hand him over.

units.la: Abbas Morbacensis dictus de Steinebrunne, obijt circa festum Luciæ, qui destructor Religionis & dissipator enormis rerum sui Monasterij dicebatur.
units.tr: The Abbot of Murbach, called of Steinbrunn, died around the feast of St Lucy. He was called the destroyer of religion and the outrageous squanderer of the goods of his monastery.

units.la: Ciues de Zouingen Rudolfum regem pro Domino suo acceperunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Zofingen accepted King Rudolf as their lord.

units.la: Petrus rex Aragonum mortuus.
units.tr: Peter, King of Aragon, died.

units.la: Richardus de Lobigaße quosdam milites de Basilea voluit occidere fraudulenter.
units.tr: Richard of Lobigau wished to kill certain soldiers of Basel by treachery.

units.la: Regem Rudolfum filij eius impetebant pro multis millibus marcarum.
units.tr: His sons pressed King Rudolf for many thousands of marks.

units.la: Ipse autem de consilio nobilium obligauit eis quasdam Imperij ciuitates.
units.tr: He, however, on the advice of the nobles, pledged to them certain cities of the Empire.

units.la: Moniales Cistertiensis ordinis de claustro Hirsau recesserunt.
units.tr: The nuns of the Cistercian order left the cloister of Hirsau.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXVI.
units.tr: M. CC. LXXXVI.

units.la: Die Paschæ quidam ciuium Columbariensium seruos Sculteti vulnerauerunt, & eos in claustrum Minorum per violentiam coegerunt. Propter hoc fuerunt illi ciues eiecti de ciuitate, & eorum domos destructæ, & eorū res à iudicibus confiscatæ.
units.tr: On Easter Day certain citizens of Colmar wounded the servants of the sheriff and forcibly drove them into the cloister of the Minorites. On account of this those citizens were expelled from the town, their houses were destroyed, and their goods were confiscated by the magistrates.

units.la: Sorores de S. Ioanne, sub-tilia, ordinis Prædicatorum, contra libertatem Religiosorum L X marcas dare à ciuibus cogebantur.
units.tr: The Sisters of St John, of the Dominican order, were compelled by the citizens to give sixty marks, contrary to the liberty of religious persons.

units.la: Philippi & Iacobi ciues Argent. in aquis & nauibus ludos exercuerunt, ad spectaculum verò venientes supra pontem se receperunt, & eo cadente plures miserabiliter perierunt.
units.tr: On the feast of Philip and James, the citizens of Strasbourg held games on the water and in boats; but those coming to watch retreated onto the bridge, and when it collapsed, many perished miserably.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus obsedit oppidum Luterburg, Episcopi Spirensis, aliquot septimanis: qui resistere regi non valentes, se regis gratiæ tradiderunt.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged for some weeks the town of Lauterburg, belonging to the Bishop of Speyer; unable to resist the king, its people surrendered themselves to the king's mercy.

units.la: Episcopus Treuerensis obijt.
units.tr: The Bishop of Trier died.

units.la: Capella in Hugeshoven, reædificatur à venerabili Abbate, Conrado de Dickere, quæ anno M. C. LXXXVI, fuerat inchoata. Ipsum autem Monasterium fuit inchoatum à Wernhero comite de Ortiberch, dicto de Hurningen, cuius longitudo octo pedum depicta communium, in eodem monasterio reperitur.
units.tr: The chapel at Hugshofen is rebuilt by the venerable Abbot Konrad of Dickers, having been begun in the year 1086. The monastery itself was begun by Count Werner of Ortenberg, called of Hohnburg, whose length of eight feet, painted in the common manner, is found in the same monastery.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus misit Henricum episcopum Basil. ordinis fratrum Minorum, ad Papam, ad diuersa negotia terminanda. Papa verò Episcopum Basil. Archiepiscopum Maguntinum, præpositum verò Maguntinum s. Diuitem, Episcopū Basil. faciebat.
units.tr: King Rudolf sent Henry, Bishop of Basel, of the order of the Minorite friars, to the Pope, to settle various matters. The Pope, however, made the Bishop of Basel Archbishop of Mainz, and the provost of Mainz, St Dietrich, Bishop of Basel.

units.la: Domini de Liechtenberg curiam prope Liechtenberg celebrabant, ad quam per se & per alios plurimos inuitabant.
units.tr: The lords of Liechtenberg held a court near Liechtenberg, to which they invited many people, both themselves and through others.

units.la: Eodem tempore Legatus à latere domini Papæ missus, cum plenaria potestate Basileam venit, & dominum Basilien sem in episcopum electum consecrauit.
units.tr: At the same time a legate sent from the side of the lord Pope came to Basel with full powers, and consecrated the lord of Basel as bishop-elect.

units.la: Turegum exusta est pro tertia parte, propter eorum superbiam: vt per obsessum Diabolus recitauit.
units.tr: Zurich was burned for a third part, on account of its pride, as the devil who was possessed recited.

units.la: Henricus episcopus Basilien sis, factus archiepiscopus Moguntinus, receptus est contra spem à suis subditis gloriosè.
units.tr: Henry, Bishop of Basel, made Archbishop of Mainz, was received gloriously by his subjects, contrary to expectation.

units.la: Rudolfus rex duo castra fortia domini de Wirtenberck noscitur obsedisse, & ea in breui tempore intelleximus expugnasse. Ipse etiam dominus de Wirtenberck cognatus regis obsessus, de castro descendit, & ad pedes adulutus, se & sua tradidit in regiam potestatem.
units.tr: King Rudolf is known to have besieged two strong castles of the lord of Württemberg, and within a short time we learned that he had taken them by storm. The lord of Württemberg himself, the king's kinsman, was besieged; he came down from the castle, and falling at the king's feet, surrendered himself and his possessions into the royal power.

units.la: Post festum S.Margarete noua de Friderico Imp. peregrini in Alsatia retulerunt.
units.tr: After the feast of St Margaret, new reports came from the pilgrims concerning Emperor Frederick in Alsace.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus obsedit plus quam xx septimanis castellum, quod dicitur Stut gart, quod situm est prope Esslingen. Et taedio affectus rex, composuit cum domino de Wirtenberck, & ad legatum in Spiram venire disposuit festinanter.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged for more than twenty weeks the castle called Stuttgart, which lies near Esslingen. Worn out by the tedium, the king came to terms with the lord of Württemberg, and resolved to come hastily to the legate at Speyer.

units.la: In die Animarum, venit Legatus Columbariam.
units.tr: On the Day of the Dead, the legate came to Colmar.

units.la: Commissae sunt sorores, quae dicuntur Poenitentes, fratribus Praedicatoribus ad regendum.
units.tr: The sisters who are called Penitents were entrusted to the Dominican friars to govern.

units.la: Legatus Teutoniae in Metim se transferebat, quia furorem Teutonicorum non immerito metuebat.
units.tr: The legate of Germany moved on to Metz, because he rightly feared the fury of the Germans.

units.la: Glacies quae fluxit in Rheno, cxv naues submersit, & villas aliquas deuastauit.
units.tr: Ice which floated down the Rhine sank 115 ships and devastated some villages.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXVII.

Legatus, a latere domini Papae missus, concilium xvii calendas Aprilis celebrare voluisset: sed per appellationem episcopi Colonien-sis, & episcopi Tullensis, Probi nomine, ordinis Minorum, fuit totaliter interruptum.
units.tr: The legate sent from the side of the lord Pope wished to hold a council on the seventeenth day before the calends of April, but through the appeal of the bishop of Cologne and the bishop of Toul, Probus by name, of the Minorite order, it was entirely interrupted.

units.la: XVI calend. Aprilis, dominus de Napolstein villam S.Hippolyti cum exercitu introiuit, eamq; & ecclesiā ignibus deuastauit. Clericus de ecclesia saltauit, & confractus periit in instanti.
units.tr: On the sixteenth day before the calends of April, the lord of Napolstein entered the village of St Hippolytus with an army and destroyed both the village and its church with fire. A cleric danced out of the church, and, broken, died on the spot.

units.la: Honorius papa obiit.
units.tr: Pope Honorius died.

units.la: Dominus de Napolstein cum exercitu terram Gallicorum intrauit, & cxx villas exussit, eorum res totaliter depraedatus.
units.tr: The lord of Napolstein entered the land of the French with an army, burned 120 villages, and utterly plundered their goods.

units.la: Sexto idus Maij, dominus de Baldecke uxorem duxit: & ciues Columbarienses res domini de Napolstein communiter inuaserunt.
units.tr: On the sixth ides of May, the lord of Baldecke took a wife, and the citizens of Colmar jointly attacked the goods of the lord of Napolstein.

units.la: Dominus de Napolstein dominum de Horburch viriliter impugnauit, atq; ad Cellisberch peruenit, vt captiuos sua potentia liberaret. Dominus autem de Horburch cum balistariis de Cellisberch descendit, eiq; octo equos interfecit, & plus quam viginti vnum equites vulnerauit.
units.tr: The lord of Napolstein fiercely attacked the lord of Horburch and came to Cellisberch, intending by his power to free the captives. But the lord of Horburch came down from Cellisberch with crossbowmen, killed eight of his horses, and wounded more than twenty-one horsemen.

units.la: Portae fratrum Praedicatorum in Argentina a ciuibus claudebantur: volebant eos cogere, vt suam per omnia facerent voluntatem.
units.tr: The gates of the Preaching friars in Strasbourg were shut by the citizens, who wanted to force them to do their will in everything.

units.la: Rudolfus rex Napolstein tribus diebus obsedit, sed ab obsidione recessit: quod eum sui morti tradere voluissent.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged Napolstein for three days but withdrew from the siege, because his own men had wished to hand him over to death.

units.la: Episcopus Probus nomine, ordinis Minorum, fuit excommunicatus in Argentina, in dedicatione ecclesiae maioris, a Gordiano ordinis fratrum Minorum.
units.tr: Bishop Probus, of the Minorite order, was excommunicated at Strasbourg, at the dedication of the greater church, by Gordianus of the Minorite friars.

units.la: Prope Brunnentrut fuerunt de hominibus Basilien-sis episcopi quidam interfecti, & plus quam duodecim milites captiuati.
units.tr: Near Pruntrut, some men of the bishop of Basel were killed and more than twelve soldiers were taken captive.

units.la: Rudolfus rex, cum ciuitatibus vicinis, castrum ligneum in Gemar, ad obsidendum castrum Napolstein noscitur construxisse.
units.tr: King Rudolf, together with the neighbouring cities, is known to have built a wooden castle at Gemar in order to besiege the castle of Napolstein.

units.la: Dominus de Napolstein homines domini Horburch & multos de Sigolsheim cepit & sine pugna ad propria perducebat, & duo marcarum soluere potuerunt.
units.tr: The lord of Napolstein captured men of the lord of Horburch and many from Sigolsheim, and led them to his own place without a fight; they were able to pay two marks.

units.la: Episcopus Metensis omnes pene Rheni episcopos, & omnes dominos quos poterat pretio conducebat, & congregauit exercitum magnum, sc. quatuor millium militum & centum equos phaleratos. Omni die quinquaginta vasa vini, & septingentas libras Metensis monetae stipendiariis ministrauit, & coegit comitem Barenfem eius misericordiam suppliciter inuocare.
units.tr: The bishop of Metz hired, for money, almost all the bishops of the Rhine and every lord he could, and gathered a great army, namely four thousand soldiers and a hundred caparisoned horses. Every day he supplied the mercenaries with fifty vessels of wine and seven hundred pounds of Metz money, and he compelled the count of Barr to implore his mercy humbly.

units.la: Consules Argentinenses ciues suos equos habere bis mille praecepere.
units.tr: The consuls of Strasbourg ordered their citizens to keep two thousand horses.

units.la: Obiit Cuonradus de Wirzi-burch / in Teutonico multorum bonorum dictaminum compilator.
units.tr: Conrad of Würzburg died, a compiler in German of many good writings in prose.

units.la: Eclipsis Lunae fuit, vndecimo Kalendas Nouembris media nocte, & Iris insequenti, seu in crepusculo videbatur.
units.tr: There was an eclipse of the moon on the eleventh day before the calends of November, at midnight, and a rainbow was seen afterwards, or at twilight.

units.la: Abbatissa Seconensis, quae & procuratrix claustri vallis Masonis, in dominam claustri montis Romatici sublimatur.
units.tr: The abbess of Seconensis, who was also procuratrix of the cloister of the Masmünster valley, was raised to be lady of the cloister of Mount Romaticus.

units.la: Episcopus Basiliensis terram comitis montis Belgardi potenter intrauit, pluresque que villas deuastauit. Comes vero de militibus episcopi plus quinquaginta de nobilioribus ac ditioribus captiuauit.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel forcefully entered the land of the count of Montbéliard and devastated several villages. But the count captured more than fifty of the bishop's soldiers, the more noble and the wealthier among them.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXVIII.
Expulit abbas Morbacensis omnes nobiles de castello <bl>Gebwiler</bl> pro eo quod se mutuo vulnerauerant fraudulenter.
units.tr: The abbot of Murbach expelled all the nobles from the castle of Gebwiler, because they had fraudulently wounded one another.

units.la: Regis Rudolphi filius, Lantgrauius Alsatiæ, cum centum equis in curia sororum de Columbaria sub tilia, requieuit.
units.tr: The son of King Rudolf, landgrave of Alsace, rested with a hundred horses in the court of the sisters of Columbaria, under a linden tree.

units.la: Vndecimo Kal. Febr. multæ aues prope montem Bilgardis conuenerunt, contra se pugnauerunt, & plus quàm trecentæ (vt dicebatur à pluribus) perierunt. Similiter & porci domestici circa eundem locum plurimi conuenerunt, & se mutuis morsibus occiderunt.
units.tr: On the eleventh day before the calends of February, many birds gathered near Mount Bilgardis, fought against one another, and more than three hundred (as many people reported) perished. Likewise, many domestic pigs gathered around the same place and killed each other with mutual bites.

units.la: Iudæi dederunt regi Rudolpho xx millia marcarum, vt illis de Wessila & de Popardia iudicaret.
units.tr: The Jews gave King Rudolf twenty thousand marks so that he would judge in favour of those of Wessila and Popardia.

units.la: Circa Purificationis venit ventus, qui magnam syluam sub Hohinnac radicitus deuastauit.
units.tr: Around the Purification a wind came that tore up a great forest by the roots below Hohinnac.

units.la: Idem ventus Flandriam Oceano inundauit, ad tria magna miliaria, & plus quàm i millia hominum interfecit.
units.tr: The same wind flooded Flanders from the ocean for three great miles and killed more than a thousand people.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus congregauit exercitum, vt obsessum castrum Maguntinensi domino archiepiscopo liberaret.
units.tr: King Rudolf gathered an army to free the castle, besieged, belonging to the lord archbishop of Mainz.

units.la: Obiit frater Henricus, ordinis Minorum, archiepiscopus Maguntinus, xiiii Kalend. Aprilis.
units.tr: Brother Henry, of the Minorite order, archbishop of Mainz, died on the fourteenth day before the calends of April.

units.la: Kalen. Aprilis, rex Rudolfus episcopus Argentinensis, & ciues Argent. & domini terræ, in Columbaria pacis fœdera iurauerunt. Inter ciues Argent. & fratres Prædicatores componere voluissent.
units.tr: On the calends of April, King Rudolf, the bishop of Strasbourg, the citizens of Strasbourg and the lords of the land swore treaties of peace at Colmar. They had wished to settle matters between the citizens of Strasbourg and the Preaching friars.

units.la: Regem Rudolfum legatus Franciæ visitauit.
units.tr: The legate of France visited King Rudolf.

units.la: Circa Kalend. Martij tantum frigus fuit, vt infra Basileam clauserit glacies aquas Rheni, & vinum congelabatur in ecclesiis, in calicibus & ampullis.
units.tr: Around the calends of March there was such great cold that ice closed the waters of the Rhine below Basel, and wine froze in the churches, in chalices and in cruets.

units.la: Dominus Ieronymus cardinalis & prouisor ordinis Minorum, in papam circa principium medium quadragesimæ consecratur.
units.tr: Lord Jerome, cardinal and provisor of the Minorite order, was consecrated pope around the beginning of the middle of Lent.

units.la: Vxorem dominus de Baldecke duxit, curiam magnam in Basilea celebrauit, in qua plus quàm dcc marcas creditur expendisse.
units.tr: The lord of Baldecke took a wife and held a great feast at Basel, at which more than 700 marks are believed to have been spent.

units.la: XVII Kalend. Maij, nocte perierunt vites.
units.tr: On the seventeenth day before the calends of May, at night, the vines perished.

units.la: Iudæa iuuecula de antiquo Iudæo in Rubiaca quatuor pueros noscitur peperisse.
units.tr: A young Jewish woman in Rubiaca is known to have borne four boys by an old Jew.

units.la: Dedicata fuit in Wissenburc area fratrum Prædicatorum.
units.tr: The courtyard of the Preaching friars at Wissenburg was dedicated.

units.la: Circa nonas Iunij, obsedit rex Rudolfus Bernensem Burgundiæ ciuitatem.
units.tr: Around the nones of June, King Rudolf besieged the Burgundian city of Bern.

units.la: Octaua Epiphaniæ venit mercator Basileam, ducens secum vinum Græcum seu Cypri, deditq; bicarium illius vini pro quinq; solidis, quartale pro libra, quod vsq; ad illud tempus fuerat inauditum.
units.tr: On the octave of the Epiphany a merchant came to Basel bringing Greek wine, or Cyprus wine, and sold a bicarium of that wine for five shillings, a quart for a pound. Until then such wine had been unheard of.

units.la: Captus est dominus archiepiscopus Colonensis.
units.tr: The lord archbishop of Cologne was captured.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus obsedit montem Beligardi, circa Kalendas Iulij.
units.tr: King Rudolf besieged Mount Belligardi around the calends of July.

units.la: VI Idus Iulij, cecidit grando magna, & fecit damnum in diuersis locis. Et fulgur exussit tectum castri, quod dicitur der Stein in Napolstein / & tecta in Türinchem deuastauit.
units.tr: On the sixth ides of July a great hailstorm fell and caused damage in various places. Lightning burned the roof of the castle called der Stein in Napolstein, and devastated roofs in Türinchem.

units.la: Mulier puerum cum quatuor dentibus pariebat.
units.tr: A woman gave birth to a boy with four teeth.

units.la: Rudolfus rex Romanorum terram Gallicorum circa Brunnendrut plus quàm tribus septimanis cum xx millibus hominum deuastauit.
units.tr: Rudolf, king of the Romans, devastated the land of the French around Pruntrut for more than three weeks with twenty thousand men.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus secundario Bernenses dicitur obsedisse.
units.tr: King Rudolf is said to have besieged the Bernese a second time.

units.la: Inclusæ de Ratzintal/in Amulshwitz se circa festum Omnium sanctorum transtulerunt, & moniales se postea vocauerunt.
units.tr: The enclosed women of Ratzintal moved to Amulshwitz around the feast of All Saints, and afterwards they called themselves nuns.

units.la: Dominus Hermannus de Napolstein/ obsedit Hohinnac castrum, & per promissiones obtinuit fraudulenter. Idem obsedit castrum in Meinrewire/ & cum exi- stentes in eo retinere non possent, sub conditionibus tradiderunt.
units.tr: Lord Hermann of Napolstein besieged the castle of Hohinnac and fraudulently obtained it through promises. He likewise besieged the castle at Meinrewire, and since those inside could not hold out, they surrendered on conditions.

units.la: M. CC. LXXXIX.
units.tr: M. CC. LXXXIX.

units.la: Alsa circa Herinstein & alias villas vicinas, circa Epiphaniam domini inundabat. Episcopus Curiensis à regis Rudolfi filio captiuatur.
units.tr: Alsa overflowed around Herinstein and other neighbouring villages about the Epiphany of the Lord. The bishop of Chur was captured by the son of King Rudolf.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus circa Quadragesimam in Egra ciuitate, prope Bohemiam curiam celebrauit.
units.tr: King Rudolf held a court about Lent in the city of Eger, near Bohemia.

units.la: Sifridus miles, quondam Sculteus Columb. v i cal. Aprilis interficitur, à Sufingo.
units.tr: Sifrid, a knight, formerly the mayor, was killed by Sufingen on the sixth day before the Kalends of April.

units.la: Ciues Bernenses obsessi, regi Rudolfo se sub conditione amicabili noluerunt tradere.
units.tr: The citizens of Bern, under siege, refused to surrender to King Rudolf on friendly terms.

units.la: Quarto Kalen. Maij venit Rudolfus rex Romanorum in Columbariam & duxit secum Camelum animal magnum, trium annorum, altitudinis inconsuetae.
units.tr: On the fourth day before the Kalends of May King Rudolf came to Columbaria and brought with him a camel, a large animal three years old and of unusual height.

units.la: Eodem die venit frater Mumio, magister ordinis Praedicatorum, in Columbariam, festinans ire in Treuirim ad Capitulum generale. Rex verò Rudolfus ob reuerentiam magistri comedit in domo fratrum Praedicatorum, festo S. Petri martyris & praedicatoris, & fecit eis & dominabus quibusdam & dominis multis conuiuium magnum & bonum, & fratribus praedicatoribus inconsuetum.
units.tr: On the same day Brother Mumio, master of the Order of Preachers, came to Columbaria, hurrying on to Trier for the general chapter. King Rudolf, out of reverence for the master, dined in the house of the Preaching friars on the feast of St Peter the martyr and preacher. He gave a great and splendid banquet for the friars, for certain noblewomen and for many lords, a feast unusual for the Preaching friars.

units.la: Eadem die proscripsit dominos de Gyrsperch, eò quòd occiderunt, Sifridū militem de Gundolsheim fraudulenter.
units.tr: On the same day he outlawed the lords of Girsberg, because they had treacherously killed Sifrid, knight of Gundolsheim.

units.la: Eodem septimana occisus est, comes de Honberch, cognatus regis à ciuibus Bernensibus violenter.
units.tr: In the same week the count of Honberg, a kinsman of the king, was violently killed by the citizens of Bern.

units.la: Gyrsperch castrum à Colmariensibus obsidetur.
units.tr: The castle of Girsberg was besieged by the Colmarians.

units.la: Ciuitas Rotwilensis exuritur.
units.tr: The city of Rottweil was burned.

units.la: Ciues Bernenses cum rege Rudolfo composuerunt, & se in suam potestatem voluntariè tradiderunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Bern came to terms with King Rudolf and voluntarily surrendered themselves into his power.

units.la: Grando magna circa Basilea fuit, quę frumentum, fructus & vineas deuastauit.
units.tr: A great hailstorm fell about Basel, which laid waste the grain, fruits and vineyards.

units.la: Dominus de Baldecke, de procuratione à rege sibi commissa, à regis filio remouetur.
units.tr: The lord of Baldecke was removed by the king's son from the administration entrusted to him by the king.

units.la: In Treuerim D C C fratres venisse ad Capitulum referuntur, fratrū seruì trecenti.
units.tr: It is reported that 700 friars came to the chapter at Trier, and 300 servants of the friars.

units.la: Castrum Ermisbuche, D. comitis Phitretarū, primo Kal. Maij à dominis arripitur fraudulenter.
units.tr: The castle of Ermisbuche, belonging to the count palatine, was seized treacherously by the lords on the first day before the Kalends of May.

units.la: Rex Angliae fratribus Praedicatoribus, qui venerunt in Treuerim ad Capitulum generale tribus diebus abundanter necessaria ministrauit.
units.tr: The king of England provided abundantly for three days the necessities of the Preaching friars who had come to Trier for the general chapter.

units.la: Filius regis Rudolfi castrum Dochinberck, abbatis S. Galli, creditur expugnasse.
units.tr: The son of King Rudolf is believed to have stormed the castle of Dochinberg, belonging to the abbot of St Gall.

units.la: In Lombardia fratres Minores habuerunt Capitulum, & venit illuc papa Nicolaus frater ordinis ipsorum, cum fratribus D C C C.
units.tr: The Franciscan friars held a chapter in Lombardy, and Pope Nicholas, a friar of their order, came there with 800 friars.

units.la: Papa Nicolaus expellitur de Roma, quia filium Caroli in regem, eis contradicentibus consecrauit, & cum illo pars Papae: vbi ex vtraq; parte plus quàm D numero perierunt.
units.tr: Pope Nicholas was expelled from Rome, because he had consecrated the son of Charles as king against their wishes; and the party of the Pope went with him. On both sides more than 500 perished.

units.la: Episcopus Coloniensis à captiuitate liberatur.
units.tr: The bishop of Cologne was freed from captivity.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus pro triginta libris argenti caueam in Basilea aui Psittaco comparauit.
units.tr: King Rudolf bought a cage in Basel for a parrot, for thirty pounds of silver.

units.la: Episcopus Metensis cepit comites ducis de Lüningen.
units.tr: The bishop of Metz captured the counts of the duke of Lüningen.

units.la: Terraemotus factus vno die quinquies.
units.tr: An earthquake occurred five times in one day.

units.la: Inclusae in Ratzental se in Amerschwiler transtulerunt, & ibidem claustrum construxerunt, & eodem anno in Capitulo Treuerensi fratribus Praedicatoribus in Columbaria committuntur. In festo Catharinę primâ missam in area propria decantauerunt.
units.tr: The enclosed women at Ratzental moved to Amerschwiler, and there built a cloister for themselves. In the same year they were entrusted, at the Trier chapter, to the Preaching friars in Columbaria. On the feast of St Catherine they sang the first Mass in their own courtyard.

units.la: Milites Alsatiae, qui parem vestem tribus annis penè tulerant, & se Nebelringin nominauerant, ad regis praesentiam citantur.
units.tr: The knights of Alsace, who had for nearly three years worn the same clothing and had called themselves the Nebelringen, were summoned into the king's presence.

units.la: Inclusae in Suntheim aream in Gebwiler centum marcis comparârunt.
units.tr: The enclosed women at Sonnheim bought a courtyard in Gebwiler for one hundred marks.

units.la: Sorores sub-Tilia tertiam domum claustri sui perfecerunt magnis expensis.
units.tr: The sisters under the linden tree completed the third house of their cloister at great expense.

units.la: Hyems calida. Herbae, flores, arbores flores & folia ante natiuitatem Domini produxerunt. Venatores tum fraga in Alsatia inuenerunt. Piceę cum gallinis ante trium regū protulerunt: vites floruerunt ante Hilarij: arbores folia antiqua retinuerunt, donec recentia prodierunt. Pueri in Egisheim in profluente balneabant.
units.tr: The winter was warm. Herbs, flowers, trees with blossoms and leaves put forth before Christmas. Hunters then found strawberries in Alsace. Pine trees put forth their cones before the feast of the Three Kings; vines blossomed before St Hilary's day; trees kept their old leaves until the new ones came out. Boys were bathing in the flowing water at Egisheim.

units.la: M. C C. X C.
units.tr: M. C C. X C.

units.la: Rudolfus rex dederat in purificatione suffodientibus castrum Girsperck mille nongentas libras, praeter victum. Crastino Agathae, domini de Girsperck, & castrum domino aduocato terrae, sine gratia comiserunt: sed semi eorū sub gratia recipiuntur. Henricus Dux Bauariæ, amicus fratrum prædicatorum, obijt.
units.tr: King Rudolf, at the Purification, had given the diggers at the castle of Girsberg 1900 pounds, besides their food. The day after St Agatha the lords of Girsberg surrendered the castle without mercy to the lord advocate of the land; but half of them were received under mercy. Henry, Duke of Bavaria, a friend of the Preaching friars, died.

units.la: Rudolfus rex in Thuringia fuit, & in ea magnam dignitatem pretio comparauit.
units.tr: King Rudolf was in Thuringia, and there he bought a great dignity for a price.

units.la: Fratres Minores in Columbaria Capitulum celebrauerunt, & Domini terræ eis plura seruitia ministrabant.
units.tr: The Franciscan friars held a chapter in Columbaria, and the lords of the land provided them with many services.

units.la: Dux Alsatiæ Rudolfus, filius regis Rudolfi, obijt, & in Praga Bohemorum sepelitur.
units.tr: Rudolf, Duke of Alsace, son of King Rudolf, died and was buried in Prague among the Bohemians.

units.la: Lector fratrum Minorum de Basilea, fecit capi in Columbaria in Capitulo suo, duas Beginas & duos Beghardos, & in Basilea plures, quos hæreticos reputabat.
units.tr: The reader of the Franciscan friars at Basel had two Beguines and two Beghards seized at Columbaria during their chapter, and many more in Basel, whom he considered heretics.

units.la: Episcopus Curiensis obijt.
units.tr: The bishop of Chur died.

units.la: Comes Egino Friburgensis, dederat filio suo, filiam ducis Lotharingiæ in vxorem.
units.tr: Count Egino of Freiburg had given his son the daughter of the duke of Lorraine in marriage.

units.la: Conradus de Lechtenberg episcopus Argentinensis, harum nuptiarum causa magnam Curiam in Argentina celebrauit.
units.tr: Conrad of Lichtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg, held a great court at Strasbourg on account of these nuptials.

units.la: Hyems calida & pluuiosa, æstas frigida & pluuiosa.
units.tr: The winter was warm and rainy; the summer cold and rainy.

units.la: In Burgundia prope Losannam cecidit grando magna, cuius lapides duorum vel trium panum magnitudinem superabant. Læsit nouem Ecclesias parochiales, & LX millia hominum computabantur periisse.
units.tr: In Burgundy, near Lausanne, a great hailstorm fell, whose stones exceeded the size of two or three loaves. It damaged nine parish churches, and 60,000 people were reckoned to have perished.

units.la: Canonici de Hanoë se in Rhinaugiam transtulerunt.
units.tr: The canons of Hanoë moved to Reichenau.

units.la: Dominus de Veldenz congregauit exercitum, venit in Alsatiam, volens in Autumno domino de Rapolstein vineas suas extirpare. Dominus de Rapolstein congregato exercitu, dominum de Veldenz prohibuit.
units.tr: The lord of Veldenz gathered an army and came into Alsace, intending in the autumn to root out the vineyards of the lord of Rappoltstein. The lord of Rappoltstein, having gathered an army, prevented the lord of Veldenz.

units.la: Inclusæ in Suntheim quarto Kal. Nouembris Gebuilr in claustrum, quod ibidem sibi construxerunt, se transtulerunt.
units.tr: On the fourth day before the Kalends of November the enclosed women at Sonnheim moved to Gebweiler, into the cloister they had built there for themselves.

units.la: Rex Rudolphus in Saxonia multa laudabiliter peregit.
units.tr: King Rudolf accomplished many praiseworthy things in Saxony.

units.la: Rhenus quater ante natiuitatem Domini inundauit.
units.tr: The Rhine flooded four times before Christmas.

units.la: Soldanus Babyloniæ Hierusalem & Accon, & omnia Christianorum penè totaliter expugnauit.
units.tr: The Sultan of Babylon almost completely conquered Jerusalem and Acre and all the possessions of the Christians.

units.la: Papa Nicolaus misit in adiutorium terræ sanctæ LX millia peditum proprijs expensis.
units.tr: Pope Nicholas sent 60,000 foot soldiers at his own expense to aid the Holy Land.

units.la: Domini de S. Ioanne dederunt in Brundusio omni volenti maria transire, ignem & panem & naulum & expensas, quas pro persona sua annus integer requirebat.
units.tr: The lords of St John gave to everyone at Brindisi who wished to cross the sea fire, bread, passage money and the expenses which one whole year required for his person.

units.la: Papa Nicolaus regi Anglorum supplicauit atq; mandauit, quatenus crucem ad transmarinas partes suscipiret: & vt hoc facere posset decimam omnium Ecclesiarum regni sui, fecit sibi per triennium fideliter ministrari. Hæc eadem faciebat regi Francorum.
units.tr: Pope Nicholas petitioned and commanded the king of the English that he should take up the cross for the lands beyond the sea; and, so that he might be able to do this, he had the tithe of all the churches of his kingdom faithfully administered to himself for three years. He did the same to the king of the French.

units.la: In Selestadio construitur ecclesia leprosorum.
units.tr: A hospital for lepers is built in Schlettstadt.

units.la: M. D. XCI.
XVIII. Calend. Februarij audita sunt tonitrua: noctu grando magna cecidit, & fulgura multa sæpe micuerunt.
units.tr: On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February (15 January) thunder was heard. In the night a great hailstorm fell, and many lightnings often flashed.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltstein congregato exercitu, dominum de Bergfen in munitione paruula capere voluit. Existentes autem in munitione Sermersheim, se viriliter defenderunt, tres occiderunt, & multos vulnerauerunt, eumq; fugere coegerunt.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein gathered an army and wished to seize the lord of Bergfen in a small fortress. But those in the fortress of Sermersheim defended themselves bravely, killed three, wounded many, and forced him to flee.

units.la: Eclipsis Lunæ, xv Kal. Martij, ante fratrum prædicatorum apparuit matutinas.
units.tr: An eclipse of the Moon appeared before the morning matins of the Dominican friars, on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.

units.la: Inuenta fuit in Hadstat manus integra, in modum iurantis, alio corpore putrefacto. Et cùm eam secundariò sepelire voluissent, guttæ sanguinis emanabant, & propter hoc eam secundariò sepelire noluerunt.
units.tr: In Hadstat a whole hand was found, in the posture of one swearing, while the rest of the body had rotted away. When they wished to bury it a second time, drops of blood flowed from it, and because of this they refused to bury it again.

units.la: Rex Angliæ omnes Iudæos regno expulit. Cædes Aureliani.
units.tr: The King of England expelled all the Jews from his kingdom. The slaughter at Orléans.

units.la: Archiepiscopus Colonensis excommunicauit omnes ciues & clericos ac religiosos, eò quòd cœperant eum in conflictu.
units.tr: The archbishop of Cologne excommunicated all the citizens, clergy and religious, because they had taken up arms against him in battle.
