units.la: Thuricenses M. D, Constantienses M. C C, Columbarienses D marcas, regi Rudolfo dederunt. Columbarienses præter hæc mille octingentas libras expenderant pro cibarijs & seruitijs dominorum.
units.tr: The people of Zurich gave 1,500 marks, the people of Constance 1,200 marks, and the Colmarians 500 marks to King Rudolf. Besides these, the Colmarians had spent 1,800 pounds on provisions and services for the lords.

units.la: Abbas Morbacensis cum monachis suis, vendidit regi Rudolfo Luceriam, pro duobus millibus marcis.
units.tr: The abbot of Murbach, with his monks, sold Lucerne to King Rudolf for 2,000 marks.

units.la: Gregorij, venit rex Rudolfus Columbariam. Dominus de Girsperg grauibus conditionibus à captiuitate liberatur: castrum totaliter deuastatur.
units.tr: On the feast of Gregory, King Rudolf came to Colmar. The lord of Girsperg was freed from captivity on harsh conditions, and his castle was utterly laid waste.

units.la: Bonifacius episcopus Bosoniensis, ordinis heremitarum, prædicatoribus Colmariensibus, Dominica ante Lætare, festo annunciationis, consecrauit altare beatæ Virginis, versus latus superius: Altare in angulo ecclesiæ beati Petri prædicatoris martyris: altare sancti Augustini.
units.tr: Boniface, bishop of Bosnia, of the order of hermits, consecrated for the Preachers of Colmar, on the Sunday before Laetare, at the feast of the Annunciation, the altar of the blessed Virgin on the upper side, toward the flank; the altar in the corner of the church of the blessed Peter, the preaching martyr; and the altar of St Augustine.

units.la: Maritus filiæ Rudolfi regis, mandauit regi Rudolfo, vt quàm statim veniret ad eum Lausannam, & vt indicet dominis Curiam Burgundiæ in Franckfurt: quod factum est.
units.tr: The husband of the king's daughter ordered King Rudolf to come to him at Lausanne as quickly as possible, and to tell the lords to hold the Burgundian court at Frankfurt. This was done.

units.la: Deinde vocatur rex ex Fråckfurt ad Lausanna, vt perficiat negotia domini Papæ.
units.tr: Then the king was summoned from Frankfurt to Lausanne, to carry out the business of the lord Pope.

units.la: Dum rex Rudolfus esset profecturus ad Principem, maritum filiæ suæ, comes Sabaudiæ insidias fecit regi, quem interimere volebat.
units.tr: While King Rudolf was about to set out to the Prince, his daughter's husband, the Count of Savoy laid an ambush for the king, whom he wished to kill.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus Curiam celebrauit, non ad suam per omnia voluntatem.
units.tr: King Rudolf held the court, but not entirely according to his own will.

units.la: Dominus de Hunnawilr à Columbariensibus interfectus, & de ciuitate plures milites expelluntur.
units.tr: The lord of Hunawihr was killed by the Colmarians, and several knights were expelled from the city.

units.la: Dominus de Napolestein incepit nouam monetam facere, quæ penè cum denarijs Friburgensibus concordabat.
units.tr: The lord of Napoltstein began to make a new coinage, which almost matched the Freiburg pennies.

units.la: Dominus de Horburc villam Richenwiler muro circumdedit & muniuit.
units.tr: The lord of Horburg surrounded the village of Richenwiler with a wall and fortified it.

units.la: Columbariam obsedit episcopus Argentinensis, cum xxx millibus pugnatorum, infra octauam natiuitatis Mariæ. Columbariæ erant tria millia pugnatorum.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg besieged Colmar with 30,000 fighters, within the octave of the Nativity of Mary. There were 3,000 fighters in Colmar.

units.la: Ventus validus partem pontis Brisacensis, x Calendas Octobris, destruxit.
units.tr: A strong wind destroyed part of the bridge at Breisach on the 10th day before the Kalends of October.

units.la: Obijt Marggrauius de Missen, iuuenis virtuosus.
units.tr: The Margrave of Meissen died, a virtuous young man.

units.la: Creuit vinum nobile.
units.tr: Noble wine grew abundantly.

units.la: Hermânus dominus de Napoltstein in Gemar castrû ligneû inchoabat struere.
units.tr: Hermann, lord of Napoltstein, began to build a wooden castle at Gemar.

units.la: Episcopus Constantiensis opposuit se filio regis Rudolfi, pro rebus quas abstulerat filio Comitis de Laufenberc violenter.
units.tr: The bishop of Constance opposed the son of King Rudolf over goods which he had violently seized from the son of the Count of Lauffenberg.

units.la: Domini de ordine Teutonicorum in Bůckhein, parant se ad prælia, vt res suas à dominis terræ defendant.
units.tr: The lords of the Teutonic Order at Bückheim are preparing for battle, to defend their goods against the lords of the land.

units.la: Consules Columbarienses dederunt ciuibus suis ligna pro domib. construēdis.
units.tr: The consuls of Colmar gave their citizens wood for building houses.

units.la: Rudolfus rex moritur. 30
units.tr: King Rudolf dies. 30 ## 1292

units.la: M. CC. XCII.
Ciues Columbarienses præposito Argentinensi, fratri episcopi Argent. de Liechtenberg fidelitatem & seruitia iurauerunt, & fideliter promiserunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Colmar swore fealty and services to the provost of Strasbourg, brother of the bishop of Strasbourg, of Liechtenberg, and faithfully promised them.

units.la: Episcopus Metensis obijt.
units.tr: The bishop of Metz died.

units.la: Sculteus Argentinensis & Zorno cum suis congregati armis inuadere voluerunt familiam Raginecк & Herbonum, propter verba quædam iniuriosa.
units.tr: The schultheiss of Strasbourg and Zorn, gathered with their men under arms, wished to attack the family of Ragineck and Herbon, on account of certain insulting words.

units.la: Hyems temperata usq; ad Purificationem: postea inualuit frigus, vt Rhenus Brisacì ex vtraq; parte pontis esset congelatus, quòd equis & bigis posset transiri.
units.tr: The winter was mild until the Purification, but afterwards the cold grew so strong that the Rhine at Breisach was frozen on both sides of the bridge, so that it could be crossed by horses and two-horse carriages.

units.la: Domini ordinis Teutonicorum, xiii. Cal. Maij, sabbato, exocularunt duos ciues Friburgenses. Iunior Comes cum ciuibus claustrum irruentes, totaliter deuastârunt.
units.tr: On the 13th day before the Kalends of May, a Saturday, the lords of the Teutonic Order blinded two citizens of Freiburg. The younger Count, with the citizens, rushed into the monastery and utterly laid it waste.

units.la: Prima Maij, electores reliqui electionem in Maguntinum tum præsente transferunt. Maguntinus comitem Adolfum de Nassow, cognatum suum, eligit: consentiunt reliqui. Hic statura fuit mediocri, agilis, amabilis, sciens Gallicum, Latinum & Germanicum.
units.tr: On the first of May, the remaining electors transferred the election to Mainz, which was present at the time. The elector of Mainz chose Count Adolf of Nassau, his kinsman, and the others agreed. He was of medium height, agile, amiable, and knew French, Latin and German.

units.la: Francofordenses expensas à rege electo petunt. Maguntinus obligauit pro rege castra ac villas, pro xx millibus marcarum. Rex exactionem in Iudæos tentauit, sed non potuit, resistente Sculteto Francfordiano.
units.tr: The Frankfurters demanded expenses from the king-elect. The archbishop of Mainz pledged castles and villages on behalf of the king, for 20,000 marks. The king attempted an exaction on the Jews, but could not, because the Frankfurt schultheiss resisted.

units.la: Rex liberos matrimonijs elocat.
units.tr: The king married off his daughters.

units.la: Equos phaleratos habuerunt, Maguntinus mille quingētos, Treuerensis M. ccc.
units.tr: They had caparisoned horses: Mainz 1,500, Trier 1,300.

units.la: Rex Aquisgrani coronatur.
units.tr: The king was crowned at Aachen.

units.la: Consilio procuratorum regni, procuratores in officijs retinet. Ottoni de Dehstein, nepoti ex sorore regis Rudolfi, Alsatiam, & quæ ab ea parte Rheni sunt, committit: Comiti à Rastenelnbogen, quæ ab alia parte Rheni.
units.tr: On the advice of the procurators of the kingdom, he kept the procurators in their offices. He entrusted Alsace and the lands on that side of the Rhine to Otto of Dehstein, nephew of King Rudolf through his sister; and the lands on the other side of the Rhine to the Count of Rastenelnbogen.

units.la: Ciuitates fidelitatem præfectis regis Adolfi promittunt.
units.tr: The cities promised fealty to the prefects of King Adolf.

units.la: Sculteus Columbariensis fidelitatem promittere recusauit: nisi aduocatus Otto de to de Ochsenstein promittat regis nomine, officium Sculteti ad vitam regis: expulsos non reducere: ciuitatem potenter non intrare.
units.tr: The schultheiss of Colmar refused to promise fealty unless the advocate, Otto of Ochsenstein, promised in the king's name: that the office of schultheiss would be for the king's lifetime; that the exiles would not be restored; and that the city would not be entered by force.

units.la: Aduocatus haec pollicetur, recepta fide, ne ciuitas Columbariensis alteri quàm regi Adolfo tradatur.
units.tr: The advocate promised these things, and having received the pledge, that the city of Colmar would not be handed over to anyone other than King Adolf.

units.la: Rex * Arragonum moritur: deuoluitur regnum ad Imperium.
units.tr: The King of Aragon died, and the kingdom fell back to the Empire.

units.la: Adolfus rex in Imperio omnes controuersias componit: Principes ad expeditionem hortatur. Episcopus Spirensis milites & LXX currus habuit, praeter bigas. Co-lonriensis ducetos milites cum equis phaleratis. Maguntinus copiosam militum multitudinem. Hi cum exteris iter dirigunt versus Vesontium.
units.tr: King Adolf settled all the disputes in the Empire and urged the princes to the expedition. The bishop of Speyer had soldiers and 70 chariots, besides two-horse carts. The archbishop of Cologne had 500 soldiers with caparisoned horses. Mainz had a large multitude of soldiers. These, together with the others, directed their march toward Besançon.

units.la: Vigilia Ascensionis, Albertus Dux mille quingentis equitib. venit Columbariam.
units.tr: On the vigil of the Ascension, Duke Albert came to Colmar with 1,500 horsemen.

units.la: Hermannus de Rapoltstein, secundo nonas Iunij, à ciuibus Argentinensibus fuit captiuatus, ad preces pauperculae mulieris.
units.tr: Hermann of Rappoltstein, on the second of the Nones of June, was captured by the citizens of Strasbourg at the entreaty of a poor woman.

units.la: Dux Austriae Albertus Turicensis obsidebat.
units.tr: Duke Albert of Austria was besieging Zurich.

units.la: Puer IX annorum Colmariae à Iudaeis interficitur.
units.tr: A nine-year-old boy was killed by Jews at Colmar.

units.la: Argentinae vicus pellipariorum per ignem totaliter devastatur.
units.tr: The quarter of the furriers at Strasbourg was utterly destroyed by fire.

units.la: Interfectus fuit in Rubiaco, frater Ioannes ordinis Minorum.
units.tr: Brother John of the Order of Minors was killed at Rouffach.

units.la: Albertus, filius regis Rudolfi, Dux Austriae, Landgravius Alsatiae, comes de Kiburg, obsedit Turegum potenter sex diebus: postea discessit, & obsedit castrum Nellenburg, quod expugnauit & fregit.
units.tr: Albert, son of King Rudolf, Duke of Austria, Landgrave of Alsace, Count of Kyburg, besieged Zurich vigorously for six days. Afterwards he withdrew and besieged the castle of Nellenburg, which he took and broke.

units.la: Episcopus Coloniensis reconciliatus ciuibus.
units.tr: The bishop of Cologne was reconciled with the citizens.

units.la: Fratres Minores ecclesiam suam magnis & altis columnis exaltabant.
units.tr: The Minor friars raised their church on great, high columns.

units.la: Fluentes aquas per plateas Argentinenses, artifex inuenit.
units.tr: A craftsman devised fountains flowing through the streets of Strasbourg.

units.la: Reginae regis Romanorum praesentatus fuit puer nutritus inter lupos: venit illa Brisacum, vigilia omnium Sanctorum.
units.tr: A boy raised among wolves was presented to the queen of the Romans. She came to Breisach on the vigil of All Saints.

units.la: Dux Lotaringiae castrum in Plummers super balnea constrvxit, vt defenderet balneantes à malis hominibus.
units.tr: The duke of Lorraine built a castle at Plombières over the baths, to protect the bathers from wicked men.

units.la: Aduocatus Alsatiae nomine reginae singulis diebus expendit duodecim libras, Basilienses monetae.
units.tr: The advocate of Alsace, in the name of the queen, spent twelve pounds of Basel money every day.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltstein accepit à hominibus suis, quintam partem vini, quod creuerat hoc anno: facit CCCCL carratas.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein took from his men a fifth part of the wine that had grown this year, which makes 450 carts.

units.la: In Hagenoia fuit torneamentum, in quo fuit miles à Scalario interfectus.
units.tr: At Hagenau there was a tournament, in which a knight was killed by Scaliger.

units.la: Adolfus rex venit Columbariam, ante natiuitatem Domini, anno bisextili BC.
units.tr: King Adolf came to Colmar before the Lord's Nativity, in the leap year BC.

units.la: Abbas Perisiensis capitur à suo subdito ordinis conuerso.
units.tr: The abbot of Pairis was captured by one of his subjects, a converted member of the order.

units.la: Castrum Ortinberg domino comiti de Liechtenberg episcopo Argentinensi tradebatur. Inuentor ac magister operis, quod in Argentina Bruscam fluere per vicos faciebat, de eo cecidit & expirauit.
units.tr: The castle of Ortenberg was being handed over to the lord Count of Lichtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg. The inventor and master of the work, who had made the Bruscha flow through the streets of Strasbourg, fell from it and expired.

units.la: Minera auri apud Heidelberg inuenitur.
units.tr: A gold mine was discovered near Heidelberg.

units.la: Comes Henricus, frater comitis de Friburc capitur, ac grauiter vulneratur.
units.tr: Count Henry, brother of the Count of Freiburg, was captured and seriously wounded.

units.la: Prope Schafusam atq; Basileam fuerunt inuenti lapides pretiosi.
units.tr: Precious stones were found near Schaffhausen and Basel.

units.la: Obijt venerabilis dominus Rudolfus de Habispurc, episcopus Constantiensis, frater comitis Gotfridi de Laufenberc, & in prandio vitam noscitur finiuisse.
units.tr: The venerable lord Rudolf of Habsburg, bishop of Constance, brother of Count Gottfried of Lauffenberg, died; he is said to have ended his life at dinner.

units.la: Natus fuit hermaphroditus in valle Keisersberch, id est qui membrum mulieris atq; virilia continebat.
units.tr: A hermaphrodite was born in the valley of Kaysersberg, that is, one who had both the genitals of a woman and those of a man.

units.la: Domini de Gisperc castrum Froberc furtiuè, expulsis habitantibus, obtinebant.
units.tr: The lords of Gisperc secretly held the castle of Frohburg, after the inhabitants had been expelled.

units.la: Eodem tempore, scilicet v Idus Iunij, aedificauit aduocatus terrae, scilicet filius sororis regis Rudolfi, castrum in Hartwille, vt castrum Ortinberg obsideret.
units.tr: At the same time, namely on the 5th Ides of June, the advocate of the land, that is, the son of King Rudolf's sister, built a castle at Hartwille, in order to besiege the castle of Ortenberg.

units.la: Ciuis Linthart nomine de Columbaria, in vigilia sancti Ioannis baptistae, cum octo viris armata manu Inclusorium de Horburc dicitur destruxisse.
units.tr: A citizen of Colmar named Linthart, on the vigil of St John the Baptist, with eight armed men, is said to have destroyed the Inclusorium at Horburg.

units.la: Castellum Watwiler & Zullisheim in praecedenti anno fuere inchoata.
units.tr: The castles of Watwiler and Zullisheim were begun in the previous year.

units.la: Castrum Ramstein prope Slecistat fuit inchoatum, à praefecto terrae contra multorum hominum voluntatem.
units.tr: The castle of Ramstein near Schlettstadt was begun by the prefect of the land, against the will of many men.

units.la: Iudaei Rubeacenses ob metum episcopi se in Columbariam transtulerunt, & Canwiren in Gebwilre turpiter capiuntur ab abbate Morbacensi.
units.tr: The Jews of Rouffach, fearing the bishop, moved to Colmar, and at Gebweiler Canwiren was shamefully captured by the abbot of Murbach.

units.la: In Rubiaca fuit interfectus .... miles dictus Zedelere, x v Calend Septembris, à dominis de Lobigasse fraudulenter.
units.tr: In Rubiaca a soldier named Zedelere was killed fraudulently by the lords of Lobigasse on 18 August.

units.la: In Rheno prope Brisacum submersa fuit navis cum hominibus LXXX. Mercatores venientes de Friburgo versus Brisacum, prope villam Alzinache, multa navis atq; multarum genera mortua invenerunt.
units.tr: In the Rhine near Breisach a ship with eighty people on board sank. Merchants travelling from Freiburg towards Breisach found many dead bodies and many kinds of goods near the village of Alzinache.

units.la: Vigilia assumptionis beatæ Virginis, duæ naves in Rheno, una prope Argentinam, alia prope Brisacum, cum multis hominibus perierunt.
units.tr: On the vigil of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin, two ships perished in the Rhine with many people, one near Argentina and the other near Breisach.

units.la: Item Rotwire exuritur, & multæ aves prope Brisacum frigore perierunt.
units.tr: Likewise Rottweil was burned, and many birds died of the cold near Breisach.

units.la: Sculteus Columbariensis vocavit dominum de Rapolstein nocte cum multis hominibus, & ei civitatem tradidit.
units.tr: The mayor of Colmar summoned the lord of Rappoltstein by night with many men and handed the city over to him.

units.la: Dominus Anshelmus de Rapolstein fratrem suum Henricum eiecit de Rapolstein, & cum omnibus suis bonis spoliavit.
units.tr: Lord Anselm of Rappoltstein drove his brother Henry out of Rappoltstein and stripped him of all his goods.

units.la: Æstas calida & sicca, & vinum bonum ut dicebatur generaliter abundavit.
units.tr: The summer was hot and dry, and good wine, as was said, was generally plentiful.

units.la: Rex Romanorum Adolfus, x v i Octob. quarta sc. feria, venit Rapoltzwire cum hominibus multis, & obsedit magna gloria violenter, in vigilia sancti Michaelis Columbariam.
units.tr: Adolf, king of the Romans, came on 16 October, a Wednesday, to Rappoltsweiler with many men, and in great glory he besieged Colmar violently on the vigil of St Michael.

units.la: Item Wilre castrum atq; castellum non valentes se defendere, regi se voluntarie tradiderunt.
units.tr: Likewise the castle and fortress of Wile, being unable to defend themselves, surrendered voluntarily to the king.

units.la: In vigilia Simonis & Iudæ castrum Werde facile expugnatur.
units.tr: On the vigil of Simon and Jude the castle of Werde was easily taken by storm.

units.la: De Rapolstein rex Romanorum recedebat, & circumduxit Sculteum Columbariensem in rota residentem, manum cum tribus digitis erectam habentem, ac periurium demonstrantem.
units.tr: When the king of the Romans was withdrawing from Rappoltstein, he led the mayor of Colmar around on a wheel, seated upon it, with his hand raised and three fingers extended, showing that he was a perjurer.

units.la: Dux Austriæ solennem Curiam fecit circa festum S. Martini in desponsatione filiæ suæ, & talis non fuit nostris temporibus celebrata.
units.tr: Around the feast of St Martin the duke of Austria held a solemn court at the betrothal of his daughter, and no such celebration has been held in our times.

units.la: In Lombardia apparuerunt in aere duo monachi parui, albus & niger, bonam horam se mutuo impugnabant, & postea in vallem & vastam solitudinem descenderunt, &c.
units.tr: In Lombardy two small monks, one white and one black, appeared in the air; for a good while they fought each other, and afterwards they descended into a valley and a vast wilderness, etc. ## M. CC. XCIIII.

units.la: M. CC. XCIIII.
Adolphus rex Romanorum in Landowe, in natiuitate Domini Curiam celebrauit.
units.tr: Adolf, king of the Romans, held a court at Landau at the Nativity of the Lord.

units.la: x v i i Kal. Februarij venit frigus tantæ fortitudinis, quòd multæ vineæ frigore perierunt: tiliæ & arbores aliæ fissæ fuerunt. Pisces in aquis, aves & homines in syluis pariter perierunt.
units.tr: On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February there came a frost of such severity that many vineyards perished from the cold; lime trees and other trees were split. Fish in the waters, and birds and men in the woods, likewise perished.

units.la: Abbas Perisiensis, circa secundum Nonas Martij ab officio remouetur.
units.tr: The abbot of Pairis was removed from his office around the second Nones of March.

units.la: Domus fratrum Prædicatorum fuit in Gebwilre recepta, & in Teutonia sex aliæ fuerunt pariter inchoatæ.
units.tr: A house of the Friars Preachers was received at Gebweiler, and six others were at the same time begun in Germany.

units.la: Dux Brabantiæ obijt, & filius eius miles efficitur, & ciues Colonienses eum sicut patrem eius, pro Domino receperunt: sed hoc episcopus Colonienis prout potuit impediuit.
units.tr: The duke of Brabant died, and his son was made a knight; and the citizens of Cologne received him as their lord, just as they had his father; but the archbishop of Cologne hindered this as far as he could.

units.la: Iudæi Bernenses puerum (vt dicitur) occiderunt.
units.tr: The Jews of Bern killed a boy, as is said.

units.la: Caristia magna fuit, & quartale frumenti pro octodecim solidis dabatur, & Sorores de Columbaria plus quàm trecenta quartalia, in vna sua grangia pauperibus erogauerunt, ante festum Mariæ Magdalenæ.
units.tr: There was a great dearth; a quarter of wheat was sold for eighteen shillings, and the Sisters of Colmar distributed more than three hundred quarters to the poor in one of their granges before the feast of St Mary Magdalene.

units.la: Venit circa Basileam ventus validus, fulgura, tonitrua, pluuiæ magnæ, quæ domus destruxerunt, & arbores magnas & fortes radicitus euulserunt.
units.tr: A strong wind came near Basel, with lightning, thunder and heavy rains, which destroyed houses and tore up large, sturdy trees by the roots.

units.la: Circa Pascha quidam de progenie Vrsina in ecclesia S. Petri, peregrinos vndecim occiderunt.
units.tr: Around Easter certain men of the Ursini family killed eleven pilgrims in the church of St Peter.

units.la: Decanus Columbariensis circa exaltationem sanctæ Crucis à Sculteto Columbariensi captiuatur.
units.tr: The dean of Colmar was taken prisoner by the mayor of Colmar around the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

units.la: In Basilea exustæ fuerunt domus penè sexcentæ, circa exaltationem S.Crucis,& homines ferè quadraginta.
units.tr: In Basel nearly six hundred houses and almost forty people were burned around the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

units.la: Apostata ordinis fratrum Prædicatorum sorores sub-tilia de Columbaria spoliauit.
units.tr: An apostate of the Order of Friars Preachers robbed the Sisters of Colmar of their small possessions.

units.la: Die S. Leodegarij abstulit Cesso castrum Lobeke à suis dominis fraudulenter.
units.tr: On the feast of St Leodegar Cesso fraudulently took the castle of Lobeke from its lords.

units.la: Rex Adolfus circa aduentum Domini terram Missinensem potenter ingressus est. Ciuitas Missina ei se tradidit, castella duodecim expugnauit, totam terram cum magna potentia deuastauit.
units.tr: King Adolf entered the land of Meissen with force around the coming of the Lord (Advent). The city of Meissen surrendered to him, he took twelve castles by storm, and he laid waste the whole land with great power.

units.la: Papa
units.tr: Pope

units.la: M. CC. XCV.
units.tr: M. CC. XCV.

units.la: Papa Celestinus papatum voluntariè resignauit.
units.tr: Pope Celestine voluntarily resigned the papacy.

units.la: Romanorum rex Adolfus expugnata terra Dominorum Missinensium, iter suū versus Alsatiam dirigebat, seq; præparabat ad eundum contra regem Franciæ, vt eum de rebus propriis extirparet.
units.tr: Adolf, King of the Romans, after storming the land of the lords of Missen, directed his march towards Alsace and made ready to go against the King of France, in order to strip him of his own possessions.

units.la: In Bara villa dæmon castrum Domini Wephimanni militis destruxit.
units.tr: In the village of Bara, a demon destroyed the castle of Lord Wephimann, a knight.

units.la: Rhenus qui longo tempore oppidum Brisacum ab Alsatia diuiserat: isto anno pro parte ad latus montis se aliud transferebat.
units.tr: The Rhine, which for a long time had divided the town of Breisach from Alsace, this year partly shifted its course to the side of the mountain.

units.la: Inundatio cuiusdam aquæ ad oppidum Rinueldin, quod est situ super Rhenum, 10 Claustrum dominarum de Olsperg repleuit, Molendinum earum destruxit, lapides & ligna in Rhenum cum magna violentia perducebat.
units.tr: A flood of a certain water filled the convent of the noblewomen of Olsberg at the town of Rinueldin, which lies above the Rhine. It destroyed their mill and carried stones and timber into the Rhine with great violence.

units.la: Item prope Basileam villa fuit Onezwire nomine, quæ à Basilea tria miliaria distabat, ac in valle sita erat, quam aqua transfire modica dicebatur. Pars montis in vallem cecidit, aquam obstruxit, quæ paulatim creuit, quòd supremam partem Ecclesiæ ab oculis hominum occultauit.
units.tr: Also near Basel there was a village called Onezwire, which was three miles from Basel and lay in a valley, which was said to be crossed by a modest stream. Part of a mountain fell into the valley and blocked the water, which gradually rose and hid the top of the church from people's eyes.

units.la: v Kal. Augusti, Fulgur pilos procuratoris Minorum in Brisaco combussit, corpore illæso.
units.tr: On 28 July, lightning burned the hair of the warden of the Franciscans at Breisach, but his body was unharmed.

units.la: Dominus de Ochsenstein cognatus & procurator ducis Austriæ, obsedit & expugnauit...... Et circa festum Mariæ Magdalenæ Zouingen cum magna homi-20 num multitudine dicitur obsedisse.
units.tr: The Lord of Ochsenstein, a kinsman and governor of the Duke of Austria, besieged and stormed ... And about the feast of Mary Magdalene, he is said to have besieged Zofingen with a great crowd of men.

units.la: In Alsatiæ villa Türinchen minera plumbi vel argenti repertitur, in qua ante paucos annos Gypsum pauperes inuenerunt.
units.tr: In the Alsatian village of Türinchen a vein of lead or silver has been found, in which poor people found gypsum a few years ago.

units.la: Adolfus rex Roman.circa Kalendas Augusti, cum exercitu magno terram Missinensium secundario subintrauit.
units.tr: Adolf, King of the Romans, about the Kalends of August, with a large army entered the land of Missen a second time.

units.la: Tertio nonas Aprilis, fuit in Brisgougia & Alsatia vehemens terræmotus.
units.tr: On 3 April there was a violent earthquake in the Breisgau and Alsace.

units.la: In Colmar vno hoc anno mortui pueri DCC septuaginta septem.
units.tr: In Colmar alone, in this year, 777 children died.

units.la: Terræmotus in Valesia quatuordecim castra pro parte destruxit,& crucem pinnaculi turris Ecclesiæ maioris deiecit, & in diuersis locis plurima deuastauit.
units.tr: An earthquake in the Valais partly destroyed fourteen castles, threw down the cross on the pinnacle of the tower of the principal church, and caused great damage in various places.

units.la: In Curia montes scissi, petræ fissæ sunt, plures campanæ pulsauerunt, quinq; ca30 stra penitus destruxit, plura verò fissa sunt, & domus multæ. Post hunc duos alij motus vna septimana plurimi retulerunt:
units.tr: In Chur the mountains were split and the rocks cracked; several bells rang; it utterly destroyed five castles, and it cracked many more, along with many houses. After this, many reported two other tremors within a week.

units.la: Romæ mortalitas magna fuit, & vno die sepulturæ septem episcopi tradebantur.
units.tr: At Rome there was a great mortality, and on a single day seven bishops were buried.

units.la: Mediocris staturæ persona regnum Teutoniæ circumibat, Imperatorem Fridericum se suis fidelibus referebat. Hic cùm in Esslingen venisset, à ciuibus capitur, hæreticus esse probatur, conuincitur & crematur.
units.tr: A man of middling stature went about the kingdom of Germany, presenting himself to his loyal followers as the Emperor Frederick. When he came to Esslingen, he was seized by the citizens, found to be a heretic, convicted and burned.

units.la: Domini de Gyrsperg reconciliati Columbariam in octaua Martini solenniter intrauerunt.
units.tr: The lords of Gyrsperg, now reconciled, solemnly entered Kolmar on the octave of St Martin.

units.la: Rex Adolfus in terram Missinensium stipendiarios transmittebat.
units.tr: King Adolf was sending mercenaries into the land of Missen.

units.la: In Alsatiæ valle Albrechtstal, in vna domo, Mulier perperit vna nocte duos pueros, duas vaccas, vtraq; duos vitulos, catus catulum, canis caniculum, scropha porcellos plurimos pariebat.
units.tr: In the valley of Albrechtstal in Alsace, in a single house, a woman gave birth in one night to two boys, and two cows each bore two calves, a cat bore a litter of kittens, a dog a litter of puppies, and a sow bore very many piglets.

units.la: 40 Quinquaginta fratres ordinis Minorum senes atq; lectores de Ordine pariter recesserunt dicentes, Fratres Minores de ordine S. Francisci simpliciter recessisse.
units.tr: Fifty friars of the Franciscan order, old men and lectors of the order, withdrew together, saying that they had simply departed from the Friars Minor of the order of St Francis.

units.la: M. CC. XCVI.
units.tr: M. CC. XCVI.

units.la: Dominus de Rapoltzstein fuit à captiuitate regis Romanorum post purificationem beatæ Virginis liberatus.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein was freed from the captivity of the King of the Romans after the purification of the Blessed Virgin.

units.la: Venerabilis dominus Petrus Basiliensis episcopus obijt, secundo Nonas Aprilis.
units.tr: The venerable lord Peter, bishop of Basel, died on the second day before the Nones of April.

units.la: Item venerabilis dominus Probus episcopus Tullensis ordinis Minorum fratrum obijt.
units.tr: Likewise the venerable lord Probus, bishop of Toul, of the Order of Friars Minor, died.

units.la: Filius Marggrauij Thuringiæ venit in Lombardiam, & quædam ciuitates eum Dominum acceperunt.
units.tr: The son of the Margrave of Thuringia came into Lombardy, and some cities received him as their lord.

units.la: Castrum Girsperg adiutorio episcopi Argentinensis reædificatur.
units.tr: The castle of Girsberg was rebuilt with the help of the bishop of Strasbourg.

units.la: Plures Tiliæ à fratre Bertoldo conuerso de Friburgo, sacrista, in Cœmiterio no-stro plantatæ fideliter referuntur.
units.tr: Many lime trees planted by Brother Berthold, a lay brother of Freiburg and sacristan, in our cemetery are reliably reported.

units.la: M. CC. XCVII.
units.tr: M. CC. XCVII.

units.la: Circa natiuitatem Domini, fuerunt cuidam clerico in ciuitate Basiliensi vitilia, propter quandam iuuenculam, detruncata, & suspensa in medio ciuitatis.
units.tr: Around the Nativity of the Lord, a certain clerk in the city of Basel had his genitals cut off on account of a young woman, and was hanged in the middle of the city.

units.la: Iudæus in anno præcedenti pro furto in Sulzematin per pedes suspenditur, qui octo diebus superuixit, & se eleuans super patibulum liberauit, sed præ læsione pedum fugere non poterat.
units.tr: In the preceding year a Jew, for theft at Sulzmatt, was hanged by the feet. He survived for eight days, and by raising himself up on the gallows he freed himself, but because of the injury to his feet he could not flee.

units.la: Cogente pestilentia atq; mortalitate, Columbarienses Canonici processionem cum reliquijs indixerunt, in vigilia purificationis. Circa tertiam ad ecclesiam homines religiosi ac clerici S. Martini conuenerunt, ac scholares & canonici cum cxx super pellicijs in principio processerunt: Fratres Minores eos sequebātur, cum quadraginta fratribus, deinde fratres Prædicatores hos cū triginta fratribus sequebātur; hos autem fratres domini de Hospitali S. Ioannis, cum decem personis venerandis sequebantur: sed monachi decem S. Benedicti fratres prædicatores præcedebant, & quandocunq; ad libitum sequebantur.
units.tr: Compelled by plague and mortality, the canons of Colmar appointed a procession with relics on the vigil of the Purification. About the third hour the religious men and clergy of St Martin's gathered at the church, and the scholars and canons with one hundred and twenty in surplices went first. The Friars Minor followed them, with forty brothers; then the Friars Preachers followed, with thirty brothers; and the lord brothers of the Hospital of St John followed these with ten venerable persons. But ten monks of St Benedict, the Friars Preachers, went before, and followed when they pleased.

units.la: Ad regem Romanorum Burgundi venientes supplicitèr deprecantes, quatenus à rege Franciæ defenderet, quia eos pro regno Arelatensi sæpius infestaret. Rex verò promisit, se ante festum Mariæ Magdalenæ venturum, & eos pro viribus defensurum. Ciuitates verò magnæ Franciæ, vt Remis, Parisius, & aliæ quàm plures portis fortibus & muris altis muniuerunt, quod vsq; hoc tempus confisi, de fortitudine facere contempserunt.
units.tr: The Burgundians came to the King of the Romans and humbly begged that he would defend them against the King of France, who was often attacking them on account of the kingdom of Arles. The king promised that he would come before the feast of Mary Magdalene and defend them to the best of his ability. The great cities of France, such as Reims, Paris and many others, fortified themselves with strong gates and high walls; having trusted until now, they had scorned to make any provision for strength.

units.la: In capite ieiunij, sc. tertio Kal. Martij, interfectus fuit Ioannes miles virtuosus, dimes, filius Sifridi Sculteti Columbariensis.
units.tr: In the beginning of Lent, namely on the third day before the Kalends of March, John, a brave and handsome knight, son of Siegfried the Schultheiss of Colmar, was killed.

units.la: Inchoatum fuit Dormitorium fratrum Prædicatorum in Columbaria.
units.tr: The dormitory of the Friars Preachers was begun at Colmar.

units.la: Diffidauit episcopus Argentinensis ciues Columbarienses, propter eorum Sculletum dominum de Bercheim.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg declared the citizens of Colmar outlawed, on account of their steward, the lord of Bergheim.

units.la: Mulier in Sclecistat peperit puerum cum duobus capitibus, cum dolore.
units.tr: A woman in Schlettstadt gave birth to a boy with two heads, with pain.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ filius Ottochari, Curiam ..... celebrauit, qualem nunquam aliquis regum, nec Assyrius, nec Salomon creditur celebrasse.
units.tr: The King of Bohemia, son of Ottokar, held a court such as it is believed no king, neither Assyrian nor Solomon, ever held.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis obsedit Mersmünstere ante festum Margaretæ.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg besieged Marmoutier before the feast of Margaret.

units.la: Translata sunt ossa ....... militis de Rubiaca in Columbariam ad fratres Prædicatores.
units.tr: The bones of a certain knight of Rappoltsweiler were transferred from Rappoltsweiler to the Friars Preachers at Colmar.

units.la: In Columbaria multa noua vina bona reperiebantur, in natiuitate S. Mariæ virginis gloriosæ.
units.tr: At Colmar many good new wines were found on the Nativity of the glorious Virgin Mary.

units.la: Rex Adolfus circa natiuitatem beatæ virginis Mariæ, D. Theobaldum comitem Phitretarum, Alsatiæ institui aduocatum.
units.tr: King Adolf, about the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, appointed Count Theobald of Pfirt as advocate of Alsace.

units.la: Comes Phitretarum descendit ad regem cum multitudine bellatorum.
units.tr: The Count of Pfirt went down to the king with a multitude of warriors.

units.la: Dominus de Lichtinberg fuit de Egenheim depraedatus.
units.tr: The lord of Lichtenberg was plundered at Ehenheim.

units.la: Rex Angliæ misit præcedenti anno regi Romanorum triginta millia marcarum, vt eiarmatos viros ad rerum suarum mitteret defensores.
units.tr: In the preceding year the King of England sent thirty thousand marks to the King of the Romans, so that he might send armed men as defenders of his affairs.

units.la: Ama boni vini in Sleziftat, pro octo denarijs vendebatur.
units.tr: An ohm of good wine at Schlierstadt was sold for eight pennies.

units.la: In decollatione Ioannis Baptistæ, venit rex Angliæ in Flandriam, cum quingentis magnis nauibus, cum sex millibus militum, cum equis dextrarijs, & tulit secum multam pecuniam quinque annis exercitui copiosam. Septem enim militibus marcam quotidie quinq; annis expendere potuissët.
units.tr: On the beheading of John the Baptist, the King of England came into Flanders with five hundred great ships and six thousand knights, with war horses, and he carried off much money, enough to supply the army for five years. For he could have spent a mark a day on seven knights for five years.

units.la: Vas vini dabatur in Alsatia pro Deo, vt vas euacuaretur. Vnum vas Rappes pro vase vacuo vendebatur. Pro conseruatione vini in locis pluribus stubæ præparabātur.
units.tr: In Alsace a cask of wine was given away for God's sake, so that the cask might be emptied. One empty cask was sold for a Rappen. In many places stoves were prepared for keeping the wine.

units.la: Rex Romanorum venit in adiutorium regi Angliæ cū equis bis mille phaleratis.
units.tr: The King of the Romans came to help the King of England with two thousand horses in trappings.

units.la: Filius Conradi Wernheri de Hadistat, miles iuuenis, rebus in aduersis virtuosus, contra regem Franciæ cum auunculo filio suo, comitis Phitretarum, armatus prosiciscitur, occiditur ab inimicis, traditus ab amicis.
units.tr: The son of Conrad Werner of Hattstatt, a young knight, brave in adverse circumstances, set out armed against the King of France with his uncle's son, the Count of Pfirt, and was killed by enemies, betrayed by friends.

units.la: Ludouicus rex Fraciæ canonisatur à Bonifacio papa, & festū eius celebrari debet in crastino Bartholomæi. Rex verò Bohemiæ canonisatus dicitur, in anno præcedēte.
units.tr: Louis, King of France, was canonised by Pope Boniface, and his feast ought to be celebrated on the day after Bartholomew. The King of Bohemia, however, is said to have been canonised in the preceding year.

units.la: In Columbaria equus fuit, qui formam in se mulieris marisq; comprehendit.
units.tr: At Colmar there was a horse which combined in itself the form of both a woman and a man.

units.la: Dominus de Bercheim Sculteus Columbariensis quondam de ciuibus expulit violenter.
units.tr: The lord of Bergheim, formerly Schultheiss of Colmar, expelled citizens by violence.

units.la: Domino præposito maioris ecclesię Constantiensis fratri sc. Comitis Friburgensis, sexaginta marcas in redditibus, quas habuit in Columbaria, per violentiā auferebat. Comes ex hoc indignatus, plures ex hominibus Imperij cepit, & eorū res & corpora deuastauit. Aduocatus autem terræ comes Phitretarum, iniuriam sibi illatam vindicauit, acceptisq; ciuibus Columbarien-sibus, alijsq; hominibus, terrā comitis Friburgensis potenter ingreditur, & vallem Glotyri & alias villas pro viribus deleuerunt.
units.tr: He took by force sixty marks in revenues, which he had at Colmar, from the provost of the greater church of Konstanz, namely the brother of the Count of Freiburg. The count, indignant at this, seized several men of the Empire and laid waste their goods and persons. The advocate of the land, the Count of Pfirt, avenged the injury done to him: taking the citizens of Colmar and other men, he powerfully entered the land of the Count of Freiburg, and they laid waste the valley of Glottertal and other villages as far as they could.

units.la: xv Kal. Decemb. colligebantur rosæ in Colūbaria, in horto fratrū Prædicatorū, & eodem die cecidit nix magna, & vsq; ad illum diem frigus modicum instabat.
units.tr: On the 15th day before the Kalends of December roses were gathered at Colmar, in the garden of the Friars Preachers, and on the same day a great snow fell, and until that day a slight cold persisted.

units.la: In Moguntia mulier vidua mulierem viduam & eius puerum interfecit, & in Rhenum eorum corpora deportauit: comprehenditur & crematur.
units.tr: At Mainz a widow killed another widow and her child, and carried their bodies to the Rhine; she was apprehended and burned.

units.la: M. CC. XCVIII.
units.tr: M. CC. XCVIII.

units.la: Idibus Februarij Columbarienses armati cum suis, vt res Argentinensis episcopi deuastarent. Comes Phitretarum aduocatus Imperij veniens eis in adiutorium, cū multis millibus rusticorum. Vallem Sulzmatin & villam Suntheim, & alias villas episcopi, per ignem, & tria Cœmiteria totaliter vastauerunt. Crucem quoq; Sanctam cum propugnaculis expugnabant.
units.tr: On the Ides of February the men of Colmar, armed with their followers, set out to lay waste the property of the bishop of Strasbourg. The Count of Pfirt, advocate of the Empire, came to their aid with many thousands of peasants. They destroyed by fire the valley of Sulzmatt, the village of Suntheim and the bishop's other villages, and they utterly laid waste three cemeteries. They also stormed the Holy Cross with its fortifications.

units.la: Friburgenses in Otinlandin hominum decem millia congregauerunt, & vt Bernenses in rebus destruerent, processerunt. Sed cùm distarent à Berna ad vnum miliare, Bernenses intellexerunt, & lætanter ac viriliter occurrerunt. Friburgenses videntes Bernenses, timuerunt, & terga vertentes fugerunt, & ea quæ secum attulerunt, reliquerunt. Bernenses multos Friburgensium ceperunt, & aliquos occiderunt.
units.tr: The men of Freiburg gathered ten thousand men in the Ottenland and set out to destroy property at Bern. But when they were within one mile of Bern, the Bernese learned of it and went out to meet them gladly and bravely. Seeing the Bernese, the Freiburgers were afraid, turned their backs and fled, leaving behind what they had brought with them. The Bernese took many of the Freiburgers prisoner and killed some.

units.la: Dominus Hiltibrandus dapifer de Pappenheim, vir iuuenis, fortis & diues, in exercitu ducis Austriæ, in treugis occiditur fraudulenter, & quinto Kal. Maij in Columbaria apud fratres Prædicatores solenniter sepelitur.
units.tr: Lord Hiltebrand, steward of Pappenheim, a young man, brave and wealthy, serving in the army of the Duke of Austria, was treacherously killed during a truce. On the fifth day before the Kalends of May he was solemnly buried in Colmar, among the Dominican friars.

units.la: Dux Austriæ venit in Brisgaudiam prope Kenzingen, ante festum S. Georgij cū Vngarorum Cumanorumq; multitudine, volens ad electionem regis Rom. peruenire, & vt eum deponerent, pro viribus laborare.
units.tr: The Duke of Austria came into the Breisgau near Kenzingen, before the feast of St George, with a multitude of Hungarians and Cumans, wishing to reach the election of the king of the Romans and to labour with all his strength to have him deposed.

units.la: Intelligens hoc Adolfus rex Romanorum cum multo meliore atq; maiore militia, cum multitudine copiosa hominum, ipsum velociter impediuit. Sed cùm rex Adolfus ad exercitum Ducis, propter aquam venire non potuisset, castellū Kencingin, à Domino de Vsenberc ad tempus pretio comparauit, vt ad exercitum Ducis posset quando vellet faciliter peruenire. Timens autem dux impetum regis, suis hæc pedítibus referebat: Hac nocte me Rinaugiam præcedetis, ego autem ad vos cras veniā festinanter. Sequenti die, circa tertiam, castra propria succendit, & suos pedites sequebatur.
units.tr: Adolf, king of the Romans, learning of this, quickly hindered him with a much better and larger army and a numerous host of men. But since King Adolf could not reach the duke's army because of the water, he bought the castle of Kenzingen for a time from the lord of Usenberg, so that he could easily reach the duke's army whenever he wished. The duke, fearing the king's attack, told his foot soldiers: "Tonight you will go ahead of me to Rhinau; I will follow you quickly tomorrow." On the next day, about the third hour, he set fire to his own camp and followed his foot soldiers.

units.la: Comes de Hegirloch procurator Ducis occiditur.
units.tr: The Count of Hegerloch, the duke's procurator, was killed.

units.la: Dominus de Haginecke capitur fraudulenter.
units.tr: The lord of Haganeck was captured by treachery.

units.la: Domina de Walchinstein, custos monasterij Sanctæ crucis, audiens regem Adolfum cum armatis in Alsatiam venturum, se cum rebus suis in Columbaria transtulit, & reliquias aliquas cum casula serica rufa, carmine hexametro texta, in qua beatus Leo cœmiterium Sanctæ Crucis & ecclesiam, consecrauit, fratribus prædicatoribus sicut suis fidelibus commendauit.
units.tr: The lady of Walchenstein, keeper of the monastery of the Holy Cross, hearing that King Adolf was coming into Alsace with armed men, moved with her possessions to Colmar. She committed to the Dominican friars, as to her own faithful, some relics, together with a red silk chasuble woven with hexameter verses, in which the blessed Leo consecrated the cemetery of the Holy Cross and the church.

units.la: Comes Phitretarum aduocatus Alsatiæ claustrum Sanctæ Crucis destruxit.
units.tr: The Count of Pfirt, advocate of Alsace, destroyed the monastery of the Holy Cross.

units.la: Rex Adolfus claustrum S. Marci & Schwarzin ..... deuastauit.
units.tr: King Adolf laid waste the monastery of St Mark and Schwarzin .....

units.la: Episcopus vero Argentinensis claustrum Eschowe dicitur deleuisse.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg is said to have destroyed the monastery of Eschau.

units.la: Ciues Hagenoenses dicuntur penè omnes villas ciuium Argentinensium deleuisse. Villam de Castineto, riuum de Schlezistat abstulerunt, ipsi autem potenter egressi Castinetum ignibus cremauerunt. Illi de Castineto de hoc doluerunt, Gallos adiutores suos vocauerunt, & potenter in Künigisheim perrexerunt, & illud per flammam totaliter deleuerunt. Illi verò de Künigisheim le congregauerunt, & illis de Castineto reditum præcluserunt, cum eis pugnarunt, & ex vtraq; parte quinque gladio perierunt.
units.tr: Almost all the citizens of Hagenau are said to have destroyed the villages of the citizens of Strasbourg. They carried off the village of Kestenholz and the stream of Schlettstadt, and they themselves, sallying out boldly, burned Kestenholz with fire. The people of Kestenholz were grieved by this, called the French to be their helpers, marched vigorously to Künigsheim and utterly destroyed it by flame. But the men of Künigsheim gathered themselves, cut off the return of the men of Kestenholz, and fought with them; on both sides five fell by the sword.

units.la: Rex Adolfus quarto Kal. Iunij ab obsidione Rubiacensium separârunt.
units.tr: On the fourth day before the Kalends of June, King Adolf withdrew from the siege of the men of Rouffach.

units.la: Rex Adolfus ab obsidione Rubeacensi in festo Barnabæ apostoli recedebat, & se in Eginsheim transferebat. Post festum Viti & Modesti, i xvi Kal.Iulij, rex Adolfus ab obsidione castelli Eginsheim recedebat.
units.tr: King Adolf withdrew from the siege of Rouffach on the feast of the apostle Barnabas and moved to Eginsheim. After the feast of Vitus and Modestus, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July, King Adolf withdrew from the siege of the castle of Eginsheim.

units.la: Mulier prope Columbariam virum interfecit proprijs armis, secunda die Iulij.
units.tr: A woman near Colmar killed her husband with his own weapons, on the second day of July.

units.la: Festo sanctorum Processi & Martiniani rex Adolfus interficitur.
units.tr: On the feast of Saints Processus and Martinian, King Adolf was killed.

units.la: Sanctam Crucem episcopus expugnauit.
units.tr: The bishop stormed the Holy Cross.

units.la: Castrum Gemer per ignem deuastatur.
units.tr: The castle of Gemer was laid waste by fire.

units.la: Ante assumptionem beatæ Virginis, venit in Argentinam Albertus rex Romanorum, & recipitur ab episcopo & populo solenniter & lætanter.
units.tr: Before the Assumption of the blessed Virgin, Albert, king of the Romans, came into Strasbourg and was received solemnly and gladly by the bishop and people.

units.la: In Vigilia assumptionis Mariæ exuruntur multæ domus in Argentina, & maius monasterium Mariæ virginis gloriosæ. 10
units.tr: On the eve of the Assumption of the glorious Virgin Mary, many houses in Strasbourg were burned, and the greater monastery of the Virgin Mary as well.

units.la: Mortalitas magna extitit, & comestio boum prohibebatur. Plebanus Brisacensis uno die homines xxxii communicauit, decem inunxit, vii flebiliter sepeliuit.
units.tr: There was a great mortality, and the eating of oxen was forbidden. The parish priest of Breisach communicated thirty-two people in one day, anointed ten, and sadly buried seven.

units.la: Octingenti currus atq; bigæ de Columbaria uno die egrediebantur, quando Rubiacum sub Adolfo rege obsidionibus grauabatur.
units.tr: Eight hundred carts and two-horse wagons went out from Colmar in one day, when Rouffach was being hard pressed by siege under King Adolf.

units.la: Castrum Landecke comes Friburgensis atq; ciues pariter obsederunt.
units.tr: The Count of Freiburg and the citizens together besieged the castle of Landeck.

units.la: Venerabilis dominus de Liechtenberg Argent. episcopus fecerat hoc anno, ante festum S. Michaelis milites, quos omnes vestiuit ad minus triplici vestimento, scilicet tunica pretiosa Surgorum ..... nobili vario Suchornam cum vario pretiosō.
units.tr: The venerable lord of Liechtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg, had this year, before the feast of St Michael, clothed his knights, each of them with at least three garments: a precious tunic of Surgorum ....., and a noble, varied Suchorna with precious varied cloth.

units.la: Pridie nonas Decembris, episcopus Argentinensis cum ciuitatibus Regis, cum exercitu terram Phitretarum Comitis intrauerunt. 20
units.tr: On the day before the Nones of December, the bishop of Strasbourg, with the king's cities, entered the land of the Count of Pfirt with an army.

units.la: Rex Romanorum in Nürenberg Curiam celebrauit, circa festum sancti Martini, ad quam duo millia militum peruenerunt.
units.tr: The king of the Romans held a court (diet) at Nuremberg about the feast of St Martin, to which two thousand knights came.

units.la: M. CC. XCIX.
units.tr: M. CC. XCIX.

units.la: Puer circiter xv annorum, factus frater ordinis Prædicatorum, & in ordine annum & plus quàm dimidium steterat in domo Columbariensi, in die sanctorum Innocentum, de consilio quorundam fratrum Minorum & auxilio eorundem ac Beginarum ipsorum, apostatauit, & se ad ordinem fratrum Minorum transferebat.
units.tr: A boy of about fifteen years, who had been made a friar of the Order of Preachers and had lived in the house at Colmar in the order for a year and more than half, on the day of the Holy Innocents, with the counsel of some Franciscan friars and the help of them and of their Beguines, apostatised and transferred himself to the Franciscan order.

units.la: Octaua Epiphaniæ venit Columbariam Alsatiæ aduocatissa cum pluribus dominabus, & dominus Ioannes de Liechtenberc, filius fratris venerabilis episcopi Argentinensis, aduocatus regis Romanorum super terram Alsatiæ, filius sororis Rudolfi de Habspurc Romanorum regis, de stirpe Ducum Zeringiæ, ferens in capite suo pileum ornatum auro, argento, lapidibus pretiosis, valentem plures marcas argenti: & cingulo circumdatus erat, qui ornatus erat auro, argento, lapidibus pretiosis, qui æstimatione hominum marcas valuit xl. 30
units.tr: On the octave of Epiphany the advocatess of Alsace came to Colmar with several ladies, and Lord John of Liechtenberg, son of the brother of the venerable bishop of Strasbourg, advocate of the King of the Romans over the land of Alsace, son of the sister of Rudolf of Habsburg, king of the Romans, of the stock of the dukes of Zähringen. He wore on his head a cap ornamented with gold, silver and precious stones, worth several marks of silver; and he was girded with a belt, adorned with gold, silver and precious stones, which by men's estimation was worth forty marks.

units.la: Obijt abbas Morbacensis, Albertus de Waldchinstein: successit dominus Bertoldus de Liebistein.
units.tr: Albert of Waldchinstein, abbot of Marbach, died; he was succeeded by Lord Berthold of Liebenstein.

units.la: Albertus rex Romanorum in purificatione Curiam celebrauit in Franckinfurt, sed in ea nihil consummauit, & propter hoc in tempus aliud protelauit.
units.tr: King Albert held a court at Frankfurt at the feast of the Purification, but accomplished nothing in it, and on account of this he put it off to another time.

units.la: Dominus Ioannes de Liechtenberc, filius fratris Argentinensis episcopi, aduocatus terræ Alsatiæ, dominam aduocatissam duci fecit de Alsatia, cum apparatu magno, in curru, quem procurator suus cx libras retulit constitisse. 40
units.tr: Lord John of Liechtenberg, son of the brother of the bishop of Strasbourg, advocate of the land of Alsace, had the advocatess escorted out of Alsace with great pomp, in a carriage which his agent reported had cost 110 pounds.

units.la: Dominus de Rinperch filium regis Adolfi de captiuitate firmissima liberauit.
units.tr: Lord of Rinperch freed the son of King Adolf from very strict captivity.

units.la: Dominus archiepiscopus Moguntinus in mensa sedes & lætus, velociter expirauit.
units.tr: The lord archbishop of Mainz, while seated at table and cheerful, died suddenly.

units.la: Episcopus Argentinensis exactionem super homines in Rubiaca posuit, & qui præcedenti anno libram dedit, isto anno marcam suo domino præsentauit: & quot libras quilibet anno præcedenti dedit, tot marcas soluere cogebatur. Insuper dominum Conradum Wernherum de Hadistat cogebat, Hadistat & alias res suas sibi voluntariè præsentare.
units.tr: The bishop of Strasbourg imposed a levy on the people of Rouffach. Whoever had given a pound the previous year was made to present a mark to his lord this year, and each person was forced to pay as many marks as he had paid pounds the year before. Moreover, he compelled Lord Konrad Werner of Hadstatt to present Hadstatt and his other possessions to him voluntarily.

units.la: Quarto Idus Aprilis, interdicta sunt diuina Columbariensibus, quòd noluerunt Basiliensibus iudicibus obedire. 50
units.tr: On the fourth day before the Ides of April, divine services were forbidden to the people of Colmar, because they refused to obey the judges of Basel.

units.la: Filius regis Adolfi oppositus est domino Archiepiscopo Maguntino, habens adiutores decem Principes, vicinos suos, terræ dominos potiores.
units.tr: The son of King Adolf was set against the lord archbishop of Mainz, having as allies ten princes, his neighbours, the more powerful lords of the land.

units.la: Comes Phitretarum à domino de Rotelsheim captiuatur.
units.tr: The Count of Pfirt was captured by the lord of Rotelsheim.

units.la: Rex Rom. Albertus abstulit ciuitatibus Imperij libertatem, quam habebat ciues, residentes in villis, quòd Dominis suis minimè seruiebant. Festo sancti Ioannis Baptistæ Columbarienses cum ciuitatibus Imperij cupientes Dominum de Horburc conculcare......
units.tr: King Albert took from the cities of the Empire the liberty which the citizens had, since those who lived in villages did not serve their lords at all. On the feast of St John the Baptist, the people of Colmar, together with the cities of the Empire, wishing to trample the lord of Horburg......

units.la: Dominus de <bl>Girsperg</bl> capitur.
units.tr: The lord of Girsperg is captured.

units.la: Post festum sanctorum Processi & Martiniani, Columbarienses armati, cum Imperij ciuitatibus exiuerunt, vt res Friburgensium deuastarent.
units.tr: After the feast of Saints Processus and Martinian, the men of Colmar went out armed, together with the cities of the Empire, to lay waste the property of the Freiburgers.

units.la: Bellum inter comitem Friburgensem & ciues Friburgenses.
units.tr: War between the Count of Freiburg and the citizens of Freiburg.

units.la: Interfectus fuit, qui Regi pecuniam deferebat.
units.tr: A man who was carrying money to the king was killed.

units.la: M. CCC.
Albertus rex Romanorum misit dominum Petrum episcopum Basiliensem Medicum, Romam, vt negotia quædam necessaria procuraret.
units.tr: Albert, king of the Romans, sent Lord Peter, bishop of Basel, a physician, to Rome to conduct certain necessary business.

units.la: xvi Kal. Februarij obijt Domina de Horburc, soror comitis Friburgensis.
units.tr: On the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February, the Lady of Horburg, sister of the count of Freiburg, died.

units.la: Albertus rex venit in Columbariam, septimo Kalendas Aprilis, receptus fuit solenniter cum religiosis & clero, & ciuibus vniuersis.
units.tr: King Albert came to Colmar on the seventh day before the Kalends of April; he was received solemnly with the religious, the clergy and all the citizens.

units.la: Tertio Nonas Iulij, hoc est quinta die, apparuit in crepusculo in Columbaria pluribus viris ac mulieribus sub Luna maiestas Dei, sedentis in cathedra, quasi in iudicio, habens de ore suo ex vtraq; parte gladium euaginatum procedentem ac populum atrociter iudicantem.
units.tr: On the third day before the Nones of July, that is, the fifth day, the majesty of God appeared in the twilight at Colmar, under the moon, to several men and women: seated on a throne as if in judgment, with a drawn sword coming out of his mouth on either side, judging the people fiercely.

units.la: Dominus de <bl>Haginecke</bl> castrum <bl>Haginecke</bl>, quod antecessores sui construxerunt, pro ....marcis vendidit, & dignitatem suam in extraneos transferebat.
units.tr: Lord of Hagenegg sold the castle of Hagenegg, which his ancestors had built, for ... marks, and transferred his dignity to strangers.

units.la: Bonifacius papa, ratione Iubilei omnibus venientibus Romam, tanta absolutionis beneficia contulit, quòd tantus factus fuit concursus Romam, vt sæpius vna die sint egressi triginta millia hominum, pariterq; ingressi, vt communiter pauperes reciperunt.
units.tr: Pope Boniface, on account of the Jubilee, granted such great benefits of absolution to all who came to Rome that such a crowd gathered at Rome that often thirty thousand men went out in a single day and came in again in the same way, and the poor were received in common.

units.la: M. CCC. I.

Circa Kalendas Iunij, cœpit Albertus rex Roman. infestare archiepiscopum Moguntinum, Coloniensem, Treuirensem, adiutoresq; eorum, & destruxit villas, castella ac castra eorum, sine conditione omnium suorum inimicorum. Ciuitatem Bingin obsedit potenter pluribus septimanis, & vsq; ad festum S. Michaelis non poterat expugnare.
units.tr: Around the Kalends of June, Albert, king of the Romans, began to harass the archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier, and their helpers, and he destroyed their villages, castles and fortresses, without terms for all his enemies. He besieged the city of Bingen powerfully for several weeks, and until the feast of St. Michael he could not take it by storm.

units.la: Ciues ciuitatis Bingin, sese Alberto regi Rom. septimo & sexto Kal. Octobris, cum Cometa se inspicientibus exhiberet, tradiderunt sub conditione.
units.tr: The citizens of Bingen surrendered to Albert, king of the Romans, under conditions, on the seventh and sixth days before the Kalends of October, when a comet was seen by those looking at it.

units.la: Præcedenti anno venit de Anglia virgo decora valde, pariterq; facunda dicens: Spiritum sanctum incarnatum in redemptionem mulierum, & baptisauit mulieres, in nomine Patris, Filij, ac sui. Quæ mortua ducta fuit in Mediolanum, ibi & cremata: cuius cineres frater Iohannes de Wilsenburc, ordinis fratrum Prædicatorum, se vidisse pluribus referebat.
units.tr: In the previous year there came from England a very beautiful and also eloquent virgin, saying that the Holy Spirit had been incarnate for the redemption of women, and she baptized women in the name of the Father, the Son, and herself. When she died she was taken to Milan and burned there; a brother John of Wilsenburg, of the order of Preaching Friars, used to report that he had seen her ashes with many others.

units.la: Iuuenis in Schlecistat in paruo riuo Rheni fuit submersus: is ante modicum temporis virginem violenter defloraverat.
units.tr: A young man in Schlecistat was drowned in a small stream of the Rhine; shortly before, he had violently deflowered a virgin.

units.la: Plebanus de <bl>Kechinhusen</bl> Canonicus Columbariensis, fuit morte subitanea pre-occupatus.
units.tr: The parish priest of Kechinhusen, a canon of Colmar, was overtaken by sudden death.

units.la: Item Vicarius in <bl>Volrahusen</bl> fuit lancea perforatus, quòd cognouit Beginam, contra parentis & matris ac fratris voluntatem.
units.tr: Likewise the vicar at Volrahusen was pierced with a lance, because he had known a Beguine against the will of her father, mother and brother.

units.la: Dominus Ioannes miles dictus de Nortgasse, contraxit matrimonium cum iuuencula de <bl>Habiftat</bl>, in festo Luciæ, bona vtriusq; voluntate.
units.tr: Lord John, knight, called of Nortgasse, contracted marriage with a young woman of Habiftat on the feast of St. Lucy, with the goodwill of both.

units.la: Sequenti die decollatus est iuuenis, qui filium nouercæ suæ fraudulenter occiderat, & ob hoc sibi ciuitas fuerat interdicta. Vxor verò eius in Rubiaca fuerat commorata. Hæc cum maritum intellexisset in Columbaria captiuatum, perijt cum dolore.
units.tr: The next day a young man was beheaded who had fraudulently killed his stepmother's son, and for this reason the city had been placed under interdict. His wife had remained at Rübach; when she learned that her husband had been taken captive at Colmar, she perished with grief.

units.la: In conuersione S. Pauli audita sunt tonitrua, & coruscationes plures, intra matutina fratrum Prædicatorum in Columbaria, videbantur.
units.tr: On the conversion of St. Paul, thunderclaps and many flashes of lightning were heard, and were seen, during the matins of the friars preachers at Colmar.

units.la: Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, archiepiscopus Coloniensis & archiepiscopus Treuirensis, Alberto regi Romanorum castrum <bl>Rinsperg</bl> post regis recessum obsederunt: quod vt rex intellexit, reuertitur, & episcopi recesserunt.
units.tr: The archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier besieged the castle of Rinsperg for King Albert of the Romans after the king's departure; when the king learned of this he returned, and the bishops withdrew.

units.la: Abbati S. Vrbani ordinis Ciftert. nasus abscissus à conuerso ordinis & duobus seruis.
units.tr: The abbot of St. Urban of the Cistercian order had his nose cut off by a lay brother of the order and two servants.

units.la: M. CCC. II.

Rex Franciæ fratrem suum Carolum, quem præcedenti anno in adiutorum papæ cum multis militibus armatis transmiserat, simpliciter reuocauit. Papa verò priuilegia domini regis Franciæ, nec non & principum eius cassauit, & totaliter dicitur deleuisse.
units.tr: The king of France simply recalled his brother Charles, whom the previous year he had sent with many armed knights to aid the pope. The pope, however, revoked the privileges of the king of France and of his princes, and is said to have wiped them out entirely.

units.la: In Spira ciues clericos expulerunt.
units.tr: In Speyer the citizens expelled the clergy.

units.la: In Brema ciues cum clero fortiter litigabant.
units.tr: In Bremen the citizens quarrelled bitterly with the clergy.

units.la: Tertia die post Philippi & Iacobi, venit regina regis Alberti in Columbariam, cum duabus reginis & apparatu magno, & subitò recedebat.
units.tr: On the third day after the feast of Philip and James, Queen Elizabeth, wife of King Albert, came to Colmar with two other queens and a great retinue, and then suddenly departed.

units.la: Ciues Bituricenses regi Franciæ in conflictu, vt dicebatur, DCC homines occiderunt.
units.tr: The citizens of Bourges killed, as was reported, 700 men of the king of France in a battle.

units.la: Beata virgo Maria cepit in Horburch/prope Columbariam, miraculis coruscare.
units.tr: The blessed Virgin Mary began to perform miracles at Horburg, near Colmar.

units.la: Nuncij Alberti regis Rom. de Roma venerunt & regi clausas literas portauerunt.
units.tr: Envoys of King Albert of the Romans came from Rome and brought the king sealed letters.

units.la: Isto anno fuit generale Capitulum ordinis fratrum Prædicatorum Bononiæ celebratum.
units.tr: In this year the general chapter of the Order of Preachers was held at Bologna.

units.la: Nocte ascensionis Domini pluit serpentes, qui vocantur Wasserkalb in Columbaria, & quibusdam aliis locis, in magna quantitate.
units.tr: On the night of the Lord's Ascension it rained serpents, which are called water-calves, in Colmar and in some other places, in great numbers.

units.la: In Remken castello puer circiter XII annorum interficitur à Iudæis.
units.tr: In the castle of Remken a boy of about twelve years of age was killed by the Jews.

units.la: Steimere ciuis Columbariensis à nobilibus de Hunnewir occiditur.
units.tr: Steimer, a citizen of Colmar, was killed by the nobles of Hunnewir.

units.la: Vitriman frater scutariorum in sacco submergitur.
units.tr: Vitriman, a brother of the shield-makers, was drowned in a sack.

units.la: Vigilia Osualdi, Rhenus inundauit, pontem Rheni læsit, pontem Brisacensem destruxit, montem* Augga circumdedit, claustrum sororum ordinis Cistercien-sis repleuit. Messem frumenti deuastauit, & maximum damnum in Brisgoia pauperibus inferebat. Argentinæ Rhenus intrauit cellaria multorum, & vnus ex ciuibus Lucium magnum in suo cellario comprehendit. Basileæ eodem tempore Rhenus equorum stabula introiuit, & eorum dorsa vndis perfundebat. Homines de Nuwenburch in Friburgum nauigio potuerunt peruenire, quod vsque ad illud tempus fuerat inauditum.
units.tr: On the vigil of Oswald the Rhine flooded: it damaged the bridge over the Rhine, destroyed the bridge at Breisach, surrounded the mountain of Augga, and filled the convent of the Cistercian sisters. It ruined the wheat harvest and caused great loss to the poor in the Breisgau. At Strasbourg the Rhine entered the cellars of many people, and one of the citizens caught a large pike in his cellar. At Basel at the same time the Rhine entered the stables of horses and washed over their backs with its waves. The people of Neuenburg were able to travel to Freiburg by boat, which until then had been unheard of.

units.la: Mulier prope Bernam in villa decem annis viro cohabitat, & cognosci à viro non potuit: iudicio spirituali à viro separatur. Romam proficiscens anno iubilæo Bononiæ à chirurgo cunnus eius scinditur: egreditur virga virilis, cum testiculis. Domũ reuersa vxorem ducit, opera rustica facit, cum vxore congreditur, legitimè & sufficienter.
units.tr: Near Bern, in a village, a woman lived with her husband for ten years and could not be known by him; by spiritual judgement she was separated from her husband. Setting out for Rome in the Jubilee year, she had her private parts cut open by a surgeon at Bologna: a male member came forth, with testicles. Returning home she took a wife, did farm work, and had intercourse with the wife, lawfully and adequately.

units.la: In natiuitate beatæ virginis capitulum prouinciale fratrum ordinis Prædicatorum fuit in Basilea, fratre Ioanne existente Priore atq; definitore, solenniter celebratum. Ad hoc Capitulum peruenerunt DLXX: ibi fuerunt lectæ literæ magistri Ordinis ipsorum, in quibus hortabatur eos suppliciter, vltrò eundum ad Barbaros seu in Græciam. Et non fuit vnus inter eos inuentus, qui hoc vellet facere, ad quod Ordo ipsorum principaliter fuit institutus.
units.tr: On the Nativity of the blessed Virgin, the provincial chapter of the Order of Preachers was solemnly celebrated at Basel, Brother John being prior and definitor. Five hundred and seventy came to this chapter. There were read there the letters of their Master-General, in which he earnestly urged them to go willingly to the barbarians or into Greece. Yet not one of them was found who would do this, which was the chief purpose for which their Order had been founded.

units.la: In hoc Capitulo fuerunt conuersi seu Begihardi, hoc est fratres non habentes domicilia, LXXX, in processione mendicantes cibaria.
units.tr: At this chapter there were lay brothers, or Beghards, that is, brothers without homes, eighty of them, who begged for food in procession.

units.la: Castellum Herlisheim prope Columbariam construitur.
units.tr: The castle of Herlisheim near Colmar was built.

units.la: Circa festum S. Michaelis, obsedit rex Franciæ ciuitatem in Flandria, habuit in exercitu suo LX millia equorum, & hominum multitudinem infinitam.
units.tr: Around the feast of St Michael, the king of France besieged a city in Flanders; he had in his army 60,000 horses and an endless multitude of men.

units.la: Albertus rex Rom. obsedit domino archiepiscopo Treuerensi ciuitatem, & habuit in exercitu suo quadringentos equos phaleratos, & hominum multitudinem infinitā.
units.tr: King Albert of the Romans besieged a city of the lord archbishop of Trier, and had in his army four hundred caparisoned horses and an endless multitude of men.

units.la: Nono Kal. Februarij & sequenti, perierunt vineæ, & magna pars frumenti, &c. & non fuit frigus ista hyeme, nisi his diebus prænominatis. Nec fuit calor æstate sequeti, nisi duob9 diebus, quibus fuerũt duo homines prope Rubiacã calore nimio suffocati.
units.tr: On the ninth day before the Kalends of February and the following days, the vines and a great part of the wheat perished, etc. And there was no frost that winter except on the days just mentioned. Nor was there heat the following summer except on two days, on which two men near Rouvray were suffocated by excessive heat.

units.la: Acre vinum atq; debile creuit.
units.tr: Sour and weak wine grew.

units.la: Eodem tempore, circa festum Martini, D. Brogilinus de Geroltsecke, cepit quatuor commendatores, i. magistros domorum hospitalis S. Ioannis, pro eo quòd emerunt castrum fratris sui, quod vendere non valebat.
units.tr: At the same time, around the feast of St Martin, Lord Brogilinus of Geroltseck seized four commanders, that is, masters of the houses of the Hospital of St John, because they had bought his brother's castle, which he was unable to sell.

units.la: In Westhusen carrata vini pro centum libris tali conditione vendebatur, vt vna libra annis singulis solueretur. Eadem carrata data fuit pro viginti libris. Tertia vice fuit data pro vinea, de qua duæ libræ denariorum quotannis soluebantur.
units.tr: At Westhusen a cart of wine was sold for one hundred pounds on the condition that one pound would be paid each year. The same cart was given for twenty pounds. A third time it was given in exchange for a vineyard, from which two pounds in money were paid yearly.

units.la: Clericus Columbariensis & clericus Basilien-sis pro canonicatu diu litigabant. In hac lite clericus Basil. interficitur. Propter hoc iudices Basil. diuina in Columbaria suspenderunt.
units.tr: A clergyman of Colmar and a clergyman of Basel long disputed over a canonry. In this dispute the clergyman of Basel was killed. Because of this, the judges of Basel suspended divine services in Colmar.

units.la: Albertus rex Romanorum circa festum Mar. Magdal. congregauit exercitum in partibus superioribus, & descendit versus Coloniam, deuastauit villas & res episcoporum, inimicorum suorum septendecim septimanis, id est vsq; ad festum Martini, dicens velle procedere versus Holandiam atq; Flandriam, & coegit episcopos componere secum. Rhenus tum apertus est, vt naues ascendere & descendere possent.
units.tr: King Albert of the Romans, around the feast of St Mary Magdalene, gathered an army in the upper regions and marched down towards Cologne, laying waste the villages and property of the bishops, his enemies, for seventeen weeks, that is, until the feast of St Martin, saying that he wished to proceed towards Holland and Flanders; and he forced the bishops to come to terms with him. At that time the Rhine was opened so that ships could go up and down.

units.la: Domini de castro Girsperc seniores, iuniores dominos de Girsperch grauiter vulnerauerunt, vnum occiderunt, castrū ceperunt, & plures de castro fugere coegerunt.
units.tr: The elder lords of the castle of Girsperc gravely wounded the younger lords of Girsperch, killed one, seized the castle, and forced many to flee from the castle.

units.la: A festo Thomæ vsq; post Epiphaniam ingens frigus. Die Stephani Bisuntij Dubis fluuius congelatus fuit, & homines glaciem ascenderunt, sub quibus glacies fregit, vt quingenti homines promiscui sexus pariter perierint. Brisaci etiā Rhenus cōgelabatur.
units.tr: From the feast of St Thomas until after Epiphany there was great cold. On St Stephen's day at Besançon the river Doubs froze, and people climbed onto the ice, beneath which the ice broke, so that five hundred people of both sexes perished together. At Breisach too the Rhine froze over.

units.la: Rhenus, quem rex Albertus aperuerat, vt omnis volens ascendere & descendere, poterat: hunc milites terræ clauserunt, vt nullus mercatorum ausus fuerit in Rheno amplius comparere.
units.tr: The Rhine, which King Albert had opened so that anyone who wished could go up and down, was closed by the knights of the land, so that no merchant dared to appear on the Rhine any more.

units.la: In Spira ciuitate ciuis diues meretrices cōgregauit, habitum eis pœnitentiæ tribuit, & cibaria ministrabat.
units.tr: In the city of Speyer a rich citizen gathered together prostitutes, gave them the dress of penitence, and provided them with food.

units.la: M. CCC. III.
Die S. Antonij, capella monachorum de Barhuß/ordinis Cistercien-sis, quæ nouiter fuerat constructa, dicitur solenniter consecrata in Columbaria.
units.tr: On the day of St. Anthony, the chapel of the Barefoot monks of the Cistercian order, which had recently been built, was solemnly consecrated at Colmar.

units.la: Ciues Columbarienses iura ac constitutiones plurimas fecerunt, & transgressoribus pœnas pro singulis conscripserunt. Insuper constituerunt, vt quicunq; Deum vel B. virginem Mariam blaphemiis vel verbis turpibus dehonestaret, decem solidos ad fabricā S. Martini dare cogeretur & mãsione ciuitatis tribus septimanarū priuaretur.
units.tr: The citizens of Colmar made many laws and ordinances, and drew up penalties for each of the offenders. Moreover, they decreed that whoever blasphemed God or the Blessed Virgin Mary, or spoke foul words, should be compelled to give ten shillings to the fabric of St. Martin's and be deprived of the city's company for three weeks.

units.la: Ciuis Basil. à domino Thuringo de Ramstein capitur, in castrū eius ducitur, Basil. insequuntur, & ab eis castrum eius velociter expugnatur atq; destruitur, ceperūt item intra decem hebdomadas quinq; castra fortia.
units.tr: A citizen of Basel was seized by Lord Thuringus of Ramstein and led into his castle. The men of Basel pursued them, and his castle was quickly stormed and destroyed by them; within ten weeks they also took five strong castles.

units.la: Carolus frater regis Fraciæ rex Siciliæ, rex Aragonū, & rex Fraciç confœderatur.
units.tr: Charles, brother of the king of France and king of Sicily, the king of Aragon and the king of France formed an alliance.

units.la: Frater Nibulungus cōuersus cū seruis, in cœmiterio nostro decē tilias plātauerunt.
units.tr: Brother Nibelung, a lay brother, with his servants planted ten lime trees in our cemetery.

units.la: In cœna domini rex Franciæ conflictū cum Flandrensibus habuit, & amisit quindecim millia hominum nominatorum, Flandrenses tria millia.
units.tr: On the Lord's Supper, the king of France fought a battle with the Flemings and lost fifteen thousand men of rank, while the Flemings lost three thousand.

units.la: Albertus filius regis Romanorum duxit vxorem comitis de Horngowe.
units.tr: Albert, son of the king of the Romans, married the wife of the count of Hornberg.

units.la: Capitulum fratrum Minorum (circa Vrbanum) fuit in Columbaria solenniter celebratum, comparuere illic c l fratres. Conuersi seu Begihardi triginta, bini & terni in processione per Columbariam transeuntes eleemosynam mendicabant.
units.tr: The chapter of the Friars Minor (around Urban) was solemnly celebrated at Colmar; one hundred and fifty friars assembled there. Thirty lay brothers or Beghards, two and three at a time, went through Colmar in procession, begging alms.

units.la: Henricus scolaris de Hohinberch meretrices congregauit, in domum cum magna diligentia clausit, & eis per mendicationem necessaria ministrauit. Et vestes lineas albas de filo grosso, & pallia breuiora, pro vestibus induebat. Decem vel viginti, vel plures in vna ciuitate in vnam domum claudebat, & eis necessaria prout potuit ministrauit.
units.tr: Henry, a scholar of Hohenberg, gathered together prostitutes, shut them up with great care in a house, and by begging supplied them with necessities. He clothed them in white linen garments of coarse thread and in short cloaks as garments. He shut up ten, or twenty, or more in one house in a single city, and supplied them with necessities as well as he could.

units.la: Festo Pentecostes, fratres ordinis Prædicatorum de Francia, capitulum generale in Bisuntio celebrauerunt, ad quod fratres ccc peruenerunt.
units.tr: At the feast of Pentecost, the Dominican friars of France held a general chapter at Besançon, to which three hundred friars came.

units.la: Octaua Io. Baptistæ venit venerabilis frater Bernhardus magister ordinis Prædicatorum in Columbariam.
units.tr: On the octave of John the Baptist, the venerable brother Bernhard, master of the Dominican order, came to Colmar.

units.la: Venerunt nuntij Alberti regis Roman. nuntiantes ei, quod D. papa prædicasset in manifesto, quòd esset verus rex Romanorum, & dilectus filius eius.
units.tr: Messengers of Albert, king of the Romans, came announcing that the lord pope had openly declared that he was the true king of the Romans and his beloved son.

units.la: Rex Arragonum composuit cum papa, & misit ei cathedram auream, & aureum scabellum ei fideliter copulato.
units.tr: The king of Aragon came to terms with the pope, and sent him a golden chair and a golden footstool, faithfully joined together.

units.la: Cardinales de Columna, qui se ad regem Arragonum contulerat, ad regem Franciæ se contulerunt.
units.tr: The cardinals of the Colonna family, who had gone over to the king of Aragon, went over to the king of France.

units.la: Tres abbates Cluniacensis, Cistercien-sis & Præmonstratensis à rege Franciæ capiuntur, quod noluerunt ei contra papam in suis constitutionibus obedire.
units.tr: Three abbots of Cluny, of Cîteaux and of Premontré were seized by the king of France, because they refused to obey him against the pope in their constitutions.

units.la: Papa regem Franciæ excommunicauit.
units.tr: The pope excommunicated the king of France.
