units.la: Rex Franciæ parlamentum in festo Ioannis Baptistę dicitur habuisse, in quo significauit, dominum papam in pluribus articulis fidei graviter excessisse. Solennis procurator regis Romanorum, quià <bl>Rinuelden</bl> vsque in <bl>Schlesiftat</bl> inclusiue dominabatur, in turrim in <bl>Ensisheim</bl> claudebatur, & rationem de sibi creditis reddere cogebatur.
units.tr: The king of France is said to have held a parliament on the feast of John the Baptist, in which he declared that the lord pope had gravely erred in several articles of faith. The procurator of the king of the Romans, who ruled from Rheinfelden as far as Schlesstadt inclusive, was shut up in the tower at Ensisheim and compelled to render account of what had been entrusted to him.

units.la: Hoc anno vinum bonum creuit.
units.tr: This year good wine grew.

units.la: Quarta feria post natiuitatem beatae Virginis, filia ciuis Basiliensis, qui dicitur de Sole, cum magna solennitate filio domini de Eptingen matrimonio copulatur.
units.tr: On the fourth day after the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin, the daughter of a citizen of Basel called "of the Sun" was united in marriage with great solemnity to the son of the lord of Eptingen.

units.la: Rex Franciae composuit cum Flandrensibus: reddidit enim eis Comitem dominum suum, & filium eius, & omnia quae petebant voluntarius admittebat.
units.tr: The king of France came to terms with the Flemings: for he restored to them their lord the count and his son, and willingly granted all that they asked.

units.la: Romae papa Bonifacius obiit, ante cuius domum rex Fráciae Ludouicus vexillum suum tribus diebus in signum victoriae dicitur suspendisse.
units.tr: At Rome, Pope Boniface died; before his house, Louis, king of France, is said to have hung his banner for three days as a sign of victory.

units.la: Sculletus de villa <bl>Stafrozhem</bl> bouem vicini suffurabatur: quod à vicinis non poterat occultari, nec aliquis eorum ausus fuerat propter malitiam hominis reuelare. Quidam autem ex suis ciuibus maioribus Argentinensium occulte reuelauerunt: qui egressi Sculletum ceperunt, & in patibulum suspenderunt.
units.tr: Scullet of the village of StAffrozheim stole an ox from his neighbours; since this could not be concealed from the neighbours, and none of them had dared to disclose it because of the man's malice, some of the leading citizens of Strasbourg secretly informed on him. Going out, they seized Scullet and hanged him on the gallows.

units.la: Archiepiscopus Treuirensis propter inobedientiam Confluentinorum obsedit eos cum quingentis equis phaleratis, & coegit eos vi, vt ei in omnibus obedirent.
units.tr: The archbishop of Trier, on account of the disobedience of the men of Koblenz, besieged them with five hundred horses in full trappings, and forced them by violence to obey him in all things.

units.la: Capitulum generale fratrum Praedicatorum celebratum Tolosae.
units.tr: The general chapter of the Friars Preachers was celebrated at Toulouse.

units.la: Episcopus Coloniensis obijt.
units.tr: The bishop of Cologne died.

units.la: Domini de Girsperc castrum suum episcopo Argentinensi tradiderunt.
units.tr: The lords of Geroldseck handed over their castle to the bishop of Strasbourg.

units.la: Domini de <bl>Hadiftat</bl> castrum <bl>Herinkein</bl> obsederunt, & villam igni tradiderunt.
units.tr: The lords of Hattstatt besieged the castle of Herrlisheim and gave the village to the flames.

units.la: Papa Benedictus post Pascha de Roma se ad ciuitatem Perusium transferebat.
units.tr: After Easter, Pope Benedict moved from Rome to the city of Perugia.

units.la: Dominus de Domo, ....... & domini de <bl>Hadiftat</bl>, militibus de <bl>Lobigasse</bl> suas possessiones cum potentia destruxerunt. Idem domini castrum <bl>Haginecke</bl> noctu cum scalis obtinuerunt, & totaliter succenderunt.
units.tr: The lord of Dom ....... and the lords of Hattstatt, with the knights of Lobsgasse, destroyed their possessions by force. The same lords captured the castle of Hagenau by night with ladders, and burned it utterly.

units.la: Rex Albertus venit in Columbariam, circa festum Viti, & abeis petijt marcas quadringentas.
units.tr: King Albert came to Colmar about the feast of Vitus, and demanded four hundred marks from them.

units.la: Flandrenses dominum de <bl>Henigowe</bl> & episcopum Traiectensem cepisse, plurimi retulerunt.
units.tr: Many reported that the Flemings had captured the lord of Hennegau and the bishop of Utrecht.

units.la: Albertus rex Romanorum mandauit militibus Alsatiç, vt in Columbariam venirent, & eum post festum Viti in armis expediti sequerentur.
units.tr: Albert, king of the Romans, ordered the knights of Alsace to come to Colmar and follow him under arms, ready equipped, after the feast of Vitus.

units.la: Venerabilem episcopum Basiliensem cepit Comes Montisfortis, causam rationabilem non habens.
units.tr: Count of Montfort seized the venerable bishop of Basel, having no reasonable cause.

units.la: Domini de Girsperc castrum suum Girsperc domino Henrico de <bl>Napoltstein</bl> tradiderunt tali conditione seu pacto, vt eis castrum quod dicitur <bl>der Stein</bl>, seu Lapis, in suam potestatem traderet, & omnes res & reditus in alios reditus transmutaret.
units.tr: The lords of Geroldseck handed over their castle of Geroldseck to Lord Henry of Napoltstein on this condition or agreement: that he should place in their power the castle called "der Stein," or Lapis, and change all their goods and revenues into other revenues.

units.la: Annus hic calidus fuit admodum sine pluuia: molendinis aquae deficiebant, hinc frumentum vile, panis carè vendebatur. Botri maturi in vigilia sancti Ioannis in Alsatia videbantur.
units.tr: This year was exceedingly hot and without rain: the mills lacked water, hence grain was cheap and bread was sold dear. Ripe grapes were seen in Alsace on the vigil of St. John.

units.la: Vir senex iuuenculam vxorem suam in <bl>Napolzwire</bl> noscitur occidisse. Mater propè Turegum filium occidit, quia eam cognoscere recusauit.
units.tr: An old man is known to have killed his young wife at Napoltzweiler. A mother near Zurich killed her son, because he refused to have intercourse with her.

units.la: Rhenus ob immodicum calorem tantae paruitatis erat, vt in pluribus locis inter Basileam & Argentinam posset transuadari.
units.tr: The Rhine, because of the excessive heat, was so shallow that in many places between Basel and Strasbourg it could be forded.

units.la: Albertus rex Romanorum Bohemiam cum maxima armatorum multitudine potenter intrauit, ad montes auri & argenti peruenit, & inde imperfecto negotio ad propria remeauit.
units.tr: Albert, king of the Romans, powerfully entered Bohemia with a very great multitude of armed men, reached the mountains of gold and silver, and from there returned home with the business unfinished.

units.la: Rex Bohemiae maiore multitudine armatorum in ciuitatibus mansit, & cum rege Romanorum congredi non audebat.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia remained in the cities with a greater multitude of armed men, and did not dare to meet the king of the Romans in battle.

units.la: Hyems diu durauit, vt stramen ouibus & alijs pecoribus comedendum praebe-retur.
units.tr: The winter lasted long, so that straw had to be provided for sheep and other cattle to eat.

units.la: Rhenus naues oneratas prae nimia paruitate portare non valebat.
units.tr: The Rhine, because of its excessive shallowness, could not carry laden ships.

units.la: Rex Romanorum Comitem de <bl>Wirtinberg</bl> dicitur obsedisse.
units.tr: The king of the Romans is said to have besieged the count of Württemberg.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: END.

units.la: CHRONICI DOMINICA- NORVM COLMARIENSIVM, PARS ALTERA,
units.tr: THE CHRONICLE OF THE DOMINICANS OF COLMAR, PART TWO,

units.la: Continens vberiorem narrationem rerum aliquot memorabilium, quarum in Annalibus concisa mentio fit.
units.tr: Containing a fuller account of several memorable events, which are mentioned only briefly in the Annals.

units.la: Rudolfi Habspurgensis ante adeptam regiam dignitatem res gesta.
units.tr: The deeds of Rudolf of Habsburg before he obtained the royal dignity.

units.la: OMNES Albertus de Habispurch/ de vxore sua liberos genuit..... Filia vna nuptui traditur comiti de Cussaberch/ altera in claustrum dominarum de Adelnhusen prope Friburgum, ordinis fratrum Prædicatorum, collocatur, in quo vitam suam laudabiliter consummauit. Vnum filium clericum fecit, eiq; beneficia plurima contulit, ied iuuenis de hoc seculo migrauit. Duobus dignitatem dominiumq; commisit, & ipse cum familia sua ad transmarinas partes trāsmeauit. Frater comitis Rudolfi Longobardiam intrauit, ibiq; capitur, & vitam suam in captiuitate miserabiliter finiuit. Comes Rudolfus se solum sentiens in dignitate constitutum, vidensq; vicinos suos comites diuitiis abundare: se autem respectu aliorum in paupertate constitutum: cogitauit quomodo posset diuitias comprehendere temporales. Considerans etiam quòd res magnas per preces aut iustitiam subitò comprehendere non valeret, deliberauit intra se, quòd vicinos suos vellet præliis impugnare.
units.tr: Albert of Habsburg had children by his wife, all of them: ..... One daughter was given in marriage to the count of Kyburg; another was placed in the convent of noble ladies at Adelhausen near Freiburg, of the order of the Preaching friars, where she ended her life in a praiseworthy manner. He made one son a cleric and bestowed many benefices on him, but the young man departed this life. He entrusted lordship and dignity to two of his sons, and he himself with his household crossed over to the lands beyond the sea. The brother of Count Rudolf entered Lombardy, where he was captured, and he ended his life miserably in captivity. Count Rudolf, feeling that he alone was held in high station, and seeing that his neighbouring counts abounded in riches while he himself was poor by comparison with the others, considered how he might lay hold of temporal wealth. Reflecting also that he could not quickly acquire great possessions by petition or by justice, he resolved within himself to attack his neighbours in war.

units.la: Natus est autem de progenie ducis Zeringiæ, anno M.CC.XVIII,.... Cal. Maij, eodem scilicet anno, quo dux Zeringiæ viam carnis ingreditur vniuersæ. Erat hic vir longus corpore, habens in longitudine septem pedes, gracilis, paruum habens caput, pallidam faciem atq; longum nasum, paucos habebat crines. Vir in cibo potu & in aliis moderatus: vir sapiens & prudens, & cum maximis diuitiis in summa tamen semper extitit paupertate. Multos habuit filios & filias, quos omnes constituit in magnas diuitias & honores.
units.tr: He was born of the family of the dukes of Zähringen in the year 1218, on the ..... of May, in the same year, namely, in which the duke of Zähringen entered the way of all flesh. This man was tall of body, being seven feet in height, slender, with a small head, a pale face and a long nose; he had little hair. He was temperate in food and drink and in other things; he was wise and prudent, and although he had very great riches, he always remained in extreme poverty. He had many sons and daughters, all of whom he set up in great wealth and honours.

units.la: Iis temporibus vixit iuuenis, dictus de Tuffenstein/ nobilis, diues, habes castrum quoddam in quo plurimum considebat. Huius res comes Rudolfus libenter habuisset, si eas comprehendere potuisset. Occasione igitur arrepta coepit iuuenem oppugnare. Sed cum eum vincere per potentiam non valuisset, pacem cum eo fraudulenter fecit, & per quosdam suos familiares insidias ei posuit, & hi eū turpiter occiderunt.
units.tr: In those times there lived a young nobleman, called of Tüffenstein, rich, who had a certain castle in which he dwelt for the most part. Count Rudolf would gladly have had his property, if he could have got hold of it. Seizing an opportunity, therefore, he began to attack the young man. But when he could not overcome him by force, he made peace with him by deceit, set an ambush for him through some of his retainers, and these shamefully killed him.

units.la: Post hæc coepit impugnare comitem Gotfridum de Lauffinberch / puerum virtuosum, filium auunculi sui, eiq; villas plurimas deuastauit. Comes vero Gotfridus mane cum ciuibus suis de Lauffinberch / Bruccum castellum adiit, apertumq; reperit, potenter intrauit, & omnia quæ ibi reperit, in castellū Lauffinberch cum gaudio trāsferebat. Multi viri cum mulieribus corporibus tantum euaserunt.
units.tr: After this he began to attack Count Gottfried of Löwenberg, a virtuous boy, the son of his own uncle, and he laid waste very many of his villages. But Count Gottfried, in the morning, went with his townsmen of Löwenberg to the castle of Brugg, found it open, entered it boldly, and joyfully carried everything he found there into the castle of Löwenberg. Many men escaped with only their bodies, along with their wives.

units.la: Comes de Kiburc filiam comitis de Sabaudia duxit vxorem. Videns autem se ex ea filios non habere posse, dignitates suas episcopo Argentinensi tradidit, tali conditione (vt quidam dixerunt) quòd comitissa quasdam res liberè possidere deberet ad tempus vitæ suæ, & postea dignitates ad episcoporum Argentinensium posteros deuenire. Mortuo vero comite de Kiburc / comes Rudolfus omnes penè res & di-
units.tr: The count of Kyburg married the daughter of the count of Savoy. Seeing, however, that he could not have sons by her, he handed over his lordships to the bishop of Strasbourg, on this condition (as some have said): that the countess should hold certain properties freely for the term of her life, and that afterwards the lordships should pass to the successors of the bishops of Strasbourg. But when the count of Kyburg died, Count Rudolf seized by violence almost all the properties and dignities,

units.la: Hartmannus senior comes de Kiburg. 1244. gnitates per violentiam obtinuit: cùm verus tamen hæres esse à pluribus negaretur.
units.tr: Hartmann the elder, count of Kyburg. 1244. although many denied that he was the true heir.

units.la: Erant in superioribus partibus nobiles Domini liberæ conditionis, filij sororis episcopi Basiliensis Henricis, qui cives Thuricenses & comitem Rudolfum aliosq; vicinos suos (vt eis videbatur) sæpius turbauerant. Eo tempore Comes Rudolfus quibusdam hominibus de Lombardia venientibus ducatum præstitit, vt possent in Alsatiam peruenire. Hi cùm prope dominium istorum Dominorum peruenissent, ipsis omnia quæ attulerât, abstulerunt. Comes Rudolfus super hoc indignatus, cives Thuricenses atq; alios amicos & vicinos induxit, vt contra Dominos de Tokinburc iuuarent, quod vellet eos fideliter vindicare. Qui gauisi, magnum sibi adiutorium promiserunt. Comes vero congregato exercitu castrum Vzinberc violenter obsedit, & reseorum alias deuastauit. Domini de Tokinburc se vt poterant defenderunt, & multis septimanis viliter tenuerunt. Et cùm multa mala passi fuissent, tandem eis victualia defecerunt, & castro derelicto cum corporibus recesserunt. Comes Rudolfus habito castro, destruxit.
units.tr: In the upper regions there were noblemen of free condition, lords, sons of the sister of the bishop of Basel, Henry, who had often harassed the citizens of Zürich and Count Rudolf and his other neighbours (as it seemed to them). At that time Count Rudolf gave safe conduct to certain men coming from Lombardy, so that they might reach Alsace. When these men had come near the lordship of those lords, they were robbed of everything they had brought. Count Rudolf, indignant at this, brought in the citizens of Zürich and other friends and neighbours, so that they might help against the lords of Tockenburg, since he wished to avenge them faithfully. They rejoiced and promised him great assistance. The count, having gathered an army, violently besieged the castle of Üsenberg and laid waste the surrounding farms. The lords of Tockenburg defended themselves as best they could and held out wretchedly for many weeks. And when they had suffered many evils, at last their provisions ran out, and, abandoning the castle, they withdrew with their persons. Count Rudolf, having taken the castle, tore it down.

units.la: Post mortem Imperatoris Friderici, imperij res, quas quilibet dominorum poterat, confiscauit. Obtinuit autem Comes Rudolfus de Habspurc Brisacum, & per tempus aliquod in sua tenuit potestate. Henricus episcopus Basiliensis dixit Comiti Rudolfo, quòd Brisacum suum deberet esse, eò quòd iure hæreditario possedisset. Comes vero dixit, si vellet ei dare M marcas argenti pro iure suo, promitteret castrum & castellum tradere in episcopi potestatem. Episcopus vero dedit DCCCC marcas, & sic obtinuit ciuitatem, quam habuit vsq; ad electionem Rudolfi in regem Romanorum.
units.tr: After the death of the emperor Frederick, he seized the imperial property which any of the lords could lay hands on. Count Rudolf of Habsburg obtained Breisach, and for some time held it in his power. Bishop Henry of Basel told Count Rudolf that Breisach ought to be his, because he had possessed it by hereditary right. The count replied that if the bishop would give him four thousand marks of silver for his right, he would promise to hand over the castle and town into the bishop's power. The bishop indeed gave nine hundred marks, and so obtained the town, which he held until the election of Rudolf as king of the Romans.

units.la: Cùm autem interim comes Rudolfus episcopum Basiliensem indebitè molestaret, episcopus Basil. accersito comite Rudolfo, dixit: Cognate, à vexatione mea quiesce, & tibi centum marcas argenti voluntariè ministrabo. Comes per illum annum voluntariè quiescebat. Sequenti anno comes Rudolfus episcopum coepit secundario perturbare: iterum dedit centum marcas, vt eum amplius non vexaret: & iterum à vexatione secundario desistebat. Tertio anno petijt comes R. ducentas marcas, eò quòd indigeret: erat enim multis debitis obligatus. Episcopus dixit: Verecundor esse de cætero tributarius.
units.tr: Meanwhile, when Count Rudolf was unjustly harassing the bishop of Basel, the bishop of Basel summoned Count Rudolf and said: "Cousin, cease my harassment, and I will willingly pay you a hundred marks of silver." The count remained quiet for that year of his own accord. In the following year Count Rudolf began to disturb the bishop a second time; again the bishop gave him a hundred marks so that he would not harass him any further, and again he desisted from the harassment for a second time. In the third year Count R. asked for two hundred marks, because he was in need; for he was bound by many debts. The bishop said: "I am ashamed to be a tributary any longer."

units.la: Post hæc coepit comes Rud. episcopum Basiliensem cognatum suum quantum potuit impugnare. Episcopus vero cum ciuibus Basiliensibus villam Bladolsheim, quæ sita est prope Rhenum, quæ tunc nouiter munita erat fossato atq; propugnaculis, potenter intrauit, & omnia quæ in eo fuerant, deuastauit.
units.tr: After this Count Rudolf began to attack his cousin, the bishop of Basel, as much as he could. The bishop, however, with the citizens of Basel, boldly entered the village of Blodelsheim, which lies near the Rhine and had then been newly fortified with a ditch and bulwarks, and laid waste everything that was in it.

units.la: Post hæc comes Rudolfus dominos de Tokinburc, filios sororis episcopi Basiliensis obsedit, & efficaciter impugnauit. Episcopus ex aduersum in odium comitis Rudolfi castrum Hertimberc, nouiter constructum & bene consummatum, euertebat. Deinde castrum Rinfelden, quod inexpugnabile videbatur, violenter obtinuit, & traxit in propriam potestatem.
units.tr: After this Count Rudolf besieged the lords of Tockenburg, the sons of the sister of the bishop of Basel, and attacked them vigorously. The bishop, in turn, out of hatred for Count Rudolf, demolished the castle of Hertenberg, newly built and well finished. Then he seized by force the castle of Rheinfelden, which seemed impregnable, and drew it into his own power.

units.la: Castellum, quod Seconis dicitur, quod tunc erat de dominio comitis Rudolfi, ignis, casu superueniès, exceptis duabus vel tribus domibus, deuastauit. Eorum enim peccatis exigentibus hoc eis creditur accidisse. Sanctus enim Fridolinus locum illum vsq; ad illud tempus custodierat, quòd nullus dominorum eos enormiter poterat infestare. Ciues vero loci illius non confidentes in domino suo S. Fridolino, pontem lapideum, quem ipse constuxerat, destruxerunt, prædas pauperum innocentum introduxerunt, & comessationibus & luxurijs insistebant. His & similibus peccauerunt, ideo perierunt. Indignationem enim suam S. Fridolinus duobus annis ante destructionem loci, pulsationibus quas faciebat in capsa, qua eius reliquiæ quiescunt, pluribus & multis vicibus ostendebat. Custos etiam ecclesiæ, domina de Gliers conditionis liberæ, solennis receptatrix fratrum Minorum atq; Prædicatorum & pauperum aliorum, dixit: S. Fridolinum filiabus suis Canonissis suis in somnis apparuisse, & indignationem suam sæpius ostendisse. Frater Hospitalis custos ecclesiæ S. Fridolini, qui in ecclesia semper iacuit eamq; custodiuit, infra duos annos sæpius eum se retulit audiuisse.
units.tr: The castle called Säckingen, which at that time belonged to the lordship of Count Rudolf, was laid waste by a fire that came upon it by chance, except for two or three houses. It is believed that this happened to them because of their sins. For Saint Fridolin had guarded that place up to that time, so that none of the lords could grievously harass them. But the citizens of that place, not trusting in their lord Saint Fridolin, destroyed the stone bridge which he himself had built, brought in the plunder of poor innocent people, and devoted themselves to carousing and debauchery. Because they sinned with these and similar things, they perished. For Saint Fridolin, two years before the destruction of the place, showed his displeasure many times over by knockings which he made in the casket where his relics rest. The custodian of the church, a lady of the family of Glirs, of free condition, a generous host of the friars Minor and Preaching and of other poor people, said that Saint Fridolin had appeared in dreams to her daughters, his canonesses, and had often shown his displeasure. A friar of the Hospital, the custodian of the church of Saint Fridolin, who always lay in the church and guarded it, reported that within the last two years he had often heard him.

units.la: Loco hoc destructo per ignem, venit venerabilis dominus Henricus Basiliensis episcoepiscopus & domos lapideas ac muros ciuitatis in locis multis deiecit, & omnia quæ ibidem reperit, deportauit.
units.tr: When that place had been destroyed by fire, the venerable lord Henry, bishop of Basel, came and threw down the stone houses and walls of the town in many places, and carried off everything he found there.

units.la: Venerabilis domina abbatissa, de genere comitum Phitretarum, post exustionem castelli, in claustrum & castellum rediit, reliquias sancti Fridolini reperit & accepit. Post hæc consilium iniit cum Canonissis suis, quid facere deberet, de reliquiis S.Fridolini. Tunc Canonissæ dixerunt: Si transtulerimus reliquias S.Fridolini ad locum solennem, scilicet in Basileam, tunc per violentiam episcopus & canonici retinebunt. Si autem fratribus Minoribus vel Prædicatoribus, vel aliis religiosis dederimus ad seruandum, ab illis episcopus auferet violenter. His consideratis dixerunt: Demus reliquias S.Fridolini alicui vicinorum dominorum, qui claustro nostro aliquo fidelitatis vinculo astrictus teneatur. Committerunt igitur comiti de Habspurc, qui eas in honestam cameram collocauit: insuper in ea noctis tenebras lumine decorauit. Quæ cum per breue tempus ibidem fuissent, indignationem suam ceperunt per pulsationem suam, familiæ demonstrare. Audiens hoc abbatissa, in Loufinberc ad Canonissarum collegium transferebat. Sed cum & ibi per tempus aliquod fuissent, indignationem suam per pulsationem suam Canonissis suis intimabat. Tunc Canonissæ cum suis reliquiis ad claustrum proprium redierunt.
units.tr: The venerable lady abbess, of the family of the counts of Pfirt, after the burning of the castle, returned to the convent and castle, found and took up the relics of Saint Fridolin. After this she took counsel with her canonesses about what they should do with the relics of Saint Fridolin. Then the canonesses said: "If we transfer the relics of Saint Fridolin to a famous place, namely to Basel, the bishop and canons will keep them by force. If, however, we give them to the friars Minor or Preaching, or to other religious, the bishop will take them away by force from them." Having considered these things, they said: "Let us give the relics of Saint Fridolin to one of our neighbouring lords, who is bound to our convent by some tie of loyalty." They therefore entrusted them to the count of Habsburg, who placed them in an honourable chamber, and moreover adorned the darkness of the night in it with light. When they had been there for a short time, they began to show their displeasure to the household by knocking. Hearing this, the abbess transferred them to the college of canonesses at Laufenburg. But when they had been there for some time as well, they made known their displeasure to their canonesses by knocking. Then the canonesses returned with their relics to their own convent.

units.la: Eodem tempore comes Rudolfus vt infestaret dominum Basiliensem Rhenum transire non poterat: unde naues quas in curru ducere poterat, fabricari fecit. Et quando voluit cum ipsis Rhenum transiuit, & hominibus episcopi superueniens improuisè eos sæpius grauiter infestauit: & post in eisdem nauibus per Rhenum rediens, eas ad tutiora loca in curribus perducebat. Videns comes Rudolfus, quòd per potentiam episcopo Henrico resistere nō valeret: militibus & ciuibus episcopi occultè dona tribuit & promisit. Milites episcopi comitem occultè & episcopum contempserunt. Intelligens hæc episcopus, cum propriis suis comitem inuadere non audebat. Sciens hæc comes Rudolfus vias suas sine timore, quò voluit, dirigebat.
units.tr: At the same time Count Rudolf, in order to harass the lord of Basel, could not cross the Rhine, so he had boats built which he could carry on a wagon. Whenever he wished, he crossed the Rhine in them, and coming upon the bishop's men unexpectedly, he often attacked them severely; afterwards, returning across the Rhine in the same boats, he carried them to safer places on wagons. Seeing that he could not withstand Bishop Henry by force, Count Rudolf secretly gave gifts and promises to the bishop's soldiers and citizens. The bishop's soldiers came to despise both the count and the bishop secretly. Learning of this, the bishop did not dare to attack the count with his own men. Knowing this, Count Rudolf directed his journeys wherever he wished, without fear.

units.la: Comes autem cum Basileam quadam vice pertransisset, intelligens hoc Marscalcus magister ciuium, ciues conuocauit, comitem Rudolfum prosequi faciebat. Ipse vero Marscalcus cum paucis persequitur fugientem, & cum quasi solus ad inimicos peruenisset, eum comprehenderunt, & velociter occiderunt. Post hæc liberè quò voluit, perrexit, quòd ciues Basilienses, propter infidelitatem suorum, eum inuadere non audebant.
units.tr: Once, when the count had passed through Basel, the Marshal, master of the citizens, learned of it and summoned the citizens and had them pursue Count Rudolf. The Marshal himself, with a few men, pursued the fleeing man; but when he had come almost alone upon the enemy, they seized him and quickly killed him. After this the count went wherever he wished unhindered, because the citizens of Basel, on account of the disloyalty of their own people, did not dare to attack him.

units.la: Comes Rudolfus exercitum congregauit, veniensq; Basileam colle Binningen ascendit: & Basileam obsedit, & ibi cum exercitu quinq; dies cum potentia morabatur. Episcopus vero cum ciuibus eum depellere nō audebat, q; ciues, quos amicos habuit, inimicos maximos reputauit. Verùm postea comes Rudolfus milites congregauit, obsidere Basil. ex alia parte Rheni volens, vt gloriæ suæ potentiam secundario demonstraret. Cùm autem plus quàm ccc milites congregasset in Brisgaudia, & cum prope Basileam potenter transitum facere voluisset, plures ex eis periculo se committere noluerunt. Comes verò se periculo comisit, cum ccc militibus prope Basileam pertransiuit, prædam secum tulit, & viam quam coeperat, adimpleuit. Basilienses eum insequuntur, sed eum comprehendere non valebant.
units.tr: Count Rudolf gathered an army, came to Basel, ascended the hill at Binningen, besieged Basel, and remained there with his army in force for five days. The bishop, with the citizens, did not dare to drive him off, since they regarded as their greatest enemies those whom they had counted as friends. But afterwards Count Rudolf gathered soldiers, wishing to besiege Basel from the other side of the Rhine, so that he might show the power of his glory a second time. When he had gathered more than 300 soldiers in the Breisgau, and wished to make a bold crossing near Basel, many of them were unwilling to risk themselves in danger. The count himself, however, committed himself to the danger, crossed near Basel with 300 soldiers, carried off booty, and accomplished the course he had begun. The Baselers pursued him, but they could not catch him.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CC.LXXXIII, venit in Basileam nuncius quidā, ab electoribus missus, dicens, se allaturum regem omnibus. Hic cum à Basilea ad comitē Rudolfum venisset, dixit: Electores vobis significant, quòd si volueritis filias vestras nuptui dare talibus dominis, in regem vos eligent Romanorum. Qui respondit: Hæc & quæcunq; alia implebo. Tunc literas electionis & confirmationis omnibus patefecit. Rex his visis, suis omnibus dixit: Pacem cum omnibus habete, & omnes captiuos restituite pristinæ libertati. His auditis atque visis, domini inuicem loquebantur: Viuat rex, & postea honorem regium sibi tribuerunt. Deinde cū vxore, filiis & filiabus ad Rhenum perrexit, & cùm in Rinueldiam veniebat, ciues eum velut regem cum magno gaudio receperunt, & castrum atq; castellum sibi liberè tradiderūt. Postea venit in Basileam, & illi eum laudabiliter receperūt. Post hæc venit Nidenburg & Brisacum, & illi eum honorificè receperunt, & necessaria tradiderunt.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1283, a certain messenger, sent by the electors, came to Basel, saying that he would bring the king to all. When he had come from Basel to Count Rudolf, he said: "The electors signify to you that if you are willing to give your daughters in marriage to such lords, they will choose you as king of the Romans." He replied: "These things, and whatever else, I will fulfil." Then he made known the letters of election and confirmation to all. When the king had seen them, he said to all his people: "Keep peace with everyone, and restore all captives to their former liberty." When these things had been heard and seen, the lords spoke among themselves: "Long live the king," and afterwards they bestowed royal honour upon him. Then he set out for the Rhine with his wife, sons and daughters, and when he came into Rheinfelden, the citizens received him as king with great joy, and freely handed over to him the castle and the fortress. Afterwards he came to Basel, and they received him with praise. After this he came to Nidenburg and Breisach, and they received him with honour and gave him provisions.

units.la: Has ciuitates & castella, dominus Henricus Basiliensis episcopus precio sibi comparauerat, vel per obsidionem obtinuerat, quae etiam episcopo libere seruiebant, & comitem Rudolfum, quantum poterant, impugnabant. De hac mutatione venerabilis dominus episcopus Basiliensis Henricus in tantum doluit, quod (vt dicebatur) mortis periculum incurrit. Omnes enim inimicos & persequutores regis Deus (vt dicebatur) de hoc seculo paulatim subtrahebat.
units.tr: These cities and castles Lord Henry, bishop of Basel, had acquired for himself by purchase or had obtained by siege; they were also serving the bishop freely, and were attacking Count Rudolf as far as they were able. Over this change the venerable Lord Henry, bishop of Basel, grieved so much that (as was said) he incurred danger of death. For God (as was said) was gradually removing from this world all the enemies and persecutors of the king.

units.la: De electione & inauguratione Rudolfi regis Romanorum.
units.tr: On the election and inauguration of Rudolf, king of the Romans.

units.la: DOMINVS de Clingen, vir liberae conditionis, personatus, diues & deuotus: vidit principes & electores imperij congregatos & dicentes: Quicunq; ex nobis hanc coronam leuare poterit, rex ab omnibus habebitur. Singulis autem se probantibus, nullus eorum leuare potuit eam. Tandem Rudolfus de Habspurc comes, coronam potenter eleuauit, seq; coronauit. Visionem hanc euentus subsequens approbauit: eligitur enim in crastino Michaelis, anno M. CC. LXXXIII. Tum igitur captiuos omnes, etiam perpetuo carceri deputatos, pristinae restituit libertati. Venit Maguntiam: hic praesentantur ei Regalia, quae praedecessores reges magna pecunia non poterant obtinere. Hinc Aquisgranum. Multitudinem hominum strata publica vsq; ad tria milliaria vix commode recipiebant. Occurrunt dux Bauariae, Saxoniae & alij cum xx millibus equitum. Panis modicus duobus denariis vendebatur, sextarius auenae pro decem Colonienfibus.
units.tr: Lord von Klingen, a man of free condition, a holder of a benefice, wealthy and devout, saw the princes and electors of the empire gathered and saying: "Whichever of us can lift this crown, shall be held king by all." But when each tried himself, none of them could lift it. At last Count Rudolf of Habsburg lifted the crown powerfully and crowned himself. The event that followed confirmed this vision: he was elected on the day after Michaelmas, in the year 1283. Then he restored to their former liberty all the captives, even those assigned to perpetual prison. He came to Mainz; here the regalia were presented to him, which earlier kings could not obtain even with great sums of money. Thence to Aachen. The crowd of people could scarcely be conveniently received along the public road for three miles. The Duke of Bavaria, the Duke of Saxony and others came to meet him with 20,000 horsemen. Bread was sold at two pennies for a small loaf, and a measure of oats for ten Cologne pennies.

units.la: Vxor Rudolfi, filia Burchardi de Hohenberc, quando rex misit pro ea, domum regebat in Brucco, descendit per Rhenum, & venit in Buken, ad viros religiosos, prouidos & honestos, de domo Teutonica: à quibus honorifice recipitur, necessariis abundanter administratis. Ciues Rinfeldenses eo communiter occurrerunt, & xenia plurima detulerunt: promittentes, se ei pro posse rebus & corpore in omnibus obedire.
units.tr: Rudolf's wife, daughter of Burkhard of Hohenberg, when the king sent for her, was living at Brugg; she went down the Rhine and came to Büren, to the religious men, prudent and honest, of the German house; there she was received with honour, and necessities were supplied abundantly. The citizens of Rheinfelden went out to meet her in a body and brought many gifts, promising that they would obey her in all things, with their goods and their persons, as far as they were able.

units.la: Basileam venit, quarto idus Octobris: magno comitatu recipitur à ciuibus, canonicis & omnibus religiosis, cum reliquiis & magna reuerentia. Dantur ei expensae & xenia multa. Descendit multis nauibus ad regem, vt cum ipso coronaretur. Columbarienses duodecim vasa vini optimi, Argentinenses sexaginta, & nauem magnam plenam frumento, obtulerunt. Ciuitates imperij omnes reginam honorifice suscipiunt, munera & xenia offerentes.
units.tr: She came to Basel on the fourth day before the Ides of October: she was received with a great retinue by the citizens, canons and all the religious, with relics and great reverence. Expenses and many gifts were given to her. She descended to the king in many boats, so that she might be crowned with him. The people of Colmar offered twelve vessels of the best wine, the people of Strasbourg sixty, and a large ship full of grain. All the cities of the empire received the queen with honour, offering gifts and presents.

units.la: In vigilia omnium Sanctorum Rudolfus rex coronatur: & tum spatio horae apparuit nubes candida, in modum crucis formata, quae postea in ruborem sanguinis est transformata. Cùm principes hoc regi retulissent, dixit Rudolfus: Si Dominus mihi vitam prosperitatemq; dederit, transmarinas partes adibo, & pro peccatis meis maximis sanguinem meum consecrabo domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: On the vigil of All Saints, King Rudolf was crowned; and at that time, for the space of an hour, a white cloud appeared, formed in the shape of a cross, which afterwards was changed into the redness of blood. When the princes had reported this to the king, Rudolf said: "If the Lord grants me life and prosperity, I will go to the lands across the sea, and for my very great sins I will consecrate my blood to the Lord Jesus Christ."

units.la: De quibusdam Rudolfi regis liberis.
units.tr: On certain children of King Rudolf.

units.la: ANNO M. CC. LXXVI, puer quinq; annorum filius Rudolfi regis, acutis febribus laborabat, sed statim restitutus est sanitati. Hic iusserat vestes pauperibus elargiri, & baldicum cuidam inclusae.
units.tr: In the year 1276 a boy of five, son of King Rudolf, suffered from acute fevers, but was at once restored to health. The king had ordered clothing to be given to the poor, and a canopy to a certain recluse.

units.la: Eodem anno vxor Rudolphi filium peperit in Rinfeldia: episcopum Constantiensem cognatum regis, vt eundem baptizaret, vocauit. Episcopus igitur Constantiensis sabbato paschae missam celebrauit, & baptismum benedixit. Frater Hartmannus socius Prioris Praedicatorum Basilienfium Euangelium, Et exultet iam, &c. decantauit. Episcopus puerum baptizauit. Alexander lector praedicatorum Constantiensium de sacro fonte leuauit. Frater Henricus alter leuantium fuit, qui & reginae medicus & amicus extitit. Puer hic paucis septimanis postea obiit, sepultus in choro Basiliensis ecclesiae. Exequiis interfuerant omnes clerici & religiosi, milites, ciues honestiores, familia reginae penè cum mulieribus vniuersis. Feretrum cooperturn fuit baldichino, quod ecclesiae reliquerunt.
units.tr: In the same year Rudolf's wife bore a son at Rheinfelden, and she summoned the bishop of Constance, the king's kinsman, to baptize him. So the bishop of Constance celebrated Mass on Easter Saturday and blessed the baptismal water. Brother Hartmann, companion of the Prior of the Preachers at Basel, sang the Exsultet, Et exultet iam, &c. The bishop baptized the boy. Alexander, lector of the Preachers at Constance, stood as sponsor at the holy font. Brother Henry, the other sponsor, was also the queen's physician and friend. This boy died a few weeks later and was buried in the choir of the church at Basel. All the clergy and religious, the soldiers, the more respectable citizens, and almost the whole of the queen's household, including all the women, attended the funeral. The bier was covered with the canopy, which they left to the church.

units.la: Regis Ottocari ortus, adolescentia, regni primordia, coniugia.
units.tr: The birth, youth, beginning of the reign and marriages of King Ottokar.

units.la: ANNO M.CC.XXX, rex Bohemiæ Ottocarus, cuius auus dux fuerat, in regem sub-limatur. Hic ex vno parente Teutonicus fuit. Huius vxor cùm puerum concepisset, somnium habuit, se lupum pro puero concepisse. Hic lupus terram Bohemiæ sibi subiugauit, ac terras vicinas sua potentia deuorauit. Hunc lupum deinde leo superueniens, suis vnguibus dirupit, ac bona eius occupauit.
units.tr: In the year 1230 Ottokar, king of Bohemia, whose grandfather had been duke, was raised to the kingship. He was German on one parent's side. When his mother was pregnant with him, she dreamed that she had conceived a wolf instead of a child. This wolf subjected the land of Bohemia to himself and, by his power, devoured the neighbouring lands. Then a lion came upon this wolf, tore him with its claws, and seized his possessions.

units.la: Natus est postmodum regi Bohemiæ filius, quem tenerrime dilexit. Hic erat iuuenis pulcher, fusco colore, statura mediocriter longa, pectore magno, ore amplo, fortis, sapiens, eloquentia sapientes & Philosophos præcellens. Huic pater vxorem dedit, & Marchionem in Merrhen constituit. Hic iuuenis regnum patris affectans, patrem tandem regno excedere coegit. Pater auxilio Marchionum Brandeburgensium & Misenensium ciuitatem …… & filium cum exercitu obsederunt. Filius ex ciuitate fugit, & regnum post hæc patri reliquit. Post hæc multiplicati sunt in Bohemia Teutonici: per hos rex ingentes diuitias collegit, ex auri & argenti fodinis.
units.tr: Afterwards a son was born to the king of Bohemia, whom he loved most tenderly. This young man was handsome, of dark complexion, of moderately tall stature, with a broad chest and a large mouth; he was strong and wise, and surpassed the wise and the philosophers in eloquence. His father gave him a wife and appointed him margrave in Moravia. This young man, aspiring to his father's kingdom, finally forced his father to give up the kingdom. With the help of the margraves of Brandenburg and Meissen, the father besieged a city ... and his son with his army. The son fled from the city and afterwards left the kingdom to his father. After this the Germans multiplied in Bohemia, and through them the king gathered great riches from the gold and silver mines.

units.la: Mortuo hoc rege, filius regnum occupauit, Teutones expellit, nobiles impugnat, vicinos subiugat. Hinc factus inuisus multis, fideles famulos paucos habebat. Huius vxor absque liberis mortua est. Rex ter dispensationem obtinuit à papa, vt matrimonium contraheret cum sorore Margareta, regina quondam Teutoniæ, mo-niali in claustro fratrum Prædicatorum apud Treuerim. Paucis annis post per hanc Austriam possedit. Cum liberos ex ea non haberet, petiit ab episcopis licentiam cum alia contrahendi. Cui episcopi responderunt: Quos Deus coniunxit homo non separet. Rex ei ciuitatem …. cum redditibus assignauit, in qua regina quasi vidua relidebat, ac paucis annis postea mortua est. Rex Cumani cuiusdam duxit vxorem, cum qua multos filios & filias procreauit. Rex de vxoribus suis multas terras habuit: turres plenas au-ro & argento collegisse, ac hostes ferè omnes vicisse dicebatur.
units.tr: When this king died, his son seized the kingdom, expelled the Germans, attacked the nobles and subjected his neighbours. Made hateful to many because of this, he had few faithful servants. His wife died without children. The king obtained three dispensations from the pope to marry his sister Margaret, formerly queen of Germany, a nun in the Dominican convent at Trier. A few years later he possessed Austria through her. Since he had no children by her, he asked the bishops for permission to marry another woman. The bishops replied: "Whom God has joined, let no man separate." The king assigned her a city ... with its revenues, where the queen lived on as a kind of widow, and she died a few years later. The king married the wife of a certain Cuman, with whom he had many sons and daughters. The king was said to have acquired many lands through his wives, to have gathered towers full of gold and silver, and to have conquered almost all his enemies.

units.la: Ortus & progressus belli gesti à Rudolfo Cæsare contra Ottocarum Bohemiæ regem.
units.tr: The origin and course of the war waged by Rudolf, Caesar, against Ottokar, king of Bohemia.

units.la: RVDOLFO rege à ciuitatibus suscepto, & in Teutonia pace facta, nobiles qui erat de regis Bohemiæ ditione, gauisi sunt multùm, sperantes à regis Bohemiæ dominio liberari. Ex tunc literas & nuntios miserunt regi Romanorum, rogantes sup-pliciter, vt ad preces ipsorum veniat, quia terras ad imperium spectantes, quas rex Bohemiæ per violentiam possidet, velint sui dominio subiugare.
units.tr: When Rudolf had been accepted by the cities and peace had been made in Germany, the nobles who were under the rule of the king of Bohemia rejoiced greatly, hoping to be freed from the lordship of the king of Bohemia. From then on they sent letters and messengers to the king of the Romans, begging him humbly to come at their request, since they wished to bring under his dominion the lands belonging to the empire, which the king of Bohemia held by violence.

units.la: Audiens hæc Bohemiæ rex timuit valde, & concilio congregato, principes literatos conuocauit, sc. Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, Præpositos, Abbates & Priores. Cùm igitur ad præsentiam sui conuenissent, dixit: Intelleximus nuper, quod comes Rodolphus de Habispurch dicat, se fore regem Romanorum, & dicit, se velle terras no-stras, quas multiplici iure possidemus, in propriam retrahere potestatem. Hæc sustinere non debemus, insuper nobis cederet in maximum detrimentum. Rogo dilectionem vestram, quatenus in fidelitatem iuramento firmetis, & vt omnes meos aduersarios de nostris finibus, pro viribus vestris expellatis.
units.tr: Hearing this, the king of Bohemia was greatly afraid, and calling a council he summoned the learned princes, namely the archbishops, bishops, provosts, abbots and priors. When they had gathered in his presence, he said: "We have recently learned that Count Rudolf of Habsburg says he will be king of the Romans, and says he wishes to draw back into his own power our lands, which we hold by many rights. We ought not to endure this; moreover it would turn to our very great loss. I ask your affection that you confirm your loyalty by oath, and that you drive all my adversaries from our borders with all your strength."

units.la: Tunc omnes pariter dixerûnt: Quicquid domino regi placuerit, faciemus. Tunc rex dixit: Iurate ergo mihi fidelitatem: tunc omnes iurauerunt. Insuper ei pueros suos obsides tradiderunt.
units.tr: Then they all said together: "We shall do whatever pleases our lord the king." Then the king said: "Swear fealty to me, then." Then they all swore. Moreover they handed over their sons to him as hostages.

units.la: Rudolphus rex, cùm literas nobilium Bohemiæ vidisset: subitò eis in adiutorium venisset, si Rheni regiones relinquere potuisset. Cùm autem rex propter literas ad terram Bohemiæ se transferre minimè potuisset: quidam ex ipsis personaliter in Alsatiam peruenerunt, regem supplicitèr deprecantes, vt ad terras re-gis Bohemiæ non differat venire, eò quòd sibi regiones suas restituent vni-uersas.
units.tr: When King Rudolf had seen the letters of the nobles of Bohemia, he would have come to their aid at once, had he been able to leave the regions of the Rhine. But since, because of the letters, the king could not possibly move himself to the land of Bohemia, some of them came in person into Alsace, humbly begging the king not to delay coming to the lands of the king of Bohemia, since they would restore all his regions to him.

units.la: Rudolphus rex Romanorum inclinatus precibus dominorum, rogauit omnes personaliter milites, quos rogare poterat, insuper omnibus suis præcepit, vt armati secum venire non differant, quia terras alias oportet eum subitò visitare. Multi sibi bona promiserunt, sed soluere minimè potuerunt. Rex terram suam cum paucis exiuit, sed de die in diem plures milites acquisiuit. Cùm autem Moguntiam
units.tr: King Rudolf of the Romans, moved by the prayers of the lords, personally asked all the knights he could, and he ordered all his own men not to delay coming with him armed, because he had to visit other lands suddenly. Many promised him goods, but they could not pay them. The king set out from his land with a few men, but day by day he gathered more knights. When he had come to Mainz,

units.la: venisset, dixit ad eum Dominus de Clingin: Domine, quis est custos vestri thesauri? Respondit rex, non habeo thesaurum, nec pecuniam quàm quinque solidos debilis monetæ. Tum dixit ei dominus de Clingin: Quomodo ergo vultis exercitui prouidere? Respondit ei rex: Sicut mihi dominus semper prouidit, sic & in hoc itinere Dominus poterit prouidere. Lætanter rex processit, & in extrema semper extitit paupertate. Processit sine contradictione, & quæ spectabant ad imperium ei voluntariè tradebantur. Castella, munitiones, fora, quorumcunque fuerint, quæ se defendere non potuerunt, ditioni suæ se voluntariè tradiderunt.
units.tr: the lord of Klingen said to him: "Lord, who is the keeper of your treasure?" The king replied: "I have no treasure, nor any money beyond five shillings of debased coin." Then the lord of Klingen said to him: "How then do you intend to provide for the army?" The king answered him: "As the Lord has always provided for me, so the Lord will be able to provide for us on this journey too." The king went on cheerfully, and was always in extreme poverty. He advanced without opposition, and what belonged to the empire was handed over to him willingly. Castles, fortifications and markets, whoever held them, which could not defend themselves, surrendered of their own accord to his rule.

units.la: Rex autem Bohemiæ non credebat, quòd rex Rudolphus auderet vel posset sine contradictione terras Austriæ devastare. Si enim rex Bohemiæ aduentum regis Romanorum veraciter timuisset, pontes aquarum, altitudines viarum, facillime cum paucis hominibus conclusisset, quo aduentum regis diutissime distulisset. Cùm autem rex Romanorum ad ducem Bauariæ filiamstrum suum peruenisset, ab eo reuerenter suscipitur, & ei suisque necessaria abundanter & voluntariè ministrantur. Composuit etiam rex Romanorum cum dominis diuersis, vt ipsorum permitterent terras liberè pertransire.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia, however, did not believe that King Rudolf would dare, or be able, to lay waste the lands of Austria without opposition. For if the king of Bohemia had truly feared the coming of the king of the Romans, he could very easily have blocked the bridges over the waters and the heights of the roads with a few men, and so have delayed the king's arrival for a very long time. But when the king of the Romans came to the duke of Bavaria, his father-in-law, he was received by him with respect, and supplies were provided abundantly and willingly for him and his men. The king of the Romans also came to terms with various lords, so that they would permit the lands to be crossed freely.

units.la: Cùm hæc ad aures regis peruenissent Bohemiæ, doluit multùm: congregatoque exercitu, venit ad regem Teutoniæ prope Viennam, vt eum de suis finibus extirparet, sed non poterat: quia regis Bohemiæ congregatio ex vna parte Danubij morabatur: regis autem exercitus Romanorum ex alia parte Danubij requieuit.
units.tr: When these things reached the ears of the king of Bohemia, he was greatly grieved. Gathering an army, he came near Vienna to the king of Germany, to drive him out of his borders, but he could not do so, because the army of the king of Bohemia stayed on one side of the Danube, while the army of the king of the Romans rested on the other side.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ totam suam fiduciam in ciuitatem quæ <bl>Nuenburch</bl> dicitur, poterat, eò quòd inexpugnabilis videretur. Est enim ciuitas in monte posita, forti muro, turribus multis, circundata. In hanc Bohemos multos ad custodiendam miserat, eisque victualia plurima ministrabat. Ordinauerat & rex, vt si Vienna ciuitas impugnaretur à rege Romanorum, quòd ciuitas <bl>Nuenburch</bl> ei in omnibus necessaria ministraret. Si ciues Viennenses se traderent regi Romanorum, quòd rex eos per ciuitatem <bl>Nuenburch</bl> atrociter impugnaret. Cogitauerat enim rex Bohemiæ per ipsam totam terram Austriæ possidere.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia put all his trust in the city called Nuenburch, because it seemed impregnable. For the city is set on a mountain and surrounded by a strong wall and many towers. He had sent many Bohemians into it to guard it, and supplied them with plenty of provisions. The king had also ordered that if the city of Vienna were attacked by the king of the Romans, the city of Nuenburch should supply it with everything it needed. If the citizens of Vienna surrendered to the king of the Romans, the king would attack them savagely through the city of Nuenburch, for the king of Bohemia had intended to possess the whole land of Austria through it.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ quatuor munitiones, quæ circa muros erant ciuitatis Viennensis munire propugnaculis coepit, & castrum nouum fortissimum, quod ædificauerat, in medio ciuitatis. Coegit & ex tunc Burgenses, milites, nobiles & Barones pueros sibi dare obsides, & castra fortissima cum armis suis, in suam tradere potestatem. Misit insuper Bohemos milites armatos in ciuitates Austriæ, & victualia misit ipsis abundanter, vt si contingeret Rudolphum regem ciuitates aliquas obsidere, ciues se non possent excusare, quoniam ciuitates suas si vellent ab impugnantibus conseruare. Præ cæteris autem ciuitatem, quæ dicitur Nouum castrum, victualibus multis muniuit, eò quòd Viennam & alias ciuitates ex ipsa pascere voluisset. Præcepit etiam ne aliquis Rudolphum regem Romanorum dominum vel regem in suo dominio nominaret. Præcepit & fratribus Prædicatoribus ne celebrarent in sua potestate prouinciale Capitulum.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia began to fortify with bulwarks the four strongholds which stood around the walls of the city of Vienna, and the very strong new castle which he had built in the middle of the city. From then on he compelled the burghers, soldiers, nobles and barons to give him their sons as hostages, and to hand over their strongest castles, with their arms, into his power. He also sent armed Bohemian soldiers into the cities of Austria and sent them provisions abundantly, so that if King Rudolf should besiege any cities, the citizens could not make excuses, since they would wish to keep their cities safe from the attackers. Above all he stocked the city called Neustadt with many provisions, because he had wished to feed Vienna and the other cities from it. He also gave orders that no one was to call Rudolf king or lord of the Romans in his dominion. He further ordered the Preaching friars not to hold their provincial chapter in his territory.

units.la: Rudolphus rex Romanorum cum duobus millibus equorum phaleratorum Bauariam veniens, tali conditione se confœderauit duci Bauariæ, vt filius ducis filiam regis duceret in uxorem: & filia ducis, filio regis matrimonio iungeretur. Quo facto tradita fuit regi terra magna, & adiuncti sunt ei milites mille cum equis phaleratis. Post hæc coepit eius exercitus militibus augmentari, aditáq; rex ciuitatem Viennensem & obsedit tam potenter, vt ex vna parte ciuitatis nullus ingredi vel egredi sine sua licentia commodè potuisset.
units.tr: Rudolf, king of the Romans, coming into Bavaria with two thousand caparisoned horses, made an alliance with the duke of Bavaria on this condition: the duke's son would marry the king's daughter, and the duke's daughter would be joined in marriage to the king's son. Once this was done, a great tract of land was handed over to the king, and a thousand knights with caparisoned horses joined him. After this his army began to grow in soldiers. The king approached the city of Vienna and besieged it so strictly that from one side no one could conveniently go in or out without his permission.

units.la: Rex verò Bohemiæ equitibus viginti millibus congregatis, exercitum suum contra regem Romanorum ex alia parte Danubij direxit, vt eum de suis finibus extirparet. Milites autem Bohemiæ regis, propter nimium timorem contra Teutonicos bellare, nullis voluerunt regis iussionibus obedire. Rex Bohemiæ suis confidere non audebat, quòd longo tempore nobilium patres, fratres, consanguineos & affines vi siue fraudulentia pro viribus occidebat, vel ipsos de Bohemiæ finibus bus extirpabat. Exercitus autem Regis Romanorum cum exercitu regis Bohemiæ libentissimè dimicasset, si eum in loco competente comprehendere potuisset.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia gathered twenty thousand horsemen and sent his army against the king of the Romans from the other side of the Danube, to drive him out of his territory. But the soldiers of the king of Bohemia, from excessive fear of fighting against the Germans, were unwilling to obey the king's orders. The king of Bohemia dared not trust his own people, because for a long time he had killed the fathers, brothers, kinsmen and relatives of the nobles by force or fraud, as far as he could, or had driven them out of the borders of Bohemia. The army of the king of the Romans would most gladly have fought with the army of the king of Bohemia, if it could have caught it in a suitable place.

units.la: Rege Romanorum Viennam diebus pluribus obsidente: misit rex Bohemiæ, episcopum de Vlmize, cum equis phaleratis multis, vt Bohemis Nuenburch ciuitas assignaretur, ne à Bauaris regi Romanorum traderetur. Festinauit igitur episcopus cum suis propter diuersos timores, quòd vno die miliaria quatuordecim cucurrerunt, & ob hoc ipsis multi nobiles equi perierunt. Dux Bauariæ senior cum hæc à fide dignis audiuisset, Rudolfum regem Romanorum adiit, & hæc sibi cum gaudio reuelauit. Dixit etiam regi: domine, rogo quatenus mihi milites trecentos assignetis, quòd insidias episcopo de Vlmize in .f.... sylua dispositui collocare: spero enim ab ipsis aliqd habituru m. Cui rex dixit, accipe quod vis, & de istis ordina sapienter. Tunc dux acceptis militibus trecentis Rheni, quibus præ aliis melius considebat, in sylvam prope ciuitatem Nuenburch collocauit, & eos prout melius poterat, occultauit. Episcopus autem sibi insidias positas intellexit, Bohemisque ciuitatem custodiendam tradidit: & acceptis multis ex ciuibus, qui sibi suisq; ducatum præberent: insidias occultè per deuia fugiens, ad amicos saluus nôscitur deuenisse.
units.tr: While the king of the Romans was besieging Vienna for several days, the king of Bohemia sent the bishop of Olmütz with many caparisoned horses, so that the city of Neuburg might be assigned to the Bohemians, lest it be handed over to the king of the Romans by the Bavarians. The bishop therefore hurried on with his men, driven by various fears, so that in one day they ran fourteen miles, and on this account many of the nobles' fine horses died. The elder duke of Bavaria, having heard these things from trustworthy men, went to King Rudolf and joyfully disclosed them to him. He also said to the king: "Lord, I ask that you assign me three hundred soldiers, so that I may set an ambush for the bishop of Olmütz in the .f.... forest; for I hope to gain something from them." The king said: "Take what you wish, and arrange matters wisely with them." Then the duke, taking three hundred Rhenish soldiers, whom he trusted more than the others, placed them in a forest near the city of Neuburg and hid them as well as he could. But the bishop learned that an ambush had been laid for him. He handed the city over to the Bohemians to guard, and taking many of the citizens to act as his guides and those of his men, he fled secretly by byways and is known to have reached his friends safely.

units.la: Dux autem in insidiis vsque ad horam nonam creditur permansisse, & suos fame grauissima puniuisse. Tunc milites duci dixerunt: Vt quid hic fame morimur? Mittatur explorator, qui de statu ciuitatis & episcopi nobis possit aliquid reuelare. Tunc dux cuidam militi dixit: Ad ciuitatem tanquam amicus subitò perge & secreta quæ poteris inuestiga. Explorator ad ciuitatem subitò veniens, statum hominum ciuitatisque requirens: reuersus retulit, dicens: episcopus ciuitatem Bohemis commisit, ciuesque secum duxit, & ad propria remeauit. Consternatus dux militibus suis dixit: Quid ergo faciemus? spe enim nostra frustrati sumus. Tunc diuersi diuersa consilia tradiderunt. Vnus autem ex illis dixit: Domine, viam nostram dirigamus ad ciuitatem, & amicos nos esse simulemus: forte recipient nos vt amicos, & sic poterimus comprehendere ciuitatem. Dux militi dixit: Bonum consilium dedisti, nec vnquam improbis operibus defecisti.
units.tr: The duke is believed to have remained in the ambush until the ninth hour, and to have punished his men with severe hunger. Then the soldiers said to the duke: "Why are we dying of hunger here? Let a scout be sent who can tell us something about the state of the city and the bishop." Then the duke said to one of the soldiers: "Go quickly to the city as a friend and find out whatever secrets you can." The scout came swiftly to the city, enquired about the condition of the people and the city, and on returning reported: "The bishop has entrusted the city to the Bohemians, has taken the citizens with him, and has gone back home." Dismayed, the duke said to his soldiers: "What then shall we do? For we have been cheated of our hope." Different men gave different advice. One of them said: "Lord, let us direct our way to the city and pretend to be friends. Perhaps they will receive us as friends, and so we may be able to seize the city." The duke said to the soldier: "You have given good advice, and you never fail in wicked deeds."

units.la: Post hæc quidam ex sapientibus suis dixit: Domine, primò duo milites præmittantur, post eos quatuor, post quos decem, postea quadraginta, & hi omnes ciues & amicos se regis Bohemiæ protestentur. Post hos exercitus subitò sequatur, vt si primi ciuitatem fuerint ingressi, per consequens ingredi liberam exercitus habeat potestatem. Sicut deliberauerunt, ita omnia perfecerunt. Appropinquantes autem primi nuntij ciuitati, clara voce pariter cantauerunt. Bohemi custodes ciuitatis, cum voce cantantium audiuisset, gaudio replebantur: suspicabantur enim ciues & amicos suos cum lætitia rediisse. Pontes demittuntur, portæ reserantur, pacificè salutantur, & ingredi liberè permittuntur. Quatuor autem milites sequentes benignissimè recepe-runt, quia prospera de suis ciuibus retulerunt. Milites autem decem qui quatuor sequebantur, suspecti custodibus habebantur, & portas aperire, sicut cæteris præcedentibus noluerunt. Tum hi decem Bohemis custodibus verbis mendacibus referebant: Nos de vestris sumus, & episcopum de Vlmice cum ciuibus ad tuta loca deduximus, & nunc ad propria remeamus. Tunc custodes portas aperuerunt, & intrare liberè permiserunt. Milites hi prædicti festinanter intrare noluerunt, sed in porta permanentes, custodes verbis fallacibus deceperunt, donec quadraginta frequentes ad ciuitatis mœnia peruenerant. Decem milites prædicti, cum nos adesse vidissent: custodes portæ euaginatis gladiis inuaserunt, & de porta fugere coegerunt. Custodes portam reliquerunt, & ad hospitia sua fugientes, se suaque saluare cupientes, ciuitatem captam omnibus nunciabant. Quinquaginta milites prædicti ciuitatis portas violenter tenuerunt, & ducem cum exercitu suo superuenientem, liberè intrare permiserunt. Cùm sic dux ciuitatem tam potenter fuisset ingressus, & ipsam cum suis obtinuisset: cœpit per præconem hæc ciuibus nuntiare: Nulli malum ex ciuibus in rebus vel corpore vel familiis inferetur. Bohe- mi tantum aduersarii nostri in custodiam publicam perducantur. Post hæc viri mulieresque militibus ducis Bohemos in domibus suis abscondito, ostenderunt, & captiuitati publicæ tradiderunt. Factum id anno M. C C. LXXVII.
units.tr: After this, one of his wise men said: "Lord, let two soldiers be sent on ahead first, then four after them, then ten, and afterwards forty; let all of them declare that they are citizens and friends of the king of Bohemia. After them let the army follow suddenly, so that if the first men have entered the city, the army may then have free power to enter." They carried out everything just as they had planned. As the first messengers approached the city, they sang together in a loud voice. The Bohemian guards of the city, hearing the voices of the singers, were filled with joy, for they supposed that their citizens and friends had returned in good spirits. The bridges were lowered, the gates unbarred, the men were greeted peacefully, and they were allowed to enter freely. The guards received the four who followed most kindly, because they brought good news of their fellow citizens. But the ten who followed the four were viewed with suspicion by the guards, and they were unwilling to open the gates as they had for the earlier men. Then these ten, with lying words, told the Bohemian guards: "We are on your side. We have led the bishop of Olmütz and the citizens to safe places, and now we are returning home." Then the guards opened the gates and allowed them to enter freely. The men just mentioned were unwilling to enter hastily; remaining in the gateway, they deceived the guards with false words until forty men in a crowd had reached the city walls. When the ten men mentioned above saw that we were near, they attacked the gate guards with drawn swords and forced them to flee from the gate. The guards abandoned the gate and, fleeing to their lodgings and wishing to save themselves and their belongings, announced to everyone that the city had been taken. The fifty men mentioned above held the city gates by force and allowed the duke, who was approaching with his army, to enter freely. When the duke had thus entered the city so forcefully and taken possession of it with his men, he began to announce through a herald to the citizens: "No harm shall be done to any citizen in goods, body or household. Only our adversaries, the Bohemians, shall be taken into public custody." After this, men and women pointed out to the duke's soldiers the Bohemians hidden in their houses, and handed them over to public captivity. This happened in the year 1277.

units.la: Expugnata ciuitate hac, venit ad eam rex cum exercitu suo, prædia diuisit, & quatuordecim diebus de rebus regis Bohemiæ, quas in ciuitatem deduxerat, exercitui suo rex necessaria tribuit abundanter.
units.tr: Once this city was taken, the king came to it with his army, divided up the estates, and for fourteen days he generously supplied his army with necessities from the goods of the king of Bohemia that had been brought into the city.

units.la: Per hanc ciuitatem obsessa fuit ciuitas Viennensis, quòd regi Bohemiæ non poterant commodè subuenire, nec rex poterat Viennenses a regis Romanorum dominio liberare. Viennensibus sic in periculo constitutis, quid facere possent ignorauerunt. Postea verò deliberatione facta, cum rege Romanorum compositerunt, & ciuitatem suo dominio tradiderunt, insuper ab eis fuit donis magnis honoratus. Cùm sic Viennenses à suo domino recessissent, & regem Romanorum pro domino recepissent: mox à rege Bohemorum pueros, quos obsides sibi dederant, petierunt. Rex autem reddere pueros contradicit. Tunc Viennenses exercitu congregato, regis Bohemiæ terminos intrauerunt, & expugnatis munitionibus & ciuitatibus pluribus ad propria redierunt. Videns autem rex Bohemiæ, quòd non posset regi Romanorum resistere, humiliauit se, & commisit se gratiæ suæ. Principes autem reges sub his conditionibus concordabantur. Debebat rex Bohemorum filiam suam filio regis Rudolphi matrimonio copulare: Regalia sua sicut deceret, ab ipso recipere, & trecentos milites cum equis phaleratis in exercitu regis ducere quando vellet.
units.tr: Because of the capture of this city, the city of Vienna was besieged, since the Bohemian king could not conveniently come to its aid, nor could he rescue the Viennese from the rule of the king of the Romans. With the Viennese placed in such danger, they did not know what they could do. Afterwards, however, having deliberated, they came to terms with the king of the Romans and handed the city over to his rule; moreover, he was honoured by them with great gifts. When the Viennese had thus withdrawn from their former lord and accepted the king of the Romans as lord, they at once demanded from the king of Bohemia the boys whom they had given him as hostages. But the king refused to return the boys. Then the Viennese, gathering an army, entered the territory of the king of Bohemia, and after storming fortifications and several cities returned home. The king of Bohemia, seeing that he could not resist the king of the Romans, humbled himself and committed himself to his mercy. The princes then agreed on these terms: the king of the Bohemians was to join his daughter in marriage to the son of King Rudolf; he was to receive his royal insignia from him, as was fitting; and he was to lead three hundred knights with caparisoned horses in the king's army whenever he wished.

units.la: Rex Bohemiæ multis militibus, equis, vestibus deauratis, gemmisque decorat sese præparauit, vt Regalia statim à rege suscipieret Romanorum. Hæc cum principes Rudolphi regis intellexissent: regi cum gaudio retulerunt: Domine præparate vos, sicut decet regem, vestibus pretiosis. Tunc rex dixit: Rex Bohemiæ griseam vestem meam sæpius derisit, nunc autem ipsum mea vestis grisea deridebit. Dein Notario suo dixit, Da pallium tuum mihi, vt rex Bohemiæ meam derideat paupertatem. Adueniente rege Bohemorum, dixit rex Romanorum militibus suis: Armis vestris induimini, dextarios vestros loricate, & ad bellum vt melius poteritis præparate, vtramq; partem viæ, per quam rex venturus est, processionaliter occupate, & armorum Teutonicorum gloriam barbaris nationibus ostendite.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia made ready with many soldiers, horses, gilded garments and jewelled ornaments, so that he might at once receive the royal insignia from the king of the Romans. When the princes of King Rudolf heard this, they joyfully reported it to the king: "Lord, prepare yourself, as a king should, with precious clothing." Then the king said: "The king of Bohemia has often mocked my grey coat; now my grey coat will mock him." Then he said to his notary: "Give me your cloak, so that the king of Bohemia may mock my poverty." When the king of Bohemia was approaching, the king of the Romans said to his soldiers: "Put on your armour, armour your horses, and prepare for battle as well as you can. Occupy both sides of the road by which the king is to come, in procession, and show the barbarian nations the glory of German arms."

units.la: Hæc sic ad regis voluntatem præparatis, venit rex Bohemiæ, cum vestibus deauratis, & gloria regia fulgente, procidit ad pedes regis Romanorum, humiliter ab eo sua Regalia mendicauit. Insuper & centum millium marcarum redditus, & quadraginta millium marcarum, quas Austriæ dux habuerat, & rex Bohemiæ de regina Margareta possederat, resignauit. Tunc rex Romanorum regi Bohemiæ regnum, nec non & Regalia concessit, & se amicum suum intimum omnibus astantibus intimauit. Rege Romanorum hæc faciente, indutus veste grisea, despectus & humilis apparebat, & in tripode residebat.
units.tr: Having made these preparations as the king wished, the king of Bohemia came, dressed in gilded garments and shining with royal splendour. He threw himself at the feet of the king of the Romans and humbly begged him for his regalia. Moreover, he gave up the revenue of a hundred thousand marks and the forty thousand marks which the duke of Austria had held and which the king of Bohemia had possessed from Queen Margaret. Then the king of the Romans granted the kingdom of Bohemia to the king of Bohemia, together with the regalia, and declared him his most intimate friend before all who stood by. While the king of the Romans did these things, he appeared despised and humble, dressed in a grey garment, and sat upon a tripod.

units.la: Post paucas septimanas pœnituit regem Bohemorum, quòd se subdiderat regi Romanorum. Vidit enim rex Bohemiæ, quòd rex Rudolphus multa possederat bonorum, & tamen in summa semper extirpit paupertate. Propter hæc & alia rex Bohemiæ filiam suam, quam filio regis Rudolphi matrimonio copulauerat, monialem fecit, & in claustrum dominarum ordinis Minorum solenniter collocauit. Post hæc rex Bohemorum congregauit occultè decem millia dominorum, volens occultè regem comprehendere Romanorum. Deus autem mirabiliter hæc impediuit. Cœperunt inter se congregati milites discordare, se mutuo capere, plagisque maximis vulnerare. His ita gestis, rex Bohemiæ manifestè regem Rudolphum diffidauit, congregauit exercitum magnum, voluit cum rege congredi Romanorum, vel in ciuitate cum ciuibus obsidere, vel ipsum de finibus Austriæ turpiter extirpare.
units.tr: A few weeks later the king of Bohemia regretted that he had submitted himself to the king of the Romans. For the king of Bohemia saw that King Rudolf possessed much wealth, and yet was always reduced to utter poverty. On account of these things and others, the king of Bohemia made his daughter, whom he had given in marriage to the son of King Rudolf, a nun, and solemnly placed her in the convent of the Minoress sisters. After this, the king of Bohemia secretly gathered ten thousand lords, intending secretly to seize the king of the Romans. But God wonderfully prevented this. The soldiers who had been gathered began to quarrel among themselves, to seize one another and to wound each other with the greatest blows. These things having been done, the king of Bohemia openly defied King Rudolf, gathered a great army, and wished either to engage the king in battle, or to besiege him in a city with its citizens, or to drive him shamefully out of the borders of Austria.

units.la: Videns etiam rex Bohemiæ, quòd regem Rudolphum nec dolo nec sapientia, nec potentia vincere potuisser, muneribus vincere cupiebat. Misit enim rex Bohemorum quibusdam militibus Austriæ pecuniam magnam, vt in bello relinquerent regem Romanorum: vel si possent, ipsum consiliis suis impedirent. Promisit & sedecim militibus, mille marcas argenti, si sibi regem Rudolphum viuum, vel vulneribus læsum, vel mortuum præsentarent. Misit & Vngariæ militibus pecuniam, ne ipsum impugnarent, vel debiliter infestarent. Hoc & rei postmodum euentus probauit. Misit & promisit etiam dominis Episcopis, Comitibus, Baronibus prope Rhenum constitutis, vt in adiutorium regis Rudolfi minimè peruenirent, vel ipsum pro suis viribus impugnarent. Quod quidam pro suis viribus fecerunt, & amplius fecissent, si rex in aliquo defecisset. Vnde & in adiutorium regi Rudolfo tantum milites ducenti numero venêre.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia, seeing that he could not conquer King Rudolf by trickery, wisdom or power, desired to conquer him by bribes. For the king of Bohemia sent a large sum of money to certain soldiers of Austria, so that they would abandon the king of the Romans in battle or, if they could, hinder him by their counsels. He also promised sixteen soldiers a thousand marks of silver if they delivered King Rudolf to him alive, or wounded, or dead. He also sent money to the soldiers of Hungary, so that they would not attack him or harass him weakly. The outcome of the event later proved this. He also sent and promised money to the lords, bishops and barons stationed near the Rhine, that they should in no way come to the aid of King Rudolf, or attack him with all their strength. Some of them did so with all their strength, and would have done more had the king failed in anything. Hence only two hundred soldiers came to help King Rudolf.

units.la: Hæc audiens rex Romanorum mandauit principibus suis, regi scilicet Vngariæ duci Saxoniæ, duci Bauariæ, militibus multis, episcopo Basiliensi,& filio suo Alsatiæ Lantgrauio, episcopis diuersis, & omnibus quibus considebat, domino de Baldeck, quatenus cum omnibus armatis, quibus possent in adiutorium sibi subitò peruenirent. Dixit enim: Si circa festum natiuitatis beatæ Mariæ non veneritis, poterit mihi in maximum cedere detrimentum. Rex Vngariæ regem Rudolphum clementer exaudiuit,& ad ciuitatem Viennensem, cum quatuordecim millibus hominum venit,ad prælium præparatis.Ex Austriæ partibus congregauerat rex Romanorum milites multos,cum dextrariis phaleratis. Habebat insuper ciuitatem Viennensem cum multis ad bellum præparatis. Sed in his omnibus rex minime considebat, nec cum eis ausus fuit, cum rege Bohemiæ dimicare. Sperabat enim filium suum venturum cum multis militibus,qui per se res & corpora periculo commisisset.Cùm autem ad sibi determinatum terminum milites prædicti venire non potuissent: tur-batur rex Romanorum supra modum. Erat enim intra se desolatus, consilio & auxilio destitutus. Præterea ciues Viennenses ad regem venerunt, dicentes: Domine vestri vos dereliquerunt,nec habetis homines, per quos regi Bohemiæ resistere valeatis. Rogamus vos quatenus nobis Dominum nos eligere permittatis, ne nos cum vestra familia pereamus. Tunc rex eos supplicitèr deprecatur, dicens: Tempus adhuc modicum sustinete, vt videamus quid facere debeamus. Ex tunc iussit castrum fideliter custodiri. Insuper seruis suis, minoribus pariterque maioribus, ne quis alicui ciuium qualibet occasione, vel superbè, vel contumaciter respponderet: posset enim hoc omnibus nobis euenire, in rerum & corporum detrimentum.
units.tr: Hearing this, the king of the Romans commanded his princes, namely the king of Hungary, the duke of Saxony, the duke of Bavaria, many soldiers, the bishop of Basel, and his son, the landgrave of Alsace, various bishops, and all those in whom he trusted, and the lord of Baldeck, that with all the armed men they could muster they should come quickly to his aid. For he said: "If you do not come about the feast of the Blessed Virgin's Nativity, it may turn out to my very great harm." The king of Hungary graciously heeded King Rudolf and came to the city of Vienna with fourteen thousand men, prepared for battle. The king of the Romans had gathered many soldiers from the parts of Austria, with caparisoned horses. Moreover, he had the city of Vienna with many men ready for war. But in all these things the king did not trust, nor did he dare to fight with the king of Bohemia. For he hoped that his son would come with many soldiers, since he had exposed his own goods and person to danger. But when the aforesaid soldiers could not come to him at the appointed time, the king of the Romans was thrown into excessive confusion. For he was inwardly desolate, deprived of counsel and help. Besides, the citizens of Vienna came to the king, saying: "Lord, your own people have abandoned you, and you have no men through whom you may be able to resist the king of Bohemia. We ask you to allow us to choose a lord for ourselves, lest we perish with your household." Then the king begged them earnestly, saying: "Endure a little while longer, so that we may see what we ought to do." From then on he ordered the castle to be faithfully guarded. Moreover, he charged his servants, both lesser and greater, that no one should answer any citizen proudly or obstinately on any pretext, for this could happen to all of us, to the loss of goods and persons.

units.la: Rege Rudolpho sic in periculo constituto: congregauit Henricus episcopus Basiliensis,ordinis fratrum Minorum, vir sapiens atque discretus, & regi Rudolpho fidelissimus amicus: Et dominus Conradus Wernherus aduocatus Alsatiæ, dictus de Hadistat, exercitum centum militum optimè præparatis cum dextrariis phaleratis.Hi duo domini militibus suis congregatis in Basilea coniunguntur. De Basilea vero in Sueuiam pariter proficiscuntur,ibique comes de ........ cum centum militibus equos phaleratos habentes,adiungitur, & iter coeptum pariter perrexerunt. Milites isti sic in itinere constituti, dominos plurimos timuerunt, vnde & pluribus diebus in armis grauibus permanserunt.
