units.tr: With King Rudolf thus placed in danger, Henry, bishop of Basel, of the order of the Friars Minor, a wise and prudent man and most faithful friend of King Rudolf, gathered his soldiers at Basel, and Lord Conrad Wernher, advocate of Alsace, called of Hadistat, gathered an army of a hundred well-equipped soldiers with caparisoned horses. These two lords joined their soldiers together at Basel. From Basel they set out together into Swabia, and there the count of ........ joined them with a hundred soldiers having caparisoned horses, and they continued the journey they had begun together. These soldiers, placed thus on the journey, feared many lords, and therefore they remained for many days in heavy armour.

units.la: Cùm autem venissent Viennam ad regem Teutoniæ,gauisus est gaudio magno. Interrogauit rex,quare filius suus in eorum societate non venisset:responderunt ei:Filius vester cum 500 militibus est in procinctu veniendi. Comes verò Phirretensis,& comes Montis pilgardi sunt in veniendo, cum multis militibus optimè præparatis. In secreto verò regi contraria his omnibus referebant. Dixeruntq;, nec filius vester, nec aliquis amicorum vestrorum subitò vobis poterit in vestris necessitatibus subuenire. Debetis igitur deliberare,quid facere debeatis.Tunc respondit eis dicens:placet vt vno die quiescatis,&ad bellum postea procedatis:sufficit mihi quòd vos habeo cum stodes capitis mei.In Deo meo confido,qui me miraculosè ad hanc gloriam noscitur elegisse,& in ea mirabiliùs confortasse: qui etiam nunc me per gratiam suam (vt spero) mirabiliter adiuuabit.
units.tr: When they had come to Vienna to the king of Germany, he rejoiced with great joy. The king asked why his son had not come in their company. They answered him: "Your son is about to set out with five hundred soldiers. The count of Pfirt and the count of Montbéliard are also on their way, with many well-equipped soldiers." But in secret they reported to the king the contrary of all these things. And they said: "Neither your son nor any of your friends can quickly come to help you in your necessities. You must therefore consider what you ought to do." Then he answered them, saying: "It pleases me that you rest for one day, and afterwards proceed to battle. It is enough for me that I have you as guardians of my head. I trust in my God, who is known to have chosen me miraculously to this glory and strengthened me in it more wonderfully; who, I hope, will also now help me wonderfully by his grace."

units.la: His dictis suis retulerunt: Ad bellum omnes vos in crastinum præparate,quia cum familia regis Bohemiæ,nos oportet fortiter dimicare. Tunc tota familia regis Rudolphi cucurrit ad Confessores, debita sua scribebant, inimicitias remittebant, & ad communicandum prout fideliùs poterant,præparabant.Periculum enim mortis videbatur omnibus imminere. Exercitus regis Rud. alba cruce desuper vtebatur: sed Bohemiæ regis exercitus crucè viridè deferebat. Rex Teutoniæ pro suis & pro se fuerat in timore maximo. Rex verò Bohemiæ certus de victoria fuit, unde dixit: Si quis mihi veraciter regē Rud. cum suis Danubium transmisisse, nunciârit, pecuniam viginti marcarum, voluntariè propinaret. Tertia die post aduentum Basil. episcopi, sc. in vigilia S. Bartholomæi, B litera dominicali, egressus est rex Rud. Viennam, cum exercitu suo, cum rege Bohemiæ prælium commissurus. Rex autem Bohemiæ cum exercitu suo prope ciuitatem venerat Viennensem.
units.tr: When these words had been spoken, they reported: "Prepare yourselves all for battle tomorrow, for we must fight bravely with the household of the king of Bohemia." Then the whole household of King Rudolf ran to the confessors, wrote their debts, remitted enmities, and prepared themselves to receive communion as faithfully as they could. For the danger of death seemed to hang over all. The army of King Rudolf carried a white cross upon them, but the army of the king of Bohemia bore a green cross. The king of the Germans was in the greatest fear for his own people and for himself. But the king of Bohemia was certain of victory, and so he said: "If anyone reports to me truly that King Rudolf has crossed the Danube with his men, I will willingly give twenty marks of money." On the third day after the arrival of the bishop of Basel, namely on the vigil of St. Bartholomew, with B as the dominical letter, King Rudolf set out from Vienna with his army, about to engage in battle with the king of Bohemia. But the king of Bohemia had come near the city of Vienna with his army.

units.la: Bohemiæ rex exercitum suum, in plures partes, sed in tres diuiserat principales. Habuit enim multa millia peditum Cumanorum. Secundum habuit exercitum equitum & hominum diuersorum: tertiū habuit exercitum equorum phaleratorum, & militum circiter nongentorum. Rex Rudolfus similiter in tres partes suum exercitum diuidebat. Habuit Vngariæ regem cum quindecim millibus Vngarorum. Rex Vngariæ puer 18 annorum extitit, & ad prælium non peruenit, quia rex Rud. ipsum noluit interesse. Episcopus Basil. sedens in dextrario phalerato decentissimo, armis indutus, ad bellum libentissimè processisset, si voluntas regia permisisset. Rudolphus rex libenter vidisset, quòd Vngari cum Cumanis congressi fuissent: sed eos ipsi inuadere minimè voluerunt. Secundum rex Rudolfus exercitum habebat, & hunc aduersus exercitum regis Bohemiæ dirigebat. Exercitus autem regis Bohemiæ fortior erat, & eos retrocedere faciebat. Videns Rudolfus suos deficere, tertium quem habebat exercitum, sc. trecentos milites, habentes equos phaleratos, in quibus etiam maximè considebat, contra regem Bohemiæ dirigebat, & magis in Domino, quàm propriis viribus considebat. Rex Bohemiæ videns regem Rudolfum contra se venientem, solus aduersarios atrociter aggrediens, multos percussionibus suis grauissimis affligebat: trecenti verò milites custodes regis, ipsum pro suis viribus adiuuabant. Tandem rex Bohemiæ fessus, ab ignobili capitur, & armis propriis spoliatur. Tum rex sic discinctus ducitur. miles quidam insequitur eum, dicens: ecce rex, qui fratrem meum turpiter interfecit. Licet igitur factum, extractoq; gladio, regem in facie perforauit. Qui autem regem Bohemiæ ceperat, doluit vehementer, & ipsum libentissimè defendisset, si suis viribus potuisset.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia had divided his army into several parts, but into three principal ones. For he had many thousands of Cuman foot soldiers. He had a second force of horsemen and men of various kinds; a third force he had of caparisoned horses, and about nine hundred soldiers. King Rudolf likewise divided his army into three parts. He had the king of Hungary with fifteen thousand Hungarians. The king of Hungary was a boy of eighteen years, and did not come to the battle, because King Rudolf did not want him to take part. The bishop of Basel, sitting on a most handsome caparisoned horse, armed, would most willingly have gone forward to the battle, had the royal will permitted it. King Rudolf would gladly have seen the Hungarians engage with the Cumans, but they themselves were not willing to attack them. King Rudolf had a second army, and this he directed against the army of the king of Bohemia. But the army of the king of Bohemia was stronger, and made them give ground. Seeing his men failing, Rudolf directed against the king of Bohemia the third army he had, namely three hundred soldiers with caparisoned horses, on which he chiefly relied, and he trusted more in the Lord than in his own strength. The king of Bohemia, seeing King Rudolf coming against him, attacked his opponents alone and fiercely, afflicting many with his most severe blows; but the three hundred soldiers who guarded the king helped him with all their strength. At last the king of Bohemia, weary, was taken by a common soldier and stripped of his own arms. Then the king, thus ungirt, was led away. A certain soldier pursued him, saying: "Behold the king who shamefully killed my brother!" And so, drawing his sword, he ran the king through the face. He who had taken the king of Bohemia was greatly grieved, and would most willingly have defended him, had he been able with his own strength.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus contra suos aduersarios fortissimè dimicauit, tandem vir fortis veniens, regem percussionibus affligebat, sed cum vincere non posset, equum regis lancea perforauit. Tum rex & equus pariter ceciderunt. Rex in terra iacens omni solatio destitutus, clypeum suum super se posuit, ne subito sub pedibus equorum turpiter moreretur. Post transitum caballorum, quidam volens eum à mortis periculo liberare, de terra prout potuit eleuauit. Tunc rex dixit, equum mihi velociter præparate: quem protinus ascendit, & suorum auxilium fortiter inuocauit. Venerunt autem ad eum de suis circiter 50. cum his igitur rex à latere exercitum regis Bohemiæ subintrauit, atq; in duas partes diuisit, & posteriorem partem fortiter impugnauit. Anterior pars exercitus Bohemorum clamauerunt, fugiunt, fugiunt, exercitum Rudolfi decipere cupientes: sed quantò plus illi clamoribus instabant, tantò magis Teutonici percussionibus eos infestabant. Posteriorem partem Rudolfus rex fortiter impugnabat, qui tandem timore territi fugerunt. Illis autem terga vertentibus, Vngari subsequuntur, pugnantes impugnant, fugientes sequuntur, capiunt & occidunt: communiter dicebatur, quod in illo prælio 14000 occubuerint.
units.tr: King Rudolf fought most bravely against his adversaries. At last a strong man came up and beat the king hard, but since he could not overcome him, he ran a lance through the king's horse. The king and the horse fell together. The king lay on the ground, deprived of all help, and he put his shield over himself so that he would not be shamefully trampled to death under the horses' feet. After the horses had passed, someone who wanted to free him from the danger of death lifted him from the ground as best he could. Then the king said, "Bring me a horse quickly!" He mounted at once and loudly called for the help of his men. About fifty of his men came to him. With these the king attacked the army of the king of Bohemia from the side and split it into two parts, and he fiercely assailed the rear part. The front part of the Bohemian army shouted, "Flee, flee!", hoping to deceive Rudolf's army; but the more loudly they shouted, the more fiercely the Germans harassed them with blows. King Rudolf attacked the rear part fiercely, and at last they fled in terror. As they turned their backs, the Hungarians followed them: they attacked those who fought, pursued those who fled, and captured and killed them. It was commonly said that in that battle 14,000 fell.

units.la: Rex Rudolfus cum suis in loco prælij permanebat, donec omnes eum securum de victoria referebant. Rex Bohemiæ eodem die moritur, & intestinis eius expositis, corpus reliquum cum sale, in fratrum Minorum monasterium collocatur. Mortuus enim fuit in excommunicatione papæ, propter hoc non poterat in cœmiterio sepeliri. Fuerunt in exercitu regis Romanorum debiles homines, clerici, monachi, diuersarum religionum conuersi, qui se in quoddam colliculum receperūt, finem certaminis expectantes, Dominum pro suis hominibus deprecantes. Hi considerauerunt, quòd in exercitu regis Bohemorū splendor & calor maximus extitit armorum. Sed exercitum regis Rudolfi quocunq; declinabat, semper nubes frigida protegebat. Ex hoc præsumebant, quod exercitus regis Rudolfi adiutorio Domini debuit præualere. Acta sunt hæc prope Viennam, in campo dicto, Gansferfeld, anno 1278, circa horam sextam, in vigilia Bartholomæi. Mortuo rege Bohemorum, intrauit rex Rudolfus terram Morauiæ, volens eam totaliter deuastare. Ciuitates communi consilio regem Rud. pro domino receperūt, & infra mensem, se & sua commiserunt, & fidelitatem iuramento firmissimè promiserunt. Regina Bohemiæ cum Rud. rege ita composuit, quòd filius reginæ filiam regis Rud. duceret vxorem, quod factum est, intra octauas S. Francisci.
units.tr: King Rudolf remained with his men on the field of battle until everyone reported to him that he was safe from the victory. The king of Bohemia died the same day, and after his entrails were removed, his remaining body was preserved with salt and placed in the monastery of the Friars Minor. For he had died under the pope's excommunication, and for this reason he could not be buried in the cemetery. In the army of the king of the Romans there were weak men, clerics, monks, and converts from various religious orders, who withdrew to a little hill, awaiting the end of the fighting and praying to the Lord for their men. They observed that in the army of the king of Bohemia there was the greatest brilliance and glare of arms. But wherever King Rudolf's army turned, a cold cloud always covered it. From this they concluded that King Rudolf's army ought to prevail by the help of the Lord. These things were done near Vienna, in the field called Gansferfeld, in the year 1278, about the sixth hour, on the eve of Bartholomew. After the death of the king of Bohemia, King Rudolf entered the land of Moravia, intending to lay it utterly waste. By common counsel the cities received King Rudolf as their lord, and within a month they committed themselves and their possessions to him and most firmly promised fealty under oath. The queen of Bohemia came to an agreement with King Rudolf, that the queen's son should marry King Rudolf's daughter; this was done within the octave of St Francis.

units.la: In loco occisorum fœtor tantus extitit, vt plures vel infirmi, vel mortui exiterint, in ea villa habitantes. Dæmonum præterea vel spirituum illusiones multos horribiliter terruerunt. Aduocatus Alsatię retulit, quòd venatores ceruum magnum infectantes, venerunt ad Heremitam, qui xii annis in solitudine cum vxore & liberis vixit.
units.tr: In the place of the slain there was such a stench that several of the people living in that village became sick or died. Moreover, illusions of demons or spirits terrified many horribly. The advocate of Alsace reported that some hunters, chasing a large stag, came to a hermit who had lived in solitude for twelve years with his wife and children.

units.la: 10 Hic venatoribus retulit, se vidisse animal à cingulo mulieris imaginem habens, quod dixit, Teutonia intra tres septimanas habebit regem, qui regnabit xv annis.
units.tr: 10 He told the hunters that he had seen an animal with the image of a woman from its girdle, and it said that Germany would have a king within three weeks, who would reign for fifteen years.

units.la: De morte reginæ Romanorum Rudolfi coniugis.
units.tr: On the death of Rudolf, queen of the Romans, the wife.

units.la: ANNO Domini M. CC. LXXXI, regina Rudolfi regis cœpit grauiter infirmari. Propter quod accersiuit consiliarium confessoremq; sibi, inquiens: Mortis periculum sentio mihi breuiter imminere. Rogo igitur vos, quomodo corpus & animam ad cœlum & ad paradisum Domini dirigatis. Qui dixit, omnes amicos vestros, omnes diuitias huius seculi, omnemque gloriam mundi de corde vestro, quantum potestis, à vestra memoria repellatis, ac Deo & hominibus satisfacere promittatis. Quæ dixit: libentissimè faciam. Post hæc Testamentum condidit, & elegit in Basilea, in maiore ecclesia ecclesiasticam sepulturam. Delegit autem locum prænominatum, eò quòd rex Rudolfus antecessoresque sui Basiliensem ecclesiam sæpius damnificassent, ac eius Episcopos perturbassent. Ordinauit enim in testamento (vt quidam dixerunt) quòd redditus duarum prebendarum Monasterio darentur, vt sic Deo & hominibus satisfaceret.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1281, the queen, wife of King Rudolf, began to fall seriously ill. Because of this she summoned her counsellor and confessor to herself, saying: "I feel that the danger of death is hanging over me shortly. I ask you, therefore, how you would direct my body and soul to heaven and to the paradise of the Lord." He replied: "Remove from your heart, as far as you can, all your friends, all the riches of this age, and all the glory of the world, and promise to make satisfaction to God and men." She said: "I will do so most gladly." After this she drew up her will and chose for her ecclesiastical burial the cathedral church at Basel. She chose that place because King Rudolf and his predecessors had often harmed the church of Basel and disturbed its bishops. For in her will (as some have said) she ordered that the revenues of two prebends be given to the monastery, so that she might thus make satisfaction to God and men.

units.la: Post hæc regina moritur, exenteratur, & veter eius fabulo & cineribus impletur: facies eius Balsamo linitur, totumq; corpus panno cereo circumdatur, ac sericis vestimentis induitur pretiosis. Caput eius albo serico peplatur, & corona sibi superponitur deaurata. Posthæc in arcam ex fago peroptimè factam, supina, manibus super pectus positis, impomitur, & ferreo clauditur instrumento. His expletis, in Basileam cū equis xl ducitur, & (vt credebatur) cum pecunia copiosa. Fuerunt in comitatu suo fratres Prædicatores duo, Minorum duo, & dominæ quas tres currus ducere potuerunt. Adiunxerunt autem se eis homines circiter quadringenti.
units.tr: After this the queen died; her bowels were removed, and her belly was filled with dung and ashes; her face was smeared with balsam, and her whole body was wrapped in waxed cloth and dressed in precious silk garments. Her head was covered with white silk, and a gilded crown was placed upon it. Afterwards she was laid, face up with her hands placed on her breast, in a chest made very well of beechwood, and it was shut with an iron fastening. When these things were done, she was led to Basel with forty horses and (as was believed) with a large sum of money. In her retinue were two Dominican friars, two Franciscans, and as many ladies as three carriages could carry. About four hundred men joined them.

units.la: Rex autem mandauerat episcopo Basilien si, vt reginam defunctam solenniter sepeliret. Episcopus clericos regulares & seculares inuitauit Basileam. Conuenerunt igitur mille ducenti, qui omnes candelas in manibus habebant, & reginæ in processione cum ornatu pretioso solenniter occurrunt, & ad maius monasterium perduxerunt. Tribus episcopis ibidem diuina celebrantibus, reginæ corpus in tumba positum erigitur, & omnibus præsentibus ostenditur, & post Missam deponitur & cum fletu nobilium sepelitur. Hoc retulerunt qui reginæ gloriam quæsiuerunt. Episcopus clericos omnes ad prandium inuitauit, & necessaria ministrauit.
units.tr: The king had ordered the bishop of Basel to bury the deceased queen solemnly. The bishop invited the regular and secular clergy to Basel. Accordingly, twelve hundred gathered, all carrying candles in their hands, and they solemnly met the queen in procession with precious ornament, and led her to the greater monastery. With three bishops celebrating divine service there, the queen's body, placed in a tomb, was raised up and shown to all those present; and after Mass it was lowered and buried with the weeping of the nobles. Those who sought the queen's glory reported this. The bishop invited all the clergy to dinner and provided what was necessary.

units.la: De Waltheri Rösselmanni sculteti Colmariensis parentibus & incrementis.
units.tr: On the parents and rise of Walther Rösselmann, mayor of Colmar.

units.la: WALTHERVS Rösselmann cerdo in villa Türincheim filium habuit Ioannem Rösselmann. Hic hospitio paterno non contentus, ad sculteturn Columbariensem se transtulit, cui fideliter seruiebat. Ea amoto, secundo & tertio seruiebat, & interdum sub iudicio præsidebat. Hic officium sculteti desiderans, modo quo potuit, obtinebat. In officio suos exaltabat, alios supprimebat. Cùm pauperes diutius id sustinere non possent, absolutionem communiter procurabant. Huic substituitur dominus de Racinhusen/ vir pius, deuotus & æquus. Io. Rösselmann depositus, in Ensisheim ad comitem Rudolfum de Habspurc se transtulit, ei seruiens. Laborabat quomodo possset Colmariam tradere in potestatem comitis de Habspurc.
units.tr: Walther Rösselmann, a butcher in the village of Türincheim, had a son, Johann Rösselmann. Not content with his father's house, Johann moved to the mayoralty of Colmar and served the mayor faithfully. When that mayor was removed, Johann served as second and then third in office, and sometimes presided at court. Desiring the office of mayor, he obtained it by whatever means he could. In office he exalted his own people and suppressed others. When the poor could no longer bear this for long, they commonly procured his removal. He was succeeded by Lord von Racinhusen, a pious, devout and fair man. Johann Rösselmann, deposed, went to Count Rudolf of Habsburg at Ensisheim and served him. He laboured to find a way to hand Colmar over into the power of the Count of Habsburg.

units.la: Post paucos annos dixit comiti: Domine, mittite pro consobrino vestro comite Gotfrido de Lauffinberg & suis militibus, & venite vnà ad Columbariam, & ego potenter vos intromittam. De inimicis nostris post hęc pro libito faciemus. Cōsensit comes. Iohannes Rößelmann amicis suis circum Columbariam commisit, vt cùm armis adsint, &c. Iohannes in vas vacuum se abscondit, Columbariam clam ingreditur, in curiam Decani fertur. Sequenti die circa diluculum, comitem Rudolfum cum suis, clam quibusdā iuuantibus, intromisit. Aduersarij Iohannis intelligentes hæc, aufugiunt, relictis omnibus quæ habebant, videlicet, sculteus, dominus de Rackinhusen/milites septem, ciues decem, quorum quilibet ditior erat Iohanne. Horum bona confiscabat & diuidebat. Et in hac gloria Ioannes pluribus annis apparebat.
units.tr: A few years later he said to the count: "Lord, send for your cousin Count Gottfried of Laufenberg and his knights, and come with them to Colmar, and I will powerfully let you in. Afterwards we will deal with our enemies as we please." The count agreed. Johann Rösselmann instructed his friends around Colmar that, when they were present with arms, and so on. Johann hid himself in an empty vat, secretly entered Colmar, and was carried into the dean's court. Early the next morning, at about dawn, he secretly let in Count Rudolf with his men, some of them helping in secret. Johann's opponents, understanding this, fled, leaving behind everything they had: the mayor, Lord von Racinhusen, seven knights and ten citizens, each of whom was richer than Johann. Johann confiscated their goods and divided them. And in this glory Johann continued to show himself for several years.

units.la: Anno M.CC.LXII, Dominus de Winegk, filius sororis domini de Horburc, cum multis militibus & terræ nobilibus, consentientibus multis ciuibus, Columbariensem ciuitatem intrare potentiam voluit. Sculteus hæc intelligens, eis in dextrario occurrit festinanter: hunc apprehensum in porta Steinenbruka atrociter occiderunt. Consanguinei sui hæc intelligētes, statim egressi plus quàm viginti nobiles occiderūt.
units.tr: In the year 1262, the Lord of Winegk, son of the sister of the Lord of Horburg, together with many knights and nobles of the land, and with many citizens consenting, wished to force an entry into the city of Colmar. The mayor, learning of this, hastily rode out on his warhorse to meet them. They seized him at the Steinenbrücke gate and cruelly killed him. His kinsmen, learning of this, immediately sallied out and killed more than twenty nobles.

units.la: Post annos duodecim, Rudolfus comes de Habspurc in regem eligitur Romanorum. Hic Waltherum, filium Ioannis Rößilman/ sculteturn in Columbaria fecit: Othonem de Ochsenstein/ nepotem ex sorore sua, Rudolfus aduocatum Alsatiæ prepositum. Sed sculteus & aduocatus terræ non per omnia concordabant. Aduocatus iubente rege, vel saltem conniuente, exactiones plurimas faciebat: sculteus & populus inuitè soluebant. Rex Rudolfus indignatus, militibus stipatus, Columbariam proficiscitur, sculteum depositurus. Sculteus præmonitus ciuitatem clausit, nec regem ingredi permisit.
units.tr: Twelve years later, Count Rudolf of Habsburg was elected King of the Romans. He made Walther, son of Johann Rösselmann, mayor of Colmar, and made Otto of Ochsenstein, his sister's grandson, provost of Alsace. But the mayor and the advocate of the land did not always agree. The advocate, at the king's command or at least with his connivance, imposed many exactions; the mayor and the people paid them unwillingly. King Rudolf, indignant, set out for Colmar with a band of soldiers, intending to depose the mayor. The mayor, forewarned, closed the city and did not allow the king to enter.

units.la: Rex Columbariam potenter obsedit. Regi nunciatur, Fridericum quendam Imperatorem in partibus inferioribus affectare regnum. Rex sibi timens, obsidionem Columbariensem soluit, & cum exercitu descendens, Fridericum cepit & igne cremauit. Inde ad obsidionem Columbariensem secundò perrexit, & ipsos cum conditionibus quibusdam ad gratiam suscepit. Sculteum Waltherū rex depositi, & Stammeheim sculteū præposuit, & eos maximis exactionibus turbauit. Stameheim sculteus in Columbaria residere non poterat: filiamstro suo officium committit, & diuersa turbatio in Columbaria quiescebat.
units.tr: The king laid a powerful siege to Colmar. It was reported to the king that a certain Frederick, calling himself emperor, was aiming at the kingdom in the lower regions. The king, fearing for his own position, lifted the siege of Colmar, and descending with an army, captured Frederick and burned him at the stake. From there he set out a second time for the siege of Colmar, and on certain conditions received the citizens back into his favour. The king deposed the mayor Walther and set Stammeheim over the city as mayor, and he troubled the citizens with the heaviest exactions. Mayor Stammeheim could not remain in Colmar, so he committed the office to his son-in-law, and the various disturbances in Colmar subsided.

units.la: Rege Rudolfo mortuo, Waltherus Rößelman / quondam sculteus, in summa paupertate constitutus, conduxit duodecim seruos vagos & inopes, cibum & vestes ministrans, per hos insidiaturus sculteo Stammeheim. Intelligens id sculteus, declinauit. Waltherus Rößelman consilio decani & aliorum amicorum, officium sculteti per violentiam occupat. Post hæc dominum de Hunnewilre / militem honestum, iuuenem, diuitem, bene parentatum, & filium eius iuuenem, sine occasione & caussa, contra Deum, homines & iustitiam interfecit, eius res diripuit, plus quàm ccc marcas inter suos distribuit. Dominos milites de Nortgassen/ Ilsich & dominum Ruslarium ciuitatem exire compulit, & res eorum confiscauit: regi se opposuit, & Columbariam Anshelmo de Rapoltstein tradidit.
units.tr: After King Rudolf died, Walther Rösselmann, the former mayor, reduced to utter poverty, hired twelve vagrant and destitute servants, providing them with food and clothing, intending to use them to ambush Mayor Stammeheim. The mayor, learning of this, kept out of the way. Walther Rösselmann, on the counsel of the dean and other friends, seized the office of mayor by violence. After this he killed, without occasion or cause, and against God, men and justice, Lord von Hunnewilre, an honourable, young, rich and well-connected knight, and his young son; he plundered their property and distributed more than 300 marks among his own people. He forced the knights Lord von Nortgassen, Ilsich and Lord Ruslar to leave the city and confiscated their goods. He defied the king and handed Colmar over to Anselm of Rappoltstein.

units.la: Bellum in Anshelmum Rapoltsteinij dominum.
units.tr: War against Anselm, Lord of Rappoltstein.

units.la: DOMINVS de Rapoltstein carnalem fratrem liberosq; fratris noscitur habuisse, qui cum eo dominium debuissent iure hæreditario possedisse. His hæreditatem dare noluit, sed de dominio, quantum potuit, extirpauit. Is dominus de Rapoltstein regem adiit Rudolfum cognatum suum, eiq; factam à fratre iniuriam flebiliter reuelauit. Rex his auditis dominum de Rapoltstein vocauit, eumq; rogauit, vt liberis fratrum suorum, nec non & fratri de hæreditate paterna propriam tribueret portionem. Tunc dominus de Rapoltstein domino regi taliter respondit: Si fratri meo liberisq; fratrum meorum hæreditatem diuiderem, inops ac pauper & sine dominio remanerem. Hoc enim facere nolo, nec in hoc alicuius precibus acquiescere.
units.tr: The Lord of Rappoltstein is known to have had a full brother and the children of that brother, who by hereditary right ought to have shared the lordship with him. He was unwilling to give them an inheritance, and drove them out of the lordship as far as he could. This Lord of Rappoltstein approached King Rudolf, his cousin, and tearfully complained of the injury done to him by his brother. The king, hearing this, summoned the Lord of Rappoltstein and asked him to grant a share of the paternal inheritance to the children of his brothers, and also to his brother. The Lord of Rappoltstein answered the lord king thus: "If I were to divide the inheritance with my brother and the children of my brothers, I would be left destitute, poor and without lordship. For I am unwilling to do this, nor will I yield to anyone's entreaties in the matter."

units.la: His completis, dixit rex domino de Baldeche, suo fidelissimo procuratori, quatenus assumptis ciuibus Columbariensibus & Keiserspergensibus, & aliis vicinis ciuitatum tatum ciuibus, Rapoltzstein fideliter obsideret. Hoc fideliter adimpleuit. Accepit enim ciues prænominatos, & Rapoltzstein obsedit: villam Bercheim per ignem destruxit: segetes & agros depopulatus est, & vineas aliquas extirpauit. Videns autem quòd ciues eum non fideliter adiuuarent, ab obsidione post triduum recedebat.
units.tr: After this, the king told the Lord of Baldeck, his most faithful agent, that he should take with him citizens of Colmar and Kaysersberg and citizens of other neighbouring cities, and faithfully besiege Rappoltstein. This he carried out faithfully. He took the citizens named and besieged Rappoltstein; he destroyed the village of Bergheim by fire, laid waste the crops and fields, and rooted out some vineyards. But seeing that the citizens were not helping him faithfully, he withdrew from the siege after three days.

units.la: Timens autem dominus de Rapolzstein regem, dominos vicinos suos adijt, eosq; supplicitér rogauit, vt nec eum nec suos propter aliquem infestarent. Hoc autem quidam de consilio regis amicabiliter admiserunt. Dominus de Horburc eius precibus acquiescere recusauit. Dominus de Rapolzstein de hoc fuit grauiter indignatus. Dominum de Horburc hostiliter impugnauit, & eius villas, quas poterat, exurebat. Super hoc rex fuit indignatus, in Alsatiam personaliter venit, & Rapolzstein potenter cum indigenis obsidebat. Septem autem de adiutoribus regis, vt dicebatur, eum morti tradere voluissent. Ordinatum enim sic fuerat, vt regi dicebatur, quòd pecuniæ quatuor bobonibus datæ fuissent, vt tentoria siue exercitus in quatuor partibus incendissent. Hinc autem strepitu facto, rex de obsidione subitò recessit, & se ab Alsatia separauit. Ordinauit autem quòd ciuitates in Cellinberg haberent equites l, qui impedirent, ne aliqui domino de Rapolzstein aliqua victualia seu necessaria ministrent. Post hæc mandauit rex eidem domino, vt ciuitates Alsatiæ congregaret, & in villa Gemer castrum ligneum fabricaret. Ipse autem intra octauam Petri & Pauli ciuitates congregauit, & castrum (vt sibi imperatum) inchoauit, & in breui tempore consummauit. Consummato castro milites ibi reliquerunt, & ad propria redierunt. Acta sunt hæc anno Domini, M. CC. LXXXVII.
units.tr: Fearing the king, however, the Lord of Rappoltstein approached his neighbouring lords and humbly asked them not to attack him or his people on any pretext. Some of the king's counsellors admitted this in a friendly way. The Lord of Horburg refused to yield to his entreaties, and the Lord of Rappoltstein was greatly angered by this. He attacked the Lord of Horburg with hostility and burned as many of his villages as he could. Upon this the king was indignant, came to Alsace in person, and besieged Rappoltstein powerfully with the local people. But seven of the king's helpers, so it was said, had intended to put him to death. For it had been arranged, as was reported to the king, that money had been given to four lads, so that they would set fire to the tents, or the army, in four places. A commotion arising from this, the king suddenly broke off the siege and withdrew from Alsace. He ordered that the cities should keep fifty horsemen at Zellenberg to prevent anyone from supplying the Lord of Rappoltstein with food or other necessities. After this the king ordered the same lord to gather the cities of Alsace and to build a wooden castle in the village of Gemer. He himself gathered the cities within the octave of Saints Peter and Paul, began the castle as he had been commanded, and finished it in a short time. When the castle was completed, the soldiers left it there and returned home. These things were done in the year of the Lord 1287.

units.la: Dominus de Rapolzstein intra Calendas Augusti, Galliam intrauit, ibiq; à domino de Blanchiberg cognato suo, pedites & equites accommodauit, noste prope villam Sigolzheim perducebat, & ibi eos in diuersis locis proinsidijs collocauit. Mane autem facto greges villæ pauci acceperunt, & velociter abierunt. Villani autem prædam insequuti, liberare pecora voluerunt. Igitur homines domini de Rapolzstein de insidijs egressi fuerunt, eosq; comprehenderunt, & eorum plus quàm CXXX ad propria perduxerunt. Homines de Horburc videntes prædam magnam, paucos homines ducentes, sine deliberatione prædam liberare volentes, similiter capiuntur, & çum aliis deducuntur.
units.tr: Before the calends of August the Lord of Rappoltstein entered France, and there from the Lord of Blanckenberg, his kinsman, he obtained foot soldiers and horsemen. He led them by night near the village of Sigolsheim and placed them in ambush at various points. When morning came, some of the village herds were taken and driven off quickly. The villagers, pursuing the booty, wanted to free the cattle. Thereupon the men of the Lord of Rappoltstein came out of the ambush, seized them, and led more than 130 of them back to their homes. The men of Horburg, seeing the great booty, came with only a few men and, without deliberation, wanting to free the spoil, were likewise captured and led away with the others.

units.la: Rudolfi regis quædam apud Moguntiam acta.
units.tr: The doings of King Rudolf at Mainz.

units.la: ANNO M. CC. LXXXVIII, rege Rudolfo existente Moguntiæ, frigus veniebat in ortu Solis, atq; frigus ipsum immodicè molestauit. Vidit igitur ex opposito domus in qua iacuit pistrinum multis viuis carbonib. abundare. Induit se rex sola tunica carbones viuos velociter visitauit. Hospita ignorans ipsum esse regem, sibi loquebatur in spiritu vehementi, dicens: Milites non debere ad mulieres pauperculas declinare. Dominus rex mulieri dicens humiliter loquebatur: O Domina nolite propter meam præsentiam turbari: sum enim antiquus miles, & omnia mea in seruitio vilissimi Rudolfi consumpsi, & contra bona promissa me patitur indigere. Mulier dixit: Sequimini regem Rudolfum vilissimum, qui totam terram destruxit, & omnes pauperes deuorauit? Hæc merito vos mala & alia comprehendunt. Rex dominæ dixit: Quæ mala vobis fecit? Mulier turpissimè regem vituperans atq; maledicens, cum magna cordis amaritudine respondebat: Ego & omnes pistores ciuitatis huius præter duos, per eum depauperati sumus, quòd temporibus nostris ad diuitias quondam habitas non possumus peruenire. Post hæc mulier dixit: Domine, recedatis: quia hic nos in nostris occupationibus retardatis. Rex autem propter verba mulieris recedere recusabat. De hoc mulier indignata, vas aquæ sustulit, prunas perfudit, & antiqui militis seu regis vestem enormiter deturpauit. Rex igitur fugit, & ad suum hospitium festinauit.
units.tr: In the year 1288, while King Rudolf was at Mainz, a cold wind was blowing at sunrise, and the cold was troubling him terribly. He saw opposite the house where he was lodging a bakery with many live coals in it. So the king, dressed only in a tunic, quickly visited the glowing coals. The hostess, not knowing he was the king, spoke to him with great vehemence, saying: "Soldiers ought not to go hanging about poor women." The lord king answered the woman humbly: "O madam, do not be disturbed by my presence. I am an old soldier, and I have spent all I had in the service of that most worthless Rudolf, and in return for the good things he promised, he allows me to be in want." The woman said: "Are you following that worthless King Rudolf, who has laid waste the whole land and devoured all the poor? These misfortunes and others justly overtake you." The king asked the woman: "What harm has he done you?" The woman, reviling and cursing the king most shamefully, answered with great bitterness of heart: "I and all the bakers of this city, except two, have been impoverished by him, so that in our times we cannot reach the wealth we once had." Then the woman said: "Sir, go away, for you are holding us up in our work here." But the king, because of the woman's words, refused to leave. Angered by this, the woman took a pail of water, drenched the coals, and shamefully fouled the clothing of the old soldier, that is, the king. The king then fled and hurried to his lodging.

units.la: Rex igitur cùm sederet ad mensam, dapifer sibi caput porci cum multis apponebat. Memor igitur rex beneficiorum quæ pistrix ei contulerat, ei retribuere cupiebat. Adiocans rex hospitam dixit ei: Hanc scutellam cum carnibus & quartale vini recipiatis, & vicinæ vestræ de antiquo milite deferatis. Agit enim ei gratias, quòd apud suos carbones de mane fuerat calefactus. His igitur peractis, recitauit rex qualiter
units.tr: So when the king sat down at table, his steward set before him a pig's head with many other dishes. The king, mindful of the kindnesses the baker-woman had shown him, wished to repay her. Calling the hostess, the king said to her: "Take this bowl with meat and a quart of wine, and bring them to your neighbour, the old soldier. For he thanks her, since he was warmed in the morning by her coals." When this was done, the king recounted how

units.la: E pistrix eum vituperauerat, atque maledixerat, & ad risum omnes magnum concitauit. Pistrix autem intellexit, quòd rex fuerat quem vituperauerat, vltra modum doluit: regem adijt, & vt sibi remitteret illãtam illi iniuriam, supplicitèr deprecatur. Rex autem remittere, nisi priùs eum vituperaret, sicut priùs fecerat in occulto, non volebat. Hoc mulier fecit, & domini sui voluntatem fideliter adimpleuit, & ad risum plurimos prouocauit.
units.tr: the baker-woman had reviled and cursed him, and this set everyone laughing loudly. But the baker-woman, learning that the man she had reviled was the king, was greatly distressed. She went to the king and humbly begged him to pardon the injury she had done him. The king, however, would not forgive her unless she reviled him again, just as she had done in secret before. She did this, faithfully carrying out her master's wishes, and provoked great laughter.

units.la: Retulit frater Alradus, prior fratrum Argentinensium. In Alsatia dicebatur, quòd Iudæi conquesti fuissent regi Rudolfo, quòd Christiani plus x l Iudeos sine causa turpiter occidissent. Christiani autem conquesti fuerunt de Iudæis, quod seruum atque Christianum in die parasceue in cellario, occulte atq; Christianis ignorantibus, occidissent. Iudæi regi Rudolfo, vt eis de illis de Wesela atq; Popardia iusticiam faceret, & eos à periculo liberaret mortis, & ipsorum Rabbi, id est supremum magistrum, cui schola Iudæorum & honores diuinos impendere videbantur, quem rex captiuauerat à captiuitate carceris liberaret, viginti sibi millia marcarum promiserunt.
units.tr: Brother Alradus, prior of the Friars of Strasbourg, related this. In Alsace it was said that the Jews had complained to King Rudolf that the Christians had shamefully killed more than forty Jews without cause. The Christians, on the other hand, complained of the Jews, because they had secretly killed a Christian servant in a cellar on Good Friday, without the Christians knowing. The Jews promised King Rudolf twenty thousand marks, so that he would do justice to them against the men of Wesel and Poppard, and free them from the danger of death, and so that he would release from prison their rabbi, that is, their chief master, to whom the Jewish school and divine honours seemed to be given, and whom the king had taken captive.

units.la: Rex Iudæorum petitionem exaudiuit, Iudæum captiuum libertati restituit, illos de Wesela atq; Popardia in marcis bis mille condemnauit, & eos à mortis periculo liberauit. Insuper fecit rex dominum Archiepiscopum Moguntinum solenniter prædicare, quòd Christiani Iudæis iniuriam maximam intulissent, & quod bonus Wernherus, qui à Iudæis occisus communiter dicebatur, qui pro diuino à quibusdam Christianis simplicibus colebatur, deberet igne cremari, & cinis corporis eius in ventum dispergi, & ad nihilum dissipari. In hac prædicatione domini Archiepiscopi plus quàm quingenti Iudei in armis sederunt, vt si aliquis Christianus in contrarium dicere voluisset, ipsum eum suis gladijs occidissent.
units.tr: The king heard the Jews' petition, restored the captive Jew to liberty, condemned the men of Wesel and Poppard to a fine of two thousand marks, and freed them from the danger of death. Moreover, the king had the lord Archbishop of Mainz publicly proclaim that the Christians had done the greatest injury to the Jews, and that the good Werner, who was commonly said to have been killed by the Jews, and whom some simple Christians venerated as a saint, ought to be burned with fire, and his ashes scattered to the wind and reduced to nothing. During this proclamation of the lord Archbishop, more than five hundred Jews sat under arms, so that if any Christian had wanted to speak against it, they would have killed him with their swords.

units.la: Proditio vrbis Colmariensis, & eiusdem per Adolfum Casarem recuperatio.
units.tr: The betrayal of the city of Colmar, and its recovery by Adolf the Caesar.

units.la: ANNO M. CC. XCIII, quarto Idus Septembris, Scultetus Columbariensis ignorantibus Senatoribus & ciuibus, Anshelmum de Rapolzstein aduocat, eiq; ciuitatem tradit, intromissis multis armatis, ac in cœmiterium duƈtis. Ciuibus dormientibus compulsantur campanæ: concurrunt ciues ad cœmiterium: pedites armatos inueniunt: terrentur: quid faciant ignorant. Ciues omnes per præconem vocantur, dicentes: Adest nobis amicus noster, D. Anshelmus de Rapolzstein, volens nos corpore & rebus iuuare. Intellexit enim quòd inimici nostri vellent nos grauiter perturbare. Venit igitur, vt ipse nobis & nos ei fidelitatem iuramento firmemus. Subiunxit: Leuate manus vestras & iurate, quod & fecerunt.
units.tr: In the year 1293, on the fourth day before the Ides of September, the Schultheiss of Colmar, without the knowledge of the senators and citizens, summoned Anshelm of Rappoltstein and handed the city over to him. Many armed men were admitted and led into the churchyard. While the citizens were asleep, the bells were rung. The citizens ran together to the churchyard and found armed foot soldiers there. They were terrified and did not know what to do. All the citizens were summoned by a herald, who said: "Our friend, the lord Anshelm of Rappoltstein, is here, wishing to help us with his person and goods. For he has learned that our enemies wish to disturb us gravely. He has come, so that he and we may bind each other by oath of fidelity." He added: "Raise your hands and swear." And they did so.

units.la: Videns dominus de Rapolzstein paucos fidelitatem iurasse, magistris Zunftarum præcipit, vt suos singulos ad singula loca vocarent: à quibus singulis petunt fideliter iurari: quod multi fecerunt inuiti. Expelluntur qui id facere recusant, milites Rustarius & domini de Nortgassen, & ex ciuibus plures diuites & honesti.
units.tr: The lord of Rappoltstein, seeing that only a few had sworn fidelity, ordered the masters of the guilds to summon their members one by one to separate places, and from each of them he demanded a faithful oath. Many did so unwillingly. Those who refused to do so were expelled: the knights Rustarius and the lords of Nortgassen, and several wealthy and respectable citizens.

units.la: Rex Adolfus reginam Brisacum mittit: ipse cum exercitu versus Coloniam proficiscitur. Ciues Columbarienses, dominica, vigilia exaltationis Crucis in montana egressi, vinum suum nondum maturum colligunt. Dominus de Rapolzstein villam Türckheim prædatur, pecoraq; abigit in domicilium suum Wilre. Columbarienses cum gaudio reuertuntur, & se præparant, quo ampliora colligant, & sibi prospiciant. Rex Adolfus hæc audiens, Aduocatum præmittit. Hic in Sletstat plurimis hominibus secum assumptis, vallem Vrbis, quæ sub castro Hohenac est, ingreditur, villas domini de Rapolstein succendit, homines capit, pecora tollit, cum gaudio redit. In Wintzenheim & Ongersheim exitum Columbariensium præstolatur. Columbarienses egredi non audebant. Rex cum exercitu Rapperschuiler obsedit, vineas destruit ac domos. Post dies decem Columbariam versus proficiscitur, molendinarum fluuium deriuat alio, singula deuastat, præter leprosorium. Ciues vallis S. Gregorij ad Wilre pergunt, vinum colligunt, & ad propria deducunt. Columbarienses licet obsessi, ex vernaculis viginti mittunt Wilrensibus subsidio. Ciues Gregorianæ vallis secundò veniunt ad Wilre, quos incautos Wilrenses & Columbarienses obruunt,
units.tr: King Adolf sent the queen to Breisach, and he himself set out with his army towards Cologne. On the Sunday, the vigil of the Exaltation of the Cross, the citizens of Colmar went out into the mountains and gathered their wine, which was not yet ripe. The lord of Rappoltstein plundered the village of Türckheim and drove the cattle off to his stronghold at Wilre. The citizens of Colmar returned joyfully and prepared themselves to gather more and to provide for themselves. King Adolf, hearing this, sent ahead his advocate. He, taking many men with him to Sletstadt, entered the valley of the city which lies below the castle of Hohenack, burned the villages of the lord of Rappoltstein, seized the men, carried off the cattle, and returned in triumph. At Wintzenheim and Ongersheim he waited for the Colmarians to come out. The Colmarians did not dare to go out. The king with his army besieged Rappoltsweiler, destroyed the vineyards and the houses. After ten days he set out for Colmar, diverted the river that drove the mills into another channel, and laid waste everything except the leper-house. The citizens of the valley of St Gregory went to Wilre, gathered the wine, and carried it home. The Colmarians, though besieged, sent twenty of their native men to the men of Wilre as reinforcements. The citizens of the valley of St Gregory came a second time to Wilre, and the men of Wilre and the Colmarians, falling upon them while they were unguarded,

units.la: Adolfus Colmariam recuperat. Vrbis Gallia profiscitur. runt, occidunt & capiunt. Aduocatus terrae dominum de Berckheim, cum D hominibus contra Wilrenses mittit. Dominus de Berckheim vallem S. Gregorij ingressus, duas machinas magnas, lapides proijcientes: & Cattum, videlicet instrumentum quo turres destruuntur, accepit, Wilre obsedit, paucis diebus obtinuit castrum, & castellum funditus euertit. Hinc cum eiusdem machinis ad Gemer profectus, quod ex prima obsidione relictum fuit, penitus deuastauit.
units.tr: Adolf recovers Colmar. He sets out from the city toward Gaul. ...ran, killed and captured them. The advocate of the land sent the lord of Bergheim with five hundred men against the men of Wilre. The lord of Bergheim entered the valley of St Gregory, and took two great engines that threw stones, and a cattus, that is, the instrument by which towers are demolished. He besieged Wilre, took the castle within a few days, and razed the stronghold to the ground. Then, with the same engines, he went on to Gemar, which had been left over from the first siege, and utterly laid it waste.

units.la: Adolfo regi cum Principibus supradictis, comitibus, nobilib. libertae conditionis, militibus suis dominis seruientibus, ex exercitu in obsidione sex septimanarum, vix decem homines morte naturali obierunt, etiam vix decem a persequutoribus interfecti.
units.tr: Of King Adolf's army, with the princes mentioned above, the counts, the free nobles, and the knights serving their lords, during a siege of six weeks, scarcely ten men died a natural death, and scarcely ten were killed by their pursuers.

units.la: Coloniensis tentorium, x l in latitudinem, centum pedes in longitudinem habuit, & c c equos phaleratos. Maguntinus, Spirensis, & Basilien-sis episcopi in eodem exercitu fuerunt, quod singulis annis habet x x millia marcarum argenti. Comes Burgundiae feuda sua ab eo recepit, seruitiumq; suum obtulit. Cui rex respondit: Iam opus auxilio non habere, sed cum fuerit opus, se eius auxilia petituram. Dux Austriae in auxilium a rege vocatus, respondit: Si principes in obsidione defecerint, mihi significato, & ego veniens obsidebo quamcunq; voluerit ciuitatem.
units.tr: The tent of the Archbishop of Cologne was forty paces in width and a hundred feet in length, and he had two hundred caparisoned horses. The bishops of Mainz, Speyer, and Basel were in the same army, the Archbishop of Mainz having an annual income of twenty thousand marks of silver. The Count of Burgundy received his fiefs from the king and offered his service. The king answered him that he did not need help now, but that when he did, he would ask for his aid. The Duke of Austria, called by the king to help, replied: "If the princes give up the siege, let me know, and I will come and besiege whatever city you wish."

units.la: Vnus exercitus regis Gemar obsidebat. Secundus exercitus, videlicet, episcopus Basilien-sis & Comes Phirretarum, vnam partem ciuitatis Columbariae obsidebant. Tertius autem, episcopi & principes supradicti. Hi diuitijs, gloria & honore caeteris antecellebant. In obsidione hac regis exercitus bonis omnibus abundabat. Annus fuit calidus & siccus, vinum optimum. Basilien-ses exercitui quaeq; bona & necessaria ministrabant.
units.tr: One army of the king was besieging Gemar. The second army, namely the Bishop of Basel and the Count of Pfirt, were besieging one part of the city of Colmar. The third army was that of the bishops and princes mentioned above. These surpassed the others in wealth, glory, and honour. In this siege the king's army abounded in all goods. The year was hot and dry, and the wine excellent. The men of Basel supplied the army with all goods and necessities.

units.la: Columbarien-ses vinum & bladum sufficientia habebant. Quartale frumenti vendebatur septem solidis: sed quartale farinae pro libra, ob aquam molendinorum alio deriuatam. Pauperes in mortarijs frumentum triuerunt, alij in molendinis speciarum: alij rotis molendinorum homines adhibuerunt, & circumire cogebant. Duas molas molentes habebant monachi de Peris, quarum vna Sculteto, altera domino de Rapoltstein seruiebat: sed nec his farinam necessariam potuerunt ministrare. Vtebatur dominus de Rapoltstein singulis diebus x i i quartalibus. Hic sex fratribus Praedicatoribus secum conclusis panem albu pro sex denarijs quotidie ministrabat. Costa autem circumferentiae hanc longitudinem comprehendit.
units.tr: The Colmarians had enough wine and grain. A quart of wheat sold for seven shillings, but a quart of flour went for a pound, because the water had been diverted from the mills. The poor ground wheat in mortars, and others in spice mills. Some people were forced to work the mill wheels and walk around them. The monks of Pairis had two millstones grinding, one serving the Schultheiss and the other the lord of Rappoltstein, but even these could not supply the flour that was needed. The lord of Rappoltstein used twelve quarts a day. Shut up with him were six Preaching friars, to whom he gave white bread for six pennies a day. The circuit of the wall measured this length.

units.la: Solenne tentorium rex non erexit, nec prandia nec coenas solennes faciebat: tantum x i i vasa vini & alia dominis quotidie ministrabat. Captus est dapifer haec referens in equo, Marscalcus quoq; regis, & nobilis quidam interfectus.
units.tr: The king did not raise a solemn tent, nor did he hold solemn dinners or suppers. He supplied only twelve vessels of wine and other things daily to the lords. The seneschal, who was reporting these things, was captured on horseback, and so was the king's marshal, and a certain noble was killed.

units.la: Tres ciues pauperes defectum diutius ferre nolentes, dixerunt: Propter Deum & iustitiam periculo nos committamus, & ciuitatē ad verum Dominum transferamus. Consilium charis & fidis indicarunt, qui omnes approbarunt. Significant hoc regi, qui gauisus auxilium promisit. Ex ciuibus ditioribus multi pauperibus consenserunt. Hi omnes regi significant, vt per balistarios suos cogat exire Columbarien-ses, prouocando. Cum autem domini ciuitatis fuerint egressi, claudemus portas, & dominos vobis committemus, ac deinde in ciuitatem vos mittemus sine periculo. Rex, vt ciues consuluerunt, fecit: sed dominus de Rapoltstein & Sculteus praemoniti, ciuitatem egredi noluerunt.
units.tr: Three poor citizens, unwilling to bear the lack any longer, said: "For God's sake and for justice let us risk danger, and hand the city over to the true Lord." They revealed the plan to dear and faithful friends, who all approved. They signalled this to the king, who, rejoicing, promised help. Many of the wealthier citizens agreed with the poor. All of them told the king that through his crossbowmen he should compel the Colmarians to come out by provoking them. "When the lords of the city have gone out, we will shut the gates, hand the lords over to you, and then send you into the city without danger." The king did as the citizens advised. But the lord of Rappoltstein and the Schultheiss, forewarned, refused to go out.

units.la: Secundò mandarunt regi, quòd domum circa diem proponerent incendere: & hominibus currentibus ad ignem, regem intrare permitterent violenter: sed nec id successit. Audiens hoc episcopus Argentinensis, venit cum c c militibus, volens fideliter iuuare Columbarien-ses. Cumq; senatores de his deliberarent: venit communitas ciuitatis, clamans: Nolumus plures homines introduci.
units.tr: Secondly, they sent word to the king that they would set a house on fire at a set time, and that, when the people ran to the fire, they would let the king enter by force. But this also did not succeed. Hearing of it, the bishop of Strasbourg came with two hundred knights, wishing to help the Colmarians faithfully. While the senators were deliberating on these matters, the commonalty of the city came, shouting: "We do not want more men brought in."

units.la: Dixerunt pauperes sumptis armis: Ad coemiterium conueniamus, & quod decretum fuerit, faciamus. Hoc facto, dixerunt: Claues portarum accipiamus, & cum diligentia conseruemus. Decanus & Sculteus responderunt: Claues, cum volueritis, praesentabimus: volentes populi voluntatem impedire. Vulgus verbis eorum non acquieuit, & ad portas vrbis subitò corruerunt, claues à portarum custodibus perluerunt. Claues à custodibus perterritis subitò exhibentur.
units.tr: The poor, taking up arms, said: "Let us gather at the cemetery and do what has been decided." This done, they said: "Let us take the keys of the gates and keep them carefully." The dean and the Schultheiss replied: "We will present the keys whenever you wish," meaning to hinder the people's will. The crowd did not yield to their words, but suddenly rushed to the city gates and snatched the keys from the gate-keepers. The keys were then handed over at once by the frightened custodians.

units.la: Habitis clauibus, ad Curiam, in qua morabatur dominus de <bl>Lichtenberg</bl>, subitò conuenerunt, violenter portas aperiunt, & dominum quærunt. Hic turbam armatorum videns, ad dominum de Rapoltstein declinauit, recitans quæ viderat & acciderant. Ambo perterriti ad fratres Minores diuertunt, consilium abeis quærunt, quid agendum existat. Hi verò eis consulere nequiuerunt. Dominus de <bl>Lichtenberg</bl> cum decem viris, per murum ciuitatis quasi nudus euasit.
units.tr: With the keys in hand, they suddenly gathered at the court where the lord of Lichtenberg was staying, forcibly opened the doors, and sought the lord. He, seeing the crowd of armed men, turned aside to the lord of Rappoltstein and told him what he had seen and what had happened. Both, terrified, turned to the Franciscans and sought their counsel on what must be done. But the friars could not advise them. The lord of Lichtenberg escaped through the city wall with ten men, almost naked.

units.la: Post paucos dies cum x l equitaturis ad Rapoltstein venit, volens eos fideliter adiuuare. Ciues verò non crediderunt ei per omnia, sed claues fidelibus mandabant, neminem ingredi vel egredi liberè voluerunt. Dominus de Lichtenberg timens, ciues Rapperschuilre idem facturos quod Columbarienses, recessit ab eis, nec amplius eos iuuare voluit. Dominus de Rapoltstein in domo Minorum se continuit, & in quibusdam angulis latitauit.
units.tr: A few days later he came to Rappoltstein with forty mounted men, wishing to help them faithfully. But the citizens did not trust him in everything. They sent the keys to loyal men and would not allow anyone to enter or leave freely. The lord of Lichtenberg, fearing that the citizens of Rappoltsweiler would do what the Colmarians had done, withdrew from them and no longer wished to help. The lord of Rappoltstein kept himself within the house of the Minorites and hid in some corners.

units.la: Ciues Columbarienses, cùm Dominos in Curijs non inuenerunt, arma & equos abstulerunt. Serui dominorum aufugiunt, atque quò possunt se abscondunt. Seruos inuentos ciues comprehendunt, ac in vincula conijciunt. Scultetus & filius cum quærentibus circumibant. Cui amicus quispiam dixit: Recedite de via, priusquam satellites regis vos comprehendant: statimq; recesserunt. Dominus de Rapoltstein vix tandem à quærentibus inuenitur, capitur & custoditur.
units.tr: When the citizens of Colmar did not find the lords in their courts, they took away arms and horses. The lords' servants fled and hid wherever they could. The citizens seized the servants they found and threw them into chains. The Schultheiss and his son went about with the searchers. A friend said to him: "Get off the road before the king's men catch you," and at once they withdrew. The lord of Rappoltstein was at last found with difficulty by the searchers, and was captured and guarded.

units.la: Capto domino de Rapoltstein, claues portarum per honestum ciuem, dictum Rebman, cum ciuitatis dominio ad regem transmiserunt. Qua re gauisi sunt interni & externi, ac vniuersus regis exercitus. Dominus episcopus Argentinensis turbatus, ad suos se transtulit festinanter.
units.tr: With the lord of Rappoltstein captured, they sent the keys of the gates, together with the lordship of the city, to the king through an honest citizen named Rebman. Insiders and outsiders alike rejoiced at this, and the whole royal army with them. The lord bishop of Strasbourg, disturbed, hastily withdrew to his men.

units.la: Ipsa nocte, dominum de Rapoltstein & cæteros captos ciues, Regi, id petenti, transmittunt. Non tradito Sculteto, indignatus Rex per præconem proclamari iussit: Centum libras habiturum, qui Scultetum præsentaret. Timens valde Sculte tus, pauperis vestem induit, clam ciuitatem egreditur, quatuor eum præcedentibus, vel sequentibus: vergens versus munitiones domini Argentinensis. Viam noluerat optimè, & Egesheim castellum in oculis habuit. Dum vsq; ad tertiam horam in sylvis & deuijs aberrasset, occurrit ei mulier. Hæc duobus viris præsentem esse Sculte tum ostendit. Hi gauisi, eum ceperunt, Regi præsentandum. Sed milites episcopi Basiliensis violenter Scultetum eripiunt, & in castrum <bl>Schwartzenburg</bl> transferunt. Hi duo viri regem adituri, obuio cuidam dixerunt, quid acciderit. Hic illicò Regi nunciat: cui Rex equum pro munere confert. Post hæc prædicti duo ciues Regi deferunt quid acciderit: regisque iussu à procuratore centum libras recipiunt.
units.tr: That same night they handed over the lord of Rappoltstein and the other captured citizens to the king, who asked for them. Since the Schultheiss had not been handed over, the indignant king ordered a herald to proclaim that whoever presented the Schultheiss would receive one hundred pounds. The Schultheiss, greatly afraid, put on a poor man's clothing and secretly left the city, with four men going before him or following him, heading for the fortifications of the lord bishop of Strasbourg. He did not know the road well, and kept Egisheim castle in sight. After he had wandered in the woods and by-paths until the third hour, a woman met him and pointed him out to two men as the Schultheiss. Rejoicing, they seized him to present him to the king. But soldiers of the bishop of Basel violently snatched the Schultheiss away and carried him to the castle of Schwarzenburg. The two men, on their way to the king, told a man they met what had happened. He at once reported it to the king, who gave him a horse as a reward. After this the two citizens reported to the king what had happened, and by the king's order received one hundred pounds from the procurator.

units.la: Ab episcopo Basiliensi Scultetum Rex postulat: Episcopus dare recusat, irregularitatis timore. Promittit Rex animam Sculteti à corpore non separare.
units.tr: The king demanded the Schultheiss from the bishop of Basel. The bishop refused to give him up, fearing irregularity. The king promised not to separate the Schultheiss's soul from his body.

units.la: Rex Scultetum vinibus personis committit, iubet vt rotæ imponatur, & perticæ impositæ in castris & ciuitatibus erigatur, ac sic circumducatur, vt ab omni populo videatur: post vesperam deponatur, & custodiatur in cippo. Martyrium rotæ requiem reputabat. Custodes eum multis contumelijs affecerunt: ex eorum cyphis eum bibere noluerunt.
units.tr: The king committed the Schultheiss to men in charge of his bonds, and ordered that he be fastened to a wheel, and that a pole be raised with him on it in the castles and cities, and so be carried round to be seen by all the people. After vespers he was to be taken down and kept in the stocks. He reckoned the martyrdom of the wheel a rest. His guards treated him with many insults; they refused to let him drink from their cups.

units.la: Rex bigam misit, vt Scultetum ad se deducerent: vestimenta Sculteti & rotam bigæ impositerunt, & eum ad bigam ligatum currere post eam coegerunt. Manum eius in modum iurantium ad stipitem ligauerunt, vt significarent, eum sæpius peierasse.
units.tr: The king sent a two-horse chariot to bring the Schultheiss to him. They put the Schultheiss's clothes and the wheel on the chariot and, binding him to it, forced him to run behind it. They tied his hand to a post in the manner of men taking an oath, to signify that he had often sworn falsely.

units.la: Pater huius dictus est Ioannes Rößelman, etiam Sculteus Columbariensis. Auus eius dictus est Waltherus Rößelman, de quibus suprà.
units.tr: The father of this man was called John Rösselman, also Schultheiss of Colmar. His grandfather was called Walther Rösselman, about whom see above.

units.la: Rex cum exercitu ad Gemar proficiscitur: dominus de Rapoltstein & alij captı vnà ducuntur, iudiciū expectatur, precibus dominorum iudicium differtur. Res domini de Rapoltstein in tres partes diuiduntur: quarum vna domino Henrico, altera filio fratris, tertiam ipse in suam traheret potestatem. Ob id hæredes omne ius in Gemere & hæreditatem in regiam potestatem tradiderunt.
units.tr: The king set out with his army for Gemar. The lord of Rappoltstein and the other captives were led along with him, and judgement was awaited, though it was postponed at the entreaty of the lords. The goods of the lord of Rappoltstein were divided into three parts: one was given to Lord Henry, another to his brother's son, and the third he drew into his own power. Therefore the heirs handed over all rights in Gemar and the inheritance to royal authority.

units.la: Infra octauam sancti Martini, dominus de Rapoltstein, in equo catenatus, & triginta vel amplius serui, duobus curribus ligati, ducebantur. Cùm dominus de Rapoltstein Columbariam transiret, fletu & eiulatu cordis dolorem & amaritudinem indicabat. Ducuntur Brisacum, hinc in castrum Sueuiæ Acheln.
units.tr: Within the octave of St Martin, the lord of Rappoltstein, chained on horseback, and thirty or more servants tied to two carts, were led away. As the lord of Rappoltstein passed through Colmar, he showed his grief and bitterness by weeping and wailing from the heart. They were taken to Breisach, and from there to the castle of Achalm in Swabia.

units.la: Hic matrem habuit filiam comitis de Froburg, patrem cognatum domini de <bl>Blanckenberg</bl>, virum pulchrum, largum, mitem, benignum, omni laude dignum: hic iuuenis moritur. Mater fuit longa corpore, facie pulchra, crine candido, voce dulci, amabili, decora. Hæc cum bonis suis se ad claustrum Minorum prope <bl>Schaf-</bl> <bl>hausen</bl> transtulit, vitam ibidem cum sacris virginibus consummauit. Filiam habuit vnicam, filios quinq; elegantes. Primus dominio male præfuit: secundus vero peius: tertius iste Anshelmus præsidebat.
units.tr: His mother was the daughter of the count of Froburg; his father was a kinsman of the lord of Blankenberg, a handsome, generous, gentle, kind man, worthy of all praise, who died as a young man. The mother was tall, with a beautiful face, white hair, and a sweet, pleasing, and graceful voice. She transferred herself with her goods to the Minorite cloister near Schaffhausen and there ended her life among holy virgins. She had one daughter and five elegant sons. The first governed the lordship badly, the second worse; the third, this Anselm, presided over it.

units.la: Habebat plerunque triginta balistarios, homines tyrannos, quibus vicinos suos grauiter lædebat. Recepit enim homines ære grauatos alieno, & in malitia obstinatos, dicens, quòd seruus habens animam, nequaquam sibi seruire posset. Ob id Deus abstulit ei corpus, res, gloriam & honorem. ccc marcas in redditibus habebat, & tamen suos magnis exactionibus grauabat. A subditis quartam partem vini auferebat. Fratrem suum Henricum & filium fratris sui, de legitimis possessionibus expulit. Hoc vnum bene gessit, quòd claustrum sancti Ioannis in <bl>Vnderlinde-</bl> <bl>n</bl> fideliter defendit, quòd pater eius multis bonis, & iure patronatus sancti Martini, donauerat. Sororem suam in eodem claustro existentem, exaudiuit in omnibus.
units.tr: He usually kept thirty crossbowmen, tyrannical men, by whom he grievously harmed his neighbours. For he took in men burdened with debt and obstinate in malice, saying that a slave who has a soul could in no way serve him. Therefore God took from him his body, goods, glory and honour. He had three hundred marks in revenues, yet he burdened his subjects with great exactions and took a quarter of their wine. He expelled his brother Henry and his brother's son from their lawful possessions. The one thing he did well was to defend faithfully the cloister of St John at Underlinden, to which his father had given many goods and the right of patronage of St Martin. He obeyed his sister, who was living in the same cloister, in all things.

units.la: Quid Adolfus recuperata Colmaria porrò in Alfatia egerit.
units.tr: What Adolf did next in Alsace after recovering Colmar.

units.la: <bl>R</bl>Ege negotijs circa Columbariam completis, viam suam versus Gemer & <bl>Herstein</bl> dirigire volente: occurrerunt ei cives Argentinenses, ipsum supplicitèr deprecantes, vt faceret pacem iuramento generaliter confirmati. Ad hæc Rex dicitur respondisse: Quando locum vestrum præcessi, hoc vos rogaui: sed vos pacem habere nullatenus voluistis. Nunc igitur vos defendite, si potestis. Secundam petitionem porrexerunt, dicentes: Domine Rex, rogamus vt castellum <bl>Herstein</bl> non obsideatis, quia nobis in maximum cederet detrimentum. Rex super hoc deliberato consilio respondit: Dominus in <bl>Herstein</bl> me diffidauit, res Imperij prout potuit, impugnauit: hunc & ego teneor impugnare. Vos verò in rebus non impugnabo: dummodò res inimici mei de vestris limitibus extirpetis. Cives regi responderunt: Muros ciuitatis <bl>Erstein</bl>, pro satisfactione funditus euertemus. Rex respondit, Per hoc mihi non est satisfactum, quia volo corpus inimici mei, res, & omnia quæ possidet in regiam trahere potestatem. Cives Argentinenses super his deliberauerunt, & quid sibi responderent inuenire minimè potuerunt.
units.tr: When he had finished his business around Kolmar and was about to direct his route toward Geberschweier and Herrenstein, the citizens of Strasbourg met him and earnestly begged him to make peace, which they had confirmed by a general oath. To this the king is said to have replied: "When I came before your city, I asked you this very thing, but you were in no way willing to have peace. Now, then, defend yourselves, if you can." They made a second request, saying: "Lord King, we ask that you not besiege the castle of Herrenstein, for this would cause us the greatest harm." The king, after deliberating on this, answered: "The lord of Herrenstein has defied me, and has attacked the property of the Empire as far as he could; I am bound to attack him as well. As for you, I will not attack your property, provided you root out my enemy's property from your borders." The citizens replied to the king: "We will tear down the walls of the town of Erstein to the ground as satisfaction." The king answered: "That does not satisfy me, because I want to bring under my royal power my enemy's person, his property, and everything he possesses." The citizens of Strasbourg deliberated on these matters, but they could by no means find what answer to give him.

units.la: Quidam de Consiliarijs confidentes in sua multitudine ac potentia, cæteris dixerunt: Opponamus nos ei, & possumus eum faciliter de nostris finibus extirpare. Ad hæc Sculletus: Ego explorando castra Regis fideliter circumiui, & vt mihi videtur, inueni plus quàm mille dextrarios, equis minoribus minimè computatis. Habet insuper Rex singulis septimanis atque mensibus de ciuitatibus homines multos, & si placuerit pauciores. Claudet insuper Rex Rhenum per principes quos habet, vt ad nos nihil poterit peruenire. Insuper claudet vias nobis, quòd commodè non poterimus ingredi vel egredi ciuitatem. Præterea, si exercitus regis requieuit prope <bl>Herstein</bl>, nos singulis diebus visitabit, & quicquid extra muros fuerit, totaliter deuastabit. Et vt mihi videtur, si obsessi rectè fuerimus, infra breue tempus in ciuitate ne tertia pars pauperum remanebit. Sed si multò pauciores haberet, quàm habeat, & potenter nos obsidere non posset. Hæc mala & maiora nobis faceret, possessiones nostras alienis traderet, & nos sine pugna penè nostris omnibus defraudaret. Præterea Rubiacam cum paucis hominibus obsideret, & illa propter homicidium militis Zedellarij nouiter factum in ea, sibi traderetur, & sic ciuitatem cum suis fautoribus obtineret, & fautores episcopi Argentinensis deleret. Sic Rubiacam in perpe-tuum retineret.
units.tr: Some of the councillors, trusting in their numbers and their strength, said to the others: "Let us oppose him; we can easily drive him from our borders." To this Sculletus replied: "I have faithfully gone around the king's camp to spy it out, and, as it seems to me, I have found more than a thousand horsemen, not counting the lighter horses. Moreover, the king has many men coming in from the towns every week and every month, and if he pleases, fewer. Furthermore, the king will close the Rhine by means of the princes he has, so that nothing can reach us from there. In addition, he will close our roads, so that we cannot conveniently go into or out of the city. Besides, if the king's army rests near Herrenstein, it will visit us every day and completely lay waste whatever lies outside the walls. And as it seems to me, if we were besieged, within a short time not a third of the poor would remain in the city. Yet even if he had far fewer men than he has, he could not besiege us effectively. These and worse evils he would inflict on us: he would hand over our possessions to strangers and rob us of nearly all of them without a fight. Moreover, he would besiege Rappoltsweiler with a small force, and that town, because of the recent murder of a Zedellarian soldier within it, would be surrendered to him; thus he would hold the town together with its supporters and destroy the supporters of the bishop of Strasbourg. In this way he would keep Rappoltsweiler forever."

units.la: Cùm hæc & his similia ponderassent ciues Argentinenses, fideliter consuluerant Domino, quòd veniam à rege quæreret & obtineret: quia si non faceret, tota sua progenies de terra breuiter deleretur. Venerabilis D. Conradus de Liechtenberg episcopus Argentinensis in arcto positus, Dominum de Liechtenberg & comitem de Werde vocauit, & cum eis ad pedes regis humiliter se prostrauit, ab eo veniam cum gratia postulauit. Rex misericordia plenus eos hilariter exaudiuit. Iniunxit autem rex domino præposito, dicto de Liechtenberg, & comiti de Werde, quòd secum in expensis propriis pergerent, donec ampliorem gratiam ab eo ac Principibus obtinerent. Hoc facto, Rex ac Principes, ac ciuitatum rectores pacem pro viribus se facturos, iuramento fideliter firmauerunt.
units.tr: When the citizens of Strasbourg had weighed these and similar matters, they faithfully sought the counsel of the Lord, and decided that they should ask the king for pardon and obtain it, for if they did not, their whole posterity would soon be wiped from the earth. The venerable lord Conrad of Lichtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg, placed in a tight spot, summoned the lord of Lichtenberg and the count of Werd, and with them humbly prostrated himself at the king's feet, and begged him for pardon along with favour. The king, full of mercy, graciously heard them. He ordered, however, that the lord provost, the aforesaid lord of Lichtenberg, and the count of Werd should go with him at their own expense until they obtained greater favour from him and from the princes. When this was done, the king, the princes, and the rulers of the cities faithfully confirmed by oath that they would make peace as far as they were able.

units.la: Causa funesti belli inter Gallia & Angliæ reges: in quo Cæsar Adolfus Anglorum partes sequutus est.
units.tr: The cause of the deadly war between the kings of France and England, in which Emperor Adolf took the side of the English.

units.la: REx Franciæ filiam suam filio regis Angliæ desponsauit, & ei pecuniam multam & ciuitatem maritimam magnam atq; bonam, cum adiacentibus sibi dedit, quando eam filio regis matrimonio copulauit. Cùm iuuenis iuvenculam per tempus aliquod habuisset, iuuencula viam carnis ingreditur, liberi post matrem breuiter sequebantur & pater hæres efficitur paruulorum. Ciues verò ciuitatis quam rex Franciæ filio regis Angliæ cum filia tradiderat, ægrè tulerunt esse sub Anglis. Rogauerunt igitur regem Franciæ, vt dominium ciuitatis supra memoratæ, quantocyus per euictionem ad se redire faceret, quia vellent ei in solutione pecuniæ pro posse suo voluntarie subuenire.
units.tr: The king of France betrothed his daughter to the son of the king of England, and when he joined her to the king's son in marriage, he gave him a large sum of money and a great and fine seaport town with its surrounding lands. After the young man had had the young woman for some time, the young woman went the way of all flesh; the children soon followed their mother, and the father became heir of the little ones. But the citizens of the town which the king of France had handed over to the son of the king of England along with his daughter were displeased to be under the English. They therefore asked the king of France to bring about, as quickly as possible, the recovery of the lordship of that town by purchase, since they would willingly help him, as far as they could, to pay the money.

units.la: Audiens hæc rex Franciæ, regi Angliæ mandauit, vt ciuitatem memoratam, pro qua dare sibi vellet pecuniam competentem, sibi redderet. Gauisus rex Angliæ dedit regi Franciæ ciuitatem, sub certa pecuniæ quantitate. Rex Franciæ cùm ciuitatem traxisset in propriam potestatem, regi Angliæ promissa soluere recusauit. De hoc Angliæ rex indignatus, regem Franciæ annis pluribus infestauit.
units.tr: When the king of France heard this, he ordered the king of England to return to him the aforesaid town, for which he was willing to give him a suitable sum of money. The king of England, rejoicing, gave the king of France the town for a fixed amount of money. But when the king of France had taken the town into his own power, he refused to pay what he had promised the king of England. Indignant at this, the king of England harassed the king of France for many years.

units.la: Circa idem tempus rex Arelatensis sine hæredibus moritur, & hæreditas ad regnum deuoluitur Romanorum. Rudolphus tunc temporis Rex extitit Romanorum, qui propter nimias occupationes, quas habuit in Teutonia, ad regnum Arelatense non poterat prouenire, vt illud in propriam potestatem traheret. Intelligens hæc rex Franciæ, mandauit Baronibus, quibus rex regnū Arelatense commiserat custodiendum, vt sibi Regnum in potestatem suam darent, alioquin totum Regnum cum armatis hominibus deuastaret. Custodes Arelatensis regni regem Franciæ supplicirer rogauerunt, quatenus Regnum non suum deleret. Vellent enim voluntatem suam regi Romanorum demandare, & quòd Regnum contra voluntatem regis Franciæ non possent per tempus aliquod retinere, quia posset Regnum cum armatis hominibus facile deuastare. Cùm hæc & his similia custodes regni Arelatensis, regi Roman. demandassent: scripsit eis, quòd se defenderent vel componerent sicut possent, quia secundum temporis statum, non posset eis in aliquo subuenire. Hæc audientes Arelatensis regni custodes, regnum regi tradiderunt, tali conditione seu pacto, vt regi Romanorum regnum redderet, vel cum eo pacificè componeret, temporibus opportunis. Rex autem Franciæ, accepto regno, filiam cum eo matrimonio copulauit.
units.tr: At about the same time, the king of Arles died without heirs, and the inheritance passed to the kingdom of the Romans. At that time Rudolf was king of the Romans, and because of the excessive business he had in Germany, he could not come to the kingdom of Arles to take it into his own power. Understanding this, the king of France ordered the barons to whom the king had entrusted the kingdom of Arles for safekeeping to hand over the kingdom to him, or else he would lay waste the whole kingdom with armed men. The guardians of the kingdom of Arles humbly begged the king of France not to destroy a kingdom that was not his. They would, they said, convey his wishes to the king of the Romans, and they could not for any length of time hold the kingdom against the will of the king of France, since he could easily lay waste the kingdom with armed men. When the guardians of the kingdom of Arles had sent these and similar words to the king of the Romans, he wrote back to them that they should defend themselves or come to terms as best they could, since given the state of affairs he could not help them in any way.
