Nor was it doubtful to the Pisans and the other nobles that, had his death not come so quickly, King Robert would have taken the kingdom by war, since his forces were too weak to defend it. He would not even have joined battle, but would have fled by ship to Narbonne as soon as the emperor's arrival was known. But if the gods had granted him the chance to hold Campania, it would be endless to tell how much that king could have achieved through the convenience of supplies and his innate courage.

units.la: Fridericus, cui fœdus cum Imperatore percussum paulò supra tradidimus, medio agens alto, vt excessisse Cæsarem è rebus humanis accipit, ingenti videlicet molestia animi consternatur: eratq; ea constantia Henriciq; amore, vt quoniam videre viuum nequiuerat, extinctum saltem contemplari exoptaret. Itaque Pisas non ob aliam rem nauigans, prolatum corpus regium inter vberes lacrymas conueneratus, recondi difficile passus est, côstantissimi ducis amicitiā immaturè sibi deplorans ademptam. Sed & Pisanus populus Henrici imitatus iudicium, quē ille socii sibi delegerat, hic Principē sortiri decreuit, vltrò ei ciuitatis delato imperio. Cæterum Fridericus satius existimās parta defendere, quàm nouis implicari, simul aliâ sibi esse rationem quam Lucenburgio fuerat, tuendi patrimonij successione auitâ aduentitiæ ciuitatis procurationi, actis gratiis duxit præferendā. Pari cautela Sabaudus Henricusq;, quorum ante meminimus, visi, delatas sibi quoq; ciuitatis habenas modeste recusarunt: ita vt tam pertinaci repugnatione Principum, Pisanos suspicio metusque haud exilis incesserit. Veteranorum Cæsaris pars multo maxima Germaniam repetiit: reliqui voluntarij nomina Pisano præsidio tribuerunt. Summa eius reipub. in subsidiū maiorum Principū, ad Vgutionem Faiolam delata est. Is & imperatoris ante nomine præfuerat Genuæ, & magnas postmodum res pro partibus Gibellinorū patrauit.
units.tr: Frederick, with whom we recorded a treaty with the emperor a little above, was at sea when he learned that the emperor had departed from human affairs. He was struck with great distress of mind, and his constancy and love for Henry were such that, since he could not see him alive, he longed at least to look upon him dead. So he sailed to Pisa for no other purpose, and, amid abundant tears, gathered round the body that had been brought out. Suffering it to be hidden with difficulty, he lamented that the friendship of the most constant duke had been snatched from him too soon. But the people of Pisa, imitating Henry's judgment in choosing the allies he had picked, resolved to choose a prince by lot as well, the rule of the city being offered to him freely. Frederick, however, thought it better to defend what had been gained than to entangle himself in new burdens. He also saw that his situation differed from that of Luxembourg: he judged that the hereditary succession to his own patrimony should be preferred to the management of an adventitious city, and so, with thanks, he declined. With similar caution the Savoyard and Henry, whom we mentioned before, when they were seen to be offered the reins of the city, modestly refused them too. Such stubborn refusal by the princes caused the Pisans no small suspicion and fear. The greater part of the emperor's veterans returned to Germany; the rest, as volunteers, gave their names to the Pisan garrison. The supreme command of the republic, in support of the greater princes, was entrusted to Uguccione della Faggiuola. He had earlier held command at Genoa in the emperor's name, and afterwards accomplished great things for the Ghibelline party.

units.la: Florentini non imperatoris modo, priusquā obiret, exulumq; formidine, sed & seditione interna pullulante, coacti imperiū ciuitatis Roberto publice detulerūt. Ac ne libertati vetustę noua immutatio noxia forte fieret, legē adijciūt, vt ne supra quinquenniū potestas cōcessa teneretur. Idē fere reliquæ ciuitates Hetruriæ Guelphæ fecerunt: ita vt euidenter appareret, eo iam necessitatū Henricī perseuerantia redactos aduersarios, vti intra paucissimos dies sub iugū mitti potuerint. Atq; iam olim variis experimētis cognitū est, cū aliis in reb. humanis, tum in bello primas obtinere partes fortunę ludibriū. Ita magnus Alexander, tentato veriùs orbe terrarū quàm domito, sed cui iā rerū vniuersitas propter felicitatē cœptorū destinaretur, in ipsis iuuentę primordijs excessit è medio. Sic Hannibal Cannēsi victoria nobilitatior quàm prudentior, occasione capiendę vrbis prætermisit. Scipiones in Hispania duo medijs rebus, mediisq; annis res humanas reliquere. Pattū quoq; nostrorū ætate, Amorates capto Byzātio Hydrunteq; direpto, omnē sibi iam despodes Italiā, intercipitur. Nuper vero Britanniæ regem Henricū, captis duab. validissimis ciuitatib. Galliæ, perterritisq; ac cōsternatis absq; dubitatione hostibus, sapientia non vita destituit. Qui aut cæcus dictus est, aut certē, si tantā opportunitatem prouidebat, neq; tamē suę fortunę obsequebatur, excors. Hos (vt dixi) casus inter fortuita reponebat antiquitas: nos ad Deū opt. max. publico consensu deferimus, è cuius æquissimo arbitrio quicquid rerum humanarum vel fit vel dicitur, sumit originem.
units.tr: The Florentines, under pressure from fear of the emperor before his death and of the exiles, and because a sedition was breaking out at home, publicly handed the rule of the city over to Robert. Lest some new change prove harmful to their ancient liberty, they added a law that the power granted should not be held for more than five years. The other Guelph cities of Tuscany did much the same. It was thus plainly evident that the opponents had been reduced to such necessity by Henry's persistence that they might have been brought under the yoke within a very few days. Indeed, it has long been known from various experiences that, in human affairs generally and in war above all, fortune's mockery holds the first place. Thus great Alexander, who had tested the world more than he had subdued it, and for whom the whole of affairs was destined because of the felicity of his undertakings, departed from the midst of things in the very beginning of his youth. So Hannibal, more famous for his victory at Cannae than wiser, let slip the chance of taking the city. The two Scipios in Spain left human affairs in the middle of their work and in the middle of their years. In the age of our fathers too, Amorates, having taken Byzantium and plundered Otranto, seemed to have all Italy already in his grasp, but was cut off. Lately King Henry of Britain, after capturing two very strong cities of Gaul, with his enemies undoubtedly terrified and dismayed, was forsaken by wisdom, not by life. He is called either blind or, if he foresaw such an opportunity and yet did not yield to his own fortune, foolish. Antiquity counted such events among chance happenings; we, by common consent, refer them to God, the best and greatest, from whose most just judgment whatever happens or is spoken in human affairs takes its origin.

units.la: Varia de genere mortis opinio. Nonnulli venenū malū niueo libello inditū asse-rūt, quod p ineffabilia mysteria cōmutatū quotannis moriturq; libamus. Monachos Prædicatorij ordinis, quib. ille ministris vtebatur in sacrificijs, horrēdi facinoris extitisse auctores, eāq; re Beneuetus Imolēsis, seculi ei°, in literas retulit. Fuisse tamē postea ex ea familia, Cartusiēsis in Fasciculo tradit, qui re delata ad Pōtificem maximū, decretū causa cognita impetrarint, quo innoxius eius veneficij Ordo vniuersus pronunciatus fuerit. Dominicani qui Luceburgi agunt, hoc amplius, cœnobij sui auctorem nō alium citāt quàm Henricū: neq; ergo fieri potuisse, vti tantū scelus in tam bene meritum perpetratū extiterit. Nobis potius in medio relinquere placet disputationem funestam, quàm de infandæ audaciæ fama, certam proferre sententiam.
units.tr: Opinions vary about the kind of death. Some assert that a wicked poison was put into a snow-white cup, the same cup which, transformed by the ineffable mysteries, we sip every year, and so die. The Dominicans of the order, whose ministers he used in the sacrifices, were said to be the authors of this dreadful crime, and Benvenuto of Imola, a writer of that century, recorded it in his writings. The Carthusian, in his Fasciculus, however, relates that a member of that family was afterwards involved in the affair; the matter was referred to the supreme Pontiff, and after the case was heard a decree was obtained by which the whole order was pronounced innocent of that poisoning. The Dominicans who work at Luxembourg go further: they name no other founder of their house than Henry, and so it could not have been that so great a crime was committed against one who had deserved so well. We would rather leave this deadly dispute undecided than pronounce a certain judgment on the report of an unspeakable audacity.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: HENRICI VII IMPERATORIS, AD IOANNEM DE EInbogen, coenobij Waldsassensis in Natiscis, abbatem, epistola.
units.tr: The Letter of Emperor Henry VII to John of Einbogen, Abbot of the Monastery of Waldsassen in Natiscis

units.la: HENRICVS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus: venerabilis Abbati Waldsassensi, Cisterciensis ordinis, devoto suo ac dilecto, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Magnus dominus & laudabilis valde, in excelso Diuinitatis suę solio residens, Imperiū suum (quod pro meritis eius inter nationes diuersas, quasi cum gentib. a suo Creatore degenerātibus, vacillabat) transfire voluit ad Romanos, vt illic praeiret Imperialis excellētia thronus, vbi erat sacerdotalis sedes & apostolica affutura: ita quod in eodem loco summi Pontificis & Imperatoris auctoritas reniteret. Nouissimis quippe temporibus, illo translato in Germanos, postquā plures Principes ad ipsum vocatos imperium, quorū quidā ipsius Imperij assumpsere diadema, quidam non: diuina cooperante clementia, per eos ad quos spectat, in Romanorum regē, futurū imperatorem, ritè & cocorditer electi, proposuimus ad Vrbē, pro coronationis nostrę suscipiēdus solennijs proficisci. Ac sanctissimū in Christo patrem dominum Clementem summum Pontificē requisiuimus, vt ad Vrbem accedens, præfata solennia nobis ibidē tradere dignaretur. Quicū ex certis causis, iuxta nostrū immēsum desiderium interesse nequiret: ne dicta coronatio ob sui absentiam impediri valeret, venerabilibus patribus, dominis Arnoldo S. sedis apostolicę legato, Leonhardo Albanēsi, & Nicolao Hostiensi ac Veltrensi episcopis, ac Francisco S. Lucia. nec non Luca, S. Mariæ in via lata diaconis Cardinalibus, commisit in hac parte plenariē vices suas,
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, to the venerable Abbot of Waldsassen, of the Cistercian order, his devoted and beloved, greeting and every blessing. The great and highly praiseworthy Lord, sitting on the lofty throne of his Divinity, wished to transfer his Empire, which because of the merits of its peoples had been wavering among various nations, as though they had degenerated from their Creator, to the Romans, so that the imperial throne of excellence might go before there, where the priestly and apostolic seat was to come, so that in the same place the authority of the supreme Pontiff and of the Emperor might shine forth together. For in the most recent times, after that transfer to the Germans, several princes were called to the empire, some of whom assumed the diadem of the Empire itself, and some did not. By the cooperating clemency of God, we were duly and harmoniously elected through those to whom it belongs as King of the Romans and future emperor, and we resolved to set out for the City to receive the solemnities of our coronation. We asked the most holy father in Christ, Lord Clement, supreme Pontiff, that on coming to the City he would deign to hand over the aforesaid solemnities to us there. Since for certain reasons he could not be present, though we very much desired it, lest the said coronation be hindered by his absence, he entrusted his vices fully in this matter to the venerable fathers, the Lords Arnold, legate of the apostolic see, Leonhard, bishop of Albano, Nicholas, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, and Francis of S. Lucia, as well as Luke, deacon of S. Maria in Via Lata, cardinals.

units.la: G cum clausula, vt si non omnes his exequendis interesse valerent, quatuor, tres, duo, vel vnus eorum, dicta coronationis nostrae negotium expediret.
units.tr: with the proviso that if not all of them could be present to carry these things out, four, three, two, or even one of them might complete the business of our coronation.

units.la: Verum dictis Leonhardo & Francisco de hac luce subtractis, per dictos dominos cardinales superstites, die festo beatorum Petri & Pauli apostolorum (quem ad hoc vt poteramus, virtute dictae comissionis, elegimus) in ecclesia S. Ioannis Lateranensis, praesente Archiepiscoporu, Episcoporu, Abbatu & aliorum praelatorum ac ecclesiasticorum ordinum Vrbis, Ducumq;, Comitu, Baronu, nobiliu ac Rom. populi, in numerosa caterua, oleo sacro vncti fuimus, nec non imperiali diademate coronati, ac alijs debitis ac consuetis solennijs insigniti. Hac aut devotioni tuae voluimus intimare, vt de nostris felicibus successibus valeas exultare. Datum Roma, quarto kalendarum Iulij, regni nostri anno quarto, Imperij vero anno primo.
units.tr: But after Leonhard and Francis had been taken from this life, the said surviving lord cardinals, on the feast day of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul (which we chose for this purpose, as far as we could, by virtue of the said commission), in the church of S. John Lateran, in the presence of archbishops, bishops, abbots and other prelates and the ecclesiastical orders of the City, and of dukes, counts, barons, nobles and the Roman people in a great crowd, anointed us with holy oil, crowned us with the imperial diadem, and invested us with the other due and customary solemnities. We wished to make this known to your devotion, so that you may rejoice in our happy successes. Given at Rome, on the fourth day before the kalends of July, in the fourth year of our reign, but the first of our empire.

units.la: AVCTORIS INCERTI FRAGMENTVM HISTORICVM, M. ALBERTI ARGENTINENSIS CHRONICO in manuscriptis Codicibus praefixum.
units.tr: Historical Fragment of an Unknown Author, Prefixed to the Chronicle of M. Albert of Strasbourg in the Manuscript Codices.

units.la: ANno ab incarnatione Domini DCXXXI, Dagebertus rex monarchiā in trib. regnis, Burgundionū, Austrasiorū, superiorū Francorū sagaciter accepit, fuitq; rex fortissimus, enutritor Francorū seuerissimus in iudicijs, & ecclesiarum largitor, pacem in cuncto regno suo statuit. In multis regnis rumor eius personuit: timore vniuersis regnis per circuitū incussit, pacificᵒ & quietus regnū obtinuit Francorū: sancto Arnulfo Metensi episcopo, Pipino duce & Erchinoldo maiore domus vtes cōsiliariis: nimio amore iustitiae flagrauit. Cuius temporibus, Dagoberti scilicet regis Francorū, vsq; ad annū quo Carolus cognomēto Magnus ex Fracigenis primus imperator Romanorū factus, & per annos circiter CLXXXI, fuerunt quindecim Imperatores Romanorū, quorū nomina haec sunt. Heraclius, Constantinus, Heracleonas, Constans, Constantinus, Iustinianus, Leontius, Absimarus, Philippus, Artemius qui & Anastasius, Theodosius, Leo, Constantinus cum Irene. Hinc Romanum imperium ad Francos commigrauit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord's incarnation 631, Dagobert received the monarchy over the three kingdoms of Burgundy, Austrasia and Upper Francia with wisdom. He was a most brave king, a most severe guardian of the Franks in matters of justice, and a generous benefactor of the churches, and he established peace throughout his whole kingdom. His fame resounded in many kingdoms, and he struck fear into all the surrounding realms. The kingdom of the Franks was held in peace and quiet, with Saint Arnulf, bishop of Metz, Pippin the duke and Erchinoald the mayor of the palace as his counsellors. He burned with an excessive love of justice. In his time, that is, the time of Dagobert king of the Franks, down to the year in which Charles, surnamed the Great, the first of the Franks to be made emperor of the Romans, was crowned, and across about 181 years, there were fifteen emperors of the Romans, whose names are these: Heraclius, Constantine, Heracleonas, Constans, Constantine, Justinian, Leontius, Absimarus, Philippicus, Artemius who was also called Anastasius, Theodosius, Leo, and Constantine with Irene. From then on the Roman empire passed over to the Franks.

units.la: Anno Domini DCXLIII, in Britania sanctus Oswaldus rex piissimus, cū regnum Anglorum & Britonum IX circiter annis strenuè administrasset, contra Pendanum regem pugnans, occubuit, & plurimis post mortem miraculis claruit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 643, in Britain, Saint Oswald, a most pious king, who had ruled the kingdom of the English and the Britons vigorously for about nine years, fell fighting against King Penda. After his death he became famous for many miracles.

units.la: Anno Domini DCXLVI, Gertrudis virgo, filia Pipini ducis, soror Grimoaldi, Niuelensis coenobii mater, virtutibus claruit. Huius soror Begga & ipsa religiosa, Angisō, sancti Arnulfi filio, nupsit. Sanctus quoq; Arnulfus, cum esset in iuuentute Dux, genuit Angisum ducē: Angisus de Begga vxore genuit Pipinum ducē, qui maior domus regni Francorū erat. Pipinus genuit Carolū seniorē, & ducē & maiorē domus Francorū. Carolus genuit Carolomannū & Caroli regē, postea imperatorē cognomēto Magnū, vt in sequentibus planiùs dicetur. Et haec est genealogia Caroli Magni.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 646, Gertrude, a virgin, daughter of Duke Pippin and sister of Grimoald, mother of the convent at Nivelles, became famous for her virtues. Her sister Begga, herself also devout, married Ansegisel, son of Saint Arnulf. Saint Arnulf too, when he was young, had been a duke, and he begot Duke Ansegisel. Ansegisel, by his wife Begga, begot Duke Pippin, who was mayor of the palace of the kingdom of the Franks. Pippin begot Charles the elder, both duke and mayor of the palace of the Franks. Charles begot Carloman and Pippin, and Charles, later emperor, surnamed the Great, as will be told more fully in what follows. And this is the genealogy of Charles the Great.

units.la: Anno Domini DCLXVIII, in Orientis partibus Constantinus huius nominis quartus imperator: Romanis imperat. cuius temporibus Constantinopolis septennio obsessa, nectamen est capta. Sub eodem Constantino floruit beatus Nicolaus archiepiscopus, qui postea apud Myream sub Iustiniano minore Imperatore, anno dominicae incarnationis DCLXXIIII, migrauit ad dominum. Eodem tempore beatus Arbogastus extitit, qui filium Dagoberti à morte suscitauit: & Florentius, qui filiam eiusdem regis à daemonio vexatam liberauit, Argentinae vicissim succedentes episcopi, claruerunt.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 668, in the eastern parts, Constantine, the fourth of that name, ruled as emperor of the Romans. In his time Constantinople was besieged for seven years, yet it was not taken. Under the same Constantine flourished the blessed Nicholas, archbishop, who afterwards died in the Lord at Myra under the emperor Justinian the Younger, in the year of the incarnation 674. At the same time lived the blessed Arbogast, who raised Dagobert's son from the dead, and Florentius, who freed the king's daughter from a demon; both were bishops of Strasbourg, succeeding one another, and both were famous.

units.la: Anno Domini DCLXXVIII, Dagebertus rex obiit, & filij eius duo regno substituuntur. Sigebertus cū Pipino duce & maiore domus regiæ, Austrasiam: Clodoueus minor cum Nanthilde matre & Erchinoldo maiore domus regię, Franciam & Burgundiam accepit. Sigebertus rex Austri, Pipino duce defuncto, Grimoaldū filium eiusdem Maiorem domus statuit. Decedente vero tempore defuncto Sigeberto rege, Grimoaldus filium eius paruulum, nomine Dagebertum totondit, & in Scotiam ad peregrinandum direxit, filium suum in regno constituens. Franci hoc valde indignantes, Grimoaldum capiunt, & ad condemnandum regi Francorum Clodoueo offerunt. Qui in Parisius ciuitate carceri mancipatus, vt erat dignus morte, quod in dominum suum exercuit, valido cruciatu finiuit vitam.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 678, King Dagobert died, and his two sons were put in his place in the kingdom. Sigebert, with Duke Pippin and the mayor of the royal palace, received Austrasia; Clovis the younger, with Nanthild his mother and Erchinoald the mayor of the palace, received Francia and Burgundy. Sigebert, king of Austrasia, after Duke Pippin's death, made Pippin's son Grimoald mayor of the palace. But when Sigebert the king died, Grimoald shaved the head of Sigebert's little son, named Dagobert, and sent him to Scotland to go on pilgrimage, setting up his own son in the kingdom. The Franks, greatly angered at this, seized Grimoald and handed him over to King Clovis of the Franks to be condemned. He was put in prison in the city of Paris and, as he deserved death for what he had done against his lord, he ended his life in severe torment.

units.la: Per idem tempus concidit regnum Francorum casibus pestiferis. Fuit namqz rex Clodoueus omni spurcitiæ deditus, fornicarius & illusor fœminarum, gulæ & ebrietati intentus. De morte huius & fine nihil historia dignum recolit. Cui vicissim filij eius Lotharius, Hildericus, Theodoricus in regno successerunt. Erchinoldo igitur defuncto, Lotharius qui tunc regnabat, Ebroinum maiorem domus constituit. Qui ob nimia scelera sua à Francis accusatus, ab Hilderico, qui fratri in regno successerat, in Luxouio monasterio Burgundiæ reeluditur, & Leudesius, quem Germani Luthericum vocant, filius Erchinoldi, consilio Leodegarij Augustudonensis episcopi maior domus palatij constituitur.
units.tr: At about the same time the kingdom of the Franks collapsed through deadly calamities. King Clovis was given over to every kind of filth, a fornicator and seducer of women, given to gluttony and drunkenness. History records nothing worth noting about his death or end. In turn his sons Lothair, Hilderic and Theuderic succeeded him in the kingdom. So when Erchinoald died, Lothair, who was then reigning, appointed Ebroin mayor of the palace. Accused by the Franks of his many crimes, Ebroin was shut up by Hilderic, who had succeeded his brother in the kingdom, in the monastery of Luxeuil in Burgundy; and Leudesius, whom the Germans call Lothar, son of Erchinoald, was made mayor of the palace on the counsel of Leodegar, bishop of Autun.

units.la: Rex igitur Hildericus cum per aliquot annos regnasset, à pestiferis conspiratoribus in aula, cum vxore sua prægnante, peremptus est. Leudesius verò & Luthericus cum Franciæ & Germaniæ principib. fratrem eius Theodericum regem constituunt, suffragantibus sibi Didone Pictauiensi episcopo, Leodegario Augustudonensi episcopo & Gerino Pictauensi comite fratre eius.
units.tr: So King Hildericus, after reigning some years, was killed in the palace by pestilent conspirators, while his wife was pregnant. Leudesius and Luthericus, however, with the nobles of France and Germany, set up his brother Theodoricus as king, with Didon, bishop of Poitiers, Leodegarius, bishop of Autun, and Gerinus, count of Poitiers and brother of Didon, supporting them.

units.la: Igitur Ebroinus de Luxouio egressus, & apostata factus, Theodoricum regem & Leudesium persequutus, regales thesauros apprehendit, & quoscunque insidiatores suos reperit, crudeli morte damnauit. Postea in Germaniam cum suis, quasi pacis sub obtentu, pro Leudesio transmisit, vt eius auxilio in gratiam regni peruenire potuisset, dispositis ei in itinere insidijs. Ille verò, licet cum omnimodis habuisset eum suspectum, tamen pro pace restauranda iter aggressus est. Cumque ad loca insidiarum peruenisset, Ebroinus cum suis ex improuiso consurgens, Leudesio cum aliquantis militibus occiso, ipse principatum regni violenter inuasit, & cum conspiratoribus suis Leodegarium episcopum captiuum interemit, Didonem episcopum auunculum eius exilio damnauit. Leudesius namque cum maior domus esset, duxerat vxorem de prosapia sancti Sigismundi regis Burgundiæ, genuitque ex ea Athicum seu Adalricum, qui patre adhuc superstite, & Hilderico regnante, vxorem duxerat Berswindam nomine, filiam sororis sancti Leodegarij, sororem videlicet reginæ. Ob hanc causam consanguinitatis à prefato rege ducatum Germaniæ adeptus est, habuitque sedem in villa regia Ehenheim & in castro quod Hohenburg nominatur: genuitque filiam à nativitate cæcam, nomine Odiliam, quæ à sancto Herhardo Ratisponensi episcopo, & Hildolfo Treuerensi baptizata, in sacro fonte visum recepit.
units.tr: Then Ebroinus, leaving Luxeuil and having become an apostate, pursued King Theodoric and Leudesius, seized the royal treasures, and condemned to a cruel death whatever conspirators of his he found. Afterwards he sent men into Germany with his followers, under the pretext of peace, to fetch Leudesius, so that with his help he might be restored to favour at court, while ambushes were laid for him along the way. Leudesius, although he had regarded him with every kind of suspicion, nevertheless set out on the journey in order to restore peace. When he reached the place of the ambush, Ebroinus and his men rose up suddenly; Leudesius was killed with some of his soldiers, and Ebroinus himself violently seized the principal power of the kingdom. With his fellow conspirators he also put to death Bishop Leodegarius, who had been taken captive, and condemned Bishop Didon, his uncle, to exile. Leudesius, being mayor of the palace, had married a woman of the family of St Sigismund, king of Burgundy, and by her begot Athicus or Adalricus, who, while his father was still alive and Hildericus reigning, married a woman named Berswinda, daughter of the sister of St Leodegarius, that is, sister of the queen. For this kinship he obtained the duchy of Germany from the said king, and had his seat at the royal estate of Ehenheim and in the castle called Hohenburg; and he begot a daughter, blind from birth, named Odilia, who, baptized at the sacred font by St Erhard, bishop of Regensburg, and by Hildulf of Trier, received her sight in the holy font.

units.la: Ebroinus igitur dum Francos crudeliter opprimeret, ab Ermenfrido occisus est, & Waranto maior domus à Theodorico constituitur. Quo defuncto, Franci in diuersa tendentes, vacillabant, & Berecharium quendam statura pusillum, sapientia ignobilem, consilio inutilem, maiorem domus palatij oberrantes statuerunt.
units.tr: While Ebroin was cruelly oppressing the Franks, he was killed by Ermenfrid, and Warato was appointed mayor of the palace by Theuderic. When he died, the Franks, pulling in different directions, were unsettled, and wandering about they chose as mayor of the palace one Bercharius, a man small in stature, lowly in wisdom and useless in counsel.

units.la: Pipinus igitur dux, filius Angisi, nepos sancti Arnulfi, decedentibus regibus, qui iamdudum dominabantur in Austria, terram sibi vendicauerat: & consurgens commoto hoste quàm plurimo contra Theodericum regem & Berecharium aciem dirigit: illisque inter se decertantibus, Theodoricus rex vnà cum Berechario terga vertit, Pipinus victor extitit, & Berecharius ab inimicis suis peremptus est. Post hæc Pipinus dux, Theoderico annuente, cepit esse in principali regimine maior domus: qui multa bella gessit cōtra Rapotonē gentilem, contra Sueuos, & quamplurimas gentes.
units.tr: Then Duke Pippin, son of Ansegisel and grandson of Saint Arnulf, claimed for himself the land of Austrasia, the kings who had long ruled there having died out. Rising up, he led a very large army against King Theuderic and Bercharius. When these two fought among themselves, King Theuderic together with Bercharius turned their backs; Pippin was victorious, and Bercharius was killed by his enemies. After this, with Theuderic's consent, Duke Pippin began to hold the chief rule as mayor of the palace. He waged many wars against the heathen Radbod, against the Suevi, and against very many peoples.

units.la: Theoderico decedente, Clodoueus filius eius regnauit, post quem Hildebertus, deinde Dagebertus. Pipinus itaque dum principatum palatij sub prædictis regibus annis xxvii egregiè administrasset, mortuus est, anno ab incarnatione Domini DCCXIIII.
units.tr: When Theuderic died, his son Clovis reigned, after whom came Hildebert, then Dagobert. Pippin, having administered the office of mayor of the palace with distinction under these kings for twenty-seven years, died in the year of the Lord's incarnation 714.

units.la: Eius temporib. duo Angli presbyteri Ewaldi, dum Saxonibus prædicaret, martyrio coronati & miraculis declarati ab ipso Coloniæ tumulati sunt, anno domini DCXXIIII. Sequenti anno sanctus Willebrodus à Sergio papa archiepiscopus ordinatus, genti Frisonum prædicans, virtutibus floruit.
units.tr: In his time two English priests, Ewald, while preaching to the Saxons, were crowned with martyrdom and made known by miracles; they were buried at Cologne by the same men, in the year of the Lord 724. In the following year Saint Willibrord, ordained archbishop by Pope Sergius, preaching to the people of the Frisians, flourished in virtue.

units.la: Igitur Pipino mortuo, Franci Raginfredum in principatum, maiorem palatij elegerunt: qui, Dageberto rege mortuo, cum Francis Danielem quendam clericum cæsariæ capitis crescente, in regnum statuit, atque Hilpericum nuncupauit. Eodem tempore Carolus dux, filius Pipini, in Austria semel & iterum exercitu commoto contra Hilpericum regem, & Raginfredum maiorem domus, pro principatu decertantibus, Hilpericus cum Raginfredo terga vertit; Carolus victor extitit. Deinde Hilperico mortuo Theodericus ei successit. Quo mortuo, Hildericus regnauit, qui tonsus & in monasterium iussu Stephani papæ reclusus est, vt in sequentibus planius dicetur.
units.tr: So when Pippin died, the Franks chose Ragenfrid as prince and mayor of the palace. When King Dagobert had died, he set up in the kingdom with the Franks one Daniel, a clerk whose hair was growing in the Caesarian tonsure, and named him Hilperic. At the same time Duke Charles, son of Pippin, in Austrasia, once and again stirred up his army against King Hilperic and Ragenfrid the mayor of the palace, who were contending for the principate. Hilperic turned his back with Ragenfrid, and Charles was victorious. Then, when Hilperic died, Theuderic succeeded him. When he died, Hilderic reigned; he was shaven and shut up in a monastery by order of Pope Stephen, as will be told more fully in what follows.

units.la: Carolus igitur dux victrici manu maior domus palatij effectus est, Raginfredo depósito: cuius regiminis quarto anno, qui est à natiuitate Domini DCCXVIII, Sarraceni Constantinopolim obsidentes, tandem diuino auxilio fame, peste & ferro repelluntur.
units.tr: Charles the duke, having been made master of the palace by victorious hand, Raginfred being deposed, in the fourth year of his rule, which is from the birth of the Lord 718, the Saracens, while besieging Constantinople, were at last driven off by divine help through famine, plague and the sword.

units.la: Sequenti anno sanctus Bonifacius à Gregorio papa Moguntiæ archiepiscopus ordinatus est, quamuis antea Moguntini episcopi suffraganei fuerint Wormatiensium episcoporum: & auctoritate apostolica duos in sua parochia episcopatus fecit, Wurzeburgensem scilicet, cui sanctum Burchardum, & Eistetensem cui Willebaldum coprouinciales primos episcopos ordinauit. Hic etiam Fuldense coenobium in saltu Bochania construxit, vbi postea cum Fresonibus praedicaret, martyrij coronam adeptus, anno Domini DCCLIIII sepultus est.
units.tr: In the following year Saint Boniface was ordained by Pope Gregory archbishop of Mainz, although previously the bishops of Mainz had been suffragans of the bishops of Worms; and by apostolic authority he made two bishoprics within his parish, namely Würzburg, to which he ordained Saint Burchard, and Eichstätt, to which he ordained Willibald, as first bishops of the province. He also built the monastery of Fulda in the wooded region of Buchonia, where he afterwards preached among the Frisians, obtained the crown of martyrdom, and was buried in the year of the Lord 754.

units.la: Anno dominicæ incarnationis DCCXXXIII, corpus sancti Augustini Hipponensis episcopi de Sardinia in Italiam à Luprando rege Longobardorum translatum est Ticinum. Sequenti anno sanctus Pirminius in Augia insula serpentes fugauit, & cœnobialem vitam ibi instituens, Ethonem postea Argentinensem episcopum, qui etiam Ethenheim cœnobium construxit, pro se abbatem constituit, ipsque Alsatiam, Alemanniam atque Bauariam, alia constructurus cœnobia, petiit, quorum nomina haec sunt: Althahe, Pheuers [Fauarias], Murbach, Schuttere, Gengenbach, Swarzahe, Wissenburg, Horenbach, Morsmünster, Nuwiltre.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord's incarnation 733, the body of Saint Augustine, bishop of Hippo, was carried from Sardinia to Italy by King Liutprand of the Lombards and transferred to Pavia. In the following year Saint Pirmin drove out the serpents on the island of Reichenau, and, establishing a monastic life there, appointed Etho, afterwards bishop of Strasbourg, who also built the monastery of Ettenheim, as its abbot. Pirmin himself went to Alsace, Alemannia and Bavaria, intending to build other monasteries, whose names are these: Altdorf, Pfäfers [Fabaria], Murbach, Schuttern, Gengenbach, Schwarzach, Weissenburg, Honau, Marmoutier, and Neuweiler.

units.la: Anno dominicæ incarnat. DCCXXXI, Beda presbyter natione Anglicus, doctor eximius migrauit ad Dominum.
units.tr: In the year of the incarnation 731, Bede, a presbyter by nation an Englishman and an outstanding teacher, departed to the Lord.

units.la: Carolus igitur dux & maior domus regni Francorum, postquam Alemanniam, Bauariam & totam prouinciam Teutonicorum subegit regno Francorum, genuit Carolomannum & Pipinum: qui diuiso post obitum eius patris regno Francorum maiores domus præfuerunt: regibus tamen in Francia, sed parua dignitate, regnatibus. Igitur Pipinus missis Romam legatis Zachariam papam de regno Francorum & ignauis eius regibus consuluit: cuius auctoritate & non multo post iussu Stephani pontificis Romani, Hilderico, qui tunc temporis regimen Francorum tenebat, depósito, atque in monasterium detrusò: Pipinus maior domus, rex Francorum electus, & Suessionis, à sancto Bonifacio Moguntinensi archiepiscopo vnctus est, anno domini DCCLII.
units.tr: Charles the duke and master of the palace of the kingdom of the Franks, after he had subdued Alemannia, Bavaria and the whole province of the Teutons to the kingdom of the Franks, begat Carloman and Pepin; and after the death of their father, the kingdom of the Franks being divided between them, they served as masters of the palace, while kings still reigned in France, but of little dignity. Then Pepin sent envoys to Rome and consulted Pope Zachary about the kingdom of the Franks and its feeble kings; by his authority, and not long afterwards by the order of Pope Stephen of Rome, Childeric, who at that time held the rule of the Franks, was deposed and thrust into a monastery, and Pepin, master of the palace, was elected king of the Franks and anointed at Soissons by Saint Boniface, archbishop of Mainz, in the year of the Lord 752.

units.la: Gens namque Merouingorum, de qua Franci reges creari sibi soliti erant, vsque ad haec tempora durauit: quae licet in Hilderico finita posset videri, tamen iamdudum nullius vigoris erat, nec quidquam in se clarum, praeter inane regis vocabulum, prae se ferebat. Nam opes & potentia regni penes palatij praefectos, qui maiores domus dicebantur, & ad quos summa imperij pertinebat, tenebantur: neque regi aliud relinquebatur, quàm vt regio tantum nomine contentus, crine profuso, barba submissa solio resideret, ac speciem dominantis effingeret, Legatos vndecunque venientes audiret, eisque abeuntibus, responsa, quae erat doctus, vel etiam iussus, ex sua velut potestate redderet: cum praeter inutile regis nomen & precarium vitae stipendium, quod ei praefectus aulae (prout videbatur) exhibebat, nil aliud proprij possideret, quàm vna praeparui redditus villa, in qua domu, & ex qua famulos sibi ministrates atq; obsequiu praebentes paucae numerositatis, habebat. Quocunq; eundu erat, carpento ibat, bubus iunctis & bubulco rustico more agente, trahebatur. Sic ad palatium, sic ad publicum populi sui conuentu, qui annuatim ob regni vtilitatem celebrabatur, ire, sic domu redire solebat. At regni administratione & omnia quae vel domi vel foris agenda vel disponenda erant, praefectus aulae procurabat.
units.tr: For the family of the Merovingians, from which the Franks were accustomed to create their kings, lasted down to these times; and although it might seem to have ended with Childeric, it had for some time been of no strength and showed nothing distinguished in itself, except the empty title of king. For the wealth and power of the kingdom were held by the prefects of the palace, who were called masters of the palace, and to whom the supreme command of the realm belonged; nothing was left to the king but to be content with the royal name alone, to sit on the throne with flowing hair and long beard and put on the appearance of a ruler, to hear envoys arriving from wherever, and when they departed, to give back the replies that he had been taught, or even ordered, to give, as though from his own authority. Beyond the useless name of king and the precarious allowance for living which the prefect of the court (as it seemed) furnished him, he possessed nothing of his own except a single small estate with its revenues, in which he had a house and a few servants to attend and serve him. Wherever he had to go, he went in a cart drawn by oxen, with a rustic ox-driver guiding them. In this way he was accustomed to go to the palace, in this way to the public assembly of his people, which was held every year for the good of the realm, and in this way to return home. The administration of the kingdom, and all that had to be done or arranged at home or abroad, was managed by the prefect of the court.

units.la: Quo officio tunc cum Hildericus deponebatur, Pipinus iam velut hæreditario iure fungebatur, qui honor non alijs dari consueuerat quàm his, qui claritate generis & opum magnitudine cæteris eminebant. Hunc cum Pipinus ab auo & patre sibi & fratri Carlomanno relictum, summa concordia diuisum, sex annis subrege memorato tenuisset: Carlomannus amore conuersationis contemplatiuæ succensus, operosa temporalis regni administratione relicta, in monte Cassino optata quiete perfruitur.
units.tr: When Childeric was deposed in this office, Pepin already held it as if by hereditary right, an honour which was not customarily given to any but those who excelled the rest in distinction of birth and magnitude of wealth. Pepin had received this office from his grandfather and father, and shared it in complete harmony with his brother Carloman; after he had held it for six years with the aforesaid king, Carloman, inflamed with love of a contemplative way of life, gave up the laborious administration of the temporal realm and enjoyed the longed-for quiet on Monte Cassino.

units.la: Pipinus autem per auctoritatem Romani pontificis ex præfecto palatij rex constitutus, cum per aliquot annos Francis solus imperaret: Stephanus papa pro auxilio contra Haistulphum Longobardorum regem poscendo, ad eum in Franciam venit, & filios eius Carolum, ob virtutum & meritorum quantitatem cognomento Magnum, & Carlomannum Parisiis reges inunxit, anno Domini DCCLIII.
units.tr: Pepin, however, was made king by the authority of the Roman pontiff, having been prefect of the palace; when he had ruled alone over the Franks for some years, Pope Stephen came to him in France to seek help against Aistulf, king of the Lombards, and anointed as kings at Paris his sons Charles, surnamed the Great on account of the greatness of his virtues and merits, and Carloman, in the year of the Lord 753.

units.la: Anno Domini DCCLIX, sanctus Othmarus, qui cellæ sancti Galli primus abbas constitutus, xl annis præerat, à Warino & Ruthardo, consensu Sidonij Constantiensis episcopi, iniquè damnatus, in Henisteiu relegatus, migrauit ad Dominum.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 759, Saint Othmar, who had been appointed the first abbot of the cell of Saint Gall and presided over it for forty years, was unjustly condemned by Warin and Ruthard, with the consent of Sidonius, bishop of Constance, was banished to Hönstein, and departed to the Lord.

units.la: Eodem anno Waifarius tyrannidem in Aquitania exercuit: cui resistens Pipinus rex, Vasconiam seu Aquitaniam invasit, & tyrannum iniustè vsurpata sub sacramento reddere coegit.
units.tr: In the same year Waifar exercised tyranny in Aquitaine; King Pepin, resisting him, invaded Vasconia or Aquitaine and forced the tyrant, who had unjustly usurped power, to give it back under oath.

units.la: Finito Aquitanico bello, quod per continuos nouem annos gerebatur, Pipinus xvii anno regni sui apud Parisios obijt: superstitibus filiis Carolo magno, & Carlomanno, ad quos successio regni diuino nutu peruenerat. Franci igitur facto generali conuentu, ambos sibi reges constituunt, ea conditione, vt totum regni corpus ex æquo partirentur. Carlomannus post administratum communiter biennio regnum, morbo decessit, & Carolus, fratre defuncto, consensu omnium Francorum rex constituitur: qui Hildegardam de gente Suaborum præcipuæ nobilitatis fœminam, in matrimonium accepit, & tres ex ea filios genuit, quorum vnus nomine patris sui Carolus, alter Pipinus, qui postea factus est rex super Italiam, tertius verò vocabatur Ludeuicus, qui fuit rex super Aquitaniam. Liberalibus disciplinis & mundanis legibus instruebat eos, & cum primò ætas patiebatur, more Francorum equitare, armis ac venationibus exerceri fecit. Tres etiam de Hildegarda filias habuit, scilicet Rudrudem, Bertam, & Giselam.
units.tr: When the war in Aquitaine, which was waged for nine continuous years, had ended, Pepin died at Paris in the seventeenth year of his reign, leaving surviving sons Charles the Great and Carloman, to whom the succession to the kingdom had come by divine will. The Franks therefore called a general assembly and set up both as their kings, on the condition that they should share the whole body of the kingdom equally. After Carloman had governed the realm jointly for two years, he died of illness, and Charles, his brother being dead, was made king with the consent of all the Franks. He took as his wife Hildegard, a woman of the Swabians of the highest nobility, and begat three sons by her: one of them, named after his father, Charles; another Pepin, who was afterwards made king over Italy; and the third, called Louis, who was king over Aquitaine. He instructed them in the liberal arts and in worldly laws, and when their age allowed, he had them trained in the Frankish manner in riding, arms and hunting. He also had three daughters by Hildegard, namely Rotrude, Bertha and Gisela.

units.la: Carolus igitur dum per xxxiii annos sub nomine regis circumquaque fortia gessit bella, Romam venit propter Leonem papam, qui à Romanis lingua præcisa & excæcatus in Saxoniam ad eum perductus fuerat: vbi Leonem de ei illatis & non probatis criminibus sacramento purgatum, sedi suæ restituit, ac temerarios iuxta leges Romanas capitali sententia addixit: sed precibus eiusdem papæ vita concessa, in exilium eos relegauit. Itaque cum tanti tamque famosi viri per totum orbem terrarum fidei probitatisve fama volauit: Romani potentissimum Romanum imperium, imò & papæ electionem sibi præscripserunt. Igitur precibus beati Leonis papæ & Principum regni, omniumque primatum admonitus, tam Dei quàm hominum voluntati consentiens, cum magno vniuersalis cleri plebisque tripudio, in die natalis Domini nostri Iesu Christi, anno incarnationis eius DCCC primo, ante altare beati Petri apostoli, Romæ a Leone papa consecratus & vnctus est Carolus Imperator, ipso Papa coronam auream capiti eius imponente, in iubilo cordis & oris Romano clero & populo acclamante: Carolo Augusto à Deo coronato magno & pacifico Imperatori, VITA ET VICTORIA.
units.tr: So while Charles, for thirty-three years under the name of king, waged brave wars on every side, he came to Rome on account of Pope Leo, who had been deprived of his tongue by the Romans and blinded, and had been brought to him in Saxony. There he restored Leo to his see, after Leo had cleared himself by oath of the charges brought against him, which were not proved; and according to Roman law he condemned the rash men to capital punishment, but at the pope's entreaty their lives were spared and he banished them. And since the fame of so great and so famous a man flew through the whole world for faith and uprightness, the Romans claimed for themselves the right to prescribe the mighty Roman empire, indeed even the election of the pope. Therefore, moved by the prayers of Blessed Pope Leo, of the princes of the realm and of all the chief men, and consenting to the will of God as well as of men, in the great joy of the whole clergy and people, on the day of the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the year of his incarnation 801, before the altar of the blessed apostle Peter at Rome, Charles was consecrated and anointed emperor by Pope Leo, the Pope himself placing a golden crown on his head, while the Roman clergy and people acclaimed with joy of heart and mouth: To Charles Augustus, crowned by God, the great and peaceful emperor, life and victory!

units.la: Sciendum est, quod primus omnium Regum vel Imperatorum post Christi nativitatem, Carolus vnctus est: bis equidem, primò in Francia cum fratre suo Carlomanno adhuc puer in regem: deinde Romæ, in Imperatorem. Ex eo reges & Imperatores, more antiqui Dei populi, vngi cœperunt. Notandum etiá quòd huius nominis tertius Valentinianus, sub quo beatus Augustinus Hipponensis doctor obiit, nouissimus Augustorum fuit in vrbe Roma: post quæ Hesperiũ cecidit regnũ: & nemo creatus est Romæ Augustus, per annos circiter cccxlviii, usque ad Carolũ magnũ: ipse enim primus post Valentinianũ Romæ imperator augustus extitit. Post quem Romanum impetiu cis mare Francorum regib. adminiftrandu, cum Cæsaris imperatoris Augusti nomine comissum est, vsq; quo deficiente in Francia & lassescente regio stemmate, Romanu imperiu à Teutonicis Principib. administratu est, vsq; in hodiernu diem. Hæc ciuitas Roma condita est à Romulo annis DXIX post Troiæ excidium: à conditione vero inclytæ vrbis vsq; ad incarnationem Domini fuerunt anni DCCLII.
units.tr: It should be noted that Charles was the first of all kings or emperors anointed after the birth of Christ. He was indeed anointed twice: first in France, while still a boy, as king together with his brother Carloman; then at Rome, as emperor. From that time kings and emperors began to be anointed, in the manner of the ancient people of God. It should also be noted that Valentinian, the third of that name, under whom the blessed Augustine, doctor of Hippo, died, was the last of the Augusti in the city of Rome; after him the Western kingdom fell, and no one was created Augustus at Rome for about 348 years, until Charles the Great; for he was the first emperor Augustus at Rome after Valentinian. After him the Roman government on this side of the sea was entrusted, under the name of Caesar and emperor Augustus, to be administered by the kings of the Franks, until in France the royal line failed and grew weak, and the Roman empire has since been administered by German princes down to the present day. This city of Rome was founded by Romulus 519 years after the fall of Troy; and from the founding of the famous city down to the incarnation of the Lord there were 752 years.

units.la: Carolus factus Imperator, Galliarum fines adiit, & locu qui Aquis, ob aquarum calidarum adeptione, traxit vocabulu, solito more venadi causa aggressus est, & pplexione fyluarum & errore viarum à sociis separatus, thermas calidorum fontiu & palatia inibi reperit, quæ quondam Granus, vnus de Romanis principibus, frater Neronis & Agrippæ, cōstruxerat: quæ longa vetustate deserta ac demolita, frutetis quoq; ac veprib. occupata, pede equi quo sedit, inter saltus riuos aquarum calidarum percepit & reperit. In quo loco sub titulo & honore beatæ Dei genitricis Mariæ, fundauit ecclesiā miri decoris, quàm auro & argento, & vario ornatu foli, æris, cæcellis quoq; & ianuis, magnificè & mirificè adornauit. Ad cuius etiā fundationis structurā cū columnas & marmora alibi habere nō posset, Roma, Rauenna ac Treueri deuehenda curauit, nullu labore ac sumtum recusans. Consecrationem vero eiusdē basilicæ quanta solennitate episcoporum & prælatorum, quāta totius regni & imperij primatu & principum numerositate celebrauerit, adscito etiā beato Leone, sanctæ Romanæ sedis præsule, series gestorum principaliu manifeste dictauit. Illius namq; ecclesiæ celeberrima dedicatio, sub præsentia metropolitanorum & episcoporum numero CCCLXV, excepta innumerabili multitudine Ducu, Marchionum, Comitu, baronu, tā Italiæ quàm Saxoniæ, tā Bauariæ quàm Alemanniæ, & vtriusq; Fraciæ, ab omnib. est gloriosissimè solennisata. Illic igitur domino apostolico & omnib. prædictis nobilib. & egregriis personis cōgregatis, Imperator meruit ab omnib. obtinere pro nimia deuotione, quam erga ipsum locu & matrē Christi habebat, vt in teplo eodē sedes unctionis regiæ locaretur, & locus regalis, & caput Galliæ trans Alpes haberetur, & in ipsa sede reges successores & heredes regni initiaretur, & sic initiati iure deinde imperialem benedictionē Romæ à domino apostolico, sine vlla interdictione, planiùs assequeretur. Confirmatum & sanctu est à domino apostolico Leone, & à Carolo Romanorum imperatore semper augusto, quatenus ratu & incouulsum hoc statutu & decretu maneat, vt Aquisgrani sedes regni trâs Alpes habeatur, sitq; caput omniu ciuitatum & prouinciarum Galliæ. Acquieuerunt vniuersi voluntati Imperatoris, qui ad hoc solene dedicationis ex diuersis regnis, cofluxerant, ac bonu & acceptu coram Deo & hominib. apostolici & imperatoris decretu astruxerunt, & omniu graduum episcoporum, abbatum quoq; banno corroborari hanc petitionem vniuersi acclamauerunt. Quàm strenuè Deo dilectus imperator materialis gladij cingulo militiæ præcinctus, laboriosum onus sustinuerit, qui scire desiderat, in catalogo virorum fortium & in Chronicis eiusdem inueniet: tamen pauca bellorum eius insignia adnotemus.
units.tr: Charles, having been made emperor, went to the borders of Gaul and came to the place that took its name from the acquisition of warm waters, Aachen (Aquae). He set out there to hunt, as was his custom. Separated from his companions by the tangle of the woods and the wrong turns of the roads, he came upon the baths of the warm springs and the palaces that Granus, one of the Roman leaders, brother of Nero and Agrippa, had once built. Long abandoned and demolished by age, they were overgrown with thickets and brambles, but he found and discovered them among the thickets and streams of warm water, with the foot of the horse on which he sat. In that place, under the title and honour of the blessed Mother of God, Mary, he founded a church of wonderful beauty, which he adorned splendidly and marvellously with gold and silver, with varied decoration in brass and bronze, and with grilles and doors. For the building of this foundation, since he could not get columns and marble locally, he had them brought from Rome, Ravenna and Trier, sparing no labour or expense. Of the great solemnity with which he celebrated the consecration of this basilica, with what number of bishops and prelates, and with what gathering of the leading men and princes of the whole kingdom and empire, and with the blessed Leo, bishop of the holy Roman see, taking part, the record of his deeds plainly sets out. For the most famous dedication of that church, attended by metropolitans and bishops to the number of 365, and by an innumerable multitude of dukes, marquises, counts and barons from Italy and Saxony, from Bavaria and Alemannia, and from both Franconias, was celebrated with great glory by all. There, therefore, with the lord apostolic and all the aforesaid nobles and distinguished persons assembled, the emperor, on account of the great devotion he had toward that place and the mother of Christ, obtained from everyone that the seat of royal anointing be set in that same temple, that the place be regarded as royal and the head of Gaul beyond the Alps, and that the kings, successors and heirs of the realm be initiated in that very seat; and, once so initiated, they might then by right more fully obtain the imperial blessing at Rome from the lord apostolic, without any prohibition. It was confirmed and sanctioned by the lord apostolic Leo and by Charles, emperor of the Romans, ever august, that this statute and decree should remain firm and unbroken: that Aachen should be held as the seat of the kingdom beyond the Alps, and be the head of all the cities and provinces of Gaul. All agreed to the emperor's will, who had gathered from various kingdoms for this solemn dedication, and they pronounced the decree of the apostolic see and of the emperor good and acceptable before God and men. All the bishops of every rank, and the abbots too, acclaimed with one voice that this petition be strengthened by the ban. How vigorously the emperor, beloved of God, girded with the belt of the material sword of warfare, bore that laborious burden, whoever wishes to know will find in the catalogue of brave men and in his Chronicles. Yet let us note a few of his notable wars.

units.la: Interim igitur dū bellu ageret cōtra Godefridū regē Nortimannorū, apud Ierusalem inter Christicolas & paganos discordia orta est adeò magna, quòd Patriarcha, vir perfectissimæ religionis, de ciuitate vi expulsus, ad imperatorem Constantinum & filium eius Leonem, qui tunc temporis illis partib. imperabat, Constantinopolim fugiendo, cum aliis Christianis peruenerit, & ei lacrymabiliter, quæ & quàta sibi sint illata, & qualiter sepulcrum Domini & sancta loca gentes inordinatè tractent, quod vniuersi Christi fidelibus deberet esse dolendum, enarrauit.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while he was waging war against Godfrey, king of the Northmen, a discord arose at Jerusalem between the Christians and the pagans so great that the Patriarch, a man of most perfect religion, was driven by force from the city. Fleeing to Constantinople, he came with other Christians to the emperor Constantine and his son Leo, who then ruled in those parts, and tearfully related to them what and how great injuries had been inflicted upon him, and how the nations were treating the Lord's sepulchre and the holy places in disorder, something all the faithful of Christ ought to lament.

units.la: Imperator igitur hostes sanctæ ecclesiæ refrenandos, sociū itineris adsciuit Carolum magnū, literis ei cum muneribus insignibus directis. Quib. ille receptis, intellexit iam se à Deo ad hoc negotium prælectum esse, & iam vsq; ad Orientales famā suæ probitatis transuolasse. Hinc gaudio gauisus est valde: sed oppidò, quòd Dominicum sepulcrum à paganis, erat obsessum, cōdolens, lacrymari coepit. Qui statim cōsilio habito, per totum Francorū regnum edicto citissimè imperat, vt omnis quicunq; ad se defendendū arma possent deferre, tam senes quàm iuuenes, secum pugnaturi in paganos versus Orienteles plagas ineuitabiliter satagant. Alioquin quicunq; huius edicti mandata non peregerit, ipse in vita sua & filij eius similiter, ex regis decreto, de capite quatuor nummos, quasi serui soluant.
units.tr: The emperor therefore, to curb the enemies of the holy Church, took Charles the Great as companion for the journey, sending him letters with notable gifts. On receiving them, Charles understood that he had now been appointed by God for this task, and that his reputation for uprightness had already flown even to the Easterners. He rejoiced greatly at this, but, grieving exceedingly that the Lord's sepulchre was besieged by pagans, he began to weep. Immediately, after taking counsel, he commanded by edict throughout the whole kingdom of the Franks, with all speed, that every man who could carry arms in his own defence, old and young alike, should hasten inevitably toward the eastern regions to fight with him against the pagans. Otherwise, whoever did not carry out the commands of this edict, he himself and his son likewise, by the king's decree, shall pay four coins for their head, like slaves.

units.la: Quid vltra? cateruatim vndique populis circumfluentibus maiorem exercitum quàm antea habuisset, breui spatio congregauit. Itaq; in nomine Domini profectus, tandem cum exercitu suo Constantinopolim longo itinere fatigatus, peruenit. Postea verò fugatis quoque paganis, ad celsam vrbem, quæ vexilla crucis viuificæ, Christique passionis retinet monumenta, lætus & supplex aduentans, patriarchæ totique Christicolæ plebi cuncta prospera, Deo opitulante, solidauit. His itaq; gestis imperatorem Constantinum licentiam repatriandi Carolus magnus subrogauit, acceptis ab eo dignis ac sacrosanctis pignoribus, sanctorum, scilicet, de spinea corona Domini octo spinas, cum roboris parte, vnum de clauis Domini & de sancta cruce, & sudarium Domini, & sanctæ Deigenitricis camisiam, & cinctorium vnde puerum Iesum in cunis cinxerunt, brachium senis Simeonis & alia multa: quæ omnia Deo dilectus Carolus post reditum suum Aquisgrani, cum multorum religiosorum virorum comitatu diligentissimè recondidit.
units.tr: What more? With peoples flocking to him in crowds from every side, in a short time he gathered a greater army than he had had before. So, setting out in the name of the Lord, he at length arrived at Constantinople with his army, weary from the long journey. Afterwards, when the pagans had also been put to flight, he came joyfully and as a suppliant to the lofty city that keeps the banners of the life-giving cross and the memorials of Christ's passion, and with God's help he secured all prosperity for the patriarch and the whole Christian people. When these things were done, Charles the Great obtained from the emperor Constantine permission to return home, receiving from him worthy and most sacred pledges: namely, eight thorns from the Lord's crown of thorns, with a piece of its wood; one of the nails of the Lord and of the holy cross; the Lord's sudarium; the shift of the holy Mother of God; the girdle with which they swaddled the boy Jesus in the cradle; the arm of old Simeon; and many other things. Charles, beloved of God, after his return to Aachen, with a company of many religious men, most carefully deposited all of these.

units.la: Itaque magnus imperator Carolus postquam multis laboribus diuersa orbis regna innumeraque vrbes à mari vsque ad mare, diuinis munitus subsidijs, inuincibili suæ potentiæ brachio subiugauit, & ab infidelium potestate liberauit, Christiano imperio subdidit. Tanto igitur sudore ac graui fatigatus labore, vt requiem sibi daret, nec amplius bellum inire proposuit. Et ecce per visum noctè intuitus est in cœlo quandam viam quasi stellatam, incipientem à mari Frisiæ, & tendentem inter terrâ Teutonicam & Italiam, inter Galliam & Aquitaniam, rectissimè trãseuntem per Vasconiam, Basculamque & Nauarriam atq; Hispaniam vsq; Galliciam, vbi corpus beati Iacobi tunc temporis latebat incognitum. Hęc igitur cum Carolus per singulas penè noctes conspiceret: apparuit ei beatus Iacobus, admonens, vt ad expugnandam perfidiam & visitandam memoriam eius in Galliciam proficisci deberet: & post eum omnes populi, à mari vsque ad mare peregrinantes, & delictorum suorum veniam implorantes, illuc ituri essent, à temporibus suis vsque ad finem seculi. Quibus im; erator excitatus & monitus, atque promissione apostolica fretus, coadunatis exercitibus multis, expugnare gentes Hispaniæ & Galliciæ aggressus est. Tunc prece ad Dominum & sanctum Iacobum fusa, muri confracti funditus corruerunt, sicut legitur diuinitus factum de muris Iericho. Itaque Sarracenos, qui baptizari voluerunt ad vitam reseruauit, eosque qui renuerunt, gladio feriendos tradidit. His auditis, cæteri Sarraceni inuictissimo Carolo vbique se se in deditionem tradebant, obuiamque ei tributa mittebant, & vrbes vltrò reddebant: totaque gens in Galicia valida & robusta, armis abiectis Imperatorem Carolum honorificè & pacificè recepit. Deinde Carolus visitato beati Iacobi sepulchro, accessit ad petram limitarem, & infixit in mari lanceam suam, agens Deo gratias & sancto Iacobo, qui huc vsque duxisset, dicens: quòd vlterius ire non posset.
units.tr: Thus the great emperor Charles, having with many labours, and with divine aid to fortify him, subdued with the invincible arm of his power the diverse kingdoms of the world and countless cities from sea to sea, freed them from the power of unbelievers, and brought them under the Christian empire. Wearied by such sweat and grievous toil, he resolved to give himself rest and to undertake no more war. Then, one night in a vision, he saw in the heavens a certain path as it were starred, beginning at the sea of Friesland and stretching between the land of Germany and Italy, between Gaul and Aquitaine, passing most directly through Gascony, Biscay and Navarre, and Spain, as far as Galicia, where the body of the blessed James then lay unknown. As Charles saw this almost every night, the blessed James appeared to him, admonishing him to set out into Galicia to subdue the faithless and to visit James's memory; and after him all peoples, pilgrimaging from sea to sea and imploring pardon for their sins, would go there from his own time until the end of the age. Roused and admonished by this, and trusting in the apostolic promise, the emperor gathered many armies and set about attacking the nations of Spain and Galicia. Then, with prayer poured out to the Lord and to holy James, the walls, broken, fell to the ground, just as it is read that the walls of Jericho fell by divine power. He spared to life the Saracens who wished to be baptized, and handed over to the sword those who refused. When the others heard this, the Saracens everywhere surrendered to the most unconquered Charles, sent tribute to meet him, and gave up their cities of their own accord; and the whole people of Galicia, strong and robust, laid down their arms and received the emperor Charles honourably and peacefully. Then Charles, having visited the sepulchre of the blessed James, came to a boundary rock and drove his lance into the sea, giving thanks to God and to St James, who had led him thus far, and saying that he could go no further.

units.la: Reuersodemum in Galliam Carolo magno, quidam rex Africæ, nomine Agiolandus cum exercitu terram Hispaniæ sibi subiugauit, interfectis vniuersis, eiectisque de oppidis & vrbibus Christianis custodibus, quos ad custodiedam terram reliquerat. His auditis, Carolus cum magno exercitu rursum proficiscitur in Hispaniam, reperitque Agiolandum in amœno prato, super fluuiù quod vocatur Teia, vbi postea basilica beatorum martyrũ Facundij & Primitiui ab ipso noscitur fabricata. Appropinquantibus autem Christianorũ exercitibus, mandauit Agiolandus Carolo optionem pugnandi secundùm velle suum, vel viginti contra viginti, vel xl contra quadraginta, vel centum contra centum, vel mille aduersus mille, vel vnũ contra vnum, vel duos contra duos decertantibus. Interea missi sunt à Carolo centum contra centũ Agiolandi milites, & interfecti sunt Sarraceni. Deinde misit Agiolandus ducentos cõtra ducentos Caroli milites, & statim occisi sunt Mauri. Iterum misit Agiolandus duo millia contra duo millia, è quibus alia pars occisa est, alia terga vertit. Tertia verò die iecit sortes Agiolandus secretò, in quibus cognouit Caroli detrimentum, & mandauit ei, vt ad pugnã plenariam contra eum die sequenti veniret: quod ab vtraq; parte concessum est. Tunc astiterunt quidam ex Christianis, qui sero ante diem belli arma sua bellica studiosè præparantes, hastas suas in terram fixerunt, erectas ante castra, scilicet in pratis iuxta præfatum flumen; quas summo mane corticibus & frondibus inuenerunt vestitas: hi scilicet, qui in acie proxima palmam martyrij pro fide Christi erant accepturi. Vnde vltra quàm dici fas est, admirantes, tantumq; miraculum diuinæ gratiæ & meritis fideiq́ue imperatoriæ adscribentes, absciderunt prope terram: quarum radices, quæ in terra remanserunt, ex se postea magna nemora, quæ adhuc in eodem loco apparent, genuerunt. Erant autem multæ ex hastis fraxineæ. Die autem sequenti commissa est contra hostes pugna, in qua occisa sunt Christianorum x l millia, & dux Milo de Angulariis, Rotlandi genitor, ibidem martyrij palmam est adeptus, cum his, quarum hastæ (vt dictum est) fronduerunt. Sed & Caroli equus in eadem pugna interemptus est.
units.tr: After Charles the Great had returned to Gaul, a certain king of Africa named Agiolandus subjected the land of Spain to himself with an army, slaying everyone and expelling the Christian guards whom Charles had left in the towns and cities to keep the land. Hearing this, Charles set out again into Spain with a great army and found Agiolandus in a pleasant meadow above the river called Teia, where a basilica of the blessed martyrs Facundus and Primitivus was afterwards known to have been built by him. As the Christian armies drew near, Agiolandus sent word to Charles offering him a choice of how to fight: twenty against twenty, or forty against forty, or a hundred against a hundred, or a thousand against a thousand, or one against one, or two against two. Meanwhile a hundred of Agiolandus's soldiers were sent against a hundred of Charles's, and the Saracens were slain. Then Agiolandus sent two hundred against two hundred of Charles's soldiers, and the Moors were at once killed. Again Agiolandus sent two thousand against two thousand: one part of them was killed, the other turned their backs. On the third day Agiolandus cast lots in secret, and through them learned of Charles's loss, and sent word to him to come against him for a full battle the next day; this was agreed to on both sides. Then some of the Christians came forward who, on the evening before the day of battle, diligently preparing their warlike arms, had fixed their spears in the ground, standing upright before the camp, namely in the meadows beside the aforesaid river. At early morning they found these spears clothed with bark and leaves: these men, that is, who were about to receive the palm of martyrdom for the faith of Christ in the front line. Marvelling beyond what it is right to say, and ascribing so great a miracle to divine grace and to the merits and faith of the emperor, they cut the spears off close to the ground. Their roots, which remained in the earth, afterwards produced great groves, which still appear in the same place; and many of the spears were of ash. On the following day battle was joined against the enemy, in which forty thousand Christians were slain, and Duke Milo of Angers, father of Roland, there obtained the palm of martyrdom, along with those whose spears, as has been said, had put forth leaves. Charles's horse also was killed in the same battle.

units.la: Tunc Imperator constanter permanens, cum duobus millibus Christianorum peditum & ipse pedes, cum se inter innumera hostium millia cerneret circumuallatum, euaginato gladio multos Sarracenorum trucidauit. Die vero aduesperascente, tam Christiani quàm Sarraceni in castra reuertuntur. Altera vero die Agiolandus in fugam versus, in Legionensium fines secessit, & triumphator Carolus in Galliam remeauit: vbi rursus multis congregatis de imperij visceribus, videlicet cxxiiii milibus; Hispaniam ingreditur, & cum Agiolando congressus, ipsum & omnes suos prostrauit: & cuncta rite disponens, victor ad propria rediit.
units.tr: Then the Emperor, standing firm with two thousand Christian foot soldiers, and fighting on foot himself, saw that he was surrounded by countless thousands of enemies. Drawing his sword, he cut down many of the Saracens. As evening drew on, both Christians and Saracens returned to their camps. On the next day Agiolandus turned to flight and withdrew into the territory of the Legionese, while the victorious Charles went back into Gaul. There he gathered again many men from the inner parts of the empire, namely 124,000, and entered Spain. He met Agiolandus in battle and overthrew him and all his men. Having arranged everything properly, he returned victorious to his own land.

units.la: Hæc bella & multò plura rex & Imperator potentissimus per annos xlviii in diuersis terrarum partibus summa prouidentia atq; felicitate gessit. Omnibus itaq; Carolus in pace & tranquillitate compositis, coronato filio suo Ludouico, & commisso ei totius regni negotio, cū more solito Aquisgrani hyemaret, febre valida correptus decubuit, & in senectute bona viam vniuersæ carnis ingressus est, v cal. Ianuarij, ætatis suæ anno lxxii, regni autè xlvii, subactæq; Italiæ xliii: ex quo Imperator & augustus appellatus est, decimoquarto: incarnationis verbi Dei anno dcc xxiiii, & in ecclesia Aquisgrani honorificè sepultus quiescit.
units.tr: The king and most powerful emperor waged these wars, and many more, over forty-eight years in various parts of the world, with great foresight and good fortune. When everything was settled in peace and tranquillity, he crowned his son Louis and entrusted to him the whole business of the kingdom. Then, wintering at Aachen as was his custom, he was struck down by a severe fever. In a good old age he entered the way of all flesh on 5 calends of January (28 December), in the seventy-second year of his life, the forty-seventh of his reign, and the forty-third after the subjugation of Italy. From that time, in the fourteenth year, he had been called Emperor and Augustus. This was in the year of the incarnation of the Word of God 824. He rests honourably buried in the church at Aachen.

units.la: Anno dominicæ incarnationis dcc. lxxviii, Hildegart regina vxor eius obiit. Eodem anno Bertha mater eius, quæ apud eum in magno honore senuerat, vita decessit, & apud maritum suum Pipinum Parisiis sepelitur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord's incarnation 778, Queen Hildegard, his wife, died. In the same year his mother Bertha, who had grown old in great honour with him, departed this life and was buried at Paris beside her husband Pepin.

units.la: Anno regni Caroli magni xlii, obiit Pipinus filius eius rex Italiæ. Sequenti anno Carolus primogenitus eius vita decessit. Solus Ludewicus ad regni gubernacula remansit. Rudrudis filiarum eius primogenita defuncta est prius quàm ipse obiret. Hæc Constantino filio Irenes desponsata erat, Græcorum imperatori. Hic Constantinus huius nominis sextus cum matre Irene imperium in Orientis partibus accepit, anno dominicæ incarnationis, dcc. lxxxiiii. Eodem anno homo quidā fodiens in longis Thraciæ muris, inuenit lapideam arcam: quā cum expugnasset, reperit virū iacentem, & conglutinatas arcæ literas, continentes hæc. Christus nascetur ex Virgine Maria, & credo in eum. Sub Constantino Irene imperatoribus ô Soliterum me videbis. Vnde cognoscere possumus, nullo tempore defuisse fideles spiritu Dei plenos.
units.tr: In the forty-second year of Charlemagne's reign, his son Pepin, king of Italy, died. The following year his firstborn, Charles, died as well, so that only Louis remained at the helm of the kingdom. Rudrudis, his eldest daughter, died before he himself did. She had been betrothed to Constantine, son of Irene, emperor of the Greeks. This Constantine, the sixth of that name, received the empire in the eastern parts together with his mother Irene, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 784. In the same year a certain man digging by the long walls of Thrace found a stone chest. When he had broken it open, he found a man lying inside, and letters fixed together on the chest, containing these words: "Christ will be born of the Virgin Mary, and I believe in him. Under the emperors Constantine and Irene, O Soliterum, you will see me." From this we can know that at no time were faithful men wanting who were filled with the Spirit of God.

units.la: Anno Domini dccc. xix, corpus sancti Marci euangelistæ, sub nomine Valentis martyris Ratholdus Veronensis episcopus à Duce Venetiæ impetrauit, & cum corpore sancti Genesij martyris in Augiam insulam attulit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 819, Ratholdus, bishop of Verona, obtained from the Doge of Venice the body of St Mark the evangelist, under the name of the martyr Valens. Together with the body of the martyr Genesius, he brought it to the island of Reichenau (Augia).

units.la: Anno Domini dccc.lxii, Tregandus Treuerensis archiepiscopus, Lothario regi & Gunthero Coloniēsi archiepiscopo consentiens in deiestione Tiburgæ vxoris, eiusdē Lotharij falso accusatæ. Imò definitū est in synodo, ad hæc machinandū collecta, quod ipsa confessa fuisset, semetipsam fratris germani incestuoso pollutam fuisse concubitu. Hanc falsam infamiam Lotharius his episcopis composuerat, cupiens hoc modo reginam abijcere, & Waldradam, sororem Guntheri Coloniēsis archiepiscopi, quā ipse adolescens concubinam habuerat, in regnum assumere. Quod cum iudicio episcoporum adeptus fuisset: sequēti anno Thregandus & Guntherus à papa Nicolao Romam, pro his causis, euocati sunt, ibiq; omni ecclesiastica dignitate priuati & depositi sunt, & Lotharius excommunicatus est.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 862, Thietgaud, archbishop of Trier, agreed with King Lothar and Gunther, archbishop of Cologne, in the deposition of Tiburga, wife of the same Lothar, who had been falsely accused. Indeed, it was decreed in a synod gathered for this purpose that she had confessed herself defiled by incestuous intercourse with her full brother. Lothar had arranged this false infamy with these bishops, desiring in this way to cast off the queen and to take as queen Waldrada, sister of Gunther, archbishop of Cologne, whom he himself had kept as his concubine when young. When he had obtained this by the judgment of the bishops, in the following year Thietgaud and Gunther were summoned to Rome by Pope Nicholas for these causes. There they were deprived and deposed of all ecclesiastical dignity, and Lothar was excommunicated.

units.la: Mortuo Nicolao papa, Adrianus ei successit: ad quem cum Lotharius rex Romam venisset, & opitulante fratre Ludewico Imperatore, pro Waldradæ concubinæ suæ matrimonio satis egisset, nihil profuit. Ea quidem conditio ei dabatur, vt si innocens esset de adulterio, fiducialiter corpus Domini perciperet: sin verò, illud nullatenus accinus accipere præsumeret. Sed ille temerarius accessit, & cum suis complicibus ineuitabile iudicium sibi suoque regno, heu nimium demens, percepit. Nam tanta cladés præsumptionem hanc diuinitus subsequuta est, ut eiusdem Lotharij regno tota virtus ac nobilitas non peste, sed hostili gladio delera esse videretur. Itaq; cum rediret domum, Placentiæ periit, fautoresq; sceleris omnes pene in itinere periere, regnumque eius rex Galliæ Carolus, patruus eius, inuasit.
units.tr: After Pope Nicholas died, Hadrian succeeded him. When King Lothar came to Rome to him, and with the help of his brother, the Emperor Louis, had pressed hard for the marriage of his concubine Waldrada, it profited him nothing. The condition offered was that if he were innocent of adultery, he should confidently receive the body of the Lord; but if not, he should by no means presume to receive it. Yet he rashly approached, and with his accomplices, alas, all too foolishly, received an unavoidable judgment upon himself and his kingdom. For such a great disaster followed this presumption by divine providence that the whole strength and nobility of Lothar's kingdom seemed to be destroyed not by plague but by the hostile sword. So when he was returning home he died at Piacenza, nearly all the abettors of the crime perished on the journey, and Charles, king of Gaul, his uncle, invaded his kingdom.

units.la: Anno domini DCCC.LXXX, Carlomannus rex Bauariæ, apud villam OEtin-gen obijt. Tertio anno Ludouicus frater eius rex Germaniæ, absque hærede decessit. Itaq; frater ipsorum Carolus rex Alemanniæ Romam veniens, vna cum regina 10 Richarda imperiali vnctione à papa coronatur, anno Domini DCCC.LXXXI.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 880, Carloman, king of Bavaria, died at the village of Oetingen. In the third year after, his brother Louis, king of Germany, died without an heir. Therefore their brother Charles, king of Alemannia, came to Rome, and together with Queen Richarda was crowned by the pope with imperial anointing, in the year of the Lord 881.

units.la: Anno Domini DCCC.LXXXVII, Richarda imperatrix adulterij vitio cum Liutwardo Vercellensi episcopo incusata, diuino iudicio se ab omni vxorum commixtione integram & virginem approbauit, quanuis iam XII annis in coniugio imperatoris apparuit: moxque ab Imperatore separata, in Andelahe, cœnobium virginum à se constructum, secessit, ibiq; Deo seruiens, virgo regina permansit. Imperator autem ab omnibus deseritur, & Arnolfus, fratris sui Carlomanni filius, rex eligitur. Itaque Imperator Carolus iam priuatus deuotè Deo seruiens (vt quidam dicunt) à suis strangulatus obijt: anno Domini DCCC.LXXXVIII.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 887, the Empress Richarda was accused of adultery with Liutward, bishop of Vercelli. By divine judgment she proved herself free from all marital intercourse and a virgin, although she had already been in the emperor's marriage for twelve years. Soon separated from the emperor, she withdrew to Andlau, a convent of virgins she had founded, and there, serving God, she remained a virgin queen. The emperor, however, was deserted by all, and Arnulf, son of his brother Carloman, was elected king. So Emperor Charles, now deprived of power and serving God devoutly (as some say), was strangled by his own men and died in the year of the Lord 888.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC. XXIIII, sanctus Vdalricus Augustæ factus est episcopus.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 924, St Ulrich was made bishop of Augsburg.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.XLIX, Lothario rege Italiæ mortuo, Berengerus regnum eius invasit, viduamq; eius Adelheidem, Rudolfi regis Burgundiæ filiam, multis iniuriis afflixit. Sequenti anno Otto rex Italiam petijt, ibiq; eam subiecit, & expulso Berengero, dominam Adelheidem liberauit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 949, after Lothar, king of Italy, had died, Berengar invaded his kingdom and afflicted his widow Adelheid, daughter of King Rudolf of Burgundy, with many injuries. In the following year King Otto went to Italy, subdued it there, expelled Berengar, and freed the lady Adelheid.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.LII, Otto rex cum filio suo Ludolpho Italiam intrauit, & regales nuptiæ cum Adelheide vidua Papiæ celebrantur. Postea priuignus regis, Ernestus dux, filius Adelheidis reginæ, qui pro excessibus, regia maiestate læsa, proscriptus & exul factus erat, per plures annos & post infinitos labores exilij sui, Imperatori reconciliari meruit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 952, King Otto entered Italy with his son Ludolf, and royal nuptials were celebrated at Pavia with Adelheid, the widow. Afterwards the king's stepson, Duke Ernest, son of Queen Adelheid, who had been outlawed and made an exile for offences against the royal majesty, deserved after many years and endless hardships of exile to be reconciled to the emperor.

units.la: 30 Anno Domini DCCCC.LXI, Otto rex filium suum Ottonem ex Adelheide, regem eligi fecit, & ipse cum exercitu Italiam petijt, accepturus imperialem coronam.
