Sequenti anno Otto rex Romam venit, repugnantem subegit, ordinari se à Ioanne papa Imperatorem exegit. Otto imperator factus Ioannem papam pro sceleribus suis arguens, minime eum corrigere potuit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 961, King Otto had his son Otto, born of Adelheid, elected king. He himself went with an army to Italy to receive the imperial crown. In the following year King Otto came to Rome, subdued those who resisted, and demanded to be ordained emperor by Pope John. Made emperor, Otto accused Pope John of his crimes, but was by no means able to correct him.

units.la: NB.
units.tr: NB.

units.la: Anno DCCCC.LXIII, imperator natalem Domini Papiæ moratus, iterum Romam venit, pro sceleribus Ioannis papæ diiudicandis. Sed eodem Ioanne papa imperatorem in Campaniam fugiente, in locum eius à Romanis & imperatore vir venerabilis Leo ordinatus est. Sequenti anno Romani Leonem papam expellunt, mortuoque Ioanne papa priore, Benedictus nolente imperatore ordinatur. Igitur 40 Roma ab Imperatore obsessa est, & tanta fame oppressa, vt sextarius furfuris væniret XXX denarijs. Non multo post dedita vrbe, traditoque Benedicto, Imperator papam Leonem restituit, & Romanos ei fidem per sacramenta promittere coegit.
units.tr: In the year 963 the emperor, having spent Christmas at Pavia, came again to Rome to judge the crimes of Pope John. When Pope John fled into Campania, the venerable Leo was ordained in his place by the Romans and the emperor. In the following year the Romans expelled Pope Leo, and after the former pope John died, Benedict was ordained against the emperor's will. So Rome was besieged by the emperor and oppressed by such famine that a sextarius of bran sold for thirty denarii. Not long after, the city surrendered and Benedict was handed over. The emperor restored Pope Leo and compelled the Romans to promise him fealty by oath.

units.la: Vsque ad hæc tempora Roma sæpius capta est. Primò capta est à conditione sua, anno CCC.XXXV, nec vnquam postea simile passa est ruinam: cuius destructionis casus hic fuit. Galli senones, duce Breuno, exercitu copioso freti, totis viribus Romam contenderunt. Hos dirè irruentes Fabius consul cum exercitu excepit, nec tamen obstitit: imo hostilis ille impetus Romanos quasi aridas segetes succidit, strauit, & transiuit vrbe destructa & incensa. Secundo Roma capta est, à conditione sua anno M.C.LXIIII, ab Alarico rege Gothorum, sub Honorio imperatore. Tertio capta est Roma, à conditione sua, anno M.CC.IX, à Genserico rege Africæ, sub Maximo imperatore. Odazer rex Torcilingorum & Rugorum, pervasa Italia Romam capit quarta iam vice, à conditione sua anno M.C.C.XXX, & Augule imperatore exiliato, ipse Romæ tyrannicè regnat. Exinde res Romanæ & omnis imperij status apud Constantinopolim solummodo esse coepit: Hesperia fere omni & Lybia barbaris addicta. His temporibus Theodoricus rex Italiæ Zenoni imperatori, qui tunc in Orientis partibus apud Constantinopolim Romanũ apicem gubernabat, cum suis Gothis militauit. Qui missus ab imperatore eodem, Odakarũ Romæ obsedit, cepit, & interemit, anno dominicæ incarnationis cccc1x, & ipse Romam consensu Zenonis & Occidentis imperiũ xxx annis obtinuit. Hic Romæ, Rauennæ, Veronæ, & alibi, per singula quæq; regia habitacula construxit: qui etiam Arrianis fauit, occisis Boethio poeta, Symmacho patricio & Ioanna papa. Iste est Theodoricus, de quo Teutonica extant carmina, filius Dietmari, de quo etiam Gregorius in dialogo scribit. ¶ Quinta vice ab incarnatione Domini D.xl v, sub Iustiniano imperatore, Totila rex Gothorum transpadanorum Romam petijt, eamq; obsidionibus circumcludit. Quæ tantam famis penuriam passa est, vt præ magnitudine inopiæ, natorum suorum carnes comedere vellent. Fessis nimiũ Romanis, nec valentibus se tueri, Totila rex vrbem ingressus est, quæ tamen citò per Narsem eunuchum & cubicularium Imperatoris recuperata est, & liberata à Gothis, ipsis pene omnibus ad internecionem deletis, & Totila rege eorum interfecto. ¶ Sexta vice à conditione sua obsessa & capta est Roma, anno Domini DCCCC.LXIIII, ab Ottone magno imperatore, vt supra dictũ est. Qui decus tanti nominis, scilicet Imperatoris, à Francigenis in Teutonicos primus magnanimiter transuexit.
units.tr: Up to these times Rome had been taken very often. It was first taken in the 335th year after its founding, and never afterwards suffered such ruin; the cause of that destruction was this. The Senones, Gauls under Brennus, relying on a large army, pressed with all their might towards Rome. Fabius the consul met them as they charged fiercely with his army, yet did not stop them; rather, that hostile onslaught cut down and laid low the Romans like dry crops, and passed through the city, which was destroyed and burned. Second, Rome was taken in the 1164th year after its founding, by Alaric, king of the Goths, under the emperor Honorius. Third, Rome was taken in the 1209th year after its founding, by Genseric, king of Africa, under the emperor Maximus. Odoacer, king of the Torcilingi and Rugi, having overrun Italy, took Rome the fourth time, in the 1230th year after its founding. With the emperor Augustulus exiled, he himself ruled Rome as tyrant. From then on Roman affairs and the whole state of the empire began to be centred only at Constantinople, and nearly all of Hesperia and Libya was given over to the barbarians. In these times Theodoric, king of Italy, served the emperor Zeno, who then governed the Roman rule in the eastern parts at Constantinople, and he campaigned with his Goths. Sent by the same emperor, he besieged Odoacer at Rome, captured and killed him, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 493. He himself held the empire of the West for thirty years, with Zeno's consent. At Rome, Ravenna, Verona and elsewhere he built royal residences in each place. He also favoured the Arians, having killed the poet Boethius, the patrician Symmachus and Pope John. This is that Theodoric about whom Teutonic songs exist, the son of Dietmar, of whom Gregory also writes in his Dialogues. Fifth, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 545, under the emperor Justinian, Totila, king of the Transpadane Goths, made for Rome and encircled it with sieges. The city suffered such a shortage of food that, from the greatness of their want, the people wished to eat the flesh of their own children. The Romans, being utterly worn out and unable to defend themselves, saw King Totila enter the city. Yet it was soon recovered by Narses, the eunuch and chamberlain of the emperor, and freed from the Goths, nearly all of whom were destroyed to the last man, and their king Totila was killed. Sixth, Rome was besieged and taken from its founding in the year of the Lord 964, by the Emperor Otto the Great, as mentioned above. He was the first to carry the honour of so great a name, that of Emperor, magnanimously from the Franks over to the Teutons.

units.la: Mirandum est, eandem ciuitatem, sc. Romam, totiés captam, nec tamẽ deletam, nec seruituti vllatenus addictam: quod in summis & præcipuis regnis non ita contigit. Nam Niniuen & Babylon, & Alexandria, & Persepolis aliquando numerosissimis imperabat, postea tributa pendebant. Roma verò etsi interdum irrupta, semper tamen libera: si plærumque humiliata, semper tamen domina. Sed de his dicta sufficiant.
units.tr: It is remarkable that the same city, Rome, was captured so many times and yet was never destroyed nor ever reduced to slavery; this has not happened so with the greatest and chief kingdoms. For Nineveh and Babylon and Alexandria and Persepolis once ruled over very numerous peoples, and afterwards paid tribute. Rome, though sometimes broken into, was always free; though often humbled, she was always mistress. But let these things suffice.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.LXXI, sanctus Vdalricus episcopus infirmus, Adalberoni, sororis suæ filio, episcopatum impetrauit. Itaq; synodo apud Ingelnheim ab episcopis collecta, beatus Vdalricus episcopus & Adalbero transgressionis Canonum accusantur: sed causa sua dicta & excusata, absoluti discesserunt.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 971, Saint Udalric, bishop, being ill, obtained the bishopric for Adalbero, the son of his sister. Accordingly a synod was gathered at Ingelheim by the bishops, and blessed Udalric the bishop and Adalbero were accused of breaking the canons; but their case was heard and they were excused, and they departed absolved.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.LXXIII, Otto magnus imperator subito mortuus apud Parthenopolim, id est Medegeburg, vbi episcopatũ fecerat, sepultus est: & filius eius Otto, cognomento Mirabilis, regnauit pro eo. Imperatrix verò Adelheidis post ipsum sanctè & regiliose viuens longo tempore, multa contulit ecclesiis de regali munificentia: & ad vltimum super littus Rheni fluminis nobile cœnobium construxit, dictum nomine Schlse, & illud prædijs & alijs opibus ditauit, vbi & ipsa postea moriens quieuit. Eodem anno, Adelbero futurus (vt sperabatur) Augustensis episcopus, obijt. Ipso etiam anno sanctus Vdalricus migrauit ad Dominum, anno ætatis suæ LXXXIII, episcopatus L. Sequenti anno sanctus Cunradus Constantiensis episcopus de hac vita decessit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 973, the emperor Otto the Great died suddenly at Parthenopolis, that is Magdeburg, where he had founded a bishopric, and was buried there; and his son Otto, surnamed the Wonderful, reigned in his place. The empress Adelheid, living holily and royally for a long time after him, bestowed many gifts on the churches from royal generosity; and at last she built on the bank of the river Rhine a noble monastery called Selz, and endowed it with estates and other wealth, and there she herself, dying later, rests. In the same year Adalbero, who was to be (as was hoped) bishop of Augsburg, died. In that same year Saint Udalric departed to the Lord, in the eighty-third year of his life and the fiftieth of his episcopate. In the following year Saint Conrad, bishop of Constance, passed from this life.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.XCI, Otto rex peragrata Italia, venit in montem Gargani, & cognouit à referentibus, angelorum obsequia nocturno tempore ibi esse, nec 40 vllum mortalium velint interesse. Cuius caussæ notitiam cum disposuisset curiosius indagare, apostolicum conuenit super hac re primum. Cui cum apostolicus consilium suum indidisset, sibi minus placere illum angelicis ministerijs interesse: parui pendit consilium Papæ, & eo ignorante proficiscitur in montem Gargani. Vbi dum pernoctaret, inter cætera quæ cognouit sanctorum mysteria, veniâ consequutus est angelorum. Quòd temerè sacratum locum introierat, tantùm ab angelis prostratus, pro quodam iudicio, quod perfecisse debuerat, nec fecit: pro negligentijs transuerberatus est. Deinde sanctus Michael iussit eũ Romam remeare, statuto sibi die, quo eum vellet inuisere. Sicq; cruentatus rex Romam repedauit, & Benedicto papæ cuncta à se visa retexuit. Igitur rex valido languore tactus, vita decessit, & ab archangelo receptus, superis est sociatus, anno domini DCCCC.XCIIII, cuius exequiæ per apostolicum condigno honore celebratæ, in porticu sancti Petri sepelitur: pro quo filius eius Otto adhuc puer regnauit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 991, King Otto, having travelled through Italy, came to Mount Gargano, and learned from those who reported it that the services of the angels take place there at night, and that no mortal wishes to be present. When he had resolved to inquire more carefully into the cause of this, he first met with the pope about the matter. When the pope gave his counsel, that it was less pleasing to him that the king should take part in the angelic ministries, Otto paid little heed to the pope's advice, and set out for Mount Gargano without the pope's knowledge. While he spent the night there, among the other mysteries of the saints which he learned, he obtained the pardon of the angels. Because he had rashly entered the holy place, he was struck down by the angels alone, and was scourged for his negligence in a certain duty which he ought to have performed and did not. Then Saint Michael ordered him to return to Rome, with a day fixed on which he would wish to visit him. And so the king, bloodied, returned to Rome and related to Pope Benedict all that he had seen. Then the king, struck by a severe illness, died in the year of the Lord 994, and, received by the archangel, was joined to the blessed above. His funeral was celebrated by the pope with due honour, and he is buried in the portico of Saint Peter's; in his place his son Otto, still a boy, reigned.

units.la: Anno domini DCCCC.XCV, Henricus dux Bauariæ, frater Ottonis magni, obijt, cuius ducatum filius eius Henricus obtinuit. Anno domini DCCCC.XCVII, Bruno, filius Ottonis ducis Alemanniae Romae papa electus & ordinatus, Gregorius quintus vocatur. Otto subactis rebellibus in Italia, Romam veniens à Gregorio papa imperialem accepit unctionem.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 995, Henry, duke of Bavaria, brother of Otto the Great, died, and his son Henry obtained the duchy. In the year of the Lord 997, Bruno, son of Otto, duke of Alemannia, was elected and ordained pope at Rome, and is called Gregory V. Otto, having subdued the rebels in Italy, came to Rome and received the imperial anointing from Pope Gregory.

units.la: Anno domini M.II, Otto imperator obijt,& Aquis sepelitur, pro quo Henricus dux Bauariae rex electus est. Eodem anno Leo papa, qui & Bruno de castro Egensheim, natus est.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1002, the emperor Otto died and was buried at Aachen, and in his place Henry, duke of Bavaria, was elected king. In the same year Pope Leo, who is also called Bruno, was born at the castle of Egisheim.

units.la: Anno Domini M. VII, Henricus rex summo studio apud castrum suum, Babenberg dictum, nobilem constrvxit episcopatum, in honore sancti Georgij martyris.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1007, King Henry, with the greatest zeal, built at his castle called Bamberg a noble bishopric, in honour of Saint George the martyr.

units.la: Anno Domini M. XIIII, Henricus rex imperiali benedictione, à Benedicto papa octavo coronatur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1014, King Henry was crowned with the imperial blessing by Pope Benedict VIII.

units.la: Anno domini M.XV, monasterium sanctae Mariae virginis in Argentina surgit primò à fundatione sua.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1015, the monastery of Saint Mary the Virgin in Strasbourg arose, first from its foundation.

units.la: Anno domini M.XXIIII, Henricus imperator absq; filijs obiens, quia coniunx sua Kunegundis virgo permansit, apud Babenberg episcopatum ambo sepeliuntur: & Cunradus de Guebelingen in regem vnctus est, & anno domini M.XXVII, à Iohanne papa decimo octavo Romae in imperatorem coronatur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1024, the emperor Henry died without sons, since his wife Kunigunde remained a virgin; both were buried in the bishopric of Bamberg. Conrad of Waiblingen was anointed king, and in the year of the Lord 1027 was crowned emperor at Rome by Pope John XVIII.

units.la: Anno domini M. XXVIII, Wernharius Argentinensis episcopus primus obijt, & Wilhelmus succedit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1028, Wernher, the first bishop of Strasbourg, died, and Wilhelm succeeded him.

units.la: Anno domini M. XXXI, monasterium sancti Thomae apostoli in Argentina, à Wilhelmo consecratur, & sancti Petri ab eodem inchoatur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1031, the monastery of Saint Thomas the Apostle in Strasbourg was consecrated by Wilhelm, and the building of Saint Peter's was begun by him.

units.la: Anno domini M. XLV, dedicatum est monasterium Hohenburg, in honore beatae Mariae virginis à venerabili Brunone, Leucorum, id est Tullensium episcopo, postea apostolico.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1045, the monastery of Hohenburg was dedicated in honour of the blessed Virgin Mary by the venerable Bruno, bishop of the Leuci, that is of Toul, afterwards pope.

units.la: Anno domini M. XLVII, Wilhelmus Argentinensis episcopus obijt: cui Hetzel successit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1047, Wilhelm, bishop of Strasbourg, died; Hetzel succeeded him.

units.la: Anno domini M. LXXVII, Bertoldus dux Carinthiorum, qui & Zeringen, vir catholicus, obijt.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1077, Berthold, duke of Carinthia, who was also called of Zähringen, a Catholic man, died.

units.la: Anno domini M. LXXIX, Wernharius Argentinensis episcopus secundus obijt, cui Otto schismaticus successit. Eodem tempore in Alemannia tria monasteria primò instituta, egregiè pollebant: sancti Blasij in nigra sylua, sancti Aurelij in Hirsaugia, sancti Saluatoris in Schafhusen, quod nauium domus dicitur. Wilhelmus etiam Hirsaugiensis abbas in causa S. Petri feruentissimus, eo tempore plura monasteria vsque quaque ex integro construxit: sancti Georgij in Nigra sylua, alterum sancti Gregorij, item aliud ad Duplicem aquam prope Danubiu, item aliud in loco qui Kamberg dicitur: aliud quoque monasteriu in Rheni fluminis ripa, Petershusen dictum, quae omnia regularibus disciplinis instituit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1079, Wernher, the second bishop of Strasbourg, died, and Otto, the schismatic, succeeded him. At that time three monasteries, newly founded in Alemannia, flourished greatly: that of Saint Blasius in the Black Forest, that of Saint Aurelius at Hirsau, and that of the Saviour at Schaffhausen, which is called the house of ships. Wilhelm too, abbot of Hirsau, most fervent in the cause of Saint Peter, at that time built many monasteries from the ground up in various places: that of Saint George in the Black Forest, another of Saint Gregory, another at Donaueschingen near the Danube, another in a place called Kamberg, and another monastery on the bank of the Rhine, called Petershausen. He established all of these under a regular discipline.

units.la: Anno domini M. LXXXXVII, sanctus Nicolaus archiepiscopus à Mitra in Barensem ciuitatem translatus est.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1097, Saint Nicholas, archbishop, was translated from Myra to the city of Bari.

units.la: Anno domini M. XC, fundata est Margbach ecclesia sancti Augustini, à militari & illustri viro Burchardo de Gebelsuilre, cuius adiutor & cooperator fidelissimus magister Manegoldus de Lurenbach extitit. In sequenti anno in Teutonicis partibus caro cum sanguine pluit, & bufones cum piscibus coelo ceciderunt, & sanguis de panibus fluere videbatur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1090, the church of Saint Augustine at Marbach was founded by the knightly and illustrious man Burchard of Gebelsweiler, whose most faithful helper and collaborator was Master Manegold of Lauterbach. In the following year flesh mixed with blood rained down in the German lands, toads fell from the sky with fishes, and blood seemed to flow from the bread.

units.la: Anno domini M. XCII, principes Alemanniae, ad defensionem sanctae matris ecclesiae, vnanimiter conuenerunt, sibique ad hoc negotium exequendum fratrem Gebehardi Constantiensis episcopi, Bertoldum de Zeringen, ducem totius Sueuiae constituerunt, qui nondum ducatum aliquem habuit, etsi iam dudum nomen Ducis habere consueuerit. Hic praeterito anno in proprio allodio Brisgaugiae Friburg ciuitatem initiauit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1092, the princes of Alemannia gathered unanimously for the defence of holy mother Church, and appointed to carry out this business Berthold of Zähringen, brother of Gebhard, bishop of Constance, as duke of all Swabia. He had not yet held any duchy, although for a long time he had been accustomed to bear the title of duke. In the previous year he had founded the city of Freiburg on his own allodial land in Breisgau.

units.la: Anno domini M.XCIII, Bertholdus dux Alemanniae, qui & de Zeringen, coenobium monachorum in honore sancti Petri in Nigra sylua constrvxit, quod postea frater eius Gebehardus Constantiensis episcopus consecrauit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1093, Berthold, duke of Alemannia, also called of Zähringen, built a monastery of monks in honour of Saint Peter in the Black Forest, which his brother Gebhard, bishop of Constance, later consecrated.

units.la: Anno domini M. XCIX, Ierusalem à gente Francorum, & à duce Godefrido capitur, & multa laudabiliter ibidem peraguntur. Eodem anno inchoatur Cistertiensis ordo, & per multas prouincias mundi dilatatur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1099, Jerusalem was captured by the Frankish people and by Duke Godfrey, and many praiseworthy deeds were done there. In the same year the Cistercian order began and spread through many provinces of the world.

units.la: Anno domini M c, facta est fames incomparabilis & mortalitas horribilis. Otto quoque Argentinensis schismaticus de Ierosolymitano itinere reuersus, sed de schismate (vt putabatur) non emendatus, diem clausit extremum: cui Baldeuuinus, sex tantum victurus hebdomadas, successit. Cui eodem anno Cuno successit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1100, an incomparable famine and a horrible mortality occurred. Otto, the schismatic bishop of Strasbourg, also returned from the journey to Jerusalem, but was not (as was thought) corrected of his schism, and closed his last day. Baldwin, who was to live only six weeks, succeeded him, and in the same year Cuno succeeded Baldwin.

units.la: Anno domini M. cxxii, Bertoldus dux de Zeringen Mollesheim occiditur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1122, Berthold, duke of Zähringen, was killed at Mollesheim.

units.la: Anno domini M. cxxiii, Cuno Argentinensis episcopus de sede pellitur: cui Bruno episcopus supraponitur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1123, Cuno, bishop of Strasbourg, was driven from his see, and Bishop Bruno was set over it in his place.

units.la: Anno domini M. cxxv, Henricus imperator iunior, in ordine Imperatorum quartus, regum vero quintus, apud Traiectum rebus humanis exemptus in ciuitate Spira patribus suis appositus est. Huius sororem Agnetem pater suus Henricus imperator cuidam Friderico de castro Stauffen, obopem sibi ferendam, in matrimonio tradiderat, eiq; ducatum Alemanniæ dederat, quem Bertoldus de Zeringen ex nobilissimis optimatibus regni prius possidendum acceperat, vt superius dictum est. Fridericus igitur dux Sueuorum & gener imperatoris factus, Bertoldum pace petere coegit. Conditio autem pacis talis fuit: vt Bertoldus ducatum exfestucaret, sic tamen vt Turegum nobilissimum Sueuiæ oppidum, à manu Imperatoris ei tenendum remaneret. Quidam totam Teutonicam terram Alemanniam dictam putant, omnesque Teutonicos Alemannos vocare solent. Sed illa tantum prouincia, id est Sueuia, à Lemanno fluuio vocatur Alemannia: populiq; eam inhabitantes solummodo vocantur Alemanni.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1125, Henry the Younger, fourth in the order of emperors and fifth of the kings, was taken from human affairs at Utrecht, and was laid with his fathers in the city of Speyer. His father, the emperor Henry, had given his sister Agnes in marriage to a certain Frederick of the castle of Staufen, to be a support to him, and had given him the duchy of Alemannia, which Berthold of Zähringen, as said above, had earlier received from the most noble nobles of the kingdom to hold. Frederick, therefore, duke of the Swabians and son-in-law of the emperor, compelled Berthold to seek peace. The condition of the peace was this: that Berthold should give up the duchy by the symbolic surrender of a straw, yet so that Zurich, the most noble town of Swabia, should remain his to hold from the emperor's hand. Some think that the whole German land is called Alemannia, and customarily call all Germans Alemanni. But only that province, that is Swabia, is called Alemannia from the river Lemannus, and the peoples inhabiting it alone are called Alemanni.

units.la: Bertoldus igitur quanuis in hoc negotio Imperatori cesserit, tamen strenuissimus ac fortissimus fuit: qui vacuum exhinc nomen Ducis gerens, id quasi hæreditarium posteris reliquit. Hic Bertoldus postea Mollesheim occisus est. Omnes enim usque ad præsentem diem Duces dicti sunt, nullum ducatum habentes, soloq; nomine sine re participantes. Nisi quis ducatum esse dicat comitatum inter Iuram & montem Iouis, quæ post mortem Wilhelmi comitis, filius suus Cunradus ab Imperatore Lothario suscepit: vel à ducatu Carentano, quæ nunquam habuerut, Ducis eos nomine honorandos contendat: in aliis tamen rerū & honoris non parua pollentes magnificentia.
units.tr: Bertold, though he yielded to the emperor in this affair, was nonetheless most vigorous and brave. Bearing thenceforth the empty name of duke, he left it to his successors as if it were hereditary. This Bertold was afterwards killed at Mollesheim. For all dukes down to the present day have been called so without having any duchy, sharing only the name without the reality. Unless someone says that the county between the Jura and Mount Jove, which Conrad, son of Count William, received from Emperor Lothar after his father's death, is a duchy, or contends that they should be honoured with the title of duke from the Carinthian duchy, which they never had. Yet they are not a little distinguished in other matters of rank and honour, in magnificence.

units.la: Fridericus autem ducatum Alemanniæ sine contradictione habuit, & ex nobilissima compare sua Agnete duos filios habuit, Fridericum ducem & Cunradum postea regem ac post multa virtutum insignia diem vltimum claudens, in proprio fundo Lorche humatus est.
units.tr: Frederick held the duchy of Alemannia without dispute. By his most noble wife Agnes he had two sons, Frederick the duke and Conrad, afterwards king. After many notable marks of virtue he closed his last day and was buried at Lorch, on his own estate.

units.la: Henricus vero imperator iunior, sororem suam Agnetem viduam, Leopaldo marchioni Orientali, id est Osteriche, in vxorem dedit, quæ ei quatuor filios & tres filias peperit. Leopaldum ducem Bauariæ, Henricum ducem Austriæ, Cunradum Salzeburgensem archiepiscopū, Ottonem Frisingensem episcopū, Gertrudem ducissam Bohemiæ, Bertā ducissam Polonorū, & Itam marchionissam de Monteferrato. Fridericus igitur dux Alemannorum, frater Cunradi postea regis, duxit filiam Henricum ducis Noricorum, id est Bauarorum, nomine Iuditham vxorem, genuitq; ex ea Fridericū postea Imperatorē, & Iuditham, quæ Matthæo Lotharingorū duci nupsit.
units.tr: Emperor Henry the Younger gave his widowed sister Agnes as wife to Leopold, margrave of the East, that is of Austria. She bore him four sons and three daughters: Leopold, duke of Bavaria; Henry, duke of Austria; Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg; Otto, bishop of Freising; Gertrude, duchess of Bohemia; Bertha, duchess of the Poles; and Itta, margravine of Montferrat. Frederick, therefore, duke of the Alemanni and brother of the later King Conrad, married the daughter of Henry, duke of the Noricans, that is of the Bavarians, named Judith. By her he begot Frederick, afterwards emperor, and Judith, who married Matthew, duke of the Lorrainers.

units.la: Henricus iste Noricorum dux erat natione Alemannus, ex antiqua & nobilissima Welphorum familia originē trahens, ac per hoc multas possessiones ex ea parte qua Pyrenæos montes attingit Alemannia, iure hæreditario habens. Hic Henricus duos filios habuit, scilicet, Henricum, Welphonem & Iuditham filiam, vt supra dictū est de ipsa. Vnus filiorum id est Henricus patri in possessione & in ducatu Noricorū successit, qui etiam Gertrudem filiam Lotharij regis cum ducatu Saxoniæ accepto, vxorem duxit. Alter filius id est Welpho, fuit princeps Sardiniæ, dux Spoleti, marchio Tusciæ. Sed vnde digressi sumus reuertamur.
units.tr: This Henry, duke of the Noricans, was an Alemannian by nation, tracing his origin from the ancient and most noble family of the Welfs. Hence he held by hereditary right many possessions in that part of Alemannia which reaches the Pyrenees. Henry had two sons, Henry and Welf, and a daughter Judith, as was said above of her. One of the sons, Henry, succeeded his father in the possessions and in the duchy of the Noricans. He also married Gertrude, daughter of King Lothar, together with the duchy of Saxony which he received. The other son, Welf, was prince of Sardinia, duke of Spoleto and margrave of Tuscany. But let us return to where we digressed.

units.la: Henrico imperatore defuncto, vti dictum est, Lotharius dux Saxonum in regem eligitur. Anno domini M. cxxviii, Lotharius rex ab Innocentio papa Romæ in Lateranensi monasterio consecratur in Imperatorem.
units.tr: Emperor Henry having died, as has been said, Lothar, duke of the Saxons, was elected king. In the year of our Lord 1128, King Lothar was consecrated emperor at Rome by Pope Innocent, in the monastery of the Lateran.

units.la: Eodem anno constructum est monasterium, quod vocatur Nouum castrum, in fundo Reinaldi Comitis de Luzelnburg, & coepit crescere in personis & rebus, & religione, ad laudem Iesu Christi.
units.tr: In the same year the monastery called Neuenburg was built on the estate of Count Reinald of Lützelburg. It began to grow in members, possessions and religion, to the praise of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Eodem anno, quarto nonas Augusti, Sol obscuratus est, sexta hora diei, & tenebræ factæ sunt.
units.tr: In the same year, on the fourth day before the nones of August, the sun was darkened at the sixth hour of the day, and there was darkness.

units.la: Anno domini M. C XXX X, facta est pugna inter Gebehardum Argentinensem episcopum & Fridericum ducem Alemanniæ apud <bl>Gügenheim</bl>. Eodem anno combustum est maius monasterium Argentinense primò.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1130, a battle took place between Gebhard, bishop of Strasbourg, and Frederick, duke of Alemannia, at Gügenheim. In the same year the greater monastery of Strasbourg was burned for the first time.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXXXVIII, Lotharius Imperator obiit: cui Cunradus frater Friderici ducis Alemanniæ, contra quorundam principum voluntatem in regno succedit.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1138, Emperor Lothar died. Conrad, brother of Duke Frederick of Alemannia, succeeded him in the kingdom, against the wishes of some princes.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXL, combustum est monasterium Argentinense secundò. Sequenti anno Gebehardus episcopus obiit: cui Burchardus successit.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1140, the monastery of Strasbourg was burned a second time. In the following year Bishop Gebhard died, and Burchard succeeded him.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXLIII, Rogerius rex Siciliæ classes in Græciam destinat, praesectis eis ducibus strenuis & nauali prælio gnaris. Qui maxima ibi præda direpta, opifices etiam qui sericos pannos texere solent, ob ignominiam Imperatoris illius, suiq; principis gloriam, captivos deducunt: quos Rogerius in Panormitano Siciliæ metropoli collocans, artem illam texendi suos edocere præcepit. Et exhinc prædicta ars illa prius à Græcis tantum inter Christianos habita, Romanis cepit parere ingeniis.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1143, Roger, king of Sicily, sent fleets into Greece, placing over them commanders who were vigorous and skilled in naval battle. They plundered there a great booty and also led away as captives the craftsmen who are accustomed to weave silk cloths, to the disgrace of that emperor and the glory of their own prince. Roger settled them in Palermo, the metropolis of Sicily, and ordered them to teach their weaving art to his own people. From then on that art, which had previously been held among Christians only by the Greeks, began to flourish among the talents of the Romans.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXLVIII, facta est expeditio Ierusalem secunda, sub Cunrado rege Romanorum, Ludouico rege Francorum, Bernhardo̅ abbate Clarauallensi.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1148, the second expedition to Jerusalem was made, under Conrad, king of the Romans, Louis, king of the Franks, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.

units.la: Anno domini M.CL, combustum est monasterium Argentinense tertiò. Eodem anno obiit Henricus filius Cunradi regis, quem pater ante expeditionem Ierosolymitanam per electionem principum regem ordinauerat, habens adhuc filium alium Fridericum nomine.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1150, the monastery of Strasbourg was burned a third time. In the same year died Henry, son of King Conrad, whom his father, before the expedition to Jerusalem, had appointed king by election of the princes. He still had another son, named Frederick.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLII, Cunradus rex obiit: cui fratris sui filius Fridericus dux Alemanniæ, in regno successit.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1152, King Conrad died. His nephew, Frederick, duke of Alemannia, son of his brother, succeeded him in the kingdom.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLVIII, monasterium in Nouo castro consecratur, sub glorioso Friderico Imperatore, anno imperij eius sexto, in prædio Reinoldi comitis, quarto nonas Maij, à reuerendis episcopis Burkardo Argentinensis & Henrico Trecensis ecclesiæ, in honore sanctæ Crucis, & beatæ Mariæ virginis.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1158, under the glorious Emperor Frederick, in the sixth year of his reign, the monastery at Neuenburg was consecrated on the estate of Count Reinold, on the fourth day before the nones of May, by the reverend bishops Burchard of Strasbourg and Henry of the church of Troyes, in honour of the holy Cross and of the blessed Virgin Mary.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXII, Mediolanum à Friderico Imperatore capitur & destruitur. Eodem anno Horburg à comite Hugone de Dagesburg destruitur. Ipso anno Burcardus Argentinensis episcopus obiit, cui Rudolfus successit.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1162, Milan was captured and destroyed by Emperor Frederick. In the same year Horburg was destroyed by Count Hugh of Dagsburg. In that same year Burchard, bishop of Strasbourg, died, and Rudolf succeeded him.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXX, beatus Thomas Cantuariensis archiepiscopus martyrium est passus.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1170, blessed Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, suffered martyrdom.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXXVI, combustum est monasterium Argentinense quartò.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1176, the monastery of Strasbourg was burned a fourth time.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXXVIII, facta est caedes magna in Lagelnheim iuxta Columbariam, Cunone de Horburg & Egelolfo de Vrselingen inter se praeliantibus.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1178, a great slaughter was made at Lagelnheim near Colmar, Cuno of Horburg and Egelolf of Urslingen fighting against each other.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXXIX, factum est Concilium magnum sub Alexandro papa, in quo fuerunt fere quingenti episcopi & abbates, aliiq; religiosi innumerabiles: in quo Bremensis archiepiscopus, Rudolfus Argentinensis, Ludouicus Basiliensis & Metensis episcopi depONUNTUR. Inchoabatur hoc Concilium, v calend. Martij, & terminatum est circa finem Aprilis.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1179, a great council was held under Pope Alexander, at which there were nearly five hundred bishops and abbots and countless other religious. At this council the archbishop of Bremen, Rudolf of Strasbourg, and the bishops Louis of Basel and of Metz were deposed. The council began on the fifth day before the calends of March and was concluded about the end of April.

units.la: Eodem anno Cunradus in vigilia Thomæ apostoli Argentinensis episcopus eligitur, qui proximo anno eodem die sepeliebatur, & Henricus cathedræ præficitur.
units.tr: In the same year Conrad was elected bishop of Strasbourg on the vigil of the apostle Thomas. The next year, on the same day, he was buried, and Henry was set over the see.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXXX, dedicata est maior ecclesia inferioris monasterij apud Hohenburg, in honore sanctæ Dei genitricis Mariæ, à Montuano apostolicæ sedis legato.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1180, the greater church of the lower monastery at Hohenburg was dedicated, in honour of holy Mary, mother of God, by Montuanus, legate of the apostolic see.

units.la: Anno domini M.CLXXXV, quidam Astronomicus Toletanus, nomine Ioannes, misit literas per omnes mundi partes, asserens, proximo sequeti anno circa mensem Septembrem omnes planetas debere conuenire in vnum domicilium, & ventum qui omne pene domicilium destructurus esset, venturum, & mortalitatem & famem, & multa alia incommoda futura, & finem mundi, & aduentum Antichristi instare: & in hoc omnes Astronomicos aliosq; Philosophos, & magos, tam Christianorum quam gentilium & Iudæorum concordare. Vnde maximus timor multos invasit, ita vt quidam fecerint sibi subterraneas domos: & per multas ecclesias ieiunia & processiones & letaniæ fiebant. Sed vt probaretur sapientia mundi huius stultitiam esse apud Deum, prædicto tempore magna aëris serenitas & tranquillitas fuit, & nihil eorum quæ prædicta fuerunt, euenit. Ipso anno castrum Brisache à rege Henrico initiatur.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1185, a certain astronomer of Toledo, named John, sent letters through all parts of the world. He asserted that in the following year, about the month of September, all the planets would have to come together into one house, and a wind would come which would destroy almost every house; that pestilence and famine and many other calamities would follow, and that the end of the world and the coming of Antichrist were at hand. He claimed that all astronomers and other philosophers and magicians, of Christians as well as of Gentiles and Jews, agreed on this. Hence great fear seized many, so that some made underground dwellings for themselves, and fasts, processions and litanies were held in many churches. But so that it might be proved that the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God, at the predicted time there was great clearness and calm of the air, and none of the things foretold came to pass. In the same year the castle of Breisach was begun by King Henry.

units.la: Anno domini M. CLXXXVI, erat hyems calida, ita quòd in Decembri & Ianuario multæ arbores florerent, in quibus circa Februarium pyra, quantitate in modum avellanæ, magna conspiciebantur. Sed proximè sequenti anno, scilicet anno domini M.CLXXXVII, circa Martium magna aëris inclementia & asperitas algoris veniens, ferè vsq; ad calend. Iunij duravit, ita quod in Pentecoste, videlicet in medio Maio, nix magna cecidit, & ferè omnia poma perierunt.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1186, the winter was warm, so that in December and January many trees blossomed, and around February pears the size of hazelnuts were seen in great numbers. But in the very next year, that is the year of our Lord 1187, about March a great harshness of the air and bitter cold set in, lasting almost until the calends of June. So at Pentecost, that is in mid-May, a heavy snow fell, and almost all the fruit perished.

units.la: Eodem anno Argentina in mense prædicto ex magna parte incendio vastata est.
units.tr: In the same year, in the aforesaid month, Strasbourg was largely laid waste by fire.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXC. beatæ memoriæ Henricus Argentinensis episcopus, in annunciatione S. Mariæ virginis, die Paschæ, ex hac luce migravit, cui Cunradus successit. Postea anno domini M.CXCIII, idem Cunradus episcopus Argentinensis capitur à quibusdam ministerialibus eiusdem civitatis.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1190, Henry, bishop of Strasbourg, of blessed memory, departed this light on the Feast of the Annunciation of St Mary the Virgin, on Easter Day, and Conrad succeeded him. Afterwards, in the year of our Lord 1193, the same Conrad, bishop of Strasbourg, was captured by certain ministerials of the same city.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXC, Imp. Fridericus assumpsit characterem crucis, & per terram, non per mare, cum magna multitudine ad liberationem terræ sanctæ processit. Et cum esset in Armenia obiit in quadam aqua, quæ vocatur Ferrum, submersus, & Antiochiæ sepultus.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1190, Emperor Frederick took up the sign of the cross and set out to free the Holy Land, going by land, not by sea, with a great multitude. When he was in Armenia he died, drowned in a stream called Ferrum, and he was buried at Antioch.

units.la: Eodem anno rex Henricus, filius Friderici Imp. huius cum exercitu in Italiā profectus est, tum pro imperiali benedictione, tum pro regni Apuliæ suscepione.
units.tr: In the same year King Henry, son of Emperor Frederick, set out with an army for Italy, both to receive the imperial blessing and to take up the kingdom of Apulia.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXCI, Clemens papa obiit: cui Celestinus, qui & Iacinctus successit, consecratus die paschæ: qui etiam Imp. Henricum secunda feria paschæ vnanimi omnium Romanorum consensu consecravit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1191, Pope Clement died. He was succeeded by Celestine, also called Hyacinth, who was consecrated on Easter Day. On the Monday after Easter, with the unanimous consent of all the Romans, he also crowned Emperor Henry.

units.la: Eodem anno Fridericus dux Alemanniæ, frater Imperatoris, in obsidione Acharon obiit, & in domo Teutonicorum sepultus est. Pro quo Cunradus frater eius ducatum Sueuiæ accepit.
units.tr: In the same year Frederick, duke of Swabia and brother of the Emperor, died at the siege of Acre and was buried in the house of the Teutonic Knights. In his place his brother Conrad received the duchy of Swabia.

units.la: Anno dni M.CXCVII, cùm Imp. circa Augustum in quodā nemore, in quo sontes erant frigidissimi, venationis delectaretur exercitio, in quo etiam maximus calor per diem & tale frigus, quod terram gelu & pruina cōstringeret fuit per noctem: quadam nocte tactus frigore, circa festum B. Sixti cepit infirmari. Quamobrem iussit ad se vsq; Messinam civitatem, quæ duabus diætis abillo distabat loco, deferri: vbi diarrhæa infirmitate laborans, & in bona confessione & cordis contritione, pridie ante festum S. Michaelis, de hoc seculo migravit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1197, the Emperor was taking pleasure in hunting around August in a certain grove where the shade was very cold. During the day the heat was great, but at night there was such frost that the ground was stiffened with ice and hoarfrost. One night, chilled by the cold, he began to fall ill about the feast of St Sixtus. For this reason he ordered himself to be carried to the city of Messina, which was two days' journey from that place. There, suffering from dysentery, and dying in good confession and contrition of heart, he departed from this life on the day before the feast of St Michael.

units.la: Anno domini M.CXCVIII, Philippus dux Sueuiæ, frater Henrici prædicti, apud Franckfurt, ab vna parte principum electus est in regem. Alia autē pars principum filium Henrici, quondam ducis Saxoniæ, nomine Ottonem, qui comes fuit Pictauiæ, regem fecerunt, atq; Coloniæ eum in regem vnxerunt. Audiens autem Philippus regis Ottonis electionem, trecentos milites cum multis aliis scutiferis Aquisgrani misit, vt & regem Ottonem ab ingressu civitatis arcerent, & sibi civitatem & sedem regni seruarent. Sed Otto rex cum suis adiutoribus ipsam civitatem obsedit, & in tempore messis cepit, atq; in sedem regni triduo sedit, ipsamq; civitatem fidelibus suis custodiendam commisit. Interim Philippus exercitum colligens, Alsatiam petiit, omne frumentum in messe pessundedit, Mollesheim expugnado cremauit, solo cœmiterio in deditionem recepto. Haldenburg præsidium cepit, cœmiterium Epiaci confregit, omnesq; homines Argent. episcopi, & comitis de Tagesburg, qui erant assentanei Ottonis regis, & totam inferiorem Alsatiam incendio & rapina vastauit. Inde procedēs, curiam Maguntiæ cum suis fautoribus, in assumptione B. Mariæ habuit, vbi a pluribus principibus solenniter electus, à Treuirensi episcopo, qui iam relicto alio etiam hunc elegerat, vnà cum Taretano archiepiscopo, qui loco Magutinensis archiepiscopi accitus erat, inunctus est. Ad eandem curiam Philippus rex Ottocarum ducem Bohemiæ regem fecit, datis sibi & vxori suæ coronis.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1198, Philip, duke of Swabia and brother of the aforesaid Henry, was elected king at Frankfurt by one party of the princes. The other party, however, made king Otto, son of Henry, formerly duke of Saxony, who had been count of Poitou, and they anointed him king at Cologne. When Philip heard of King Otto's election, he sent three hundred knights with many other shield-bearers to Aachen, to keep King Otto from entering the city and to secure the city and the seat of the kingdom for himself. But King Otto, with his supporters, besieged that city, and took it at harvest time. He sat for three days in the seat of the kingdom, and he entrusted the city to his loyal followers to guard. Meanwhile Philip gathered an army and made for Alsace. He destroyed all the grain at harvest, stormed and burned Mollesheim, and took the cemetery by surrender, leaving only the ground. He captured the garrison at Haldenburg, broke into the cemetery at Epiacum, and laid waste with fire and plunder all the men of the bishop of Strasbourg and of the count of Tagesburg who were supporters of King Otto, and the whole of Lower Alsace. Proceeding from there, he held a court at Mainz with his partisans on the feast of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin. There he was solemnly elected by many princes, and he was anointed by the bishop of Trier, who had already chosen him earlier, along with the archbishop of Tarentaise, who had been summoned in place of the archbishop of Mainz. At the same court King Philip made Ottokar duke of Bohemia king, giving crowns to him and to his wife.

units.la: In ipso tempore Constantia imperatrix in Sicilia defuncta est, & filius Fridericus post multos labores ibidem coepit regnare.
units.tr: At about this time the Empress Constance died in Sicily, and her son Frederick, after many hardships, began to reign there.

units.la: Anno M.CXCIX, rex Philippus iterum collecto exercitu, tempore messis Alsatiam petiit, & omne frumentum pessundedit, aduersas domos in Rubiaco cōfregit: multa præsidia Argent. episcopi & comitis Alberti destruxit, ipsamq; civitatē obsedit. Tandem mediantibus Bertoldo duce de Zeringen, & aliis multis principibus, talis compositio positio pacis inter regem & episcopum Argentinensem facta est: quòd beneficia quæ pater & frater suus ab episcopio tenuerunt, omnimodè libera dimitterent, & episcopus ei ad retinenda regni gubernacula pro posse faueret.
units.tr: In the year 1199, King Philip again gathered an army and, at harvest time, made for Alsace. He destroyed all the grain and broke down the houses opposing him at Rouffach. He demolished many garrisons of the bishop of Strasbourg and of Count Albert, and he besieged that city. At last, through the mediation of Berthold, duke of Zähringen, and many other princes, a settlement of peace was made between the King and the bishop of Strasbourg: that the fiefs which his father and brother had held from the bishopric should be wholly released, and that the bishop should support him, as far as he could, in holding the reins of the kingdom.

units.la: Inde expeditione facta, exercitum versus Aquisgrani movit, atq; Mosellam fluvium transiit: sed inde infecto negotio rediit, obstantibus sibi Ottone rege & fautoribus suis. Habuit præterea magnum conventum principum apud Babenberg, vbi multi episcopi & Saltzburgensis archiepiscopus affuit, vbi ipse cum episcopis ossa S. Henrici & S. Kunegundis leuauerunt, sicut ab Innocentio papa canonizati fuerant, & pluribus miraculis prius coruscauerant.
units.tr: After this campaign, he moved his army towards Aachen and crossed the river Moselle, but he returned from there without accomplishing his business, because King Otto and his supporters opposed him. Moreover, he held a great assembly of princes at Bamberg, where many bishops and the archbishop of Salzburg were present. There he and the bishops raised the bones of St Henry and St Cunegund, who had been canonized by Pope Innocent and had earlier shone forth with many miracles.

units.la: Contigit eo tempore res miranda, & nostris temporibus valde inaudita; apud Rhetiæ Augustam. Nam quædam mulier dum communicare deberet, corpus dominicum in ore reseruauit, quod postea cera circumdedit, & apud se domi retinuit, nescio quid tali machinatione tentatura. Postea poenitentia ducta, ad quendam presbyterum religiosum & bonæ famæ accessit, & ei peccatum suum indicauit: qui nullam ei poenitentiam iniungere voluit, quin prius corpus Domini redderet, quod apud se malè domi habuit. Abiit illa & Dominicum corpus, vt erat in cera, presbytero. Qui assumptis secum multis aliis fidelibus, honorificè illud recepit, & aperiés ceram, inuenit corpus illud Dominicum & panem mysticum in veram carnis sanguinisq; mutatam esse substantiam. Ad cuius rei notitatem non tam de propinquis regionibus, quàm de longinquis partibus terræ multitudo maxima confluit, & multa ibi Dominus miracula in laudem nominis sui operatur.
units.tr: At that time a remarkable thing happened, and one most unheard of in our own days, at Augsburg in Rhaetia. A certain woman, when she ought to have communed, kept the Lord's body in her mouth. Afterwards she covered it with wax and kept it at home, intending to attempt I know not what by such a contrivance. Later, moved by repentance, she went to a certain religious priest of good reputation and disclosed her sin to him. He would impose no penance on her unless she first gave back the body of the Lord, which she had kept badly at home. She went away and gave the Lord's body, still in its wax, to the priest. He, taking with him many other faithful people, received it with honour, and opening the wax, found that the Lord's body and the mystical bread had been changed in substance into true flesh and blood. To learn of this matter, a great crowd gathered not only from nearby regions but from distant parts of the earth, and the Lord worked many miracles there to the praise of his name.

units.la: In eodem anno ante natiuitatem Domini, combustum est monasterium Hohenburg.
units.tr: In the same year, before Christmas, the monastery of Hohenburg was burned down.

units.la: Anno domini M.CC.Otto comes, frater Philippi regis, in bona confessione & longa ægritudine apud Bisuntium defungitur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1200, Count Otto, brother of King Philip, died at Besançon, in good confession and after a long illness.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCI, præclarissimus princeps Philippus rursus exercitum colligens, Mosellam transiuit, Coloniam obsedit, Brunonem episcopum cepit, & sic ciuitatem & totam prouinciam ad deditionem coegit. Postea Aquisgranum veniens cum multis Principibus in sede, vnà cum regina, regni sedit, ac deinde prosperè ad propria rediit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1201, the most distinguished prince Philip again gathered an army, crossed the Moselle, besieged Cologne, captured Bishop Bruno, and so forced the city and the whole province to surrender. Afterwards he came to Aachen, and with many princes sat on the royal throne in the seat of the kingdom together with the queen, and then returned safely to his own lands.

units.la: Anno M.CCII, Cunradus episcopus Argentinensis obiit: cui Henricus de Veringen successit. Hic religiosè cepit viuere, & guerras & prælia declinare.
units.tr: In the year 1202, Conrad, bishop of Strasbourg, died, and Henry of Veringen succeeded him. He began to live a devout life and to avoid wars and battles.

units.la: Ipso tempore cum sedes Moguntinensis esset in errore, vix à domino Apostolico licentiam ordinationis suæ impetrauit. Tandem vt Senonensis archiepiscopus ipsum consecraret, vix obtinuit, anno domini M.CC VII. Qui in Pentecoste in Argentina celebrans ordines, XVI calend. Iulij fere quingentos clericos ordinauit & consecrauit: summa verò sacerdotum CIIII extitit. Ipsa die Christianissimus rex Philippus in vrbe fuit cum principibus suis.
units.tr: At the same time, when the see of Mainz was in schism, he scarcely obtained permission from the lord Apostolic to be ordained. Finally he barely secured that the archbishop of Sens should consecrate him, in the year of the Lord 1207. At Pentecost, celebrating ordinations at Strasbourg, on 16 days before the Kalends of July he ordained and consecrated almost five hundred clerics; the total number of priests was 104. On that very day the most Christian King Philip was in the city with his princes.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCVIII, cùm piissimus rex Philippus in procinctu itineris esset eundi in Saxoniam, vt diutina ibi finem accipere deberet, atque Babenberg venisset, & militum collectionem expectaret, ibiq; venam incidisset, & cum quibusdam regni fidelibus in secreto loco palatij quiesceret: Palatinus de Witelsbach, qui lubricus erat & multorum nobilium homicida, veniens, sicut diu dolum in corde concepe rat, introitum petiit & impetrauit, spatha extracta quasi ioculator ludum simulans, nacta opportunitate regem circa ceruicem percussit, & statim fugere cepit: & de ictu illo vitam finiuit. Corpus eiusdem ibidem humatur, sed postea reuoluto tempore à Friderico rege Spiram ad sepulturam regiam ossa deportantur, ac gloriosè ibi tumulantur. Marschalcus verò de Cathalin illum persequens, apud quandam grangiam sitam apud Danubium occidit, & caput eius in aquam proiecit. Regina verò audita ipsius morte, & sentiens vnicum solatium in eo (quia peregrina erat) perdidisse, & cum esset prægnans, dolorem dolori cumulans, ad Stoup castrum deducta est cum festinatione, vbi post modicum tempus abortum fecit, & sic vitam cum fœtu finiuit, & ad monasterium Lorche deportatur, & ibi gloriosè sepelitur. Paulatim verò longa concertatio de regni electione quieuit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1208, when the most pious King Philip was about to set out on a journey into Saxony, so that a long dispute might come to an end there, he came to Bamberg and waited for the gathering of soldiers. There he had a vein opened, and he rested in a private place in the palace with some faithful men of the kingdom. Then the Count Palatine of Wittelsbach, who was treacherous and a murderer of many nobles, came, as he had long been plotting in his heart. He asked for and obtained entrance. Drawing his sword as if he were a jester playing a game, he seized his opportunity and struck the king on the neck, and at once began to flee; and from that blow the king ended his life. His body was buried there, but later, after time had passed, King Frederick had the bones carried to Speyer, to the royal burial place, and they were gloriously entombed there. Marshal von Kathalin, pursuing him, killed him at a certain farmstead beside the Danube and threw his head into the water. The queen, on hearing of his death, and feeling that she had lost her only comfort in him (because she was a foreigner), and being pregnant, heaping grief upon grief, was hastily taken to the castle of Stoup. There after a short time she miscarried, and so she ended her life together with her child. She was carried to the monastery of Lorsch and honourably buried there. Gradually the long contention over the election of the king subsided.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCIX, Otto rex pro imperiali benedictione tempore messium. Romam proficisci, qui etiam ab Innocentio papa in Imperatorem consecratur, iuramento prius praestito, quòd terram & bona sancti Petri, quae sui antecessores usque ad id temporis contra iustitiam tenuisse videbantur, Romanae ecclesiae libera dimitteret.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1209, King Otto, at harvest time, set out for Rome to receive the imperial blessing. He was also consecrated Emperor by Pope Innocent, but first he swore an oath that he would release to the Roman Church the lands and goods of St Peter, which his predecessors had seemed to hold unjustly up to that time.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCX. Imperator non sano usus consilio rupit foedus iuramenti quod fecerat cum Papa & Romanis, occupando & vendicando sibi bona sancti Petri contra pactum. Unde à Papa saepius admonitus & correptus, desistere contempsit, & ob hoc meritam excommunicationis sententiam incurrit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1210. The Emperor, acting on unsound counsel, broke the covenant of the oath he had made with the Pope and the Romans, seizing and claiming for himself the goods of St Peter contrary to the agreement. Therefore, having been warned and rebuked by the Pope many times, he refused to desist, and on this account he incurred the sentence of excommunication that he deserved.

units.la: Eodem anno Otto Imperator profectus ab Italia transiit in Apuliam, ut terras illas, quas hereditario iure possidebat Fridericus, filius Henrici quondam Imp. sibi subiugaret, ipsumque Fridericum persequi & exterminare intendebat, pravo usus consilio: quia si statim post coronationem repatriasset, omnia in prosperum sibi cessissent.
units.tr: In the same year Emperor Otto set out from Italy and crossed into Apulia, intending to subject to himself those lands which Frederick, son of the late Emperor Henry, held by hereditary right, and he meant to pursue and drive out Frederick himself, acting on a wicked plan: for if he had returned home straight after his coronation, everything would have turned out well for him.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXI, mandante papa per totam Alemanniam promulgari coepit sententia excommunicationis lata in Ottonem. Omni autem tempore Ottonis per totum regnum Alemanniae summa pax & securitas fuit, ita ut omnes mirarentur, quòd etiam in absentia eius, dum esset in Sicilia, tanta pax esse potuit in terra.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1211, at the Pope's command, the sentence of excommunication pronounced against Otto began to be published throughout Germany. But at all times there was the greatest peace and security throughout the kingdom of Germany while Otto was away, so that everyone marvelled that such peace could exist in the land even in his absence, while he was in Sicily.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXII, Otto Imperator ab Apulia & Italia reversus est ad partes Teutoniae, celebrauitque curiam apud Franckenfurt, & circa messes coadunato exercitu, movit expeditionem in Turingiam, adversus Hermannum Lantgravium sibi adversantem: ubi etiam expugnavit & destruxit duas munitiones satis munitas, scilicet Rotenberg & Saltzungen: & inde progrediens, obsedit oppidum Wizense, quod similiter expugnavit usque ad arcem. Ibi tunc primum coepit haberi usus instrumenti bellici, quod vulgo Trybock appellari solet.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1212, Emperor Otto returned from Apulia and Italy to the parts of Germany, and held a court at Frankfurt. Around harvest time, having gathered an army, he launched an expedition into Thuringia against Hermann, the Landgrave, who opposed him. There he also stormed and destroyed two fortresses that were quite strongly fortified, namely Rotenberg and Saltzungen; and advancing from there, he besieged the town of Weissensee, which he likewise took by storm as far as the citadel. There, for the first time, the use of a siege engine, commonly called a trebuchet, began to be employed.

units.la: Ipso tempore facta est nugatoria quaedam expeditio, parvis & stultis hominibus sine aliqua discretione signum crucis arripientibus, curiositatis causa potius quàm salutis. Pergebant autem de utroque sexu pueri & puellae, non solum minores sed adulti etiam, nuptae cum virginibus, euntes vacua crumena, non solum per totam Alemanniam, sed etiam per partes Galliarum & Burgundiae: nec retineri ullo modo poterant à parentibus & amicis, quin totis conatibus iter illud arriperent, in tantum ut passim per villas & agros, relictis instrumentis suis, & his quae tunc praे manibus habebant, transeuntibus se sociabant. Et sicut ad tales novitates saepe & de facili credula turba sumus, multi quidem arbitrati sunt, hoc non de levitate mentis, sed per divinam inspirationem fieri, & ex quadam pietate. Unde & subveniebant eis in expensis, victum & necessaria ministrantes. Clericis autem & quibusdam aliis, quibus erat mens senior, contradicentibus, & iterum illud vanum & inutile iudicantibus, vehementer laici resistebant, dicentes: clericos esse incredulos, ipsosque propter invidiam & auaritiam huic facto se opponere magis, quam propter veritatem & iustitiam. Sed quoniam omne negotium quod sine libramine rationis & sine vigore consilii fuerit inchoatum, non bonum sortitur exitum: postquam haec stolida multitudo pervenit ad partes Italiae, diffusi sunt & dispersi per civitates & oppida, quorum multi ab indigenis terrae detenti sunt in servos & ancillas. Alij dicuntur venisse ad mare, qui seducti à nautis & marinariis, transfuctique ad alias partes terrarum remotas. Reliqui vero pervenientes Romam, cum viderent quòd non poterant habere processum, utpote nulla fulti auctoritate, tandem laborem suum cognouerunt esse friuolum & inanem: & tamen à voto crucis minime fuerunt absoluti, praeter pueros, infra annos discretionis existentes, & eos, quos senium deprimebat. Sic ergo decepti & confusi, redire coeperunt: & qui prius gregatim & per turmas suas, & nunquam sine cantu celeumatis transire solebant per terras, modò singillatim & in silentio, nudipedes & famelici redeuntes, facti sunt omnibus in derisum: quia plurimae virgines raptae sunt, & florem pudicitiae suę amiserunt. Redeamus nunc ad Historiam de Ottone.
units.tr: At the same time a certain frivolous expedition took place, in which small and foolish people, without any discernment, took up the sign of the cross out of curiosity rather than for the sake of salvation. Boys and girls of both sexes went forth, not only the younger ones but adults too, married women along with virgins, setting out with empty purses, not only throughout all Germany but also through parts of France and Burgundy. Neither parents nor friends could hold them back in any way; they were so set on that journey with all their strength that everywhere, through villages and fields, they left behind their tools and whatever they had in hand and joined themselves to those passing by. And since a credulous crowd is often and easily swayed by such novelties, many thought that this was done not from lightness of mind but through divine inspiration and a certain piety. Hence they even helped them with money, supplying food and necessities. But when the clergy and certain others, whose minds were more mature, objected and judged that venture to be vain and useless, the laity resisted vehemently, saying that the clergy were unbelievers and that they opposed this undertaking out of envy and greed rather than out of truth and justice. But since every enterprise begun without the balance of reason and without the strength of counsel does not reach a good end, after this foolish multitude arrived in the parts of Italy, they were scattered and dispersed through cities and towns, and many of them were seized by the native inhabitants and made into male and female slaves. Others are said to have come to the sea, where they were seduced by sailors and seamen and carried across to other remote lands. But the rest, arriving at Rome, when they saw that they could make no progress, being supported by no authority, at last recognised that their labour was frivolous and empty; yet they were by no means released from their vow of the cross, except for the boys who were below the age of discretion, and those whom old age weighed down. So, deceived and confused, they began to return; and those who had formerly been wont to travel through the lands in flocks and troops, never without the singing of a song of praise, now came back one by one and in silence, barefoot and starving, and became a laughing-stock to all: for very many virgins had been ravished and had lost the flower of their chastity. But let us now return to the history of Otto.

units.la: Videns igitur Papa pertinaciam Ottonis, quem prius in omnibus foverat, & in altum sublimauerat, cum neque pro absolutione nec pro compositione aliqua laboraret, misit in Siciliam, & eduxit inde Fridericum, supra praememoratum Henrici quondam Imperatoris filium, & literas suas direxit vniuersis terrae principibus, quibus dedit in mandatis, ut eundem Fridericum loco regis suscipierent & manutenerent, & in omnibus eiustarent, sibiq; transeunti per terras quisq; suo loco conductum honorificè præberent: quod & factum est.
units.tr: The Pope, therefore, seeing the obstinacy of Otto, whom he had previously favoured in everything and raised to a high position, and since Otto was making no effort either for absolution or for any settlement, sent to Sicily and brought out from there Frederick, the son of the late Emperor Henry mentioned above, and he sent his letters to all the princes of the land, in which he gave them instructions that they should receive and uphold the same Frederick in place of the king, and obey him in all things, and that each of them should honourably provide him with safe conduct in his own territory as he passed through the lands. And this was done.

units.la: Competiens ergo Otto Friderici aduentum, desistens ab impugnatione Langrauij, proficiscitur obuiam aduersario. Qui dum in partibus Sueuiæ conuenissent, Otto cum suis cedere compulsus est, & prævalere non potuit: quia pro tenacitate sua multitudem reliquerant. Qui secedens inde reuersus est in Saxoniam, conducentibus cum quibusdam terræ nobilibus. Fridericus autem obsesso & dedito sibi castro Hagenowe, quod adhuc tenebant fideles Ottonis, veniebat de ciuitate in ciuitatem, & receperunt eum, & in breui obtinuit terram. Idem Fridericus iam duxerat vxorem, reginam Arragonum, de qua genuit filium, nomine Heinricum, postea regem.
units.tr: Otto, therefore, learning of Frederick's arrival, gave up the attack on the Landgrave and set out to meet his opponent. When they had come together in the parts of Swabia, Otto was forced to yield with his men and could not prevail, because on account of their own obstinacy they had abandoned the multitude. Withdrawing from there, he returned into Saxony, with some of the noblemen of the land accompanying him. Frederick, however, having besieged and received the surrender of the castle of Hagenau, which the loyal followers of Otto still held, went from city to city, and they received him, and in a short time he gained possession of the land. This same Frederick had already married a wife, the queen of the Aragonese, by whom he had a son named Henry, later king.

units.la: Anno domini M CCXIII, Fridericus curiam Aquisgrani in festo B. Iacobi habuit, vbi de consensu principum locatus est in sedem regni.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1213, Frederick held a court at Aachen on the feast of St James, where, with the consent of the princes, he was installed on the seat of the kingdom.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXV, celebrata est sancta & vniuersalis synodus Romæ, in ecclesia Saluatoris, quæ Constantiniana vocatur, mense Nouembri, præsidente domino Innocentio papa, pontificatus eius anno XVIII, in qua fuerunt episcopi CCCCXV. Inter quos extiterunt de præcipuis Patriarchis duo, videlicet Constantinopolitanus & Ierosolymitanus. Antiochenus autem graui languore detentus, venire non potuit: sed misit pro se vicarium Anteradenum episcopum. Alexandrinus verò sub Sarracenorum dominio constitutus, fecit quod potuit, mittens pro se diaconum germanum suum. Primates autem & metropolitani LXXIIII, cæterum Abbates & Priores vltra DCCC. Procuratorum archiepiscoporum, eporum, abbatum, priorum, capellanorum absentium non fuit numerus comprehensus. Legatorum verò regis Siciliæ, in Romanum Imperatorem electi, Imperatoris Constantinopolitani, regis Franciæ, regis Angliæ, regis Vngariæ, regis Ierosolymitani, regis Cypri, regis Arragonum, nec non aliorum principum ac magnatum, ciuitatum etiam aliorumque locorum, ingens fuit multitudo.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1215, the holy and universal synod was celebrated at Rome, in the church of the Saviour, which is called the Constantinian, in the month of November, with Pope Innocent presiding in the eighteenth year of his pontificate. There were 415 bishops in it. Among them were two of the chief patriarchs, namely those of Constantinople and Jerusalem. The Patriarch of Antioch, however, held back by a grievous illness, could not come, but sent in his place a vicar, Bishop Anteradenus. The Patriarch of Alexandria, being under the rule of the Saracens, did what he could, sending in his place his own brother, a deacon. There were 74 primates and metropolitans, and more than 800 abbots and priors. The number of proxies of absent archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors and chaplains was not counted. The envoys of the king of Sicily, elected as Roman Emperor, of the Emperor of Constantinople, of the king of France, the king of England, the king of Hungary, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Cyprus, the king of the Aragonese, and likewise of other princes and magnates, and of cities and other places, were a huge multitude.

units.la: Ante tempora huius Concilij fere triennio, disponente Deo, hæretici, qui peruerso dogmate latenter seducunt fideles ecclesiæ, comprehensi sunt in ciuitate Argentina. Producti verò cùm negarent hæresin, iudicio ferri candentis ad legitimum termi-num reseruantur, quorum numerus fuit LXXX vel amplius de vtroque sexu, & pauci quidem ex eis innocentes apparuerunt. Reliqui omnes coram ecclesia conuicti, per adustionem manuum damnati sunt, & incendio perierunt.
units.tr: About three years before this council, by God's ordering, heretics, who secretly lead the faithful of the Church astray with a perverse doctrine, were apprehended in the city of Strasbourg. When they were brought forward and denied the heresy, they were reserved for the ordeal of red-hot iron until the appointed day; there were 80 or more of them, of both sexes, and only a few of them appeared innocent. All the rest, convicted in the presence of the Church, were condemned by the burning of their hands and perished in the fire.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXVI, Innocentius papa obiit: cui Honorius successit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1216, Pope Innocent died, and Honorius succeeded him.

units.la: Eodem quoq; tempore Otto Imperator obiit.
units.tr: At the same time Emperor Otto also died.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXIX, Fridericus rex pro imperiali benedictione Romam proficiscitur, vbi ab Honorio papa, circa festum beatæ Ceciliæ, in Imperatorem consecratur & inungitur.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1219, King Frederick set out for Rome to receive the imperial blessing, where, around the feast of St Cecilia, he was consecrated and anointed Emperor by Pope Honorius.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXVII, Henricus filius Imperatoris admodum puer, quasi decennis, per Ottonem Wirzeburgensem episcopum, cuius tutelæ deputatus suerat, à patre de consensu principum in regem electus, copulata sibi vxore filia ducis Austriæ, ex qua duos filios habuit, cum ipso duce & Saltzeburgensi archiepiscopo, & aliis multis principibus gloriosè in sede Aquisgrani est inthronisatus, vnà cum regina. Ipse quoque Imperator Fridericus, mortua vxore sua regina Arragonum, matre prædicti Henrici, postea duxit vxorem filiam regis Ierosolymitani, de qua suscepit filium, nomine Cunradum, postea regem.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1227, Henry, the Emperor's son, while still a boy of about ten years old, was elected king by his father with the consent of the princes; he had been placed in the guardianship of Otto, Bishop of Würzburg, by whom he was installed on the throne at Aachen with great solemnity, together with his queen, the daughter of the Duke of Austria, who was joined to him in marriage, with the duke himself, the Archbishop of Salzburg, and many other princes. By her he had two sons. The Emperor Frederick himself, after his queen, the mother of the aforesaid Henry, the queen of the Aragonese, had died, afterwards married the daughter of the king of Jerusalem, by whom he had a son named Conrad, later king.

units.la: Anno domini M. CCXXXII, de terra Persarum exercitus magnus valde & fortis egressus de finibus suis, per adiacentes sibi prouincias transitum fecit, qui dicebantur fuisse homines magnæ proceritatis & staturæ horribilis: quod tamen non credimus. Sed qua de caussa egressi fuerint, vel quid egerint, ignoramus: in breui reuersi sunt ad propria. Dicebant tamen quidam, quòd versus Coloniam vellent ire, & tres magos de gente eorum natos ibidem accipere. Vnum tamē scimus, quòd Iudæorum gens super eode m rumore ingenti lætitia exultabant, & vehementer sibi applaudebant, nescio quid de futura libertate sua ex hoc peruenire sibi sperâtes: vnde & regem multitudinis illius filium Dauid appellabant.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1232, a great and very strong army came out of the land of the Persians, left its borders, and passed through the neighbouring provinces. They were said to be men of great height and terrifying size, though we do not believe this. Why they set out, or what they did, we do not know; they soon returned home. Some said, however, that they meant to march towards Cologne and take three magi born among their people there. One thing we do know: the Jewish nation exulted greatly over this rumour and loudly congratulated itself, hoping that some kind of freedom would come to it from this, and for that reason they even called the king of that multitude the son of David.

units.la: Anno domini M. C CXXIII, orta est pestilentia maxima pecorum & iumentorum rum, incipiens (vt dicebatur) ab Vngaria & per omnes prouincias interiacentes trāiens, vsq; ad nos, quæ etiam durauit amplius quàm per triennium.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1223, a very great pestilence among the flocks and the draught animals arose, beginning (as it was said) in Hungary and passing through all the provinces in between as far as us. It lasted for more than three years.

units.la: Ipso anno Henricus episcopus Argentinensis obiit: cui Bertoldus successit. Hic cùm esset iuuenis, sano semper vtens consilio, in omnibus agendis suis seniorem se gessit in opere, quantum ad augmentum suæ ecclesiæ: quam suis temporibus plus ditauit, quàm omnes sui antecessores, & quocunque se vertebat prosperis successibus pollebat, & monasteria in suo episcopio sita, satis humanè & sine magno grauamine protexit & fouit, atque suis rebus contentus fuit: & idcirco gloriosum nomen sibi acquisiuit.
units.tr: In the same year Bishop Henry of Strasbourg died, and Bertold succeeded him. Although he was young, and always followed sound counsel, he conducted himself in all his undertakings like an elder in his work, as far as the growth of his church was concerned. In his time he enriched it more than all his predecessors had done, and wherever he turned he prospered with favourable outcomes. He protected and cherished the monasteries situated in his diocese quite humanely and without great burden, and he was content with what was his own. For this reason he won for himself a glorious name.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXVI, fundata est domus apud Argentinam in honore sanctæ Trinitatis, à Wernhero Marschalco, non sine graui impensa Marbacensis.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1226, a house in honour of the Holy Trinity was founded at Strasbourg by Werner the Marshal, not without great expense to the Marbach house.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXVII, Bertoldus Argentinensis episcopus completo fere vno mense in obsidione castri Bernstein, tandem expugnauit & obtinuit illud.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1227, Bertold, bishop of Strasbourg, after almost a full month of siege, finally took the castle of Bernstein and held it.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXVIII, dissensio grauis orta est, inter Bertoldum de Teck Argentinensem episcopum, & cognatos ipsius comites de Pfirt, quæ dum magis ac magis inualesceret, tota fere prouincia usque ad triennium incendiis & rapinis afflicta est penitus & vastata. Igitur episcopus cum multas sustinuisset iniurias sui & suorum, tandem collecto exercitu, ipse & comes Albertus de Habesburg, qui simili modo damnificatus erat in multis, parauerunt se ad resistendum. Nihilominus & Pfirretenses freti auxilio & fauore regalium ciuitatum, & habentes secum in auxilio comitem Egenonem de Friburg, contrahentes magnam copiam armatorum, occurrerunt eis inter Bladoltzheim & Hirtzefeld, & facta congressione, in fugam versi sunt comites de Pfirt & eorum adiutores, relinquentes ibi spolia castrorum plurima in papilionibus, in vestibus, in armatura, in animalibus: quæ omnia sublata sunt à parte aduersa: plures ibi mutilati & vulnerati, plurimi captiuati sunt. Ex hoc autem Pfirretenses & ciuitates regis tantum pudorem & rerum amissionem non ferentes, commoti sunt ira vehementi, cum etiam regis indignatio super hoc accensa fuisset, & augmentato postmodum exercitu, sequenti videlicet anno, villas episcopi plurimas incendio concremantes depopulati sunt.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1228, a serious dispute arose between Bertold of Teck, bishop of Strasbourg, and his kinsmen, the counts of Pfirt. As it grew stronger and stronger, almost the whole province was for nearly three years afflicted and utterly laid waste by fires and plunder. So the bishop, having suffered many injuries to himself and his people, at last gathered an army. He and Count Albert of Habsburg, who had likewise been harmed in many ways, prepared to resist. Nevertheless, the men of Pfirt, relying on the help and favour of the royal cities, and having with them as an ally Count Egeno of Freiburg, raised a large force of armed men and met the others between Bladolsheim and Hirtzfelden. When the battle was joined, the counts of Pfirt and their helpers turned to flight, leaving behind many spoils of their camp: tents, clothing, armour and animals. All of these were seized by the opposing side. Many were maimed and wounded there, and very many were taken captive. The men of Pfirt and the royal cities could not bear such shame and loss, and were stirred to fierce anger. The king's indignation was also kindled over this, and afterwards, with the army increased, namely in the following year, they burned and laid waste many of the bishop's villages.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXIX, prænunciatum est à quodam magistro Toletano, qui dicebatur Andreas, & à quibusdam prædicatum est in tectis, quòd post septem annos venturi essent venti turbinis, tantæ vehementiæ, qui ædificium omne destruant & subuertant, & multas ciuitates terræmotu ruituras, & eclipsin Solis futuram: corruptionem quoque aëris & exinde mortalitatem hominum, & alia quædam inaudita mortalibus. Hoc idem vaticinium plenius scriptum reperies, in his eiusdem Chronicis, si retro perquiras, ante annos ferme quadraginta quatuor.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1229, a certain master of Toledo, who was called Andrew, foretold, and some preached on the roofs, that after seven years there would come winds of a whirlwind of such violence that they would destroy and overthrow every building, and that many cities would fall in an earthquake, and that there would be an eclipse of the sun, as well as corruption of the air and consequently the death of men, and certain other things unheard of among mortals. You will find this same prophecy written out more fully in these same Chronicles, if you look back, nearly forty-four years earlier.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXX, reconciliati sunt rex Henricus & episcopus Argentinensis, & pace reddita siluit & quieuit terra à tumultu bellorum.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1230, King Henry and the bishop of Strasbourg were reconciled, and once peace was restored the land fell silent and rested from the tumult of war.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCXXXI, facta est persecutio contra hæreticos, hostes fidei, veritatis inimicos, quorum multitudo magna latitabat in populo Dei, in ciuitatibus, oppidis, & villis, subuertentes & in errorem mittentes quos poterant de ecclesia.
