units.la: Veniente autem Friderico cū forti exercitu valde, & castrametante iuxta Franckfurt apud Saxenhausen: Petrus Moguntinus naues afferens, victualia iuxta Moguntiā abstulit Friderico. Exercitus autem Moguntini, Treuerensis & Bohemi, se ex inferiori parte Mogani collocauit. Inductus est autem dux Ludouicus Bauariæ iunior, qui & aliàs Friderico præualuit in conflictu, quòd contra eum eligi se permisit: quia in pro- missione facta Friderico, ipse Ludouicus intelligebatur exceptus. Inductus est etiam N. miles Goldemari Brandeburgensis, habens ab eo mandatum sufficiens in genere eligendi, Ludouicum elegit contra domini voluntatem. Electi sunt igitur in discordia, in die beati Lucæ Euangelistæ, anno domini M.CCC.XIIII, Fridericus dux Austriæ, ab archiepiscopo Coloniensi, à Rudolpho Bauaro, Palatino Rheni, & à duce Saxoniæ Ludouicus verò, à Petro Moguntinensi, Balduino Treuerensi archiepiscopis, Woldemaro Marchione, & Ioanne rege Bohemiæ: nec ij principes conuenerant, sed quisq; in suo exercitu, per se vel per procuratorem elegit, & in suis exercitibus publicarunt. Fridericus autem Austrialis præfame recedere est coactus, multiq; dextrarij in ascen- su manserunt in via.
units.tr: Frederick came with a very strong army and encamped near Frankfurt at Sachsenhausen. Peter of Mainz brought ships and carried off the provisions meant for Frederick near Mainz. The armies of Mainz, Trier and Bohemia took up positions on the lower side of the Main. Duke Louis the Younger of Bavaria, who had also prevailed over Frederick in a skirmish, was induced to allow himself to be elected against him, because it was understood that Louis had been excepted in the promise made to Frederick. Also, a certain knight N., a follower of Goldemar of Brandenburg, who had from him a sufficient mandate to elect in general, was induced to elect Louis against his lord's wishes. Thus they were elected in discord, on the feast of St Luke the Evangelist, in the year of the Lord 1314: Frederick, duke of Austria, by the archbishop of Cologne, by Rudolf of Bavaria, Count Palatine of the Rhine, and by the duke of Saxony; and Louis by Peter of Mainz and Baldwin of Trier, archbishops, by Waldemar, margrave, and by John, king of Bohemia. These princes had not met together, but each elected in his own army, either in person or through a proxy, and each published his election in his own army. Frederick of Austria was then forced to withdraw from the aforesaid place, and many of the warhorses remained stuck on the road.

units.la: Ludouicus itaq; Aquisgrani à Moguntino & Treuerensi, in loco quo debuit, sed non à quo debuit: Fridericus verò in Bunna à Coloniense, à quo debuit, sed non in loco in quo debuit, coronati sunt. Adhæserunt autem Ludouico ciuitates inferiores Rheni, vsq; Seltz: Friderico autem, Seltz, & superiores regni ciuitates, exceptis Berna & Solodora, quæ neutrum curabant. Descendit autem Lupoldus dux Austriæ frater Friderici cum grandi exercitu Spirā, contra Ludouicum: vbi Ludouicus ceslit de campo in cœmiterium Iudæorum. Lupoldus autem villas Spirensium & aliorum inibi aduersariorum comburens, ascendit. Trāsiuit post hæc ipse Lupoldus iuxta Augustam, flumen Lech, & in superiori Bauaria multa, & inter alia oppidum Landspeg per se victum, ignis incendio deuastauit.
units.tr: Louis was crowned at Aachen by the archbishop of Mainz and the archbishop of Trier, in a place where he ought to have been crowned, but not by the one who ought to have crowned him. Frederick was crowned at Bonn by the archbishop of Cologne, who ought to have crowned him, but not in the place where he ought to have been crowned. The lower cities of the Rhine as far as Seltz adhered to Louis; the cities of Seltz and the upper parts of the kingdom adhered to Frederick, except Bern and Solothurn, which cared for neither. Leopold, duke of Austria, brother of Frederick, came down with a great army to Speyer against Louis. There Louis withdrew from the field into the Jewish cemetery. Leopold, burning the villages of the Speyerers and of other enemies there, moved on. After this Leopold himself passed by Augsburg, across the river Lech, and in upper Bavaria he laid waste many places, among them the town of Landsberg, which he took by himself, and destroyed it with fire.

units.la: Indicta est autem Basileæ curia in festo Pentecostes solennissima per Australes, vbi inter Fridericum electum & filiam regis Arragonum, & Lupoldum & filiam co- mitis Sabaudiæ, nuptiæ celebrantur. Ibi quot & quanta hastiludia, etiam torniamenta peracta sint, quis enarraret? Vbi comes de Katzenellenbogen, per dictum Grat de Gebwilre militem hastiludio prostratus, cum maxima poenitentia moriens, cum magno fletu mulierum Basilensium, ad Rhenum est deductus. Monstrabantur ibi sanctuariorum insignia, quæ regum dicuntur, scilicet lancea, clauus, pars crucis Saluatoris, corona, gladius Caroli, & alia, per quendam Cisterciensem: & ceecidit machina, præ multitudine hominum, vbi plurimi sunt oppressi. Cecidit & tempore hastiludij alia machina, vbi læsæ sunt plurimæ dominarum, & multa clenodia subtracta. Vbi Ioannes de Clingenberg, præteritis & præsentibus, & postea xxx annis cōtinuatis, valentissimus militum censebatur.
units.tr: The court was announced for the most solemn feast of Pentecost at Basel by the Austrians, where the marriages were celebrated between Frederick the elected king and the daughter of the king of Aragon, and between Leopold and the daughter of the count of Savoy. Who could recount how many and how great the jousts and tournaments were that were held there? There Count Katzenellenbogen, struck down in a joust by a knight named Grat of Gebwilre, died in the deepest repentance and was carried to the Rhine amid the loud weeping of the women of Basel. There the relics of the sanctuaries, which are called royal, were displayed: namely the spear, the nail, a piece of the cross of the Saviour, the crown, the sword of Charles, and others, shown by a certain Cistercian. A scaffold collapsed under the crush of people, and many were crushed there. Another scaffold also fell during the jousting, where many ladies were injured and much jewellery was stolen. There John of Clingenberg was considered the most valiant of knights, both past and present, and for thirty years afterwards.

units.la: Obsedit autem Lupoldus Solodorum, & ad recognoscendum fratrem suum pro rege coegit. Ascenditq; cum magno exercitu versus Suiciam, volens fratri villas illas, quæ sunt de iure Imperij, subiugare. Et cum Ottho comes de Strasberg cum vno exercitu ex parte ducis ingrederetur, per vallem Vnderwalden, artans eam partem, ac declinare volens ad ducem, & ascendente ducis exercitu magno ex alia parte montium: ecce descendit populus Suiciæ cum impetu per cliuum montis quendam, & læsis ibi atq; sine misericordia interfectis melioribus nobilibus, qui præcesserant, ducem cum exercitu suo lamentantem fugauerunt. Et Otto de Strasberg intelligens, per cliuum montis, per quem descenderant pedites, festinanter ascedit: ex quo læsus intrinsecus, postea breuiter est sepultus. Perierunt autem ibi mille quingenti. Sicq; valles illæ post adhuc stant inuictæ.
units.tr: Leopold besieged Solothurn and forced it to acknowledge his brother as king. Then he advanced with a great army towards Switzerland, wishing to subdue those villages which belong to the empire. Count Otto of Strassberg, with one army on the duke's side, was entering through the valley of Vnderwalden, pressing hard on that part and wishing to turn toward the duke, while the duke's great army was climbing on the other side of the mountains. Then the people of Switzerland came down with force by a certain mountain slope, and, wounding and mercilessly killing the foremost and best nobles who had gone ahead, they put the duke and his army to flight, lamenting. Otto of Strassberg, realising that the foot soldiers had come down by that mountain slope, hastened up it; there he was wounded inwardly and was afterwards buried briefly. Some fifteen hundred perished there. And so those valleys still stand unconquered.

units.la: Celebrauit autem Clemens papa quintus post mortem H. Cæsaris concilium Viennæ, reuocans sententiam Imp. contra Robertum regem prolatam: & eidem sancto Imperatori periurium impinxit, multas faciens constitutiones, quas non publicauit, morte praeuentus. Obiit autem Burdegalæ, vbi curiam habuit: cuius thesaurum eius patruus occupauit. Vacauit autem curia plus quàm per annum.
units.tr: After the death of the Emperor Henry, Pope Clement V held a council at Vienne, revoking the sentence the emperor had pronounced against King Robert. He also charged that holy emperor with perjury, and drew up many constitutions, which he did not publish, being overtaken by death. He died at Bordeaux, where he had held his court, and his nephew seized his treasure. The papal see then stood vacant for more than a year.

units.la: Post hæc Cardinales congregati Auinionem, per Robertum regem inclusi, Iacobum episcopum Caturcensem, ipsius regis olim cancellarium, elegerunt in Papam, anno domini M.CCC.XXV, mense Augusto: & vocatus est Ioannes XXII, qui constitutiones Clementis publicauit & sanctum Ludouicum ordinis Minorum, prædicti Roberti fratrem Marsiliæ sepultum, canonizauit: episcopum Caturicensem ex quadam suspicione sortilegij in papam facti, degradatum, excoriari fecit, & in omnibus fauit Roberto.
units.tr: Afterwards the cardinals, gathered at Avignon and held in by King Robert, elected as pope Jacques, bishop of Cahors, formerly chancellor of that same king, in August of the year of the Lord 1325. He was called John XXII. He published Clement's constitutions, and canonised Saint Louis of the Franciscan order, brother of the aforesaid Robert, who was buried at Marseilles. On a certain suspicion of having practised sorcery for the sake of the papacy, he had the former bishop of Cahors degraded and flayed alive, and in all things he favoured Robert.

units.la: Postea Fridericus & Ludouicus electi Romanorum reges cum magnis exercitibus in Sueuia iuxta Eslingen, pro regno quod vtrque habere conabatur, conuenerunt, vbi in fluuio Neccaro non ex proposito, sed casu, adaquantibus equos hincinde abeuntes, & adiuuantibus vtrisque suos paulatim, magna est facta strages vtriusque, multíque nobiles vtriusque capti. Vbi & Wernherus comes de Honberg est captus, Neccarusque sanguineus videbatur, propter occisionem equorum.
units.tr: Afterwards Frederick and Louis, the elected kings of the Romans, met in Swabia near Esslingen with great armies, contending for the kingdom each was trying to obtain. There, in the river Neckar, not by design but by chance, as the horses were drinking and went off hither and thither, and as each side gradually came to the aid of its own men, a great slaughter of both sides took place, and many nobles on both sides were captured. There Count Werner of Honberg was also taken, and the Neckar seemed bloody on account of the slaughter of the horses.

units.la: Indixitque Lupoldus dux curiam in Baden, in terra sua: ad quam quanta multitudo nobilium confluxerit, quantaque hastiludiorum solennia sint peracta, de machinis spectaculorum, de XII candelabris, & candelarum magnitudine & longitudine, quarum vnam vix XII viri portabant, & multis aliis, quis enarrabit? Ibique soror dominorum ducum Austriæ, Ludouico seniori de Oettingen est coniuncta, quæ ante ex sorore comitis de Wirtenberg habuit filium & filiam: qui Ludouicus ante fuit secretarius Ludouici electi, & seruitor: postea eum persequebatur ad vnguem.
units.tr: Duke Leopold then held a court at Baden in his own land. What a great crowd of nobles gathered there, and what splendid jousts were held, the spectacles and machines, the twelve candelabra, and the size and length of the candles, one of which twelve men could hardly carry, and many other things, who could recount? There too the sister of the lords, the Dukes of Austria, was joined in marriage to the elder Louis of Oettingen, who had previously had a son and daughter by a sister of the Count of Württemberg. This Louis had formerly been secretary and servant of Louis the elected king, but afterwards he pursued him in every detail.

units.la: Lupoldus quoque dux iterum cum grandi exercitu versus Spiram descendit, aduersantium villas comburendo, & cùm ascendisset, dimissa gente sua, illico sibi nunciatur, Ludouicum ascendere cum magno equitatu feroci. Ipse Lupoldus dilapsa gente sua, nuncios misit, ad comitem Vdalricum Ferretarum & Ioannem episcopum Argent. repente descendit: qui duo cum suis populis ad Broscam flumen (ab Occidente versus Orientem fluens in Argentinam) se cum magno tremore locarunt. Et venit super Bruscam Ludouicus electus, cum Treuerensi, Bohemo, gente Maguntini, & aliis, cum quatuor millibus galeatorum electis. In nocte autem comes Ferretarum de Brusca versus Mollesheim, præ timore recessit. Mane autem reuersus ad Bruscam, populi, quos aduersarij quodam modo comedissent; illi asserentes, se nolle cum rusticis pugnare, Bruscam iuxta Argentinam transibant, se iuxta Thoreltzheim collocantes, tamdiu cōfligere differendo, quoad Lupoldo gens magna equitum & peditum affluebat. Argentinensium autem pars vna, scilicet Zornonum Friderico: alia vero, scilicet Mulnheimensiū Ludouico fauebat. Et cum Argentini prius Friderico recepissent, nunc in trāsitu Ludouicum multis cū armatis ingredientē & citò egredientē, more regio in maiori ecclesia receperunt, qui & ipse eorum priuilegia confirmauit, anno domini, M.CCCXXX, de mense Augusto.
units.tr: Duke Leopold again came down with a great army towards Speyer, burning the villages of his opponents, and when he had gone up again, having dismissed his men, he was suddenly informed that Louis was advancing with a large and fierce body of cavalry. Leopold himself, his men having dispersed, sent messengers and quickly withdrew to Count Ulrich of Pfirt and John, bishop of Strasbourg. These two, with their people, posted themselves in great fear by the river Bruscha, which flows from west to east into Strasbourg. Louis the elect came upon the Bruscha with the Trier men, the Bohemians, the people of Mainz and others, with four thousand picked men-at-arms. During the night the Count of Pfirt withdrew from the Bruscha towards Mollesheim, out of fear. In the morning, when they returned to the Bruscha, the men who had been, as it were, eaten up by their opponents, declaring that they would not fight with peasants, crossed the Bruscha near Strasbourg, and posted themselves near Thoreltzheim, delaying the battle until a great body of horse and foot had flowed in to Leopold. Part of the Strasbourgers, namely the Zornheimers, favoured Frederick; the other part, namely the Mülnheimers, favoured Louis. And although the Strasbourgers had previously received Frederick, now, when Louis entered with many armed men and left quickly on his way through, they received him royally in the greater church; he too confirmed their privileges in the year of the Lord 1330, in August.

units.la: Fridericus autem cum in Austria de congregatione Ludouici intellexisset, cū paucis spadonibus cursu velocissimo properauit ad Rhenum. Veniensque Rinaugiam, intellecto discrimine fratris, properauit ad ipsum, & appropinquans aciei Ludouici, quā credebat esse Lupoldi, retrocedentes per aliam viam ad aciem Lupoldi venerunt: qui amplectens fratrem præ gaudio, fleuit amarè, dicens: O domine, quàm diu & in quanto periculo me dimisisti? & distabant acies in plano campo ad inuicem, non ad quartam partem miliaris, paratæ ad conflictum. Gens autem Lupoldi abductis equis se parauit ad pugnam, clamatūque fuit sub poena capitis, ne quis calcaria retineret: gaudiique sunt de Friderici aduentu. Dicto autem in acie Ludouici, de aduentu Friderici, missus est miles cum conducto de acie Ludouici ad tentādum, de pugna ad aciem Lupoldi. Pręs tenderant enim inferiores, se nolle confligere cum Lupoldo: quia eo victo, sine negocij quo ad Fridericum non haberent. Adducto autem milite coram Friderico, dixit Fridericus militi: Dicite auunculo meo, me hic ad cōflictum paratum, & tempus esse vt fine nostrę guerræ, imperij fidelibus faciamus. Et cùm iā superiores, in angustia & tremore cōstituti fuissent, eò q; inferiores nobilissimā habētes militiā, euaginatis iā gladiis sc istos seiftos simulauerant inuasuros: ecce reuersi sunt vltra Bruscam, quantocyus poterât descendentes, quos isti per biduum sunt sequuti.
units.tr: When Frederick heard in Austria of Louis's gathering of forces, he hurried to the Rhine with a few attendants at the greatest speed. Arriving at Rheinau, and learning of his brother's peril, he hastened to him; and approaching the line of Louis, which he believed to be Leopold's, they turned back by another road and came to Leopold's line. Leopold, embracing his brother for joy, wept bitterly, saying: "O lord, how long and in what danger have you left me!" The two lines were drawn up for battle on the open plain, not a quarter of a mile apart. Leopold's men led off their horses and prepared for combat, and a proclamation was made under penalty of death that no one should keep spurs on; and they rejoiced at Frederick's arrival. When news of Frederick's arrival had been spoken in Louis's line, a knight with a retinue was sent from Louis's line to test Leopold's line before the battle. For the lower ranks had resolved not to fight with Leopold, since if he were defeated they would have no further business with Frederick. When the knight was brought before Frederick, Frederick said to him: "Tell my uncle that I am here, ready for battle, and that the time has come to end our war and to act for the faithful of the empire." And when the upper ranks, placed in fear and trembling, had been pretending that the lower ranks, who had the noblest knighthood, with swords already drawn, would attack them: behold, they turned back beyond the Bruscha, descending as quickly as they could, and those men followed them for two days.

units.la: Eisdem temporibus, anno M. CCC. XIX, mense Iulio, obijt Woldemarus Marchio Brandenburgensis absq; liberis, Marchionatus dispositione ad Imperium devoluta, fuitq; cum magna lamentatione manifeste sepultus, quem postea ad 28 annos viuere dixerunt. Dequo Marchionatu Ludouicus princeps postea Ludouico, filio suo primogenito, prouidit, de quibus infrà dicetur.
units.tr: In the same times, in the year 1319, in July, Waldemar, Margrave of Brandenburg, died without children; the margraviate, by the arrangement, fell back to the empire. He was buried openly with great lamentation, although they later said he lived on for twenty-eight years. Concerning this margraviate, Prince Louis afterwards provided it for Louis, his firstborn son, as will be said below.

units.la: Eisdem temporibus, Gerhardo de Senar episcopo Constantiensi mortuo, & electis in discordia in Curia Romana litigantibus, H. de Klingenberg praepositio, & H. de Werdenberg canonicis Constantiensibus, ijdemq; per sententiam deberent excludi, & spes esset de Mathia custode Monasterij Morbacensis, ordinis S. Benedicti, Basilien sis dioecesis, fratre Hugonis comitis de Buchegge, seruitoris Roberti regis Siciliae, post exclusionem electorum promouendo: ecce moritur Petrus archiepiscopus Moguntinensis. Quo intellecto in Curia, Ioannes Papa, ad preces praedicti Roberti regis Siciliae, ob seruitia praedicti Hugonis, eidem Mathiae de Buchegge, dilecto etiā ducibus Austriae, de Moguntinensi archiepiscopatu prouidit. Qui descendens primū Spiram, à clero honorificè receptus, cum processione & crucibus venit Moguntiam, honorificè quoq; ibi receptus, qui ipsam ecclesiam quinq; annis potentissimè gubernauit, cuiin magnanimitate & virtutibus similis tunc non est vitus.
units.tr: In the same times, Gerhard of Sennen, bishop of Constance, having died, and the elected men quarrelling in dispute at the Roman court, Hugh of Klingenberg, provost, and Hugh of Werdenberg, canons of Constance, were to be excluded by sentence, and there was hope that Matthias, custodian of the monastery of Murbach of the Benedictine order in the diocese of Basel, brother of Hugh, count of Buchegg, servant of King Robert of Sicily, would be promoted after the exclusion of the electors. Then Peter, archbishop of Mainz, died. When this was known at the court, Pope John, at the request of the said King Robert of Sicily and on account of the services of the said Hugh, provided to the same Matthias of Buchegg, also beloved of the Dukes of Austria, the archbishopric of Mainz. He first came down to Speyer, where he was honourably received by the clergy, and came to Mainz with procession and crosses, where he was also honourably received. He governed that church most powerfully for five years, and in magnanimity and virtues there was none like him at that time.

units.la: Exclusis autem dictis electis, Rudolphus de Montefortí per ipsum Papa ad Constantiensem ecclesiam est promotus, cui etiam vacans monasterium S. Galli committitur. Sed eo tam diu assistente Ludouico, idem monasterium ad preces Hugonis de Buchegge, collocatum est N. de Bonstetten, auunculo Berengarij de Landenberg, qui se fecit extra coemiterium sepeliri.
units.tr: With the said elect set aside, Rudolf of Montfort was promoted by the Pope himself to the church of Constance, and the vacant monastery of St. Gall was committed to him as well. But while Louis still held sway there, the same monastery, at the request of Hugo of Buchegg, was given to N. of Bonstetten, uncle of Berchtold of Landenberg, who had himself buried outside the cemetery.

units.la: Mortuo Basileae illis diebus Vdalrico, vnico comite Ferretarum, absque filijs, & Comitatu pro maiori parte ad ecclesiam Basiliensem devoluto, iamq; in ipsius comitatu populus aduentum Basiliensis episcopi expectaret: ecce Iohanna comitis filia cum dominio traditur duci Alberto: & post multa discrimina, post submersionem Montanam, nuncij plures literas legentes, post expugnationem aliquam castrorum per chabilonem factam, de episcopatu litigante cum commissione Basiliensis, post multos processus, tandem cessit Hartungus dispensatione super beneficijs, & pro receptis obtenta.
units.tr: Udalric, the sole count of Pfirt, died at Basel in those days without sons, and most of his county fell to the Basel church. The people of his county were already awaiting the arrival of the bishop of Basel, when behold, Joanna, the count's daughter, was handed over with her lordship to Duke Albert. After many dangers, after the sinking at Mont..., after several messengers reading letters, after the capture of some castles effected by Chabilon, after a dispute over the bishopric with the commission of Basel, and after many lawsuits, Hartung at last yielded, and was granted a dispensation regarding the benefices, and the receipts were obtained.

units.la: Egressus est autem de Austria sub anno M. CCC. XXI, Fridericus electus cum gente magna in Bauariam, ad quem Lupoldus frater eius cum D CCC galeatis de Sueuia properauit. Ludouicus autem cum exercitu suo, antequam fratres conuenire possent, aciem suam ad inuadendum Fridericum direxit. Lupoldus autem iuxta Monacum Bauariae Iseram transiens, se satis ambiguè committens fortunæ, Ludouici exercitum sequebatur repente. Quod Ludouicus intelligens, recessit de campo, munitionibus se committens. Sicq; Fridericus & Lupoldus conuenientes (quod non posse fieri credebatur) mirabiliter sunt gauisi, terramq; Ludouici superiorem Bauariam decem hebdomadis ignis incendio, omniq; inquietudine vastauerunt.
units.tr: In the year 1321 Frederick, the elect of Austria, set out from Austria into Bavaria with a large force, and his brother Leopold hastened to him from Swabia with 800 mailed horsemen. Louis, however, before the brothers could join forces, directed his battle line to attack Frederick with his army. Leopold, crossing the Isar near Munich in Bavaria and committing himself rather recklessly to fortune, suddenly followed Louis's army. When Louis learned of this, he withdrew from the field and entrusted himself to his fortifications. Thus Frederick and Leopold met (which was believed could not happen), rejoiced greatly, and for ten weeks laid waste Louis's land of Upper Bavaria with fire and every kind of disturbance.

units.la: Post haec miserunt Australes Heinricum fratrem ipsorum cum exercitu, in fauorem Papae Ioannis Brixiam in subsidium partis Gelfae: qui cum inibi aliquandiu stetisset, non multum viriliter agens, concordatus cum Cane Veronensi aduersario, clam comportauerat pro conducto: & simulans se cum exercitu suo quosdam Gibellinos inuasurum, repente recessit, & in Austriam est reuersus.
units.tr: Afterwards the Austrians sent their brother Henry with an army to Brescia, in support of Pope John and in aid of the Guelf party. He stayed there for some time but did not act very manfully. Having come to terms with Can of Verona, the adversary, he had secretly taken pay for it; and pretending that he would attack some Ghibellines with his army, he suddenly withdrew and returned to Austria.

units.la: Ingressi sunt itaq; iterum superiorem Bauariam sub anno Domini M. CCC. XXIII, de mense Septembri, Fridericus & Heinricus Australes, cum duobus millibus & ducentis galeatis, & quatuor milibus Hungarorum & gentilium sagittariorum, missis sibi a rege Hungariae, & de Sueuia Lupoldus frater eorum cum D CCC galeatis electis. Tardante autem se Lupoldo in vastatione terrae Wilhelmi comitis de Môteforti, qui tunc Ludouico adhaesit, cui aderant Ioannes rex Bohemiae & Balduinus archiepiscopus Treuerensis cum exercitu suo, scilicet mille D galeatis, & cum XXXX M peditum ad Friderici exercitum declinauit, vexillum conflictus committens comiti de Schlüsselberg. Ipse autem inet Ludouicus duodecimus in armis blaueis, cum albis crucibus, ne cognosceretur, absq; signis regijs apparebat. Non enim dubitauit, se si vince-retur, occidi. Aderant etiam sibi Ludouicus Burggrauius de Nurnberg, duo de Oettingen, Wilhelmus de Monteforti, multiq; Comites & Barones. Cumq; venissent ad flumen paruum, quod eorum exercitus diuidebat, sagittarij Austral is ipsum adeo infestabant, quod ad castrum suum vicinum situm super ipso flumine, scilicet Wasser-burg, declinauit, mane transeuntes ibidem. Intellecto autem quod Bauari transiuissent, & consulentibus pluribus quod Fridericus paulatim discederet versus iter Lupoldi declinando: ipse Fridericus animosus nimis, omnino se disposuit ad conflictum in armis regijs contra suorum consilium procedendo, & praemisit aciem quingentorum galeatorum, quam sequebantur cum vexillo acies octingentorum galeatorum. Postremò ipse in acie octingentorum processit, & progredientibus ad conflictum, fractoq; vexillo Bauari, acriterq; certantibus Austral ibus, & praesertim Friderico manu sua, qui valentior in pugna reputatus est inter omnes, cedenteq; acie Bauarorum, itaquod Austral is vicisse credebatur omnino: ecce equites Bauari reuocantes pedestres qui cesserat; ac se terrae committentes, cum illis reuersi sunt ad conflictum. Post haec venit Burggrauius de Nurenberg cum acie equitum, cum clamore: & fugientibus sagittarijs Austral ibus, multisq; cum illis, captoq; Heinrico Austral i, ac deiecto Austral ium vexillo, eisq; pro maiori parte terga vertentibus, & valentioribus captis, tandem armiger quida Fridericum desolatum a suis, equo etiam eius perforato, eoq; se demittente ad terram, capere volens, nec eum cognoscens, quaesitus fuit ab illo, cuius esset seruitor. Quo respondente, quod Burggrauij: Fridericus fecit Burggrauium aduocari, cui gladium porrexit, & eius gratiae se commisit, qui cum certificatus de vita, Bauaro praesentauit. Salutante autem eum Bauaro, & dicente: Auuncule, libenter videmus vos. Ille autem consternatus animo, non respondit. Licet autem multi consuluerint, quod in signum victoriae per noctem in campo manerent: Ludouicus tamen timens aciem Lupoldi recessit. Lupoldus hoc intelligens, dolenter recessit, miratus, quod rex Romanorum in discordia captus, non esset occisus. Et factus est conflictus in die sancti Michaelis, quo quinquaginta anni fuerant, quod auus amborum, Rudolphus de Habspurg, in regem electus est Romanorum, & postea Australes in potentia decreuerunt.
units.tr: In September of the year of the Lord 1323 Frederick and Henry of Austria entered Upper Bavaria again, with 1,200 mailed horsemen and four thousand Hungarian and Gentile archers sent to them by the king of Hungary, while from Swabia their brother Leopold came with 800 picked mailed horsemen. But Leopold delayed in ravaging the land of Count Wilhelm of Montfort, who then adhered to Louis, and to whom John, king of Bohemia, and Baldwin, archbishop of Trier, were present with their army, namely 1,500 mailed horsemen and 40,000 foot soldiers. Leopold turned to the army of Frederick, entrusting the standard of battle to the count of Schlüsselberg. Louis himself, the twelfth in armour of blue with white crosses so that he would not be recognised, appeared without royal insignia; for he did not doubt that he would be killed if he were defeated. With him were also Louis, burgrave of Nuremberg, the two of Oettingen, Wilhelm of Montfort, and many counts and barons. When they came to a small river that divided their armies, the Austrian archers harassed it so much that Louis turned aside to his nearby castle Wasserburg, situated on that same river, and they crossed there in the morning. When it was learned that the Bavarians had crossed, and many advised that Frederick should gradually withdraw, moving aside towards Leopold's route, Frederick, too spirited, resolved entirely to engage in battle with the royal arms, acting against the advice of his men. He sent ahead a line of 500 mailed horsemen, followed by a line of 800 mailed horsemen under the standard. Finally he himself advanced with the line of 800. As they moved into the fight, the Bavarian standard was broken, and the Austrians fought fiercely, especially Frederick himself with his own hand, who was reckoned the strongest in battle among all; the Bavarian line gave way, so that the Austrians were fully believed to have won. Then the Bavarian horsemen recalled the foot soldiers who had retreated, and turning back with them they returned to the fight. After this came the burgrave of Nuremberg with a line of horsemen, shouting; the Austrian archers fled, and many with them. Henry of Austria was captured, the Austrian standard was thrown down, and most of them turned their backs, and the stronger men were taken. At last a certain squire, seeking to capture Frederick, who was abandoned by his men and whose horse had been pierced so that it was sinking to the ground, did not recognise him and asked whose servant he was. When he answered that he belonged to the burgrave, Frederick had the burgrave summoned, handed over his sword, and committed himself to his mercy. When he had been assured of his life, the burgrave presented him to the Bavarian. As the Bavarian greeted him and said, "Uncle, we are glad to see you," he, dismayed in spirit, made no reply. Although many advised remaining on the field through the night as a sign of victory, Louis, fearing the line of Leopold, withdrew. Leopold, learning this, withdrew sorrowfully, wondering that the king of the Romans, captured in the battle, had not been killed. The battle took place on the feast of St. Michael, fifty years after the grandfather of both, Rudolf of Habsburg, had been elected king of the Romans, and afterwards the Austrians decided on a policy of power.

units.la: Habuit autem Ludouicus quendam Martinum monachum deuotum & humilem, postea facto sacerdotem, qui sibi multa futura praedixit. Hic ante medium annum, Fridericum ante diem Michaelis finitum captiuandum praedixit, curiam suam in valore centum marcarum cuidam de Monaco, pacisceni in contrarium, ad certa summam pecuniae obligans super eo: & in die sancti Michaelis, alter, inuito Martino, & continuò dicente, Vos aliud audietis, curiam per iudicium occupauit: quae sibi, comperta veritate, est restituta: ipsoq; Martinus pecuniam acquisitam iussus est recipere.
units.tr: Louis had a certain Martin, a devout and humble monk who was afterwards made a priest, who predicted many future things to him. This man foretold, before the middle of the year, that Frederick would be taken captive before the end of the feast of St. Michael. He bound his own court, valued at a hundred marks, to a certain man of Munich by a set sum of money, agreeing to the contrary on this matter. On the feast of St. Michael, another man, against Martin's wishes, and Martin constantly saying, "You will hear otherwise," seized the court by judgment. When the truth was discovered, it was restored to him, and Martin was ordered to receive the money that had been acquired.

units.la: Heinricus quoq; Austral is captus regis Bohemiae, restitutis ipsi regi quibusdam munitionibus Morauiae, quas Australes occupauerant, liberatur: Fridericus vero in castro Traufsnit Ludouici fortissimo detinetur, multiq; Austral ium, praesertim de Walsee, dure tenti in magnis sunt pecunijs talliati.
units.tr: Henry of Austria, too, was captured by the king of Bohemia and was released after returning to the king certain fortifications of Moravia that the Austrians had occupied. But Frederick was held in the castle of Trausnitz, the strongest of Louis's fortresses, and many Austrians, especially of Walsee, were held harshly and assessed heavy sums of money.

units.la: Ciuitates autem Elsatiae, Columbaria, Schletstat, Ehenheim, Rosheim, Hagenoue, quae Friderico adhaeserat, territq; Albertum Humelionem de Liechtenberg militem Sueuum, in aduocatum Ludouici nomine receperunt. Ioannes quoq; episcopus Argentinensis conuenit cum eis, de non assistendo alicui eorunde. Marchiones vero de Baden perseuerantes in Lupoldo, oppidu Seltz Imperiale eis obligatum per Fridericum, ingressi, infestationes plurimas patiebantur. Lupoldus autem veniens Basileam, militiam conuocauit. Congregati vero sunt nobiles vtriusq; sexus, qui Lupoldum chorisare & iocundari quantum poterant compulerunt: at ille fecit omnia absq; risu. Misit autem l galeatos in Ensisheim, qui Columbarienses cum inquietudine infestarent, quos post haec in Seltz destinauit: qui ciuitates & Bauaros spolijs & incendijs infestantes, inibi potenter sunt obsessi. Lupoldus autem gentem in nauibus traducens, quamuis respectu obsidetium minima, liberauit obsessos, & contra suorum consilium, suadentium cum tutius vltra Rhenum reuerti, per Elsatiam est reuersus, vndiq; cum incendio praetereundo. Argutus autem ab Argentinensib. damnificatis per incendia, male malè in seaſtum eſſe, & ob hoc ſe huiuſmodi incendia non obmiſſurum reſpondit. Verecundantes autem Bauari, quòd ob tam paucam gentem recedeſſerant de obsidio-ne,ſcripserunt Lupoldo: qui iam verſus Apri- Monaste rium aſcenderat, ſe cum eo,ſi eos expeſtaret per biduum, pugnaturos: quos cum biduo expeſtaſſet, aſcendit.
units.tr: The cities of Alsace, Colmar, Schlettstadt, Ehnheim, Rosheim, and Hagenau, which had adhered to Frederick, received as their advocate in Louis's name Albert Humel of Liechtenberg, a Swabian knight, who had frightened them. John, bishop of Strasbourg, also came to an agreement with them not to support any of them. The margraves of Baden, however, persisting in support of Leopold, entered the imperial town of Seltz, which Frederick had pledged to them, and suffered many attacks. Leopold, coming to Basel, summoned the militia. Nobles of both sexes assembled, and they compelled Leopold to dance and make merry as much as they could, but he did everything without laughter. He sent 50 mailed horsemen into Ensisheim to harass the Colmarians with disturbances, whom he afterwards sent to Seltz; these men, attacking the cities and the Bavarians with plunder and burnings, were powerfully besieged there. Leopold, however, transported his people by boat, though the besiegers were very few in comparison, freed the besieged, and against the advice of his men, who urged him to return beyond the Rhine more safely, he went back through Alsace, burning everything along the way. When the Strasbourgers, who had suffered damage from the fires, reproached him that things were going badly for them, he answered that he would not leave off such burnings. The Bavarians, ashamed that they had withdrawn from the siege for so small a force, wrote to Leopold that they would fight with him if he would wait for them for two days. When he had waited two days for them, he moved on towards Apri-Monasterium.

units.la: Post haec Eberhardus de Wirtenberg, caſtrum Richenberg, quod Marchiones de Baden tenebant, potenter obsedit. Matthias Maguntinus cum magna gente ſubuenit eiſdem.
units.tr: After this, Eberhard of Württemberg laid a powerful siege to the castle of Richenberg, which the Margraves of Baden held. Matthias of Mainz came to their relief with a large force.

units.la: Inuenit autem Lupoldus tunc temporis expertum nigromanticum, cum quo de eductione Friderici tractauit. Confidentibus autem ipsis duobus solis in camera bene firmata, Lupoldo, & magistro faciente characteres suos: ecce venit daemon stans coram eis, in specie viatoris, habentis calceos corruptos, & pileum in capite, oculosque lippos. Cui Lupoldus ait, Noftis me? at ille ait: Bene nosco te, & quaesitis aliquibus, iniunctoq; sibi, quòd absq; omni periculo deduceret Fridericum à captiuitate: Daemone respondente, quòd sic eum educeret, dummodo ei consentiret, nimis territus est Lupoldus. Daemonq; veniens ad castrum Trauf znit in specie scholaris cuiusdam, in partibus Ergouiae, habentis pannum circumuolutum per collum, ac si in eo panes portare vellet, dixitq; Friderico: Ingredere hunc pannum, & ducam te ad tuum fratrem Lupoldum. Quo respondente, quis esset? & illo dicente, Non cura, si ingrederis, securè te ducam: Fridericus facto crucis signo, & inuocato Christi nomine, demonem profugauit, dicens custodibus suis, quòd per aliquas reliquias vel preces à daemone se custodirent, quod & factum est diligenter. Qui postea liberatus, videns scholarem dixit: Hic fuit daemon, qui voluit me eduxisse.
units.tr: At that time Leopold found a practised necromancer, with whom he discussed the release of Frederick. The two of them were alone in a well-fortified room, and the magician was drawing his characters while Leopold waited. Suddenly a demon appeared before them in the likeness of a traveller, with worn-out shoes, a cap on his head and bleary eyes. Leopold said to him, "Do you know me?" He replied, "I know you well." After some questions, and after he had been given his instructions, that he would lead Frederick out of captivity without any danger, the demon said he would bring him out, provided Leopold consented to the terms. Leopold was greatly alarmed. The demon came to the castle of Trauf in the likeness of a certain schoolboy from the parts of Argau, with a cloth wrapped about his neck, as if he meant to carry bread in it. He said to Frederick, "Get into this cloth, and I will lead you to your brother Leopold." When Frederick asked who he was, the demon said, "Never mind. If you get in, I will lead you safely." Frederick made the sign of the cross and, calling on the name of Christ, drove the demon off. He told his guards to guard themselves against the demon with some relics or prayers, and they did so carefully. Afterwards, when he was freed and saw the schoolboy, he said, "This was the demon who wanted to lead me away."

units.la: Eo tempore mortuo Matthaeo Mediolanensium domino, relictis Galeatio, Ioanne, Marco, Luca, & Stephano filijs, & Galeatio seniore dominium occupante, cum Papae Ioannis mandatis pluribus paruisset, tandem eo non desistente, parere contempsit: qui citatus personaliter, etiam de articulis fidei responsurus, non comparens, excommunicatus, post annum de haeresi est damnatus. Hic à Ludouico electo Romanorum rege, cùm Fridericum cepisset, regimen Mediolanense assumpsit. Conglutinatis autem Papa, Franco & Lupoldo: Papa Ludouicum super eo, quòd nondum approbatus per sedem apostolicam, iura Imperij administraret, & Galeatium haereticum foueret, Auinionem citauit, & non comparentem excommunicauit, & post annum similiter de haeresi condemnauit (contra quos tamen processus Ludouicus electus ex quibusdam causis rationabilibus appellauit, ipsamq; appellatione eidem Papae intimauit) priuationis iuris electionis, ducatus sui & dominiorum, & aliis pluribus in eum, & filios, & fautores eius, successiue sententijs promulgatis: quas Lupoldus vndiq; vbi potuit in odium Ludouici procurauerat promulgari.
units.tr: At that time Matthew, lord of the Milanese, died, leaving sons Galeazzo, John, Mark, Luke and Stephen. Galeazzo the elder seized the lordship. He had obeyed several commands of Pope John, but when the Pope persisted, he refused to obey further. Summoned in person, and to answer also on the articles of faith, he did not appear, and was excommunicated; a year later he was condemned for heresy. When Ludwig, elected king of the Romans, had captured Frederick, he took over the government of Milan from Galeazzo. The Pope, Francis and Leopold formed an alliance. The Pope summoned Ludwig to Avignon, because he, though not yet approved by the apostolic see, was administering the rights of the Empire and supporting Galeazzo the heretic. When Ludwig did not appear, he excommunicated him, and a year later likewise condemned him for heresy. (Ludwig, though, appealed against these proceedings for certain reasonable causes, and notified the Pope of the appeal.) Then successive sentences were issued against him and his sons and supporters: deprivation of his right of election, of his duchy and of his lordships, and many others. Leopold, wherever he could, had these sentences published everywhere to bring Ludwig into hatred.

units.la: Conuenerant autem Francus & Lupoldus in Bare, vbi multa, & praesertim contra Ludouicum tractauerunt, papa eis annuente. Conuenerunt & principes ecclesiastici, nuncij Papae & Franci, ac Lupoldus in Rens, prope Confluentiam, ac soli ducti super Rhenum in naui, diu tractauerunt de Franco in Imperatorem promouendo. Sed per fratrem Berchtoldum de Buchec, Commendatorem domus Teutonicorum in Confluentia, fratrem domini Matthiae Moguntinensis archiepiscopi principaliter extitit impeditu: de quo eum secretarijs Papae Ioan. decanus Moguntinensis detulit, quod ipsum post mortem Matthiae Maguntini, ab ipsius fratris Berchtoldi prouisione retraxit. Reuersae sunt autem praedictae ciuitates Alsatiae à Ludouico ad Lupoldū, nomine fratris sui Friderici captiui, & creuit potentia Lupoldi. Qui aliquoties scribens Franco vel Papae, tali titulo utebatur: LVPOLDVS Dei gratia, Austriae, Styriae, Carinthiae & Moraviae dux: dominus Carniolae & portus Naonis, Comes in Habspurg & in Kiburg, ac Lantgraujus superioris Alsatiae.
units.tr: Francis and Leopold met at Baar, where they discussed many things, especially against Ludwig, with the Pope's consent. Ecclesiastical princes, the Pope's envoys, Francis and Leopold also met at Rhens, near Koblenz, and they were alone, carried out on the Rhine in a boat, where they long discussed raising Francis to the Emperor's dignity. But the plan was chiefly hindered by Brother Berthold of Buchegg, commander of the house of the Teutonic Knights at Koblenz, brother of the lord Matthew, archbishop of Mainz. John, dean of Mainz, reported this to the Pope's secretaries, that after Matthew's death, he withdrew it from the provision of his brother Berthold. The aforesaid cities of Alsace were returned by Ludwig to Leopold, in the name of his captive brother Frederick, and Leopold's power grew. Writing several times to Francis or to the Pope, he used this title: "LEOPOLD, by the grace of God, duke of Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Moravia; lord of Carniola and of the port of Nauen; count of Habsburg and Kyburg, and landgrave of Upper Alsace."

units.la: Obsedit autem eo tempore Ludouicus oppidum Burggowe, ducis Lupoldi, tempore hyemali, quo Dux in illa parte eum impedire posse nullatenus credebatur. Scripsit autem dux Burchardo de Ellerbach, ministro suo, quòd se viriliter teneret, quia eū infra dies xiiii liberaret, & repente veniens cum gente forti, cum illis ignorantibus appropinquaret, Ludouicus tardè intelligens, dimissis ex prato, ne eum insequeretur Burchardus, machinis & castris euasit. Tractabatur autem sæpe de liberatione Friderici: & impediente liberatione eius, quòd Dux insignia sanctuariorum Imperij, lanceâ videlicet & alia, noluit resignare. Dicentibusq; suis, quòd frater suus esset eius captiuus: Dux prænoscēs astutiam Ludouici, dixit tractatoribus: Ecce ne hoc mihi impingatur à vobis, dabo vobis ea insignia, & scio quòd nec adhuc prout tractastis compositionem, fratrem meum rehabebo. Quod etiam cum factum esset, Lupoldus Ludouicum adeò infestauit: quòd tandem Ludouicus cum Friderico, communicate eos ambos post Missam vno Cartusiensi, eorum confessore, & seruare pacta iurantibus, latenter conuenit. Emisso autem Friderico, & seruante pacta, Lupoldus vsq; ad mortem suam restitit Ludouico.
units.tr: At that time Ludwig besieged the town of Burgau, belonging to Duke Leopold, in the winter season, when it was in no way believed that the duke could prevent him in that region. The duke wrote to Burkhard of Ellerbach, his minister, that he should hold out bravely, because within fourteen days he would relieve him. Suddenly he came with a strong force and drew near while they were unaware. Ludwig, understanding too late, let go the meadow lest Burkhard pursue him, and escaped with his siege engines and camp. The release of Frederick was often discussed, but his release was hindered because the duke refused to give up the insignia of the sacred relics of the Empire, namely the lance and the rest. His followers said that his brother was Ludwig's captive. The duke, knowing Ludwig's cunning, said to the negotiators: "Lest this be laid to my charge by you, I will give you those insignia, and I know that you have not yet agreed to a settlement as you proposed, but I will get my brother back." When this had been done, Leopold harassed Ludwig so severely that at last Ludwig secretly met with Frederick. They both took communion after Mass from one Carthusian, their confessor, and they swore to keep the agreement. When Frederick was released and kept the agreement, Leopold resisted Ludwig until his death.

units.la: Obsedit autem Lupoldus oppidum S. Hippolyti, Lantgrauij Elsatiæ, seruitoris Ludouici, qui ipsi Lupoldo, sæpe Veneris causa Argentinam eunti, dicebatur insidias posuisse. Ipse Lupoldus muros destruens funditùs, villam tenebat. Quamuis autem medici sibi prædixerint, quòd eum labores necarent, non destitit ab expeditione, sed cum exercitu descendens Spiram obsedit. Spira reuersus, Argentinæ in curia dominorum de Ochsenstein decumbens & insaniens, absq; pœnitentia diem clausit extremum.
units.tr: Leopold besieged the town of St Hippolyte, belonging to the landgrave of Alsace, a servant of Ludwig, who was said to have laid ambushes for Leopold himself, often when he went to Strasbourg for the sake of pleasure. Leopold himself, utterly destroying its walls, held the village. Although his physicians had warned him that his labours would kill him, he did not desist from the expedition, but going down with his army he besieged Speyer. Returning from Speyer, he lay sick and raving at Strasbourg, in the court of the lords of Ochsenstein, and closed his last day without repentance.

units.la: Iuerat autem illis diebus Ludouicus in Lombardiam, quem Galeatius dominus Mediolanensis sumptuosè deduxit, quem tamen post magnam sibi datâ pecuniam, Romam quasi captiuatum traduxit, Wilhelmo de Monte forti Mediolanum committens: quòd non Imperij, sed facta sua agens, & pecuniam ad partes transmittens, Imperium negligebat: propter quod, quamuis æstimaretur in virilibus gestis valentior huius mundi, non tamen exitit ibi nimiùm commendatus.
units.tr: Meanwhile Ludwig had gone into Lombardy, where Galeazzo, lord of Milan, escorted him sumptuously. Yet after a large sum of money had been given to him, Galeazzo led him to Rome as if he were a captive, leaving William de Montfort in charge at Milan. Ludwig, not acting for the Empire but for his own affairs, and sending money to his own lands, neglected the Empire. For this reason, although he was thought the most valiant man of this world in manly deeds, he did not become very highly regarded there.

units.la: Fuit autem Ludouicus Mediolani in ecclesia S. Ambrosij, à Ioanne archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, in festo Pentecostes, cum Margareta vxore sua, anno regni sui xiii, corona ferrea coronatus: & post hæc Romam veniēs à Romano clero & populo gaudenter & counter est receptus, ac xvii die Ianuarij, qua cantatur, Omnis terra, anno regni sui xiiii, ex parte totius Romani populi, per Senatores, præfectum vrbis & cancellarium populi Romani, omnibus nobilibus acclamantibus, in ecclesia S. Petri, cum ipsa coniuge, Imperiali exitit diademate insignitus. Prætenderant enim vrbici, hoc eis competere, Papa etiam nolente: præsertim cùm Senatores priùs Papâ requisierant, vt ad vrbem se transferret. Ludouicus etiam Ioanni Papæ pro tunc crimen lesæ maiestatis & hæresim impingebat.
units.tr: Ludwig was crowned at Milan with the iron crown in the church of St Ambrose, by John, archbishop of Milan, on the feast of Pentecost, with his wife Margaret, in the thirteenth year of his reign. After this he came to Rome and was received joyfully and with applause by the Roman clergy and people. On 17 January, the day on which the introit Omnis terra is sung, in the fourteenth year of his reign, on behalf of the whole Roman people, through the senators, the prefect of the city and the chancellor of the Roman people, with all the nobles acclaiming, he was invested with the imperial diadem in the church of St Peter, together with his wife. For the citizens of the city claimed that this belonged to them, even though the Pope was unwilling; especially since the senators had earlier asked the Pope to transfer himself to the city. Ludwig at that time also charged Pope John with the crime of treason and heresy.

units.la: Post hæc Petrum de Corbario fratrem Minorem in summum Pontificem, quantum in eis est, creauerunt, & ob hoc multis creatis Cardinalibus & Episcopis, per illos magnum in ecclesia Dei scandalum est subortum.
units.tr: After this they created Peter of Corvara, a Minorite friar, as supreme pontiff, as far as lay in them. For this reason, many cardinals and bishops having been created, a great scandal arose in the Church of God.

units.la: Ipse autem Ludouicus habitis tractatibus cum rege Siciliæ, terram Roberti regis, sc. Apuliam, ingredi intendebat. Robertus quoq; collectis omnibus terram illâ relinquere, si Cæsar acceleraret, & in Prouinciam intenderat se transferre. At ipse Cæsar segnis tanto tempore, stetit otiosus in vrbe, quòd quasi omnia expendebat. Quadam autem vice veniēs idem Princeps in vrbe ad castellum, in quo olim Conradinus decebatur decapitatus, ipsum funditùs demoliuit.
units.tr: Ludwig himself, after negotiations with the king of Sicily, intended to enter the land of King Robert, that is, Apulia. Robert, too, had gathered all his forces and had planned to withdraw from that land and transfer himself into Provence, if the Emperor should hasten. But the Emperor was so slow, and stayed idle in the city for so long, that he spent almost everything. On one occasion the same prince, coming in the city to the castle where Conradin was once said to have been beheaded, utterly demolished it.

units.la: Mortuis autem inclytis principibus Lupoldo, Henrico & tandem Friderico ducibus Austrialibus, & in Rüningefelt monasterio, vbi pater eorum Albertus rex fuit, sepultis: Ludouicus in Alemanniam est reuersus. Dicebatur autem tunc temporis, quòd quidam miles Friderico quiddam ad comedendum dederit, per quod eum in sui fauorem inclinaret, per quod à pediculis mundari non valens, paulatim defecit. Et hi omnes quanquam valentissimi fuerunt, sine masculis filijs sunt defuncti.
units.tr: When the illustrious princes Leopold, Henry and finally Frederick, dukes of Austria, had died and been buried in the monastery of Königsfelden, where their father, King Albert, had been, Ludwig returned to Germany. It was said at that time that a certain knight gave Frederick something to eat, by which he might win him over to his side. Unable to be cleansed of lice by it, he gradually wasted away. All these men, although they were most powerful, died without sons.

units.la: Ludouico autem egrediente de vrbe, cum Wilhelmo de Monteforti, Azzonem filium Galeatij, secum in Lombardia regnare permiserat, post eorū egressum quicquid potuit occupauit, & nil in partibus illis remansit.
units.tr: When Louis was leaving the city, together with William of Montfort, he had allowed Azzo, son of Galeazzo, to rule with him in Lombardy. After their departure, Azzo seized whatever he could, and nothing remained in those parts.

units.la: In diebus illis post egressum Ludouici Principis de Italia, viuente Ioanne Papa, Ioannes rex Bohemiæ cum consensu Principis ingressus est Italiam, & diu inibi manēs, Lucanam ciuitatem pro se tenens, quæ cum pro domino recepit: non more patris sui quondam Henrici de Lutzelburg Imperatoris. Qui inibi viriliter se tenuit, & constanter se tenens, ac se successorem Imperatoris & pacificatorem Italiæ scribens, Papæ & Imperatori complacere cupiens, & ambobus displicens, obligata Luca cum verecunrecundia reuersus est, nulla sibi vel Principi in Italia parte relicta.
units.tr: In those days, after Prince Louis had left Italy, while Pope John was still living, King John of Bohemia entered Italy with the consent of the Prince. He stayed there a long time, holding the city of Lucca for himself, which he received as its lord, not in the manner of his father, the late Emperor Henry of Luxembourg. He held himself there manfully and firmly, and wrote himself the successor of the Emperor and the pacifier of Italy. Wishing to please both the Pope and the Emperor, he displeased them both. He returned home in disgrace, having pawned Lucca, and with nothing left to him or to the Prince in any part of Italy.

units.la: Erat autem in diebus illis Bononiæ legatus Papæ, Bertrandus de Pogeto, Hostiensis episcopus, dominium ciuitatis durè tenens, crudeliter multis occisis: qui Bononiam muro circundans, & sibi fortissimum castrum inibi construens, multaq; mala peragens, cui quamuis Guelfissimo ipse rex Bohemiæ familiaris extitit: tandem per rumorem populi victo repente castro & funditus demolito, turpiter est fugatus.
units.tr: At that time Bertrand de Pouget, bishop of Ostia, was the Pope's legate at Bologna. He held the lordship of the city harshly and killed many people cruelly. He surrounded Bologna with a wall, built a very strong castle there for himself, and committed many evils. Although King John of Bohemia was very familiar with him, and he was most devoted to the Guelf cause, he was at last, when the people rose up, suddenly overcome: the castle was razed to the ground, and he was shamefully put to flight.

units.la: Habuit autem rex Bohemiæ duos filios, quorum maior Carolus nomine, qui marchio Moraviæ nominabatur, habuit sororem Philippi regis Franciæ in uxorem. Minor verò habuit filiam M. ducis Carinthiæ. Habuit & duas filias, quarum unam habuit Ioannes primogenitus regis Franciæ: aliam Henricus dux Bavariæ. Et ecce mortuo duce Carinthiæ sine filio, sola ipsius regis Bohemiæ nuru relicta, cùm ipse rex sine omni briga crederet in ipso ducatu filium successurum: Ludouicus princeps de ipso ducatu duces Austriæ, filios sororis ipsius, quondam ducis Carinthiæ, inuestiuit: filio autem regis Bohemiæ comitatus Tirolis remansit. Ex quo ipse rex contra principem mouebatur odio capitali: iuramento affirmans publicè, se nunquam reformaturum eidem: Papam etiam, regem Franciæ, & Henricum ducem Bavariæ, item reges Hungariæ & Cracouiæ incitans contra ipsum.
units.tr: The king of Bohemia had two sons. The elder, Charles, who was called margrave of Moravia, took as his wife the sister of Philip, king of France. The younger married the daughter of M., duke of Carinthia. He also had two daughters: one was married to John, the eldest son of the king of France, and the other to Henry, duke of Bavaria. Now, when the duke of Carinthia died without a son, leaving only the king of Bohemia's daughter-in-law, the king believed without any dispute that his son would succeed to the duchy. But Prince Louis invested the dukes of Austria, the sons of his sister, the late duke of Carinthia, with the duchy; and only the county of Tyrol remained to the king of Bohemia's son. For this reason the king was moved to a deadly hatred of the Prince. He publicly swore that he would never be reconciled with him, and he incited the Pope, the king of France, Henry duke of Bavaria, and also the kings of Hungary and Cracow against him.

units.la: Papa autem Ioannes de militari progenie natus, ditans fratris & sororum suarum filios & nepotes diuitijs & honoribus, anno pontificatus sui xix moriens, reliquit Sedidecies septies centum millia florenorum, anno M. CCC. XXXIIII. Erat autem quidam vicinus episcopus Romæ, in via eundi ad Curiam Auinionensem ad papam, cui in nocte mortis Papæ in somno apparuit quidam dicens: Papam quæris? non est. Et post pusillum: Vis videre Papam, ecce ipse est, monstrata sibi persona magna incognita. Qui procedens in itinere, audiuit de morte Papæ Ioannis. Veniens autem Auinionem, iuit in consistorium: ingredientes diligenter inspiciens singulos Cardinales. Et cùm non vidisset personam sibi monstratam, quæsiuit à quodam, numquid omnes Cardinales ingressi fuissent? Et responso accepto, quòd omnes, excepto Cardinali Blanco, ordinis Cistercien-sis, illum quæsiuit in domo ipsius, ipsumq; inspiciès faciem perpendit monstratam, sibiq; soli in camera sua dixit: Pater, vos estis papa futurus. De quo cùm ille risisset (nulla enim fuit spes promotionis eius, cùm esset humilior & pauperior inter omnes) episcopus expositio sibi somnio adiecit: Pater, ille qui mihi monstrauit faciem vestram, introduxit me ad stabulum immundissimum, stercoribus plenum, vbi vidi arcam marmoream albissimam, sed vacuam. Vos estis illa arca, quam debetis in officio vestro implere virtutibus & signis. Et ô pastor & stabularie, Curiam & sedem apostolatus, iam immundissimum stabulum, ab auaritijs & sumoniacis stercoribus expurgate, vobisque sanctam Romanam ecclesiam & vrbem recommissas habete.
units.tr: Pope John, who was born of a knightly family, enriched the sons and grandsons of his brothers and sisters with wealth and honours. In the nineteenth year of his pontificate, when he died in the year 1334, he left one million, seven hundred thousand florins. Now there was a certain bishop near Rome, on his way to the Curia at Avignon to the Pope. On the night of the Pope's death, someone appeared to him in a dream and said: "Are you looking for the Pope? He is not here." And after a little while: "Do you want to see the Pope? Behold, it is he," and a great person, unknown to him, was shown to him. Going on his journey, the bishop heard of the death of Pope John. On arriving at Avignon he went into the consistory and carefully inspected each cardinal as they entered. When he did not see the person who had been shown to him, he asked someone whether all the cardinals had gone in. Having received the answer that all had, except Cardinal Blanc of the Cistercian order, he sought him out at his house. Looking at him closely and weighing the face that had been shown to him, he said to him alone in his room: "Father, you are going to be Pope." At this the cardinal laughed, for there was no hope of his promotion, since he was humbler and poorer than all the others. The bishop then added the interpretation of the dream: "Father, he who showed me your face led me into a most filthy stable, full of dung, where I saw a most white marble chest, but empty. You are that chest, which you must fill with virtues and signs in your office. O shepherd and stableman, purge the Curia and the seat of the apostolate, now a most filthy stable, of the dung of avarice and simony; and keep the holy Roman Church and the city entrusted to you."

units.la: Et ecce in electione à tot cardinalibus quasi inscijs, sub altercatione electus extitit: Ego N. nomino illum: qui si esse non poterit, nomino Blancum, quòd repertum est à duabus partibus nominatum, dictusq; Benedictus xii. Itaque statim pro reformatione ecclesiæ S. Petri in urbe l milia expendit florenorum. Et sic vt à Ioanne Papa discrepabat in statura (ille enim fuit pallidus statura & voce pusillus: iste in corpore maximus, facie sanguineus, & voce sonorus) ita & in moribus discrepabant. Ille ad magnificandum & ditandum consanguineos, ad regnandum nobilibus, & exaudiendis eorum petitionibus, ad vestiendum annuatim plus quàm lxx comites & milites intendebat: iste de talibus non curauit. Dixit enim: Absit, quòd rex Franciæ, si per consanguineos meos super me diraretur, me sicut prædecessorem meum ad sua quæuis vota coartaret. Fuit enim ex Tholosa regis Francię, filius pistoris, Theologorum summus, sed nullus in iure, quem inter omnes à longissimis temporibus iustissimum æstimabant, cui & ante suam mortem quidam sanctus homo, se pro eo captiuum tradès, quòd illo anno moreretur, prædixit, quod & factum est.
units.tr: And so, in the election by so many cardinals, as if they knew nothing, he was chosen amid dispute. One said: "I name him; and if he cannot be, I name Blanc." It was found that he had been nominated by two parties, and he was called Benedict XII. Straightaway, for the reform of the church of St Peter in the city, he spent fifty thousand florins. And as he differed from John in stature (John was pale, small in body and voice; this one was very large in body, ruddy in face, and sonorous in voice), so they also differed in their morals. John devoted himself to magnifying and enriching his kinsmen, to ruling through the nobles and hearing their petitions, and to clothing yearly more than seventy counts and knights. Benedict did not care for such things. For he said: "Far be it from me that the king of France, if he were to gain power over me through my relatives, should bend me, as my predecessor was bent, to all his wishes." He was from Toulouse, the son of a baker, the highest of theologians but no lawyer. Among all men, from very early times, he was esteemed the most just. Before his death a certain holy man, offering himself as a captive in his place, foretold that he would die that year, and so it happened.

units.la: Huic Benedicto in principio creationis suæ Philippus rex Franciæ mittens legatos, audacter, quasi nihil sibi denegare auderet, petijt inaudita: inter alia scilicet, vt filium suum primogenitum, generum regis Bohemiæ, faceret regem Viennæ: quòd se faceret vicarium Italiæ: quòd sibi per totam Christianitatem daret decimam decimarum per decennium: & sibi daret totum ecclesiæ thesaurum in subsidium terræ sanctæ. De quo ipse & cardinales tenti, se reformare cum Ludouico Romanorum principe decreuerunt.
units.tr: To this Benedict, at the beginning of his papacy, Philip, king of France, sent envoys. Boldly, as if he dared to deny him nothing, he asked for unheard-of things. Among other things, he asked that his eldest son, son-in-law of the king of Bohemia, be made king of Vienne; that the Pope make him vicar of Italy; that he give him, throughout all Christendom, a tenth of the tithes for ten years; and that he give him the whole treasure of the Church for the relief of the Holy Land. The Pope and the cardinals, held by these demands, decided to reconcile themselves with Louis, prince of the Romans.

units.la: Quid Ludouicus princeps ex scriptis quorundam familiarium suorum, quos in curia Papæ semper habuit, qui & hoc ex Cardinalibus certissimè intellexerant, intelligens: statim Papæ & collegio nuncios & literas humillimas destinauit, qui nuncij à Papa & fratribus edocti, qualiter & sub qua forma redire deberent, & sub quibus articulis absolutionem & gratiam petere: iterum à Principe, cum illis articulis & mandatis sufficientissimis sunt reuersi. Inter quos duo erant comites de Otingen, & præpositus Augustensis, & Marquardus de Randecke canonicus Augustensis R. Bambergensis, postea per Papam eiusdem ecclesiæ præpositus effectus: & magister Vdalricus protonotarius Principis, decretista. Et propositio in publico consistorio, per prædictum de Randeck ex parte Principis humillimè, super petitione absolutionis & restitutionis, facundo sermone, de quo omnes qui aderant mirabantur: Papa gratiosissimè respondens, dixit: Se & fratres suos de hoc, quòd nobilis ramus ecclesiæ Alemanniæ, qui se in persona domini Ludouici, lædi per ecclesiam æstimans, iam ab arbore ecclesiæ separati cœperat, eidem arbori cum tanto honore sedis redintegraretur, plurimùm gratulari: multùm commendans Alemanniæ, & dominum Ludouicum, quem nobiliorem mundi dicebat: conquerens regi Italiæ per tyrannos, ac regnum Armeniæ capi à Paganis, cuius principes tempore Ioannis Papæ & suo Christianorum improbantur auxilium, ac terram sanctam propter Imperatoris carentiam occupari: unde merito dixit absolutionem eidem impertiri se debere, quæ & dari crastino sperabatur.
units.tr: Prince Louis, learning this from the writings of some of his friends whom he always kept at the papal court, and who had discovered it most certainly from the cardinals, immediately sent messengers and very humble letters to the Pope and the college of cardinals. These messengers, instructed by the Pope and the brothers as to how and in what form they should return, and on what conditions they should seek absolution and grace, came back again from the Prince with those conditions and with very ample instructions. Among them were two counts of Oettingen, the provost of Augsburg, Marquard von Randeck, canon of Augsburg and of Bamberg, who was afterwards made provost of that church by the Pope, and Master Udalrich, the Prince's protonotary and a canonist. The proposal was made in public consistory by the aforesaid Randeck on behalf of the Prince, most humbly, concerning the petition for absolution and restoration, in an eloquent speech at which all who were present marvelled. The Pope answered most graciously: he and his brothers greatly rejoiced that the noble branch of the German Church, which, thinking itself wronged by the Church in the person of Lord Louis, had already begun to be cut off from the tree of the Church, was being restored to that same tree with such great honour of its seat. He spoke at length in praise of Germany and of Lord Louis, whom he called the noblest in the world. He complained that the king of Italy was held by tyrants, and that the kingdom of Armenia was being taken by the pagans, whose princes, in the time of Pope John and his own, were refused the help of the Christians; and that the Holy Land was being occupied because of the lack of an Emperor. Therefore, he said, he rightly ought to grant absolution to him, which was expected to be given the next day.

units.la: Verùm prædictus rex Franciæ, & rex Siciliæ, seu Apuliæ, omnes quasi Cardinales à proposito auerterant præconcepto. Venerant enim ad impediendum factum ad Curiam, duo archiepiscopi, duo episcopi, & duo comites, ex parte regis Franciæ, & totidem ex parte regis Roberti: proponentes erroneum esse, tantum hæresiarcham præponere dominis eorum ecclesiæ fidelissimis: Papam & cauere debere, ne fautor hæreticorum diceretur. Papa verò dicente: Quid volunt domini vestri, quòd non sit Imperium? illis verò proterue dicentibus: Pater non impingatis hoc dominis nostris, vel nobis, quod non dicimus. quia contra imperium non loquimur, sed contra personam Ludouici damnatam. Cumque dicerent, Ludouicum multa contra ecclesiam fecisse, Papa dixit: Imò nos fecimus contra eum: ipse enim cum baculo venisset ad pedes prædecessoris nostri, si voluisset, sed ipse noluit eum recipere: & quicquid ille fecit, quasi prouocatus fecit. Quantumcunque autem Papa assereret, se meliora pacta ab ipso Ludouico, pro prædictis regibus, eorum regnis & posteris extracturum, quàm si eum in turri tenerent: penitus nil profecit. Rex Franciæ etiam in terra sua vndiq; bona & reddit...
units.tr: But the aforesaid king of France and the king of Sicily, or Apulia, had turned almost all the cardinals away from the settled purpose. For two archbishops, two bishops, and two counts had come to the Curia to hinder the matter, on behalf of the king of France, and as many on behalf of King Robert. They argued that it was wrong to set over their most faithful lords of the Church a man who was the chief of heretics. The Pope should take care not to be called a supporter of heretics. The Pope replied: "What do your lords want? That there should be no Empire?" They answered insolently: "Father, do not attribute this to our lords or to us, for we do not say it. We do not speak against the Empire, but against the person of Louis, who has been condemned." When they said that Louis had done many things against the Church, the Pope said: "Indeed, we have done them against him. For he came to the feet of our predecessor with a staff, if he had wished it, but he would not receive him. And whatever he did, he did as one provoked." However much the Pope asserted that he would obtain from Louis better terms for the aforesaid kings, their kingdoms and their successors, than if they kept him in a tower, he achieved nothing at all. The king of France also, in his own land on every side, ... goods and revenues ...

units.la: Cardinalium interdixit & occupauit. Scripserant etiam illis diebus ad Curiam, Ioannes rex Bohemiæ, & Heinricus dux Bauariæ, gener eius, quòd de auxilio Hungariæ & Cracouiæ regum & aliorum, alium vellent constituere regem Romanorum potenter. Et sic Cardinales Papam pro tunc ab absolutione principis retraxerunt, dicentes: cum sui in partibus suis vellent eum destituere, inconsultum esse sedi, si propter impotentem & inopem tot Principes offensaret. Sic dato alio termino deliberationis, nuncij principis infecto negotio sunt reuersi.
units.tr: He forbade the cardinals and seized their goods. In those days John, king of Bohemia, and Henry, duke of Bavaria, his son-in-law, had also written to the Curia that with the help of the kings of Hungary and Cracow and others they meant to set up another king of the Romans by force. The cardinals therefore held the Pope back from absolving the prince, saying that since his own people in their regions wished to depose him, it would be unwise for the Holy See to offend so many princes for the sake of one powerless and needy man. A further period was granted for deliberation, and the prince's envoys returned with the business unsettled.

units.la: Et ecce illis diebus Carolus rex Hungariæ, filius fratris prædicti Roberti regis, terram ducum Austriæ, tunc fautorum Principis, ingressus, ipsam multis hebdomadis potenter vastauit. Prędicti autè Bohemiæ & Cracouiæ reges, & H. dux Bauariæ, terræ principis Bauariam superiorem ingredi intendebant. Princeps autem gentè inuictissimam congregans terram Henrici ducis inferiorem Bauariæ ingressus est, cū septem millib. galeatis, illam xvii hebdomadis devastando. Rex autè Hungariæ audiens tam fortè exercitum adesse Principi, ab Austria sine mora recessit, aduentū eius etiam in Hungaria pertimescens. Alij verò tres, quamuis magnam haberet gentem, expectare Principe in campo non audebant. Veniens autè dux Austriæ ad Principem, exercitum eius in Bohemiam ducere nitebatur. Exercitus verò diu in campo fatigatus, se graem reddebat, ita q hinc inde exercitus sunt reuersi. Dicebatur autè, quòd exercitus Principis, quādiu habuisset victū, in omni parte mūdi iacuisset inuictus. Gloriabatur autem Papa Benedictus ab exercitu Principis, cum sibi referebatur, dicens ad Cardinales: nales: Isti dicunt eum esse destitutum (notando principem Ludouicum) sed quis adhuc ingressus est locum suum?
units.tr: Meanwhile Charles, king of Hungary, son of the brother of the aforesaid King Robert, invaded the lands of the dukes of Austria, then supporters of the prince, and laid them waste for many weeks. The aforesaid kings of Bohemia and Cracow, and Duke Henry of Bavaria, intended to enter Upper Bavaria, the prince's land. The prince, however, gathered a most unconquered army, entered the Lower Bavarian lands of Duke Henry with seven thousand men-at-arms, and devastated them for seventeen weeks. When the king of Hungary heard that the prince had so strong an army, he withdrew from Austria without delay, fearing his coming into Hungary as well. The other three, though they had a large force, did not dare to await the prince in the field. The duke of Austria came to the prince and tried to lead his army into Bohemia. But the army, wearied for a long time in the field, grew weary, so that the armies returned on both sides. It was said that the prince's army, as long as it had victory, had lain unconquered in every part of the world. Pope Benedict took pride in the prince's army when it was reported to him, and said to the cardinals: "They say he has been deposed" (meaning Prince Louis), "but who has yet entered his place?"

units.la: Obsidentibus quoq; oppidis Imperialibus ad mandatum Ludouici, oppidum Reisersberg, regi Bohemiae obligatum: conuentum est: quòd nisi rex Bohemiae infra certum tempus ipsos liberare posset, Ludouico ex tunc obedirent. Rege verò Bohemiae eos non liberante: Ludouicus ad ius imperij oppida Reisersberg, Türckheim, Münster, castrum Blickesberg, prius per se obligata Bohemo, retraxit.
units.tr: When the imperial towns were also besieging places at Louis's command, it was agreed that the town of Reisersberg, pledged to the king of Bohemia, should obey Louis from then on unless the king of Bohemia could free them within a certain time. The king of Bohemia did not free them, so Louis took back into the right of the Empire the towns of Reisersberg, Türckheim and Münster and the castle of Blickesberg, which had earlier been pledged by him to the Bohemian.

units.la: Misit autem Papa solennem legatum ad Ludouicū, episcopum Magalonensem, qui mores & motū Principis erga ecclesiam indagaret. Prætendebat etiā Papa occupationem archiepiscopatus Maguntinensis per Balduinum Treuerensem archiepisc. postulatum per capitulū ecclesiæ Moguntinensis factā, & exclusione Henrici de Virnenberg archiepiscopi sedis Mogūtinæ prouisi, reformationi obstare. Volensq; procedere contra Treuerensem, & Treuerensis cū H. prouiso concordatus, archiepiscopatū Moguntinensem, quē potenter tenuit, Capitulo resignauit. Capitulū verò, præsertim magister Ioānes Vnderschopf, Decanus sedis puisus, adhærētes Imperatori, prædictū Henricum archiepiscopū, ligantem se, primò principi, retentis in manib. Capituli sex castris, & abiuratis per eū ne variare posset, sc. Oppenheim/Bingē/Erctuela/Starckenberg/Lonstein & Miltenberg, concorditer receperūt, qui & postea feruēter Ludouico adhæsit. Rex quoq; Ioannes Bohemiæ videns se non proficere, se cū Principe refotmauit, homagiū præstando eidem. Dataq; certa pecunia eidē Bohemo per Australe, in recompensam ducatus Carinthiæ, cū Australi concordati sunt Hungarus & Bohemus. Quantūcunq; autem Benedictus Papa ad absolutionem Principis niteretur: in prædictis tamen Franciæ & Apuliæ regibus, & quasi omnib. Cardinalibus, seductis per eos, assensum habere nequiuit. Vnde tandem legatis Principis sæpe ad Curiam veniētibus, quibus & legati regis Franciæ plures in Curia verecundias inferebant, in tantū, quòd nullū poterant habere finem: respondit, asserens, sibi hoc non à homine, sed à S. spiritu inspiratū. Et creditur habuisse reformationē in animo, non cū tanto honore & cōmodo prædicti regis & sedis, sed cū eorū detrimento & scādalo processurā: quod & ipsius regis discrimina subscripta demonstrant. Et ex tunc Papa, qui ab initio quasi mortem non curans, ea quæ gessit in animo, patefecit, motum suū didicit occultare.
units.tr: The Pope sent a solemn legate to Louis, the bishop of Maguelonne, to investigate the prince's character and his attitude towards the Church. The Pope also pretended that the occupation of the archbishopric of Mainz by Baldwin, archbishop of Trier, who had been requested by the chapter of the church of Mainz, and the exclusion of Henry of Virneburg, provided to the see of Mainz, stood in the way of reform. Wishing to proceed against Trier, and Trier having come to terms with the provided Henry, Baldwin resigned to the chapter the archbishopric of Mainz, which he had held by force. But the chapter, above all master John Underschopf, dean of the vacant see, who adhered to the Emperor, unanimously received the said Henry as archbishop; he bound himself first to the prince, six castles being kept in the hands of the chapter, and he swore to them lest he could change his mind: namely Oppenheim, Bingen, Eltville, Starkenburg, Lahnstein and Miltenberg. Afterwards he also adhered fervently to Louis. King John of Bohemia, seeing that he was getting nowhere, reconciled himself with the prince, doing homage to him. A certain sum of money was given to the same Bohemian through Austria, in recompense for the duchy of Carinthia, and the Hungarian and the Bohemian came to terms with Austria. However hard Pope Benedict pressed for the prince's absolution, he could not obtain assent from the kings of France and Apulia and almost all the cardinals, who had been won over by them. Hence, when the prince's envoys often came to the Curia, and the envoys of the king of France heaped many insults on them there, so that there was no end to it, the Pope at last replied, asserting that this had been inspired in him not by man but by the Holy Spirit. And it is believed that he had a reform in mind which would proceed not with the honour and advantage of the said king and see, but to their harm and scandal; the subsequent misfortunes of the king himself show this. From then on the Pope, who at the beginning had revealed his intentions as if he did not care about death, learned to conceal his movements.

units.la: In diebus illis Spiræ conuenientibus Principe, Henrico Moguntinensi de Virnenburg archiepiscopo, itē Argentinensi, Augustensi, Eistettensi, Spirēsi, Curiensi, & quibusdā alijs episcopis prouinciæ Maguntinæ, conuocatis, missisq; per eos literis & nuncijs, scilicet episcopo Curiēsi & Gerlaco comite de Nassawe ad Papā, pro absolutione Principis: & deliberato per eos, si Papa nollet, q; iterum cōuenire deberent, & deliberare, quid faciendū esset de eo. Cùm Papa Benedictus nuncios recepisset benignè, in aurē nuncijs flens quasi conquerebatur, q; ad Principem esset inclinatus, & quòd rex Franciæ sibi scripserit certis literis, si Bauarum sine eius voluntate absolueret, peiora sibi fierent, quàm Papæ Bonifacio à suis prædecessoribus essent facta: nuncijq; ad rogatum Papæ, per Delphinum per montana sunt vsq; Lausannam perducti.
units.tr: In those days, when the prince was meeting at Speyer, Henry of Virneburg, archbishop of Mainz, together with the bishops of Strasbourg, Augsburg, Eichstätt, Speyer and Chur, and some other bishops of the province of Mainz, were summoned. Letters and messengers were sent through them, namely the bishop of Chur and Count Gerlach of Nassau, to the Pope, to seek the prince's absolution. It was decided by them that if the Pope refused, they should meet again and deliberate what should be done about him. When Pope Benedict had received the envoys kindly, he complained tearfully in their ear that he had been inclined to the prince, and that the king of France had written to him in certain letters that if he absolved the Bavarian without the king's will, worse things would be done to him than Pope Boniface had suffered at the hands of his predecessors.
