Next morning, when they wished to divide the tournament among the helmets, and found a helmet without a crest, and understood that it was the king's, they took counsel among the knights and ceased from the tournament. For they said that if the king were endangered among us, it could be said in future that the king had been betrayed by the Swabians. Coming to Ulm, he was received there by twenty-four Swabian towns, under certain agreements and oaths. Wishing to go to Nuremberg and then to Bohemia, but with ambushes laid for him by the margrave of Brandenburg, he returned to Ulm, and then, coming to Nuremberg by another route, went back to Bohemia.

units.la: Eodem anno de mense Martio, misit magnam gentem de Bohemia, quæ terram Ruperti ducis Bauariæ, Palatini, plurimum deuastauit. Constantia autem Thuregum, & quædam alia oppida vicina, ipsum recipere noluerunt.
units.tr: In the same year, in March, he sent a great host from Bohemia, which laid waste much of the land of Duke Rupert of Bavaria, the Count Palatine. But Constance, Zurich and certain other neighbouring towns refused to receive him.

units.la: Interea Engelmarus miles, qui comitatum Tirolis tradidit marchioni Brandeburgensi, cum vxore ex quadā suspicione per Marchionē capitur, & ante castrū suum forte, quod tenuit frater eius, decollatur, & successiuè omnia sua, per Marchionem, mediante duce Conrado de Teck, sibi fidelissimo, occupantur.
units.tr: Meanwhile the knight Engelmar, who had handed over the county of Tyrol to the margrave of Brandenburg, was seized by the margrave together with his wife, on some suspicion, and was beheaded before his castle, which his brother happened to hold. All his possessions were then seized one after another by the margrave, through Duke Conrad of Teck, who was most loyal to him.

units.la: Eodem tempore oppidani in Mülhusen Alsatiæ, vsurpantes sibi regimen oppidi, nobiles eiecerunt, manente cum eis Happone Monachi, nouo Sculteto. Venientem autem Io. de Vinstingen præsidem Alsatiæ, nisi cum paucis intromittere voluerunt. Ille verò iratus recedens, cū multa gente reuertitur. Oppidanis verò discordantibus, & præsidem sub quibusdā pactis intromittētibus, cū paucis vt credebant, ipse cū multis de auxilio generis de Domo, ingrediēs, multos populares banniuit, occupās res eorū. Veniens autē Columbaria, & cum cautione ingrediens, videns populū in eum commorum, propter factum in Mülhusen, repente recessit, nam & ipsi Columbarienses Henricum de *Wickersheim & suos, qui diu inibi rexerant, excluserunt.
units.tr: At the same time the townsmen of Mülhausen in Alsace, seizing the government of the town for themselves, expelled the nobles, with Happo of Monk remaining among them as new mayor. When John of Finstingen, governor of Alsace, came, they were willing to admit him only with a few men. He, angry, withdrew, but returned with a large force. The townsmen then being divided, and some admitting the governor under certain agreements, as they believed with only a few men, he himself entered with many, with the aid of the Domo family, banished many of the common people and seized their goods. Coming to Colmar, and entering with caution, but seeing the people stirred up against him because of what had happened at Mülhausen, he suddenly withdrew; for the Colmarians themselves had also shut out Henry of Wickersheim and his men, who had long ruled there.

units.la: Brisacum quoq;, Australi per olim Ludouicum principem obligatū, eo mortuo se ab Australi retraxit, dicens se vltra vitā illius obligari non posse. Rege autē nolente eos recipere, tenuere seipsos: qui postea mense Octobri, mandate rege, duci denuo iurarūt.
units.tr: Brisach likewise, which had formerly been pledged to Austria by the late Prince Ludwig, withdrew from Austria on his death, saying that it could not be bound beyond his lifetime. The king being unwilling to receive them, they held themselves apart. Afterwards, in October, by the king's command, they swore allegiance again to the duke.

units.la: Eodem anno, scilicet XLVIII, de mense Ianuarij, Magister ordinis Teutonicorum Sueuus, cum XXII milibus equitum ingressus terram regis Lituaniæ gentilis, sex hebdomadis terram vastauit, quem in reuersione, vsq; ad glaciem fluuij reuertentem, rex Lituaniæ cum XL milibus insequitur, animo eos cum simul ad glaciem venissent, submersubmergendi. At Christiani, qui iam super glaciem partim venerant, videntes illos, reuersi de glacie, ad campum iniere conflictum, illosque trudentes ad glaciem, ipsorum circa sex milia submerserunt, & circa duodecim milia occiderunt, reliquos vero fugientes ad syluas Lituaniæ insequuntur. Duo autem Regis fratres non valentes effugere, arbores ascenderunt: quas cum Christiani succidere vellent, illi videntes se non posse euadere, ne de Christianorum morerentur manibus, cum cingulis suis ad ramos arborum se suspenderunt. Christianorum etiam electorum occisi sunt quinquaginta, vel circa.
units.tr: In the same year, that is XLVIII, in January, the Master of the Teutonic Order, a Swabian, entered the land of the heathen king of Lithuania with 22,000 horsemen and laid waste the country for six weeks. On his return, as far as the river's ice, the king of Lithuania pursued him with 40,000 men, intending to drown them once they had all come onto the ice. But the Christians, some of whom had already reached the ice, seeing them, turned back from the ice and joined battle on the plain; pushing them onto the ice, they drowned about six thousand of them and killed about twelve thousand, and the rest, fleeing, they pursued into the Lithuanian forests. Two brothers of the king, unable to escape, climbed trees; when the Christians wished to cut the trees down, they, seeing they could not get away, and so as not to die in Christian hands, hanged themselves from the branches with their belts. About fifty of the chosen Christians were also killed.

units.la: Eodem anno, mense Februario, Conradus de Kirckel, minister Moguntinensis ecclesiæ, à Ioanne iuniore Comite de Nassawe, cum multis armatis capitur, & Cuno de Valkenstein Canonicus Moguntinensis in ministerio per Capitulum subrogatur, qui surrogatus nullis pactis Conradum liberare valens. Audito etiam quòd captor etiam eum captum optabat, Gerlacum patrem de Nassawe, natum quondam Adolphi regis Romanorum, ignis incendio & omni inquietudine infestauit, eidem vltra LXX villas comburens: Carolone rege in Bohemia existente, nec eundem Comitem in aliquo adiuuante, quanuis Conradum captum diutius tenuerit, propter regem. Emisso autem capto ad tempus, sub cautione aut dandi VIII millia florenorum, vel se representandi: non minùs idem Comes per ministros Moguntinenses, & oppida in Wederaugia extitit infestatus, ita quod tandem captos dimisit, & cum H. archiepiscopo concordauit. At H. archiepiscopus & prædictus minister de Valkenstein, Conradum de Kirckel, etiam petentem, non vltra ad ministerium admiserunt: timentes eum conuenisse clam de aliquibus munitionibus archiepiscopatus tradendis cum captore: propter quod inter ipsos Conradum & Cunonem dissensio fuit suborta, propter impensas & damna, quas & quæ Conradus de Kirckel in ministerio se asseruit sustinuisse. Mortuo interim Io. de Columna Cardinali, præposito ecclesiæ Moguntinensis, prædictus Cuno de Valkenstein & Reinhardus de Spanheim Canonici ecclesiæ Moguntinæ, in discordia sunt electi.
units.tr: In the same year, in February, Conrad of Kirkel, minister of the Church of Mainz, was captured with many armed men by John the Younger, Count of Nassau, and Cuno of Valkenstein, a canon of Mainz, was substituted in the ministry by the chapter. Once substituted, he was unable to free Conrad by any agreement. Hearing also that the captor even wished the captive dead, Gerlach, father of Nassau, son of the late Adolf, King of the Romans, harassed him with fire and every kind of disturbance, burning more than seventy villages belonging to him; King Charles being in Bohemia, and not helping the same count in any way, although he held Conrad captive for a long time because of the king. Then, the captive being released for a time, under surety either of giving eight thousand florins or of presenting himself again, the same count was no less harassed through the ministers of Mainz and the towns in the Wetterau, so that at last he released the captives and came to terms with Archbishop Henry. But Archbishop Henry and the aforesaid minister Valkenstein would no longer admit Conrad of Kirkel to the ministry, even when he sought it, fearing that he had secretly made an agreement with the captor about handing over some fortifications of the archbishopric. On account of this a dispute arose between Conrad and Cuno, over the expenses and losses which Conrad of Kirkel claimed to have borne in the ministry. Meanwhile, on the death of John of Colonna, cardinal and provost of the Church of Mainz, the aforesaid Cuno of Valkenstein and Reinhard of Sponheim, canons of the Church of Mainz, were elected amid discord.

units.la: Rex autem ipse Carolus licet Comites de Wirtenberg & Burggrauium de Norenberg in parte promissorum expedierit, alios tamen multos pluribus mensibus Bohemiæ expectantes, graviter pagati de promissis, minime expediuit. Vxor enim eius & Ioannes frater, aliique Bohemi, ne per tantas erogationes terram Bohemiæ destrueret, maximè ei restiterunt: collecta enim inibi imposita, quæ Vrsus dicitur, & de nouo regi creato debita, apud Bohemos remansit.
units.tr: King Charles himself, although he had satisfied the counts of Württemberg and the burgrave of Nuremberg in part of what had been promised, nevertheless did not satisfy the many others who had waited in Bohemia for several months, and were heavily put off with promises. For his wife, and his brother John, and the other Bohemians strongly resisted him, lest through such great expenditures he should ruin the land of Bohemia; the tax levied there, called the "Ursus," which was owed to the newly created king, remained among the Bohemians.

units.la: Mortuo autem, vt supra, Ludouico Principe, Beatrix de Holandia relicta eius, cum priuignis suis amicabiliter concordans, ipsos in agendis suis plurimum confortauit. Discordantibus autem Rodolpho & Ruperto fratribus, ac Ruperto eorum fratrueli, duabus Bauariæ, & Palatinis Rheni, cum filijs defuncti Principis, pro eo quod dicebant, sibi in inferiori Bauaria similiter cum illis ius hæreditarium competere, dataque & promissa eis certa pecunia, & huiusmodi dissensione sopita: ecce H. Moguntinus, Ludouicus marchio Brandenburgensis, Rupertus Palatinus, cui in hoc alij duo consenserant, & Ericus Dux Saxoniæ, cui ex successione patris sui senioris, Rodolpho duci ius eligendi competere dicebatur, quanuis Rodolphus Caroli elector quædam dominia, quibus principatum annexum asserit, se habere prætendat, de eligendo rege alio, cum electione Caroli irritam asserant, concordarunt. Missique per eos pluries solennibus nuntijs ad Eduardum Angliæ Regem, sibique electione oblata, remissisque per eum nuntijs literisque, sibi sub castro Lonstein, de non variando, sub sigillis ipsorum Principum assignatis, eoque deliberationem suam diutius protrahente, eò quòd inter ipsum & Francum tractabatur de treugis: Francoqj sciente, Anglum electionem Romani regni appetere, & ob hoc (ne crescat eius potentia) treugas alias sibi gratissimas, recusante: Angloque propter litem cum Franco in festo beati Ioannis Baptistæ renouatam, de electione de ipso facta intromittere se nolente: cum literis sibi desuper datis, remissis, principibus rescripsit, se ijsdem Principibus fauoris sui auxilium polliceri. Quo facto, ijdem Principes Electores vocato Friderico marchione Missenensi, ab nepote quondam Friderici Imperatoris ex filia eius, genero prædicti Ludouici Principis defuncti, in principio mensis Iunij in Kans rex Rom. declaratus. Bauariæ conuenerunt, vbi inter eos actum est, quòd idem Marchio prædictam Beatricem, olim Imperatricem, in vxorem duceret, & de Romano regno ad eorum electionem intromittere se deberet. Oppidum quoq; Nurenberg eiectis potentioribus Regis fautoribus, dicente populo, se non consensisse in regem, Marchionem de Brandenburg, pro rege acceptauit.
units.tr: After the death of Prince Ludwig, as mentioned above, his widow Beatrix of Holland, reconciling herself amicably with her stepsons, greatly strengthened them in their affairs. But when the brothers Rudolf and Rupert, and Rupert their cousin, the two Bavarias, and the Palatines of the Rhine, together with the sons of the late prince, disagreed, because they claimed that a hereditary right similarly belonged to them in Lower Bavaria, and when certain sums of money had been given and promised to them and this dispute had been quieted, behold: Henry of Mainz, Ludwig, margrave of Brandenburg, Rupert the Palatine, to whom two others had consented in this matter, and Eric, Duke of Saxony, to whom the right of electing was said to belong by succession from his elder father, although Rudolf, elector of Charles, claimed to hold certain lordships to which he asserted the principality was attached, agreed to elect another king, declaring Charles's election void. They sent solemn envoys to Edward, King of England, several times, and the offer of election was made to him; the envoys and letters sent back by him, given under the seals of the princes, promised him, at the castle of Lonstein, not to change his mind; but he delayed his deliberation for a long time, because at that time a truce was being negotiated between him and the French. The French, knowing that the English king was seeking the election to the Roman kingdom, and refusing on this account to grant him the truce he most wanted (lest his power grow), and the English king, because of the quarrel with the French renewed at the feast of St John the Baptist, being unwilling to intervene in the election made concerning him, wrote back to the princes, sending their letters back to them, promising the same princes the help of his favour. This done, the same princes, the electors, having summoned Frederick, margrave of Meissen, a grandson through his daughter of the late Emperor Frederick and son-in-law of the late Prince Ludwig, declared him king of the Romans at the beginning of June at Kans. They met in Bavaria, where it was agreed among them that the same margrave should marry the aforesaid Beatrix, formerly empress, and should interfere in the Roman kingdom at their election. The town of Nuremberg also, after the more powerful supporters of the king had been expelled, the people saying that they had not consented to the king, accepted the margrave of Brandenburg as king.

units.la: Post hæc Marchio Missenensis desistens à propósito, receptis à rege Carolone x millibus marcis, facto sibi homagio, & excepto ne contra filios defuncti Principis faceret, à rege ipso feudorum Imperialium investituram accepit quanuis enim iuuenis, arthritico tenebatur, & infra biennium moritur.
units.tr: After this the Margrave of Meissen gave up his purpose. He received ten thousand marks from King Charles, did homage, and, with the exception that he would not act against the sons of the late prince, received the investiture of the imperial fiefs from the king himself. Although he was young, he was afflicted with gout, and he died within two years.

units.la: Interea inter Bohemiam & Austriam, Carolone rege prædicto & Alberto Australi, pro perficiendis nuptijs inter eorum liberos, conuenientibus in vicino, & dicente Australi tractatoribus, quòd scire vellet, quòd rex non assisteret Comiti C. de Medeburg, in confinio Austriæ, Vngariæ & Bohemiæ residenti. Rex verò eundem Comitem, tanquam seruitorem, diceret se relinquere non posse: ambo sic infecto negotio sunt reuersi. Idem enim Comes iuuenis & elegatis formæ tempore obsidionis in Kales, in seruitio Franci existens, & relictam quondam domini de Kussi, filiam quondam Lupoldi ducis Austriæ visitans, & præhabitis pluribus internuncijs, cum ea insció patruo matrimonium contrahens, ipsius Alberti patrui (dolentis eam cum impare contraxisse, & forsan timentis se per ipsum Comitem super hæreditate vexari) indignationem incurrit.
units.tr: Meanwhile, King Charles and Duke Albert of Austria met nearby between Bohemia and Austria to arrange the marriage of their children. Albert told the negotiators that he wished to know whether the king would support Count C. of Medeburg, who lived on the border of Austria, Hungary and Bohemia. The king replied that he could not abandon the count, who was his servant. Both sides went home with the matter unsettled. The count, a young man of fine appearance, had served the Frenchman during the siege of Calais. He visited the widow of the late lord of Kussi, daughter of the late Duke Leopold of Austria, and after several intermediaries he married her without the knowledge of her uncle. This drew the anger of Albert himself, her uncle, who was grieved that she had married beneath her and perhaps feared that the count would harass him over the inheritance.

units.la: Postea tamen reuersi ipsi rex & Dux, liberorum nuptias perfecerunt: Duce tamen in huiusmodi amicitia excipiente liberos quondam Ludouici Principis, quibus in vita Principis extitit alligatus.
units.tr: Afterwards, however, the king and the duke returned and arranged the marriage of the children. In this friendship the duke excepted the sons of the late prince, to whom he had been bound while the prince was alive.

units.la: Reuerso autem de partibus Apuliæ Vngaro propter pestilentiam: Albertus Dux Carolum Bohemum, Ludouicum Bauarum, marchionem in Brandeburg & alios multos in Patauiam, ad dominicam post Iacobi, pro tractanda concordia, convocauit. Interea fama euolauit, quòd tractante duce Brabantiæ, ac Treuerensi & Marggrauio Iuliacensi, Bohemus nomine Romani regis terras Holandiæ & Selandiæ, quas Wilhelmus filius quondam Ludouici Principis tenet, filijs Regis Angliæ & Iuliacensis contulit, amicitia inter Bohemum & Anglum contracta: in qua tamen Bohemus Francum excepit. Propter quæ Bohemus & Brandeburgensis, à Patauia, ad quam Marchio cum duobus millibus equitum venerat, infecto negotio recesserunt: Marchione quod nunquam Bohemum pro Rege Romano ex prædicta electione habeat, asserente. Bohemus autem & Australis nauigio Austriam descenderunt. Signa autem Imperialia aquilarum, Patauiæ hospitiis Bohemi inpicta, per familiam Marchionis, præsertim Hugonem Comitem de Hohenberg, stercoribus sunt deleta, & barræ in vicubus hospitiorum Bohemi violenter apertæ. Factis autem & alijs terminis minime concordarunt.
units.tr: When the Hungarian returned from Apulia because of the plague, Duke Albert summoned Charles of Bohemia, Louis of Bavaria, the Margrave of Brandenburg and many others to Passau, for the Sunday after St James's Day, to negotiate a settlement. Meanwhile a rumour spread that, while the Duke of Brabant, the Archbishop of Trier and the Margrave of Jülich were negotiating, Bohemia, in the name of the King of the Romans, had granted the lands of Holland and Zeeland, which William, son of the late Prince Louis, holds, to the sons of the King of England and of the Duke of Jülich. A friendship had been formed between Bohemia and the Englishman, though in it Bohemia excluded the Frenchman. Because of this, Bohemia and the Brandenburger left Passau, where the margrave had come with two thousand horsemen, and the matter was left unsettled. The margrave declared that he would never acknowledge Bohemia as King of the Romans by that election. Bohemia and Albert went down to Austria by ship. The imperial eagle standards painted on Bohemia's lodgings at Passau were smeared with dung by the margrave's household, especially Count Hugo of Hohenberg, and the bars in the lanes outside Bohemia's lodgings were violently broken open. Even after further terms were set, they did not agree at all.

units.la: Obiit autem eo tempore de Francia vxor regis.
units.tr: At that time the king's wife died in France.

units.la: Eo tempore in principio Augusti, liga pacis Alsatiæ, castrum Frundesberg, propter quosdam Mercatores Sueuos, in terminis ligæ inibi captos, destruxit, captiuos absoluens.
units.tr: At that time, at the beginning of August, the League of Peace of Alsace destroyed the castle of Frundesberg because some Swabian merchants had been seized there within the league's borders. It freed the prisoners.

units.la: Treuerensis archiepiscopus cum magna gente castrum Isfenburg obsedit, & læsis pluribus de suis, parante quoque H. Moguntino se ad obuiandum ei, quasi confusus recessit.
units.tr: The Archbishop of Trier besieged the castle of Isenburg with a large force. After several of his men were wounded, and with Henry of Mainz preparing to oppose him, he withdrew as if dismayed.

units.la: Rodolphus autem dux Saxoniæ quendam in terra sua, similem quondam Wolmaro marchioni in Brandenburg, inueniens, eumque Marchionem fingens esse (prætensis multis figmentis, qualiter olim Marchio se fingens mortuum, a terra clam recesserit, ex causa pœnitentiæ, alio nomine ipsius defuncti) multas ciuitates Marchiæ ad recipiendum eundem induxit. Et veniens rex repente cum magno exercitu Bohemorum, quasi totam Marchiam, à Ludouici marchionis ditione retraxit. Gens enim terræ luxuriam cum filiabus & vxoribus suis, & quòd liberi sui non sint legitimi, nec digni tanto principatu, impingere dicebatur. Ipse vero Marchio celeriter cum exercitu suo ingrediens, in oppido terra Franckfordensi se recepit, quem Carolus ibidem obsedit, sed factis pluribus insultibus hinc inde recessit.
units.tr: Duke Rudolph of Saxony found in his land a man resembling the late Margrave Wolmar of Brandenburg. Pretending that this man was the margrave, with many fabricated stories of how the margrave, feigning death, had secretly left the land for reasons of penance under another name, he persuaded many cities of the march to receive him. Then the king suddenly came with a great army of Bohemians and drew almost the whole march away from the rule of Margrave Louis. It was said that the people of the land charged him with luxury with his daughters and wives, and that his children were not legitimate nor worthy of so great a principality. The margrave himself entered quickly with his army and took refuge in a town in the Frankfurt region. Charles besieged him there, but after several assaults he withdrew from one place and another.

units.la: Post haec venit Dux Rupertus Bavariae iunior, filius quondam Adolphi Palatini, habens vxorem Siculam, cum Comite de Schwartzenburg, & multis aliis, ex parte patruelis sui Ludouici Marchionis, in Marchiam, viriliter se tenens. Visaque in campo multitudine inimicorum, dixit Comes: Domine, expedit nos abire. At ille: Valentissime Comes, ne loquaris ita, quod in primo conflictu meo recedam. Quo audito, aggressi sunt inimicos, ipsos vincentes. Confortatus itaque Rupertus progressus nimis in partes inimicorum, temereque quaerens conflictus, tandem captus est, & per Rudolfum, Ducem Saxoniae multis annis detentus.
units.tr: After this came Duke Rupert the Younger of Bavaria, son of the late Count Palatine Adolf, who had a Sicilian wife. With Count of Schwarzenburg and many others, acting on behalf of his cousin Margrave Louis, he entered the march and held himself bravely. Seeing the multitude of enemies in the field, the count said: "Lord, it is advisable for us to withdraw." But Rupert replied: "Most valiant count, do not speak so, for I will not retreat in my first encounter." Hearing this, they attacked the enemy and defeated them. But Rupert, strengthened, advanced too far into the enemy's ranks and rashly sought combat. At last he was captured and held for many years by Rudolph, Duke of Saxony.

units.la: Reuerso autem propter pestilentiam Vngaro, Ioanna relicta Andreae fratris sui, vxor Ludouici Ducis Thoraciae de auxilio Papae Neapolim reuertitur, & eiectis Vngari fidelibus, terra sibi iterum subiugatur: Wernhero de Vrselingen, Sueuo (qui primo Vngaro adhaesit, & abeo propter quandam suspicionem falso sibi impactam, vt dixit, licentiatus fuit) eidem Ioanna propter pecuniam assistente. Nicolaus enim tribunus vrbis, fautor Vngari, disparens, sede inibi quasi praevalente, eo tempore non erat potens in Vrbe.
units.tr: When the Hungarian returned because of the plague, Joanna, widow of her brother Andrew and wife of Louis, Duke of Durazzo, returned to Naples with the Pope's help. The Hungarian loyalists were expelled, and the land was again brought under her rule. Werner of Urslingen, a Swabian, assisted Joanna for money. He had at first adhered to the Hungarian, and was dismissed by him, as he said, on account of a suspicion falsely cast on him. Nicholas, the tribune of the city and a supporter of the Hungarian, had disappeared; his party seemed to have prevailed there, but at that time he was not powerful in the city.

units.la: Vendidit autem ipsa Ioanna, quantum in ipsa fuit, Papae ciuitatem Auinionensem, pro multa pecuniae quantitate.
units.tr: Joanna herself, as far as lay in her power, sold the city of Avignon to the Pope for a large sum of money.

units.la: Eodem anno M. CCC. XLVIII. mense Ianuarij, in conuersione Sancti Pauli, factus est terraemotus generalis & magnus, ex qua homines pati syncopam putabantur, & in aliquibus locis multis diebus durauit, praesertim in Carinthia, vbi oppidum grande Villach cum multis castris & villis eiusdem vallis corruerunt & perierunt, & in multis locis ex hoc incredibilia euenerunt.
units.tr: In the same year, 1348, in January, on the feast of the Conversion of St Paul, there was a great general earthquake. Men were thought to suffer a swoon from it, and in some places it lasted for many days, especially in Carinthia. There the large town of Villach, with many castles and villages of that valley, collapsed and perished, and in many places incredible things happened because of it.

units.la: Facta est & Pestilentia mortalitatis hominum praesertim in partibus vltramarinis & maritimis & aliis, qualis a tepore diluuij non est facta, aliquibus terris hominibus penitus euacuatis, multisque triremibus in mari cum mercibus habitatoribus extinctis, sine rectore repertis. Marsiliae episcopus: cum toto Capitulo, & quasi omnes Praedicatores & Minores cum dupla parte inhabitantium perierunt. Quot vero in Montepessulano, in Neapoli, & alijs regnis & ciuitatibus mortui sint, nemo posset enarrare: Auinione in curia per contagionem morbi infecta, ex quo multi sine sacramento perierunt. Nec curam habebant parentes de filiis, nec econtra, nec socij sociorum, nec famuli dominorum, quod domus cum omni supellectile vacuae fuerunt, quas nullus ingredi audebat. Horror est scribere vel narrare: Nulla fuit ibi causarum agitatio. Papa inclusus camerae habenti ignes magnos continue, nulli dabat accessum, terrasque haec pestis transibat: nec poterant philosophantes, quamuis multa dicerent, certam de his dicere rationem, nisi quod Dei esset voluntas. Haecque nunc hic, nunc alio loco, per integrum annum & plures annos durabat.
units.tr: There was also a pestilence of men, especially in the lands overseas and by the sea and elsewhere, such as had not occurred since the time of the flood. Some lands were entirely emptied of people, and many triremes were found at sea with their merchandise and their inhabitants dead, without a master. The bishop of Marseille perished with the whole chapter, and almost all the Preachers and Minorites perished with half of the inhabitants. No one could recount how many died in Montpellier, in Naples, and in other kingdoms and cities. At Avignon, in the curia, the disease spread by contagion, and many died without the sacraments. Parents took no care of their children, nor children of their parents, nor companions of their companions, nor servants of their masters. Houses were left empty with all their furniture, and no one dared enter them. It is horrible to write or relate: no cases were pleaded there. The Pope, shut in a chamber with great fires burning continually, admitted no one. This plague passed over those lands. The philosophers, although they said many things, could give no certain rational account of these events, except that it was God's will. It lasted now here, now in another place, for a whole year and several years.

units.la: Et infamati sunt Iudaei, quod huiusmodi Pestilentiam fecerint, vel auxerint, fontibus & puteis iniecto veneno: & cremati sunt a mari vsq; ad Alemanniam, praeterquam Auinione, vbi eos papa Clemens sextus defendit.
units.tr: The Jews were defamed as having caused or increased this pestilence by poisoning springs and wells. They were burned from the sea as far as Germany, except at Avignon, where Pope Clement VI defended them.

units.la: Post haec tortis quibusdam in Berna, in comitatu Friburgensi & alibi, & reperto in Zofingen veneno, extinctisque Iudeis in pluribus locis, scriptoque de hocconsulibus Basiliensis, Friburgensis & Argentinensis ciuitatum, maioribusque ad defensionem intendentibus Iudaeorum, ac quibusdam etiam nobilibus Basilae, ob quandam iniuriam Iudaeis illatam ad longum tempus bannitis: ecce irruit populus cum Banneriis ad Palatium Consulum. Quibus territis, & quaerente Magistro, quid velint? responderunt: se nolle redire, nisi bannitis reuersis: pro quib. illico est transmissum, Consulibus non audentibus egredi, quousque banniti venirent. Adiecitque
units.tr: Afterwards, some men were tortured at Bern, in the county of Freiburg and elsewhere; poison was found at Zofingen; and Jews were killed in many places. A letter about this was written to the consuls of the cities of Basel, Freiburg and Strasbourg, and the greater men who were working to defend the Jews, and certain nobles at Basel as well, who had been banned for a long time because of some injury done to the Jews. Behold, the people rushed with banners to the consuls' palace. Terrified by them, and with the magistrate asking what they wanted, they replied that they would not go home unless the banished men were restored. Because of this a message was sent at once, the consuls not daring to go out until the banished men came. And they added

units.la: Terramo-tus. populus, se nolle quòd inibi amplius remanerent Iudæi. Et iuratum est per consules & populum, quod in c c'annis ibi nunquam Iudæi residerent. Conueneruntque pluries nuntij meliores earundem trium ciuitatum, quibus cordi erat retentio Iudæorum, sed populi timuerunt clamorem. Capti sunt autem vndique Iudæi in partibus illis.
units.tr: that the people did not want the Jews to remain there any longer. It was sworn by the consuls and people that the Jews would never reside there for a hundred years. The better men of those three cities met several times, those who had at heart the retention of the Jews, but they feared the clamour of the people. The Jews were then captured everywhere in those parts.

units.la: Indictus est autem terminus in Bennefelt Alsatiæ, vbi conuenerunt episcopus, Domini & Barones & nuntij comitum, nuntijs Argentinensibus dicentibus, se nil mali scire de Iudæis suis: quæsitum est ab eis, cur vrnæ de eorum puteis fuerint sublatæ, omnis enim populus clamabat contra eos. Conuenerunt autem episcopus Argentinensis, Domini Alsatiæ, & ciuitates Imperij, de non habendis Iudæis, & sic modò in vno loco, & postea in alio, sunt cremati. Alicubi autem sunt expulsi: quos vulgus apprehendens, hos cremauit, alios interfecit, alios in paludibus suffocauit. Cremati sunt igitur absque sententia, ad clamorem populi, omnes Iudæi Basilienses, in vna insula Rheni, in domo noua eis facta, feria sexta ante Hilarii, anno Domini M.CCC.XLIX, & sequenti feria sexta in Friburgo, duodecim ditioribus retentis, vt per illos possent eorum debitores artare.
units.tr: A day was set at Benfeld in Alsace, where the bishop, the lords and barons, and the envoys of the counts gathered. The envoys of Strasbourg declared that they knew nothing of any wrong done by their Jews. They were asked why the urns had been removed from the wells, since the whole populace was crying out against them. The bishop of Strasbourg, the lords of Alsace, and the cities of the Empire agreed not to admit Jews. So they were burned, first in one place and then in another. In some places they were expelled, and the common people seized them, burned some, killed others, and drowned others in marshes. Thus all the Jews of Basel were burned without any sentence, at the clamour of the people, on an island in the Rhine, in a new house built for them, on the Friday before Hilary, in the year of the Lord 1349. The following Friday the Jews of Freiburg were burned too, though twelve of the richer ones were kept back so that through them their debtors could be pressed.

units.la: Spiræ autem Iudæi in domibus suis congregati, seipsos combusserunt, aliqui per populum interfecti fuerunt, sabbato post Epiphaniam Domini, anno prædicto, & in plateis mortui iacuerunt: aliqui etiam effugerunt cremationem, qui reseruabantur ac baptisabantur. Populus etiam Spirensis, timens acrem infici ex fœtore cadauerum in plateis iacentium, etiamsi comburentur, fecerunt eadem cadauera in vasis vacuis vinosis includi, & in Rhenum deduci. Consules etiam ciuitatis edictum fecerunt publicum, ne quis de populo domos Iudæorum ingrederetur, & vicos Iudæorum firmarunt, ne quis introire posset, & totum thesaurum per Iudæos abscondituм quæsierunt, & repertum conseruarunt: ferebatur enim magnum thesaurum in auro & argento se inuenisse. Wormatienses etiam Iudæi, vt Spirenses, Oppenheimenses & Maguntini, se ipsos combusserunt. Quidam etiam inuenti sunt, quasi omnia maleficiorum genera commisisse, sed in Hispania habito per eos dudum consilio, de veneficijs, conuenisse: item de multorum puerorum nece, defalsis literis, de corruptione monetarum, furtis, & aliis multis, in quibus offendebant Altissimi maiestatem.
units.tr: At Speyer the Jews gathered in their houses and set themselves on fire; some were killed by the people, on the Saturday after the Epiphany of the Lord that year, and the dead lay in the streets. Some who escaped the burning were kept back and baptized. The people of Speyer, fearing a deadly contagion from the stench of the corpses lying in the streets even when burned, had the bodies sealed in empty wine vessels and carried down to the Rhine. The consuls of the city also issued a public edict that no one of the people should enter Jewish houses. They barricaded the Jewish quarters so that no one could get in, and they sought out the whole hidden treasure of the Jews and, once found, kept it safe, for it was reported that they had discovered a great treasure of gold and silver. The Jews of Worms, like those of Speyer, Oppenheim and Mainz, also burned themselves. Some were found to have committed, as it were, every kind of wickedness. In Spain, a council had long before been held among them about poisonings, and it was agreed upon; likewise about the killing of many boys, forged letters, the debasing of the coinage, thefts, and many other crimes by which they offended the majesty of the Most High.

units.la: Aliqui etiam Argentinæ vt sedarent clamorem populi, super rotis sunt positi statimque necati, ne super rotis viuentes quid dicere possent: ex quo contra maiores ciuitatis maior suspicio est suborta. Fuerant autem quidam Iudæi diuites Argentinæ ad domum vnam super Bruscam ducti, quasi vt abduci possent, qui postea ducti sunt ad Cœmiterium eorum, in domum combustioni paratam, & in ducendo per vulgum, vestibus sunt omnino nudati, in quib. magnus thesaurus florenorum est repertus, quem secum cum vestibus volebant comburi.
units.tr: At Strasbourg, to quiet the outcry of the people, some were placed upon wheels and killed at once, lest they might say something while still living on the wheel. From this a greater suspicion arose against the leading men of the city. Some wealthy Jews of Strasbourg had been led to a house above the Brusca, as if they were to be taken away elsewhere, and afterwards they were led to their cemetery, into a house prepared for burning. While being led through the crowd they were stripped entirely of their clothes, and in these clothes a great treasure of florins was found, which they had wanted to be burned along with them.

units.la: Pauci autem defensi sunt in ciuitatibus baptismum eligentes, vt combustionem euaderent, & plures Iudæ pulchræ quasi inuitæ, multique pueri erepti, ab inuitis sunt baptizati, multique prosilientes de igne & per plateas currentes sunt interfecti. Pluresque Duces & Barones & milites propria castra habentes, suos tenuerunt, qui per Iudæos baptizatos & Christianos multa intoxicasse dicuntur, multique talium fatentes ea, postea sunt cremati. Pluresque Christiani torti, falsi sunt, se recepta à Iudæis pecunia, & dictis quibusdam verbis super eos per Iudæos, promisisseque per eos de intoxicando, in tantam peruenisse dementiam, quòd libenter omnes Christicolas occidissent. Vnde successiue omnes quasi baptisati Iudæi sunt cremati: quia fatebantur, eos omnes culpabiles. Indignatæ sunt autem ciuitates Alsatiæ contra omnes, tenentes in suis partibus Iudæos. Vnde minister Ducum Austriæ vix obtinuit, ne obsideretur, quòd captis omnibus Iudæis Ducum in Ensisheim, nuncium in Austriam destinaret.
units.tr: In the cities a few were spared by choosing baptism to escape the burning. Many Jewish women, as if unwilling, and many boys, snatched away, were baptized against their will, and many who leapt out of the fire and ran through the streets were killed. Many dukes, barons and knights, who held their own strongholds, kept their own people, who are said to have poisoned many by means of baptized Jews and Christians; many who confessed these things were afterwards burned. Many Christians were tortured and falsely confessed that they had received money from the Jews, and that after certain words had been spoken over them by Jews they had promised through them to poison people. Such madness spread that they would gladly have killed all Christians. Hence, one after another, all the Jews, even the baptized, were burned, because they confessed them all to be guilty. The cities of Alsace, which kept Jews within their territories, were indignant against everyone. So the minister of the Dukes of Austria barely prevented a siege by sending a messenger into Austria, after all the Jews of the Dukes had been seized at Ensisheim.

units.la: Rupertus etiam Dux Bauariæ in oppido Heidelberg, & alijs munitionibus, & Engelhardus de Hirtzenhorn miles in oppido Semesheim Iudæos tenuerunt, qui de ciuitatibus Spiræ & Wormatiæ effugerant, propter quòd coniura ipsos munita à Ciuitatibus fuit: quia magnam pecuniam ab eis habuerunt. Insultu quoque in eos facto in Franckfurt, post regis Caroli recessum, se & omnes domos suas, & sibi vicinas cremarunt.
units.tr: Duke Rupert of Bavaria kept Jews in the town of Heidelberg and in other strongholds, and Engelhard of Hirtzenhorn, a knight, kept them in the town of Semesheim. These were Jews who had fled from the cities of Speyer and Worms, because the cities had strengthened the conspiracy against them, and the lords had received great sums of money from them. Also, after King Charles had left, an attack was made on the Jews at Frankfurt, and they set fire to themselves, their houses, and the houses next to theirs.

units.la: In fine autem Augusti, Moguntiæ multis fidelibus se flagellantibus aduenis, facto rumore ex abscissione vnius bursæ, & credente populo, quòd rumor esset contra Iudæos: ecce omnis populus irruit in Iudæos, & occilis multis Christianis per eos, videntes se non posse euadere, combusserunt domos suas, & seipsos cum rebus in eisdem. Iudæi etiam omnium ciuitatum Imperialium & aliorum locorum, quia quondam Ludouicus Princeps, ipsis dum vixit, tanquam seruis suis, satis fuerat fauorabilis, & ergo ante cremationem & ipsorum interemptionem mortuo Principe, multùm fuerant de nece sua dolorosi: quia talem spem habuerunt, ex quo in tantùm populus Israel creuit, quòd de suo auxilio in breui omnes Christicolas debebant occidisse. Ciuitates autem domorum Iudæorum interemptorum fractorum cum lapidibus super sepulcris constitutis, & Cœmeteriorum suorum, & thesauro reperto, turres nouas in suis ciuitatibus construxerunt, ac cum lapidibus muros refecerunt, & thesauros repertos in vsus Reipublicæ conuerterunt. Facta sunt hæc & multa alia de Iudæis, anno Domini M. CCC. XLIX. dominica ante Valentini.
units.tr: At the end of August at Mainz, while many faithful pilgrims were flogging themselves, a rumour arose from the cutting of a purse. The people, believing the rumour was against the Jews, rushed upon them all at once. Many Christians had been killed by the Jews, and the Jews, seeing they could not escape, burned their houses and themselves with their goods inside them. The Jews of all the imperial cities and of other places, because Prince Louis had been quite favourable to them while he lived, treating them as his own servants, and therefore before the burning and their slaughter, with the prince now dead, had been very sorrowful over his death, since they had hoped that the people of Israel had grown so strong that with his help they would soon have killed all Christians. The cities, meanwhile, built new towers in their towns from the stones of the demolished houses of the slain Jews and from their cemeteries, repaired their walls with the stones, and turned the treasures found to public use. These and many other things were done concerning the Jews in the year of the Lord 1349, on the Sunday before Valentine's day.

units.la: Cum autem indictus fuisset dudum conflictus, ad diem beati Ioannis Baptistæ prædicti, vt supra anno M. CCC. XLIX, inter Angliæ & Franciæ Reges: tanta fuit vtriusque regni pestilentia, quòd vix tertia pars hominum dicebatur remansisse, propter quæ conflictus est prorogatus. Comesque Flandriæ, qui recusata filia Angli, quâ ducturum se promiserat, à terra recedens, ducis Brabantiæ filiam duxit, & ambo Franco fauerunt, reuersus Flandriam, in populi fauorem Anglo adhæsit.
units.tr: A battle between the kings of England and France had long been arranged for the day of the blessed John the Baptist mentioned above, in the year 1349. But the plague in both kingdoms was so great that scarcely a third part of the people was said to be left, and on account of this the battle was postponed. The Count of Flanders, who had refused the daughter of the Englishman whom he had promised to marry, withdrew from the land and married the daughter of the Duke of Brabant, and both favoured the Frenchman. On returning to Flanders, however, he attached himself to the Englishman, to win the favour of the people.

units.la: Incipiente autem paulatim Pestilentia, in Alemannia, coeperunt se populi flagellare, transeuntes per terram, & venerunt CC de Sueuia Spiram, anno prædicto XLIX, in medio Iunij, habentes inter se vnum Principalem, & duos alios magistros, quorum mandatis omnino parebant. Et cum hora primæ Rhenum transissent, accurrente populo, fecerunt Circulum in ciuitate Spira ante monasterium latum valde, in cuius medio se exuentes, depositis vestibus & calceamentis, habentes in modum bracæ camisias à femore ad talos prætensas, circumiuerunt, vnusquè post alium in circulo se in modum crucifixi prostrauit: quilibetque eorum super quoslibet transeuntes passibus, & leniter prostratos flagellis tangentes, vltimi qui se primò strauerunt, primò surgentes se flagellauerunt, flagellis habentibus nodos cum quatuor aculeis ferreis, transeuntes cum cantu vulgari inuocationis Dominicæ, habente multas inuocationes: & sterterunt tres in medio circuli sonori valde, præcinentes, flagellando se, post quos alij canebant: in quo diu immorantes, ad vnum pretentum omnes genu flexi, in modum crucifixi in facies suas corruerunt, cum singultu orantes, & transierunt iuxta circulum Magistri, monentes eos, vt orarent ad Dominum pro clementia super populum, item super omnes eorum benefactores & malefactores, & omnes peccatores, & in Purgatorio existentes, & pluribus alijs. Post hæc se leuantes, extensis manibus in cælum, genu flexi canebant: & iterum surgentes, diu se flagellabant, euntes vt prius, quibus se induentibus alia pars eorum, quæ indumenta & substantiam suam custodierat, se exuens, idem fecit. Post hæc surrexit vnus sonorus, legens literam, quia aliqui fuerant inter eos sacerdotes & literati, nobiles & ignobiles, mulieres & pueri, cuius literæ tenor similis in sententia esse dicebatur, in ecclesia S. Petrii in Hierusalem per angelum præsentata, in qua narrat Angelus: Christum offensum contra mundi prauitates plurima exprimes crimina, violationum diei Dominicæ, & quòd non ieiunetur feria sexta, blasphemias, vsuras, adulteria. Christiũq; rogatũ per beatá virginé & angelos pro misericordia, respondisse: quemlibet per triginta quatuor dies se debere exulando flagellare, vt misericordiam Dei consequantur.
units.tr: As the plague gradually began to spread in Germany, the people began to flagellate themselves as they travelled through the land. In the middle of June in the year 1349, two hundred from Swabia came to Speyer, having among them one leader and two other masters, whose orders they wholly obeyed. When they had crossed the Rhine at the hour of prime, and the people came running up, they made a circle in the city of Speyer in front of a very wide monastery. In the middle of this circle they took off their clothes and shoes and went round wearing shirts stretched from the thigh to the heel, like breeches. One after another they threw themselves prostrate in the circle in the manner of one crucified. Each of them struck lightly with whips those who passed over the prostrate men. The last to have thrown themselves down rose first and flogged themselves with whips having knotted cords with four iron spikes, while passing by they sang in the vernacular a chant of invocation of the Lord, which had many invocations. Three stood loudly singing in the middle of the circle, leading the chant as they flogged themselves, and the others sang after them. Remaining there a long time, all kneeling at a single signal, they fell on their faces in the manner of the crucified, praying with sobs. They then passed by the circle of the masters, urging them to pray to the Lord for mercy upon the people, and likewise for all their benefactors and evildoers, all sinners, those existing in Purgatory, and many others. After this, rising and stretching their hands to heaven, they knelt and sang; then rising again, they flogged themselves for a long time and went on as before. When they had put their clothes back on, another part of them, who had kept their garments and property, stripped and did the same. After this one of them rose with a loud voice and read a letter, for among them there were some priests and literate men, nobles and commoners, women and children. The content of this letter was said to be similar to one presented by an angel in the church of St Peter in Jerusalem, in which the angel tells how Christ, offended by the wickedness of the world, lists many crimes: violations of the Lord's day, the failure to keep Friday as a fast, blasphemies, usury, and adulteries. When Christ was asked for mercy by the blessed Virgin and the angels, he replied that each person must flog himself for thirty-four days while wandering as an exile, so that they might obtain the mercy of God.

units.la: Tantus erat Spirensium affectus ad eos, quòd citò omnibus inuitatis, non inueniebantur, qui inuitari possent: non enim recipiebant cuiusuis eleemosynam in specie, sed in genere, proparandis contortis cereis & vexillis. Habebant enim pretiosissima vexilla de serico & purpura, & ornatè depicta, cum quibus processionibus transibant: sed inuitati de Magistrorum suorum licentia ibant, vocati, nec audebant inuitare per ditiores vocati. Hocque faciebant bis in die, aut in ciuitate, vel in campis, & quilibet clam semel in nocte: non loquebantur mulieribus, nec super plumis iacebant: omnes gestabant cruces, ante & retro in veste & pileo, habentes flagella vestibus appensa, nec in vna parochia vltra vnam noctem manserunt.
units.tr: Such was the Speyer people's affection for them that, once invitations had been issued, there were hardly any left to invite. They did not accept alms for particular persons but in general, for the preparation of twisted candles and banners. They had very precious banners of silk and purple, richly painted, with which they walked in procession. Those who were invited went with their masters' permission, and when they were invited they did not dare to invite richer people. They did this twice a day, either in the city or in the fields, and each man also flogged himself once secretly at night. They did not speak to women, nor did they lie on feather beds. All wore crosses, in front and behind, on their garments and caps, and carried whips hung from their clothes. They never stayed more than one night in any one parish.

units.la: Ingressi sunt fraternitatem eorum humillime, centum & plures de ciuitate Spirensi circa mille Argentinensium, promittentes per prędictum tempus obedientiam prędictis Magistris. Nullus recipiebatur, nisi promitteret seruare prędicta, per prędictos dies, & nisi haberet expendere in die ad minus quatuor denarios, ne mendicet, & nisi promitteret se esse confessum & contritum, & remisisse omnem iniuriam inimicis, & habere vxoris suæ assensum. Diuiseruntque se Argentinæ, pars enim descendit, altera pars ascendit, Magistros inter eos similiter diuidentes. Magistri quoque Argentinis repentinam castigationem nimiam prohibebant. Tantaque ad omnes confluebant multitudines, ascendentium, descendentium & transuersalium, quòd nemo poterat numerare.
units.tr: Very humbly, more than a hundred people from the city of Speyer, and about a thousand from Strasbourg, joined their fraternity, promising obedience to the said masters for the stated period. No one was admitted unless he promised to keep these rules for the said days, unless he had at least four pence to spend each day so that he would not have to beg, unless he promised that he was confessed and contrite and had forgiven all injuries to his enemies, and unless he had his wife's consent. They divided themselves at Strasbourg: one part went down and the other part went up, and the masters divided themselves among them in the same way. The masters also forbade the people of Strasbourg any sudden and excessive castigation. Such crowds flocked to them, of those going up, those going down and those crossing over, that no one could count them.

units.la: Post hæc in ciuitate Spira penè ducenti pueri, duodecim annorum ætate, colligationem fecerunt, & se flagellauerunt. In ciuitate Argentinensi tanto confluebant multitudines flagellantium, quòd nemo poterat numerare.
units.tr: After this, in the city of Speyer, nearly two hundred boys aged twelve formed a brotherhood and flogged themselves. In the city of Strasbourg the crowds of flagellants gathered in such numbers that no one could count them.

units.la: De quo Carolus rex & plures Ordinum Mendicantium, & multi sacerdotum dolebant, & propter aliquas colligationes & nimias multitudines, & quia volebant fraternitates facere durabiles, desistere sunt coacti.
units.tr: Charles the king, several of the mendicant orders, and many priests were distressed by this. On account of some of the brotherhoods and the excessive crowds, and because they wished the fraternities to last, they were forced to desist.

units.la: De Basilea enim ciuitate de melioribus centum vel circa colligationem fecerunt, & secundum modum prędictū se flagellauerunt, & ex devotione Auinionem iuerunt: vbi cum venissent & se flagellassent, relatum fuit Clementi papæ de modo pœnitentium, ipse pro eo quòd subiipsi huiusmodi afflictionem & pœnitentiam iniungebant, volebat eos incarcerasse. Sed quidam Cardinales eos excusabant, quòd non credidissent male in hoc fecisse. Et papa sub pœna excommunicationis latæ sententiæ ipsis & omnibus Christifidelibus prohibuit, ne de cætero flagellationibus publicis vterentur, sed pœnitens solus in Camera posset carnem suam flagellare.
units.tr: From the city of Basel about a hundred or so of the better sort formed a brotherhood and flogged themselves in the manner described above. Out of devotion they went to Avignon, and when they had arrived there and flogged themselves, Pope Clement was informed about the manner of these penitents. Because they had imposed this kind of affliction and penance on themselves, he wanted to have them imprisoned. But some cardinals excused them, since they did not think they had done wrong in this. The pope, under penalty of excommunication latae sententiae, forbade them and all Christian faithful from using public flagellations from then on. Only a penitent alone, in his own room, might flog his flesh.

units.la: Guntherus Comes de Schuartzenburg Thuringiæ, ætatis circa XLV annorum, virtuosus, bellicosus, strenuus & prudens in bellis: qui in seruitio Heinrici Moguntini & quondam Ludouici Principis plurimùm laborauit, quique in pluribus conflictibus feliciter prævalens proprijs, capiendo & talliando Barones, plurimùm est ditatus, à Principibus, Carolo contrarijs, vt se intromitteret de regno, rogatur. Qui primò renuens, tandem eo pacto annuit, si in Franckfurt per Principes & nobiles sententiatum fuerit, vacare Regnum & Imperium, maiorque pars Principum, qui similiter per sententiam declarati fuerint ius habere, ipsum absque omni Simonia elegerint propter Deum, dicens: se expositurum periculis pro Deo & imperio corpus suum. Hoc facto, cum exercitu suo in campo se posuit iuxta Franckfurt, feria sexta post Hilarij, anno M.CCC.XLIX.
units.tr: Count Günther of Schwarzburg in Thuringia, about forty-five years old, was virtuous, warlike, vigorous and prudent in war. He had laboured much in the service of Henry of Mainz and the late Prince Louis, and, prevailing successfully in many conflicts, had grown very rich from his own captures and ransoming of barons. The princes opposed to Charles asked him to intervene in the kingdom. At first he refused, but at last he agreed on this condition: that if at Frankfurt the princes and nobles declared by judgment that the kingdom and empire were vacant, and the greater part of those princes, who were likewise declared by judgment to have the right, elected him without any simony, for God's sake, he would expose his body to danger for God and the empire. This being done, he pitched camp with his army in the field near Frankfurt on the Friday after Hilary, in the year 1349.

units.la: Conuenientibusque inibi Principibus quatuor, & multis alijs Baronibus, & per sententiam decreto, Imperium vacare, & eisdem quatuor competere ius eligendi: electus est in Purificatione, per Henricum archiepiscopum Moguntinum, Ludouicum marchionem de Brandenburg, Rudolfum de Bauaria palatinum Rheni, annuente Ruperto suo fratre, & capto tum Ruperto fratrueli eorum, & Ericum Ducem Saxoniæ, in regem Romanorum. Huic etiam Erico, tanquam filio fratris senioris Rudolfi Ducis, electoris Caroli, decernebatur ius eligendi habere.
units.tr: Four princes and many other barons assembled there, and by decree the empire was declared vacant, and those four had the right to elect. At the Purification he was elected king of the Romans by Henry, archbishop of Mainz, Louis, margrave of Brandenburg, and Rudolf, duke of Bavaria and count palatine of the Rhine, with the assent of his brother Rupert, while their cousin Rupert was then taken prisoner, and also by Eric, duke of Saxony. For this Eric, as son of the elder brother of Duke Rudolf, the elector Charles, it was decreed that he should have the right of election.

units.la: Cumque Cumq; idem Guntherus per sex hebdomadas potenter iacuisset in campis Franckfurt/more regio per eandem ciuitatem est receptus. Aliaq; ciuitates imperij in Wederaugia, eum similiter receperunt.
units.tr: After Günther had lain encamped for six weeks in the fields near Frankfurt, he was received into the city with royal honours. The other imperial cities in the Wetterau likewise received him.

units.la: Intelligens autem Carolus Guntherum iacere in campo, ad Rhenum se transferens, Treuerensem, & Colonien�sem archiepiscopos Leodiensem episcopum, Ducem Brabantiæ & alios Principes amicos alloquitur. Scribens etiam Baronibus & ciuitatibus quæ eum receperant pro subsidio, & quòd in villa Castel, ex opposito Moguntiæ, castrametari vellet, dominica Estomihi: ad quos logij & terminum Guntherus quasi in derisum torneamentum indixit.
units.tr: Charles, learning that Günther lay in the field, moved to the Rhine and addressed the archbishops of Trier and Cologne, the bishop of Liège, the duke of Brabant and other friendly princes. He also wrote to the barons and cities which had received Günther, asking for aid, and said he wished to pitch camp at the village of Castel, opposite Mainz, on the Sunday of Estomihi. To those places and their quarters Günther, as if in mockery, proclaimed a tournament.

units.la: Carolus autem quia fuerat viduus, tractauerat cum Rudolfo de Bauaria Palatino, qui Guntherum elegerat, de sponsalibus cum filia Rudolfi Palatini, quæ vnica fuerat filia ex matre de Carinthia, & duxit eam vxorem: quamuis ipsi duo Carolus & Rudolfus, quondam Rudolfi regis pronepotes fuerant, ipsèque Rudolfus & quondam vxor eius mater sponsæ, similiter fuerunt eiusdem Rudolfi regis pronepotes, super quo nunquam dicitur fuisse dispensatum: materque sponsę & sponsus similiter liberi duarum sororum fuêre. Cum autem Carolus pro tunc Guntherum præpotentia sua & sibi adhærentium, inuadere non posset: indixit Colloquium Spiræ, ad dominicam Letare tunc sequentem, de villa Castel recedendo. Cumque Spiram venisset, conuenientibus ibidem Treuerensi, Gerlaco Moguntinensi, Eberhardo Comite de Wirtemberg / multisque baronibus & ciuitatum nunciis, cum speraretur Guntherum in vicino venturum, pro concordia inter electos tractanda, prout Principes ipsi Guntherò scripserant: ipse scriptum spernens, castrum Friteberg obsedit, cuius castrenses sibi rebellabant: & tandem vicit. Post hæc in principio Maii infirmante Guntherò in Franckfurt / magister Fridanckus famosus medicus, & Comitibus de Nassowe antiquitus familiaris, cum Gunthero potionem dedisset, quam asseruit eidem expedire, eam (licet inuitus) ad mandatum Guntheri primò tentauit & probauit, ipso præsente. Post hæc Gunthetus eam sumpsit. Statim Medicus in facie incœperat decolorari, & infra triduum moriebatur. Guntherus inflatus, quò ad valentiam corporis statim inutilis est effectus, & creditur famulum Medici iniecisse potioni venenum.
units.tr: Charles, being a widower, had negotiated with Rudolf, the Palatine of Bavaria, who had elected Günther, for a betrothal to Rudolf's daughter, the only child of his wife from Carinthia, and he married her. Although Charles and Rudolf were great-grandsons of the late King Rudolf, and Rudolf himself and his late wife, the mother of the bride, were likewise great-grandchildren of the same King Rudolf, no dispensation is ever recorded for this. The mother of the bride and the bridegroom were also children of two sisters. When Charles could not at that time attack Günther with his own power and that of his adherents, he called a conference at Speyer for the following Sunday, Laetare, and withdrew from the village of Castel. When he came to Speyer, the archbishop of Trier, Gerlach of Mainz, Count Eberhard of Württemberg, many barons and messengers of the cities gathered there. It was hoped that Günther would come nearby to negotiate concord among the electors, as the princes had written to him. But he, scorning their letter, besieged the castle of Friedberg, whose garrison rebelled against him, and at last he conquered it. After this, at the beginning of May, while Günther was ill at Frankfurt, master Fridanck, a famous physician long familiar with the counts of Nassau, gave Günther a potion which he claimed would do him good. At Günther's command, and against his own will, the physician first tried and tasted it in Günther's presence. Afterwards Günther took it. At once the physician began to turn pale in the face, and within three days he died. Günther swelled up and immediately became useless in bodily strength, and it is believed that the physician's servant had put poison in the potion.

units.la: Mortuo autem illis diebus Luca de Mediolano, occupatore quasi Lombardiæ, ac Ioanne fratre suo, scilicet archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, se intromittente de dominio: mittitur pro Marchione de Brandeburg / qui vadens ad Comitatum Tirolis, Tridentum & quædam alia ibi obtinuit, quæ in Bohemi devotione fuerunt. Quod audiens Ioannes de Pistorio prouisus Tridentinus sedis, clero & populo Tridentino exosus, recessit. Cui papa postea de Episcopatu Spoletano prouidit.
units.tr: In those days Luchino of Milan died. He had been, as it were, the usurper of Lombardy, and his brother John, namely the archbishop of Milan, took over the lordship. The Margrave of Brandenburg was summoned, and on going to the county of Tyrol he obtained Trent and certain other places there, which were devoted to Bohemia. Hearing this, John of Pistoia, who had been provided to the see of Trent and was hated by the clergy and people of Trent, withdrew. Later the pope provided him to the bishopric of Spoleto.

units.la: Eo tempore ad preces Ioannis, filij quondam Ioannis Bohemi, quem Comitem Tyrolis nominauit, Papa commisit episcopo Curiensi a captiuitate liberato, vt si inuenire consanguinitatis vel affinitatis, vel aliud impedimentū inter eum & Margaretham, quondam Hainrici ducis Carinthiæ filiam, Ludouico de Bauaria, nominanti se Marchionem Brandenburgensem, de facto copulatam fore, quòd ob maleficium diuortium celebratum: quod si non inuenerit cum x annis & interim per continuum triennium cohabitauerint, operam copulæ dantes, nec potuerint commisceri, nō posset sibi reddi sine strage & scandalo, ipsèq; se habilem asserat ad alias mulieres, & cupiat esse pater, quod iustum fuerit decernat. Qui Curiensis inter eos diuortium propter maleficium quod inuenit, celebrauit.
units.tr: At that time, at the prayers of John, son of the late John of Bohemia, whom he named Count of Tyrol, the pope committed the matter to the bishop of Chur, newly freed from captivity. If he found any kinship, affinity or other impediment between Louis of Bavaria, who called himself margrave of Brandenburg, and Margaret, daughter of the late Duke Henry of Carinthia, who had been joined to him in fact, and if a divorce had been celebrated on account of witchcraft (maleficium), then the bishop should act accordingly. But if he found none, and they had lived together for ten years, and for a continuous three years in the meantime had made efforts at intercourse without being able to unite, then she could not be returned to him without slaughter and scandal; and since he declared himself capable with other women and wished to become a father, the bishop should decree what was just. The bishop of Chur, finding the witchcraft, celebrated the divorce between them.

units.la: Intenderat autem Rex & Marchio simul pro perficienda concordia se transferre ad Papam, sed quia archiepiscopus Mediolanensis scripsit Papæ, literam quandam sibi directam, in qua narrabatur, Regem Aquisgrani ex novo consensu Principum, electum & coronatum in Regem, ex vacatione quondam Ludouici Principis: de hoc Papa commotus scripsit Regi, sicque ambo manserunt. Marchio autem cum Mastino Veronensi ligam contraxit, eiusque filio, suam ex prædicta Margaretha filiam, desponsauit.
units.tr: The king and the margrave had intended to go together to the pope to bring about a concord. But because the archbishop of Milan wrote to the pope a letter addressed to him, in which it was reported that the king had been elected and crowned king at Aachen by a new consent of the princes, the late Prince Louis's office being vacant, the pope was moved by this and wrote to the king, and so both remained where they were. The margrave, however, formed a league with Mastino of Verona, and married his daughter by the aforesaid Margaret to Mastino's son.

units.la: Reuersi autem sunt Mediolanum post mortem Lucæ tres filij fratris sui quondam Stephani Marchionis, Matheus, Barnabas & Galeatius, quos Lucas eiecerat de terra, ne dominaretur loco patris, quos quondam Aimo comes Sabaudiæ nutriuit, cum filio suo nunc Comite: qui tenentes singulariter Palatium, strenuè se tenent, quos & archiepiscopus Mediolanus abhorret. Reliquit autè Lucas duos filios, quos prædictus Galeatius suos esse prætendit, cum uxorem Lucę, eo viuente, clam cognouisset adultere frequenter.
units.tr: After the death of Luchino, the three sons of his late brother, Marquis Stephen, returned to Milan: Matthew, Barnabas and Galeazzo. Luchino had driven them out of the country so that they would not rule in their father's place, and Aimo, the late Count of Savoy, had raised them along with his own son, who is now count. Each of them holds the palace on his own, and they keep a firm grip on it. The archbishop of Milan detests them. Luchino left two sons, whom Galeazzo claims as his own, since he had secretly and repeatedly discovered that Luchino's wife was an adulteress while Luchino was still alive.

units.la: Conuocauit autem rex Carolus exercitum ad Moguntiam, in Maio anni prædicti. Moguntini enim sibi in odium Heinrici archiepiscopi qui eos læserat, & Franckfurtensium, à quibus rex obstulerat nundinas, dansque eas Moguntinis, firmiter adhæserant. Intentio autem Moguntinorum fuit, expugnare oppidum cum castro Altenwill, constructum per Moguntinum super Rhenum, ad duas leucas distans à Moguntia. Guntherus autem letaliter infirmus, cum gente sua se in Altenwill apud Henric. Moguntinum tunc collocauit. Transeunte autem Carolo rege Rhenum, ducenti equites Guntheri impetum facientes, Carolum terruerunt. Accelerantes autem equites Eberhardi de Wirtenberg, & quidam alij fugarunt eosdem: de qua fugatione multi milites noui sunt creati.
units.tr: King Charles called up an army to Mainz in May of that year. The Mainzers, out of hatred for Archbishop Henry, who had wronged them, and for the people of Frankfurt, from whom the king had removed the fairs and given them to the Mainzers, firmly took sides with the king. The Mainzers intended to storm the town with the castle of Altenwill, which the Mainz archbishop had built on the Rhine two leagues from Mainz. Meanwhile Gunther, who was gravely ill, had lodged himself and his people in Altenwill with Henry of Mainz. When Charles crossed the Rhine, two hundred of Gunther's horsemen made an attack and frightened him. But horsemen of Eberhard of Württemberg and some others came up quickly and put them to flight. Many knights were newly created from that rout.

units.la: Veniens autem marchio de Brandenburg sine gente, habitis tractatibus cum rege Carolo de concordia, videns etiam Guntherum factum inualidum: negotium inter eos comportauit, ita quòd Gunthero pro renuntiatione iuris suæ electionis, data sunt viginti duo millia marcarum argenti, & duo oppida Thuringiæ imperialia, pro tempore vitæ suæ. Quod ipse Guntherus, licet infirmus, difficulter consensit: si sanus fuisset, nullatenus consensisset, de Principum suorum electorum, specialiter Bauarorum, perfidia multa conquerendo. Obiit autem ipse Guntherus post comportationem huiusmodi, infra mensem, in Franckfurt, & in ecclesia parochiali ibidem, præsente rege Carolo, fuit cum lamentatione sepultus. Quo sepulto, Francofordenses in perpetuam memoriam, solenne ut decet regem, fecerunt sepulchrum. Rex Carolus ex tunc Franckfurtensibus omnia sua priuilegia confirmauit & nundinas restituit, datis sibi viginti millibus marcarum, quæ recepta sunt à Iudæis crematis ibidem.
units.tr: The Margrave of Brandenburg came without an army. After holding talks with King Charles about a settlement, and seeing that Gunther had been made powerless, he arranged the matter between them: for Gunther's renunciation of his right to the election, he was given twenty-two thousand marks of silver and two imperial towns in Thuringia for the duration of his life. Gunther himself, though ill, agreed to this with difficulty; had he been well, he would not have agreed at all, complaining at length of the treachery of his fellow electors, especially the Bavarians. Gunther died within a month of this agreement, at Frankfurt, and was buried with lamentation in the parish church there, in the presence of King Charles. After the burial, the people of Frankfurt built a tomb, a splendid one fitting for a king, in perpetual memory of him. From then on King Charles confirmed all the privileges of the Frankfurters and restored the fairs to them, in exchange for twenty thousand marks, which had been collected from the Jews burned there.

units.la: Descendit autem circa finem Iulij rex cum uxore versus Aquisgranum, sed præ multitudine peregrinorum se flagellantium, inibi recipi non poterat: sed expectauit in Bunna, vbi Aquensibus omnia antiqua & plura noua priuilegia sigillauit.
units.tr: Towards the end of July the king went down with his wife towards Aachen, but because of the great crowd of pilgrims who were flagellating themselves, he could not be received there. He waited at Bonn, where he confirmed all the old and many new privileges for the people of Aachen.

units.la: Descenderat autem Ludouicus marchio cum rege. Interim autem Romanus, frater Ludouici, in terra Brandenburg conflictum iniens cum aduersariis, vbi miles viriliter est effectus, feliciter triumphauit: captis pluribus & occisis, alij autem se acriùs firmantes, plurimùm Marchionem infestant.
units.tr: Margrave Ludwig had gone down with the king. Meanwhile Romanus, Ludwig's brother, engaged in combat with his opponents in the land of Brandenburg, where he acquitted himself manfully as a soldier and triumphed happily: many were taken and killed, but the others, holding their ground more fiercely, greatly harassed the Margrave.

units.la: Reuersus est autem rex Spiram, vocatisque Baronibus & ciuitatibus tractans cum eis, de pace generali circa Rhenum, sed non perficiens. Conquerebantur tum ciuitates Rhenenses, quòd Rupertus Dux Bauariæ haberet Castrum dictum noua Curia, distans ad vnam leucam à ciuitate Spira, in qua latitarent latrones, qui Mercatores, transeuntes publicâ viam versus Wormatiam, in nemore dicto Rechholz despoliarent. Rex hoc audito, statim bannerium suum, quod dicitur Sturmfahn, super turrim ecclesiæ Spirensis constituit, & populo ciuitatis ad arma mandari per Magistros ciuium præcepit: & egressus ciuitatem cum sua gente armatus, populo eum sequente cum Bannerio ante castrum prædictum, ipsum funditus destruxit.
units.tr: The king returned to Speyer and, having summoned the barons and towns, discussed with them a general peace along the Rhine, but did not bring it to completion. The Rhenish cities then complained that Duke Rupert of Bavaria held a castle called Neue Kurie, one league from the city of Speyer, in which robbers lay hidden and plundered merchants passing along the public road towards Worms, in the wood called Rechholz. When the king heard this, he at once set up his banner, which is called the Sturmfahne, on the tower of the church of Speyer, and ordered the magistrates of the citizens to call the people of the city to arms. Going out of the city armed with his troops, with the people following him and the banner before him, he utterly destroyed the castle.

units.la: Postea reuersus ad ciuitatem Spiram, conquerens Dominis & Ciuitatibus de Metensibus, eum pro rege habere nolentibus, vel scribere regem Romanorum: sed non habens responsum ab eis super scripto suo, & in expensis Spiræ deficiens, iuit ad Nurenberg, vbi nolente Marchione regi reformato cum Gunthero eis assistere, sub gratia est receptus, & quodam dolo receptis ciuium armis, & extorta ab eis pecunia, Bohemiam est reuersus, circa finem Septembris. ptembris, male terra regni pacata. Reliquit autē in Sueuia præsidem Eberhardum de Wirtenberg.
units.tr: Afterwards he returned to the city of Speyer and complained to the lords and cities about the people of Metz, who were unwilling to regard him as king or to write him as King of the Romans. But receiving no answer from them to his letter, and running short of money at Speyer, he went to Nuremberg. There, since the Margrave, who had been reconciled to the king, was unwilling to assist them along with Gunther, he was received under the protection of the city. By a certain trick he took the citizens' arms and extorted money from them, and then went back to Bohemia around the end of September. He left Eberhard of Württemberg behind in Swabia as his governor, and the land of the kingdom was ill pacified.

units.la: Eberhardus autē de Wirtenberg, præses Sueuiæ, cum oppida imperialia, Nordlingen, quod consueuit respicere Comites de Oettingen, & Werde super Danubio, quod in dominio Bauarorum ab antiquo steterat, ad suam nomine regis obedientiam assumpsisset: tunc inter duces Bauariæ, Comitesque de Oettingen / contra ipsum Eberhardum odium est subortum. Ciuitates autem Sueuiæ ipsi præsidi vicinæ, aliis quantum audebant fauentes, præsidem, sicut & patrem & auum, habuerunt exosum. Ipse Eberhardus oppidum Ladenburg super Neccaro, episcopi Wormatiensis 10 quod ante Rupertum ducem Bauariæ defensorio nomine episcopi respexit, sibi de episcopi consensu attraxit. Ex quo inter Ducem & Comitē exercitus congregantur & remittebantur. Tandem oppidum ipsum Comes propter bonum pacis dimisit, & sic permansit in Ducis defensione. Quem etiam Ducem incolæ oppidi à sua potestate excluserunt, & Walramum Comitem de Spanheim pro defensore elegerunt & assumpserunt, Salmanno Episcopo patiente & sciente.
units.tr: Eberhard of Württemberg, governor of Swabia, in the king's name took under his obedience the imperial towns of Nördlingen, which had been accustomed to look to the Counts of Oettingen, and Donauwörth, which had long stood in the dominion of the Bavarians. Then hatred arose between the dukes of Bavaria and the Counts of Oettingen against Eberhard himself. The cities of Swabia, neighbouring the governor, favoured the other side as far as they dared, and they held the governor in as much hatred as they had his father and grandfather. Eberhard himself, with the consent of the bishop, drew to himself the town of Ladenburg on the Neckar, which belonged to the bishop of Worms and had, before Duke Rupert of Bavaria, been under the protection of the bishop. As a result, armies were gathered and sent back between the duke and the count. At last the count, for the sake of peace, gave up the town, and it remained under the duke's protection. But the inhabitants of the town also drove the duke out of their power, and with the consent and knowledge of Bishop Salmann, they chose and took as their protector Count Walram of Sponheim.

units.la: Rupertus autē dux in Bohemia Carolo regi nimis familiaris est effectus, qui & vicarius Regis effici dicebatur: postquam fratruelem suum Rupertum, quem & Arnestum nominant, de captiuitate redemit. Postquam in Brandenburg pro pace laborauit plurimùm, ciuitates Sueuiæ contra Comites de Wirtenberg acriter incitauit: ac multi episcopi & Comites, qui Eberhardum de Wirtenberg habere credebantur exosum, propter eius virtutes, & quia malam timuerunt consequentiam, si aduersus illum oppida præualerent, se mutuo colligarunt, sicque furor vulgi quieuit.
units.tr: Duke Rupert in Bohemia became very close to King Charles, and he was even said to be the king's vicar, after he ransomed his cousin Rupert, whom they also call Arnest, from captivity. After he had laboured greatly for peace in Brandenburg, he vigorously stirred up the cities of Swabia against the Counts of Württemberg. Many bishops and counts, who were believed to hold Eberhard of Württemberg in hatred because of his virtues, and who feared a bad outcome if the towns prevailed against him, bound themselves together, and so the rage of the common people subsided.

units.la: Interea anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quadragesimo nono moritur Walramus de Iuliaco, archiepiscopus Coloniensis & postea de mense Decembri, frater eius marchio Iuliacensis à filiis suis capitur, de vitio Sodomiæ suspectus. Decanus verò Olmuncensis Cancellarius regis, ad petitionem eius apud Papam pro archiepiscopatu laborat. Sed Papa Wilhelmo præposito de Tuft, vni de gremio Capituli Coloniensis, magna summa pecuniæ pro eo suscepta, de eo 30 prouidit. De quo rex (cui Papa de omnibus Episcopatibus Alemanniæ, tempore quo se de regno contra Ludouicum Principem intromisit, promiserat prouidere personis per regem præsentatis) plurimum est commotus, de hoc Cardinalibus & alibi conquerendo. Papa autem, mortuo Comite Conuenarum sine masculis, vnam de filiabus Comitis, filio fratris sui, matrimonio copulauit, cum pecunia per Coloniensses sibi data: omnes redditus sedecim millia florenorum annuos, relictæ & aliis filiabus Comitis assignauit, Comitatu eidem fratris filio remanente.
units.tr: Meanwhile, in the year of the Lord 1349, Walram of Jülich, archbishop of Cologne, died; and afterwards, in December, his brother, the Margrave of Jülich, was taken by his sons, being suspected of the vice of sodomy. Dean Olmütz, the king's chancellor, at his request laboured at Rome for the archbishopric. But the Pope, having received a large sum of money from Wilhelm, provost of Tuft, one of the chapter of Cologne, provided him to the see. The king, to whom the Pope had promised, at the time when he meddled in the kingdom against Prince Ludwig, that he would provide to all the bishoprics of Germany the persons presented by the king, was greatly angered by this, and complained of it to the cardinals and elsewhere. The Pope, however, when the Count of Cuyk died without sons, joined one of the count's daughters, the son of his brother, in marriage, with money given by the people of Cologne; and he assigned the whole income of sixteen thousand florins a year to the widow and the other daughters of the count, the county remaining to the same nephew.

units.la: Humbertus verò Delphinus, vitæ quodammodo tædiosus, terram suam, retentis aliquot munitionibus, nepoti regis Franciæ, ex filio primogenito, venDelphinatum Galliæ feudum ab imperio. 40 dens, frater Prædicatorum est effectus. Breue tamen tempus stans in ordine, egressus, factus est Cardinalis, & postmodum Patriarcha. Rex autem Carolus Romanus eundem nepotem Franci, filium sororis suæ, de ipso Delphinatu, qui est feudum ab imperio, inuestiuit.
units.tr: Humbert the Dauphin, somewhat weary of life, sold his land, keeping back some fortresses, to the nephew of the king of France, son of his eldest son; the Dauphiné is a fief of the empire. He became a friar of the Preachers. Yet after standing in the order for a short time, he left it, was made a cardinal, and afterwards a patriarch. King Charles of the Romans invested that same nephew of Francis, the son of his sister, with the Dauphiné itself, which is a fief of the empire.

units.la: Baldewinus autem archiepiscopus Treuerensis, cum quadraginta duobus annis ecclesiam suam laudabiliter rexisset, ac propter senium & tenacitatem nihil amplius proficeret, cum frequenter solitarius vitam quasi Cartusiensium duceret: Ioannem de Liechtenberg, qui & in Argentinensi ecclesia præposituram, decanatum, Cātoriam & Pincernatum simul tenebat, valentem & prouidum, in spiritualibus & 50 temporalibus administratorem & vicarium ecclesiæ suæ deputauit, qui tamē assumpta administratione illico discessit abinde.
units.tr: Baldwin, archbishop of Trier, had ruled his church commendably for forty-two years, but because of old age and obstinacy he accomplished nothing more, living for the most part a solitary life like that of the Carthusians.
