He appointed as administrator and vicar of his church in spiritual and temporal matters John of Lichtenberg, a capable and prudent man, who also held at the same time the provostship, the deanery, the chantorship and the cupbearership in the church of Strasbourg. But once he had taken up the administration, he left it at once.

units.la: Cuno verò de Falckenstein Canonicus & minister Heinrici Moguntini, inuito Papa, Carolo rege, & Gerlaco prouiso sedis, viriliter administrat, omnesque fructus & redditus, quos ecclesiæ collegiatæ, siue personæ priuatæ, siue Monasteria Religiosorum, & omnium indifferenter Henrico Moguntino non parentium extra ciuitatem Moguntinam existentes, siue consisterent in blado, vel in vino, recepit, & ad castrum & munitiones sibi subiectas, deduxit: tenens semper familiares tot & tantos, quod in his Gerlacum prouisum nec suos formidabat. Gessit enim suam administrationem tam viriliter, quòd in ciuitate Moguntina familiares sui ipso Cuno (vt ferebatur) annuente, Conrad. de Ansenbruch concanonicum occiderunt. Henricus etiam Moguntinus, quòd in quondam Gunthero de Schwarzenburg electo, fideliter egerit, ab omnibus laudatur, Bauari verò de perfidia diffamantur.
units.tr: Cuno of Falckenstein, a canon and minister of Heinrich of Mainz, carried on the administration vigorously, although the Pope, King Charles and Gerlach, the provisor of the see, opposed him. He collected all the revenues and income, whether in grain or in wine, from the collegiate churches, from private persons and from the monasteries of religious orders, and from everyone outside the city of Mainz who did not obey Heinrich, and he conveyed them to the castle and fortresses under his control. He kept so many retainers, and such strong ones, that he feared neither Gerlach the provisor nor his own people. He conducted his administration so vigorously that in the city of Mainz his retainers killed his fellow canon Konrad von Ansenbruch, with Cuno's consent, as was reported. Heinrich of Mainz is praised by all for the faithful way he acted towards the late Günther of Schwarzburg, the elect, while the Bavarians are spoken of as treacherous.

units.la: Iisdem temporibus in Curia Auinionensi Ioanne de Gottingen Episcopo Frisingensi, Medico famosissimo mundi mortuo, Papa Alberto de Hohenberg (cui dudum de Episcopatu Herbipolensi prouiderat; quem tamen propter potentiā N de Hohenloh detentoris eius obtinere nequiuit) de ipso episcopatu Frisingensi prouidit. Rex enim Carolus ipsum detentorem, propter seruitia sibi per eum & fratrem eius Episcopum Babenbergensem in negotio regni impensa quantum potuit promouit: vnde Albertus ipse de Hohenberg in facto suo difficilem processum habuit.
units.tr: At the same time, in the Curia at Avignon, Pope Albert of Hohenberg (whom he had earlier provided to the bishopric of Würzburg, but could not obtain it because of the power of N. of Hohenlohe, who held it) provided Albert with the bishopric of Freising, which had belonged to John of Göttingen, bishop of Freising, the most famous physician in the world, who had died. King Charles promoted the present holder, as much as he could, on account of the services rendered to him by that man and by his brother, the bishop of Bamberg, in the business of the kingdom. For this reason Albert of Hohenberg himself had difficulty in carrying his case through.

units.la: Moriuntur quoque eodem quadragesimo nono, circa finem in pestilentia filia Caroli Romani regis, & Bohemiae, regina Hungariae, & soror eiusdem regis, vxor Ioannis primogeniti Franci: item vxor Franci de Burgundia, qui Francus filiam regis Nauarrae pulcherrimam, de suo genere, duxit vxorem. Item primogenitus Ducis Brabantiae, gener praedicti Ioannis: item & domina de Couzin, filia quondam Lupoldi Ducis Austriae, & Conrad. de Medeburg maritus eius. Item filia regis Siciliae, vxor Stephani Ducis Bauariae, relictis sibi pluribus liberis. Qui Stephanus filiam Burggrauij in Nurenberg duxit vxorem: tantaque fuit in Francia & Anglia pestilentia, vt Parisiis & in pluribus locis vix nonus homo dicitur remansisse.
units.tr: Also in that same year of 1349, towards its end, there died of the plague: the daughter of King Charles of Rome and queen of Bohemia and Hungary, and the sister of the same king, wife of John, the eldest son of the Frank; likewise the wife of the Frank of Burgundy, who had married a most beautiful daughter of the king of Navarre, of his own rank. Also the eldest son of the duke of Brabant, son-in-law of the aforesaid John; and the lady of Couzin, daughter of the late Leopold, duke of Austria, and Conrad of Medeburg, her husband. Also the daughter of the king of Sicily, wife of Stephen, duke of Bavaria, who was left with several children. This Stephen had married a daughter of the burgrave of Nuremberg. The plague was so severe in France and England that in Paris and many other places it is said that barely one man in nine survived.

units.la: Anglus quoque, qui durante pestilentia quieuit, non inquietando Francum, iterum cessante pestilentia in Vasconia per suos Francum inuadit, aliquas munitiones expugnans, & terram quasi vsque ad Tholosam suae subiicie ens ditioni.
units.tr: The Englishman, too, who had kept quiet while the plague lasted, and had not harassed the Frenchman, when the plague ceased again attacked France through his men in Gascony, storming several fortresses and bringing almost the whole land as far as Toulouse under his power.

units.la: Circa principium anni Domini, quinquagesimi, Francus clam vni seruitorum regis Angliae Lombrado, tenenti custodiam vnius portae in Cales, pro traditione munitionis pecuniam maximam pollicetur: at ille breui termino deliberandi recepto, velociter Anglum alloquitur. Iussusque recipere pecuniam ipsam à Franco recepit, & gentem Franci venire iubet hora ad haec assignata. Anglus autem cum filio suo & suis nocte veniens per mare, gentem Franci, intromissamque multitudinem videlicet nobilium maximam, interfecit, & aliquos captiuauit, conflictum nimis dubium iniendo. Habita autem victoria, sciscitatus, quis ab vtraque parte valentior fuerit in conflictu, & nominato sibi quodam milite Franci capto sibi coronam destinauit in turri, prolem eius liberatione pacicens. Postea mense Iunio, cum iterum congredi vellent, missis per Papam nuntiis & data Anglo pecunia, induciae firmantur ad annum. Anglus autem dicens, pacem violatam fore, misit gentem in Britanniam contra Francum, quos Francus per suos inuadens, praeualuit Anglis, multis occisis. Breuiter Francus moritur, circa finem Augusti, anno Iubileo, & Ioannes eius filius primogenitus coronatur.
units.tr: Around the beginning of the year of the Lord 1350, the Frenchman secretly promised a very large sum of money to Lombrado, one of the servants of the king of England, who held the guard of one gate at Calais, if he would betray the fortress. Lombrado, having taken a short time to deliberate, quickly spoke with the Englishman. Ordered to receive that money, he took it from the Frenchman, and told the Frenchman's men to come at the hour appointed for this. The Englishman, however, came by sea at night with his son and his men, and killed the Frenchman's men, who had been admitted, together with a very great multitude of nobles, and took some prisoners, engaging in a very doubtful battle. When the victory was won, he asked which side had been stronger in the fight. When a certain captured knight of the Frenchman was named to him, he sent the knight's crown to the tower, bargaining for his liberation with the knight's offspring. Afterwards, in the month of June, when they were again about to join battle, messengers were sent by the Pope and money was given to the Englishman, and a truce was confirmed for a year. The Englishman, however, saying that the peace had been broken, sent troops into Brittany against the Frenchman; the Frenchman attacked them through his own men and prevailed over the English, many being killed. In short, the Frenchman died around the end of August, in the Jubilee year, and his eldest son John was crowned.

units.la: Hic Ioannes Francus Comitem de Gines valentissimum, patris sui capitaneum fidelissimum, & inter Francos excelsum, qui dudum in seruitio Franci captus per Anglum, & saepe sub cautione emissus, cum nullum liberationis adiutorium posset habere à Francis, patre vel filio, pro LX millibus aureorum, tandem Anglo pro liberatione sua, duas de suis munitionibus assignantem, pro eo improbe decollauit. Hic Ioannes anno domini M.CCCLI, de mense Ianuario, Curiam Romanam accedens duodecim Cardinales procurauit promoueri per Papam. Anglus verò super promotione vnius solius scribens Papæ, non est exauditus: propter quòd omnes in regno suo per Papam ad beneficia quæcunque promotos expulit, sub pœna submersionis, ne quis inibi literas apostolicas qualescunq; & cuiuscunq; tenoris exequatur inhibendo. Francus autem timens de vxore sua, duos terræ magnates decapitat, propter colloquium habitum cum eadem.
units.tr: This John the Frenchman had a most powerful count of Guines, his father's most loyal captain and the most eminent among the French. He had been taken earlier in the service of the Frenchman by the Englishman, and was often released on bail. When he could get no help towards his liberation from the French, neither from the father nor from the son, the Englishman demanded sixty thousand gold crowns for his release and, in the end, two of the Frenchman's fortresses; and since the French did not pay, the count was shamefully beheaded in their place. This John, in January of the year of the Lord 1351, went to the Roman Curia and procured that twelve cardinals be promoted by the Pope. The Englishman, however, wrote to the Pope about the promotion of one man alone, and was not heard. For this reason he drove out of his kingdom all who had been promoted by the Pope to any benefices whatever, under threat of drowning, forbidding anyone there to carry out any apostolic letters of whatever kind or content. The Frenchman, however, fearing for his wife, beheaded two great men of the land on account of a conversation they had had with her.

units.la: Cum autem Clemens papa VI quinquagesimum annum perpetuò statueret Iubileum, quem Bonifacius octauus centesimum statuerat, quasi nouum inchoans, timorosus, dicente ipso Clemente, quinquagesimum magis Leuitico conuenire: ecce inchoante eodem anno, & per totum quinquagesimum, tanta Romam Christicolarum confluit multitudo, qualis non illic ab Vrbe condita confluebat.
units.tr: When Pope Clement VI decreed that the Jubilee be held every fiftieth year instead of every hundredth, as Boniface VIII had decreed, he was beginning, as it were, something new. He was fearful, as Clement himself said, that the fiftieth year rather suited Leviticus. So, when that year began and throughout the whole fiftieth year, such a multitude of Christians flocked to Rome as had never flocked there since the city was founded.

units.la: Requisitus autem Papa per Carolum regem Romanorum, processum dedit, quo Flagellatorum sectam detestans, eos inhiberi præcepit, & religiosos eis fauentes, per episcopos captiuari: castigationes tamen occultas in hospitijs bona intentione permittens. Prætendit quoque in processu, quòd sicut manus in necem Iudæorum, quos pietas Christiana defendit, laxarunt: similiter de eis contra probos alios sit timendum.
units.tr: At the request of King Charles of the Romans, the Pope issued a decree by which he condemned the sect of the Flagellants and ordered them to be prohibited, and commanded that the religious who favoured them be taken captive by the bishops. Nevertheless, he allowed their secret penances in hostels, out of good intention. He also argued in the decree that just as hands were loosed for the slaughter of the Jews, whom Christian piety protected, so something similar was to be feared from them against other good people.

units.la: Natus est autem iisdem diebus Carolo regi in Bohemia, ex noua vxore, filia Rudolphi Ducis Bauariæ, filius Wenceslaus ex proauo nominatus, qui rex Ioannes fratri suo Marchionatum Morauiæ, vt iuxta suæ hæreditatis in Bohemia cederet, assignauit. Quamuis autem modicam pacem Germanis, magnam tamen procurat Bohemis, omnes indifferenter decapitado raptores, unde inibi potens est, plebiq; acceptus, qui & Pragam magnificauit in duplo.
units.tr: At the same time, King Charles had a son, Wenceslaus, born to him in Bohemia by his new wife, the daughter of Rudolf, duke of Bavaria. He was named after his great-grandfather. King John assigned the margraviate of Moravia to his brother, so that it would pass to him according to his inheritance in Bohemia. Although he secured only a little peace for the Germans, he secured a great deal for the Bohemians, by beheading all robbers without distinction. Hence he became powerful there and was popular with the common people, and he also enlarged Prague twofold.

units.la: Eodem anno quinquagesimo, de mense Martij, Thuricenses, qui ante paucos annos Ioannem Comitem de Habspurg occiderant in conflictu (vbi B. Garius de Laudenberg miles fortissimus oculum post magnum laborem amisit) Ioannem eiusdem Ioannis filium, ex persuasione quorundam intrinsecorum nocte cum multis armatis ingredientem, animo capiendi ciuitatem, ceperunt: Berengario prædicto multisque bonis occisis. Qui multos ciuitatenses decapitarunt, multosque flexerunt super rotas. Egressi sunt autem ante oppidum Raprechtswiler ipsius Comitis: quod fratres eius iuuenes, occidi captum timentes, aperuerunt eidem: in quo itinere Rodolphus Bruno Magister ciuitatis, diuque potior ibidem, quamuis plebeius, est miles effectus.
units.tr: In the same year of 1350, in the month of March, the people of Zurich, who a few years before had killed John, count of Habsburg, in battle (where the very brave knight Berchtold of Laudenberg lost an eye after great toil), captured John, the son of that same John, who entered the city by night with many armed men intending to seize it, on the persuasion of certain men inside the city. Berchtold, mentioned above, and many good men were killed. The Zurichers beheaded many of the citizens and broke many on the wheel. They marched out before the town of Rapperswil of the same count, which the young brothers of the count opened to them, fearing that their captured brother would be killed. On that march Rudolf Bruno, master of the city, who had long been the most powerful man there, though a commoner, was made a knight.

units.la: Antea autem habentibus Waldenariis de Sulz Alsatiæ litem, cum Molitore milite Thuricensi, & nolentibus Thuricensibus aliquam illis facere iustitiam coram ciuitatibus vel alibi, nisi coram Sculteto ipsorum, illisq; pignorantibus Thuricenses: ecce centum ciues Basilienses, & septuaginta Argentinenses in peregrinatione euntes ad monasterium Heremitarum, captiuati sunt in Thurego, & induciati ad tempus sub maxima cautione. Et cum à Thuricensibus intollerabilia peterentur, sunt in captiuitatem reducti: & confœderatis ad quinquennium cum Ducibus Austriæ, Argentinensi, Basiliensi, Friburgensi & Brisacensi ciuitatibus, indictisque exercitibus, omnibusque paratis & volentibus Argentinensi & Basiliensi episcopis cum illis in personis propriis proficisci, captiui ciuitatum sunt restituti.
units.tr: Previously, when Waldenar of Sulz of Alsace had a lawsuit with Molitor, a knight of Zurich, and the Zurichers were unwilling to do him any justice before the cities or elsewhere, except before their own mayor, and the Zurichers held his people as pledges, then a hundred citizens of Basel and seventy of Strasbourg, who were going on a pilgrimage to the monastery of the hermits, were taken captive in Thurgau and held for a time under very strict security. When the Zurichers demanded intolerable terms, they were led back into captivity. Then, with the cities of Strasbourg, Basel, Freiburg and Breisach, and the dukes of Austria, allied for five years, and armies levied, and all being ready, and the bishops of Strasbourg and Basel being willing to set out with them in person, the captives were restored to their cities.

units.la: Eodem anno quinquagesimo cum rex Carolus Romanus pluribus ciuitatibus & aliis Rheni noua contulit thelonia, per quæ traducentes vina & alias merces, plurimum sunt turbati. Argentinenses verò tamdiu Rhenū obstruxerunt, quòd tandem obmissis nouis theloniis in Maio, sub anno LI, Rheno aperto magna cum vino nauium multitudo descendit.
units.tr: In the same year of 1350, King Charles of the Romans granted new tolls to several cities and others on the Rhine, by which the carriers of wine and other merchandise were greatly harassed. The people of Strasbourg, however, blocked the Rhine for so long that at last, when the new tolls were dropped in May of the year 1351, the Rhine was opened and a great multitude of boats loaded with wine went down the river.

units.la: Eodem anno quinquagesimo primo, medio Iunij, vineis dudum efflorescentibus, grana communiter sufficiebant ad agrestam: ita quòd non est memoria, blada & vina adeo floruerunt tempestiuè: & aperto Rheno, cum crederetur precium bladi & vini ascendere, ipsum valde descendit, & circa Spiram & Wormatiam ante diem Ioannis Baptistæ blada sunt collecta, vinaque optima ipso anno creuerunt.
units.tr: In the same year, the fifty-first, in the middle of June, when the vines had long been in blossom, the grain was generally sufficient for the harvest. There is no memory of the corn and wine flourishing so early. When the Rhine was opened, people believed the price of grain and wine would rise, but it fell sharply. Around Speyer and Worms the grain was gathered in before the feast of John the Baptist, and that same year the best wines grew.

units.la: Eodem anno, in festo Pentecostes, fuit Capitulum generale Augustinensium in Basilea, vbi fuerant x i x Magistri Theologiae. Papa quoque omnibus fratribus ibidem venientibus, dedit eam gratiam, quam in Iubilaeo habuissent in vrbe. Quibus fuit per Papam, Basil. & Argentinensem Episcopos, aliosque contribuentes, egregiè ministratum, & concordauit Capitulum in M. Thomam de Garburg, priori anno generalem electum, vita & scientia excellentem.
units.tr: In the same year, at Pentecost, the general chapter of the Augustinians was held at Basel, where there were nineteen masters of theology. The Pope also gave to all the brothers who came there the same grace they would have had at the Jubilee in the city. They were splendidly entertained by the bishops of the Pope, of Basel and of Strasbourg, and by others who contributed. The chapter agreed on Master Thomas of Garburg as general, who had been elected the previous year, a man excellent in life and learning.

units.la: Eo tempore Treuerensis episcopus castrum Munckler fortissimum diu obsidens, expugnauit.
units.tr: At that time the bishop of Trier, after besieging the very strong castle of Münckler for a long time, took it by storm.

units.la: Eodem anno l r, quidam Carmelita lector, faciens sermonem in Missa Papae, cum & Cardinales de eorum vitiis adeo reprehendit; quod omnes qui aderant terrebantur, qui extitit propter hoc à statu honoris rotatus.
units.tr: In the same year, the fifty-first, a certain Carmelite lecturer, preaching at the Pope's Mass, denounced the Cardinals for their vices so severely that all who were present were terrified. For this he was removed from his position of honour.

units.la: Affixa quoque fuit quaedam clausa litera ostio Cardinalis, Papae & Cardinalibus directa: qua aperta, reperitur, quòd Leuiathan princeps tenebrarum salutat vicarium suum Papam & Cardinales seruitores suos; quorum ope iam vincat Christum, nitentem exaltare pauperes & humiles contra Rempublicam mundi, & introductis Prophetis, eos de omnibus commendat vitiis, & salutat eos mater eorum Superbia, & sorores eorum Auaritia, Luxuria, & caeterae, quae se iactant eorum adiutorio bene stare, & multa talia. Et scribitur: Datum in centro inferni praesente caterua Daemonum. Et commotus Papa perquirere nititur, & postea statim in infirmitate grauissima detinetur, de qua tamen conualuit, sed scriptor literae praedictae certificari non valuit.
units.tr: A sealed letter was also fixed to the door of a Cardinal, addressed to the Pope and the Cardinals. When it was opened, it was found to say that Leviathan, the prince of darkness, greets his vicar the Pope and his servants the Cardinals, and that with their help he will now overcome Christ, who strives to exalt the poor and the humble against the world's commonwealth. It then brought in the Prophets, condemned them for all their vices, and greeted them, along with their mother Pride and their sisters Avarice, Lust and the rest, who boast that they are doing well with the help of the Cardinals; and it contains many such things. It ends: Given in the centre of hell in the presence of the company of demons. The Pope, deeply disturbed, tried to find out who had written it, and afterwards was at once seized by a very grave illness, from which he nevertheless recovered; but the writer of the aforesaid letter could not be identified.

units.la: Anno quinquagesimo secundo, Anglus munitionem fortem nepotis Papae iuxta Tholosam obtinuit, de quo Papa plurimùm conturbatur.
units.tr: In the fifty-second year, an Englishman took a strong fortress near Toulouse belonging to the Pope's nephew, and the Pope was greatly distressed by this.

units.la: Infirmatus autem Papa obiit in die S. Nicolai, anno l i i, & positus in calce pro destructione carnis, in monasterio Casae Dei, in quo olim Abbas fuerat, iussit se sepeliri.
units.tr: The Pope fell ill and died on the feast of St Nicholas in the year 1352. Having been placed on the ground for the destruction of the flesh, he ordered himself to be buried in the monastery of Casa Dei, where he had once been abbot.

units.la: Mortuo Clemente Papa infra x i i i i dies electus est concorditer, Stephanus de prinu Claremontensis Francus, qui fuerat summus poenitentiarius Clementis, & Hostiensis Episcopus, & vocatus est Innocentius sextus, qui in die Epiphaniae Domini postmodum coronatus, statim reuocat omnes reseruationes factas per priorem Papam Clementem, exceptis maioribus Praelaturis, & in omnibus ostendit se rigidum, qui antea in magna clementia fuerat constitutus erga etiam Cardinales. In die Conuersionis Pauli, facit gratiam pauperibus cum rigida examinatione, & reuocauit omnes gratias praedecessoris non consequutas ius in re. Hic iustus est reputatus. Nicolaum quoq; Laurentij, olim Tribunum in Vrbe, captum per Clementem, absolutum dimisit: qui reuersus ad Vrbem, resumptus est honorifice in Tribunum. Qui postea Innocentio Papae commendans se resumptum in tribunum cum obsequij exhibitione.
units.tr: After the death of Pope Clement, within fourteen days Stephen de Prinu of Clermont, a Frenchman who had been chief penitentiary to Clement and bishop of Ostia, was unanimously elected, and was called Innocent VI. He was crowned afterwards on the feast of the Epiphany of the Lord, and at once revoked all the reservations made by the previous Pope Clement, except the greater prelacies. In all things he showed himself strict, though before this he had been very merciful, even towards the Cardinals. On the feast of the Conversion of Paul he granted favours to the poor, but only after a rigorous examination; and he revoked all the favours of his predecessor that had not yet taken effect in reality. He was regarded as a just man. He also released Nicholas, son of Laurence, formerly tribune in the city, who had been captured by Clement, and sent him away absolved. Nicholas returned to the city and was restored with honour as tribune; afterwards he commended himself to Pope Innocent, who was restored to his tribunate with a display of obedience.

units.la: Ludouicus quoque Marchio, mediante Carolo Rege, anno l i cum Duce Saxoniae & Episcopo Magdeburgensi comportatur, promissis eisdem x v i i millibus marcarum, vt Arnestus Palatinus, dux de Bauaria, liberaretur.
units.tr: Also, the Margrave Louis, through the mediation of King Charles, was brought in the year 1351 together with the Duke of Saxony and the bishop of Magdeburg, with a promise of seventeen thousand marks to them, so that Arnold the Palatine, duke of Bavaria, might be freed.

units.la: Postea anno l i i in Februario, actum est inter Marchione & fratres suos quòd Romanus Marchio efficitur, & fratri suo Alberto pars Marchiae datur, & filia Comitis de Mechelberg copulatur: Ludouico autem olim Marchioni, cedit tota superior Bauaria, attingens ad Comitatum Tirolis; & tertia pars inferioris Bauariae: Wilhelmo autem remaneret comitatus Holandiae, Selandiae & Hennegoiae, quae nolebant diuidi: constituto matri annuo redditu multorum millium florenorum, pro tempore vitae suae. Ludouicus autem Marchio de mense Decemb. cum Mediolanensi & sororio suo Mastino Veronensi, parlamentum habuit in Tridento.
units.tr: Afterwards, in February of the year 1352, an agreement was reached between the Margrave and his brothers: Roman was made Margrave, a part of the March was given to his brother Albert, and he was joined in marriage to the daughter of the Count of Mecklenburg. To Louis, formerly Margrave, was granted the whole of Upper Bavaria, reaching to the county of Tyrol, and a third part of Lower Bavaria. To William was to remain the county of Holland, Zeeland and Hainault, which did not wish to be divided; and his mother was to be assigned an annual income of many thousands of florins for the rest of her life. In December, Margrave Louis held a conference at Trent with the Milanese and his brother-in-law Mastino of Verona.

units.la: Conuenerant autem rex Carolus & Ludouicus marchio in Nurenberg de mense Aprili concordantes omnino. Et cum Rex non posset concordare occupatores Marchionatus cum Marchione, quòd cederent: ipse Marchioni adhaerens, alios coram se citauit, fictumque Marchionem cum suis bannivit. Marchio quoq; lanceam, clavos, partem crucis Christi, & alia insignia, quae imperio dicutur per Ludouicum Imperatorem patrem suum relicta, regi praesentauit, recepta cautione de reducendis infra triduum, vel in Nurenberg, vel in Francfurt, per regem: quod non fuit impletum, sed ea Pragam perduxit, de quo Bohemia nimium gratulatur.
units.tr: King Charles and Margrave Louis met at Nuremberg in April, and they were in complete agreement. Since the king could not persuade the occupiers of the March to give it up to the Margrave, he himself took the Margrave's side, summoned the others before him, and put the Margrave, who had been falsely accused, and his followers under the ban. The Margrave also presented to the king the lance, the nails, a part of the Cross of Christ, and other insignia which are said to belong to the empire, and which had been left by Emperor Louis, his father. The king accepted a pledge that they would be returned within three days, either at Nuremberg or at Frankfurt. This was not carried out; instead, the king took them to Prague, which greatly rejoiced Bohemia.

units.la: Ioannes autem frater regis, filiam Ducis Poloniæ, quam de Tropo we nominant, inscio rege traduxit vxorem, de quo (cum multi sint eorundê Poloniç Ducum, attingentes versus Bohemiam) vtique rex perturbatur.
units.tr: John, the king's brother, took as his wife, without the king's knowledge, the daughter of the Duke of Poland whom they call "de Tropowe". The king was certainly disturbed by this, since many of those Polish dukes border on Bohemia.

units.la: Postea anno quinquagesimo secundo, mense Martij, Wenceslao fratri regis ex Francigena, inuito rege, filia Ducis Brabantiæ copulatur, & terra Lutzelburg in Comitem assumpsit eundem.
units.tr: Afterwards, in the fifty-second year, in March, Wenceslaus, the king's brother by his French wife, was joined in marriage, against the king's will, to the daughter of the Duke of Brabant, and the king made him count of Luxembourg.

units.la: Ludouicus autem marchio, de mense Iulij & Augusti, ingreditur Marchiam, cum M. c c galeatis, plurima reacquirens, cui per totum annum praeteritum rex Daciæ cum trecentis galeatis & quingentis scutiferis aderat in Marchionatu, cum Romano, fratre Marchionis virili: qui rex ad priorem gentem suam ducentos galeatos, & quingentos scutiferos de nouo transmisit. Marchio quoquo Missenensis, filius sororis Marchionis, similiter ad gentem per annum ibidem habitam, tantundem transmisit. Recepta autem multa pecunia, idem Ludouicus filio Mastini Veronensis, sororem suam, quondam Ludouici Principis filiam, matrimonio copulauit: ex quo rex Vngariæ, cuius frater similiter eius sororius est, plurimum, nec immerito, conturbatur.
units.tr: Margrave Louis entered the March in July and August with 1,200 men-at-arms, recovering many places. For the whole of the previous year the king of Denmark had been with him in the March with three hundred men-at-arms and five hundred squires, together with Roman, the Margrave's brother, a man of courage. This king sent to his people two hundred men-at-arms and five hundred squires in addition. Margrave Meissen, the son of the Margrave's sister, likewise sent as many people as had been stationed there for the year. Having received a large sum of money, the same Louis joined his sister, formerly the daughter of Prince Louis, in marriage to the son of Mastino of Verona. Because of this the king of Hungary, whose brother is likewise his brother-in-law, is greatly and not undeservedly disturbed.

units.la: Peregrini quoque Iubilæi, licet vndiq; competenti pace potirentur: circa partes Rheni plurimum periclitati fuerunt, tam in submersione nauium circa Brisacum & Rhinaugiam, ex quo plurimi perierunt, quàm inuasione prædonum. Bertoldus enim Comes de Eberstein, Baldemarum militem dictum der rote Baldemar, de Westerreich, de Vrbe redientem, cepit, & in aureorum grossorum sex millibus taliauit. De quo tamen multi nobiles sunt gauisi, quia idem miles multos diebus iuis, post etiam cruciatus magnos, excoriauit ad vnguem.
units.tr: The pilgrims to the Jubilee, although they enjoyed general peace, were in great danger around the Rhine region, both from the sinking of ships near Breisach and Rheinau, by which very many perished, and from attacks by robbers. Count Berthold of Eberstein seized Baldemar, a knight called "der rote Baldemar" of Westerreich, as he was returning from Rome, and ransomed him for six thousand gold groschen. Many nobles rejoiced at this, because this knight had for many days, and even after great tortures, flayed people completely.

units.la: Iisdem temporibus, de mense Decembri, Hannemannus dominus in Liechtenberg, qui spernens dominam de Liningen, sororem Emiconis comitis de Liningen, coniugem suam legitimam & probam, cuidam Lisæ mulieri adhæsit adulterinæ, ex qua plures liberos procreauit, quarum vnam filio Gotzonis de Brostein militis Argentinensis, matrimonio copulauit, in castro suo Liechtenberg: per Henric. filium suum & Emiconem prædictum captiuatur, & Lysa præcipitatur ab alto: priùs enim fuerat capta, & per multas petitiones dimissa, iterum ipsi Hannemanno adhæsit, & post reditum ab Vrbe, in vxoris & filii mortem machinando. Qui Hannemannus data cautione de non exhæredando filio, liberatur.
units.tr: At the same time, in December, Hannemann, lord of Liechtenberg, who scorned the lady of Liningen, sister of Count Emicho of Liningen, his lawful and virtuous wife, attached himself to a certain adulterous woman named Lisa, by whom he had several children. One of these daughters he joined in marriage, at his castle of Liechtenberg, to the son of Gotzo of Brostein, a knight of Strasbourg. He was seized by his son Henry and the aforesaid Emicho, and Lisa was thrown from a height. For she had previously been taken prisoner, and released after many entreaties, and had again attached herself to Hannemann; and after his return from Rome she was plotting the death of his wife and son. Hannemann was freed after giving a pledge that he would not disinherit his son.

units.la: Anno Domini, millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo primo, venit Nicolaus Laurentii, de mense Iulii, olim tribunus Romanus, Pragam incognitus inibi: qui propter quosdam eius sermones, à Pragensi Episcopo detinetur diu captiuus, quem postea de mense Iulii, Carolus rex Papæ transmittit. Rex quoque tunc infirmitate grauissima & durabili detinetur, quod multi ex toxico factum fuisse crediderunt. Mukos enim Dominorum Bohemiæ, munitionibus & bonis suis, per patrem regis eisdem obligatis, spoliauit: dicens, eos recepisse plurima vltra sortem.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1351, in July, Nicholas, son of Laurence, formerly tribune of Rome, came unknown to Prague. On account of certain of his sermons he was held for a long time in captivity by the bishop of Prague; afterwards, in July, King Charles sent him to the Pope. The king was also at that time held by a very grave and lasting illness, which many believed had been caused by poison. For he had despoiled the lords of Bohemia, the Mukos, of their fortresses and property, which his father the king had pledged to them, saying that they had received much more than the principal.

units.la: Conualuit autem competenter, ac sub anno millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo primo, de mense Maii Ducem Austriæ visitat, inter alia fratrem suum Patriarcham Aquilegiensem reconciliando cum rege, amicè etiam se gerens cum Marchione de Brandenburg, eius aduersariis aduersatur. Quilibet etiam eorum baro nes alterius, qui tempore eorum inimicitiæ de tradendo dominum suum, cum altero vias quæsierant, patefecit. Marchio etiam quàuis se exinaniuerit in expensis, in Marchia tamen feliciter triumphauit, victisque quibusdam munitionibus, inhabitantes cremauit.
units.tr: He recovered sufficiently, and in the year 1351, in May, he visited the Duke of Austria, reconciling among other things his brother, the Patriarch of Aquileia, with the king. He also behaved in a friendly way toward the Margrave of Brandenburg and opposed his adversaries. He revealed that each of their barons, during their enmity, had sought ways with the other to betray his lord. The Margrave, although he had exhausted himself in expenses, nevertheless triumphed successfully in the Mark. Having overcome certain fortresses, he burned the inhabitants.

units.la: Romanus autem frater eius, venit ad matrem in Holandiam, assistens matri contra fratrem suum Wilhelmum, quem terra illa pro Domino ad mandatu matris recepit, quam mater aspirans ad cuiusdam imparis matrimonium, vt dicitur, nititur rehabere: at illi Wilhelmo assistit, & inter ipsos discrimina oriuntur. Scripsit autem mater filio, si eum obtinuerit, ipsum in quatuor partes diuideret: ipso econtra, si eam obtinuerit, vt matrem tractaturum benignè, scribente, inito conflictu in lacu, ex parte matris perierunt c c viriles, & vltrà, multiq; Anglorum.
units.tr: His brother Romanus came to their mother in Holland, supporting her against his brother William, whom that land had received as lord at the mother's command. It is said that the mother, aspiring to the marriage of some unequal man, strives to recover the land. But Romanus supports William, and dangers arise between them. The mother wrote to her son that if she got him, she would divide him into four parts; he, on the contrary, wrote that if he got her, he would treat his mother kindly. A battle was joined on the lake, and on the mother's side two hundred men and more perished, along with many English.

units.la: O Eodem anno LI, de mense Iunij, marchio Iuliacensis, quem filii biennio tenebant captiui, penitus liberatur. Dominus enim de Schönecke, qui postea in obsidione Munckler iactu periit, filios litibus infestauit, cui tandem Colonien-sis & Treuerensis archiepiscopi assistebant: Filii n. capto patre (quamuis antiquior haberet Comitatum Montium) in substantia & sumptibus defecerunt, debitis onerati: unde pater cum filiis bene concordat, ut dominium restaureretur. Dux quoque Gelriae à iuniore fratre suo, dicente, eum inutilem, de adiutorio Comitis Marchiae impugnatur.
units.tr: In the same year, 1351, in June, the Margrave of Jülich, whom his sons had held captive for two years, was wholly freed. The lord of Schönecke, who later perished by a missile at the siege of Munckler, harassed the sons with lawsuits, and the archbishops of Cologne and Trier finally supported him. For once the father had been captured, the sons (although the elder held the County of Mont) ran short of resources and expenses, burdened with debts. Whence the father came to a good agreement with the sons, so that the lordship might be restored. The Duke of Guelders was also attacked by his younger brother, who called him useless, with the help of the Count of the Mark.

units.la: Anglus eodem anno LII, de mense Aprili, cum uxore & liberis veniens in Calès, terram praedicti Comitis de Gines inuadens, obtinuit fere totam, & contra Comitem Lemouicensem, eum cum Franci auxilio aggredientem, conflictu obtinens, & postea cum Comite Belloniensi pari modo confligens, Comitem cepit, multis occisis, & pluribus captiuatis, diuersis insultibus feliciter triumphando. Comitatu quoque Bellifortis, quem frater Papae tenuit, omnino quasi destruxit. Fracus aut fratri & nepoti Papae, ut cum expressis armatorum multitudinibus ad eum venirent, sub priuationis feudorum, marschalco vero Papae, sub capitis poenis, mandauit.
units.tr: In the same year, 1352, in April, the Englishman came with his wife and children to Calais. Invading the land of the aforesaid Count of Guînes, he obtained almost all of it. Attacking the Count of Limoges with French aid, he prevailed in battle; and afterwards, fighting in the same way with the Count of Beaumont, he captured the Count, killing many and taking many prisoners, and triumphed successfully in various assaults. He also almost wholly destroyed the county of Beaufort, which the Pope's brother held. The Frenchman, however, ordered the Pope's brother and nephew to come to him with their armed multitudes, under penalty of deprivation of their fiefs, and the Pope's marshal under penalty of death.

units.la: Erat autem eo tempore lis durissima in Westrania, Episcopo & ciuitate Metensi ac Comitissa Barrensi ex una: Ducissa Lotharingiae, Comitibus de Sarbrug & Geminopote, dominis de Vinstingen & plurib. aliis, ex parte altera, se omni discordia vastantibus hinc inde, quos Francus, ut ab eis mutuo, more solito haberet auxilium suo tempore, pacare conatur. Destructis autem mutuo aliquibus munitionibus & conuenientibus vtrinque circa Metim in Augusto ambarum partium armatura, habentibus extrinsecis circa duo millia & quadringentos galeatos, factisque multis militibus, negotium comportatur. Inter Francum quoque & Anglum facto conflictu, in quo pars Franci praevaluit, ad annum inducię confirmatur. Et post haec anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo secundo, de mense Iulij, Francus castrum Gines obsedit.
units.tr: At that time there was a very hard dispute in the Westrich. On one side were the bishop and city of Metz and the Countess of Bar; on the other the Duchess of Lorraine, the Counts of Saarbrücken and Zweibrücken, the lords of Finstingen and many others, all laying waste on every side. The Frenchman tried to pacify them, so that in his own time he might have their aid in return, as usual. Some fortresses having been destroyed on both sides, the armed forces of both parties gathered around Metz in August, the outside contingents numbering about 2,400 helmeted men, and many knights were made. The business was carried through. Between the Frenchman and the Englishman a battle was fought, in which the French side prevailed, and a truce for a year was confirmed. After these events, in the year of the Lord 1352, in July, the Frenchman besieged the castle of Guînes.

units.la: Anno Domini M. CCC LI, de mense Augusti, venit Albertus Dux Austriae ad partes Rheni, redimens à Comite de Widewe oppidum imperiale Rinfelden, dudum Ducibus ab imperio obligatum: sicq; habuit de oppidis imperialibus super Rheno, Schaffhusen/Rinfelden/Fuenburg & Brisacum.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1351, in August, Duke Albert of Austria came to the parts of the Rhine and redeemed from the Count of Widewe the imperial town of Rheinfelden, which had long before been pledged to the Dukes by the Empire. Thus he held, of the imperial towns on the Rhine, Schaffhausen, Rheinfelden, Laufenburg and Breisach.

units.la: Obsedit autem Turegum, cum duobus millibus galeatorum, & xx millibus peditum, de auxilio Basilien-sis & Argentinensis episcoporum & ciuitatum: item Friburgensium, Bernensium, de Wirtenberg Comitum, de Hohenberg, & aliorum multorum. Confoederati autem erant Turicensibus valles Suitiae, Brah, & Vnderwalden, & oppido Lucern ipsius ducis, quod se ab eius ditione retraxit: & compromissum est in quatuor arbitros, Agnete olim regina Vngariae, sorore Ducis, pro superiore electa. Qua concordante cum arbitris Ducis, post recessum exercitus, illiusque Turicensibus pronuntiationi parere nolentibus, sed xvi obsides meliorum Turicensium in Brucke & in Baden positos in obstagio, in obseruatione obstagii quasi perpetuo dimittentibus, qui turribus sunt inclusi: Dux ergo in mense Nouembri, ciuitatum hominibus dimissis, equites & sagittarios pro custodia munitionum suarum & pro infestandis illis, & ne eis adduci possent victualia, destinauit. Vxore eius Ioanna de Ferreto interim, relictis quatuor filiis & duabus filiabus, mortua, Austriam est reuersus, Ioanne de Habspurg captiuo manente.
units.tr: He besieged Zürich with two thousand helmeted men and twenty thousand foot soldiers, with the aid of the bishops and cities of Basel and Strasbourg, and likewise of Freiburg, Bern, the Counts of Württemberg, of Hohenberg and many others. The Zürichers were allied with the valleys of Schwyz, Uri and Unterwalden, and with the town of Lucerne, which belonged to the same Duke but withdrew from his dominion. A compromise was made into four arbiters, with Agnes, formerly Queen of Hungary and the Duke's sister, chosen as the superior. She agreed with the Duke's arbiters. After the army withdrew, the Zürichers refused to obey the award, yet still kept, as good as in perpetuity, the sixteen hostages of the better Zürichers held at Brugg and Baden, who were shut up in towers. Therefore the Duke, in November, dismissed the townsmen and sent horsemen and crossbowmen to guard his fortifications, to harass the Zürichers, and to prevent provisions from being brought to them. Meanwhile his wife Joanna of Ferrette died, leaving four sons and two daughters, and the Duke returned to Austria, John of Habsburg remaining captive.

units.la: Suitenses autem vallem Ducis Glaris, destructo inibi castro Hermanni de Landenberg, subegerunt. Burkardus autem de Ellerbach capitaneus Ducis, equites Argentinenses, Basilienses & Friburgenses ciuitatum, circa ducentos posuit in locum Balneorum, extra oppidum Baden. Turicenses autem in die sancto nativitatis Domini de nocte cum quatuor millibus peditum armatorum, duobus millibus bragantum, & ducentis equitibus armatis, latenter egressi, cum post castrum Balnearum descendentes, viam arboribus inuenissent obstructam: in tolendo obstacula vsque circa ortum Solis fuerunt impediti. Equites vero ciuitatum cum equitibus Ducis dispositi erunt, post Missam, ipso die Stephani, visitare Turegum, & ob hoc equos & arma paratos haberent. Illis venientibus, dimissis missis omnibus suis, vix cum equis & armis ad oppidum euaserunt. Turicenses vero tollentes spolia, locum Balneorum & quaedam alia, incendio vastauerunt.
units.tr: The Swiss subdued the valley of Glarus, having destroyed the castle of Hermann of Landenberg there. Burkhard of Ellerbach, the Duke's captain, posted about two hundred horsemen of the cities of Strasbourg, Basel and Freiburg at the place of the Baths, outside the town of Baden. On the holy day of the Lord's Nativity, at night, the Zürichers went out secretly with four thousand armed foot soldiers, two thousand light troops and two hundred armed horsemen. Descending past the castle of the Baths, they found the road blocked by trees, and were hindered in removing the obstacles until about sunrise. The horsemen of the cities, together with the Duke's horsemen, were stationed to visit Zürich after Mass on St Stephen's day, and they kept their horses and arms ready for this. When the Zürichers came, the city horsemen, having dismissed all their attendants, barely escaped with horses and arms to the town. The Zürichers, taking spoils, put to fire the place of the Baths and some other places.

units.la: Et cum circa occasum solis reuerterentur, alii cum CCC equitibus, & DCCC peditibus de Brucke & Baden eos sequerentur: Turicenses se de sylua montis trahentes ad planum conglutinauerunt. Et appropinquantibus istis, equites Turicenses dixerunt eis: Vah vos non audetis. Alii vero dixerunt: Vah, vos fugitis. Et ecce sub banerio Basilien si, qui hoc illa vice forte obtinuerunt, in crepusculo iniere conflictum, & ceciderunt de parte Ducis centum & vltra. Ex parte Thuricensium ceciderunt CCCC, & prae nocte ab inuicem discesserunt. Interea ante reditum Ducis in Austriam, Thuricenses & sui successiue omnia Ducum & suorum in illis partibus extra munitiones incendio vastauerunt, oppidum Zuge, saepe tentantes expugnare, sed propter Argentinenses nequiuerunt.
units.tr: As they were returning about sunset, others from Brugg and Baden followed them with three hundred horsemen and eight hundred foot. The Zürichers drew themselves out of the mountain forest and gathered on the plain. As these pursuers approached, the Zürich horsemen called out to them, "Ha, you do not dare!" Others shouted, "Ha, you are fleeing!" And behold, under the banner of Basel, which perhaps prevailed on that occasion, they joined battle at dusk. More than a hundred fell on the Duke's side, and four hundred on the Zürich side, and at nightfall they parted from one another. Meanwhile, before the Duke's return to Austria, the Zürichers and their men in turn laid waste with fire all the properties of the Dukes and their followers in those parts outside the fortifications. They often tried to take the town of Zug, but could not, because of the men of Strasbourg.

units.la: Anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo secundo, de mense Aprili, promisit dux CCC Astrales in Baden contra eos, & ipse subsequitur de mense Iulii, omnibus quos habere poterat conuocatis. At Suitenses Zuge machinis, cattis & iaculis igneis adeo infestarunt, quod oppidani emissis extraneis, Suitensibus se dederunt. Dux vero cum duobus millibus galeatorum equitum, & x millibus peditum armatorum Thuregum obsedit: inter quos erat Lud. marchio de Brandeburg, multi Comites & Barones. Constituto autem Eberhardo de Wirtenberg inuito quasi per multas preces capitaneo, cum alii familiares Ducis, eo inscio omnia tractarent, & res esset in spe compositionis, pro duce, Eberhardo recedente: totus exercitus negotio infecto recessit. Et est tandem compositum, quod Thuricenses & sui, nullum de hominibus Ducis reciperent in Burgenses. Et liberatus est Ioannes de Habspurg, restituta sibi Marchia & oppido Naprechtswiler / restitutaque sunt Duci Glaris, Zuge, & Lucerna ac Thune, cum pertinentiis in Suize, & nihilominus ligâ contraxere iuratam. Post haec finita liga Bernensium cum Ducibus, ipsi se Suitensib. & Thuricensibus colligarunt.
units.tr: In the year 1352, in April, the Duke promised three hundred Austrian men-at-arms against them at Baden, and he himself followed in July with all the men he could muster. But the Swiss so harassed Zug with siege engines, cats and fire-missiles that the townsfolk, having sent out the foreigners, surrendered to the Swiss. The Duke, with two thousand helmeted horsemen and ten thousand armed foot soldiers, besieged Zürich. Among them were Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg, and many counts and barons. Eberhard of Württemberg was appointed captain, though almost unwillingly, after many entreaties, while other members of the Duke's household managed matters without his knowledge. The affair was in hope of a settlement, but Eberhard withdrew, and the whole army departed with the business undone. Finally it was agreed that the Zürichers and their people would receive none of the Duke's men as burghers. John of Habsburg was freed, and the March and the town of Naprechtswil were restored to him. Glarus, Zug, Lucerne and Thun, with their dependencies in Schwyz, were restored to the Duke, and nevertheless they made a sworn league. After this, when the league of Bern with the Dukes had ended, they joined themselves to the Swiss and the Zürichers.

units.la: Item eodem anno quinquagesimo secundo, rex Litouiae cum auxilio Tartarorum innumerabili, per Russiam (quâ quasi destruxit) transiens, animo destruendi Cracouiam, cum rehabuisset fratrem suum Ludouicum captiuum dudum, & cum omnes vicinae terrae ad eius resistentiam properarent, recessit, in pristina perfidia perseverans.
units.tr: In the same year, 1352, the king of Lithuania, with countless Tartars to help him, passed through Russia, which he nearly destroyed. He meant to destroy Cracow. He had recently recovered his brother Ludwig, who had long been a captive, and when all the neighbouring lands hurried to resist him, he withdrew, persisting in his old treachery.

units.la: Item eodem anno Liga pacis generalis Alsatiae finita festo Martini, Rodolphus Palatinus, nominans se Vicarium imperii, & Hugo de Hohenberg cum ciuitatibus Imperii Alsatiae, noluerunt prorogare ligam pacis, nisi nonus cognitor, qui ante fuit Argentinensium, detur ciuitatib. Imperialibus: Episcopo autem & ciuitate Argentinensi nolentibus mutare in hoc morem antiquum, liga expirat. Quo facto, Rodolphus de Wegersheim armiger Argentinensis, qui dominis de Winstingen multùm seruierat, de multorum auxilio, Hagenowenses (pro eo quòd in anno Iubileo Ioannem fratrem suum decapitauerant) hostiliter inuadens, ipsos ad magnâ artauit emendam. Anno enim Iubileo Ioannes de Wegersheim praedictus valens & robustus in sacra foresta, in inuasione quorundam Angliae peregrinorum, captus cum famulo, euadente Ioanne de Wolffgangsheim adiutore suo, licet probationes pro eo offerrentur, quòd pignorare voluerit regem Angliae, in cuius seruitio plurima expenderit, post preces innumerabiles nobilium Argentinensium, virorum & mulierum & dominorum Alsatiae, in Hagenowe decollatur.
units.tr: Also in the same year the general peace league of Alsace ended at the feast of St Martin. Rudolf the Palatine, calling himself vicar of the empire, and Hugh of Hohenberg, with the imperial cities of Alsace, refused to extend the league of peace unless a ninth judge, who had formerly been the Strasbourgers' man, were given to the imperial cities. The bishop and the city of Strasbourg, unwilling to change the ancient custom in this matter, saw the league expire. Upon this, Rudolf of Wegersheim, an esquire of Strasbourg who had served the lords of Winstingen well, with the help of many men attacked the people of Hagenau with hostility, because in the Jubilee year they had beheaded his brother John, and he pressed them hard for a heavy fine. In the Jubilee year that John of Wegersheim, a strong and robust man, had been captured with his servant in the sacred forest, during an attack on some English pilgrims, while his helper John of Wolfgangsheim escaped. Although proofs were offered that he had meant to hold the king of England to pledge, in whose service he had spent a great deal, he was beheaded at Hagenau after countless pleas from the nobles of Strasbourg, men and women alike, and the lords of Alsace.

units.la: Anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo tertio, rex Carolus egreditur de Bohemia, mense septembri & veniens Vlmam, ligam pacis generalis fecit omni Sueuiae imperii ciuitatum. Et cum iussisset Eberhardum de Wirtenberg praesidé huiusmodi ligam iurare, & ille diceret, se velle deliberare cum fratre: Rex indignatus dixit: delibera quantum velis. Tunc territus Comes, iurauit. Venit autem rex Constantiam, vbi cum inuenisset ciues quasi omnes armatos, & catenas per vicos, omnia tolli iussit. Erant autem omnia paramenta mensae suae ad comedendum & bibendum, & nauicula continens eleemosynam illius mensae, omnia de auro puro, nec quicquam inibi apparebat argenti: omnia autem inferiorum mensatū paramenta, etiā pro garrionibus, & currus ducens nauem, continētem eleemosonam, de argento fuerunt. Conuenitque ad eum multitudo Baronum, & missum est pro Thuricensibus, pro discordia cum Duce sedanda. At illi cum valibus Suitiæ nolentes duci subiici, se ad seruiendum regi & imperio obtulerunt: sicque venit Thuregum, & ostendūtur priuilegia Imperatorū pro Vallibus antiqua. Et cum per ministros Ducis diceretur, cur ea nō antea monstrassent: responderūt: quòd pro nullo motu ea alteri, quàm eorum Domino principi Romanorum, monstrarent. Et obedierunt regi valles, quæ in xxxvi annis nulli parebant. Et descendens rex per Basileam & Brisacum, venit Argentinam, vbi honorificè est receptus.
units.tr: In the year 1353 King Charles set out from Bohemia in September. Coming to Ulm, he made a general league of peace with all the cities of the Swabian part of the empire. He ordered Eberhard of Württemberg, its leader, to swear to this league, but Eberhard said he wished to deliberate with his brother. The king, indignant, said: "Deliberate as long as you like." Then the count, frightened, swore. The king came to Constance, where he found the citizens almost all armed and chains stretched across the streets, and he ordered everything removed. All the table settings for his eating and drinking were of pure gold, and the little ship holding the alms for that table was gold too; no silver appeared there at all. But all the settings of the lower tables, even those for the pack-horses, and the wagon that drew the ship holding the alms, were of silver. A crowd of barons gathered around him, and he sent for the men of Zurich to settle their dispute with the Duke. They, together with the valleys of Schwyz, unwilling to be subjected to the Duke, offered to serve the king and the empire. So he came to Zurich, and the privileges of the emperors for the ancient Valleys were shown. When the Duke's officials asked why they had not shown these before, the men replied that they would show them to no one, under any pressure, except their lord, the Roman prince. And the valleys, which for thirty-six years had obeyed no one, obeyed the king. The king, going down through Basel and Breisach, came to Strasbourg, where he was honourably received.

units.la: Decubuit autem infirmitate durabili in Mollesheim, Berchtoldus Episcopus Argentinensis, qui Ioannem de Liechtenberg (qui in ecclesia Argentinensi praepositum & decanatum in lite, Cantoriam verò & Pincernatum sine lite tenebat) Regis secretarium, vicarium constituit, in spiritualibus & temporalibus, & pro eo praficiendo ecclesiæ, Episcopus cum capitulo, & rex, Papæ literas dirigunt seriosas.
units.tr: Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, was lying at Mollesheim with a lasting illness. He appointed as his vicar, in spiritual and temporal matters, John of Lichtenberg, the king's secretary, who held the provostship and deanship of the Strasbourg church in dispute, but the cantorship and the butlership without dispute. To install him over the church, the bishop with the chapter and the king sent serious letters to the Pope.

units.la: Eo Autumno tanta fuit vini abundantia, quòd bona mensura vini communiter pro Obulo, vas autem vacuum pro triginta solidis Argentinensibus vendebatur. Multitudo quoque agrorum in Alsatia incolecta remansit, & etiam circa festum Luciæ, in bonis vincis erant adhuc botri. Et venit rex Hagenouiam, vbi in die Omnium sanctorum communicatus fuit. Facta est etiam liga pacis ibidem ad triennium, in qua quindecim iudices sunt statuti, duo per Episcopum, & duo per ciuitatem Argentinensem, tres per oppida Imperij, vnus per inferiorem Landgrauium, vnus per Dominos de Liechtenberg, de Ochsenstein & Beroltsecke in Vosago, vnus per Abbatem Morbacensem, dominos de Rapoltstein, de Beroltsecke in Mortenowe, & de Ysenberg, vnus per Episcopum, & vnus per ciuitatem Basiliensem, & quindecimus per regem. Recessit autem Weckerius Marchio de Baden, nolens esse in liga, cuius frater Fridericus, & Hermannus patruus, in breui sunt ante defuncti.
units.tr: That autumn there was such an abundance of wine that a good measure was commonly sold for a halfpenny, and an empty cask for thirty Strasbourg shillings. Many fields in Alsace also remained uncultivated, and even about the feast of St Lucy there were still grape clusters on the good vines. The king came to Hagenau, where he received communion on All Saints' Day. A league of peace was also made there for three years, in which fifteen judges were appointed: two by the bishop, two by the city of Strasbourg, three by the imperial towns, one by the lower Landgrave, one by the lords of Lichtenberg, Ochsenstein and Bärenstein in the Vosges, one by the abbot of Marmoutier, one each by the lords of Rappoltstein, Bärenstein in Mortenau and Isenburg, one by the bishop, one by the city of Basel, and the fifteenth by the king. Margrave Wecker of Baden withdrew, unwilling to be in the league. His brother Frederick and his uncle Hermann had died shortly before.

units.la: Concordauit etiam Sletzstatenses, introducens expulsos, & instituit telonia super Alsa quæ breuiter reuocauit. Ascendens quoque rex visitat Bertoldum episcopum Argentinensem, in Mollesheim decumbentem, & crastino, casu in die Florentij, veniens Haselahe, aperit tumbam Florentij, trecentis annis auro & argento reclusam, & inuenit caput & corpus eius. Et faciens ibi tabelliones, instrumenta sibi dari iussit, de inuentione huiusmodi, quia Canonici Argentinenses S. Thomæ, vbi sepultus fuit, asserunt se caput & corporis maiorem partem habere: & aderant ibi Moguntinus, & plures Episcopi. Visitat etiam rex Monasterium de Andelahe, vbi est corpus beati Lazari, & monasterium in Erstein, vbi est corpus beati Vrbani, tunc & ante nunquam apertum. Et de his omnibus & aliis multis ibi & alibi reliquiis partes accepit, animo Bohemiam traducendi. Et deponit Hugonem de Hohenberg præsidem.
units.tr: The king also reconciled the people of Schlettstadt with the exiles they had admitted, and set up tolls on the Ill, which he soon revoked. Going on, he visited Bishop Berthold of Strasbourg, who lay sick at Mollesheim. On the following day, which happened to be the feast of St Florentius, he came to Haselach and opened the tomb of Florentius, which had been sealed with gold and silver for three hundred years, and found his head and body. There he had notaries draw up instruments recording this discovery, since the canons of St Thomas at Strasbourg, where Florentius was buried, claimed to have the head and the greater part of the body. The archbishop of Mainz and several other bishops were present. The king also visited the monastery at Andlau, where the body of the blessed Lazarus lies, and the monastery at Erstein, where the body of the blessed Urban lies, which had never been opened before. From all these and many other relics, here and elsewhere, he took portions, intending to carry them to Bohemia. And he deposed Hugh of Hohenberg as president.

units.la: Reuersus aut rex Argentinā per Hagenowiam, Wissenburg, & Landawe, venit Spiram, vbi ad eum venit cum cautione Cuno de Waldenstein, ministerⅼ Henrici de Birnenberg, archiepiscopi Moguntini depositi. Qui Cuno dominum suum contra Papam & regem, ac dominum de Nassawe & suos, manu tenens, in tantum praevaluit, quod pluribus annis omnia bona quorumuis Clericorum, ciuitatis & dioecesis Moguntinæ beneficialia & matrimonialia, Gerlaco prouiso sedis adhærentium, sine lite recepit, multisque qui mandatis Apostolicis paruerant, trucidatis, & exequentibus aliquibus submersis, multisque exulare coactis, literas quoque apostolicas gratiosas vel alias repertas apud quoslibet, laniauit. Nouum telonium apud Oppenheim instituit, & empta Curia Monachali super Mogano, ad vnum miliare à Moguntia, ibidem castrum construxit. Seruantes mandata Apostolica vndique per dioecesim tanquam excommunicatos vitari coegit, fauorem quasi omnium habuit, pro eo quòd Domino suo & Ludouico Principi adhaesit depositò, tantæ constantiæ fidelitatem ostendit: & reputatus est animosior Alemannus. Plura ecclesiæ Moguntinæ bona obligata redemit. Hoc anno quinquagesimo tertio, quatuor millia plaustra vini, & xl millia maltera bladi collegit; seruitores habuit prudentissimos constantes, quibus omnia regenda commisit, ipse venationibus & iocunditatibus assistebat. Cui cum rex Spirae plura commissa contra imperium obiecisset: ipse se super his non deliberasse respondit. Et quantumcunq; sibi magna exhibérentur, ipse nil se auditurum, per quod Dominus suus cederet, respondendo, recessit.
units.tr: The king returned to Strasbourg through Hagenau, Wissembourg and Landau, and then came to Speyer. There Cuno of Waldenstein, the minister of Henry of Virneburg, the deposed archbishop of Mainz, came to him under safe-conduct. Cuno, holding his lord's cause against the Pope and the king, and against the lord of Nassau and his people, prevailed so far that for several years he took, without dispute, all the benefices and marriage revenues of any clergy in the city and diocese of Mainz, with Gerlach having been provided to the see by the adherents of the Pope. Many who had obeyed apostolic mandates were slaughtered, some were drowned while carrying out orders, and many were forced into exile. He also tore up apostolic letters, whether favourable or otherwise, wherever he found them. He set up a new toll at Oppenheim, bought the monastic court above Mainz, a mile from the city, and built a castle there. He forced those who kept the apostolic mandates to be shunned throughout the diocese as excommunicates. He won the favour of almost everyone, because he clung to his deposed lord and to Prince Louis and showed such steadfast loyalty, and he was regarded as the most spirited German. He redeemed many of the pledged possessions of the church of Mainz. In this year, 1353, he gathered four thousand wagonloads of wine and forty thousand malters of grain. He had very prudent and steadfast servants to whom he entrusted the management of everything, while he himself devoted his time to hunting and pleasures. When the king at Speyer charged him with many things done against the empire, he replied that he had not deliberated on these matters. However great the rewards offered to him, he answered that he would hear nothing by which his lord might be made to yield, and so he withdrew.

units.la: Et descendit rex Moguntiam, comportans cum Gerlaco Moguntino & Capitulo potétium, quod restituta sunt sibi nomine Imperij Oppenheim, Odertsheim op-pida Imperialia super Rhenum, cum castris & villis attinentibus, quæ obligata fuerant ecclesiæ Moguntinæ pro x c millibus florenorum. Et feria quarta ante Thomæ in atrio ecclesiæ Oppenheim, ipse Gerlacus absoluit vniuersitatem ibidem, ipsaque nomine Imperii regi iurauit.
units.tr: The king went down to Mainz, bringing from Gerlach of Mainz and the chapter a document by which Oppenheim and Odernheim, imperial towns on the Rhine, with their castles and villages, were restored to him in the name of the empire. These had been pledged to the church of Mainz for 100,000 florins. On the Wednesday before St Thomas's day, in the atrium of the church at Oppenheim, Gerlach himself absolved the community there, and they swore allegiance to the king in the name of the empire.

units.la: In die vero beati Thomæ, rex cum Principibus & Baronibus Moguntiæ præsidens, declarauit, Cunonem in multis contra Imperium fecisse, super quibus respondere & iustitiam facere renuit coràm rege: inhibens omnibus authoritate regia ne quis assisteat eidem. Et declaratum est per Principes & Imperij fideles, quòd quicunque scienter contra hoc fecerit, corpus & res ad gratiam regis amisisset.
units.tr: On the feast of St Thomas, the king, presiding at Mainz with the princes and barons, declared that Cuno had done many things against the empire. He refused to answer for these or do justice before the king, and by royal authority he forbade anyone to assist him. The princes and the faithful of the empire declared that whoever knowingly acted against this command would forfeit body and goods to the king's grace.

units.la: Eodem die venit Treuerensis notans Cunonem, morituq; Henricus de Virnenberg Archiepiscopus depositus, paralysi, quem fingunt viuere tractatores Cununis. Et componit eos rex amicè de consilio & auxilio Ioannis de Liechtenberg, electi Argentinensis, quòd Cunoni remanet castrum Vogtsperg pro tempore vitæ, & quòd sibi & hæredibus remanet pignus Erenfels, cum multa terra vicina, quousque redimantur per Archiepiscopum pro quadraginta millibus florenorum. Item quòd remoto Wilhelmo Pintschon Gallico, sedis prouiso, præpositura Cunoni permaneat in quiete, ipseque Cuno in blado & vino retinebit collecta, & quòd archiepiscopus contracta debita per quinque administratores, dudum per Henricum archiepiscopum & Capitulum electos, soluere teneatur, & quòd collecta & facta per quondam Henricum etiam post depositionem rata manebunt, & ipsius & suorum fiat per papam, vel eius authoritate, absolutio & relaxatio generalis: sicque expeditis omnibus, statim factus est Cuno regis & Archiepiscopi intimus & dilectus. Dataque sunt suis fidelibus, præsertim Herbotoni, humili seruitori eius & prudentissimo, prouisiones & munera ab eisdem. Qui Cuno postmodum factus est Archiepiscopus Treuerensis. In die vero beati Stephani, rex præsidens Moguntiæ coronatus.
units.tr: On the same day the man from Trier came, denouncing Cuno. Henry of Virneburg, the deposed archbishop, was dying of paralysis, though Cuno's agents pretend he is still alive. The king, with the advice and help of John of Lichtenberg, elect of Strasbourg, kindly reached an agreement: Cuno keeps the castle of Vogtsberg for his lifetime; he and his heirs keep the pledge of Erenfels, with much of the neighbouring land, until the archbishop redeems it for forty thousand florins. Likewise, once Wilhelm Pintschon the Frenchman was removed, the provostship, filled by the see, was to remain with Cuno in peace, and Cuno himself was to keep the grain and wine collected. The archbishop is to pay the debts incurred through the five administrators earlier elected by Archbishop Henry and the Chapter. The levies collected and made by the late Henry, even after his deposition, shall stand valid, and a general absolution and release for him and his people shall be obtained from the pope or by his authority. With all this settled, Cuno at once became the king's and the archbishop's intimate and favourite. Gifts and provisions were given by them to his followers, especially to Herbot, his humble and very prudent servant. Cuno was afterwards made Archbishop of Trier. On the feast of St Stephen, the king, presiding at Mainz, was crowned.

units.la: Hac hyeme anni LIII, Marschalcus Prussiæ, cum multis aduenis glaciem transiens cum quinquaginta millibus, in terram regis Litouiæ veniente pluuia (ne fracta glacie reditus præcludatur) illico est reuersus, & fratrum exercitus est dispersus. Interim rex conuocatis duobus fratribus suis, cum multa gente venit illis insciis, ad conflictum paratus. Et intelligens illos transisse, confortata noctibus glacie, per viam illorum Prussiam ingreditur, & per integrum diem vastàs & cõburens, multa millia hominum captiua traduxit, illico reuertendo, filius autem regis cum multis, a-perta & fracta in parte illa glacie, est submersus.
units.tr: In the winter of the year 1353, the Marshal of Prussia crossed the ice with many foreign men, fifty thousand strong, into the land of the king of Lithuania. Because rain was coming, which would break the ice and cut off their return, he immediately turned back, and the army of the brothers was scattered. Meanwhile the king summoned his two brothers and came with a large force, unknown to them, ready for battle. Understanding that they had crossed, and the ice having been strengthened by the nights, he entered Prussia by their route, and for a whole day he laid waste and burned, and led away many thousands of captives, returning at once. The king's son, however, with many others, was drowned, because the ice had opened and broken in that part.

units.la: Anno Domini M. CCCLIIII, in Ianuario, reuersus à rege Balduinus Treuerensis Archiepiscopus moritur, & statim Comes de Sarbrugge archidiaconus conditer eligitur, & breuiter confirmatur & consecratur à Papa. Post hæc venit rex ad ciuitatem Metensem, vbi honorificè receptus, multis ibi diebus permansit, faciens ibi ex Comitatu Lutzelburgensi Ducatum, & ex Comitatu Barrensi Marchionatum. Non tamen eum receperunt tanquam regem, dicentes, se soli imperatori ad plura iura teneri. Deinde in hebdomada sancta Reiserberg Alsatiae reuersus, ibi Pascha peregit. Et venit in monasterium Hohenberg, quinto nonas Maii, & tumbam beatæ Otiliæ, vnà cum Ioanne Episcopo Argentinensi paulisper aperuit, tollens ex integro corpore ibi reperto, partem brachii dextri fideliter ipsam recludens.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1354, in January, Baldwin, Archbishop of Trier, died on his return from the king. Immediately the Count of Saarbrücken, the archdeacon, was elected, and was quickly confirmed and consecrated by the pope. After this the king came to the city of Metz, where he was honourably received and stayed many days, making a duchy of the county of Luxembourg and a marquisate of the county of Bar. Yet they did not receive him as king, saying that they were bound to the emperor alone by many rights. Then, in Holy Week, he returned to Reiserberg in Alsace and celebrated Easter there. On the fifth day before the nones of May he came to the monastery of Hohenberg and, together with John, Bishop of Strasbourg, briefly opened the tomb of St Odilia. From the whole body found there he took a part of the right arm, faithfully closing it up again.

units.la: Cum autem Albertus Australis scire vellet, an rex manu forti sibi vellet assistere contra Thuricenses & valles Suitiæ, & confœderatos eis: rex in Aprili ascendens Thuregum, libenter induxisset eos: quòd Duci reliquissent sua, scilicet Lucernam, Zuge & Glaris. Illi responderunt, sibi placere, quod duci darent ea, ad quæ tenerentur eidem: sed nolebant sinere, quòd Dux vel sui, munitiones in sua potestate tenerent, prætendentes, quitasse cum illis. Rege vero dicente, eos tanquam Imperii homines non potuisse sine rege talia iurare, cum eius authoritas sit excepta: illi vero dicentes: se simplices talia non intelligere, omnino suo proposito inhærebat. Sicque rex factis inter eos treugis ad prædicendum per unum mensem; negotio infecto recessit. Interim autem tractauerat cum Thuricensibus, de emendo pro Imperio Lucernam & Zuge munitiones, Australis, ratione quarum tot scandala sunt suborta. Dicens etiam rex, se illidaturum plures & meliores circa Austriam, pro lite sedanda: quæ Dux intelligens, nimium est commotus, dicens: se melius posse emere bona regis.
units.tr: When Albert the Southerner wished to know whether the king would stand by him with a strong hand against the Zürichers, the valleys of Switzerland and their confederates, the king went up to Zurich in April and would gladly have persuaded them to give up to the duke what was his, namely Lucerne, Zug and Glarus. They replied that they were willing to give the duke what they owed him, but they would not allow the duke or his men to hold fortifications in their territory, claiming that they had been released from that obligation with them. When the king said that they, as men of the Empire, could not swear such things without the king, since his authority was thereby excluded, they replied that they were simple folk and did not understand such matters, and they stubbornly kept to their purpose. So the king arranged a truce between them, to be proclaimed for one month, and departed with the business undone. Meanwhile he had negotiated with the Zürichers about buying, on behalf of the Empire, the fortifications of Lucerne and Zug from Albert the Southerner, which was the cause of so many scandals arising. The king also said that he would summon more and better men from around Austria to settle the dispute. When the duke understood this, he was greatly disturbed and said that he could buy the king's property better himself.

units.la: Conueniunt autem in Ratispona, Rex, Dux & Marchio Brandeburgensis, extra ciuitatem tamen manens, accedere nolens regem: & irato Duci dixit rex: Se credidisse ei complacere in tractatibus prædictis: sed ex quo ei displicent, se in propria persona, cum omni gente Imperii, cum Duce, in Thuricensium obsidionem iturum. Et egressus est Dux de Austria, anno prædicto de mense Iulii, cum innumerabili pecunia, & gente magna Australium & Suevorum, monens omnes ciuitates sibi colligatas, ac fideles quoscunque. Rex quoq; monebat omnes ciuitates & fideles Imperij in Ducis subsidium contra illos.
units.tr: The king, the duke and the Margrave of Brandenburg then met at Regensburg, though the margrave stayed outside the city and was unwilling to approach the king. The king said to the angry duke that he had believed he would please him in the aforesaid negotiations, but since they displeased him, he himself would go in person, with the whole people of the Empire, together with the duke, to besiege the Zürichers. The Duke of Austria set out from Austria in July of that year with immense sums of money and a great force of Austrians and Swabians, summoning all the cities allied to him and all loyal supporters. The king too urged all the cities and loyal subjects of the Empire to give the duke aid against them.

units.la: Dux autem descendit in Brucke, cum c galeatis, & mittuntur ei secunda die mensis Augusti, ab Argentina centum galeati meliores & nobiliores ciuitatis, & trecenti pedites, quorum quilibet sex habuerat currum sex equorum ab Argentina, præter alios currus & bigas, omnia eis necessaria deferetes: quorum flores Ioannes Zornius miles in Brucka moritur.
units.tr: The duke came down to Brugg with a hundred armoured knights. On the second day of August, from Strasbourg, a hundred of the city's best and most noble armoured men and three hundred foot soldiers were sent to him, each of whom had six wagons drawn by six horses from Strasbourg, besides other wagons and two-horse carts, carrying everything they needed. Among them, John Zorn, the flower of the knights, died at Brugg.

units.la: Similiter & aliæ ciuitates & domini Sueuiæ & Rheni fecerunt. Confluit autem ad Ducem contra Turicenses nimia multitudo. Rex vero veniens iuxta Regensperg, distans per unum miliare a Thurego, castra metatur. Graue autem erat ciuitatibus imperialibus obsidere Thuregum imperiale, nisi & illorum sermone audito. Obtulit autem rex ciuitatibus, quòd ex parte Ducis & sui, omnia committerentur: dummodo & illi facerent, arbitrio ciuitatum. Et missis in Thuregum cuiuslibet ciuitatum nuncis, & exposito Thuricensibus ciuitatum fauore, & oblato eis tali compromisso: illi, quòd omnia libenter in ciuitates compromitterent, excepta liga, cum aliquibus Ducis munitionibus, responderunt. Et obiecto eis, quòd si contingeret Regem eis aduersari, an eis assistere vellent, petebant, ne intricaretur eorum iuramentum, & sic ciuitates infecto negotio sunt egressi.
units.tr: Other cities and lords of Swabia and the Rhine did likewise. A very great multitude gathered to the duke against the Zürichers. The king, coming near Regensberg, a mile from Zurich, pitched his camp. It was a grave matter for the imperial cities to besiege imperial Zurich without hearing its side too. The king offered the cities that, on behalf of the duke and himself, everything would be submitted to arbitration, provided the Zürichers did the same, to the judgment of the cities. Messengers from each city were sent to Zurich, setting out to the Zürichers the goodwill of the cities and offering them such a compromise. They replied that they would gladly submit everything to the cities, except their league, and some of the duke's fortresses. When it was objected to them that, if the king should happen to oppose them, they would be asked whether they wished to assist them, they asked that their oath not be entangled, and so the cities departed with the business undone.

units.la: Vincitur autem villa Meilan magna, Thuricensium, & multi occiduntur, hortusque deliciarum inter Raprechtzwiber & Thuregum vastatur omnino. In progressu autem ad Thuregum, vbi iuxta vallum quod Thuricenses & Suitzenses non longè ante ciuitatem fecerant, & ibi in campo posuerant, vbi timebatur confictus: Ioannes Windlock Episcopus Constantiensis, Ducis Cancellarius, voluit, quòd Vexillum suum & omnes Sueui sub illo, iuxta antiquum ius Suevorum, præire deberent. Quod cum Dux nollet, sed suum præire Vexillum: Episcopus cum suis recessit, nolens minuere eius Suevorum, de quo Dux nimium est commotus. Gens namque Suevorum a tempore Caroli & aliorum Principum, quod in expeditionib. primum conflictum habere debeant, viribus & virtutibus meruerant.
units.tr: The large Zürich village of Meilen was captured, many were killed, and the pleasure garden between Rapperswil and Zurich was completely laid waste. On the march towards Zurich, near the rampart which the Zürichers and Swiss had made not far outside the city and set up in the open field, where a clash was feared, John Windlock, Bishop of Constance and the duke's chancellor, wished that his banner and all the Swabians under it should go in front, according to the ancient law of the Swabians. When the duke refused this and insisted that his own banner go first, the bishop withdrew with his men, unwilling to diminish the honour of his Swabians, and the duke was very angry at this. For the Swabian people, since the time of Charles and other princes, had earned by their strength and valour that on campaigns they should have the first encounter.

units.la: Postquam autem Dux septem hebdomadis circa Thuregum vastauit, dimisso exercitu (quia rex manere noluit) reliquit Equites in munitionibus circumquaque, qui impedientes illis adduci victualia captionibus & interfectionibus se mutuò infestarunt. Dux autem cum R. filio suo Austriam est reuersus, animo breuiter reuertendi.
units.tr: After the duke had laid waste the area around Zurich for seven weeks, he dismissed the army, since the king would not stay. He left riders in the fortresses round about, who, preventing supplies from being brought in to the enemy, harassed one another with captures and killings. The duke returned to Austria with his son R., intending to come back soon.

units.la: Et in Decembri, cum afferretur bladum Thuricensibus, & cum viginti quatuor nauibus armatorum, bladum deducere voluissent: Hermannus de Laubenberg hæc prænintelligens, abscondit nauibus suis cum armatis, illos retro inuadit. At illi fugientes de nauibus, occisis pluribus, pedes euadunt, nauibus Hermanno relictis. Dux autem post Pascha dirigit multo plures. Iisdem temporibus.... de <bl>Hohenlo</bl>, episcopus Herbipolensis, de auxilio Moguntini & comitum de Wirtenberg & aliorum, ciuitatem Herbipolensem potenter obsedit, pro eo quòd vnus Ciuitatensis praebendam ecclesiae Herbipolensis contra ecclesiae consuetudinem, quae nunquam ciuitatenses receperat, impetrauit à sede. Et non obstante appellatione Capituli, ad inuocationem executoris, bona Capituli occuparunt. Et veniens Rex illic negotium reformauit: ita quòd ciues curias Canonicorum, quas interim destruxerant, reaedificare deberent, & quaelibet pars in suis libertatibus remanere.
