units.tr: In December, when grain was being carried to the Zürichers, and they wished to convey it with twenty-four armed ships, Hermann of Laubenberg, foreseeing this, hid his armed men with his ships and attacked them from behind. The Zürichers fled from their ships, many were killed, and the rest escaped on foot, leaving the ships to Hermann. After Easter the duke sent many more. At the same time ... Hohenlohe, Bishop of Würzburg, with the help of the Mainz men, the counts of Württemberg and others, powerfully besieged the city of Würzburg, because one citizen had obtained a prebend of the church of Würzburg from the see, contrary to the custom of the church, which had never admitted citizens. Despite the Chapter's appeal, the bishop's men, at the invocation of an executor, seized the Chapter's goods. The king, coming there, settled the matter: the citizens were to rebuild the canons' courts which they had meanwhile destroyed, and each party was to remain in its liberties.

units.la: Eodem anno de mense Septembri, moritur Ioannes archiepiscopus Mediolanensis: & tres fratrueles eius, Matheus, Barnabas & Galeatius, filij quondam Stephani, dominia occuparunt. Dederat autem ipse archiepiscopus pecuniam dudum Wernhero de Vrselingen capitaneo societatis, quod in patria est reuersus, & breuiter in Suevia sepultus.
units.tr: In the same year, in September, John, archbishop of Milan, died, and his three cousins, Matthew, Barnabas and Galeazzo, sons of the late Stephen, seized the lordships. The archbishop had earlier given money to Werner de Vrselingen, captain of the company, who returned to his homeland and was buried shortly afterwards in Swabia.

units.la: Post cuius obitum alia surrexit societas x millium equitum & vltra, in partibus Lombardię, quibus primò praefuit frater Memorialis hospitalarius, apostata prouincialis, strenuus & prudens in armis, qui recedens cum societate sua, & per Vrbem de conducta Tribuni transitum faciens, propter quandam suspicionem decollatus est à Tribuno. Qui Nicolaus Laurentij tribunus in breui postea facto insultu, occiditur à Romanis, praecipuè à Columnensibus, quibus & in hoc fauebant Vrsini. Populi autem videntes eum mortuum, ne viderentur illis suspecti, ipsum conciderunt in frusta. Societas autem, recedente Prouinciali R. de Landawe Sueuum, de genere comitum, pro Capitaneo, tanquam virilem recepit. Haec societas semper morabatur in campis ad dandum sibi victualia Dominos & ciuitates cohercens. Haec societas diu stipendiata est à Venetis, in regis fauorem. Et iacebant iuxta ciuitates Mediolanensibus subditas, à quibus ne infestarent eas, victualia receperunt. Tenebant autem inter se maximam pacem & iudicium, & afferentibus venalia, securissimum dabatur conductus. Post haec se transferebant ad partes Rauennae, & postea in Apuliam.
units.tr: After his death another company arose, of ten thousand horsemen and more, in the parts of Lombardy. It was first led by Brother Memorialis, a hospitaller and former provincial, a brave and prudent soldier. When he withdrew with his company, and crossed through the city on the Tribune's hired service, he was beheaded by the Tribune on account of some suspicion. Shortly afterwards, Nicholas Laurentius, the Tribune, was killed in a sudden attack by the Romans, chiefly by the Colonna family, whom the Orsini also favoured in this. The people, seeing him dead, and not wishing to appear suspect to them, cut his body into pieces. The company then, when the provincial R. de Landau withdrew, received as its captain Sueuus, of the family of counts, as a man of courage. This company always stayed in the open countryside, compelling lords and cities to supply it with provisions. For a long time it was paid by the Venetians, in the king's favour. It camped near the cities subject to the Milanese, and to keep them from harassing it, it received provisions from them. Among themselves they kept the greatest peace and justice, and to those bringing goods for sale a very safe passage was granted. After this they moved to the region of Ravenna, and later into Apulia.

units.la: Rex eodem anno MCCCLIIII, mense Septembri, quasi occultè cum paucis ingreditur Lombardiam, & veniens Mantuam, mittit ad ciuitates Alemanniae, & episcopos & ad alios, vt sibi gentes armatas dirigant, iuxta morem. Et Robertum seniorem Bauarum Palatinum Rheni, tempore absentiae vicarium regni constituit generalem. Rex quoque in Decembri, factis treugis inter Venetos & Mediolanenses, cum tribus fratribus Mediolanensibus reformatur, recepta ab eis grandi pecunia, & promissis sibi annuis redditibus de terra, ita quod illi nomine regis ministri terrae maneat, sicut ante: sicque Mediolani honorificè est receptus, & in palatium episcopi traductus, ab archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, quem de genere praedictorum Vicecomitum papa praefecerat, corona ferrea coronatur.
units.tr: In the same year, 1354, in September, the king entered Lombardy almost secretly with a few men, and coming to Mantua he sent to the cities of Germany, to the bishops and to others, asking them to send armed troops to him, as is customary. He appointed Robert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine of the Bavarians, as general vicar of the kingdom during his absence. The king also, in December, after truces had been made between the Venetians and the Milanese, was reconciled with the three Milanese brothers, having received a large sum of money from them and promises of yearly revenues from the land, so that they would remain ministers of the land in the king's name, as before. And so he was honourably received at Milan and taken to the bishop's palace, and was crowned with the iron crown by the archbishop of Milan, whom the pope had appointed, from the family of the aforesaid Visconti.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CCC.LV, in Ianuario, Rex oblatis sibi portarum clauibus à Pisanis & Senensibus, Pisas perrexit, vbi ad eum in Februario Regina peruenit, & habuit mille galeatos Bohemos & paucos Alemannos. Hostiensis verò episcopus Cardinalis, crastino Purificationis flens, animo coronandi regem à papa, recessit, associatis omnibus Cardinalibus ad duas leucas, dicens, se timere, se amplius non visurum. Rex autem in festo Paschae coronatus à Cardinalibus, Pisas reuertitur, quia se non mansurum in Vrbe promisit. Imperatore autem ab Vrbe in die coronationis recedente, factis multis militibus super ponte, eoque quinque diebus ante Pascha latitante in vrbe, templaque visitante latenter, & in reuersione à Senensibus & aliis gloriosè recepto, duorum fratrum filiorum, quondam Principis Moregiae, quos Vngarus à captiuitate reliquit, vnus iunior in Apulia manens, sibi societatem aliquā assumens, & Ludouicum patruelem, scribentem se regem Siciliae, & habentem Ioannam quondam coniugem Andreae regis iugulati & eius dominia, dilectu nimis sedi Apostolicae vehementer infestabat. Alter vero maior, qui & antea dudum forsan simulatè coram Franco patrueli suo Vngaro, duellum indixit, castrum fortissimum Prouinciæ, in quo idem Ludeuicus thesaurum suum habuit, obtinens, militem, de quo prædictus Ludouicus confidit, custodientem castrum, qui & Clementis papæ habuit filiam, cum vxore deiecit, omnibus per eum occupatis in castro repertis. De quo cum papę Petragoricensem Cardinalem, ipsorum fratrum auunculum, & quosdam alios Cardinales sibi faventes, de fautoria haberet suspectos, vt eis ablationem pilei, ipsi vero sibi diuisionem capitis minarentur: nimia Avinioni scandala sunt suborta. Papaque conquisitis stipendiariis ad custodiendum se in palatio, cum Petragoricensis cum suis, plures Cardinalium assistentes papæ, de suis curiis eiecisset, papa Rhodanum in tuitionem Franci transiuit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1355, in January, the king, having been offered the keys of the gates by the Pisans and the Sienese, went to Pisa, where in February the queen joined him, and he had a thousand helmeted Bohemians and a few Germans. But the bishop of Ostia, a cardinal, weeping the day after the Purification, withdrew, intending to have the king crowned by the pope, all the cardinals accompanying him for two leagues, saying that he feared he would never see him again. The king, however, was crowned at Easter by the cardinals, and returned to Pisa, since he had promised not to stay in the city. The emperor left Rome on the day of the coronation, after many soldiers had been stationed on the bridge; he had lain hidden in the city for five days before Easter, secretly visiting the churches, and on his return he was gloriously received by the Sienese and others. One of the two sons of the late Prince of Morea, whom the Hungarian had left after the captivity, the younger, remaining in Apulia and taking some company to himself, and his cousin Louis, who wrote himself king of Sicily and had Joanna, former wife of the murdered king Andrew, and her lands, attacked the Apostolic See very violently, to its extreme displeasure. The elder, who perhaps earlier had feigned it before his cousin Francis the Hungarian, declared war; he seized the very strong castle of the province in which the same Louis had his treasure, and he threw down the soldier whom Louis trusted, who was guarding the castle, and who also had a daughter of Pope Clement, together with his wife, after taking everything found in the castle. Because of this, the pope suspected the cardinal of Périgord, their uncle, and some other cardinals favouring him, of supporting them, and they threatened to take away his hat, and he threatened to divide their heads. Great scandals arose at Avignon. The pope, having gathered mercenaries to guard himself in the palace, drove the cardinals who attended him out of his courts, with the cardinal of Périgord and his followers; the pope then crossed the Rhône into the protection of Francis.

units.la: His diebus Veneti Ducem suum, cum quibusdam aliis, decollarunt.
units.tr: In these days the Venetians beheaded their doge, together with some others.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CCC.LVI, in festo beati Lucæ Euangelistæ, corruit ciuitas Basilea, ex vehementi terræmotu, & plura castra & alia ædificia corruerunt. Ille terræmotus venit circa vesperas. Et in sequenti nocte fiebant plus quam decem, ex quibus etiam plus quam x l castra circa Basileam sunt subuersa: per plures etiam dies sequentes, fiebant plures terræmotus.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1356, on the feast of the blessed Luke the Evangelist, the city of Basel collapsed in a violent earthquake, and many castles and other buildings fell. That earthquake came about evening. And in the following night more than ten shocks occurred, of which more than forty castles around Basel were overthrown; for several days afterwards more earthquakes also took place.

units.la: Eodem anno venit Carolus imperator ad ciuitatem Metensem in aduentu Domini, celebrans ibidem natalem Domini: fuerunt que ibi Principes Electores, & Officiales seu ministrales Imperij, quorum quilibet ministrabat Imperatori sedenti in mensa, in officio seu ministerio suo proprio. Quilibet autem veniebat super equo, vsq; ad mensam. Descendente vero de equo coram mensa, histrionibus & mimis datur equus: & aliæ plures solennitates fiebant ibi, de quibus longum esset scribere. Erat enim solennior curia, quâ de aliquo Imperatore scribitur temporibus retroactis multis.
units.tr: In the same year Emperor Charles came to the city of Metz at Advent, celebrating the Lord's Nativity there. The prince electors and the officials or servants of the empire were there, each of whom served the emperor seated at table, in his own proper office or ministry. Each one came riding on horseback as far as the table; on dismounting before the table, the horse was given to the jesters and mimes. Many other solemnities were held there, of which it would be long to write. For it was a more solemn court than has been recorded of any emperor in many past times.

units.la: Anno domini M.CCC.LXV, crastino Georgij, venit Imperator Carolus Argentinam, & susceptus fuit cum magna solennitate, tanquam Imperator: dudum enim receptus erat, tanquam rex Romanorum. In festo vero sancti Marci, recessit versus Auinionem ad papam. In festo autem Petri & Pauli reuersus fuit Argentinam per nauigium: inde recedens iuit in Seltze.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1365, the day after St George's day, Emperor Charles came to Strasbourg and was received with great solemnity as emperor; for he had already been received as king of the Romans. On the feast of St Mark he departed towards Avignon to the pope. On the feast of Saints Peter and Paul he returned to Strasbourg by boat; from there he went on to Selz.

units.la: Feria sexta sequenti, quæ erat festum Vdalrici, intrauit quidam Capitaneus, cuiusdam societatis Anglicanorum, qui dicebatur Archipresbyter, cum sua societate, videlicet populo innumerabili, habens secum x I I millia equorum, vt æstimabatur, in Alsatiam, & de nocte combusserunt quam plurimas domos in Rünigeshofen/ apud lobium ibidem situm. Sequenti Sabbato eadem multitudo ipsius societatis infra prandium vel circa meridiem, apparuit impetuose ante muros ciuitatis Argentinensis; offerens se ad bellandum. Ex cuius terrore & horrore omnes forenses & incolæ villarum & camporum circumquaque, ad ciuitates & munitiones seu fortalitia fugerunt.
units.tr: On the following Friday, which was the feast of Ulrich, a certain captain of an English company, who was called the Archpriest, entered Alsace with his company, that is, an innumerable crowd, having with him, as was estimated, twelve thousand horses. At night they burned very many houses in Rünigeshofen, near the village situated there. On the following Saturday the same multitude of that company, during or about midday, suddenly appeared before the walls of the city of Strasbourg, offering to fight. From their terror and dread, all the outsiders and inhabitants of the villages and fields round about fled to the cities and fortresses or strongholds.

units.la: Eodem tempore venit Carolus de Auiniona, vt dictum est, & morabatur per aliquot dies in oppido Seltze. Hic congregauit exercitum magnum ad expulsionem societatis. Quod percipiens archipresbyter cum suis, fugit ex partibus Alsatiæ, & dixit se illuc venisse ex iussu Imperatoris, culpans Imperatorem, quòd iniquè circa se egisset, eo quòd exercitum ad expellendum eum congregasset.
units.tr: At the same time Charles came from Avignon, as has been said, and stayed for some days in the town of Selz. Here he gathered a great army to drive out the company. When the Archpriest with his men perceived this, he fled from the parts of Alsace, and said that he had come there by order of the emperor, blaming the emperor for having treated him unjustly, since he had gathered an army to drive him out.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CCC.LXVI, vigilia annunciationis beatæ Mariæ, Egeno comes in Friburg, cum suis fautoribus voluit fraudulenter cepisse ciuitatem seu oppidum Friburg: sed ciues præmoniti parum, clauserunt portas suas, & exteriores fraudati sunt desiderio suo. Postea intra Pascha & Pentecosten destructum fuit castrum Friburg, per ciues Friburgenses: ex hoc oritur briga inter comitem & ciues.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1366, on the vigil of the Annunciation of the blessed Mary, Count Egeno in Freiburg, with his supporters, wished to seize the city or town of Freiburg by fraud; but the citizens, though little forewarned, closed their gates, and the outsiders were cheated of their desire. Afterwards, between Easter and Pentecost, the castle of Freiburg was destroyed by the citizens of Freiburg; from this arose a quarrel between the count and the citizens.

units.la: Anno Domini M.C C C.LXVII, in die beati Lucæ, bellatum seu pugnatum fuit à comite & ciuibus prædictis apud Endingen, & prævaluit comes, ciuibus graviter succumbentibus: ita quòd ex parte ciuium & eorum fautorum, plus quam mille occisi sint, & plurimi captiui abducti. Cæteri fugerunt à facie comitis. Hæc acciderunt eis propter superbiam eorum, quia ita elati erant, quòd nolebant Dominum suum prædictum recognoscere pro domino suo, & quia renuerunt habere ligam pacis cum Argentinensibus, quàm prius plus quam x l annis cum eis habuerant. Quam si tenuissent cum eis, hæc nullatenus contra eos attentata fuissent. Posthæc subdiderunt diderunt
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1367, on the day of the blessed Luke, there was fighting or battle by the count and the aforesaid citizens at Endingen, and the count prevailed, the citizens being heavily overcome; so that on the side of the citizens and their supporters more than a thousand were killed, and very many were taken captive and led away. The rest fled from the face of the count. These things happened to them because of their pride, since they were so puffed up that they were unwilling to acknowledge their aforesaid lord as their lord, and because they refused to keep the league of peace with the people of Strasbourg, which they had previously kept with them for more than forty years. Had they kept it with them, these things would in no way have been attempted against them. Afterwards they submitted.

units.la: Basilea terræmotu corruit 1356.
units.tr: Basel was damaged by an earthquake in 1356.

units.la: Imperialis curia Metensis celebrata.
units.tr: The imperial court was held at Metz.

units.la: Carolus 4. Argentinæ Genet 1365.
units.tr: Charles IV at Strasbourg, 1365.

units.la: Britannorum in Alsatiam irruptio.
units.tr: Invasion of Alsace by the English.

units.la: Periculum urbi Friburgensi 1366.
units.tr: Danger to the city of Freiburg, 1366.

units.la: Clades ad Endingam Brisgoia 1367. diderunt se Duci Austriæ, magna summa pecuniæ data comiti, pro iure suo, quod habuit infra muros seu territorium, iure extraneo sibi reseruato: & sic propter superbiam eorum ira Dei ascendit super eos, & occidit pingues eorum, & omnem eorum actum impediuit, ita quòd nunc non seruiunt Domino suo, sed diis alienis.
units.tr: Defeat at Endingen in Breisgau, 1367. They surrendered themselves to the Duke of Austria, and a large sum of money was given to the count for his right, which he had within the walls or territory, the foreign right being reserved to himself. And so, because of their pride, the wrath of God rose up against them and struck down their rich men, and hindered all their undertakings, so that now they do not serve their Lord, but strange gods.

units.la: Anno Domini M. CCC. LXVIII, post Pascha, circa Calend. Maij transtulit se Vrbanus V papa de Auinione ad vrbem Romanam, quasi ibi iugiter manendo, quia curia Romana vel sedes Apostolica permultos annos steterat in Auinione, & sequenti anno reuersus est Auinionem. Iterum intentionem habuit reuertendi Romam, sed morte peruentus fuit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1368, after Easter, about the first of May, Pope Urban V transferred himself from Avignon to the city of Rome, as if to remain there continually, since the Roman court or the Apostolic See had stayed at Avignon for very many years; and in the following year he returned to Avignon. Again he intended to go back to Rome, but he was overtaken by death.

units.la: Anno Domini M. CCC. LXXIII, captum erat castrum Herlesheim per præsidem Alsatiæ, & oppida Imperij, & Argentinenses, & comprehensi sunt in eo quinquaginta prædones, & alij pessimi nequam, quorum aliqui capitibus truncati sunt, reliqui vero patibulis sunt suspensi.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1373, the castle of Herlisheim was taken by the governor of Alsace, and the towns of the Empire and the people of Strasbourg; and fifty robbers were seized in it, and other very wicked men, some of whom were beheaded, and the rest hanged on the gallows.

units.la: Anno M. CCC. LXXIIII, venerunt tres inundationes aquarum succedentes se, infra festum Epiphaniæ, & festum sancti Valentini: ita quòd interim non erat transitus per fluuium dictum Snelling, nisi mediante nauigio.
units.tr: In the year 1374, three floods of water followed one another, between the feast of the Epiphany and the feast of St. Valentine, so that in the meantime there was no crossing over the river called the Schlingen, except by boat.

units.la: Anno prædicto, scilicet LXXIIII, circa festum Martini, ciuitas Argentina coepit ampliari, id est suburbia nouis muris circumdari. Et inchoatum fuit an der steinstrassen/bey dem weissen thurn, licet eadem turris & alia turris eiusdem nominis apud sanctam Aureliam, multis ante annis constructæ fuissent. Tertia vero turris, dicta Kronenburg an dem Bruch propè capellam, etiam priùs constructa erat, sub anno Domini M. CCC. LXIX. Prædicti vero muri per has tres turres perducti fuerunt, vsq; ad flumen Brusche, apud fratres Teutonicos. Et hæc est tertia ampliatio ciuitas Argentinensis.
units.tr: In the same year, 1374, about the feast of St. Martin, the city of Strasbourg began to be enlarged, that is, its suburbs were surrounded with new walls. And work was begun at the Steinstrasse, by the White Tower, although that tower and another tower of the same name near St. Aurelia had been built many years earlier. The third tower, called Kronenburg, on the Bruch near the chapel, had also been built earlier, in the year of the Lord 1369. The aforesaid walls were carried out through these three towers as far as the river Brusche, at the Teutonic brothers' house. And this is the third enlargement of the city of Strasbourg.

units.la: Primitus enim ipsa ciuitas protracta fuerat, à monasterio sancti Stephani, vsque ad hospitalem antiquum, scilicet capellam sancti Erhardi: ita quòd ecclesia sancti Martini erat extra muros. Nam vallum fossarum, iam comprehendens cloacas multas, transiens tunc temporis per vicum Sporergaß, & per locum vbi iam sunt Prædicatores, in vallum dictum Kunt schnider grabe, tunc temporis non fuit omnino in tali loco, vt iam est. Nam forum annonæ, scilicet der Holtweg vnd Oberstraße, hoc tantùm fuit extra muros Argentinenses. Etiam patibulum & locus supplicij malefactorum, fuerat tunc vbi iam est collis & capella sancti Michaelis, apud domum Augustinensium, vbi etiam beatus Arbogastus, pontificum Argentinensium sanctissimus, Christi volens sequi vestigia, sibi sepulturam elegit. Igitur sanctus Arbogastus apud patibulum, vt viuens disposuit, sepultus, multis signis & virtutibus ab eodem loco deportatur, & in memoria sanctæ sepulturæ & deuotionis loci, capella sancti Michaelis ibidem ædificatur, in qua retro altare sepulchrum eius eleuatum adhuc cernitur, ac patibulum ad locum, vbi iam est, transfertur. In cuius etiam sancti Arbogasti honore, Dagobertus rex Francorum, cuius filius à morte suscitatur à sancto Arbogasto, construxit duo cœnobia: vnum super Alsam fluuium prope Argentinam, & aliud in Sarburg, quæ largissimè dotauit, in quibus & corpus sancti præsulis requiescit. Deinde idem locus pratis amœnus, fontibus irriguus, & variis commoditatibus vtilis & opportunus, à multis hominibus cœpit inhabitari. Igitur ciuitas Argentinensis prima vice ampliatur, & protrahitur vsque ad sanctum Petrum seniorem, circa annum Domini M. CC. L.
units.tr: For at first the city itself had been extended from the monastery of St. Stephen as far as the old hospital, namely the chapel of St. Erhard, so that the church of St. Martin lay outside the walls. For the rampart and ditches, which then took in many sewers, running at that time through the Sporergasse and through the place where the Preachers now are, to the ditch called the Kunstschneidergraben, were not at that time at all in the place where they now are. For the grain market, namely the Holzweg and the Oberstrasse, was then outside the walls of Strasbourg. Also the gallows and the place of execution of malefactors had been at the place where now there is a hill and the chapel of St. Michael, near the house of the Augustinians, where also blessed Arbogast, the most holy bishop of Strasbourg, desiring to follow the footsteps of Christ, chose a burial place for himself. So St. Arbogast, having been buried at the gallows as he had arranged while living, was afterwards carried from that place with many signs and virtues, and in memory of his holy burial and the devotion of the place, the chapel of St. Michael was built there, in which behind the altar his raised tomb can still be seen; and the gallows was moved to the place where it now is. In honour of this St. Arbogast also, Dagobert, king of the Franks, whose son was raised from the dead by St. Arbogast, built two monasteries: one on the river Ill near Strasbourg, and another at Saverne, which he endowed most generously, and in which the body of the holy prelate rests. Then the same place, pleasant with meadows, watered with springs and useful and convenient for various needs, began to be inhabited by many people. Therefore the city of Strasbourg was first enlarged and extended as far as St. Peter the Elder, about the year of the Lord 1250.

units.la: Deinde secunda vice, processo aliquantulum temporis spatio, ampliatur & protrahitur à sancto Petro seniore, vsque ad sanctum Petrum iuniorem, vsque ad turrim versus Pœnitentes, circa annum Domini M. CCC. Deinde cum ciuitas Argentinensis haberet versus Rhenum nisi vnum vallum, & vnum murum: tunc construitur Metzger thurn exterior, cum suo muro & vallo, tendente à sancta Agnete, vsque ad Ʊtengasse, anno M. CCC. XXIIII: reliqua vero pars eiusdem muri, vsque ad turrim prope sanctam Catharinam, cum ipsa turri, quæ tendit vsq; ad Torrentem, fluentem de sancto Ioanne, construitur, anno M. CCC. XLIII. Dein mœnia muri antiquitatis prædictæ, exaltata sunt, cum peribulo seu deambulacro nouo, anno M. CCC.LXX. Postea vero anno domini M.CCC.LXXIIII, ampliatur ciuitas tertio, & incipitur, An der steinstrassen, vt patet supra.
units.tr: Then, a second time, after some lapse of time, it was enlarged and extended from St. Peter the Elder as far as St. Peter the Younger, as far as the tower towards the Penitents, about the year of the Lord 1300. Then, since the city of Strasbourg had only one rampart and one wall towards the Rhine, the outer Metzger tower was built, with its wall and rampart, extending from St. Agnes as far as the Uttengasse, in 1324; and the rest of that wall, as far as the tower near St. Catherine, together with that tower, which runs as far as the stream flowing from St. John's, was built in 1343. Then the walls of the aforesaid ancient wall were raised, together with a new parapet or walkway, in 1370. Afterwards, in the year of the Lord 1374, the city was enlarged a third time, and work began at the Steinstrasse, as is evident above.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CCC.LXXVI, feria tertia, infra hebdomadam festi Pentecostes, electus est Wenceslaus, filius Caroli Bohemi Imperatoris, in Romanorum regem, patre suo adhuc viuente, & eandem electionem fieri procurante per omnes Imperij electores concorditer, non sine magna pecunia. Quæ facta & celebrata est in Franckfort, in ecclesia sancti Bartholomæi apostoli.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1376, on the Tuesday of the week after the feast of Pentecost, Wenceslaus, son of Charles, Emperor of Bohemia, was elected King of the Romans while his father was still living, the electors of the whole Empire agreeing and arranging this election, not without a great sum of money. It was made and celebrated at Frankfurt, in the church of the apostle St. Bartholomew.

units.la: Item eodem anno, nono Cal. Augusti, obiit Domicellus Ioannes Landtgrauius Alsatiæ, in quo cessauit progenies Landtgrauiorum Alsatiæ. Licet idem Ioannes ipsum dominium prius vendiderit Ioanni de Liechtenberg episcopo Argentinensi, sub anno Domini M.CCC.LVIII. Ipsi etiam domini Landtgrauij quondam dicti sunt, comites de Werdeck.
units.tr: Likewise in the same year, on the ninth day before the Kalends of August, the nobleman John, Landgrave of Alsace, died, in whom the line of the Landgraves of Alsace ended. Although the same John had previously sold that lordship to John of Lichtenberg, bishop of Strasbourg, in the year of the Lord 1358. The same lords, formerly called Landgraves, are also called counts of Werdenberg.

units.la: Anno Domini, M.CCC.LXXVII, facta est cædes seu conflictus inter ciuitates Imperiales Sueuiæ; per dominum Eberhardum de Wirtenberg, qui succubuit, & ex parte eius occisi sunt comites & barones tres, scilicet dominus de Schwartzenberg, dominus de Zolre, & dominus de Tuwingen; nobiles. Filius autem prædicti domini de Wirtenberg per fugam euasit, cum aliis quam pluribus. Facta sunt hæc apud oppidum Rutelingen, pridie Idus Maij.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1377 there was a slaughter or clash between the imperial cities of Swabia, by Lord Eberhard of Württemberg, who was defeated; and on his side three counts and barons were killed, namely the lord of Schwarzenberg, the lord of Zollern, and the lord of Tübingen, nobles. The son of the aforesaid lord of Württemberg escaped by flight, with many others. These things happened at the town of Reutlingen, on the day before the Ides of May.

units.la: Anno Domini M.CCC.LXXVIII. Obiit Carolus quartus Romanorum Imperator & Rex Bohemiæ, in vigilia Andreæ apostoli.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1378, Charles IV, Emperor of the Romans and King of Bohemia, died on the eve of the apostle Andrew.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: FINIS.

units.la: DE BERTOLDI A BVCH- ECKE, EPISCOPI ARGENTINENSIS, REBVS GESTIS COMMENTARIVS:
units.tr: CONCERNING BERTHOLD OF BUCHEGG, BISHOP OF STRASBOURG: A COMMENTARY ON HIS DEEDS

units.la: Auctore, M. Alberto Argentinensi.
units.tr: By the author, M. Albert of Strasbourg.

units.la: Ex quo superius sermo processit, de Berchtoldo de Buchecke, episcopo Argentinensi, de progenie ipsius, & origine, & de gestis eius, atque tempore ipsius, scribere nitendo, sic incipiendo.
units.tr: Having written above of Berchtold of Buchegg, bishop of Strasbourg, I now undertake to write of his family and origin, of his deeds and of his times, beginning thus.

units.la: ENRICVS comes de Buchecke, Landtgranius in Burgunden, ex filia comitis de Strasberg coniuge sua, hos reliquit liberos: spectabilem Hugonem comitem in Buchecke, Bertoldū commendatorem & prouincialē Alemanniæ, ordinis sanctæ Mariæ Theutonicorū, qui sapiens valde & mitis in omni Germania in vulgari sermone eloquentior dicebatur: Mathiam custodem monasterij Morbacensis, Dominam in Klingen, olim comitissam in Friburg, liberis carentem, Dominam in Sigenowe, Dominam in Munsingen, & Abbatissam in Frauenburne, quæ tandem ex humilitate, abbatiæ renuntians, in ipso Monasterio, vitam duxit quietam.
units.tr: Henry, count of Buchegg, landgrave in Burgundy, left the following children by his wife, a daughter of the count of Strasberg: the noble Count Hugo of Buchegg; Berchtold, commander and provincial of Alemannia of the Order of St Mary of the Teutonic Knights, who was very wise and gentle, and was said to be the most eloquent in the vernacular throughout all Germany; Mathias, custodian of the monastery of Murbach; Lady of Klingen, formerly countess of Freiburg, who had no children; the Lady of Sigenau; the Lady of Münsingen; and the abbess of Frauenburg, who at last, out of humility, resigned her abbacy and led a quiet life in the same monastery.

units.la: Hugo autem in armis miles strenuus (quod in exercitibus Alberti regis Romanorum, cuius & consanguineus extitit, in Bohemia & in obsidione Pinguiæ, & alibi, cum magnanimitate ostendit) cum Henrico Imperatore, nato de Lutzelburg, in Italiam proficiscens, in illius gloriosissimis expeditionibus, & strenuissimis actibus (quibus quasi omnibus interfuit) adeo virilem se ostendit, quòd idem Imperator de Roma recedens, ipsum Capitaneum, & vrbis senatorem reliquit. Hic Hugo per quotidianos quasi conflictus, Romam quasi totam obtinuit, quam ipse Cæsar habere nequiuit. Cæsari autem in obsidione diutina Florentiæ, per mortem & recessum Alemannorum, adeo gens parua remansit, quòd de se ipso diffidens, eundem Hugonem cum quadringentis galeatis, quos Romæ habuit, postposita vrbe, ad se celeriter venire præcepit. Qui cum omni multitudine Gelforum, qui se apud Perusium, ad impediendum ipsius Hugonis transitum congregauerant, cum prædictis quadringentis Alemannis conflictum iniens ineuitabilem, turbam multorum millium equitum armatorum & peditum, viriliter inuadens, multis occisis, aliisque fugatis, vltra trecentos ex ipsis captos, Cæsari apud Florentiam præsentauit.
units.tr: Hugo was a vigorous soldier in arms, and showed great courage in the armies of King Albert of the Romans, of whose family he was also a kinsman, in Bohemia, at the siege of Pinguia and elsewhere. He set out for Italy with Emperor Henry, born of Luxembourg, and in that emperor's most glorious campaigns and most vigorous exploits, in nearly all of which he took part, he showed himself so manly that when the emperor left Rome he left Hugo as captain and senator of the city. Through almost daily skirmishes Hugo gained nearly all of Rome, which the emperor himself had been unable to hold. Later, during the long siege of Florence, the Emperor's forces were reduced by the death and departure of the Germans, and he became so distrustful of his own strength that he ordered Hugo to come to him quickly with the four hundred mailed knights he had in Rome, abandoning the city. Hugo, engaging in an unavoidable battle with the whole host of Ghibellines who had gathered at Perugia to block his passage, together with those four hundred Germans, attacked boldly the multitude of many thousands of mounted and foot soldiers. Many were killed and others put to flight, and more than three hundred were taken and presented to the emperor at Florence.

units.la: Hic Hugo, intoxicato Imperatore in calice per quendam prædicatorem, ipsum communicante post Missam, & Pisis sepulto: dominam Catharinam, filiam prædicti regis Alberti, quæ eidem Imperatori, si vixisset, nuptura erat, de Austria Duci Calabriæ, filio Roberti regis Siciliæ, in vxorem traduxit: cum qua Neapoli & in partibus illis manens, eiusdem Roberti (cognoscentis eius strenuitatem in seruitio Imperatoris peractam, cuius idem Robertus aduersarius extitit principalis) Princeps militiæ & familiaris dilectissimus est effectus. In cuius seruitio Genuam quæ tunc ipsi Roberto adhæsit, assumpto eius exercitu, ab obsidione, qua eam Gibellini obsederant, liberauit: in omnibus eiusdem regis Roberti expeditionibus se fidelissimum & animosum ostendens. Eodem autem Roberto, qui & comes Prouinciæ est, cum domino papa Ioanne XXII, tunc nouiter creato, in Auinione ciuitate sua Prouinciæ (in qua idem papa cum sua residebat curia) commorante, duobusq; inhabilibus pro episcopatu Constantiensi in curia litigantibus, dictoque Roberto (quem dictus papa olim eius existens Cancellarius, fauore prosequebatur, pro cunctis mundi principibus gratioso) eidem Hugoni spem faciente, de promotione fratris sui Mathiæ prædicti, ad episcopatum Constantiensem, post exclusionem litigantium in breui futuram: ecce vacauit Archiepiscopatus Maguntinus, de quo ipse papa prædicto domino Mathiæ, custodi Morbacensi, ad preces ipsius Roberti, & ob cognitam ipsius Hugonis fidem, prouidit.
units.tr: This Hugo, after the emperor had been poisoned in a chalice by a certain preacher who gave him communion after Mass, and after he had been buried at Pisa, married Lady Catharine, daughter of the aforesaid King Albert, who, had she lived, would have been wed to the same emperor, to the duke of Calabria, son of King Robert of Sicily. Remaining with her at Naples and in those parts, he became, because Robert recognised his valour shown in the service of the emperor (of whom Robert was the chief adversary), the commander of the army and a most dear familiar of the king. In Robert's service he took his army to Genoa, which then adhered to Robert, and freed it from the siege by which the Ghibellines had beset it, showing himself most faithful and spirited in all the expeditions of the same King Robert. While Robert, who is also count of Provence, was staying in Avignon, the city of his Provence (where Pope John XXII, lately created, then resided with his court), and while two unfit men were litigating at the court over the bishopric of Constance, Robert, whom the pope, who had formerly been his chancellor, favoured above all the princes of the world, held out hope to Hugo that his brother Mathias, mentioned above, would be promoted to the bishopric of Constance soon after the litigants were excluded. Then the archbishopric of Mainz fell vacant, and at the request of Robert, and because of Hugo's known loyalty, the pope provided it to Lord Mathias, custodian of Murbach.

units.la: Mathiam a Buchecke, Hugonis frater archiepiscopum Moguntinum.
units.tr: Mathias of Buchegg, brother of Hugo, archbishop of Mainz.

units.la: Hic Mathias terram Maguntinam sine obstaculo potenter ingressus, vitam duxit caltissimam. Ignoranti ei cum Camerarij sui quandam pulchram foeminam intromisissent in cameram suam, credentes, iuxta dictum medicorum, continentiam eius sanitati obesse: ipse foeminam pulchre alloquens, prout bene sciuit, post eius recessum, Camerarios redarguit iracunde, iurans, eos: si amplius facerent, in sui familia non mansuros. In largitate quoque & potentia omnes qui in illa sede ante eum fuerant, antecessit, extinctisque multis illius terrae Nobilibus sibi rebellibus, tandem Landtgravium Hassiae iniuriantem Ecclesiae suae, super quibusdam dominiis, cum exercitu validissimo persequitur, cum quo decem hebdomadis in terra Hassiae copiosissime manens, factis conflictibus, combusta terra, captisque aliquibus munitionibus, mirabilia & inaudita peregit.
units.tr: Mathias entered the land of Mainz powerfully and without opposition, and led a most chaste life. When his chamberlains once, while he was unaware, admitted a certain beautiful woman into his chamber, believing (according to the physicians' saying) that his continence was harmful to his health, he spoke to the woman courteously, as he well knew how, and after she had left he angrily rebuked the chamberlains, swearing that if they did so again they would not remain in his household. He also surpassed in generosity and power all who had been in that see before him. After he had destroyed many of the nobles of that land who rebelled against him, he at last pursued with a very strong army the landgrave of Hesse, who was harming his Church over certain lordships. He remained for ten weeks in the land of Hesse, and by many battles, by burning the country and by taking some strongholds, he performed marvellous and unheard-of deeds.

units.la: Hic filiam sororis suae de Signowe, Eberhardo comiti unico de Kyburg tradidit in uxorem, qui licet antea impotens crederetur, multos ex ipsa filios & filias procreauit.
units.tr: He gave the daughter of his sister of Signau in marriage to Eberhard, the sole count of Kyburg, who, although he had been thought impotent before, begot many sons and daughters by her.

units.la: Iste Mathias Rudolphum Marchionem de Baden affinem suum, ab obsidione Ulrici comitis de Wirtemberg, viriliter liberauit. In cuius Marchionis favorem, captum Conradum Risen militem strenuum Marchionis inimicum, tandem nolente Marchione dimisit, qui miles in ipsius archiepiscopi seruitio in Ruffberg fideliter magna peregit. Hunc Mathiam papa Iohannes valde diligens, sibi & consanguineis suis multas fecit gratias.
units.tr: This Mathias valiantly freed his kinsman Rudolf, Margrave of Baden, from the siege by Count Ulrich of Württemberg. In favour of this margrave he took captive the brave knight Conrad Risen, the margrave's enemy, but later released him against the margrave's will. This knight afterwards served the archbishop faithfully and accomplished great things at Ruffberg. Pope John, who loved this Mathias greatly, granted many favours to him and to his kinsmen.

units.la: Inter alia Ioannem Sennem de Munsingen, filium sororis suae, Canonicum Maguntinum, & praepositum S. Victoris Maguntini, creando.
units.tr: Among other things, he appointed John Senn of Münsingen, son of his sister, as canon of Mainz and provost of St Victor at Mainz.

units.la: Habuit autem ipse Mathias confessorem, fratrem Ulricum de Lentzburg, lectorem ordinis Heremitarum ordinis sancti Augustini, qui in magnam familiaritatem ratione ipsius domini Mathiae assumptus, tandem post multos labores, post domini Mathiae obitum per ipsum papam in Curiensem episcopum est promotus. Hic Augustinensis strenue se tenens, dominum de Vatz, antiquum ecclesiae Curiensis persequutorem, usque ad ipsius de Vatz mortem, persequi & destruere non cessauit, qui antea episcopos Curienses & dominos eis assistentes destruxit.
units.tr: Mathias had as his confessor Brother Ulrich of Lenzburg, lecturer of the Order of the Hermits of St Augustine. Received into great intimacy on account of Lord Mathias, he was at last, after many labours and after Lord Mathias's death, promoted by the same pope to the bishopric of Chur. This Augustinian held his ground bravely and did not cease to pursue and destroy Lord von Vaz, an old persecutor of the Church of Chur, until von Vaz's death; von Vaz had earlier destroyed the bishops of Chur and the lords who supported them.

units.la: Vacante quoque episcopatu Spirensi per obitum domini Emicomis de Liningen, praedictus dominus Mathias, fratri suo domino Berchtoldo commendatori praedicto quasi inuito, cum armatae militiae miles strenuus fuerit, per dominum papam de ipso episcopatu procurauerat prouideri. Hic Berchtoldus, qui semper in ordine vixit egregie, sibique Basilea domum, sui ordinis domui contiguam, construxerat speciosam, in qua cogitauit vitam habere quietam, cum difficultate & dubio barbam rasit, in vestitu & aliis, pro episcopo degerendo. Et ecce Rhenum descendens, fratrem in Miltenberg decumbentem inuenit. Qui in omni virtute honoris & corporis, crastino natiuitatis beatae virginis, anno domini M.CCC.XXIX, ab hac luce subtractus, in medio Moguntinensis ecclesiae est sepultus. Hugo autem frater eorum qui & ipse interfuit, ad curiam illico est profectus.
units.tr: When the bishopric of Speyer also fell vacant by the death of Lord Emicho of Leiningen, the aforesaid Lord Mathias, who was a brave soldier in arms, had arranged for it to be provided, through the pope, to his brother Lord Berchtold, commander mentioned above, who was almost unwilling. Berchtold, who had always lived excellently in the Order, and had built for himself at Basel a fine house adjoining the house of his Order, had intended to live a quiet life there. With difficulty and reluctance he shaved his beard and changed his dress and other things to take up the office of bishop. And behold, while he was going down the Rhine, he found his brother lying sick at Miltenberg. Mathias, who was outstanding in every virtue of honour and of body, was taken from this light on the day after the Nativity of the blessed Virgin, in the year of the Lord M.CCC.XXIX, and was buried in the middle of the church of Mainz. Hugo, another brother of theirs, who was present, at once set off for the court.

units.la: Audita vero morte archiepiscopi, comes de Wirtemberg & alij Barones munitiones ecclesiae Spirensis occupantes, eidem Bertholdo, ne episcopatu Spirensem posset ingredi, restituerunt. Qui Bertholdus diu stans in Wormatia sumptuose, ab amicis & aliis extitit desolatus. Conradus autem de Kirkel thesaurarius Argentinensis se de ipso fideliter intromittens, initis cum praedictis Baronibus quibusdam compositionibus, ipsum Bertholdum ad ecclesiam Spirensem & eius munitiones traduxit, promissis inter alia domino de Wirtemberg, & post Argentinae solutis, marcis mille trecentis.
units.tr: When the death of the archbishop was heard, the count of Württemberg and other barons, who were occupying the strongholds of the church of Speyer, gave them back to Berchtold, so that he could not enter the see of Speyer. Berchtold, staying for a long time at Worms at great expense, was abandoned by his friends and others. Conrad of Kirkel, treasurer of Strasbourg, who took up his cause faithfully, made certain agreements with the aforesaid barons and led Berchtold into the church of Speyer and its strongholds. Among other promises made to the lord of Württemberg, and paid afterwards at Strasbourg, were 1300 marks.

units.la: Stante autem ipso Bertholdo in Luterburg, Hugo sibi apud papam, pro Moguntino archiepiscopatu instetit, quod papa ob dilationes & scripta magistri Ioannis Vnderschopff de Constantia, Decani Moguntinensis, quem praedictus quondam Mathias pauperem clericum suum, ad Canonicatum & decanatum promouit, tam diu distulit, quousque ipse decanus & Capitulum Maguntinense, dominū Baldewinum Treuerensem archiepiscopum, contra reseruationem sedis Apostolicae, in administratorem Maguntinae ecclesiae receperunt, sibi castris & munitionibus praesentatis.
units.tr: While Berchtold was staying at Lauterburg, Hugo pressed the pope on his behalf for the archbishopric of Mainz. But the pope delayed, because of the postponements and the writings of Master John Underschopf of Constance, dean of Mainz, whom the former Mathias had promoted from being his poor clerk to a canonry and the deanery. The dean and the chapter of Mainz received Lord Baldwin, archbishop of Trier, as administrator of the church of Mainz, against the reservation of the Apostolic See, after presenting him with castles and strongholds, and the pope delayed until then.

units.la: Quem archiepiscopatum, hoc facto prædictus Hugo, à papa volente pro fratre suo, tanquam ineuincibilem, renuit acceptare. De quo ipse papa Henrico præposito Bunnensi, fratri comitis de Firnenberg, repente prouidit. Qui tenente prædicto Baldeuino violenter multis annis ipsum archiepiscopatū penurias, tribulationes, & angustias est perpessus. Prædictus quoq; Ioannes Decanus, fratrib. domini sui Mathiæ, & aliis consanguineis suis, se post hæc infidelem ostendit.
units.tr: This archbishopric, once this had been done, the aforesaid Hugo refused to accept, since the pope wanted it for his own brother, as though it could not be won. The pope at once provided it to Henry, provost of Bonn, brother of the count of Firnenburg. While the aforesaid Baldwin held it by force, Henry suffered for many years want, tribulations and distress in the archbishopric. The aforesaid Dean John, too, afterwards showed himself faithless to the brothers of his lord Matthias and to his other kinsmen.

units.la: Decumbente autem Ioanne episcopo Argentinensi & de eius morte ad curiam rumore delato, papa Ioannis prædicto Bertholdo Spirensi electo, de Argentinensi episcopatu prouidit. Et quanuis cum ille viueret, doluerit se delusum, ac irascceretur Hugoni: intellecta tamen veritate mortis illius, nihilominus in memoriam defuncti Mathiæ, inuitis pluribus Cardinalibus, ipsi Bertholdo iterato prouidit. Geberhardo autem de Friburg præposito Argentinensi habente in se magnam partem Capituli, & ad episcopatū Argentinensem aspirante, ipsi Bertholdo obstaculū faciente: ipse Bertholdus acquisitis pro maxima pecunia dominis & Baronibus terræ, & melioribus in ciuitate Argentinensi, mediante dicto thesaurario, sibi fideliter adhærenti, desistente etiam dicto præposito: Argentinam cum sexcentis galeatis potentissimè est ingressus, in festo sancti Thomæ, anno Domini, M. CCC. XXVIII, iura & munitiones ecclesiæ obtinendo quietè.
units.tr: When John, bishop of Strasbourg, lay ill and word of his death reached the curia, the pope provided Berthold, the elected bishop of Speyer, to the bishopric of Strasbourg. Although John, while he was still alive, was angry at having been deceived and was incensed against Hugo, yet, when the truth of his death became known, the pope nonetheless, out of regard for the memory of the deceased Matthias and against the wishes of many cardinals, provided Berthold a second time. Geberhard of Freiburg, provost of Strasbourg, had a large part of the chapter on his side and aspired to the bishopric of Strasbourg, and he put an obstacle in Berthold's way. Berthold, however, won over the lords and barons of the land and the better men of the city of Strasbourg for a very large sum of money, through the aforesaid treasurer, who was faithfully attached to him, and the aforesaid provost also gave up his claim. Berthold then entered Strasbourg most powerfully, with six hundred mailed horsemen, on the feast of St Thomas in the year of the Lord 1328, and obtained the rights and fortresses of the church quietly.

units.la: Hic Bertholdus duas filias sororis suæ de Sigenowe, vnam Conrado comiti Friburgensi: alteram Vlrico domino in Schwartzenberg, & filiam sororis suæ de Munsingen, Dieterico de domo, solutis per eum duobus, tradidit in vxores. Hæ omnes filiæ, quasi ex quadam simplicitate faciat, viris suis sciunt se amabiles ad amplexus venereos exhibere, & ideo liberis sunt felices. Hic Bertholdus ex nimiis debitis anxius, cùm à Iudæis suis trecentas marcas mutuo habere non posset, de concordi consilio suorum, dicentium Iudæos excoriasse populum suū, vna sabbato hora prima, omnes Iudæos suos capiens sex millia marcarum recepit ab ipsis. Iudæi autem non minùs sub ipso manentes, in breui postea in oppido suo Mutziche, clam masculum annorum XI, necauerunt, qui post clamorem populorum contra Iudæos, sub rota molendini inuentus est, in vno latere habens vulnera infinita: & tortis quibusdam ex Iudæis, & consitentibus maleficium, & ex perspicuis indiciis, contra eos sententia est prolata. Et positis tribus super rotis, alij diuites Iudæi, qui die illo, quo masculus disparuit, inibi fuerant, sunt proscripti: & captis aliquibus, aliis Columbariam fugientibus, contra quos, Officialis Basiliensis ad requisitionem iudicij in Mutziche, eorum exequendo sententiam, sua iurisdictione processit: à quibus etiam dictus episcopus, duo millia marcarum extorsit.
units.tr: Berthold gave in marriage two daughters of his sister of Sigenowe, one to Count Conrad of Freiburg and the other to Ulrich, lord of Schwartzenberg, and the daughter of his sister of Münsingen to Dietrich von Domo, after he had paid off two of them. All these daughters, as if out of a certain simplicity, know that they are pleasing to their husbands in venereal embraces, and for this reason they are blessed with children. Berthold, anxious over his heavy debts, could not borrow three hundred marks from his Jews. By the united counsel of his people, who said that the Jews had flayed their own people, he seized all his Jews on a Sabbath at the first hour and received six thousand marks from them. The Jews, however, remaining under him no less, shortly afterwards secretly killed a boy of eleven years in his town of Mutzig. After the outcry of the people against the Jews, the boy was found under a mill-wheel, with countless wounds on one side. Some of the Jews were tortured and confessed the crime, and on the clear evidence sentence was pronounced against them. Three were placed upon the wheel. The other rich Jews who had been there on the day the boy disappeared were outlawed, and some were captured while others fled to Colmar. Against these the official of Basel, at the request of the court at Mutzig, proceeded under his jurisdiction to carry out their sentence. From them too the said bishop extorted two thousand marks.

units.la: Hic Bertholdus diu Spirensem & Argentinensem Episcopatus tenuit, Spirensem gubernatorem se scribens, quousq; Iohannes papa Walramo de Veldentze decano ecclesiæ Argentinensis & præposito Spirensis, de episcopatu Spirensi prouidit. Contra quem ipse Bertholdus ratione grauium expensarum, diu munitiones Spirensis tenuit cum magno scandalo, ipsas super turribus de Argentina cibando. Familia autem comitis de Wirtemberg Walramo assistentes, oppidum Bruchsal fraude coeperunt. Castrum verò Rottenburg vi ab ipso Bertholdo, captis qui ex parte sui desuper fuerant, est euictum. Kiselowe verò & Luterburg tenuit, quousque sibi à Iohanne papa, quòd hæc dimitteret, est præceptū. De quo ipse papa poenitens (audito, quòd ipse Walramus, Ludowico Principi à se damnato, obedientiam fecerat) ipsi Bertholdo, vt munitiones retineret, quas iam resignauit, rescripsit.
units.tr: Berthold held the bishoprics of Speyer and Strasbourg for a long time, styling himself governor of Speyer, until Pope John provided Walram of Veldenz, dean of the church of Strasbourg and provost of Speyer, to the bishopric of Speyer. Against him Berthold himself, on account of heavy expenses, held the fortifications of Speyer for a long time, to great scandal, supplying them with food from the towers of Strasbourg. The retainers of the Count of Württemberg, who supported Walram, took the town of Bruchsal by treachery. The castle of Rottenburg, however, was taken by force by Berthold himself, after those who were on his side above it had been captured. He held Kiselowe and Luterburg until Pope John ordered him to give them up. The pope himself, repenting of this (having heard that Walram had made his submission to Prince Louis, whom the pope had condemned), wrote back to Berthold that he might keep the fortresses which he had already resigned.

units.la: Creuit autem magna inuidia inter Bertholdum & comitem supradictos. Cum autem idem comes de Wirtemberg, tempore Iohannis episcopi, eo inuito, à Waltero & Burckardo dominis de Horburg, carentibus liberis, dominium de Horburg (cuius magna pars, ab ecclesia Argentinensi tenebatur, in Feudum) pro septem millibus marcis emisset, relicto vsu fructu eorum, cuilibet suæ partis, & partem iam mortui Waltheri teneret: ipse Bertholdus conuocatis suæ ecclesiæ Vasallis, & ad requisitionem sui in genere factam, pronunciato per eos, quòd Feudum alienatum à Vasallo sine domini consensu, ad dominum devoluteretur: congregato exercitu, se
units.tr: Great enmity now grew between Berthold and the aforesaid count. The same Count of Württemberg, in the time of Bishop John and against his wishes, had bought the lordship of Horburg for seven thousand marks from Walter and Burkhard, lords of Horburg, who had no children. He left them the usufruct of their respective parts and held the part of the already dead Walter. Berthold himself summoned the vassals of his church, and at the general request of his people, they declared that a fief alienated by a vassal without the lord's consent reverts to the lord. Having gathered an army, he set himself

units.la: P posuit in Osteim, prope Cellenberg, volens totum dominium in Horburg euincere. Et habito tractatu, cum dictus comes & Burckardus de Horburg, resistere non possent, concordati sunt, quòd datis per episcopum comiti sexcentis marcis, comes de omnibus cederet, quæ prædicti fratres in feudum ab ecclesia tenuerunt, scilicet Zellenberg castrum oppidum, villam, cum omnibus bannis & attinentiis. Item Benwilre: item redditus viginti marcarum de Egensheim. Item curiam in Wettelsheim, cum hominibus suis: Item ius quod dicitur, die Scheffa, cum quibusdam aliis, quorum suam partem dictus Burckardus pro vita sua tenere deberet, post eius obitum ad Argentinensem ecclesiam devoluendam, non obstante etiam si liberos procrearet: & sic posito vexillo episcopi ad castrum Zellenberg, ipsum possedit per suos, per sex hebdomadas & tres dies. Licet autem ipsi episcopus & comes, sic reformati fuerant: comes tamen episcopo inuidebat.
units.tr: at Osteim, near Zellenberg, wishing to recover the whole lordship of Horburg. After negotiation, since the said count and Burkhard of Horburg could not resist, they agreed that the bishop would give the count six hundred marks, and the count would cede everything that the aforesaid brothers held in fief from the church: namely the castle, town and village of Zellenberg with all its banns and appurtenances; likewise Benwihr; likewise the revenue of twenty marks from Eguisheim; likewise the court at Wettolsheim with its men; likewise the right called die Scheffa, with certain others. Of these, Burkhard was to hold his share for his lifetime, and after his death it was to revert to the church of Strasbourg, even if he should have children. So the bishop's banner was set up at the castle of Zellenberg, and he held it through his men for six weeks and three days. Although the bishop and the count had thus been reconciled, the count nevertheless envied the bishop.

units.la: Post hæc cum Reinboldus miles de Stouffenberg Albertum militem de Owe, episcopi seruitorem, in sua parte castri Stoffenberg molestaret, nec in ipsa parte sinueret commorari. Episcopus monitis Argentinensibus, sibi tunc coniuratis, idem castrum potenter obsedit, & funditus demoliuit: propter quod Rodolphus Marchio de Baden, dictus de Pfortzheim, cuius seruitor extitit Reinboldus prædictus, de auxilio comitis de Wirtemberg, per dominium Rodolphi Marchionis senioris de Baden, dilecti affinis episcopi, ex alia parte Rheni, terram ecclesiæ Argentinensis & eius homines, inuaserunt. Requisitus autem sæpè per episcopum, prædictus Marchio ne talia fieri sineret per terram suam, respondit: se non esse episcopi ianitorem: propter quod ipse episcopus monitis Argentinensibus, terram Marchionis potenter ingressus, ipsam præter munitiones, ignis incendio deuastauit, comite de Wirtemberg cum quadringentis galeatis existente cum Marchione prædicto, ita quod episcopus Stolhoffen & Baden quæ obsederat, euincere non valebat. Relicto autem exercitu in terra Marchionis, episcopus cum ducentis armatis ad villam Hergesheim prope Landawe, rogatus per Ottonem ducem Austriæ, ad colloquium, quod idem Dux cum rege Bohemiæ habuerat, est profectus. In qua villa Rex & Dux prædicti, & cum Duce prædictus Argentinensis,& Rodolphus Constantiensis episcopi: Cum rege verò Walramus Spirensis prouisus, & frater eius comes de Veldenze, & prædictus de Wirtemberg, vtrinque cum multis comitibus & Baronibus, conuenerunt. Vbi idem Otto in crepusculo noctis iurauit, eiusdem regis filiam se ducturum: ipsáque nocte nimis tenebrosa, idem episcopus per sylvam cum suis non sine cura ad oppidum Luterburg, quod adhuc tenuit, est profectus, in ipso egressu, se quasi ad conflictum disponens: cum prædicti, prouisus Spirensis, & duo comites, eius capitales existerent inimici: & crastino ad exercitum rediens, terra Marchionis combusta recessit. Prædictus autem Dux, cuius & suorum Marchiones ab antiquo fuerant seruitores, conuenientib. ad eū in Bischoffsheim iuxta Rhenum, episcopo, comite, Marchionibus & Reinboldo prædictis, ipsos, data Reinboldo per Ducem certa summa, & concessso vt Stouffenberg reædificaret, totaliter reformauit.
units.tr: Afterwards, when Reinbold, a knight of Stauffenberg, harassed Albert, a knight of Ow and servant of the bishop, in his part of the castle of Stauffenberg, and would not allow him to remain in that part, the bishop, with the men of Strasbourg who had sworn to him, powerfully besieged the same castle and razed it to the ground. On account of this, Margrave Rudolf of Baden, called of Pforzheim, whose servant Reinbold was, with the aid of the Count of Württemberg, invaded the land of the church of Strasbourg and its people from the other side of the Rhine, through the lordship of the elder Margrave Rudolf of Baden, a beloved kinsman of the bishop. Often asked by the bishop to stop such things being done through his land, the aforesaid margrave replied that he was not the bishop's doorkeeper. Therefore the bishop himself, with the men of Strasbourg, entered the margrave's land in force and laid it waste with fire, apart from the fortifications. The Count of Württemberg was with the aforesaid margrave with four hundred mailed men, so that the bishop could not take Stollhofen and Baden, which he had besieged. Leaving his army in the margrave's land, the bishop went with two hundred armed men to the village of Hergesheim near Landau, at the request of Duke Otto of Austria, for a conference which the same duke had held with the King of Bohemia. In that village the said king and duke met, with the duke the aforesaid bishop of Strasbourg and Rudolf, bishop of Constance; with the king came Walram, provided to Speyer, and his brother the Count of Veldenz, and the aforesaid Württemberg, with many counts and barons on both sides. There Otto swore at nightfall that he would marry the king's daughter. On that very dark night the same bishop went with his men through the forest, not without care, toward the town of Luterburg, which he still held, and on leaving he prepared himself as though for battle, since the aforesaid Walram, provost of Speyer, and the two counts were his chief enemies. Returning to the army the next day, and having burned the margrave's land, he withdrew. The aforesaid duke, whose margraves had been his servants from of old, gathered the bishop, the count, the margraves and the aforesaid Reinbold to himself at Bischoffsheim on the Rhine, and completely reconciled them. Reinbold was given a certain sum by the duke, and was permitted to rebuild Stauffenberg.

units.la: Iis autem temporibus mortuis succesiue Magnificis Principibus, Henrico, & postea strenuissimo Lupoldo, & tertio serenissimo, Friderico, qui pro rege se gessit, Austriæ ducibus, ac domino Ludouico de Vrbe (vbi à Populo Romano in Imperatorem coronatus fuit: vbi filium ex vxore sua genuit: vbi Antipapam creauit in odium Domini Ioannis Papæ, quem è contra Hæreticum asserluit) in Alemanniam reuersó: Iohannes papa pro impediendo eodem Ludouico, apud Duces Austriæ & per se creatos episcopos, feruenter instetit. Et ecce Dux Otto de Austria, cum auxilio prædicti Bertholdi Argentinensis, & Rudolphi Constantiensis episcoporum sibi vnitorum, Columbariam diu potenter obsedit, eodem domino Ludouico cum rege Bohemiæ, comite de Wirtemberg, & multis potentibus è contrario Hagenoiam veniente. Prædictus autem Berchtoldus episcopus habens circa Munziche armatos multos, apud Ducem, vt contra dominum Ludouicum descendet incessanter instetit. Egrediente autem dicto Berchtoldo, vno dierum de oppido suoBenesuo Benefelt versus Mollesbeim, comes de Wirtemberg credens episcopum versus Argentinam iturum, cum ducentis armatis versus Benefelt ad insidiandum episcopo, est profectus. Cumque quatuor praecedentes appropinquantes portæ Benefelt, ibi neminem inuenissent (erant enim omnes incolæ pro habendo consilio sub Lobio congregati) vnum miserant qui xx, eos sequentes, sustinere præcepit. Qui vno misso pro sequentibus, portam celeriter sunt ingressi, certantes cum incolis, quousque & cæteri aduenerunt. Et sic comes obtento oppido multis septimanis, eiectis incolis, omnia sibi vsurpauit. Credente autem papa & episcopis, quòd Dux vellet Domino Ludouico, more fratrum, viliter aduersari, iam enim papa nuntiis Ducis respônderat, quòd ei l, milia florenorum dare vellet, & ad suâ voluntatem cöferre episcopatus Alemanniæ vacaturos: ecce Dux reformatus est cum domino Ludouico, sibi Brisaco Nuwenburg, & quibusdam aliis munitionibus: Regi verò Bohemiæ Keisersberg & multis aliis munitionibus, pro certis pecuniæ quantitatibus assignatis: episcopo Benefelt vacuo restituto, & pro damnis quatuor millib. marcis promissis, & raro solutis. Sicq; delusò papa & episcopis, princeps cum prædictis, rege & Duce, per Alsatiam, Basileam, & (vt supra) receptis homagiis, potenter transiuit.
units.tr: After these times, the magnificent princes Henry, then the most valiant Leopold, and third the most serene Frederick, who acted as king, dukes of Austria, and Lord Louis of Rome (where he was crowned emperor by the Roman people, where he begot a son by his wife, and where he created an antipope out of hatred for Lord John the Pope, whom in turn he declared a heretic) had died one after another, and Louis returned to Germany. Pope John vigorously pressed the dukes of Austria, and the bishops he had himself appointed, to hinder Louis. And behold, Duke Otto of Austria, with the help of the aforesaid Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, and Rudolf, bishop of Constance, who had joined him, laid a long and powerful siege to Colmar, while Lord Louis, with the king of Bohemia, the count of Württemberg and many powerful men, came against them to Hagenau. The said Bishop Berthold, having many armed men near Munich, pressed the duke unceasingly to march against Lord Louis. But as Berthold was leaving one day from his town of Benfeld towards Mollsheim, the count of Württemberg, believing the bishop was going to Strasbourg, set out with two hundred armed men towards Benfeld to lie in wait for him. When four of his men, going ahead, came near the gate of Benfeld and found no one there (for all the inhabitants had gathered under the linden tree to hold a council), he ordered one of them to send back word for the twenty who followed to wait. One of them was sent back for the rest, and they quickly entered the gate, fighting with the inhabitants until the others arrived too. And so the count, having taken the town, drove out the inhabitants and seized everything for himself, and held it for many weeks. Meanwhile the pope and the bishops believed that the duke, in the manner of brothers, would meekly oppose Lord Louis; for the pope had already answered the duke's messengers that he was willing to give him fifty thousand florins and to confer on him the bishoprics of Germany as they fell vacant at his will. Behold, however, the duke was reconciled with Lord Louis, and was given Breisach, Neuenburg and some other fortresses; the king of Bohemia received Kaysersberg and many other fortresses, for fixed sums of money; and the bishop had Benfeld restored to him empty, with four thousand marks promised for his losses, though these were seldom paid. Thus the pope and the bishops were deceived, and the prince, with the said king and duke, passed powerfully through Alsace and Basel, having received homage as described above.

units.la: Post hæc Conradus & Ioannes de Schouwenburg dicti de Winterbach de auxilio quorundam seruitorum electi Spirensis & comitis de Wirtemberg, oppidum Oberkirche, positis scalis de nocte furtim apprehendere tentauerat, sed ruptis scalis & audita ruptura, vigiles clamantes, incolas vocauerunt, ita quòd conatus non habebat effectum. Propter quod idem Bertholdus episcopus, non solùm dictos duos sed omnes de Schawenberg quorum aliquos olim Ioannes episcopus delicatè fouerat, depauperauit quantum potuit & destruxit: Conrado Risen tunc aduocato suo in Vlemburg ipsos persequente ad vnguem: castrum autem Schowenburg habere nequibat. Econtra autem homines ecclesiæ illius districtus, per multos dominos, illis assistentes, damna & in corpore & in rebus plurima sunt perpessi. De Schmalstein autem miles, super optimo castro Wineftein, sustinens Conradum de Winterbach, episcopum ad multas coegit expensas: propter quod ipse episcopus & Hagennowenses, quos etiam idem miles læserat, idem castrum x hebdomadis potenter obsidentes, quatuor machinis, duobus cattis; & lxxx fossoribus ipsum funditus destruxerunt. Et antequam discederet de loco episcopus, obiit Burckardus dominus de Horburg: & aduocatus Rubiacensis castrum Zellenberg obsidens, ipsum & oppidum cum villa Bebelnheim & omnibus attinentiis, apprehendit. Nam dominus altæ Rapoltzsteinæ, cuius sororem habuit dictus Burckardus, prædicta omnia, nomine infantis prædictæ sororis, detinere volebat: quem infantem prædictus Burckardus de Horburg, cum natus iam esset, post prædictam compositionem, Tardum seu Spaten vocauit, dicens quòd in duobus annis nunquam cognoucrit matrem eius. Et sic hodie ecclesia Argentinensis tenet illam partem dominij in Horburg quietè.
units.tr: After this, Conrad and John of Schauenburg, called of Winterbach, with the help of some servants of the elect of Speyer and of the count of Württemberg, tried secretly at night to take the town of Oberkirch by setting up ladders. But the ladders broke, and at the noise of the breaking the watchmen cried out and called the townspeople, so that the attempt had no effect. For this reason Bishop Berthold impoverished and destroyed as far as he could not only the two named men but all the Schauenburgs, some of whom Bishop John had formerly cherished with favour; his advocate Conrad Risen pursued them to the last detail in Ullenburg. The castle of Schauenburg, however, he could not take. On the other hand, the men of the church of that district suffered great losses both in person and in property at the hands of many lords who supported them. Meanwhile the knight of Schmalstein, holding the excellent castle of Wineck against Conrad of Winterbach, forced the bishop to very great expense. Because of this, the bishop himself and the men of Hagenau, whom the same knight had also injured, besieged that castle powerfully for ten weeks, and with four engines, two cats, and eighty diggers they utterly destroyed it. Before the bishop left the place, Burkhard, lord of Horburg, died; and the advocate of Rappoltsweiler, besieging the castle of Zellenberg, seized it together with the town of Bebelnheim and all its appurtenances. For the lord of Hohenrappoltstein, whose sister Burkhard had as his wife, wanted to keep all these things in the name of the infant of that sister. Burkhard of Horburg, when the child was born after the aforesaid agreement, called him Tardus or Spaten, saying that in two years he had never known his mother. And so today the church of Strasbourg quietly holds that part of the lordship of Horburg.

units.la: Illis diebus Waltherus de Tuwingen, dominus in Gerolsecke, in Swannowe & in Schuttera, quique oppidum Erstein tenuit nomine pignoris, in quibusdam læsit Argentinenses. Regnabant autem tunc Argentinæ populares, exclusis nobilibus, propter magnam cædem multorum nobilium, inter Zornones & Mulnheimnenses, & eorum partes factam. Et ecce in die Parasceue mane venientes Argentini oppidû Erstein expugnantes coeperunt, cuius muros & turres post destructionem castri Swannowe, funditus destruxerant. Ipsi quoque & episcopus prædictus, item Basilienses & Friburgenses, & omnes ciuitates imperij harum partium, castrum Swannowe fortissimum, & in omni Alemannia, propter nimia mala inde facta, famosum, illico vigorosissimè, & cum omnib. parametis, quæ excogitari quasi poterant, obsederunt: facientes pontem cū nauibus vltra Rhenû. Transeuntes quoque de obsidione oppidum Schutter & solenne monasterium, ignis incendio vastauerunt, muris oppidi funditus demolitis: quibus postea reparatis, denuò ab Argentinensibus demoliuntur, anno domini, M. CCC.XXXIIII in autumno. Victo etiam castro Swannowe, & radicitùs demolito, vnus miles & alij xlix,
units.tr: In those days Walter of Tuwingen, lord of Geroldseck, Schwanau and Schuttern, who held the town of Erstein as a pledge, wronged some of the Strasbourgers. At that time the common people ruled Strasbourg, with the nobles excluded, because of a great slaughter of many nobles that had taken place between the Zorn and Mülnheim factions. And behold, on the morning of Good Friday the Strasbourgers came and began to storm the town of Erstein, whose walls and towers they had utterly destroyed after the destruction of the castle of Schwanau. They, the bishop just mentioned, the Baselers and the Freiburgers, and all the free cities of those regions, at once besieged the very strong castle of Schwanau most vigorously, with every siege engine that could almost be devised, famous throughout all Alemannia for the great evils done from it. They built a bridge across the Rhine with ships. Passing over from the siege, they laid waste the town of Schuttern and its famous monastery with fire, and tore down the walls of the town utterly. These were afterwards repaired, but were demolished again by the Strasbourgers in the autumn of the year of the Lord 1334. After the castle of Schwanau was also taken and razed to the ground, one knight and forty-nine others

units.la: Bellum Argentinense contra Gerolzeckium anno 1333. Erstein. Schwannow. Schuttern. qui ipsum custodierant, capite sunt truncati. Magistri quoque carpentarij, & fabri qui intus fuerant, ligati tanquam lapides versus castrum machinis sunt proiecti. Episcopus autem cum suis equitibus, & omni multitudine garcionum de Swanowe transcendens, villam Steinbach sub castro Yberg, quod tum tenuerunt pignore comites de Oetingen, aduersarij episcopi, & tres domus vallatas in ipsa villa, quarum domini auxiliatores fuerunt eorundem de Schowenberg, ignis incendio demoliuit.
units.tr: War of Strasbourg against Geroldseck, 1333. Erstein. Schwanau. Schuttern. who had guarded it were beheaded. The master carpenters and smiths who had been inside were bound like stones and hurled against the castle by siege engines. The bishop, with his horsemen and the whole crowd of servants, crossed over from Schwanau and burned to the ground the village of Steinbach below the castle of Yberg, which the counts of Oettingen, enemies of the bishop, then held as a pledge, and three fortified houses in that village, whose lords had been helpers of the same Schauenburgs.

units.la: Incitabant autem illis diebus praedicti comitis de Wirtemberg & de Oetingen dominum Ludouicum Principem contra episcopum. Qui princeps episcopum, vt ei faceret homagium de regalibus suis, indicto exercitu infestauit. episcopus autem e contra de auxilio episcopi Metensis & Ducis Lotharingiae, qui sibi coniurauerant, exercitum congregauit. Manente autem pro tunc Principe, episcopus oppidum Richenwilro comitis de Witemberg expugnauit, de ipso oppido, sibi fidelitatem praestante, plurima vina traducens. Nitebatur autem exercitum suum traducere Rhenum, ad obsidendum Offenburg & Gengenbach oppida imperij: sed in Gallicis maxime propter auram mutatam, habere nequiuit. Reuersis autem Gallicis positisque multis armigeris in oppida Reineken & Oberkirche, pro eorum custodia, quae oppida praedicta Imperij plurimum infestabant, episcopus ad pratum iuxta Vinstingen, vbi indictum fuit duellum, inter Ioannem fratrem comitis de Sarwerdc, & Henricum dominum de Vinstingen, ad eundem Henricum seruitorem & vasallum suum, cum ccc galeatis accessit. Expectante autem in termino eodem Henrico armato intra circulum, aduersarius qui in eo loco duellum obtulit, prae multitudine quae ad Henricum venerat, (habuit enim circa quatuor millia galeatorum, exceptis peditibus) accedere non audebat. Plures autem quibus oppidum Reinekem commissum fuerat cum ad duellum accessissent: Ecce praedicti comites de Wirtemberg & de Oetingen oppidum Reineken viriliter expugnarunt, duodecim armigeros, & rusticos qui ibi remanserant capientes, qui tamen se quantum poterant viriliter tenuerunt, Henricum de Lapide militem comitis de Wirtemberg validissimum, occidentes. Vnus autem captiuorum incola oppidi euadens, circa meridiem, cum esset intensus calor, oppidum in pluribus locis incendit, ita quod comes de Oetingen & sui, qui in oppido remanserant, vix euadentes, in equis & armis damnificati sunt.
units.tr: In those days the aforesaid counts of Württemberg and Oettingen were stirring up Lord Louis, the prince, against the bishop. The prince, in order to make the bishop do him homage for his royal rights, attacked him with an army he had called up. The bishop, on the other hand, gathered an army with the help of the bishop of Metz and the duke of Lorraine, who had sworn an alliance with him. While the prince remained at that time, the bishop stormed the town of Rhinau, belonging to the count of Württemberg, and led away a great quantity of wine from the town itself, which swore fealty to him. He strove to lead his army across the Rhine to besiege the free towns of Offenburg and Gengenbach, but he could not manage it, chiefly because of the French, who were unwilling to go because of the changed air. When the French had returned and many men-at-arms had been posted in the towns of Rheinau and Oberkirch to guard them, since these free towns were greatly harassed, the bishop went with three hundred helmeted men to a meadow near Wingen, where a duel had been announced between John, brother of the count of Saarwerden, and Henry, lord of Finstingen, against Henry, his servant and vassal. Henry waited within the lists, armed, at the appointed place; but his opponent, who had challenged him to a duel there, did not dare to come forward, because of the great number who had come to Henry (he had about four thousand helmeted men, besides foot soldiers). Meanwhile, while several of those to whom the town of Rheinau had been entrusted had gone to the duel, behold, the aforesaid counts of Württemberg and Oettingen valiantly stormed the town of Rheinau, capturing twelve men-at-arms and the peasants who had remained there. These, however, defended themselves as bravely as they could, and killed Henry of Stein, a very strong knight of the count of Württemberg. One of the captured townsmen, escaping, set fire to the town in several places about midday, when the heat was intense, so that the count of Oettingen and his men who had remained in the town barely escaped, and were injured in their horses and arms.

units.la: Venit autem Princeps quasi latenter repente Hagenogiam, cum magna multitudine armatorum. Episcopus autem quasi perplexus cum gentes praesertim Gallicas, quae nuper ab eo recesserant, adeo celeriter rehabere non posset: cum suis equitibus quos habere poterat, in castrum suum Kochersberg, collocauit. Intrusus autem per Principem in ecclesia Herbipolensi contra prouisionem papae, scilicet dominus de Liechtenberg in Sueuia, scholasticus Spirensis, cancellarius Principis, cum valde circa Herbipolim Principis indigeret, concordiam inter Principem & episcopum ordinauit, scilicet, quod ipse episcopus Principis officiatos in Alsatia non impedire, sed promouere deberet. Pro tunc autem homagium renuit exhibere.
units.tr: The Prince suddenly came to Hagenau, as it were secretly, with a large force of armed men. The bishop, as if bewildered, could not quickly regain the French troops who had lately left him, so he withdrew with the horsemen he could muster into his castle at Kochersberg. John of Liechtenberg, lord of Liechtenberg in Swabia, scholasticus of Speyer and chancellor of the Prince, had been intruded into the church of Würzburg by the Prince, against the papal provision. Since the Prince greatly needed him around Würzburg, he arranged a concord between the Prince and the bishop, namely that the bishop should not hinder but should promote the Prince's officials in Alsace. At that time, however, the bishop refused to render homage.

units.la: Erat autem liga pacis illis diebus, inter Argentinenses, Basilienses, & Friburgenses quibus episcopus (nisi & ipse contra eos cgnoscere deberet, quando sibi assistere tenerentur, sicut quaelibet praedictarum ciuitatum in suo facto cognouit) vniri noluebat, sed cum terra ducum Austriae ligam contraxit.
units.tr: There was then a league of peace among the Strasbourgers, the Baselers and the Freiburgers, which the bishop refused to join (unless he too might take cognizance against them when they were bound to assist him, as each of those cities had taken cognizance of its own case). Instead he made a league with the lands of the dukes of Austria.

units.la: Tempore autem Benedicti papae, cum Bertholdus episcopus Argentinensis monuisset omnes rectores ecclesiarum, & alios ad sacerdotium adstrictos, vt ad sacros ordines ascenderent, & ob hoc conspirantibus contra eum Geberhardo de Friburg praeposito: Conrado de Kirkel thesaurario, & quasi toto Capitulo, multisque de clero, multisque appellationibus interpositis, ad sedem Apostolicam, factisque per episcopum absolutionibus ad cautelam, renouatisque processibus & iterum appellato, inter episcopum & clerum graue nimis scandalum est subortum.
units.tr: In the time of Pope Benedict, Berthold, bishop of Strasbourg, admonished all the rectors of churches and others bound to the priesthood to advance to holy orders. On account of this, Geberhard of Freiburg, provost, Conrad of Kirkel, treasurer, and almost the whole chapter, together with many of the clergy, conspired against him.
