Many appeals were lodged with the Apostolic See, and the bishop, as a precaution, issued absolutions and renewed the proceedings, and again appeal was made. Thus a very grave scandal arose between the bishop and the clergy.

units.la: Mortuo autem illis diebus Ioanne de Chabilone episcopo Lingonensi, & administratore Basiliensis ecclesiarum, qui & eo tempore castrum Pfefingen, Walrami comitis rami comitis de Tierstein, potenter obsedit: capitulum Basiliense Ioannem Sennen, filium sororis prædicti Argentinensis episcopi, in pastorem elegit. Quem cum archiepiscopus Bisuntinus, ob scripta papæ, non confirmaret: Idem electus cum auuncu-lo suo Hugone comite de Buchecke, ac pluribus comitibus, Canonicis, & magistro civitatis Basiliensis, ad curiam proficiscens, ac per annum post renunciationem in consistorio per se factam (eò quod Capitulum Basiliense olim fuit perpetuo iure eligendi priuatum) in curia manens: tandem ob fauorem ipsius Hugonis, per Benedictum papam prouisus extitit, & in curia consecratus.
units.tr: In those days John of Chabeuil, bishop of Langres and administrator of the church of Basel, died. At that time he was also vigorously besieging the castle of Pfeffingen, belonging to Count Walram of Thierstein. The chapter of Basel then elected as minister John Senn, the son of the sister of the aforesaid bishop of Strasbourg. When the archbishop of Besançon, because of the papal letters, would not confirm him, the same elect went to the court together with his uncle Count Hugo of Buchegg, several counts, canons and the master of the city of Basel. He had renounced the election in consistory himself, since the chapter of Basel had formerly been deprived of the perpetual right of electing, and he remained at court for a year. At last, through the favour of Hugo himself, he was provided by Pope Benedict and consecrated at court.

units.la: Mortuo autem Gebehardo præposito Argentinensi, anno Dn. M.CCC. XXXVII, 10 in die sanctæ Petronellæ, ac Ioanne de Liechtenberg, & Vlrico de Sygenowe, filio sororis prædicti Bertholdi episcopi, in discordia ad præposituram electis, ac Vlrico per ipsum episcopum: Ioanne vero postea per Henricum archiepiscopum Maguntinum in discordia confirmatis: habentibus etiā Conrado de Kirkel, Nicolao de Kagenecke præposito sancti Petri Argentinensis & pluribus aliis rancorem & odium contra episcopum: ecce ipse episcopus in villa Hafelach, in curia præpositi, circa mediam noctem, per Rhodolphum de Hohenstein, & complices suos, & alios, prædictorum Conradi à Kirkel, & Iohannis de Liechtenberg familiares, captus, primùm ad castrū Waldecke, & postea ad castrum Kirckel adductus, honorificè sed tutissimè est detentus. Eductus autem fuit nudo corpore, sub anno domini M. CCC. XXXVII, 20 quarto idus Septembris. Quod intelligens Benedictus papa, illico prædicto Basiliensi episcopo, Argentinæ ecclesiæ administrationē committit, ac contra prædictū Conradū de Kirckel, & alios culpabiles processus durissimos destinauit. Rodolphus autē de Andelah Vicedominus episcopi, crastino captiuitatis, incœpit ab officiatis episcopi & munitionibus, quòd sibi parerent tempore captiuitatis, recipere iuramenta.
units.tr: When Gebhard, provost of Strasbourg, died in the year of the Lord 1337, on the day of St Petronilla, John of Liechtenberg and Ulrich of Sigenow, the bishop's sister's son, were elected to the provostship in dispute. Ulrich was confirmed by the bishop himself, and John afterwards by Henry, archbishop of Mainz, also in dispute. Conrad of Kirkel, Nicholas of Kagenecke, provost of St Peter at Strasbourg, and many others harboured rancour and hatred against the bishop. Then the bishop himself, at the village of Hafelach, in the provost's court, about midnight, was seized by Rudolf of Hohenstein and his accomplices and others, familiars of the aforesaid Conrad of Kirkel and John of Liechtenberg. He was first taken to the castle of Waldeck and afterwards to the castle of Kirkel, where he was held honourably but most securely. He was led out with his body bare, in the year of the Lord 1337, on the fourth day before the Ides of September. Learning of this, Pope Benedict at once committed the administration of the church of Strasbourg to the aforesaid bishop of Basel, and he sent very harsh processes against the said Conrad of Kirkel and the other guilty persons. Rudolf of Andlau, the bishop's vicedominus, on the day after the captivity, began to receive oaths from the bishop's officials and fortresses, that they would obey him during the captivity.

units.la: Venit autem illis diebus Argentinam Albertus Dux Austriæ, episcopi confœderatus de Aquisgrani, qui in peregrinatione descenderat, cuius intentio ad obsidendum Nuwilre, & alias munitiones Ioannis de Liechtenberg & Sigismundi fratris sui, omnimodè versabatur: sed officiati rehabere dominū quibusdam pactionibus nitebantur. Quamuis autem notorium fuerit, prædictum thesaurarium fuisse principalem detentorem, & habuit domicilium Argentinæ: quamuis etiam Vicarius episcopi decreuerit interdictum seruandum, iuxta Consilium prouinciale, quod & Augustinensibus placuisset: Prædicatores tamen & Minores, ac Clerus maioris ecclesiæ, non veritatem, sed affectum priuatum considerans, celebrarunt.
units.tr: At that time Duke Albert of Austria, a confederate of the bishop, came to Strasbourg from Aachen, where he had stopped on his pilgrimage. His whole intention was to besiege Neuweiler and the other fortresses of John of Liechtenberg and his brother Sigismund, but the officials sought to recover their lord by certain agreements. Although it was notorious that the aforesaid treasurer was the principal holder of the bishop and had his residence at Strasbourg, and although the bishop's vicar had decreed that the interdict must be observed, in accordance with the provincial council, which the Augustinians too had approved, the Preachers and the Minorites and the clergy of the greater church nevertheless held services, considering not the truth but their own private affection.

units.la: Fuit autem liga pacis illis diebus inter Argentinenses, Basilienses, & Friburgenses: item alia liga inter Argentinenses & oppida Imperij: item alia inter episcopum & Ducē Austriæ & terras ipsorū. Noluit enim episcopus esse in liga Argentinensiū, nisi & ipse cognoscere posset in suo sibi illato, sicut & ipsi habebant. Et ob hoc, & quia episcopus confirmauit Sigellinum de Mulnheim contra Vlricum Suffen, ad præposituram sancti Thomæ, Argentinensis, & ob hoc pars Zornonum prouocata fuerat 40 contra ipsum: à ciuitate Argentina auxiliū aliquod non habebat. Habuit autē ab ipso episcopo Conradus de Kirckel officialatū Argentinēsem, cū sigillo & cū emolumēto & potestate ponēdi officiatos: Itē Cantoriā Spirensem, & scholastriā Argentinensem cum Thesauraria, cum multis officiis & prebendis, ad suā voluntatē collatis. Venit autē episcopus Basiliensis ad castrū Dachenstein ecclesiæ Argentinensis, cōstituens Ioanne Erlini scholasticū S. Thomę vicariū priorē episcopatus, autoritate apostolica vicariū generalē. Qui facta autoritate Conradi prædicti penitus reuocauit, latis hinc inde mutuis excommunicationum sententiis & appellationibus interiectis. Tandē post multos tractatus amicorū episcopi, episcopus cū xvi hebdomadis captus iacuisset in Kirckel, cū multis fideiussoribus & obsidibus, cū variis pactis, inscijs 50 amicis, extitit liberatus, quorum fideiussorum aliqui in fauorem episcopi, aliqui se in fauorem Conradi strinxerūt. Inter alia autem pacta actum fuit, quòd dare deberet mille quingentas Marcas argenti: item procurare præposituram Argentinensem Ioanni de Liechtenberg: item multas ecclesias certis personis procurare: item prædictum Conradum cum viginti personis ab omni iurisdictione episcopi eximere: item quòd ecclesiam Argentinensem in spiritualibus & temporalibus regeret, iuxta consilium & consensum prædicti Conradi, & omnium amicorum eius amicitiam procuraret.
units.tr: There was then a league of peace among the Strasbourgers, the Baselers and the Freiburgers; likewise another league between the Strasbourgers and the towns of the Empire; and another between the bishop, the Duke of Austria and their lands. The bishop was unwilling to be in the Strasbourgers' league unless he too could take cognizance of the injury done to him, as they did. Because of this, and because the bishop confirmed Sigellin of Mulnheim against Ulrich Suffen for the provostship of St Thomas at Strasbourg, the party of Zorn had been provoked against him, and he had no aid from the city of Strasbourg. Conrad of Kirkel had received from the bishop the officialate of Strasbourg, together with the seal, the emoluments and the power of appointing officials; likewise the cantorship of Speyer and the scholastry of Strasbourg with the treasurership, with many offices and prebends, all conferred at his pleasure. The bishop of Basel came to the castle of Dachstein, belonging to the church of Strasbourg, and by apostolic authority appointed John Erlin, scholasticus of St Thomas, as general vicar and prior of the bishopric. Erlin, by the authority of the aforesaid Conrad, completely revoked those acts, and sentences of excommunication were hurled back and forth and appeals interposed. At last, after many negotiations by the bishop's friends, the bishop, who had lain sixteen weeks as a captive at Kirkel, was released, with many sureties and hostages and various pacts, without the knowledge of his friends. Some of the sureties bound themselves in the bishop's favour, others in Conrad's. Among the other pacts it was agreed that the bishop should give 1500 marks of silver; that he should procure the provostship of Strasbourg for John of Liechtenberg; that he should procure many churches for certain persons; that he should exempt the said Conrad and twenty persons from all the bishop's jurisdiction; and that he should govern the church of Strasbourg in spiritual and temporal matters according to the counsel and consent of the said Conrad, and secure the friendship of all Conrad's friends.

units.la: Episcopus autem Basilienfis & plures consanguineorum videntes episcopum sine eorum cautione dimissum, promiserunt inter se, nolle conuenire cum illis nisi de communi eorum placito, & specialiter, quòd nollent Vlricum de Sigenowe desistere à præpositura. Prima autem die captiuitatis episcopi, inclusa fuerunt eius Sigilla, & pluribus sigillis signata. Basilienfis autem etiam post liberationem episcopi, di- cens eum non plenè restitutum, per se & vicarium prædictum, iurisdictionem aliquandiu exercebat: prohibens episcopo restitui Sigilla vel prædicto Conrado in officialatu parere. Verùm tandem episcopus omnino volens rehabere sigilla, & rehabens, prædictum Conradum in omnem potestatem iurisdictionis restituit, in qua erat, & prædicto Ioanni de Liechtenberg, tanquam præposito parere præcepit. Expletis autem pluribus liberationis articulis, ac episcopo valde laborante, vt Basiliensis & cæteri amici reformationis literas sigillarent, sed non proficiente, eoque se offerente ad dandam in promptu prædictam pecuniam, & ad explendum illico omnes liberationis articulos sibi possibiles, & ad cauendum sufficienter de aliis articulis seruandis, & quàm primum posset explendis, & quòd sibi obsidum litera redderetur, nec aliquo modo apud prædictum Conradum posset liberationem obsidum obtinere: ipsos pro toto licut pro parte obstagium seruare promisit. Offerens se tamen ad liberandum eos totaliter, non in parte, prout aliqui sapientes & probissimi eum posse & debere decernerent, iuxta literam cautionis. Propter quòd iterum inter prædictos Conradum & Ioannem & eorum complices, graue scandalum est subortum.
units.tr: The bishop of Basel and several of the bishop's relatives, seeing him released without their security, promised one another not to agree to anything with those men except by common consent, and especially that they would not allow Ulrich of Sigenow to give up the provostship. On the first day of the captivity the bishop's seals had been shut up and marked with several seals. The bishop of Basel, even after the bishop's release, claimed that he had not been fully restored, and for some time exercised jurisdiction himself and through the aforesaid vicar. He forbade the seals to be returned to the bishop and forbade obedience to Conrad in the officialate. At last the bishop, wholly wishing to recover his seals, got them back, restored Conrad to all the power of jurisdiction he had held, and ordered obedience to John of Liechtenberg as provost. After several articles of the release had been fulfilled, the bishop, labouring hard, asked the bishop of Basel and his other friends to seal the letters of reform, but without success. He offered to pay the said money at once, to fulfil immediately all the articles of release that were possible for him, and to give sufficient security that the other articles would be observed and fulfilled as soon as he could; and he asked that the letter concerning the hostages be given back to him, since he could in no way obtain the release of the hostages from Conrad. He promised to keep them bound, wholly as well as in part. Yet he offered to free them entirely, not in part, as some wise and most upright men judged he could and ought to do, according to the wording of the security. On account of this, a grave scandal again arose between Conrad and John and their accomplices.

units.la: Veniente autem illis diebus Ludouico Principe Columbariam, prædicti Argentinensis & Basilienfis episcopi, ipsum cum magna armatorum multitudine accesserunt, qualiter circa Argentinensem actum est narrantes. Ille autem simulans se dolere, ad attrahendum eos suo seruitio insistebat: Argentinensis autem congregationem episcoporum prouinciæ Maguntinæ persuasit. Quibus ferè Spiræ congregatis, ac Henrico Archiepiscopo Moguntino similiter sedis Apostolicæ prouiso (qui & ipse Principi se colligauerat) ad inducendum in id ipsum Argentinensem, plurimùm laborante: communi consilio missi sunt, Vlricus episcopus Curiensis, & Gerlacus comes de Nassowe, ex parte episcoporum Maguntinæ prouinciæ, ad papam & Cardinales, pro reformatione Principis laborantes, quibus papa præ timore regis Franciæ annuere non audebat: sicque infecto negotio celeriter sunt reuersi. Interim autem facta est liga pacis generalis, de authoritate Principis in Alsatia, tam per episcopum, quam ciuitates, ix cognitoribus desuper constitutis. Rodolphus autem & alij de Hohenstein, Castrum Hohenstein, cuius maior pars fuit episcopi Argentinensis, pro se tenentes, ab ipso castro custodes episcopi excluserunt. Restituto autem episcopo ad mandatum nouem cognitorum, episcopus afferens ipsos de Hohenstein infregisse pacta castri: idem castrum fortissimum funditus demoliuit. Papa autem Benedictus denuntians iuramenta episcopi & obsidum nulla, & relaxans, dedit executores, qui contra prædictum Conradum & sibi assistentes multipliciter procedendo, ipsum Conradum, Ioannem de Schwartzenberg decanum, & plures Canonicos, & alios prælatos, & Clericos, suis ecclesiis & prælaturis ordine iudiciario denunciando priuatos, ac ipsorum beneficiorum redditus colligendo, prædictum quoque Vlricum de Sygenowe in præposituram restituens, fructus collegit eiusdem, prædicto Ioanne de Lichtenberg etiam fructus præposituræ quos colligere potuit, colligente. Prædicti quoque Conradus & Ioannes eorumq; complices villam Gugenheim episcopi, & quasdam adiacentes, incendio deuastarunt.
units.tr: When in those days Prince Ludwig came to Columbaria, the aforesaid bishops of Strasbourg and Basel came to him with a large force of armed men and told him how things had gone around Strasbourg. He, pretending to be sorry, kept working to draw them into his service, and he persuaded the bishop of Strasbourg to a gathering of the bishops of the Mainz province. When they had nearly assembled at Speyer, and Archbishop Henry of Mainz, likewise appointed by the Apostolic See (who had also bound himself to the Prince), laboured hard to bring the bishop of Strasbourg into the same course, it was agreed by common counsel to send Ulrich, bishop of Chur, and Count Gerlach of Nassau, on behalf of the bishops of the Mainz province, to the pope and cardinals, to work for the Prince's reform. The pope did not dare to agree to them for fear of the king of France, and so they returned quickly, the business left undone. Meanwhile a general league of peace was made in Alsace under the Prince's authority, by the bishop as well as the cities, with nine arbiters appointed for the purpose. Rudolf and others of Hohenstein, holding Hohenstein castle for themselves, most of which belonged to the bishop of Strasbourg, shut the bishop's guards out of the castle. When the bishop was restored at the order of the nine arbiters, he declared that the men of Hohenstein had broken the terms of the castle, and he utterly demolished that very strong fortress. Pope Benedict, declaring the oaths of the bishop and the hostages null and absolving them, appointed executors who proceeded against the aforesaid Conrad and his supporters in many ways. By judicial sentence they declared Conrad, John of Schwarzenberg the dean, and many canons, prelates and clerics deprived of their churches and prelacies, and collected the revenues of those benefices. They also restored the aforesaid Ulrich of Sigenau to the provostship and collected its fruits, while John of Lichtenberg collected whatever fruits of the provostship he could. The aforesaid Conrad and John and their accomplices also laid waste with fire the bishop's village of Gugenheim and some neighbouring villages.

units.la: Cum autem Princeps & Maguntinus prædictum Bertholdum episcopum ad concordandum cum ipsis & ad recognoscendū sua regalia à dicto Principe, precibus, munerib. vel minus inducere nequiuissent: ipsi principes asserentes, ipsum episcopum asseruisse, si nuntij prædicti infecto negotio reuerterentur à papa, se velle concordare cum illis, quod ipse negauit, & quòd ipsi se pro liberatione episcopi fideiussores, obsides restituerint, & quod eos liberare nollet: ligę pacis generalis Rheni inferioris acriter sunt conquesti. Produxerant enim instrumentum sub sigillo Curiæ Argentinensis, quòd prædictus Conradus detentor habebat, in quo apparuit, Episcopum eidem Conrado, rogandi fideiussores, & ad liberandum eos se obligandi potestatem dedisse: & aliud, in quo ipsos Principes se astrinxisse pro Episcopo liquebat. Episcopus autem sibi nunquam docuisdem Principibus factam fuisse mentionem, dicebat: unde iudices inferioris ligæ pro dictis Principibus decernentes, diffidarunt.
units.tr: When the Prince and the archbishop of Mainz could not persuade the said Bishop Berthold, by entreaties, gifts or any other means, to come to terms with them and to acknowledge his regalia from the said Prince, those princes complained bitterly to the judges of the lower Rhine league. They asserted that the bishop had said that if the messengers returned from the pope without success, he would agree with them; he denied this. They also complained that they had stood surety for the bishop's release and had handed back the hostages, and that he would not release them. They produced a document under the seal of the Strasbourg court, which Conrad the holder had, in which it appeared that the bishop had given Conrad power to ask for sureties and to bind himself to free them. They also produced another in which it was plain that the princes had bound themselves on the bishop's behalf. The bishop, however, said that no mention of those princes had ever been made to him. Whereupon the judges of the lower league, deciding for the said princes, declared them defied.

units.la: Præmiserat autem Episcopus aliquoties Papæ & Cardinalibus nuntios & literas pro consilio & auxilio, vel quòd sibi indulgeretur, quòd posset Principi homagium exhibere, cum non præsumeret se posse finaliter reluctari. Papa autem dicens, illum coronam Imperialem non accepisse, respondit: quod si in eiusmodi consentiret Homagium, per hoc posset Romanæ ecclesiæ præiudicium generari: & quòd ipse Episcopus in resistendo illi, sine iactura Ecclesiæ, faceret posse suum. Licet autem multi Cardinalium ad subueniendum Episcopo feruenter instarent, papa perpendens factum, dixit: Isti vellent quod facerem perire istum bonum hominem, quem scio reluctari non posse.
units.tr: The bishop had earlier sent messengers and letters to the pope and cardinals, seeking counsel and help, or leave to render homage to the Prince, since he did not presume he could hold out to the end. The pope, saying that the Prince had not received the imperial crown, replied that if the bishop consented to such homage, it might cause prejudice to the Roman Church; and that the bishop himself should do all he could to resist the Prince, provided the Church suffered no loss. Although many of the cardinals urged eagerly that the bishop be helped, the pope, weighing the matter, said: "These men would have me let this good man perish, whom I know cannot hold out."

units.la: Monuit autem Princeps civitates Imperiales Alsatiæ contra Episcopum. Sletzistatenses autem, quorum Ioannes de Eckerich & plures alii fuerunt prædictorum Conradi & Ioannis seruitores, primò Episcopum diffidarūt, ipsum ignis incendio inuadentes, quos Episcopus potenter obsedit. Aderant autem sibi homines Ducum Austriæ, item Episcopus Basiliensis, cum quatuor millibus peditum, & ducentis galeatis. Item Abbas Morbacensis, miserat etiam sibi Vlricus comes de Wirtemberg trecentos galeatos, ita tamen, quòd nil contra oppida Imperii attentarent, cum quibus & cum Zabernensibus, oppidum Nuwilre eisdem diebus obsedit, & hi Sueui nemini pepercerunt. Episcopus quoque recedens de Slethstat, vallem Idberachtal, in odium Ioannis de Eckerich, cum exercitu est ingressus, omnia inibi reperta deuastans. Dispositi autem in sero, mane sub castro Eckerich castrametari, verùm quidam de exercitibus Ducum & Basiliensis summo mane comburētes villam Idberach/ direxerunt cornu exercitus extra vallem: de quo turbatus Episcopus egred-iebatur cum illis. Equitibus autem Basilensibus custodiam postremam habentibus, cum venisset ad locum nimis arctum, ecce Equites de Eckerich sagittis & lanceis insequentes, rusticis etiam lapidib. aciem Episcopi infestantibus de montanis, terruere postremos. Et volente regredi Episcopo, Iacobus Erberter fecit vexillum Episcopi cum acie progredi festinanter, ita ut vltimi ipsos quasi fugere æstimabant. Cumq; per viam arctam transissent, inimicis constitutis in arcto, dixit Iacobus, modò reuertamur in illos: hisque irruentibus in illos, vnus inimicorum prostatus in via arta, totam aciem impediuit, aliàs multi eorum capti fuissent. Quidam etiam ascendentes montana, rusticos fugauerunt, sicque in obsidione Sletzstat Episcopus reuertens, vineas deuastauit, remittensque Ducum & Basiliensium acies, repente ad obsidionem Nuwilre accessit, vbi Ioannes de Turckelstein, & alii aliquot occisi & capti fuerunt: quod cum aliquandiu obsedisset, recessit. Oppida quoque Columbaria & Ehenheim Episcopum diffidarunt. Venientes quoque Conradus de Kirckel, & Nicolaus de Salmis, Ehenheim cum pluribus equitibus, aliquas villas Episcopi incenderunt. Episcopus verò cum ducentis galeatis ad locum Ehenheim accedens, & aliqua comburens, cum multi de Ehenheim egressi sagittarent, irruente in eos Ioanne domino de Liechtenberg ferè vsque ad muros oppidi, aliisque repente sequentibus, multos illorum vulnerauit & captiuauit. Eodem autem die Columbarienses & Sletzstatenses, villas Pfaffenheim & Geblerswilre incendio vastauerunt. Erat autem tota gens Episcopi superioris Mundat & Abbas Morbacensis cum eis ad cōflictum praparata: sed Bertholdus Waldener aduocatus Episcopi grauis, gentem retrahens, factum confudit. Post hæc Rodolphus de Ochsenstein, & quidam alij de gente Episcopi, auferentes quosdam equos iuxta Sletzstat, omnes quasi de Sletzstat (quibus ex parte Principis aderant Albertus & Hugo de Hohenberg præsides) exire & agitare fecerunt. Cum autem prædictus Rudolphus, equitibus Episcopi, qui fuerunt in Aprimonasterio & in Thanbach, huiusmodi agitationem intimasse debuisset, vt prospere egisset: solus cum paucis deducere spolium credidit versus Tanbach. Sletz-statensibus autem repente insequentibus, multos de Tambach vulnerauerunt, occiderunt & captiuarunt.
units.tr: The Prince warned the imperial cities of Alsace against the bishop. The people of Schlettstadt, among whom John of Eckerich and many others were servants of the aforesaid Conrad and John, first defied the bishop and attacked him with fire; the bishop besieged them vigorously. With him were the men of the Dukes of Austria, also the bishop of Basel with four thousand foot soldiers and two hundred men-at-arms, and the abbot of Murbach. Count Ulrich of Württemberg had also sent him three hundred men-at-arms, on condition that they attempt nothing against the imperial towns. With these and with the men of Zabern he besieged the town of Neuweiler in those days, and these Swabians spared no one. The bishop, withdrawing from Schlettstadt, entered the valley of Itterach with his army, out of hatred for John of Eckerich, laying waste everything he found there. He had arranged to encamp under Eckerich castle that evening, but early in the morning some men of the Dukes' armies and of Basel, burning the village of Itterach, sent a wing of the army out of the valley. Disturbed by this, the bishop came out with them. The Basel horsemen held the rearguard, and when they came to a very narrow place, behold, the horsemen of Eckerich pursued them with arrows and lances, while peasants from the mountains also assailed the bishop's line with stones, and terrified the rear. As the bishop wished to turn back, James Erberter hurried the bishop's standard forward with the line, so that the last men thought they were fleeing. When they had passed through the narrow way, with the enemy posted in the narrows, James said, "Now let us turn back on them." As they charged, one of the enemy, thrown down in the narrow way, blocked the whole line; otherwise many of them would have been captured. Some of the bishop's men climbed the mountains and put the peasants to flight. So the bishop returned to the siege of Schlettstadt, laid waste the vineyards, sent back the lines of the Dukes and of Basel, and suddenly moved to the siege of Neuweiler. There John of Türkelstein and some others were killed and captured. After besieging it for some time, he withdrew. The towns of Columbaria and Ehenheim also defied the bishop. Conrad of Kirchel and Nicholas of Salm came to Ehenheim with several horsemen and burned some of the bishop's villages. The bishop then came to Ehenheim with two hundred men-at-arms and burned some places. When many men of Ehenheim came out and shot arrows, John, lord of Lichtenberg, charged at them almost up to the town walls, others suddenly following, and he wounded and captured many of them. On the same day the men of Columbaria and Schlettstadt laid waste the villages of Pfaffenheim and Geblerswiller with fire. The bishop's whole force of Upper Mundat and the abbot of Murbach were made ready with them for battle, but Berthold Waldner, the bishop's heavy advocate, called back the people and so spoiled the enterprise. After this Rudolf of Ochsenstein and certain others of the bishop's men seized some horses near Schlettstadt and caused all the people of Schlettstadt, for whom the Prince's governors Albert and Hugo of Hohenberg were present, to come out and be driven off. But when the aforesaid Rudolf ought to have announced this raid to the bishop's horsemen who were at Aprimonasterium and Tanbach, so that the affair might succeed, he thought he could lead the booty away towards Tanbach alone with a few men. The men of Schlettstadt suddenly pursued them, and wounded, killed and captured many of the men of Tambach.

units.la: Cumque huiusmodi dura commotio diu duraret, nec fuisset aliqua villa ex utraque parte, quae non fuisset incensa, vel cum aduersariis de pecuniarum summis pacisci coacta, Ducesque Austriae genti suae, ne Episcopo contra Principem assisterent, inhiberent, Argentinensesque in immensum damnificati fuissent: Ecce Argentinenses inito consilio, nisi concordaret cum Principe, diffidarunt. Tunc Episcopus in expensis exhaustus, & a suis derelictus, metuensque se a suis oppidis excludi, propter fauorem Argentinensi anxius, licet paulo ante in Capitulo suo respondens consulibus Argent. dixerit, potius se velle reuerti in ordinem suum Teutonicorum, quam Principi homagium exhibere: de communi consilio omnium suorum fidelium, Spirae Principem accedens, sibique homagium faciens, regalia suorum ab eo tanquam Imperatore investitura accepit: protestans in Principis praesentia, eo consentiente, quod non minus domino suo papae vellet in omnibus obedire: protestans etiam ante accessum in praesentia multorum Comitum & Baronum, quod huiusmodi homagium faceret, non voluntarius, sed coactus. Sicq; in Choro maioris ecclesiae Spirensis cum Principe & cum Maguntino Missas audiuit. De omni quoque controuersia Episcopi ac Conradi, & Ioannis praedictorum in ipsum Principem ac in Vlricum de Wirtemberg, & Ludouicum & Fridericum, de Oettingen Comites, Episcopi fideles, extitit compromissum: qui Princeps, post plures tractatus in Monaco Bauariae habitos coram eo, cum non possent partes concordari, ratione praepositurae Argentinensi, tandem pronuntiauit cum aliis, quod Episcopus omnia quae promiserat praedictis Conrado & Ioanni ante captiuitatem, in captiuitate vel post captiuitatem, seruare deberet, & ipsi e contra. Quicquid autem partes desuper haberent inter se experiri, ipsis saluum esse deberet, quam pronuntiatione pars utraque commendauit. Comes enim Vlricus qui Episcopo in praedictis itineribus multos honores exhibuit, ipsam pronuntiationem sigillare noluit, nisi Episcopo placuisset. Cum autem coram Consulibus Argentinensibus super praedictis verbis fuisset plurimum disputatum, tandem Princeps omnia interpretaretur contra Episcopum, de quo & Maguntino liquere incepit, quod captiuitatis Episcopi fuerunt conscii & authores, Argentinenses omnes destitutos a beneficiis restituerunt, & Episcopum ad restituendum praedictum Conradum ad officialatum, quodammodo coegerunt. Tandem post multa differimina, datis per Episcopum mille marcis praedicto Conrado, ac mille marcis praedicto Ioanni, ac trecentis marcis Rodolpho de Hohenstein, pro sua parte castri, & multis aliis eidem Conrado factis cautionibus, & specialiter de annuis CCCC. L libris denariorum sibi dandis, de sigillo curiae, ac restituto iudicio ipsi Episcopo; & Vlrico de Sigeno we praepositi remanente, ipsisq; Episcopo Conrado, & Ioanne ligam iuratam contrahentibus, fuerunt in simul reformati.
units.tr: While this harsh disturbance went on for a long time, there was not a village on either side that had not been burned, or that had not been forced to bargain with its enemies over sums of money. The Dukes of Austria forbade their people to support the bishop against the Prince, and the men of Strasbourg were damaged beyond measure. Then the men of Strasbourg, taking counsel, defied the bishop unless he came to terms with the Prince. The bishop, exhausted by expenses and abandoned by his own people, feared being shut out of his towns and was anxious about the favour of Strasbourg. Although shortly before, answering the consuls of Strasbourg in his chapter, he had said that he would rather return to his order of the Teutonic Knights than render homage to the Prince, now, by the common counsel of all his faithful men, he went to the Prince at Speyer, did homage to him, and received the regalia of his lands from him by investiture, as from the Emperor. In the Prince's presence, and with his consent, he protested that he would be no less willing to obey his lord the pope in all things. He also protested, before the ceremony and in the presence of many counts and barons, that he made this homage not willingly but under compulsion. And so he heard Mass in the choir of the greater church of Speyer with the Prince and the archbishop of Mainz. The whole controversy of the bishop and of the aforesaid Conrad and John, against the Prince himself and against Ulrich of Württemberg and Counts Ludwig and Friedrich of Oettingen, faithful to the bishop, was submitted to arbitration. After many negotiations held before him at Munich in Bavaria, the Prince, since the parties could not be reconciled over the provostship of Strasbourg, at last pronounced with the others that the bishop should observe all that he had promised to the aforesaid Conrad and John before, during or after their captivity, and they likewise to him. Whatever the parties had against one another was to remain open for them to contest, and both parties committed themselves to this pronouncement. Count Ulrich, who had shown the bishop many honours on the aforesaid journeys, refused to seal the pronouncement unless the bishop was pleased with it. When the matter had been much disputed before the consuls of Strasbourg about these words, the Prince at last began to interpret everything against the bishop. It became clear to him and to the archbishop of Mainz that they had been aware of and were authors of the bishop's captivity. All the Strasbourg men who had been deprived of their benefices were restored, and the bishop was in some measure forced to restore the aforesaid Conrad to the officialate. Finally, after many delays, the bishop paid a thousand marks to the aforesaid Conrad, a thousand marks to the aforesaid John, and three hundred marks to Rudolf of Hohenstein for his share of the castle, and gave many other guarantees to Conrad, especially of 450 pounds of money to be paid to him yearly, together with the court seal and the restoration of the court's jurisdiction to the bishop himself, while Ulrich of Sigenau remained provost. With the bishop, Conrad and John entering a sworn league, they were reconciled together.

units.la: Post haec mortuo Ludouico de Strasberg Cantore Argentinensi, Episcopus praedicto Ioanni de Lichtenberg contulit Cantoriam. Spectat autem ad solum Cantorem capituli conseruare sigillum. Papa autem ob hoc Episcopum pro excommunicato non habuit, nec eo minus ei causas scienter commisit. Ligam etiam praedicti Ludouici Principis ac regis Franciae, dissimulans aegre tulit. Rogatus etiam ipse Benedictus super promotione suorum respondit: Si mei non fuerint damnati, tunc immaculatus ero.
units.tr: After this, when Ludwig of Strassberg, cantor of Strasbourg, had died, the bishop conferred the cantorship on the aforesaid John of Lichtenberg. But it belongs to the cantor alone to keep the seal of the chapter. The Pope, on account of this, did not regard the bishop as excommunicated, and nonetheless knowingly entrusted cases to him. He also bore it badly, though he pretended not to, that the bishop had joined the league of the aforesaid Ludwig, prince and king of France. When Benedict himself was asked about the promotion of his own people, he replied: "If mine are not condemned, then I shall be spotless."

units.la: Mortuo autem Benedicto, successit ei Clemens VI, per quem Bertoldus Episcopus est absolutus, praestito iuramento, quod eidem Lodouico de cetero non assistat, nisi fuerit cum ecclesia reformatus.
units.tr: On the death of Benedict, Clement VI succeeded him, and through him Bishop Berthold was absolved, on taking an oath that he would no longer assist this Ludwig unless he were reconciled with the Church.

units.la: Hvivs etiam Episcopi temporibus scilicet anno M.CCC.XLVIII, in mense Ianuario, in die conuersionis S. Pauli factus est terraemotus generalis & magnus, ex quo homines pati syncopem putabantur, qui & in aliquibus locis multis diebus durauit. Praesertim in Carinthia multa castra subuersa sunt. Nam in valle Steintal castrum Osterburg cecidit: Lenzeburg & Rosach ceciderunt: Ortemberg, Waldemberg, Schellemburg, Schwarzenburg ceciderunt: ciuitas magna nomine Villach cum omnibus muris, claustris & ecclesiis suis cecidit, ibiq; duodecim homines perierunt. Item <bl>Waldenstein / Wildemburg / Hohenburg / Wartemburg / Remmeke / Tranburg / Krancke / Lümburg /</bl> omnia ceciderant cum hominibus & rebus. Item mons quidam in eadē prouincia, qui iacet prope castrum <bl>Löwenburg</bl> cecidit, transferens se per dimidium miliare à loco proprio, unde maximus fumus exiuit, ibique lacus factus est per duo miliaria, qui submersit villas x v i i i, item castrum <bl>Landenburg</bl> situatum super quodam monticulo, in eadem valle, per impetum aquæ portatum est per dimidium miliare, & tunc primo cecidit mons & castrum <bl>Nuwenburg / Gutenowe / Gutenburg / Bemburg / Geilenstein /</bl> ibi cecidit mons super montem, cum arboribus, lapidibus, & domibus. In multis etiam locis aliis ex hoc incredibilia euenerunt.
units.tr: In the time of this same bishop, namely in the year 1348, in January, on the day of the conversion of St Paul, there was a general and great earthquake, from which men were thought to suffer fainting. In many places it lasted for many days. Especially in Carinthia many castles were overthrown. In the valley of Steintal the castle Osterburg fell. Lenzeburg and Rosach fell. Ortemberg, Waldemberg, Schellemburg and Schwarzenburg fell. The great city called Villach fell with all its walls, cloisters and churches, and twelve people perished there. Likewise Waldenstein, Wildemburg, Hohenburg, Wartemburg, Remmeke, Tranburg, Krancke and Lümburg had all fallen, with men and goods. Likewise a certain mountain in the same province, which lies near the castle Löwenburg, fell, moving itself half a mile from its own place. A very great smoke came out of it, and a lake two miles long was made there, which submerged eighteen villages. Likewise the castle Landenburg, situated upon a small hill in the same valley, was carried half a mile by the force of the water, and only then did the mountain and castle fall. Nuwenburg, Gutenowe, Gutenburg, Bemburg and Geilenstein fell; there a mountain fell upon a mountain, with trees, stones and houses. In many other places also, incredible things happened as a result of this.

units.la: Facta est autem pestilentia mortalitatis hominū, præsertim in partibus vltra marinis & maritimis, & aliis vicinis, qualis à tempore diluuii non est facta, aliquibus terris hominibus penitus euacuatis, multisque nauibus in mari cum mercimoniis, habitatoribus extinctis, sine rectore repertis. Marsiliæ episcopus cum toto Capitulo & quasi omnes Prædicatores, & Minores cum dupla parte inhabitatium, perierunt. Quid in monte Pessulano, in Neapoli, & in aliis regnis & ciuitatibus actum sit, quis narraret? Multitudinem morientium Auinione in curia contagione morbi, ex qua sine sacramentis perierant homines, vt nec parentes filiorum, nec è contra, nec socii sociorū, nec famuli dominorum curā habuerint? quòd domus cum omni supellectile vacuæ fuerint, quas nullus ingredi audebat? Horror est scribere, vel narrare. Nulla fuit ibi causarum agitatio, papa inclusus Camerae, habenti ignes magnos continuè, nulli dabat accessum, terrasque hæc pestis transibat, nec poterant Philosophantes, quamuis multa dicerent, certam de his dicere rationem, nisi quòd Dei esset voluntas: hoc nunc hic, tunc ibi per integrum annum, imo plures, durabat.
units.tr: There was also a pestilence of human mortality, especially in the lands beyond the sea and on the coasts, and in other neighbouring regions, such as has not occurred since the Flood. Some lands were entirely emptied of their people, and many ships were found at sea laden with merchandise, their inhabitants dead and no master aboard. The bishop of Marseilles perished with the whole chapter, and almost all the Preachers and Minorites perished, with half the inhabitants. What shall I say of what happened at Montpellier, at Naples, and in other kingdoms and cities? Who could recount the multitude dying at Avignon in the Curia from the contagion of the disease, by which men perished without the sacraments, so that parents had no care for their children, nor children for their parents, nor companions for companions, nor servants for their masters? Houses were left empty with all their furniture, and no one dared enter them. It is horrible to write or to tell. There was no pursuit of lawsuits there. The Pope, shut up in the Chamber, where he kept great fires burning continually, admitted no one, and this plague passed through the lands. Nor could the philosophers, although they said many things, give any certain account of these events, except that it was the will of God. It lasted here for a time, then there, for a whole year, indeed for more.

units.la: Peruenit autem ad ciuitatem Argentinam hæc pestilentia, anno Domini M. CCCXLIX, in æstate, & moriebantur ibi (vt dicebatur) x v i millia hominum. Iudæi autem propter pestilentiam præcedentis anni infamati sunt, quòd eam fecerint vel auxerint, fontibus & puteis iniecto veneno, & cremati sunt à mari vsq; ad Alemanniam: præterquam Auinioni, vbi ipsos papa defendit.
units.tr: This pestilence reached the city of Strasbourg in the year of the Lord 1349, in summer, and there (as it was said) sixteen thousand people died. The Jews, however, were defamed because of the pestilence of the previous year, as having caused or increased it by putting poison into springs and wells. They were burned from the sea as far as Germany, except at Avignon, where the Pope defended them.

units.la: Posthæc tortis quibusdam in Berna, in Comitatu Froburg & alibi, & reperto in Zofingen veneno, extinctisque Iudæis in pluribus locis, scriptoque de hoc Consulibus Basiliensis, Friburgensis & Argentinensis ciuitatum, maioribusque ad defensionem nitentibus Iudæorum, ac quibusdam etiam Nobilibus Basileæ, pro quadam iniuria Iudæis illata, ad longum tempus bannitis: ecce irruit populus cum bannerris ad Palatium Consulum. Quibus territis & quærente Magistro quid vellent? Responderunt, se nolle abire, nisi bannitis reuersis: pro quibus illico est transmissum, consulibus non audentibus egregi, quousque venerunt. Adiecitque populus, se nolle quòd inibi amplius remanerent Iudæi. Et iuratum est per consules & populum, quod in ducentis annis inibi nunquam residerent Iudæi. Conuenerantq; plureis, nuntii meliores earundem trium ciuitatum, quibus cordi erat retentio Iudæorum, sed populi timuerunt clamorem, capti sunt autem vndique in partibus illis Iudæi.
units.tr: Afterwards, certain men were tortured at Bern, in the county of Froburg and elsewhere, poison was found at Zofingen, and Jews were killed in many places. A letter was written about this to the consuls of the cities of Basel, Freiburg and Strasbourg, and the greater men strove to defend the Jews, as did certain nobles at Basel, who had been banished for a long time for a wrong done to the Jews. Then behold, the people rushed with banners to the consuls' palace. Terrified by this, the consuls asked what they wanted. They replied that they would not leave unless the banished men were brought back, and for these men a messenger was at once sent, the consuls not daring to resist until they came. The people added that they did not want the Jews to remain there any longer. And it was sworn by the consuls and the people that for two hundred years no Jews should ever reside there. Many gathered, the better messengers of those three cities, to whom the retention of the Jews was dear; but they feared the outcry of the people. And Jews were seized everywhere in those parts.

units.la: Indictus est autem terminus in <bl>Benefelt</bl> Alsatiæ, vbi conuenerunt, episcopus, domini, ac Barones, & nuntii ciuitatum. Nuntiis autem Argentinensium dicentibus, se nil mali scire de Iudæis suis: quæsitum est ab eis, cur vnæ de eorum puteis sunt sublatæ. Omnis enim populus clamabat contra eos. Conuenerunt autem Episcopus, domini Alsatiæ, & ciuitates Imperii de non habendis Iudæis. Et sic modò in vno loco postea in alio sunt cremati. Alicubi autem sunt expulsi. Quos vulgus apprehendens, hos cremauit, aliquos interfecit, alios in paludibus suffocauit. Nitebatur autem Petrus Swarber magister scabinorum & aliqui alii Argentinenses adhuc defendere eos, dicentes populo: Si Episcopus & Barones in hoc eis præualuerint, nisi & in aliis præualeant, non quiescent. Sed nihilominus inualuit vulgi clamor. Cremati sunt igitur absque sententia ad clamorem populi omnes Iudæi Basilienses in vna insula Rheni, in domo noua eis facta, feria sexta post Hilarii, anno Domini M. CCCXLIX, & sequenti feria sexta Friburgi, duodecim ditioribus retentis, vt per illos possent eorum debitores, arctare. Spiræ autem & Wormatiæ Iudæi in vna domo congregati combusserunt se ipsos, & inuenti sunt quasi omnia maleficiorum genera comisisse, scilicet in Hispania habito per eos dudum consilio, de veneficiis conuenisse. Item de nece multorum puerorum, de falsis literis & corruptione monetarum, furtis & aliis multis, quæ offendebant altissimi maiestatem. Aliqui autem Argentinæ, vt sedaretur clamor, sunt positi super rotis, statimq; necati, ne super rotis viuentes quid dicere possent. Ex quo contra maiores, maior suspitio est suborta. Factus est autem exosus propter potentiam suam, Petrus magister Argentinensis prædictus, tam Nobilibus quàm plebeis, & reformata est dura dissensio meliorum; cupientium habere quatuor magistros, quemlibet per quartam partem anni regentem, sicut seruatum est ab antiquo, præterquam xviii annis, post cedem magnam inter partes factam, quibus duo magistri, & vnus magister scabinorum perpetui, præfuerant ciuitati.
units.tr: A day was appointed at Benfeld in Alsace, where the bishop, lords, barons and messengers of the cities assembled. When the messengers of the Strasbourgers said they knew of no harm done by their Jews, they were asked why one of their wells had been removed, for the whole populace was clamouring against them. The bishop, the lords of Alsace and the imperial cities assembled, resolving not to have Jews. And so, first in one place and then in another, they were burned; elsewhere they were expelled. The mob seized them, burning some, killing some, and smothering others in marshes. Peter Schwarber, master of the aldermen, and some other Strasbourgers still strove to defend them, saying to the people: "If the bishop and barons prevail over them in this, they will not rest until they prevail in other things too." Nevertheless the outcry of the crowd prevailed. Therefore all the Jews of Basel were burned, without sentence, at the clamour of the people, in one island of the Rhine, in a new house built for them, on the Friday after Hilary, in the year of the Lord 1349. On the following Friday at Freiburg, twelve of the richer Jews were kept back, so that through them the Christians could press their debtors. At Speyer and Worms the Jews gathered in one house and burned themselves. They were found to have committed almost every kind of crime: that in Spain they had long before held a council to meet about poisonings; likewise the murder of many children, forged letters and the corruption of coinage, thefts and many others, which offended the majesty of the Most High. Some at Strasbourg, to quiet the clamour, were placed upon wheels and killed at once, lest while still alive upon the wheels they might say something. From this a greater suspicion arose against the magistrates. The aforesaid master Peter of Strasbourg became hated, on account of his power, both by the nobles and by the commons, and the harsh dispute of the better men was renewed. Some wished to have four masters, each ruling for a quarter of the year, as had been the custom from antiquity, except for eighteen years after a great slaughter between the parties, when two masters and one perpetual master of the aldermen had presided over the city.

units.la: Anno autem Domini, M. CCC. XLIX, Dominica ante Valentini, conuenientibus Episcopo & dominis Argentinæ in negotio Iudæorum, & crastino venientibus quibusdam carnificibus ad domum Petri prædicti, petentibus aliquid dari mechanicis de pecunia Iudæorum. Illoque commoto & aliquos in curia retinere volente, illi excepto vno, vi sunt egressi per vicos, clamantes ad arma. Venerunt̄ q; mechanici cum paneriis ante ecclesiam maiorem, armatiqué sunt Nobiles & eorum fautores. Cumque plura paneria fuerint cum magistro, ipse territus, omnes ad hospitia redire mandauit: manentibus autem carnificibus & timentibus se banniri, illis primi pellifices astiterunt. Relato autem aliis plebeis qui recesserant, illos mansisse: illi illico sunt reuersi, carnificibus assistentes. Mandantibus autem Magistris vt abirent, ipsos cum cuspidibus petierunt. Abeunte autem Petro in domum suam, alii duo iuerunt ad stubam societatis prope monasterium, vbi iussi per populum, officium resignarunt. Et euntes simul in domum Petri, se absoluì iuramento, eumque resignare officium, & dare claues portarum, Campanæ, sigilla & omnia talia, petierunt: quibus cum timore factis, & illo disparete, quatuor magistros, & vnum carnificem magistrum scabinorum, annales & nouos consules creauerunt: multis recitatis latisque sententiis contra Petrum. Sicque sabbato sequenti, Iudæi, qui per priores magistros ducti fuerant ad domum super Bruscam infimam, dictam Stolzencke, quasi vt abducì possent, ducti sunt ad eorum cimiterium, in domum combustioni præparatam, & in ducendo per vulgum vestibus sunt omnino nudati, in quibus multa pecunia est reperta. Defensi sunt autem pauci baptismum eligentes, & plures mulieres pulchræ, quasi inuitæ, multiq; pueri erepti ab invitis, sunt baptizati. Omnes alii sunt cremati, multiq; prosilientes de igne sunt interfecti. Duces autem Austriæ & Maguntini tenuerunt suos, qui per Iudæos baptizatos & Christianos multa intoxicasse dicuntur, multiq; alii talium facientes ea, postea sunt cremati, pluresq; Christiani torti, fassi sunt se recepta à Iudæis pecunia, & dictis quibusdam verbis super eos per Iudæos, promissoq; per eos de intoxicando, in tantam deuenisse dementiam, quòd libenter omnes Christicolas occidissent. Vnde successiuè omnes quasi baptizati Iudæi sunt cremati, & fatebantur eos omnes culpabiles.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1349, on the Sunday before St Valentine's, the bishop and lords of Strasbourg gathered over the business of the Jews. On the next day some butchers came to the house of the aforesaid Peter, asking that something be given to the craftsmen from the Jews' money. When he was disturbed, and wanted to keep some of them in the court, they, all but one, forcibly went out through the streets, calling to arms. The craftsmen came with baskets before the main church, and the nobles and their supporters armed themselves. When several baskets were gathered with the master, he, terrified, ordered everyone to return to their lodgings. But the butchers remained, fearing to be banished, and the first furriers stood by them. When the other commons who had withdrawn were told that these had stayed, they at once returned and took their stand beside the butchers. When the masters ordered them to go away, they attacked them with spears. While Peter went away to his house, two others went to the society's stove near the monastery, where, ordered by the people, they resigned their office. Then going together to Peter's house, they asked to be released from their oath, and that he resign his office and hand over the keys of the gates, the bell, the seals and all such things. When this was done in fear, and he had departed, they created four masters, and a butcher as master of the aldermen, annalists and new consuls, many sentences having been pronounced against Peter. And so on the following Saturday the Jews, who had been led by the former masters to the lower house above the Brusca called the Stolzencke, as if they were to be led away, were led to their cemetery, to a house prepared for burning. In being led through the crowd they were stripped of their clothes entirely, and much money was found in the clothes. A few who chose baptism were spared, and many beautiful women, as if unwilling, and many boys taken from unwilling parents, were baptized. All the others were burned, and many who leapt out of the fire were killed. The dukes of Austria and the men of Mainz held back their own people, who were said to have poisoned many Christians through the baptized Jews. Many others who did such things were afterwards burned, and several Christians, under torture, confessed that they had received money from the Jews, that certain words had been spoken over them by the Jews, and that they had promised poisoning, and had come to such madness that they would gladly have killed all Christians. Hence, successively, all the Jews, even the baptized ones, were burned, and they all confessed themselves guilty.

units.la: Indignatę sunt aut ciuitates Alsatiæ contra omnes tenentes Iudæos: vnde minister Ducum Austriæ, vix obtinuit, ne obsideretur, quòd captis omnibus Iudæis Ducum in Ensisheim, nuncium Austriam destinaret. Vlricus verò de Hasenburg experta perfidia, per se seruatos cremauit. Post hæc in fine Iulii Iudæi in Oppenheim sunt occisi. Insultu quoq; in eos facto in Franckfort, post regis recessum, se & omnes domos suas & vicinas cremauerunt. In fine autem Augusti, Maguntiæ flagellantibus se multis aduenis, facto rumore ex abscissione burse, & credente populo quòd rumor esset contra Iudæos: ecce omnis populus irruit in Iudæos, & occisis multis Christianis per eos, videntibus se non posse euadere, combusserunt domos suas, & seipsos cum rebus suis.
units.tr: The citizens of Alsace were indignant at all who held Jews, so much so that the minister of the Dukes of Austria barely managed to prevent a siege, after all the Jews had been seized in Ensisheim and he had sent a messenger to Austria. Ulrich of Hasenburg, however, having experienced their treachery, burned those he had kept safe. After this, at the end of July, the Jews were killed in Oppenheim. Likewise, when a crowd attacked them in Frankfurt after the king had left, they burned themselves together with their own houses and those nearby. At the end of August in Mainz, while many newcomers were flogging themselves, a rumour spread about the cutting of a purse, and the people, believing the rumour was against the Jews, suddenly all rushed upon them. After many Christians had been killed by them, the Jews, seeing they could not escape, burned their houses and themselves with their possessions.

units.la: ORTA sunt antem iisdem diebus, scilicet anno Domini M. CCC L, contentio inter partes in Gewilre & vicinia, & Abbatem Morbacensem, qui partem sculketi tenuit: postquam sopitam, Ritter de Stouffenburg & alii quidam, Hannemannum Waldener nepotem Argentinensis & Basiliensis Episcoporum, in oppido Lore, in mensa sedentem, noctè occidentes, vltra muros fugerunt. Quapropter Bertholdus Episcopus Argentinensis qui & ante castrum Stouffenberg destruxit, totaliter, iterum in anno Iubileo de mense Augusti, pro parte prædicti Rüter / funditus demolijt. Hic Reuter postea anno Domini L v in Iulio à Conrado de Waschenstein, duobus de Hadestat, Ioanne Waldener, & aliis de nocte intromissis, per quosdam famulos traditores, in ipso castro crudeliter est occisus.
units.tr: Around the same days, namely in the year of the Lord 1350, a dispute arose between the parties in Gewiller and the neighbourhood and the Abbot of Murbach, who held part of the Schlettstadt territory. When it had been quelled, Ritter of Stoffenberg and some others, while Hannemann Waldener, nephew of the bishops of Strasbourg and Basel, was sitting at table in the town of Lohr, killed him at night and fled beyond the walls. For this reason Bertold, bishop of Strasbourg, who had also earlier destroyed the castle of Stoffenberg, again in the jubilee year, in August, on behalf of the aforesaid Reuter, utterly demolished it. This Reuter was afterwards cruelly killed in the same castle in July 1355, when Conrad of Waschenstein, two men of Hadestat and John Waldener, with others, were admitted by night through some traitorous servants.

units.la: Bertoldus quoq; Episcopus Argentinensis redemit à Marchionibus de Baden, de consensu regis, oppida Offenburg / Gengenbach / Zell / cum attinentiis, obligans pro hiis telonium Argentinense: Item constituit Ioannem de Liechtenberg præpositum Argentinensem administratorem Episcopatus, post mortem, & iurauerunt ei vt sit minister, etiam de consensu & ordinatione consulum. Quæ Conradus de Kirkel thesaurarius & Lodouicus de Tierstein Camerarius, & quidam alii papæ scribentes, scandalum suscitarunt. Decubuit autem infirmitate durabili in Mollesheim Bertholdus Episcopus prædictus, qui Ioannem de Liechtenberg prædictum regis secretarium, vicarium constituit, in Spiritualibus & temporalibus, & pro eo perficiendo Ecclesiæ, ipse Episcopus cum Capitulo, & rex, papæ literas dirigunt seriosas.
units.tr: Bertold, bishop of Strasbourg, also redeemed from the Margraves of Baden, with the king's consent, the towns of Offenburg, Gengenbach and Zell with their dependencies, pledging for these the toll of Strasbourg. He likewise appointed John of Lichtenberg, provost of Strasbourg, administrator of the bishopric after his death, and they swore an oath to him as minister, also with the consent and ordinance of the magistrates. Conrad of Kirkel, the treasurer, and Louis of Thierstein, the chamberlain, and certain others writing to the pope, stirred up a scandal over this. Bertold, the aforesaid bishop, however, took to his bed in Mollesheim with a lasting illness, and he appointed John of Lichtenberg, the aforesaid secretary of the king, as vicar in spiritual and temporal affairs; and to bring this about for the Church, the bishop himself with the chapter and the king sent serious letters to the pope.

units.la: Mortuus est autem venerabilis Bertholdus Episcopus Argentinensis in Mollesheim / anno Domini M. CCCLIII, in vigilia sanctæ Catharinæ, in nocte: & in die Catharinæ in Ecclesia Argentinensi in Capella, per se in honorem beatæ Catharinæ præciosissimè constructa, & pro quatuor presbyteris lautè dotata, cum veneratione maxima sepelitur. Cuius progenici Lantgrauiorum de Buchecke nullus de genere masculino remansit. Et vacat Clypeus aureus cum tribus rosis rubeis, à summo decorsum, de Buchecke. Et statuitur Ioannes de Lampertheim officialis per Capitulum vicarius in Spiritualibus & temporalibus generalis. Et quarto nonas Decemb. eligitur conconditer, Ioannes de Liechtenberg prædictus, & quarta Ianuarii per Abbatem S. Albani Maguntini, autoritate Gerlaci Mogunt. Archiepiscopi, in ecclesia Argent. solenniter confirmatur, & sibi inscio per sedem similiter prouidetur. Quod audiens cessat ab administrando, non habitis adhuc literis. Et curiam ingrediens, sabbato quo cantatur Introit, Diaconus & presbyter, & crastino Episcopus, ordinatur. De præpositura verò Lutoldo de Krenckingen, præsenti Argentinensi Canonico, prouidetur.
units.tr: Now the venerable Bertold, bishop of Strasbourg, died in Mollesheim in the year of the Lord 1353, on the eve of St Catherine's day, at night; and on St Catherine's day he was buried with the greatest reverence in the church of Strasbourg, in the chapel which he himself had built most splendidly in honour of blessed Catherine and generously endowed for four priests. No male heir of his line, the landgraves of Bucheck, survived. And the golden shield with three red roses, borne from the top of the arms of Bucheck, is now vacant. John of Lampertheim, the official, was appointed by the chapter as general vicar in spiritual and temporal affairs. On the fourth of the Nones of December [2 December] John of Lichtenberg was jointly elected, and on the fourth of January he was solemnly confirmed in the church of Strasbourg by the abbot of St Alban's in Mainz, by authority of Gerlach, archbishop of Mainz; and by the see, without his knowledge, a provision was likewise made for him. On hearing this he ceased from administering, as he had not yet received letters. Entering the court, on the Saturday on which the Introit is sung, he was ordained deacon and priest, and on the following day bishop. The provostship was given to Lutold of Krenkingen, at that time a canon of Strasbourg.

units.la: Episcopus autem sequenti feria quarta in ecclesia Cathedrali celebrat primam missam: & in die Palmarum reuersus, in coena Domini Chrisma conficit, & pœnitentes introducit in nouillari & mille homines communicat. Zabernie verò festum Paschale peragès, ordines celebrat, magnamq; Baronum, & militum solennitatem habens, nimis se religiosum ostendit. In qua religione vsq; ad mortem perdurauit.
units.tr: The bishop, on the following Wednesday, celebrated his first mass in the cathedral church; and returning on Palm Sunday, on Maundy Thursday he consecrated the chrism, admitted penitents in the novitiate and gave communion to a thousand people. Then, keeping the Easter festival at Zabern, he conferred holy orders and, holding a great solemnity of barons and knights, showed himself excessively devout. He persevered in this devotion until his death.

units.la: FAMILIA BVCHECKIANA, CVIVS SEDES IN EA PARTE Burgundiæ minoris seu Cisiurane fuere, quæ olim pagus Auenticensis, nunc vero Nuithlandia dicitur, & Helvetiis paret.
units.tr: THE FAMILY OF BUCHECK, WHOSE SEAT WAS IN THAT PART OF LOWER BURGUNDY, OR CIS-JURANE, which was once the district of Avenches and is now called Nidau territory, and which is subject to the Swiss.

units.la: Hugo comes de Bucheck 1315, heros rerum gestarum gloria clarus. Berchtoldus, ordinis Teutonici, Spirensis primum, dein Argentinensis episcopus 1356. Mathias, ordinis Benedict. archiepiscopus Moguntinus. Filia à Bucheck. N. de Clingen baro maritus. Filia de Bucheck. N. de Signow baro maritus. Vlricus de Signowe canonicus Argentinensis. Anna de Signowe, Conradus comes Friburgensis maritus. Hugo de Signowe, monachus Murbacensis. Filia, de Signowe, Eberhardus comes Wirtembergensis. Filia, de Signowe. Vlricus baro in Suartzenburg. Iohanna de Bucheck. Burkardus Sen de Münsingen, baro & eques. Ioannes Sen episcopus Basil. 1356. Benignosa Scania, Fridericus von Hausen eques, Alisia, maritus. Filia de Bucheck, abbatissa in Frawenbrunn prope Bernam. Henricus comes in Bucheck, Lantgravius Burgundiæ. N. comitissa de Straßberg, coniunx 1390.
units.tr: Hugo, count of Bucheck, 1315, a hero renowned for his deeds. Berthold, of the Teutonic Order, first bishop of Speyer, then of Strasbourg, 1356. Matthias, of the Benedictine order, archbishop of Mainz. Daughter of Bucheck, married to N. of Klingen, baron. Daughter of Bucheck, married to N. of Signau, baron. Ulrich of Signau, canon of Strasbourg. Anna of Signau, married to Conrad, count of Freiburg. Hugo of Signau, monk of Murbach. Daughter of Signau, married to Eberhard, count of Württemberg. Daughter of Signau, married to Ulrich, baron of Schwarzenburg. Johanna of Bucheck. Burkhard the Elder of Münsingen, baron and knight. John the Elder, bishop of Basel, 1356. Benigna of Scania, married to Frederick von Hausen, knight. Alice, married. Daughter of Bucheck, abbess at Frauenbrunn near Bern. Henry, count of Bucheck, landgrave of Burgundy. N., countess of Strassberg, wife, 1390.

units.la: SERENISSIMO PRINCIPI DOMINO K. REGI Francorum illustri, consanguineo carissimo, Wenceslaus D.C. Romanorum rex, salutem, & fraternæ dilectionis mutuum incrementum.
units.tr: To the most serene prince, the lord K., illustrious king of the Franks, dearest kinsman: Wenceslaus, by the grace of God king of the Romans, greetings, and a mutual increase of brotherly affection.

units.la: SERENISSIME Princeps, consanguinee carissime. Venientibus ad nos proximè honorabilibus ambasiatoribus vestris, in facto sanctæ matris ecclesiæ hucusq; miserabiliter laniatæ, deliberauimus ad serenitatem nostram, serenissimos principes & dominos, Sigismundum regem Vngariæ fratrem nostrum carissimum, ac W. regem Poloniæ, Marchiones Moraviæ patruos nostros carissimos, ac Duces Poloniæ, nostro regno Bohemiæ subiectos aliosq; nostros Imperij sacri regniq; Bohemiæ principes ecclesiasticos & seculares, prælatos & nobiles aduocare. Verùm dictorum regum imminens necessitas & occupatio grandis natalium sedium, eorum aduentum ad nos, quamquam nobis inuitis, pertraxit. Veruntamen cum eisdem regibus & Principibus tali sumus intentione concordes, quòd ulteriori mora postposita, apud nos in ciuitate nostra Vratislauia, intra festum natalis Domini debebunt finaliter conuenire. Quibus auspice Deo nobiscum conuenientibus, ipsorumq; consilio, in facto sanctæ matris ecclesiæ, & signanter super via cessionis, sicut expedit, communicato: serenitati vestræ in huiusmodi facto per ambasiatores nostros solennes finale responsum volumus destinare.
units.tr: Most serene prince, dearest kinsman. Since your honourable ambassadors recently came to us concerning the affair of holy mother Church, until now miserably torn apart, we have resolved to summon to our serene presence the most serene princes and lords: Sigismund, king of Hungary, our dearest brother, and W., king of Poland, marquesses of Moravia, our dearest uncles, and the dukes of Poland subject to our kingdom of Bohemia, as well as the other ecclesiastical and secular princes, prelates and nobles of our holy Empire and kingdom of Bohemia. But the pressing need of the said kings and their great occupation with affairs in their own seats has drawn them to us, though not without our reluctance. Nevertheless, we are of one mind with these same kings and princes that, with any further delay set aside, they shall finally assemble with us in our city of Breslau before the feast of the Lord's Nativity. With them meeting us, God willing, and with their counsel taken on the affair of holy mother Church, and especially on the way of resignation, as is fitting, we wish to send your serenity a solemn and final answer in this matter through our ambassadors.

units.la: Præsertim cum etiam à Domino nostro apostolico, domino Bonifacio, de intentione & desiderio vestro nondum obtinemus responsum. Ideoq; eandem serenitatem vestram studiosius exoramus, quatenus vestra dilectio serenitati nostræ regiæ non imputet, quòd hucusq; vobis, absque dictorum regum & Principum, quorum in hac parte res agitur, quorumque consilia vitare non possumus, ne videantur esse contempti, quodq; omnes tangit, debet ab omnibus approbari: & quod à pluribus quaeritur, facilius inuenitur, responsum non valuimus exhibere, singularis in eo vobis amoris gaudium ostensuri.
units.tr: Especially since we have not yet received a reply from our lord the apostolic, Lord Boniface, concerning your intention and desire. Therefore we earnestly beseech your serenity that your love will not impute to our royal serenity that we have not until now been able to give you a response, without the said kings and princes, whose affairs are at stake in this matter, and whose counsel we cannot avoid, lest they seem to be slighted; and because what touches all ought to be approved by all, and what is sought by many is more easily found. We do this to show you the singular joy of our love in this matter.

units.la: Si enim à dictis regibus, quorum hucusque aduentum, confecti tædio, præstolati fuimus, responsum & consilium participassemus, dudum dilectioni vestræ responsum debitum dedissemus. Datum in Burgelins, die sexta decima mensis Octobris Anno &c. M. CCC. XCVIII.
units.tr: For if we had shared a response and counsel with the said kings, whose arrival we have awaited until now, worn out with weariness, we would long since have given your love the response owed. Given at Burgelins, on the sixteenth day of October, in the year 1398.

units.la: SENTENTIA EXAVTORATIONIS 30 ET PRIVATIONIS DOMINI WENCESLAI ROMANORUM regis, lata ab Imperij Electoribus, anno Domini M.CCCC.
units.tr: THE SENTENCE OF DEPOSITION AND DEPRIVATION OF LORD WENCESLAUS, KING OF THE ROMANS, pronounced by the Electors of the Empire, in the year of the Lord 1400.

units.la: N nomine Domini, Amen. Nos Ioannes Dei gratia sanctæ Moguntinensis ecclesiæ archiepiscopus, sacri Romani Imperij per Germaniam archicancellarius, notum facimus vniuersis, præsentibus & futuris. Quàm varia, multiplicia & grauia cum incommoda tum dissidia multis abhinc annis, in sacram ecclesiam inuecta sint, etiamnum durantia, atque indies vberiùs pullulantia, in sacri Romani imperii (quod ecclesiæ Dei & orbi Christiano præsidio esse debebat) grauissimam conuulsionem, imminutionem & dissipationem: id omne vt scribi nequit, sic mala indies ingruëtia, manifestè satis docent atque comprobant. Eamque ob rem sacri Romani iuperii domini Electores, interuenientibus sacræ ecclesiæ, Principum, dynastarum, ciuitatum, prouinciarum & subditorum sacri imperii, prudentem moderatorem expetentium, ardentibus precibus, illustrissimum Principem dominum Wenceslaum Bohemiæ regem, tum sua, tum amicorum opera, literis denique, iampridem, persæpe & seriò nobiscum admonuere, eique diligenter ob oculos posuere, priuatim ac publicè, indecentes ac detestabiles eius in imperando mores & actiones, nec non eiusmodi ecclesiæ orbisque Christiani defectus, incommoda atque dissidia, grauissimasque item membrorum sacri Imperii auulsiones, diminutionesque, contra nominis sui dignitatem damnosè factas, fierique permissas, nempe quòd pacem in ecclesia non promouerit, quanquam id summa orbis Christiani necessitas, nec non ipsius, ceu aduocati & defensoris ecclesiæ munus flagitaret, & ad id faciendum sæpiùs rogatus, requisitus & admonitus effet: ipso nihilominus imperiū membris aliquot perniciosè mutilante, & mutilum reddi permittente. In quorum numero sunt Mediolanum & prouincia Longobardiæ, quæ iuris sacri Romani imperij fuerant, redeuntibus inde ad imperium amplissimis emolumentis: in qua ditione Mediolanensis, veluti minister, sacri imperij partibus fungebatur: cum is, contra quàm eius sublimitatem & dignitatem decebat, accepta pecunia Mediolani ducem & comitem Papiensem creauit. Complures insuper vrbes terrasq; tam in Germania quàm Italia, ad imperium pertinentes, quarum quedam ad idem redierant, alienauit: parum pensi habens, vt eas sacro imperio retineret.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. We, John, by the grace of God archbishop of the holy Church of Mainz, archchancellor of the holy Roman Empire through Germany, make known to all, present and future, that the many and various, serious troubles and dissensions, both inflicted on the holy Church for many years now, still continuing and daily breaking out more widely, have brought the most grievous convulsion, diminution and dispersal upon the holy Roman Empire, which ought to be a safeguard to the Church of God and to the Christian world. All this, though it cannot be fully written down, the evils that grow daily make plain enough and prove. For this reason the lords Electors of the holy Roman Empire, with the intervention of the holy Church, of princes, dynasts, cities, provinces and subjects of the holy Empire, who sought a prudent ruler, with burning prayers, have often and earnestly admonished with us, over many years, the most illustrious prince Lord Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia, both by their own efforts and those of friends, and finally by letters, and have set before his eyes, privately and publicly, his unseemly and detestable conduct and actions in ruling, as well as the defects of the Church and of the Christian world, the troubles and dissensions, and also the very grave tearing away and diminishing of the members of the holy Empire, shamefully done and permitted to happen against the dignity of his name. Namely, that he has not promoted peace in the Church, although the supreme need of the Christian world and the office of him as advocate and defender of the Church demanded it, and although he was often asked, required and admonished to do so; yet he himself has harmfully mutilated some members of the Empire and permitted them to be mutilated. Among these are Milan and the province of Lombardy, which had belonged to the right of the holy Roman Empire, with very great advantages to the Empire returning from them. In that dominion the Milanese was serving the parts of the holy Empire as its minister, when he, contrary to what his eminence and dignity befitted, created a duke and count of Pavia for money received. Moreover, he alienated several cities and lands, both in Germany and in Italy, which belonged to the Empire, some of which had returned to it, caring little that he should keep them for the holy Empire.

units.la: Præterea, membranas perplures nudas, rasasq; suæ tamen maiestatis sigillo munitas, amicis pecunia vendidit, in quibus cum illis, tum aliis, in quorum manus istiusmodi membranæ venerunt, sub regio sigillo quæ scribere vellent, licuit. Qua ex re, ob sacri Romani imperij iurium & emolumentorum damnosam imminutionem & dissipationem, graues querelæ subortæ sunt. Controuersias porrò bellaque, quæ (proh dolor) Germaniam, aliasq; sacri imperij terras miserè afflixerunt & pessundederunt, atq; etiamnum pessundant, nil vnquam curæ habuit. Hinc prædationes, incendia & latrocinia orta, adeo funestis vel hodie incrementis, vt nulli neq; clerici, neque laici, neq; agricolæ neq; mercatores, neq; viri neque mulieres, siue terra siue mari, tuti versentur: templa, cœnobia, & domus sacræ, quas sacrum imperium manu asserere atq; tueri decebat, rapinis & incendiis pateant & ad interitum redigantur. Eò res abiit, vt quiuis contra iuris & æqui rationem, alium pro arbitrio tractàrit, ac etiamnum tractet, absq; vlla sacræ, spretæq; diu, imperialis auctoritatis reformidatione: sic vt & locus conueniendi quempiam, vbi nomine imperij iuris defensio & patrocinium suscipiatur, planè ignoretur. Denique, quod horrendum & immane dictu, cum propria, tum aliorum facinorosorum quos secum habet, manu, reuerendos sacrorum antistites, sacerdotes & spirituales personas, alios item plures honestæ notæ homines, contra iuris normam, secus quam Romanorum regem decebat, neci dedit, aquis submersit, igne cremauit, miserabiliter ac truculenter peremit. Quæ quidem memorata, aliaq; multa grauia facinora atq; damna adeò diuulgata sunt & palam nota, vt excusari vel celari nullatenus queant. Nos igitur, vt præscripsimus, sæpius eum perquam studiosè orauimus, admonuimus & requisiuimus, vt indecenti hac vitæ ratione repudiata, id sibi studij & laboris sumeret, quò sacræ ecclesiæ, opem eius veluti Romanorum regis & aducati sui multoties implorantis, pacem & tranquillitatem, sacro autem imperio pristinum honorem, terras, ditiones, emolumenta deniq; sua recuperaret, in subsidium & consolationem orbis Christiani, hoc nomine grauiter debilitati atq; oppressi.
units.tr: Besides, he sold for money to his friends very many blank parchments, bare and scraped, yet marked with his majesty's seal, so that both those and others into whose hands such parchments came were allowed to write whatever they wished under the royal seal. From this, because of the harmful diminution and dispersal of the rights and advantages of the holy Roman Empire, grave complaints have arisen. Furthermore, the controversies and wars which (alas) have wretchedly afflicted and ruined Germany and the other lands of the holy Empire, and still ruin them, he never cared about at all. Hence plunder, arson and robbery have arisen, with such deadly increase even today that neither clergy nor laity, neither farmers nor merchants, neither men nor women, whether by land or sea, live in safety; temples, monasteries and holy houses, which the holy Empire ought to have upheld and protected with its hand, lie open to plunder and fire and are reduced to ruin. Things have gone so far that anyone at all has treated another at his own will, contrary to the rule of right and justice, and still treats him, with no fear of the holy and long-despised imperial authority; so much so that a place where, in the name of the Empire, the defence and protection of right might be undertaken is quite unknown. Finally, which is horrible and monstrous to say, with his own hand and that of the criminals he keeps with him, he has put to death, against the norm of law and in a manner unbefitting the King of the Romans, reverend bishops, priests and spiritual persons, and other persons of honourable standing in large numbers; he has drowned them in water, burned them with fire, and killed them miserably and savagely. These and many other grave crimes and losses mentioned are so widely spread and so openly known that they cannot in any way be excused or hidden. Therefore we, as we have written above, have very earnestly and often begged, admonished and required him to put aside this unseemly manner of life and to take up the care and labour of restoring to the holy Church, which has many times implored his aid as King of the Romans and its advocate, peace and tranquillity, and to the holy Empire its former honour, lands, dominions and finally its advantages, for the help and comfort of the Christian world, which is gravely weakened and oppressed on this account.

units.la: Etsi verò prædicto domino Wenceslao, hos aliosq; graviores defectus, ipsum tanquam Romanorum regem imperiumq; concernentes, clarissimè explicuerimus, ac scriptis exhibuerimus: auditis tamē illius responsis, reiteratisq; seriis nostris exhortationibus, communicato quinetiam sacræ sedi Romanæ negotio, nunquam adhuc deprehendimus, cum, sic vt Romanorum regem decet mores composuisse, scilicet ad ecclesiæ pacem, orbi Christiano summè necessariam, sacro item imperio dignitates, terras ac ditiones suas, recuperandas, & fructuosè conseruandas: id quod per vniuersas imperij prouincias est notissimum.
units.tr: Although, indeed, we have clearly set out to the aforesaid Lord Wenceslaus these and other more serious defects, which concern him as King of the Romans and the Empire, and have presented them in writing, yet, having heard his replies and having repeated our earnest exhortations, and having even communicated the business to the holy Roman See, we have never yet found that he has conducted himself as the King of the Romans ought, namely by seeking the peace of the Church, which is most necessary to the Christian world, and by recovering and wisely preserving for the holy Empire its dignities, lands and dominions. This is most widely known throughout all the provinces of the Empire.

units.la: Quoniam igitur commemoratos pluresque alios defectus, sacram ecclesiam & imperium, graui cum damno gemituque tangentes, ob instantes prædictorum preces, maximè verò sacramenti ratione, quo nos, ceu sacri Imperij proximè superiora membra, eidem obstringimur, nec reticere nec sustinere diutius potuimus: idcirco ex officio debito cogitandum annitendumque nobis fuit, vt sacro imperio, cuius vecordi & negligenti administratione incommoda isthæc irrepserunt, in orbis Christiani præsidium & consolationem, rectius & salubrius prouideretur. Et sanè vt is parendo nobis rem gratam præstitisset, sic eum sufficienter & seriò vocauimus atque citauimus, adeò vt ei significauerimus, nisi loco & die definitis præsto esset, fore, vt cum exhibitarum nobis precum, tum iuramenti nostri respectu, eiusmodi consilia capere & inire cogeremur, quibus sacrum imperium melius constitueretur: literis id nostris clarissimè attestantibus. Eapropter loco & tempore præscriptis, vnà cum Coelectoribus nostris sufficiēter exoratis,cæteris itē sacri imperij principibus & vrbibus, comparuimus,de die in diem expectantes,num præfatus dns Wenceslaus comparitūrus esset,morbis p̄dictis remediū adhibiturus:ac S.Imperij rebus rectiùs deinceps cōsulturus.
