At is nec cōparere nec quenq̄ procuratorio nomine ad nos destinare dignatus est.Quare cum tot prægnantium & perniciosorum, defectuum caussa, eum crebrius priuatim & benignè,inde verò,cum nil proficeremus, coram principibus, optimatibus & vrbibus imperij,in diuersis conuentibus, non sine magnis grauibusq; expensis, absq; tamē vllo fructu,admonuerimus & redarguerimus:ideò cōmemorata omnia, ad sacram sedem Romanā detulimus.Cæterum cum nec tum cuncta hæc quicquam pensi habuerit:nil aliud inde coniicere potuimus, quàm eum & ecclesiæ & Christiani orbis,inprimis autem sacri Imperij,curā deposuisse. Idcirco malum hoc,toti Christianæ reip.exitiale minime diutius ferendum & tolerandum censentes, animo bene confirmato,post multos variosq; tractatus consultationesq;, tum inter nosipsos, tum etiam cum aliis principibus & optimatibus sacri Imperij seriò habitos, pro ecclesiæ salute,Christiani orbis consolatione, sacri Imperij honore & vtilitate, præfatum dominum Wenceslaum, tanquam negligentem & destructorem Imperij, eoq; indignum,à sacro Romano imperio, omniq; eius dignitate hoc tempore penitus remouendum esse,duximus.
units.tr: Since, therefore, we could no longer keep silent about or endure the aforementioned and many other defects, which touch the holy Church and the Empire with grave loss and lamentation, on account of the pressing prayers of the aforesaid men, and above all by reason of the oath by which we are bound to him as the members of the holy Empire nearest above him, it was incumbent on us, from our bounden duty, to consider and strive how the holy Empire, through whose mad and negligent administration these troubles have crept in, might be better and more wholesomely provided for the protection and comfort of the Christian world. And indeed, so that he might render us the favour of obeying, we summoned and cited him sufficiently and earnestly, so that we made it plain to him that, unless he were present at the appointed place and day, we would be compelled, both by reason of the prayers presented to us and of our oath, to take and adopt such measures as would better establish the holy Empire; our letters bear clear witness to this. Therefore, at the prescribed place and time, together with our fellow Electors, sufficiently persuaded, and with the other princes and cities of the holy Empire, we appeared, awaiting from day to day whether the aforesaid Lord Wenceslaus would come to apply a remedy to the aforesaid evils and to take better counsel henceforth for the affairs of the holy Empire. But he deigned neither to appear nor to send anyone to us with a power of attorney. Wherefore, since by reason of so many pressing and harmful defects we had admonished and rebuked him more often, privately and kindly, and then, when we achieved nothing, before the princes, nobles and cities of the Empire at various assemblies, not without great and heavy expense, yet without any fruit, we therefore carried all these matters to the holy Roman See. But since even then he did not care at all for any of these things, we could conclude nothing else from this than that he had laid down the care of the Church and of the Christian world, and above all of the holy Empire. Therefore, judging that this evil, deadly to the whole Christian commonwealth, must no longer be borne and tolerated, with our resolve well confirmed, after many varied deliberations and consultations held seriously both among ourselves and with other princes and nobles of the holy Empire, for the salvation of the Church, the comfort of the Christian world, and the honour and advantage of the holy Empire, we have judged that the aforesaid Lord Wenceslaus, as a negligent man and destroyer of the Empire, and therefore unworthy, must at this time be entirely removed from the holy Roman Empire and from all its dignity.

units.la: Nos itaq; Ioannes archiepiscopus,nomine prædictorum dominorum sacri Rom. imperij Coelectorum,nostroque, tum commemoratis,tum pluribus aliis insignibus defectibus caussisq; moti,hac nostra sententia,quam præsenti scripto damus atq; ferimus,prædictum dominum Wenceslaum,ceu inutilem,negligentem,dissipatorem & indignum sacri Romani imperij defensorem,eodem Rom. imperio, omniq; eius gradu, dignitate ac ditione ad idem pertinente, priuamus & submouemus: cunctis principibus,optimatibus,equitibus, ingenuis, vrbibus, puinciis & subditis sacri Romani imperij denunciantes,eos ab omni homagio & iuramento,personæ Wenceslai, nomine imperij,præstito,prorsus esse liberos:requirentes atq; monentos eos, sub iurisiurandi fide,qua sacro imperio adstricti tenētur,ne prædicto domino Wenceslao, tanquam Rom.regi deinceps obediant & obsequantur,neq; illi ius vllum, obsequiū, censum,reditum,aut vllam aliam obuentionem, quocunq; nomine tandē appellāda veniat,ceu Rom.regi pendant,exhibeāt,aut exhiberi permittāt: sed eiusmodi debita vtili & idoneo Rom.regi,diuino fauente numine deinceps sufficiendo,asserunt.
units.tr: We, therefore, John the archbishop, in the name of the aforesaid lords, the fellow Electors of the holy Roman Empire, and moved by our own reasons, both those mentioned and many other notable defects and causes, by this our sentence, which we give and pronounce by this present writing, deprive and remove the aforesaid Lord Wenceslaus, as useless, negligent, a squanderer and a man unworthy to defend the holy Roman Empire, from the same Roman Empire and from every rank, dignity and dominion pertaining to it; declaring to all princes, nobles, knights, freemen, cities, provinces and subjects of the holy Roman Empire that they are wholly free from all homage and oath sworn in the name of the Empire to the person of Wenceslaus; requiring and warning them, under the faith of the oath by which they are bound to the holy Empire, not to obey or comply with the aforesaid Lord Wenceslaus any longer as King of the Romans, nor to render or allow to be rendered to him any right, service, tax, revenue, or any other income, under whatever name it may be called, as due to the King of the Romans; but to assign such dues to a suitable King of the Romans, to be appointed henceforth by the favour of the divine will.

units.la: In quorum omnium fidē & testimonium, nos Ioannes archiepisc. Moguntinus, præsens instrumentum,per subscriptos Notarios,hac forma patente,confici,& maius nostrum sigillū appendi curauimus. Lecta & renunciata fuit sententia præmissa,per nos Ioannem archiep.Moguntinum,nostro & dominorū Coelectorum nostrorum ante memoratorum nomine,sub castro Lonstein ad Rhenum,Treuerēsis diœcesis, Brubachium uersus progressi,è publico folio,in tribunalis vsum ereēto,dominis Coelectoribus nostris ibidem iudicio assidentibus:anno dominicæ incarnationis 1400, indictione octaua, feria sexta, die 20 mensis Augusti,paulùm ante Nonarum tempus:Pōtificatus sanctissimi in Christo patris ac domini,domini Bonifacij noni,diuina prouidentia papæ,anno xi:præsentibus illustrissimis principibus ac dominis, Ioāne, illustriss.principis ac domini Ruperti ducis Bauariæ, & comitis Palatini ad Rhenum filio,Friderico Burggrauio Norimbergēsi,nobili Philippo, domino in Nassau & Sarbrucke,Emichone de Liningen,Ioanne de Zigenhaim,Cunrado Burggrauio,canonico nostro Moguntino, comitibus: Bernhardo à Westerburg, Ioanne à Limpurg, Reinhardo de Hanowe baronibus.Domino Nicolao Browin sacræ paginæ, Ioanne à Witenburg & Nicolao Burgman decretorū,domino Hermanno præposito S.Gereonis Colonien.legum Doctoribus.Item,strenuo equite Sigfrido de Lindowe vicedomino nostro in Ringaugia,Ioāne Bossen à Waldeck, burggrauio nostro Beckelnheim,& fidelibus Henrico Rulmanno à Dadenberg,Gerardo ab Emēberg, domino in Lantscron,Friderico de Sachsenheim,Kulmāno à Coneren, Ioanne de Dalburg, Rudolfo de Zeissikon,nec non pluribus aliis dominis,equitibus & ingenuis,spiritualibus & secularibus,magno numero astantibus , ad suprascripta vocatis atq; rogatis.
units.tr: In witness and confirmation of all these things, we, John, archbishop of Mainz, had this instrument drawn up in open form by the undersigned notaries and our greater seal appended. The aforesaid sentence was read and published by us, John, archbishop of Mainz, in our own name and in the name of our fellow electors mentioned above, at the castle of Lahnstein on the Rhine, in the diocese of Trier, as we advanced towards Braubach, from a public platform erected for the use of a tribunal, our fellow electors sitting in judgment there. This was in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1400, in the eighth indiction, on Friday, the 20th day of August, a little before the time of Nones; in the eleventh year of the pontificate of the most holy father in Christ and lord, Lord Boniface IX, pope by divine providence. Present, and summoned and asked to attend as stated above, were the most illustrious princes and lords: John, son of the most illustrious prince and lord Rupert, duke of Bavaria and count palatine on the Rhine; Frederick, burgrave of Nuremberg; the noble Philip, lord of Nassau and Saarbrücken; Emich of Leiningen; John of Ziegenhain; Conrad, burgrave, our canon of Mainz; the counts; Bernhard of Westerburg, John of Limpurg and Reinhard of Hanau, the barons. Master Nicholas Browin, of sacred page; John of Witzenburg and Nicholas Burgman, doctors of decrees; Master Hermann, provost of St Gereon's in Cologne, doctor of laws. Also the valiant knight Sigfrid of Lindau, our vice-dom in the Rheingau; John Bosse of Waldeck, our burgrave at Bökelheim; and the faithful Henry Rulman of Dadenberg, Gerard of Ebernburg, lord of Lantscron, Frederick of Sachsenheim, Kuhlmann of Coneren, John of Dalberg, Rudolf of Zeiskam, and many other lords, knights and freemen, spiritual and secular, standing by in great number.

Columbariam obsidet 28,12 expugnata terra dominorum Missinensium iter suum versus Alsatiam dirigit, vt Franciæ regē reb. propriis spoliaret 29,3 in Missinensiū terram stipendiarios transmittit 29,38 Colmariam recuperaturus proficiscitur 50,46 Rapperschuiler obsidet ibid. 50. eius copiæ 51,17,18 recuperata Colmaria porro in Alsatia quid egerit 52,27 Gallos infestat 54,45 Albertū Argentina progressum insequitur 59,45 in acie cadit vincente Alberto 60,19 Auftrium transitu prohibere conatur 58,28 inter Adolfum Cæsarem & Henricum Angliæ regem fœdus 54,50 Adolfi regis filius Moguntino episcopo se opponit 32,50 regis in Gallos expeditio 27, 6 in Flandriam expeditio 30,48 Alsatia discedit 31,53 interficitur 31,5
units.tr: Adolf, King of the Romans, besieges Colmar 28,12. After the land of the lords of Missen is conquered, he turns his march toward Alsace, so that he may despoil the King of France of his own possessions 29,3. He sends mercenaries into the land of Missen 29,38. He sets out to recover Colmar 50,46 and besieges Rappoltsweiler, ibid. 50; his forces 51,17–18. After Colmar is recovered, what he did next in Alsace 52,27. He harasses the French 54,45. He pursues Albert, who has advanced to Strasbourg 59,45. He falls in battle, Albert being victor 60,19. He tries to prevent Albert crossing into Austria 58,28. Alliance between Adolf Caesar and Henry, King of England 54,50. The son of King Adolf opposes the Bishop of Mainz 32,50. The king's expedition against the French 27,6; expedition into Flanders 30,48. He departs from Alsace 31,53 and is killed 31,5.

units.tr: Adolf, Count of Nassau, Roman king 26,42; 109,28. Crowned at Aachen, ibid. 50. He buys the margraviate of Meissen 109,48. He falls in battle 110,38. Pope Hadrian dies 13,17.

units.la: Æstus tantus quod per Iulium & Augustum oua in fabulo coquerentur 6,15
units.tr: Such great heat that eggs were cooked in the sand in July and August 6,15.

units.tr: Agiolandus, king of Africa, subjugates Spain to himself 79,39. His conflict with Charlemagne, ibid. 45; he is put to flight 80,14. Aimo, Count of Savoy 152,3. Albert the Great, lecturer at Cologne 14,17; his death 17,33. Albert, Duke of Austria 18,49. Besieges Zurich 27,13. A German prince 64,46. Takes up arms against Adolf 110,14. Elected King of the Romans, ibid. 55; his children, ibid. 31. He aspires to the kingdom of Bohemia 112,24. He seeks war with the electors on the Rhine, ibid. 34. Captured in one eye 109,16. Cruelly killed at the River Reuss 114,23, 27. Buried in the monastery at Königsfelden, ib.; afterwards carried to Speyer, ib. 31. Albert, Count of Habsburg 37,1. King of the Romans, designated at Mainz 58,51; 59,12. His deeds 60,34, 49. Summoned to the empire, he seeks the assembly under arms 57,40. He consults his own safety by flight 58,43. He charges the princes of the Rhine, burdened with tolls, 61,32. He wars against the Elector of Mainz, ibid. 31. He lays waste the lands of three archbishops and other bishops 62,28. Hostile to the spiritual electors 33,27. He enters Bohemia 36,44. The king holds court at Frankfurt 32,36. He makes war on the bishops of Cologne and Trier 35,4. His children 105,10. Albert of Haigerloch 106,4, called the prop of the Roman empire, ib. 23; abandoned by his own men near the castle of Lichtenstein and killed, ibid. 106,27. Albert, Count of Hohenberg 110,20. Bishop of Freising 154,11. Albert of Falkenstein, abbot of Morbach, dies 32,35. Albrechtsthal, a valley of Alsace 29,39; 106,8. The castle of Alkirch besieged 59,36. The seat of the duchy of Swabia 75,31. Alemannia, only a part of Germany 84,23. The monastery of Allenspach near Kaysersberg 19,9. Alexander of Macedon, born of his mother Olympias and of a dragon [...] 64,18 (called Hammon). Alsa frozen 8,13. Flooding of the Ill 23,55. The Alsatians pass over to the side of Louis 122,44. Lower Alsace is devastated by fire and plunder 86,41. Assembly of the estates of Alsace 177,43. The Landgraves of Alsace revolt 91,32. The Alsatian league, formed under the authority of Emperor Louis 174,37. The Alsatian war against the Bishop of Strasbourg, a rebel against the emperor 175,46. Andrew, King of Sicily, strangled through Joanna his wife and his cousin 105,55. Andrew, son of Andrew, King of Hungary, called in hope of the kingdom of Apulia 129,46; treacherously killed 130,29. The Angelic castle 71,27. The English successes in France 158,9. Truce between the English and the French 128,37. Renewal of war 154,30. The cause of the disastrous war 137,33. He pleads against the papal curses 126,6. He takes from the king of Bohemia the Alsatian towns pledged to him 127,4. Reconciled with Edward, king of the English 128,40.
